zu.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance variants can run Leaf Blade over Leaf Storm to have a more consistent Grass STAB move to clean, better dealing with walls such as Poliwrath and Carbink. However, Leaf Blade is worse at wallbreaking in the early- and mid-game because it lacks raw power and relies on Swords Dance.

Checks and Counters

Colbur Berry: Thanks to Colbur Berry, Uxie and Cofagrigus can stomach a boosted Knock Off from Shiftry and OHKO it back with U-turn and Body Press respectively.

Dark-resistant Pokemon: Dark-resistant foes such as Silvally-Dark, Gurdurr, and Alcremie can comfortably take Shiftry's Knock Off and OHKO Shiftry with their super effective moves. However, most of these Pokemon have to watch out for Shiftry's less spammable Leaf Storm, which can heavily damage them, and are obliterated by a boosted Solar Blade.

U-turn: Shiftry's 4x weakness to Bug makes it extremely susceptible to common U-turn users such as Silvally-Dark, Liepard, and Thwackey.

Faster Attackers: While Shiftry's Sucker Punch is very powerful and able to easily clean teams after a single Swords Dance, it is not strong enough to threaten faster Pokemon when unboosted. Therefore, faster attackers such as Silvally-Poison, Articuno, and Rotom-S can force Shiftry out.

Priority Moves: While Shiftry resists Thwackey's Grassy Glide and opposing Shiftry's Sucker Punch, it takes heavy damage from other priority moves such as Kangaskhan's Fake Out, which can pick off a very weakened Shiftry in sun. Piloswine's Ice Shard and Gurdurr's Mach Punch are noteworthy, as they need significantly less chip damage to take out Shiftry.

Mixed Attacker.description:
Shiftry is a powerful mixed attacker and stallbreaker. Sucker Punch lets Shiftry pick off faster attackers that have been weakened, such as Rotom, Manectric, and Jynx. Leaf Storm acts as a powerful special nuke, heavily damaging physical walls such as Qwilfish, Gurdurr, and Cofagrigus. Swords Dance lets Shiftry act as a late-game cleaner by empowering its Sucker Punch and also lets it wallbreak more easily with Knock Off, OHKOing Altaria that have been weakened after a Swords Dance. Defog is an alternative if the team lacks a Defogger and takes advantage of Shiftry's good matchup against common entry hazard setters such as Rhydon and Uxie.

Shiftry is a good pick for any offensive team looking for a strong wallbreaker with a great stall matchup. Qwilfish is an amazing partners that punishes U-turn with Rocky Helmet; in return, Shiftry improves the effectiveness of its Spikes by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Rapidash with Knock Off. Other physical wallbreakers such as Silvally formes, Sawk, and Kangaskhan appreciate Shiftry weakening physical walls such as Tangela with the combination of Knock Off and Leaf Storm. Shiftry also appreciate VoltTurn support from users such as Articuno, Uxie, and Rotom, which can safely bring it onto the field. Faster threats that resist Sucker Punch, like Sawk and Alolan Persian, are able to consistently force out Shiftry; therefore, checks to them like Rotom-S and Poliwrath are appreciated.

Sun Sweeper.description:
Shiftry is a powerhouse in sun, outspeeding the whole unboosted metagame and most Choice Scarf users. Shiftry's deadly STAB combination lets it OHKO most Pokemon it outspeeds, and it can easily break through defensive teams after a Swords Dance or Growth. Sucker Punch lets Shiftry revenge kill faster attackers when sun is not up. Sun-boosted Heat Wave lets Shiftry OHKO strong physical walls that can take its other moves, such as Shiinotic and Tangela, as well as OHKO Abomasnow.

Shiftry is a staple on sun teams due to it raw power and lack of offensive and defensive checks under sun. Sun setters such as Uxie, Liepard, and Exeggutor make for great partners that enables Shiftry to wallbreak or sweep. The former two can even safely bring Shiftry onto the field with U-turn. Other Chlorophyll users such as Exeggutor can also take advantage of sun and form a Grass spam core with Shiftry, weakening each other's checks. Fire-types like Ninetales and Rapidash can also utilize sun to boost their STAB moves and weaken Shiftry's checks like opposing Fire-types, Piloswine, and Gurdurr.

Shiftry is the most viable Chlorophyll sweeper in the tier, being able to muscle past common checks to Grass-types and sweep with its near perfect coverage at +2. Solar Blade helps Shiftry wallbreak more effectively if run on full sun teams, although Leaf Blade is more consistent once sun runs out and against other weather teams. Knock Off provides wide neutral coverage, hitting Grass-resistant Pokemon such as Noivern, Metagross, and Galarian Slowbro. Low Kick hits most Steel-types harder and has a chance to 2HKO Incineroar. Heat Wave is boosted by sun, hitting Fairy-types like Galarian Weezing and Togekiss neutrally as well as OHKOing Chople Berry Cobalion and Heracross, but it misses out on Incineroar and hits most Low Kick targets such as Registeel for slightly lower damage. Protect is an option that significantly improves Shiftry's matchup against teams that rely on Golisopod to check sun, although it sacrifices a valuable move.

Shiftry only fits on teams with sun setters, so Torkoal or Ninetales is a mandatory partner. Torkoal fits best on full sun teams, providing Stealth Rock and setup opportunities with Yawn, while Ninetales is more of a standalone wallbreaker that can form a semi-sun core with Shiftry. Darmanitan can also take advantage of sun, breaking down the opposing team's defensive structure and bring Shiftry into Water-types with U-turn. Heliolisk can similarly wallbreak under sun and pivot out of Ground-types. Entry hazard removal is necessary, as sun teams will often have multiple hazard-weak Pokemon, and Shiftry can get chipped into KO range of priority moves easily. Defog Noivern is a good utility option for this role, while Xatu can bounce back hazards and pivot with Teleport. Other hazard setters such as Rhyperior and Cobalion are needed if running Ninetales.

pu.overview: Shiftry possesses several unique qualities that make it a decent, if niche, Defog user. Its typing and Synthesis allow it to reliably handle offensive threats like Jellicent, Trevenant, and Coil Sandaconda. These traits also let Shiftry easily threaten common entry hazard setters like Gigalith and Sandslash. Shiftry is also good at pressuring foes like Charizard and Doublade, which pester other entry hazard removers, because of its decent offenses and powerful STAB Knock Off. However, Shiftry's defensive typing leaves it vulnerable to many common threats, such as Ribombee and Archeops. Shiftry is also 4x weak to U-turn, which means it usually must cede momentum to users like Togedemaru and does not reliably check Wishiwashi. To make matters worse, Shiftry sits at an awkward Speed tier, with prevalent threats such as Gallade outrunning it and pressuring it out as a result. Finally, though Shiftry tends to be less passive than other entry hazard removers like Eldegoss and Whimsicott, they are more consistent due to their better defensive profiles and utility movepools.

Defog.description: By running a defensive set, Shiftry can check foes like Gigalith and offensive Sandslash while comfortably supporting its team throughout the game. Leaf Storm is Shiftry's strongest viable STAB move and doesn't become weaker if Shiftry gets burned. 96 Speed EVs let Shiftry outspeed Timid Jellicent. Pickpocket punishes foes like Audino for removing Shiftry's Heavy-Duty Boots by stealing a foes' item. Clerics such as Ribombee can keep Shiftry healthy in case it gets statused, which is not unlikely given it likes to switch in on defensive Water- and Ground-types. Ribombee also checks Fighting-types like Gallade and appreciates Shiftry for punishing switch-ins like Charizard with Knock Off. Shiftry should be paired with Pokemon that can exploit the Steel- and Poison-types that it tends to draw in. Doublade and Galarian Articuno are offensive Pokemon that fulfill this role and benefit from Shiftry removing entry hazards for them. Walls like Sandaconda and Wishiwashi also serve this purpose on top of better handling Gigalith. Sandaconda can also run Rocky Helmet to punish the use of U-turn, with Shiftry's typing making it easier to bait the move out.

Swords Dance (Grass).description:
Shiftry has decent Attack and fairly decent Speed with incredible wallbreaking potential thanks to Swords Dance, Black Glasses, and Dark-type STAB moves and is strictly seen on Sunny Day variant Grass teams. Shiftry is great for Psychic- and Ghost-type matchups and beats common threats such as Dragapult and Indeedee. Substitute is useful for avoiding moves like Will-O-Wisp, Toxic, and Strength Sap from Pokemon such as Galarian Corsola, Mew, and Toxapex; with Substitute up, Shiftry can get a free Swords Dance and wall break. The combination of Sucker Punch and Substitute makes it difficult for revenge kills from Pokemon like Trace Gardevoir or Gengar to happen. Chlorophyll doubles its Speed, making Shiftry a fiercer wallbreaker to eliminate. Knock Off is useful for inflicting massive damage and removing the item of anything that tries to switch in against it, while Sucker Punch is useful for KOing faster sweepers such as Dragapult and Gengar. Maximum Speed investment allows Shiftry to outspeed Choice Scarf Charizard and Salazzle in sun, and maximum Attack investment with an Adamant nature permits Shiftry to reach its full wallbreaking potential.

Whimsicott and Virizion are viable options to set up Sunny Day, allowing Shiftry to outspeed Pokemon such as Mew and Jirachi because of Chlorophyll. Whimsicott is a better Sunny Day setter that helps with Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types thanks to Moonblast; Choice Scarf Virizion is useful for outspeeding threats like Alolan Ninetales, Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan, and Choice Scarf Charizard and has access to Smart Strike, Stone Edge, and Close Combat, which is useful for the Ice-type matchup. Appletun is one of the only Grass-types that can properly tank Fire-type attacks from Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Dragapult. Venusaur is another Pokemon that takes advantage of sun and can use Life Orb and Growth or Choice Specs and helps in the Fairy- and Steel-type matchup because of Weather Ball and Sludge Bomb. Ferrothorn is one of the best defensive utilities that has access to entry hazards such as Stealth Rock and Spikes; it is useful for tanking attacks from offensive Pokemon like Weavile and Cloyster and is very crucial for the Ice-type matchup. Rotom-C cripples Pokemon with Choice Scarf and Trick, which is incredibly useful for against Pokemon such as Corviknight, Mew, and Toxapex. Finally, Celebi gets Stealth Rock, which allows Ferrothorn to run Spikes, and has a number of coverage moves such as Psychic and Earth Power which helps fend off Poison- and Fighting-type Pokemon better.

Defensive Utility.description: The Defense investment lets it survive a Close Combat from Cobalion.

pu.overview: Gallade is a devastatingly powerful wallbreaker thanks to its strong STAB combination, excellent Attack stat, and solid coverage moves, which hit common physical walls such as Sandaconda and Doublade for super effective damage. With access to Shadow Sneak, it can pick off faster threats like Galarian Articuno and Whimsicott. Its STAB Close Combat is naturally strong in a tier with Rock- and Steel-types like Regirock and Togedemaru everywhere, and its Psychic-type STAB moves take on Fighting-resistant Pokemon like Comfey and Garbodor pretty well. With access to Swords Dance, Gallade can become even more powerful at the cost of losing coverage options. However, Gallade's Speed, while useful for outspeeding other slow wallbreakers like Centiskorch and Perrserker, is overall lackluster, and it relies heavily on ensuring faster foes like Ribombee and Sneasel are within Shadow Sneak range if it cannot survive a hit from them. Gallade's special bulk is decent, but its physical bulk is very subpar, which, combined with its few resistances and weaknesses to popular Fairy-, Flying-, and Ghost-type moves, leaves Gallade with little defensive utility. Finally, Gallade lacks recovery, and thus it gets quickly worn down by residual damage from entry hazards, Rocky Helmet, and stray hits.

All-out Attacker.description: Psycho Cut allows Gallade to avoid activating Rocky Helmet and Aftermath, which gives Gallade more opportunities to wallbreak. Psycho Cut is fully accurate and doesn't make contact, but Zen Headbutt has more power and can help Gallade get past answers like Aromatisse with brute force. Thunder Punch and Leaf Blade deny switch-ins such as defensive Charizard and Sandaconda. Knock Off hits bulky Psychic-types like Uxie and cripples other switch-ins like Jellicent. Muscle Band ensures 2HKOs on Pokemon like Quagsire and Hattrem with Close Combat and Knock Off, respectively. Assault Vest grants Gallade more defensive utility and allows it to survive one hit from super effective special attackers like Ribombee and Charizard, but it sacrifices power. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option to avoid entry hazard damage, which can quickly wear Gallade down; however, Muscle Band is heavily recommended due to granting better odds for OHKOs and 2HKOs. Justified punishes weak Knock Offs from Pokemon like Audino. Gallade appreciates the support of pivots like Ninjask and Wishwashi; the former can threaten Gallade's offensive checks like Galarian Articuno and baits in Pokemon like Gigalith and Togedemaru for Gallade to threaten, while the latter can switch into Pokemon like Charizard that force Gallade out and provide a free switch via its slow U-turn. Entry hazards support from Pokemon like Gigalith and Ferroseed helps wear down Gallade's answers like Alcremie and Comfey, especially if Gallade removes their Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off.

Swords Dance.description: Swords Dance turns Gallade into an even more powerful wallbreaker, with +2 STAB moves OHKOing Pokemon like Sandaconda and Regirock after minimal chip damage. Psycho Cut helps Gallade avoid activating Rocky Helmet and Iron Barbs, while Zen Headbutt is stronger but less consistent. Shadow Sneak is recommended to pick off faster foes like Ribombee at +2, but Knock Off can always be used to wear down switch-ins like Jellicent to sweep more easily later. Life Orb ensures the 2HKO with Close Combat on Quagsire, which can otherwise take a +2 hit due to Unaware, and provides more general power. Lum Berry is useful for avoiding status and allows Gallade to set up on Pokemon like Jellicent, Weezing, and Hattrem. A Jolly nature lets Gallade outspeed as many foes as possible, such as Modest Magmortar, and Speed tie with Timid Mesprit; an Adamant nature is unnecessary due to the sheer power behind a +2 Life Orb Gallade. This set fits mainly on more offensive teams due to its volatile nature, and it appreciates fast pivots like Ninjask and Archeops; in turn, they enjoy Gallade scaring out Togedemaru and Regirock, respectively. Without Shadow Sneak, Gallade is helpless against revenge killers like Gourgeist-S and Whimsicott, so Pokemon that can take advantage of them like Charizard and Choice Scarf Togedemaru are heavily appreciated.

nu.overview: Gallade sets itself apart from other Fighting-types in the metagame like Toxicroak and Passimian due to its part-Psychic typing, allowing it to threaten the tier's bulky Poison-types like Vileplume, Weezing, and Garbodor. It is an equally, if not even more, dangerous wallbreaker thanks to Knock Off and Swords Dance, letting it cripple and eventually muscle past common physically defensive Pokemon like Mudsdale and Quagsire. However, it matches up poorly against the tier's common offensive threats: Gallade's Speed tier is average at best and, considering its frailty, makes it very vulnerable to getting revenge killed by faster threats like Talonflame, Tauros, and Aerodactyl. It also faces tough competition from the aforementioned Toxicroak and Passimian, which have better defensive profiles and viable set diversity.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band gives Gallade the immediate power to cleanly 2HKO Quagsire; however, being Choice locked makes it easier to play around. Choice Scarf lets Gallade outspeed and revenge kill faster threats such as Salazzle, Toxicroak, and Tauros; however, it is generally outclassed by Passimian in this role due to it having U-turn. Assault Vest can make use of Gallade's solid special bulk to soft check special attackers like Salazzle, Rotom-C, and Heliolisk; Swords Dance is then dropped for Drain Punch to give Gallade a source of recovery, making more use of its added bulk.

Checks and Counters

Revenge Killers: Due to its middling Speed tier, Gallade is outsped and OHKOed by faster threats like Aerodactyl, Talonflame, and Tauros. Even though Talonflame hates getting its Heavy-Duty Boots removed, it has the bulk and typing to withstand any attacks thrown by Gallade, punish non-Protective Pads variants with a Flame Body burn, and gain momentum afterwards via U-turn.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Without a boosting item, Mudsdale, Quagsire, and Sylveon can comfortably tank a +2 attack from Gallade and retaliate with Toxic or, in the latter's case, a Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice. Moreover, thanks to Unaware, Quagsire ignores any Swords Dance boosts Gallade tries to accumulate.

Contact Effects: Non-Protective Pads variants can be extremely crippled by Talonflame's Flame Body, one of Gallade's best switch-ins. Poison-types like Vileplume, Weezing, and Garbodor that would otherwise lose to Gallade are more free to switch in on a predicted Fighting-type attack just to punish it with Effect Spore or Rocky Helmet and subsequently switch out to a Psychic-resistant teammate. The accumulated damage from Rocky Helmet and even Garbodor's Aftermath can easily put Gallade in range of being revenge killed, especially with the chip damage from Life Orb.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Knock Off targets Psychic-types like Xatu and Galarian Articuno; cripples walls like Quagsire, Sylveon, and Mudsdale; and reliably hits Ghost-types like Dhelmise, Decidueye, and Golurk without risking a Zen Headbutt miss. Protective Pads keeps Gallade safe from contact effects like Talonflame's Flame Body, Vileplume's Effect Spore, Weezing's Rocky Helmet, and Garbodor's Aftermath. Alternatively, Lum Berry lets it ignore Talonflame's Flame Body and Vileplume's Effect Spore once while enabling it to safely set up against status inducers like Vaporeon and Mudsdale. Life Orb allows +2 Gallade to OHKO Vaporeon and potentially 2HKO Mudsdale, as well as Quagsire, which would otherwise ignore any of its Swords Dance boosts with Unaware. If running Life Orb, Psycho Cut should be used over Zen Headbutt to give Gallade a non-contact attack for Vileplume and Weezing that still nails the OHKO at +2. A Jolly nature is used to outspeed Tsareena, Tyrantrum, and Decidueye.

Gallade fits well on offensive teams that appreciate its wallbreaking prowess. Pivots like Rotom-C, Tsareena, and Talonflame can bring Gallade into the field safely on their switch-ins like Vileplume, Weezing, and Stakataka. Talonflame in particular can also switch into faster threats like Tauros that would otherwise revenge kill Gallade. Swords Dance Silvally-Ground is a potent setup sweeper that can help threaten Talonflame with Rock Slide and enjoys Gallade pressuring Weezing and overwhelming shared checks in Mudsdale and Quagsire. Silvally-Ground can also run U-turn to bring Gallade in safely on Weezing.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Mega Gallade can opt to run Bulk Up and Drain Punch in lieu of Swords Dance and Close Combat; Drain Punch acts as a form of passive recovery, while Bulk Up makes Mega Gallade even tougher for physical attackers to deal with. However, the immediate damage output from Swords Dance and Close Combat is generally preferred. Substitute may be used to help Mega Gallade set up against passive Pokemon like Toxapex while avoiding status conditions from foes like Mega Sableye and Rotom-W, and it is opted for on Bulk Up sets, but it forces Mega Gallade to give up Knock Off or Shadow Sneak which are preferred in most cases.

Checks and Counters

Psychic

Fairy-types: Fairy-type Pokemon like Mega Diancie and Mimikyu can threaten to OHKO Mega Gallade with their powerful STAB moves. However, Mega Diancie needs to be wary of Mega Gallade winning the speed tie, while Mimikyu is easily threatened if Disguise is broken. Bulky Fairy-types like Hatterene can also check Mega Gallade effectively.

Ghost-types: Ghost-type Pokemon such as Gengar and Choice Scarf Blacephalon can outspeed and OHKO Mega Gallade with their Ghost-type STAB moves. However, they need to be wary of Shadow Sneak.

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive walls such as Mega Slowbro and Mega Sableye can easily switch in against Mega Gallade and proceed to burn it with Scald or Will-O-Wisp, respectively. Mega Sableye in particular is immune to both of Mega Gallade's STAB options and takes reduced damage from Knock Off, completely walling Mega Gallade.

Revenge Killers: Faster revenge killers such as Mega Lopunny, Zeraora, Tapu Koko, and Choice Scarf Latios can all threaten to KO Mega Gallade after very little chip damage. However, Pokemon weak to Shadow Sneak like Latios need to watch out for it.

Status: All forms of status can cripple Mega Gallade greatly. Poison puts Mega Gallade on a timer, limiting its ability to act as a reliable wallbreaker. Paralysis allows Mega Gallade to easily be revenge killed. Burn greatly weakens it as a wallbreaker.

Swords Dance (Psychic).description:
An excellent Speed tier, a sky-high Attack stat, and a great secondary type in Fighting that aids greatly against Steel and Dark teams make Mega Gallade an amazing physical wallbreaker on Psychic teams. Swords Dance allows Mega Gallade to further increase its already high Attack stat, allowing it to easily break through a majority of teams and walls like Celesteela. Close Combat is Mega Gallade's primary STAB option, dealing with troublesome Steel-, Dark-, Normal-, and Rock-types like Bisharp, Zarude, Porygon2, and Tyranitar. Zen Headbutt allows it to deal with Poison- and Fighting-types like Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Keldeo. Psycho Cut can be used in lieu of Zen Headbutt at the cost of some Base Power as a more accurate option that also avoids damage from Rocky Helmet and Rough Skin, as well as Poison from Toxapex's Baneful Bunker. Knock Off helps against opposing Psychic-types like Slowbro and Victini that resist both of Mega Gallade's STAB options while also helping with Ghost-types like Galarian Corsola and Aegislash. Knock Off also gets rid of items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots, crippling the foe as a result. Shadow Sneak can be used instead of Knock Off as a form of priority that also helps against fast Psychic- and Ghost-types like Latios and Choice Scarf Blacephalon. However, Knock Off is generally preferred for the increased power against bulky Psychic- and Ghost-types like Slowbro and Galarian Corsola, and Shadow Sneak proves to be counter-productive when paired with Tapu Lele. Justified, prior to Mega Evolution, allows Gallade to switch into weak Dark-type moves like Mega Sableye's Knock Off and gain an Attack boost. Maximum Speed investment along with a Jolly nature makes Mega Gallade outspeed threats like Choice Specs Blacephalon, Keldeo, and Landorus.

All of Mega Gallade's teammates appreciate its ability to deal with Dark-types like Hydreigon and Mega Tyranitar. Steel-types like Jirachi and Metagross pair up well with Mega Gallade, as they deal with Fairy-types like Mega Diancie and Clefable that threaten it, and they can better handle Dragon-type attacks like Draco Meteor from Latios and Latias while also being able to provide Stealth Rock support. Victini and Mega Gallade form a formidable physical wallbreaking core while also synergizing well against Steel teams, as Victini deals with threats like Celesteela, while Mega Gallade in return takes care of Heatran reliably. Latios and Latias act as the most reliable Choice Scarf users on Psychic-type teams and can provide Defog support. Latias in particular can provide Healing Wish support for Mega Gallade, which it appreciates greatly. Fairy-types like Hatterene and Tapu Lele further improve the Dark matchup while also dealing with Dragon-type threats like Mega Altaria and Dragonite. Slowbro provides a reliable defensive pivot, can act as a reliable Fire-resistant Pokemon against Pokemon like Cinderace, and is also able to bring Mega Gallade safely into the field thanks to Teleport. Celebi is a great teammate, as it reliably deals with Water- and Ground-types that threaten Mega Gallade such as Mega Swampert and Excadrill. Deoxys-S breaks through Flying-type teams thanks to its BoltBeam coverage in conjunction with Nasty Plot. Albeit not common, Meloetta can provide a reliable switch-in against Ghost-type attacks directed at Mega Gallade from the likes of Gengar and Blacephalon.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Bulk Up and Drain Punch may seem appealing to offer some form of recovery, but they fail to break through Corviknight in the same manner as Swords Dance. Shadow Sneak also seems nice, as it gives Mega Gallade a priority move, but it has no relevant targets and is simply not better than any of the listed options.

Checks and Counters

Strong Priority: Rillaboom's Grassy Glide, Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch, Aegislash's Shadow Sneak, and Mega Mawile and Bisharp's Sucker Punch bypass Mega Gallade's solid Speed tier and threaten to deal heavy damage to it.

Revenge Killers: Faster revenge killers such as Tapu Koko, Ash-Greninja, and Mega Lopunny all scare Mega Gallade out. None of these Pokemon can switch into it though, nor can they check a full health Mega Gallade due to its solid bulk.

Status: Being burned severely impedes Mega Gallade's ability to break through bulkier cores, and being Paralyzed ruins its solid Speed tier, leaving it vulnerable to slower foes such as Tapu Lele, Tapu Fini, and Zapdos.

Fairy-type Pokemon: Fairy-types such as Mega Mawile, Clefable, and Tapu Lele can stomach a hit from Mega Gallade, and threaten it back with their STAB moves.

Swords Dance.description:
As a Psychic / Fighting wallbreaker, Mega Gallade often draws comparison to Mega Medicham. Although Mega Medicham has more immediate power, Mega Gallade's access to Swords Dance, a higher Speed tier, and Knock Off differentiate it enough to give it a niche. Swords Dance allows Mega Gallade to clean up easier in the late game, when checks such as defensive Landorus-T are weakened into Zen Headbutt range. Knock Off can be used to threaten Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Slowking and cripple Pokemon that rely on their item, such as Volcarona, Zapdos, and Moltres. Ice Punch can be used to revenge kill Garchomp as well as nailing Gliscor, Mega Latias, and Landorus-T. It is important to note that upon Mega Evolving, Mega Gallade gains Inner Focus, protecting it from Landorus-T's Intimidate. Justified is the chosen ability prior to Mega Evolving to get an Attack boost by absorbing a weak Knock Off from Tangrowth or Toxapex. Maximum Speed investment and a Jolly nature allow Mega Gallade to outspeed Kartana and Garchomp as well as Speed tying Mega Latias and threatening the aforementioned Pokemon with an OHKO.

Quite possibly the best partner for Mega Gallade is Tapu Lele, as it appreciate Mega Gallade's ability to break through Corviknight, Slowking, and Heatran, and it provides Psychic Terrain to boost the power of Mega Gallade's Zen Headbutt, allowing it to break through Clefable. Other teammates that appreciate Mega Gallade's ability to pressure Corviknight, Slowbro, and Heatran include Garchomp, Volcarona, and Serperior. Additionally, solid checks to Fairy-types are appreciated, such as Ferrothorn and Jirachi. Jirachi is an especially great teammate, as its Healing Wish gives Mega Gallade a second opportunity to sweep. Solid entry hazard removal is also mandatory to give Mega Gallade more longevity, so Defoggers such as Corviknight, Zapdos, and Rotom-W pair well. Mega Gallade also appreciates Tyranitar and Weavile's ability to threaten Zapdos and trap Psychic-types.

ubers.overview: With its great bulk and good offensive stats, Giratina-O acts as a good attacker that threatens many top-tier threats, including Necrozma-DM, Groudon, Eternatus, Calyrex-S, and Calyrex-I. With strong physical and special Ghost-type STAB moves and Griseous Orb, it's one of the tier's few attackers to succeed both physically and specially. Levitate makes Giratina-O a good check to Ground-types such as Groudon, Landorus, and Landorus-T. Even though its bulk is great, however, Giratina-O has no reliable recovery and is vulnerable to chip damage from Stealth Rock and status. As a base 90 Speed Pokemon, Giratina-O can be outsped by defensive staples like Ho-Oh, and the special set is outsped by non-invested offensive threats like bulky Groudon and Kyogre. It also faces competition as a Ghost-type from Lunala and Calyrex-S; Lunala is a defogger that possesses better bulk with Shadow Shield and reliable recovery, which let it better check threats like Zekrom, while Calyrex-S hits harder, can severely cripple Yveltal with Trick, and sweeps weakened teams better with As One and Astral Barrage.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Giratina-O can opt for Roar or Dragon Tail to deal with bulky setup sweepers like Zygarde and Groudon. However, as it has no means of recovery, Giratina-O can struggle late-game to deal with these threats. Dragon Pulse can be used instead of Draco Meteor to avoid the Special Attack drop while still OHKOing Zygarde before Power Construct activates. However, it lacks power against non-Dragon-type foes. Outrage is an option over a status move on the physical set to let Giratina-O lure in Chansey, Blissey, and Zygarde. However, being locked into the move means Giratina-O will easily be revenge killed. Finally, a fully offensive set with Hone Claws alongside an EV spread of 252 Atk / 4 Def / 252 Spe and an Adamant nature can be used on Sticky Web teams. However, Giratina-O struggles to set up due to its lack of recovery and mediocre defensive typing; it also has a difficult time breaking through defensive cores even with the boosts.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Dark-types: Tyranitar, Zarude, and Yveltal are bulky enough to take any hit from Giratina-O, heal back the damage, and heavily threaten it with their Dark-type attacks. Jungle Healing Zarude can even use Giratina-O as a setup fodder.

Xerneas: Xerneas heavily threatens Giratina-O with Moonblast. Defensive Xerneas can use Giratina-O to support its team with Aromatherapy, while the offensive variant can set up with Geomancy without caring about it much. However, being 2HKOed by status-boosted Hex means Xerneas can't be switched in blindly, especially if it is asleep.

Chansey and Blissey: Both Chansey and Blissey completely wall all variants of Giratina-O, barring its Hone Claws variant, with their immense bulk. Plus, they cripple Giratina-O with either Toxic or Thunder Wave and can absorb status with ease thanks to Natural Cure.

Ghost- and Dragon-types: While they can't switch into Giratina-O, the Ghost- and Dragon-types of the tier such as Calyrex-S, Marshadow, Zekrom, Eternatus, and Zygarde offensively check it.

Status: Both burn and poison heavily reduce Giratina-O's longevity and power, while paralysis means Calyrex-I and defensive Kyogre can take advantage of it.

Special Attacker.description:
This set utilizes Giratina-O's great Special Attack and Griseous Orb to pressure common bulky threats such as Zygarde, Groudon, and Necrozma-DM. Shadow Sneak allows Giratina-O to safely revenge kill weakened, faster threats like Calyrex-S, Lunala, Kyogre, and Rayquaza. 28 Speed EVs allow Giratina-O to outpace Adamant Calyrex-I, while 12 Attack EVs ensure the OHKO on Calyrex-S with Shadow Sneak after Stealth Rock. The remaining Defense investment helps Giratina-O handle foes like Groudon, Necrozma-DM, Zamazenta-C, and Ho-Oh.

Pairing Giratina-O with another Ghost-type is valuable to exploit the tier's lack of switch-ins to Ghost-types. Calyrex-S and Marshadow greatly benefit from Giratina-O crippling Dark-types like Yveltal, Zarude, and Tyranitar with Will-O-Wisp or weakening them with Draco Meteor, allowing both Ghost-types to overwhelm them. Calyrex-S can further cripple these Dark-types with Trick + a Choice item, while Marshadow can take advantage of them with Bulk Up; both Ghost-types also help Giratina-O by KOing Blissey. Due to Giratina-O lacking recovery, having defensive switch-ins is valuable for it; Necrozma-DM offers a Fairy-resistant partner and utility with Knock Off, Stealth Rock, and Thunder Wave, while Yveltal resists Ghost and Dark while offering Defog and U-turn support. Clerics such as Calyrex-S, Blissey, and Xerneas help Giratina-O, with Blissey also offering Wish and an answer to special attackers like Xerneas, Kyogre, and Eternatus, and Xerneas providing a Dragon immunity.

Physical Attacker.description:
This set focuses on Giratina's great Attack stat to beat common threats such as Necrozma-DM and Kyogre. Griseous Orb-boosted Poltergeist deals great damage to any non-Ghost-resistant foe. Stone Edge safely 2HKOes even bulky Yveltal as well as Ho-Oh. 76 Speed EVs allow Giratina-O to outspeed uninvested Yveltal and force mindgames with Stone Edge, while 176 HP EVs let it survive Choice Specs Ice Beam from Kyogre after Stealth Rock.

Physical Giratina-O has a better chance to break through Yveltal and doesn't have to rely on Stealth Rock damage to OHKO Calyrex-S. However, it has difficulty beating physical walls like Zygarde, Bulk Up Groudon, Zarude, and Buzzwole due to its inability to boost its Attack. Special wallbreakers like Kyogre and Xerneas are good teammates for Giratina-O, with Xerneas also offering Aromatherapy to prevent status from severely hindering it. Kyogre especially appreciates Defog to keep Water Spout at maximum power. Being able to lure in Yveltal thanks to Stone Edge helps teammates such as Calyrex-S and offensive Lunala, which have trouble breaking through it.

1v1.comments:
Other Options

Skill Swap: Rest can be run instead of Moonlight, but this is generally not recommended, as Cresselia oftentimes enjoys the immediate 50% recovery from Moonlight. However, Rest allows Cresselia to defeat Pokemon that use Toxic such as Pressure stall Entei. Reflect can be used instead of Skill Swap to deal with certain physical attackers, but this is more common on a Kee Berry set.

Icy Wind: Psyshock can be used instead of Stored Power, but this is generally not preferable, as it sacrifices reliability in the Tapu Fini matchup despite helping versus Acid Spray + Meteor Beam Nihilego, where using Calm Mind into Psyshock generally KOs Nihilego while avoiding a KO by Nihilego. Rest can also be used over Moonlight to help versus certain Toxic users like Pressure Entei and Chansey, but this sacrifices reliability in matchups versus Pokemon such as Choice Band Zeraora, so it is generally not advised.

Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf Cresselia can run maximum Speed EVs with a Timid Nature, which allows Cresselia to defeat Pheromosa without running the risk of losing to Skitter Smack variants as well and improves the Sawk matchup. However, this is generally not advised, as it requires Cresselia to lose some bulk as well as run more Speed, which is generally inadvisable when Cresselia enters Struggle wars versus opposing Choice Scarf Trick + Rest users, as being slower allows for the slower Struggle.

Defensive Kee Berry: Cresselia can run a fast Kee Berry set that sacrifices reliability against physical attackers such as Galarian Darmanitan but gains a better matchup against common stall answers such as Taunt Tapu Fini. This allows Cresselia to outspeed Taunt, giving it the opportunity to boost with Calm Mind and eventually overpower Tapu Fini. Additionally, a Rocky Helmet set with Psychic is an option for Cresselia to punish physical attackers, most notably Power-Up Punch Metagross and Taunt Zeraora, allowing Cresselia to flip these matchups while retaining many other physical attackers and reducing chances to get critical hit.

Skill Swap.description:
Set Description

Leftovers combined with Calm Mind allows Cresselia to defeat Icy Wind + Encore Primarina sets. Moonlight provides reliable recovery allowing Cresselia to defeat Choice Band Zeraora and non-Swords Dance Landorus-T. Stored Power allows Cresselia to break through opposing Calm Mind Pokemon such as Primarina; or power through resists such as non-Swords Dance Ferrothorn and some Celesteela. Psyshock can be used to still help break through opposing Calm Mind users as well as defeating Nihilego at the expense of being worse into Psychic-resistant foes. Skill Swap allows Cresselia to defeat Aroma Veil Aromatisse and be better against Regidrago as well as defeating some Unaware Pokemon if running Psyshock such as Clefable and Quagsire but notably not Pyukumuku. Substitute allows Cresselia to improve odds of not getting KOed by a critical hit while using Calm Mind as well as beating Goodra and improving the matchup against Yawn Sylveon.

EVs

The Special Defense investments allows Cresselia to take a 252+ Primarina Moonblast into Torrent Hydro Cannon. The Speed EVs let its outspeed base-60 foes such as Primarina, Sylveon, and Magnezone. The rest is put into Defense to take hits from Pokemon such as Zeraora, Landorus-T, and Haxorus.

Usage Tips

Most matchups are straightforward: use Calm Mind until Stored Power is strong enough such that using Calm Mind again has less of a return on investment. For example, if Stored Power can 3HKO at +3 and 2HKO at +4, and Cresselia does not need the Special Defense boost, it is preferable to start attacking earlier. That way, it gets more chances to critical hit, potentially turning Stored Power into a 2HKO. Otherwise, use Moonlight whenever Cresselia is low on HP, and be wary of Moonlight's measly eight PP. If possible, attempt to keep Cresselia's HP high enough such that even a critical hit will not KO Cresselia. Finally, Skill Swap is generally used for Aromatisse, taking Aromatisse's Aroma Veil so that Aromatisse can neither use Encore nor Disable on Cresselia. It can also be used versus some Regidrago sets where Cresselia should use Skill Swap on turn one. This reduces the damage of special attacks the same amount as Calm Mind would, with the added benefit of also weakening the damage of Regidrago's physical attacks. Against Unaware Pokemon such as Clefable and Quagsire, Cresselia will need to use Skill Swap if not running Stored Power while avoiding being Encored into Skill Swap so Cresselia can OHKO with a Calm Mind-boosted Psyshock. Cresselia should be unpredictable with using Skill Swap while using Calm Mind to boost and Moonlight to stay healthy. Be aware that Pyukumuku is generally favored as an Unaware user due to being able to use the combination of Taunt, Mirror Coat, and Recover to prevent Cresselia from boosting fast enough without being taken out by Mirror Coat. Finally, versus Landorus-T, Cresselia should use Moonlight on turn one and then use Skill Swap to improve the matchup against Choice Band Knock Off Landorus-T.

Icy Wind.description:
Set Description

Leftovers paired with Calm Mind and Icy Wind gives Cresselia a good matchup against most sets of the Water / Fairy types: Primarina, Tapu Fini, and Azumarill. Moonlight allows Cresselia to set up safely in front of many Pokemon that do not outdamage Leftovers + Moonlight recovery such as Kyurem and Choice Specs Naganadel. Stored Power allows for Cresselia to defeat some opposing Calm Mind users, including the aforementioned Tapu Fini and Primarina as well as breaking through resistant foes such as Steelix and non-Metal Sound Magnezone. Icy Wind flips many matchups, most notably versus Taunt users such as Tapu Fini, Tapu Koko, and Tapu Bulu as well as Swords Dance variants of Garchomp and Landorus-T.

EVs

The Special Defense EVs are to take a maximum Special Attack Modest Choice Specs Volcanion Steam Eruption into +1 Steam Eruption, assuming burn. The Speed EVs are to outspeed Garchomp after an Icy Wind, while the rest of the EVs are put into Defense to have the best odds to take attacks from Garchomp, Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan, and Tapu Bulu.

Usage Tips

Cresselia should use Calm Mind versus Tapu Fini; Icy Wind should only be used if Tapu Fini Taunts Cresselia. Since Cresselia loses to Trick Tapu Fini regardless of the move used, using Calm Mind turn one is optimal. Icy Wind should be used turn one versus Garchomp and Landorus-T, as this allows Cresselia to use Moonlight in the face of potentially getting 2HKOed by Choice Band Outrage from Garchomp and provides Cresselia better rolls to 2HKO Swords Dance + Knock Off variants of Landorus-T. Cresselia generally outspeeds most Tapu Bulu variants, so using Calm Mind turn one is generally safe, and subsequently alternating between Icy Wind and Stored Power after getting Taunted to avoid potentially losing a turn to Disable. It is worth noting that Tapu Bulu can win if it uses Taunt on turn one but this risks losing to Trick Cresselia, thus turning the matchup into a fifty-fifty. Finally, Calm Mind should be used against Tapu Koko and, Icy Wind should only be used after getting Taunted.

Scarf.description:
Set Description

Choice Scarf in combination with Trick allows for Cresselia to force passive Pokemon to use weak attacks or status moves while it heals with Rest. This allows Cresselia to defeat stall Cresselia, Tapu Koko, and Pressure stall Entei. Psychic defeats Urshifu-R, while Psyshock is better against Nihilego; both attacks help against Sawk. Ice Beam gives Cresselia a favorable matchup against Garchomp as well as most Landorus-T sets. Moonblast is an option to defeat no-bulk Urshifu-S, while Calm Mind provides a better matchup against Sylveon, especially when combined with Moonlight. Moonlight gives Cresselia more reliable recovery at the expense of being weaker against status moves and having less PP. This helps against certain Spectrier sets but gives up matchups against some stall foes like Chansey.

EVs

64 Special Attack EVs are used to 2HKO 4 SpD EVs Haxorus. 232 Speed EVs allow Cresselia to outspeed Tapu Koko. 196 HP with 16 Def EVs combined with a Bold Nature allows Cresselia to take 2 Adamant Haxorus Outrages while maximizing its HP. If running Moonblast instead of Ice Beam, Cresselia should run 44 Special Attack EVs to still 2HKO Haxorus while OHKOing 4 SpD Urshifu-S, 232 Speed EVs to outspeed Tapu Koko, and 232 HP EVs to still take 2 Adamant Haxorus Outrages.

Usage Tips

Cresselia should generally use Trick to lock the opponent into a move, which, due to Cresselia's bulk combined with recovery from Rest or Moonlight, allows for Cresselia to stall out many attacks. However, Cresselia should be wary of using Trick against opposing Choice item Pokemon; instead, Cresselia should use an attack if it can KO the foe first, such as versus Naganadel and Urshifu-R. Additionally, versus weaker Choice Scarf + Trick Pokemon such as Tapu Fini, Cresselia should use Trick first as if Scarf Tapu Fini uses an attack Cresselia can stall by using Rest, and if both use Trick, then this will reset the position. This should be repeated until Trick is out of PP; then, Rest should be used to win the resulting Struggle battle.

Defensive Kee.description:
Set Description

Kee Berry, maximum Defense EVs, and Reflect allows Cresselia to defeat most physical attackers, most notably Choice Band Galarian Darmanitan. Reflect also helps against Choice Band Haxorus Outrage, as its Unnerve ability means that Cresselia's Kee Berry does not get consumed. Calm Mind + Stored Power allows for Cresselia to break through Psychic-resistant foes such as Celesteela and Ferrothorn. Moonlight provides reliable recovery, allowing Cresselia to remain healthy while boosting up. Psyshock is an option to defeat Nihilego, but this loses reliability versus the aforementioned Steel-types. Skill Swap can be used to defeat Aromatisse as well as some Sylveon and Regidrago at the cost of reliability against many physical attackers.

EVs

Maximum Defense EVs with a Bold Nature is used to provide Cresselia the best odds to defeat Choice Band Galarian Darmanitan.

Usage Tips

Defensive Kee Berry Cresselia is straightforward to use. Versus physical attackers, Cresselia should generally use Reflect, followed up by boosting with Calm Mind and healing with Moonlight whenever low, and finally KOing with Stored Power. Versus special attackers, Cresselia should forgo using Reflect and instead start setting up immediately with Calm Mind. When facing Ferrothorn in particular, Cresselia should use Calm Mind first instead of Reflect, as Cresselia is not immediately threatened by Ferrothorn's attacks and should only use Reflect when Ferrothorn uses Swords Dance to minimize wasted Reflect turns. Finally, it is important to be aware that this Cresselia set in particular provides many opportunities for foes to critical hit through Cresselia's boosts or get powerful secondary effects, so one should be wary of this. This set is particularly vulnerable to Taunt Pokemon such as Tapu Fini and Tapu Koko due to the lack of Icy Wind, resulting in Cresselia's inability to outspeed the Taunt users and being forced to use a weak 20-Base Power Stored Power.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a newly introduced Pokemon. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B+ Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Calm Mind.description:
• Cresselia is the bulkiest option avaliable for a Calm Mind user.

  • Stored Power takes time to gain power, but after 2 Calm Minds, it becomes Cresselia's most powerful STAB attack. Psyshock can be used to defeat Tapu Fini in Calm Mind wars if they lack Taunt, win against Raikou, and deal massive damage to Nihilego.

  • Ice Beam hits a lot of high value targets hard, such as Landorus-T, Salamence, and Garchomp. Moonblast still does good damage to Dragon-types, and makes Cresselia less vulnerable to Dark-types like Urshifu-S.

  • Substitute allows Cresselia to set up in the face of status users such as Celesteela, Swampert, and Hippowdon that lack Whirlwind. However, this makes Cresselia completely useless against Dark-types, so don't choose it in team preview if they are seen.

Items

  • Kee Berry's Defense boost helps Cresselia against powerful Dynamaxing threats such as Cinderace and Landorus-T, all while giving another 20 BP boost to Stored Power.

  • Sitrus Berry gives Cresselia a short burst of extra health, making it more difficult to break past in the short term.

  • Leftovers gives more long-term recovery, which is helpful in slower-paced matches.

  • Rocky Helmet is useful for punishing Pokemon that commoningly use physical contact moves, such as Cinderace and Urshifu-R.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Bold / 4 Spe Bold: This spread maximizes Cresselia's physical bulk.

  • 252 HP / 100 Def / 156 Spe Bold: This spread is suggested for Substitute Cresselia. It outspeeds up to Timid Celesteela, allowing Cresselia to set up Substitute before Celesteela hits with Leech Seed.

Trick Room Support.description:
• Cresselia is an extremely bulky option for Trick Room, and with Lunar Dance, it's the only viable one that can give Trick Room sweepers another chance at sweeping.

  • Psychic is a reliable STAB option if Cresselia needs to do some damage, but Ice Beam hits a wide variety of targets harder such as Landorus-T, Salamence, and Garchomp.

  • Even though this Cresselia often sacrifces itself with Lunar Dance, Moonlight is still good to have to potentially wall certain Pokemon.

  • When using this Cresselia, always pair it with 1-2 slow Pokemon that can take advantage of Trick Room. Glastrier is by far the most dangerous Trick Room sweeper, so it comes highly recommended. Other options for slow Pokemon include Celesteela, Heatran, Magnezone, and Ferrothorn.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry gives Cresselia a quick burst of recovery. This is more valuable than Leftovers, since Cresselia often sacrifices itself anyways.

  • Rocky Helmet is still good for punishing contact moves from common foes such as Cinderace and Urshifu-R.

camomons.comments:
Other Options

Cresselia can pass on a more useful defensive typing by running Stored Power to capitalize on Calm Mind boosts. However, this set is very slow and opens Cresselia up to crippling status moves like Toxic. Cresselia can also forego Calm Mind and use Trick instead to cripple opposing defensive Pokemon with its Black Sludge and provide counterplay to opposing Trick users. However, this is inconsistent, since many defensive threats hold Black Sludge as well, and an incorrect timing of the move could result in Cresselia holding undesirable items like a Choice Scarf. Cresselia's great bulk and access to recovery also make it a reliable Trick Room setter to support slower offensive teammates like Glastrier and Melmetal.

Checks and Counters

Mold Breaker Ground-types and Thousand Arrows: Earthquake Haxorus and Excadrill are big threats to Cresselia, as their ability Mold Breaker allows them to hit with a super effective STAB move. Thousand Arrows from Zygarde-10% also bypasses Levitate. However, none of these threats are able to OHKO Cresselia without boosting to at least +2 Attack.

Steel-types: Cresselia is walled and forced out by offensive and defensive Steel-types like Mew, Hydreigon, Garchomp, and Melmetal. They are immune to Toxic, resist Cresselia's main STAB move, and can punish it with their Steel-type STAB attacks.

Psychic-types: Psychic-type attackers like Tapu Lele and Psychic Volcarona threaten out Cresselia's Toxic set and can hit other sets for strong neutral damage.

Clefable: Cresselia is forced out by all versions of Clefable. Dark / Poison Unaware Clefable ignores Calm Mind boosts and can't be poisoned, while offensive Magic Guard Clefable can set up with Calm Mind and quickly use up Cresselia's Moonlight PP.

Physical Wall.description:
Cresselia's impressive bulk and useful ability in Levitate along with access to reliable recovery, status, and setup moves make it a defensive behemoth that is difficult to wear down and break through. Its Poison typing from Toxic pairs nicely with Levitate, making it immune to both the poison status and Ground-type attacks while leaving it with only two weaknesses. Toxic puts offensive threats like Fire / Grass Volcarona and Hydreigon on a timer to prevent them from using setup moves effectively. Moonblast is a spammable attack that grants Cresselia a Fairy typing, which gives it an immunity and stacks useful resistances with its Poison typing. Moonlight is Cresselia's reliable recovery and keeps it healthy. Calm Mind keeps Cresselia from being overly passive and allows it to set up on other passive Pokemon like Blissey and Slowbro, or boost alongside opposing Calm Mind users like Electric / Dragon Latios, wearing all the aforementioned Pokemon down with Toxic as it sets up. Thunder Wave is another option that punishes offensive threats that Toxic can't, like Poison-type Garchomp, Latias, and Naganadel. It provides a great defensive typing with only one weakness thanks to Levitate and useful resistances to Flying- and Electric-type attacks that Toxic variants take neutral damage from. Shadow Ball gives Cresselia another unique typing with multiple immunities, mainly to high-powered Normal-type attacks like Extreme Speed, Facade, and Boomburst. It also allows Cresselia to have more coverage when it sets up with Calm Mind, but it makes Cresselia vulnerable to Ghost-type STAB moves like Shadow Claw and Shadow Ball, which are commonly seen on Facade and Boomburst users like Heracross and Noivern. Black Sludge is the item of choice for Poison-type Cresselia, as it increases Cresselia's longevity and punishes Trick users, while other Cresselia sets opt for Leftovers. A Bold nature with full investment in HP and Defense allows Cresselia to take on numerous physical attackers like Landorus-T, Lycanroc-D without Iron Head, and most unboosted Extreme Speed users outside of Zygarde-10% with Thousand Arrows.

While Cresselia is bulky, it is still vulnerable to high-powered neutral attacks like Guts-boosted Facade from Heracross and Triple Axel from Choice Band Pheromosa. Each of these attacks can 2HKO Cresselia with prior damage, so it is important to pair Cresselia with teammates that can stomach these hits like defensive Water / Poison Slowbro and Normal-resistant Pokemon such as Steel-type Buzzwole. These teammates also help cover Cresselia's few remaining weaknesses to types like Poison, Psychic, or Steel, depending on Cresselia's typing. Magnezone can pair with Cresselia to trap and eliminate Steel-types like Buzzwole and Scizor. While Cresselia can use Calm Mind to combat certain opposing setup threats, others like Psychic Volcarona and Taunt Spectrier can quickly overwhelm it. Defensive Dark / Poison Pokemon such as Unaware Clefable and Toxapex make great partners for Cresselia to handle the setup threats that can break past it.

2v2doubles.comments:
Other Options

Cresselia can hold Colbur Berry or Tanga Berry to reduce damage taken from Pokemon such as Incineroar, Pheromosa, and Genesect, but Sitrus Berry's instant healing is better in most matchups. Mental Herb can be used to bypass Pokemon that try to Taunt or Encore Cresselia such as Sableye and Victini.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Cresselia is unable to damage Steel-types. Genesect can 2HKO it, and Celesteela can easily stall it with Leech Seed. Metagross and Heatran do much more damage to Cresselia then it can do back. Metagross is also unaffected by Cresselia's Calm Mind.

Dark-types: Incineroar and Tyranitar take very little or no damage from Cresselia's attacks and can threaten back with powerful Dark-type moves.

Taunt and Encore: Cresselia can be Taunted by Victini and Galarian Zapdos, preventing Calm Mind or Moonlight, while Sableye can use Encore against Cresselia. Both scenarios limit the longevity of Cresselia and make it considerably less useful in a battle. Mental Herb can help patch this weakness, though.

Calm Mind.description:
Cresselia is a great defensive sweeper thanks to its tremendous bulk and solid defensive typing, which allow it to easily set up Calm Mind. Psyshock lets Cresselia threaten Pheromosa, Nihilego, Naganadel, and Galarian Zapdos. Moonlight provides Cresselia with recovery, allowing it to outlast foes such as Indeedee, Volcanion, and Tapu Lele. Ice Beam hits Zygarde, Landorus, Rillaboom, and Landorus-T. Icy Wind is a weaker alternative that provides speed control. Trick Room allows Cresselia and its teammates to move before faster foes. Helping Hand allows damaging partners like Diancie and Volcanion to OHKO Galarian Moltres and Assault Vest Rillaboom. Protect is an effective answer to Fake Out, allowing Cresselia to safely set Trick Room on turn 2. The Special Defense EVs ensure Cresselia survives a +1 Bug Buzz from Life Orb Genesect, while the Defense investment allows it to deal with physical attackers like Rillaboom better. Using a Calm nature is optimal for sets without Trick Room, while sets opting for Trick Room should use a Sassy nature to ensure Cresselia is as slow as possible.

Cresselia is found on slow, bulky teams that appreciate Trick Room's or Icy Wind's speed control and Cresselia's ability to outlast foes. Fire-types such as Incineroar, Heatran, and Volcanion are great partners, since they deal with the Steel-types that Cresselia struggles against such as Genesect and Metagross. Volcanion in particular also defeats Incineroar. In return, Cresselia can deal with Landorus, Landorus-T, and Zygarde with Ice Beam or Icy Wind. Rock-types such as Diancie and Rhyperior also make fantastic partners, as they can defeat Incineroar and Galarian Moltres. In return, Cresselia can threaten Zygarde, Landorus, and Landorus-T with Ice Beam.

Choice Scarf.description:
Zacian is a good revenge killer in AG due to its good Speed and Attack stat, which are further boosted by Choice Scarf and its ability Intrepid Sword. Its good bulk allows it to revenge kill Yveltal and deal with Dragon Dance Zygarde-C. Play Rough allows Zacian to OHKO many prominent Pokemon such as Yveltal, Zekrom, and Marshadow, while Close Combat hits Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Ferrothorn. Crunch allows Zacian to dispatch weakened Necrozma-DM while also ensuring that it can revenge kill a healthy Calyrex-S and is not completely walled by Lunala. Wild Charge heavily damages Ho-Oh, which otherwise walls Zacian very well and threatens to burn it with Sacred Fire. Wild Charge also gives Zacian a functional super effective option for Kyogre. Solar Blade takes advantage of Drought and heavily damages Groudon while also OHKOing Quagsire, which otherwise walls Zacian easily. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature and Choice Scarf allows Zacian to outspeed almost the entire metagame, even Pokemon such as Zekrom and Groudon at +2 Speed, making it easy to revenge kill foes.

Zacian best fits as a revenge killer on bulky offense and balance teams. Pokemon such as Zygarde-C, Ferrothorn, and Eternatus provide great support by switching into its counters in Necrozma-DM and Quagsire and forcing them out. Ferrothorn can set Spikes, allowing Zacian to KO chipped foes, while also checking Kyogre and Xerneas. Groudon provides sun for Solar Blade variants of Zacian. In return, Zacian can deal heavy damage to Pokemon such as Xerneas, Zekrom, and Kyogre that threaten these teammates. Necrozma-DM can switch into Zacian-C, which can OHKO Zacian, and chip it down so Zacian can revenge kill it with Close Combat or Crunch. In return, Zacian pressures Yveltal and Zygarde-C, forcing them to switch out. However, it must be wary of Knock Off and Glare while switching in. On balance teams, Gothitelle can trap Necrozma-DM and Quagsire, allowing Zacian to put huge dents in the opponent's team.

Choice Band.description:
These are sample sets while we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

Other Options

Fire Fang can be used with Groudon to 2HKO a chipped Necrozma-DM, but locking into it puts Zacian at a disadvantage against Pokemon such as Zygarde-C, Zekrom, and Eternatus.

Checks and Counters

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM is the most reliable check for Zacian, since it can take whatever Zacian can dish out while being able to recover health. It can also heavily damage Zacian using Sunsteel Strike in return. Rocky Helmet variants can chip Zacian, allowing priority users such as Marshadow to revenge kill it, and make Zacian's moves less spammable.

Quagsire: Quagsire is a good check to Zacian due to its typing and Unaware ignoring Intrepid Sword's boost. Quagsire can also cripple it using Toxic or Scald. However, it must beware Solar Blade variants, since they can easily OHKO it.

Eternatus: Eternatus's great bulk allows it to soft check Zacian by switching into its moves and stalling it out while consistently recovering its health. Eternatus can also threaten Zacian with Sludge Bomb. However, a specially defensive Eternatus needs to be at full health to switch into Play Rough.

vgc2022.overview: Zacian-C is arguably VGC 2022's best Restricted Pokemon due to its high Speed, allowing it to outpace the entire metagame outside of Calyrex-S and Regieleki, its sky-high offensive presence, and Behemoth Blade, which allows it to check or outright OHKO many of the metagame's top Dynamax options such as Venusaur and Calyrex-I. Its Speed and immediate power make Zacian-C great at cleaning up weakened teams and pair well offensively with other Restricted Pokemon such as Palkia, Kyogre, Groudon, and Calyrex-S. Zacian-C does struggle against some of the format's common threats such as Groudon, Kyogre, and, most importantly, Incineroar; however, it often takes fairly minimal support for Zacian-C's few checks to be handled. For example, Defiant Thundurus checks Kyogre and benefits from Landorus-T's and Incineroar's Intimidate. Groudon and Kyogre are good restricted partners for Zacian-C, as the former checks Incineroar, Thundurus, and Regieleki and offers additional support against Kyogre with Drought, while the latter checks common Zacian-C answers like Incineroar and Landorus-T.
vgc2022.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance allows Zacian-C to offset Intimidate from the likes of Incineroar and Landorus-T and pose a more immediate sweeping threat. However, this leaves Zacian-C more vulnerable to status, more easily pinned down by Fake Out, and gives up its ability to waste Dynamax turns with Substitute. Imprison with a Jolly nature and max Speed allows Zacian-C to potentially outspeed and disable opposing Zacian-C; however, because of the variance of Zacian-C's attacking moves and the possibility of losing a speed tie to opposing Zacian-C, Imprison is inconsistent at shutting down opposing Zacian-C completely and comes with the significant opportunity cost of dropping Substitute or a third attack. Close Combat can be used for a stronger Fighting-type option, but lowers Zacian-C's defenses and doesn't ignore stat changes on opposing Pokemon.

Offensive.description:
• Play Rough allows Zacian-C to slam Palkia hard, 2HKO Kyogre after Intimidate, and 2HKO Seismitoad, Support Thundurus, and Gastrodon.

  • Sacred Sword gives Zacian-C a way to hit Incineroar super effectively and ignore defense boosts from Max Steelspike or Ferrothorn's Iron Defense.

  • Substitute is great to take advantage of passive Pokemon like Amoonguss and Grimmsnarl by avoiding their status moves and to stall out Dynamax turns of slower Pokemon. Running three attacks with Fighting coverage over Substitute is viable; however, Substitute is generally more valuable.

  • Zacian-C can afford to invest in its bulk without compromising its sweeping capabilities too much, and it gains benefits such as living Modest Life Orb Venusaur's Max Quake and -1 Life Orb Calyrex-I's Max Quake. Moreover, bulk investment is especially good alongside common damage mitigation tactics such as dual screens Grimmsnarl and Intimidate Incineroar. 236 HP investment gives Zacian-C an optimal number for Substitute. This being said, Zacian-C's EV spread is extremely flexible, as it can also viably run maximum Speed and Attack investment with a Jolly nature, especially on hyper offense teams where its bulk is less valuable.

Zacian-C is the the best Restricted Pokemon in Series 11 due to its sky-high Attack stat, great Speed, and great defensive typing. Behemoth Blade is an excellent STAB move that is able to punish Dynamax-reliant Pokemon like Venusaur and Thundurus. Sacred Sword and Close Combat maul threats that resist Behemoth Blade like Kyogre, Urshifu-S, and mainly Incineroar, which a Fairy-type STAB move wouldn't be as effective against. Sacred Sword is weaker, but its ability to get around Max Steelspike's boosts keeps it optimal, while Close Combat is an explosive attack that can OHKO physically defensive Incineroar at +1. Substitute protects Zacian-C from status conditions and Intimidate while punishing passive plays; meanwhile, Swords Dance allow Zacian-C to keep its offensive presence even after getting crippled by Intimidate and Max Wyrmwind. The Adamant nature optimizes the Attack gain from Intrepid Sword and Swords Dance, while the Speed EVs allow it to outspeed even Venusaur in sun while at +1. Its good bulk allows it to survive Venusaur's Max Quake and opposing Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, and with dual screens support it can even survive Landorus-T's Max Quake and Venusaur's Max Flare.

Grimmsnarl's dual screens and speed control in Scary Face allow Zacian-C to more safely pressure targets like opposing Zacian-C, Groudon, Venusaur, and Landorus-T. Thundurus can punish Intimidate from Incineroar while also boosting Zacian-C's Speed and Attack with its Max Airstream and Max Knuckle. Venusaur, Charizard, and Coalossal are all great early residual damage inflicters thanks to their G-Max Moves, which can put foes in range of Zacian-C's hits during the endgame. Landorus-T and Incineroar can stack Intimidate drops against threats like Groudon and opposing Landorus-T, protecting Zacian-C from physical attacks, while also being good Venusaur checks. Zacian-C also greatly appreciates Lapras's G-Max Resonance and its ability to OHKO Fire- and Ground-types like Landorus-T and Incineroar.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: These sets are for one of the final Battle Stadium Singles metagames for this generation. If you feel there is anything wrong or missing, please post in this thread.

All-out Attacker.description:
EV Spreads

  • 236 HP / 252 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 12 Spe with Adamant: This bulky EV spread maximizes Zacian-C's power, while still outspeeding Garchomp.

  • 236 HP / 180 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 84 Spe with Adamant: This spread outspeeds Timid Lugia at the cost of some power.

  • 236 HP / 92 Atk / 4 Def / 164 SpD / 12 Spe with Adamant:: This Specially Defensive spread survives Modest Life Orb Yveltal's Max Flare and Timid Choice Scarf Kyogre's Water Spout.

  • 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed allows Zacian-C to outspeed Eternatus and Marshadow, at the cost of having the bulk to effectively trade blows.

Swords Dance Sweeper.description:
EV Spreads

  • 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed lets Zacian-C defeat Marshadow with Stealth Rock support, outspeed Eternatus, and is the best bet against opposing Zacian-C after Swords Dance.

  • 236 HP / 180 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 84 Spe with Adamant: This spread sacrifices some power to survive Focus Sash Landorus-T's Earthquake, and still outspeed Timid Lugia.

Offensive.description:
Zacian-C is one of the top threats in Anything Goes, boasting an insanely high Attack stat, nearly unrivaled Speed, a brilliant typing and ability, and access to a plethora of coverage options that make it extremely difficult to handle offensively and defensively. Behemoth Blade is the preferred STAB move, since it's stronger and 100% accurate and deals more damage to Dynamaxed Pokemon than Play Rough. Wild Charge is essential coverage for targets like defensive Ho-Oh, Arceus-Water, and Primal Kyogre that resist Behemoth Blade. Close Combat destroys Ferrothorn and heavily dents Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon, two of Zacian-C's best switch-ins. Swords Dance allows Zacian-C to sweep once the opposition is weakened and revenge killers like Ditto have been eliminated, while also forcing the Dynamax from Necrozma-DM in order to beat it. Assurance along with Close Combat takes out Necrozma-DM on the switch after Stealth Rock damage. Crunch is an option over Assurance in order to still pressure Necrozma-DM when entry hazards are not present. Although Crunch hits said foe for the same damage as Close Combat, it has a chance of a Defense drop and doesn't lower Zacian-C's own defenses, which can be vital in preventing Necrozma-DM from reliably switching in to Zacian-C multiple times. It also targets defensive Lunala harder than Assurance and lets Zacian-C avoid a mind game with Ultra Necrozma. Substitute may be used to ease prediction against common counterplay to Zacian-C, and works particularly well due to Zacian-C's tendency to force a plethora of switches. Notably, it also shields Zacian-C from Ditto. Protect is useful for scouting Ditto and stalling out foes' Dynamax turns. Play Rough can be used in the fourth moveslot to break through defensive Zygarde-C, which checks Zacian-C otherwise. A Jolly nature is preferred with Swords Dance, as it can be used to Speed tie with opposing Zacian-C and outspeed Mega Mewtwo Y and +1 Necrozma-DM. Otherwise, an Adamant nature is preferred for the extra damage output, which notably allows Zacian-C to 2HKO defensive Arceus-Ground after little to no prior chip damage, and to put more pressure on Necrozma-DM.

Ho-Oh is one of the best teammates for Zacian-C, as it checks Arceus-Ground and can scout Ditto fairly reliably. A good check to Primal Groudon like Arceus-Water, Arceus-Ground, defensive Zygarde-C, or Mega Rayquaza is appreciated, as it's one of the few Pokemon that can switch into Zacian-C and force it out. Wallbreakers like Primal Kyogre, Geomancy Xerneas, Mega Rayquaza, and Yveltal can help to break down checks like Necrozma-DM, Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and Ho-Oh, allowing Zacian-C to clean up late-game. Ferrothorn can switch into support Arceus formes and provide Spikes support, helping Zacian-C to pick up on more KOs. Ditto is Zacian-C's greatest nemesis, so setup sweepers that beat it like Yveltal, Arceus-Ghost, and Zygarde-C are appreciated, and cores that can pivot around a Ditto that has copied Zacian-C like Ho-Oh + Primal Groudon + Necrozma-DM are helpful.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Fire Fang can be used if Zacian-C is specifically paired with Groudon to 2HKO Necrozma-DM under sun. However, it is hard to justify using over another coverage move, especially because Assurance can already 2HKO Necrozma-DM on the switch if Stealth Rock or Spikes is up. If running Fire Fang, use Play Rough instead of Close Combat. Substitute is an option over Assurance to block Ditto from transforming into Zacian-C. However, replacing Assurance or Swords Dance means that Zacian-C has almost no way to deal with Necrozma-DM. Crunch is an option on Zacian-C to pressure Necrozma-DM without relying on Stealth Rock or Spikes. It is also more reliable than Close Combat at pressuring Necrozma-DM, as it doesn't lower Zacian-C's defenses. A specially defensive set with Rest and Sleep Talk is an option for bulky balance and stall teams that need counterplay to mixed Life Orb or Taunt Yveltal; even without investment, Zacian-C's damage output is impressive. Its lack of passivity serves to distinguish it from Tyranitar, the Pokemon that is more typically used to answer offensive Yveltal on such teams, but it is generally overshadowed by the latter as it checks fewer threats overall.

Checks and Counters

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM is by far the most reliable check to Zacian-C, being able to tank most of its attacks thanks to its great bulk and threaten it back with Sunsteel Strike or chip damage from Rocky Helmet. However, Necrozma-DM without Heavy-Duty Boots cannot reliably switch into Zacian-C if Stealth Rock or Spikes is on its side of the field, as it risks being crippled by Assurance, putting it into OHKO range for Close Combat. It also has to recover with Morning Sun if it switches in on Close Combat, which teams can take advantage of due to its very low PP. Non-Earthquake Necrozma-DM cannot handle Swords Dance Zacian-C without Dynamax.

Faster Revenge Killers: Faster revenge killers such as Calyrex-S, Choice Scarf Kyogre, and offensive Eternatus can outspeed and KO Zacian-C with their STAB or coverage moves, easily forcing it out.

Quagsire: Although Quagsire can only fit on stall teams, it's a very strong check to Zacian-C due to its resistance to Behemoth Blade, Unaware ignoring Intrepid Sword and Swords Dance boosts, and sufficient bulk. However, Quagsire struggles to switch in on Zacian-C's Close Combat or Play Rough if it is severely weakened.

Wallbreaker.description:
Zacian-C is a centralizing force in AG that threatens offense and balance alike with its Intrepid Sword-boosted Attack, excellent STAB combination, great coverage, and fantastic Speed. Its good bulk and typing allow it to deal with Xerneas, Eternatus, and Yveltal, offering valuable defensive utility. Behemoth Blade is preferred over Play Rough for preventing Pokemon such as Yveltal and Groudon from effectively using Dynamax defensively against Zacian-C while also reliably OHKOing Xerneas. Wild Charge OHKOes specially defensive Yveltal after minimal chip damage, deals with Ho-Oh, and devastates Kyogre. Close Combat provides good coverage for Ferrothorn and 2HKOes a weakened Necrozma-DM. Assurance deals great damage to Zacian-C's most reliable check in Necrozma-DM if it switches in while Stealth Rock or Spikes is on the field and prevents Lunala from reliably checking it. Zacian-C can alternatively run Swords Dance, boosting its already terrific Attack to break through physically defensive walls such as Zygarde-C, Giratina, and Necrozma-DM. However, this makes Zacian-C and its team more vulnerable to Ditto. Play Rough is also a decent pick, letting Zacian-C defeat Zygarde-C, Zekrom, and Giratina. An Adamant nature enhances Zacian-C's damage output while leaving it fast enough to outspeed much of the metagame. The given spread ensures that Zacian-C will survive +2 Max Lightning from Geomancy Xerneas after Stealth Rock, while also outspeeding Modest Eternatus. Some other spreads are possible as well: for example, a spread of 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with an Adamant nature can be used on offensive teams or balance teams with strong counterplay to Xerneas and Yveltal. If a team desires speed control, a Jolly nature with 112 Speed EVs can be used to outspeed Adamant Zacian-C and anything slower. Speed investment beyond this is generally not desirable and detracts from Zacian-C's good bulk.

Zacian-C is an excellent fit on bulky offense and balance teams due to its great wallbreaking potential, amazing Speed tier, bulk, and typing, which make it a decent check to Xerneas, Eternatus, and Yveltal. However, Zacian-C can be revenge killed by the likes of Calyrex-S, Choice Scarf Kyogre, and offensive Eternatus. Therefore, teammates that can deal with these threats such as Yveltal, Eternatus, and Calyrex-S, respectively, are appreciated. Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn can provide Stealth Rock or Spikes support for Zacian-C, invalidating Necrozma-DM as a switch-in to Assurance Zacian-C if it lacks Heavy-Duty Boots. Kyogre's Drizzle is useful for Zacian-C, as it restricts Necrozma-DM's ability to consistently heal with Morning Sun. Partners like Necrozma-DM and Ho-Oh should be used in order to check Ditto once it has copied Zacian-C. Offensive teammates such as Calyrex-S, Life Orb Yveltal, and Xerneas can pressure physically defensive checks to Zacian-C such as Necrozma-DM, Zygarde-C, and Giratina. Xerneas also forms a great offensive core with Zacian-C; Xerneas is able to stall out Dynamax turns from Necrozma-DM with Substitute and 2HKO it with Thunder at +2, leaving it weakened so Zacian-C can KO it. In return, Zacian-C can take care of Ferrothorn. Gothitelle is another noteworthy pick on balance teams, as Zacian-C can lure in Necrozma-DM so Gothitelle can trap it and PP stall it.

ubers.overview: When one first sees Zamazenta's well-rounded stats, it may look like an excellent Choice item user; however, Zamazenta is unfortunately hindered by a poor typing and an even worse movepool. Despite having several serviceable coverage moves, Zamazenta can't piece them together in any threatening combination. Therefore, it can't consistently break through defensive cores using common Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, and Zygarde-C. Zamazenta's STAB Close Combat also has low PP, which common physical walls such as Xerneas, Zygarde-C, Necrozma-DM, and Eternatus easily exploit. Despite Dauntless Shield and high stats, Zamazenta is paradoxically fragile and struggles to find defensive utility. Lacking reliable recovery or other support options, it cannot take repeated hits from common physical attackers such as Zekrom, Groudon, and Marshadow. Other Choice item users such as Dracovish, Calyrex-I, and Urshifu-S should be considered long before Zamazenta.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Zamazenta does not have any other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Physical Walls: Without proper coverage and prediction, Zamazenta fails to break through common walls like Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, and Zygarde-C. Note that these Pokemon can also cripple Zamazenta with a status move. Further, bulky setup sweepers such as Groudon and Buzzwole can use Zamazenta as setup fodder.

Pivots: Bulky Pokemon such as Toxapex and Ho-Oh can scout Zamazenta, as it fails to OHKO them. They can then heal off the damage they have taken with Regenerator or Recover and switch into another threat.

Status: Zamazenta hates status. Burn from Toxapex's Scald or Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire negates all damage it may do, paralysis from Zygarde-C's Glare or Ho-Oh's Thunder Wave ruins its great Speed, and poison from Eternatus's Toxic or Toxic Spikes greatly reduces its switch-in opportunities.

Eternatus: While it does not want to switch into a Psychic Fangs, Eternatus doesn't mind any of Zamazenta's other moves. Moreover, its Pressure quickly depletes Close Combat's PP. Dynamax Cannon, even from a defensive variant, can chunk Zamazenta. Eternatus can also poison Zamazenta with Toxic or Toxic Spikes, which puts it on a timer.

Xerneas: Xerneas's great bulk allows it to ignore any attacks coming from Zamazenta bar Iron Head. It can OHKO Zamazenta with its STAB Moonblast. Finally, Geomancy Xerneas can use Zamazenta as setup fodder.

Faster Pokemon: Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Kyogre can threaten Zamazenta with their STAB moves. However, they cannot switch into it.

Choice Band.description:
The idea behind this set is pretty straightforward: do as much damage as possible each time Zamazenta can get in. Crunch beats Ghost-types, including Lunala and Calyrex-S, and Psychic Fangs offers a solid answer to Poison-types like Eternatus and Toxapex. The last moveslot depends on what the team needs: Wild Charge is used for Ho-Oh, Iron Head hits Xerneas hard, and Ice Fang pressures Zygarde-C. With great base 138 Speed, Zamazenta is only outsped by Jolly Marshadow, Calyrex-S, offensive Eternatus, and the rare Regieleki and Pheromosa. With a Jolly nature, Zamazenta outspeeds all variants of Marshadow and Eternatus, but an Adamant nature allows it to break through defensive Necrozma-DM more consistently, as well as always 2HKOing physically defensive Eternatus and Xerneas after Stealth Rock damage. While it does have Dauntless Shield, Zamazenta remains fragile, and it should be brought in with a slow pivot or on a non-damaging move. Also, despite it resisting Dark, you should be wary of switching Zamazenta in on Yveltal, since Knock Off cripples it.

Because it struggles to break through physical walls, entry hazard support is invaluable for Zamazenta. Spikes is especially good, since premier physical walls such as Zygarde-C and Necrozma-DM resist Stealth Rock. Ferrothorn, Necrozma-DM, and Eternatus are all great hazard setters, being able to switch into threats that Zamazenta cannot handle like opposing Ferrothorn, Necrozma-DM and Choice Scarf Kyogre. Strong special attackers such as Kyogre, Calyrex-S, and Eternatus also help pressure Zygarde-C and Necrozma-DM. Eternatus, notably, can also spread poison to Zygarde-C. Finally, because it is very weak to status, clerics such as Blissey and Calyrex-S support Zamazenta well. The former is able to tank special hits that Zamazenta cannot handle, and the latter provides great specially offensive pressure.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options
