Sucker Punch is an option to pick off the likes of Jirachi and Azelf as well as other revenge killers like Lycanroc-D, but forgoing coverage or added utility isn't great for Nidoking. While you forgo the additional power from Life Orb, a Choice Scarf set is a solid revenge killer while still being an effective wallbreaker.

Checks and Counters

Chansey: Thanks to Chansey's tremendously high special bulk, it is able to switch into any of Nidoking's attacks and can proceed to whittle it down with Seismic Toss, set up Stealth Rock, or recover its HP with Soft-Boiled.

Water-types: Keldeo and Rotom-W outspeed and threaten Nidoking. Crawdaunt and Azumarill can both effectively revenge kill Nidoking thanks to Aqua Jet. Slowking can tank a Thunderbolt and deal heavy damage with Scald or pivot out into a revenge killer.

Ground-types: Pokemon like Diggersby, Excadrill, and Zygarde-10% can comfortably revenge kill Nidoking. Swampert and Hippowdon can switch into most attacks, but must be wary of switching into Earth Power as it can 2HKO. Gastrodon can switch in relatively easily and threaten it.

Psychic-types and Psychic-type Coverage: Psychic-types such as Necrozma, Azelf, and Starmie can hit Nidoking super effectively with their STAB moves. Psychic-type Coverage like Psychic on Thundurus-T and Psychic Fangs on Lycanroc-D keep Nidoking from switching into them.

Wallbreaker.description:
Sludge Wave is Nidoking's strongest STAB move, hitting Pokemon like Hatterene, Tangrowth, and Primarina super effectively, as well as discouraging Rotom-W and Rotom-H from switching in freely. Earth Power slams Steel- and Poison-types such as Jirachi, Cobalion, and Nihilego. Fire Blast roasts Celesteela, Skarmory, and Scizor. It also OHKOes Amoonguss after Stealth Rock. Thunderbolt allows Nidoking to nail Water- and Flying-types like Slowking, Gyarados, and Mandibuzz. Alternatively, Substitute makes Nidoking much less prediction reliant, giving it free turns against foes that it forces out like Nihilego and Tangrowth. Ice Beam heavily pressures Hippowdon and OHKOes Salamence and Noivern, but these Pokemon get pressured by Nidoking's STAB attacks anyway. A Modest nature should be run to increase Nidoking's damage output against threats like Slowking and Mandibuzz, since it doesn't miss out on any notable Speed benchmarks. Life Orb and Sheer Force pair together to negate the health loss of Life Orb while giving an effective 70% power boost, which is a big factor behind Nidoking's power.

Nidoking fits best on offensive teams that are able to bring it in many times to wallbreak and tear through defensive Pokemon like Amoonguss and Skarmory. As a result, pivots such as Rotom-W, Zarude, and Moltres make for good partners. Zarude forces out Swampert and Hippowdon while Rotom-W lures in Tangrowth for Nidoking and OHKOes Krookodile. Chansey is also a great partner for Nidoking, providing pivot support while beating its common checks like Rotom-W and Hydreigon. Switch-ins to Psychic-, Ground-, and Water-type attacks like Jirachi, Tangrowth, and Amoonguss can be paired with Nidoking on bulkier teams. Jirachi also provides entry hazard support, allowing Nidoking to reliably KO Celesteela, and Healing Wish support to let it wallbreak even more. Tangrowth and Amoonguss are also able to handle Electric-types in the tier much better than Nidoking and can pivot into the likes of Zygarde-10% and Keldeo excellently. Late-game cleaners like Scizor and Cobalion are great teammates to break through Chansey, which Nidoking struggles against. Sticky Web support from Ribombee offsets Nidoking's average Speed tier, allowing it to outspeed and OHKO threats like Tentacruel, Excadrill, and Lycanroc-D.

ou.overview: Nidoking is equipped with an incredible STAB combination that is amplified by its ability Sheer Force and a Life Orb, allowing it to operate as a powerful special wallbreaker despite its mediocre base Special Attack. In addition, it boasts phenomenal coverage options such as Ice Beam, Flamethrower, and Thunderbolt that allow it to reliably pressure switch-ins to its STAB attacks such as Corviknight, Ferrothorn, Slowking, and Landorus-T. Nidoking's defensive typing is solid as well, letting it take advantage of Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Clefable for wallbreaking opportunities as well as providing it with a handy Toxic and Thunder Wave immunity. However, its bulk and Speed tier leave much to be desired. It is very prone to being revenge killed by faster threats like offensive Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Tapu Lele and struggles to find natural wallbreaking opportunities due to its frailty, relying on pivoting allies that can switch it in safely. Despite its good defensive typing, Nidoking's fragility also makes it difficult to utilize consistently, especially if it sustains prior chip damage. On top of this, Nidoking is reliant on its item to do damage due to its mediocre Special Attack, making it susceptible to Knock Off. This can be particularly troublesome against Clefable, which Nidoking can otherwise take advantage of. Special walls such as Blissey and Slowking are problematic as well, having no qualms switching into most of its attacks and gaining momentum on its escape with Teleport.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Taunt allows Nidoking to exploit its small subset of switch-ins by incapacitating most forms of progress, such as Teleport and entry hazard removal, or hazard setup. Taunt mainly punishes Blissey, greatly limiting its utility and providing the Nidoking user with an opportunity to capitalize on it. However, Taunt is a move that needs to be used aggressively to get value, which can conflict with Nidoking's role as a wallbreaker. Alternatively, Focus Punch can be used for the luring and dispatching of Blissey, putting it in range of a subsequent STAB move. This can open Nidoking for more wallbreaking opportunities against teams that are overreliant on Blissey as their special backbone; however, Focus Punch is extremely matchup reliant and has little to no utility against other Pokemon. Lastly, Stealth Rock can be used on teams lacking a Stealth Rock setter, enabling Nidoking to set the hazard on forced switches. Though, using the move limits Nidoking's wallbreaking potential greatly.

Checks and Counters

Faster Pokemon: Nidoking is extremely susceptible to revenge killing from a wide range of offensive Pokemon like Landorus-T, Rillaboom, Dragapult, and Urshifu-R that can take advantage of its mediocre bulk and Speed tier to force it out and create progress with options such as Stealth Rock, Knock Off, and U-turn.

Ground-types: Landorus-T and Garchomp can scare out Nidoking with their greater Speed and super effective STAB attacks. Landorus-T, particularly, is not bothered by Nidoking's STAB attacks but can easily be overwhelmed by its coverage if utilized recklessly. Gastrodon and Swampert, additionally, are willing to take on Nidoking and scare it out with their respective STAB moves; the latter, however, can also be overwhelmed due to its lack of reliable recovery.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Blissey is a counter to most Nidoking variants that can reliably switch into any one of its special attacks, being only somewhat deterred by Taunt and the situational Focus Punch. Galarian Slowking, Slowking, and Tyranitar are also capable of taking its hits if healthy.

Item Removal: Nidoking is reliant on its Life Orb for its damage output; for this reason, Nidoking losing its Life Orb to Knock Off or Trick greatly mitigates the threat of its power. Additionally, given Knock Off's prevalence, Nidoking's susceptibility to the move allows Knock Off users to safely force progress using it against the Nidoking user's team.

Wallbreaker.description:
Flamethrower reliably OHKOes Ferrothorn and Scizor and can apply pressure to Corviknight. Ice Beam targets Landorus-T, Garchomp, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T. Thunderbolt is an alternative to threaten super effective damage on Slowking. Thunder applies much more pressure to Slowking and OHKOes Tornadus-T as they switch in at the cost of a lower accuracy; however, a Modest nature is necessary if Thunder is used to create a more favorable roll to KO Slowking with a subsequent Sludge Wave. Substitute is another option that lets Nidoking fully capitalize on a forced switch and safely force damage on a target of its choice without the threat of being knocked out beforehand, which greatly eases the need for prediction, but forces Nidoking to drop an additional coverage option. A Modest nature provides the Nidoking user with a more fruitful damage output and a much more favorable roll to 2HKO Slowking with Thunderbolt. However, Timid allows Nidoking to outspeed Tapu Bulu, Modest Tapu Lele, and Zapdos.

Nidoking's inability to find many natural wallbreaking opportunities makes it a phenomenal partner with offensive pivots such as Tapu Koko and Dragapult that can provide it with opportunities to switch in safely. The former is able to apply great pressure to checks like Corviknight and Slowking while pivoting against bulky Grass-types like Ferrothorn; its Electric Terrain, additionally, boosts Nidoking's Thunderbolt, which is prominent against Slowking. The latter pivots against bulky Fairy-types like Tapu Fini and Clefable while applying pressure to Slowking with its Ghost-type STAB attacks. Additionally, it is capable of utilizing Thunder Wave to slow down Pokemon such as Tornadus-T, turning them into wallbreaking fodder for Nidoking. Nidoking also pairs well with defensive pivots like Corviknight and Rotom-W, which give Nidoking a safe wallbreaking opportunity against Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Grass-types like Tangrowth. They, additionally, can give Nidoking a good escape option against potential revenge killers like Tapu Lele for Corviknight and Landorus-T in Rotom-W's case. Slowking can also find good pivoting opportunities against Tapu Koko and Tangrowth while giving Nidoking the ability to exploit Toxapex for a wallbreaking opportunity. In addition, entry hazards and Knock Off are valuable tools that can greatly aid Nidoking's wallbreaking abilities by forcing checks like Slowking and Landorus-T to fold to its coverage. Ferrothorn, for example, boasts access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Knock Off to remove Slowking's Heavy-Duty Boots and more effectively pressure it. Landorus-T is also capable of using Stealth Rock and Knock Off, as well as pivoting against opposing Tangrowth, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Fini with U-turn and providing Nidoking with a wallbreaking opportunity. Clefable is also a solid Stealth Rock setter that has access to Knock Off.

monotype.overview:
Ground

Nidoking is Ground's best special wallbreaker due to its various coverage moves boosted by Sheer Force and Life Orb, which let it break past physically defensive walls such as Skarmory, Amoonguss, and Ferrothorn that are otherwise difficult for the type to break through. Nidoking also helps against types like Fairy, Flying, Steel, and Grass, as they lack sturdy defensive switch-ins to it. Its part-Poison typing provides useful defensive utility by letting it switch in on Fairy-type attacks and remove Toxic Spikes. It is additionally the only way for Ground teams to set Toxic Spikes themselves. However, while Nidoking can pressure many physically defensive walls, its Speed tier leaves it outsped and KOed by a plethora of offensive Pokemon, such as Tapu Lele, Excadrill, and Hydreigon, to name a few. Nidoking's mediocre bulk also makes it difficult to come in on Pokemon that it can deal with but can wear it down, such as Celesteela, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Bulu. This frailty also makes it vulnerable even to revenge killers lacking super effective moves such as Spectrier.

Poison

Nidoking is one of the best wallbreakers that Poison has to offer thanks to its powerful combination of Life Orb and Sheer Force. Its role as a wallbreaker is very important in the Steel matchup, as Earth Power + Flamethrower demolishes Steel teams after Heatran's Air Balloon has been popped. Nidoking also offers Poison an Electric immunity to prevent Volt Switch spam from Electric-types like Regieleki and Tapu Koko. Its access to BoltBeam coverage allows Nidoking to apply more pressure on Flying teams, which is nice, since Stealth Rock cannot pressure Flying much because of how often it uses Heavy-Duty Boots. Nidoking is, however, slower than many faster threats like Excadrill, Cinderace, and Keldeo and weak to Water-, Ice-, and Ground-type moves like Scald, Ice Beam, and Earthquake. These flaws mean, Nidoking can only come in on certain passive walls or slower Pokemon like Galarian Weezing, Skarmory, and Toxapex.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Sludge Wave can be used over Earth Power to 2HKO defensive Pokemon that can tank the rest of Nidoking's moves easily such as Rotom-W and Moltres. However, forgoing Earth Power means Nidoking can't break through Heatran, limiting its effectiveness in the Steel matchup. Fire Blast over Flamethrower notably 2HKOes specially defensive Celesteela, but it is less reliable. Substitute is an option to make Nidoking harder to revenge kill, but it is very hard to fit.

Poison

Sludge Wave can be used to notably hit Clefable, because, otherwise, Nidoking may be at risk of losing its item from Knock Off.

Checks and Counters

Ground

Specially Defensive Walls: Specially defensive walls such as Blissey and defensive Rotom-W can tank multiple hits from Nidoking and retaliate.

Revenge Killers: Powerful revenge killers such as Alolan Raichu, Barraskewda, and Spectrier can force out Nidoking easily by threatening an OHKO with their STAB moves. Priority users such as Rillaboom and Mamoswine can outspeed and KO Nidoking with little to no chip damage.

Super Effective Moves: Super effective moves from foes faster than Nidoking such as Tapu Lele, Urshifu-R, and Latios can heavily pressure it. Nidoking must also be wary of super effective attacks from slower foes such as Hippowdon, Slowbro, and Swampert, as it fails to OHKO them.

Poison

Knock Off: Nidoking does not appreciate its item being removed and it being weakened by Knock Off users like Clefable and Tornadus-T.

Priority Moves: Priority moves like Aqua Jet and Ice Shard from Pokemon like Crawdaunt, Azumarill, and Mamoswine can KO Nidoking if their users are running a damage-boosting item like Choice Band or Life Orb, or after some prior chip damage.

Super Effective Attacks: Fast Ground-type Pokemon like Landorus-T, Excadrill, and Garchomp threaten Nidoking out with Earthquake. They also fear switching into Nidoking, though, since they are at risk of being hit by Ice Beam. Water-types like Keldeo, Urshifu-R, and Barraskewda can KO Nidoking with their Water-type STAB moves but do not always appreciate switching in risking a Thunderbolt. Ice-types like Kyurem, Weavile, and Mamoswine can KO Nidoking with Ice-type moves bar Ice Shard, which requires prior chip damage. However, yet again, they fear switching in, this time due to Earth Power or Flamethrower.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Specially bulky Pokemon like Piloswine, Blissey, and Snorlax can sponge all of Nidoking's attacks. Piloswine can KO Nidoking with Earthquake and set Stealth Rock for chip damage, while Blissey and Snorlax can recover from and switch into its moves whenever due to their high bulk. Blissey can set up Stealth Rock and generate momentum with Teleport, while Snorlax can set up Curse and recover off damage with Rest. Slowking can also generate momentum with Teleport or deal chip damage with Scald, while Mandibuzz can remove Nidoking's Life Orb with Knock Off and recover with Roost.

Revenge Killers: Naturally faster threats like both Urshifu formes, Tapu Lele, and Excadrill, and Choice Scarf users like Galarian Darmanitan and Heracross have no problem KOing Nidoking.

Wallbreaker (Ground).description:
Earth Power is the preferred STAB move, as it covers walls such as Heatran, physically defensive Gastrodon, and Tyranitar. Flamethrower provides great coverage against Steel- and Grass-types such as Skarmory, Amoonguss, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Bulu, hitting them for massive damage. Ice Beam nails Flying- and Dragon-types such as Zapdos, Dragonite, and Garchomp, as well as potential switch-ins like Landorus-T, Latias, and Hydreigon. It also deals with Cradily better than Earth Power. Thunderbolt hits additional Flying-types that are neutral to Ice Beam such as Mantine, Pelipper, and Celesteela super effectively. Toxic Spikes can be used over Earth Power to support the team and quickly wear down grounded foes such as Porygon2. However, Nidoking's poor bulk gives it limited opportunities to set Toxic Spikes, and Earth Power is needed to break through Heatran. Sheer Force works well in tandem with Life Orb, preventing Nidoking from being worn down by Life Orb recoil and stacking damage boosts. A Timid nature allows Nidoking to outspeed the likes of Tapu Bulu and Heatran.

Teammates such as Mamoswine, Landorus-T, and Excadrill appreciate Nidoking's ability to deal with threats like Skarmory and Celesteela. Hippowdon is a good partner, as its Sand Stream and Stealth Rock support wears down foes quickly for Nidoking. Additionally, its good bulk lets it come in on physical attackers such as Choice Scarf Excadrill, Garchomp, and Galarian Zapdos. Excadrill breaks through troublesome specially defensive walls such as Blissey and Slowking for Nidoking, beats Psychic- and Ice-types that it struggles against such as Tapu Lele, Alolan Ninetales, and Kyurem, and provides Rapid Spin support. Under Hippowdon's sand, Excadrill can also outspeed a handful of other offensive threats for Nidoking such as Choice Scarf Blacephalon, Dragapult, and Spectrier. Gastrodon and Seismitoad both provide a Water immunity for Nidoking; Gastrodon's Recover makes it more reliable against threats like Barraskewda, Keldeo, and Tapu Fini, and Seismitoad can check the highly dangerous Azumarill. Mamoswine is a powerful wallbreaker that can revenge kill some faster threats that give Nidoking trouble such as Latias, Dragapult, and Thundurus-T with Ice Shard. Choice Scarf Landorus-T is able to revenge kill additional fast foes such as Spectrier, Tapu Lele, and Volcarona while providing entry hazard removal with Defog. Its Ground immunity is also useful to handle threats such as Excadrill and Garchomp. Bulk Up + Gravity Landorus-T is another option to make Nidoking's Earth Power more spammable while helping in matchups like Poison. Choice Scarf Krookodile can act as a dangerous revenge killer against Ghost- and Psychic-types like Spectrier, Victini, and Latios. Krookodile also provides an immunity against Psychic-type attacks directed at Nidoking.

Wallbreaker (Poison).description:
Nidoking's powerful Earth Power damages Steel-, Electric-, Rock-, and Poison-types like Heatran, Tapu Koko, Rhyperior, and Toxapex. It appreciates Flamethrower for consistency to help with Steel-, Bug-, and Grass-types like Skarmory, Ferrothorn, Buzzwole, and Tapu Bulu, whereas Fire Blast is nice for picking up more KOs against bulkier Steel-types like Celesteela and Corviknight. Both Earth Power and Flamethrower are needed to deal with Steel's defensive cores members: Aegislash, Heatran, and Celesteela, but, Thunderbolt or Ice Beam is needed to pop Heatran's Air Balloon. Thunderbolt is useful for hitting Water- and Flying-types like Mantine and Slowbro, whereas Ice Beam helps with Ground-, Grass-, and Flying-types like Hippowdon, Appletun, and defensive Zapdos. Stealth Rock allows Nidoking to compress the role of entry hazard setter, but the presence of Heavy-Duty Boots reduces the need for hazards. Maximized Speed EVs allow Nidoking to Speed tie an opposing Nidoking and outpace Diggersby and Togekiss.

Nidoking offers the entire team its Electric immunity, but Toxapex appreciates it more than other teammates due to its weakness to Electric. Toxapex's bulk and Scald allow it to switch into physical attackers that threaten Nidoking like Barraskewda and Cinderace while also shutting down setup sweepers like Weavile and Cloyster with Haze. Galarian Weezing provides a Dragon immunity, which is important to switch into a Draco Meteor or Dragon Darts that could KO Nidoking, while also having utilities like Defog to get rid of entry hazards, Will-O-Wisp and Toxic Spikes to spread status, and Pain Split for longevity. Nidoking is weak to Psychic, so adding a Psychic-immune teammate like Skuntank or Drapion helps with Pokemon like Latias, Alakazam, and Tapu Lele. The former has Defog and Sucker Punch to revenge kill Psychic- and Ghost-types like Blacephalon and Alolan Raichu, while the latter has useful utilities like Knock Off, which removes Heavy-Duty Boots and makes Stealth Rock more effective and Whirlwind to phaze setup sweepers like Jirachi and Spectrier. Amoonguss is the best check to Ground-type Pokemon, notably Mold Breaker Excadrill, which threatens Nidoking and most of its teammates with Earthquake. Amoonguss also helps break Steel teams, as it has Spore to give Nidoking opportunities to come in while also forming a Regenerator core with Toxapex; together, they help Nidoking deal with Ground-, Rock-, and Water-type Pokemon like Excadrill, Rhyperior, Terrakion, and Urshifu-R. Nihilego runs Choice Scarf to revenge kill Pokemon like Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Victini and appreciates Nidoking's ability to threaten Steel-types it cannot properly deal with, like Ferrothorn and Aegislash. It has nice coverage moves like Thunderbolt, Dazzling Gleam, Power Gem, and Grass Knot, which improve quite a few matchups like Flying, Dragon, Fire, and Ground. Gengar is an option over Nihilego and supports Drapion or Skuntank in dealing with Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon like Galarian Corsola and Slowbro with Shadow Ball, and it also deals with bulky Pokemon like Toxapex and Aegislash. Galarian Slowking's ability to sponge Psychic-type attacks that KO Nidoking from Pokemon like Alolan Raichu and Latias is appreciated, and it forms a triple Regenerator core with Toxapex and Amoonguss, making Poison teams harder to break.

Offensive.description: Nidoking uses its incredible coverage and Sheer Force to be a terrifying special wallbreaker. Earth Power is an excellent go-to move that forces out slower, Ground-weak Pokemon like Toxapex and Heatran and 2HKOes common walls like Seismitoad and Ferrothorn. Gunk Shot can be used to outright 2HKO Blissey and deal massive damage to other special walls like Slowking, which improves the stall matchup, while Shell Side Arm is good for chunking Blissey and dealing consistent damage to Pokemon like Rotom-W. Gunk Shot's only drawback is the lower accuracy, making it slightly inconsistent in important situations. Ice Beam deals with Hippowdon and Tornadus-T, and Flamethrower deals with Steel- and Flying-types, rounding out Nidoking's perfect coverage on every Pokemon. Alternatively, Thunderbolt hits Slowking, Tornadus-T, and various Steel- and Flying types, but Ice Beam and Flamethrower are more effective. Nidoking typically uses a Rash nature to amplify its power as much as possible, but a Naive nature can be used to outspeed Pokemon like Adamant Excadrill, Jolly Buzzwole, and Timid Heatran. It should be noted that Nidoking's Poison typing can allow it to switch in on predicted Toxic from foes like Heatran and defensive Buzzwole. Nidoking can also switch in against Electric-types like Zeraora and Rotom-H. That being said, Nidoking doesn't like being chipped, so pivots like Corviknight, Cinderace, Rotom-W, and Tornadus-T allow it to get in more easily to wallbreak more often. Fast cleaners and wallbreakers are also appreciated as teammates to make up for Nidoking's lackluster speed, so Weavile, Cinderace, and Aerodactyl are all great partners.

bdspou.overview: Nidoking's presence in the BDSP OU metagame is marked by its powerful, Sheer Force boosted moves. Between its good STAB combination, wide variety of coverage moves, and the large number of Pokemon threatened by its strong attacks, such as Heatran and Clefable, it naturally performs well against balance and stall teams. However, Nidoking can struggle against more offensive teams thanks to its underwhelming Speed tier and weakness to common offensive typings like Water, Ground and Psychic. Furthermore, even in good matchups it can feel a bit prediction reliant, as the opponent can pivot around its moves into a faster threat.

Wallbreaker.description:
Ice Beam mainly hits Gliscor and Garchomp, but it is generally a good middle ground-option to hit Dragon- and Ground-types in general, such as Dragonite, Donphan, and Latias. Flamethrower is used to OHKO Scizor and Skarmory, as well as ease prediction against Steel-types. A Timid nature allows Nidoking to outspeed Timid Heatran, Jolly Feraligatr and Adamant Lucario, but the power boost Modest provides can be appealing to some teams.

Nidoking mainly fits on balance and bulky offense, as it is a useful tool for dismantling bulkier teams. Due to its poor defensive profile, Nidoking can struggle to get onto the field; therefore, it appreciates pivoting support from teammates such as Rotom-W and Scizor. The former can even switch into Water types that might give Nidoking trouble, while the latter can do the same for Psychic types. It also pairs well with more offensive pivots, like Choice Band Infernape, who can pressure Blissey, the best answer to Nidoking. Entry Hazards can amplify Nidoking's wallbreaking potential, and as such, setters like Heatran and Skarmory are great partners. Dragon-types like Dragonite and Latias enjoy the pressure Nidoking puts on Clefable and Steel-types.

Other Options

Nidoking can run Focus Punch over Flamethrower to lure in and heavily damage Blissey, leaving it unable to answer it anymore. However, the lack of any use beyond this specific matchup makes the reliability of Flamethrower more valuable for most teams. Toxic Spikes can help wear down some of its checks like the afromentioned Blissey, as well as Slowking, while supporting its teammates. However, this can limit Nidoking's wallbreaking capabilities. A Focus Sash set with Stealth Rock is another option, as Nidoking beats Gliscor, one of the best Defoggers in the tier, and can get something done even in unfavorable matchups. However, dropping Life Orb leaves Nidoking unable to net some important KOs, such as against Scizor and Rotom-W. Nidoking can also run Thunderbolt as another useful coverage option to hit bulky Water types that might otherwise give it trouble, like Milotic and Slowking, but those targets aren't common enough to warrant the move's usage most of the time.

Checks and Counters

Revenge Killers: Due to its average speed and middling bulk, a lot of fast Pokémon can easily revenge kill Nidoking, such as Latias, Garchomp, Weavile, and Starmie. Crawdaunt and Azumarill can OHKO it with Aqua Jet.

Blissey: Blissey is by far the best answer to Nidoking, easily tanking all its moves aside from the rare Focus Punch while sporting reliable recovery in Soft-Boiled. While it can be overwhelmed through team support, it is often a hard stop to anything Nidoking does.

Water-types: Some Water-types, like Slowking or Milotic, can switch into most of Nidoking's attacks and threaten it back with their Water STAB moves. Choice Scarf Rotom-W can switch into anything but Sludge Wave, outspeed it and threaten it with Hydro Pump.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Poison

Nidoking can run Fire Blast over Flamethrower, as the extra Base Power lets it OHKO Melmetal and 2HKO specially defensive Celesteela, while dealing more chip damage to neutral targets. However, due to its lower PP count and worse accuracy, it is riskier than Flamethrower. Substitute is a neat option for Nidoking to ease prediction; however, it limits Nidoking's wallbreaking potential, as it takes the place of an important coverage slot.

Wallbreaker (Poison).description:
Flamethrower, in tandem with Earth Power, pressures Steel-type Pokemon; it notably wrecks Ferrothorn, a Pokemon that Poison generally struggles to break through. Furthermore, Ice Beam and Thunderbolt make for excellent coverage across the metagame; Ice Beam alleviates matchup pressure against Ground- and Flying-type teams, which contain hard-to-break Pokemon such as Hippowdon and defensive Gliscor. Thunderbolt helps combat Water and Flying teams, notably hitting foes like Tapu Fini and Mantine, allowing Nidoking to make progress. Stealth Rock can be used as an option over Thunderbolt to further increase pressure on the opposing team with entry hazards, as not many Poison-types can learn the move.

Amoonguss and Mega-Venusaur assist Nidoking by switching into revenge killers such as Excadrill and Landorus-Therian, status them with sleep and poison, and switch into the Water-type attacks aimed at Nidoking. Alolan Muk is able to combat Pokemon that easily pivot into Nidoking such as Slowking and Blissey while also providing an important Psychic immunity. Muk also appreciates Nidoking's presence, as Nidoking pressured Pokemon that Alolan Muk fails to beat such as Hippowdon and Celesteela. If Stealth Rock is used over Thunderbolt, Gengar and Nihilego are good teammates, as they can both utilize Electric- and Grass-type coverage to make up for Nidoking loses upon dropping Thunderbolt. Crobat, Toxapex, and Galarian Slowking make for exceptional teammates that all appreciate NIdoking's Electric immunity. Crobat is immune to Ground-type attacks and can revenge kill foes such as Mega Gallade, Keldeo and Greninja. Toxapex can pivot into the Water- and Ice-type attacks that force Nidoking out while providing Toxic Spikes support. Finally, Galarian Slowking provides Future Sight support, which makes Nidoking's offensive pressure even harder to handle. Future Sight allows Nidoking to even break Pokemon such as opposing Mega-Venusaur. Galarian Slowking can also switch into Nidoking revenge killers such as Keldeo or Tapu Lele.

pu.overview: Clefairy fulfills a niche as one of the few viable pure Fairy-types within the tier, lacking the weaknesses that Ribombee has to Fire and Flying while keeping the defensive utility of a Fairy-type. Its main niches over other Fairy-types like Aromatisse are its access to Knock Off, which makes common Fairy-type switch-ins like Charizard and Centiskorch bad options, and Magic Guard, which means it doesn't care about chip damage. With a wide support movepool featuring moves like Stealth Rock and Encore, along with reliable recovery, it can compress roles on certain teams effectively. However, despite these qualities, Clefairy is heavily reliant on its item to keep its bulk. It also suffers from competition with other pure Fairy-types like Aromatisse and Comfey; the former has more physical bulk and is less hindered by its item being removed, while the latter has Taunt and priority in Triage Draining Kiss. Finally, without Encore, Clefairy is liable to be taken advantage of by setup sweepers like Uxie and Doublade.

Defensive.description: Moonblast lets Clefairy hit foes like Thievul and Absol, while Seismic Toss deals consistent damage to targets with high Special Defense like Gigalith and Steel-types like Aggron. Knock Off cripples Pokemon heavily reliant on their items like Doublade and Charizard. Encore prevents setup and can deter recovery moves from being used. Thunder Wave cripples faster foes like Galarian Articuno and Jellicent. Running 10 Speed IVs is an option to always avoid the 2HKO from Gyro Ball Ferroseed; however, this means that Clefairy underspeeds important Pokemon like Gigalith and Quagsire. Clefairy struggles against Poison- and Steel-types like Weezing and Ferroseed, so switch-ins to them like Wishiwashi and Charizard are heavily appreciated. Wishiwashi sponges Knock Off from Gallade and Sandslash for Clefairy, while in return, Clefairy is able to take on its checks like Lanturn; as for Charizard, Clefairy switches into Rock-types like Gigalith and Regirock for it.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

Calm Mind Clefairy makes for an excellent late-game sweeper. Physically defensive Clefairy tends to be the most reliable as a wall, but specially defensive Clefairy has a niche in checking Hattrem and Electabuzz. An offensive set with Life Orb and additional coverage attacks like Ice Beam can surprise as a wallbreaker, notably hurting walls like Vullaby and Tangela, but generally is less effective compared to faster wallbreakers.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Strong Poison-types like Roselia, Ivysaur, and Gastly prey on the passivity of Clefairy, and defensive examples like Mareanie and Koffing wall it out.

Steel-types: Clefairy has a hard time detering Steel-types like Ferroseed, Klang, and Metang, but Ferroseed cannot deal with Flamethrower.

Wallbreakers: Any wallbreaker that doesn't mind Clefairy's usual coverage like Rufflet, Raboot, Lampent, and Lairon can switch in against it and break past its defenses.

Utility.description:
With a solid defensive typing, above average bulk, and Magic Guard to absorb status, Clefairy makes for a great physical defensive wall which provides teams with reliable utility. Moonblast is Clefairy's primary attack, dealing solid damage to common Fighting- and Dark-types such as Gurdurr, Vullaby, and Machoke, although it should be wary of Machoke's Heavy Slam. Soft-Boiled gives Clefairy the longevity to be a reliable defensive wall throughout the game as well as a scouting tool. Knock Off removes opposing Eviolites, weakening the defensive capability of foes like Klang and Hattrem. Thunder Wave cripples setup sweepers like Wartortle and faster attackers like Thwackey that try to take advantage of Clefairy's passive nature. Alternatively, if the team is lacking a Stealth Rock user, Clefairy can fulfill that role while Flamethrower can be used to deal some damage to Steel-types such as Ferroseed, which typically switch in on Clefairy.

Clefairy should use Soft-Boiled to remain as healthy in order reliably check physical threats like Piloswine and Fraxure. Clefairy's Eviolite should be preserved, as it requires its item to perform its role as a wall. If Clefairy is running Stealth Rock, it should only try to set it up once an opposing Hattrem is removed. Knock Off should be used often early-game to remove as many Eviolites as possible to help with cleaners like Gurdurr and Wartortle. Wallbreakers, such as Rufflet and Piloswine, also appreciate Knock Off support as well as Clefairy's ability to lower the speed of opposing Pokemon with Thunder Wave. Specially defensive walls like Klang, Mareanie, and Ferroseed make for solid partners and are reliable switch-ins to Gastly so that Clefairy is not as easily revenge killed by it. Clefairy is very passive and works best when paired with U-turn and Parting Shot users such as Raboot and Galarian Linoone to avoid losing too much momentum.

WishPass.description:
Clefairy is a reliable Wish passer due to its great HP stat, defensive typing, and Teleport for slow pivoting. Moonblast is this set's only attacking move, dealing with Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types and stopping it from being completely susceptible to Taunt. Wish can heal both Clefairy and its teammates like Machoke and Hattrem that lack recovery. Protect allows Clefairy to guarantee it receives its Wish as well as scout common Choice item holders such as Raboot and Hattrem. Alternatively, Moonlight works for its instantaneous recovery.

Clefairy should switch into physical attackers, such as Gurdurr and Piloswine, or relatively passive Pokemon like Galarian Corsola in order to heal its teammates safely. Wallbreakers that lack recovery such as Lampent, Piloswine, and Raboot all benefit from the healing provided by Clefairy to enable them to switch in more reliably; these three may also switch into anticipated Poison- and Steel-type attacks that target Clefairy. Fighting- and Fire-types like Gurdurr and Raboot can cover for Clefairy's Steel-type weakness, and in return Clefairy is able to keep them healthy. Clefairy's passivity makes it vulnerable to setup sweepers like Klang and Wartortle, so use Teleport to safely bring in wallbreakers and revenge killers like Raboot and Thwackey to deal with these sweepers.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Clefairy has access to a lot of other utility options including Thunder Wave, Healing Wish, Wish, and Aromatherapy. However, they are often hard to justify running due to how good the moves listed on the main set are. Clefairy can try to run a Calm Mind set, but it is usually outclassed by Alcremie, Spiritomb, and Galarian Rapidash. Physically defensive sets are also outclassed by Alcremie due to the latter's ability to absorb Knock Off and thus check more physical attackers.

Checks and Counters

Poison- and Steel-types: Attackers like Silvally-Poison, Swords Dance Qwilfish, Klinklang, and Alolan Dugtrio can easily switch into Moonblast and Toxic and threaten Clefairy with their super effective STAB moves. However, most of them hate losing their item to Knock Off.

Physical Wallbreakers: Swords Dance users like Thwackey, Silvally-Dark, and Rapidash can easily break Clefairy after a boost, whereas Choice Band users like Silvally, Gourgeist-S and Lycanroc-N can outright 2HKO Clefairy.

Item Disruption: Clefairy relies on its Eviolite to switch into strong hits from wallbreakers like Thievul, Exeggutor, and Jynx, thus it should avoid losing its item to Knock Off users like Tangela, Sawk, Gurdurr, and Liepard. Similarly, Trick users like Rotom and Jynx lure Clefairy in and can cripple it with their Choice items.

Stallbreakers: Due to Moonblast's abysmal damage output, Clefairy can struggle against stallbreakers with a way to circumvent Toxic like Galarian Rapidash, Taunt Froslass, and Substitute + Nasty Plot Rotom.

Specially Defensive.description:
Clefairy is an excellent special wall in ZU due to its awesome Eviolite-boosted bulk, coveted Fairy typing, and its wonderful ability in Magic Guard. Magic Guard makes it hard to weaken Clefairy through normal means like entry hazards and Toxic. Knock Off lets it cripple its switch-ins that rely on their item to check Clefairy in the long run like Klinklang, Skuntank, and Rapidash. Toxic is Clefairy's best way to wear down opposing walls, as its Moonblast is really weak but most opposing walls are heavily threatened by Toxic and cannot threaten Clefairy back. Teleport is an option to let Clefairy act as a defensive pivot and bring a partner on the field, however it is incompatible with Knock Off and Soft-Boiled, meaning Clefairy has to rely on the Moonlight, which has more limited PP and prevents Clefairy from checking Choice Specs Abomasnow. Clefairy can also run Stealth Rock if one of its partner isn't running it.

Clefairy works best on the more defensive teams like stall and balance. Ground-types like Alolan Dugtrio, Stunfisk, and Galarian Stunfisk make for amazing partners for Clefairy; they can check Steel- and Poison-types like Klinklang and Silvally-Poison for it, run Stealth Rock which frees up one of Clefairy's moveslot for Toxic, and also bring an Electric-immunity that prevents the likes of Rotom and Manectric from freely using Volt Switch on Clefairy. In return, Clefairy can check attackers like Jynx, Thievul, and Exeggutor. Physical walls such as Tangela and Miltank help Clefairy dealing with physical attackers like Silvally, Thwackey, and Kangaskhan; Knock Off absorbers like Alcremie, Sableye, and Poliwrath are also invaluable. Fast but frail attackers like Froslass, Liepard, and Accelgor appreciate Clefairy's ability to use Teleport to bring them safely.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Utility and Calm Mind Clefable can use an EV spread of 252 HP / 160 Def / 96 SpD with a Calm nature to survive a +2 Tectonic Rage from Nasty Plot Hydreigon, but it loses the ability to comfortably check Mega Lopunny, making this spread somewhat undesirable. Wish can be used on utility sets to give Pokemon that lack reliable recovery such as Heatran and Ferrothorn tons of needed support; however, Wish sets are extremely passive and easy for Pokemon to overwhelm. A Clefable set using Moonblast / Wish / Protect / Teleport makes it even easier to pass Wishes; unfortunately, it's very easy for Clefable to get overwhelmed by a plethora of dangerous Pokemon such as Mega Scizor, Landorus-T, Rillaboom, and Tapu Lele, which can make it hard to pass Wish and keep Clefable healthy at the same time. Ice Beam can be used on Calm Mind Clefable to always KO Landorus-T and especially Gliscor, but it loses the ability to hit Heatran and Mega Scizor for neutral damage.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Melmetal, and Mega Mawile all pose threats to Clefable because they resist Moonblast and can easily overwhelm it. However, they are all very susceptible to Calm Mind Clefable with Flamethrower.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Heatran, Volcarona, and Mega Charizard Y are very good checks to Clefable; their STAB attacks are able to overwhelm and force Clefable to recover multiple times versus them. However, none of them want to be hit by Knock Off or Thunder Wave.

Strong Attackers: Clefable's average bulk can leave it easily overwhelmed by neutral hits and attackers such as Choice Specs Tapu Lele, Tapu Koko, and Kyurem; however, they all lack longevity, meaning that Clefable can outlast them.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Clefable is one of the best wincons in National Dex due to its large movepool, great defensive typing, passable bulk, and especially amazing ability in Magic Guard, which allows Clefable to find many setup opportunities against some of the best Pokemon in the metagame, such as Slowbro, Corviknight, and Zapdos. Calm Mind makes it an extremely potent Pokemon against bulky teams that do not have a way of preventing it from setting up freely. Thunder is largely preferred over Thunderbolt because of its extremely high paralysis chance, letting Clefable cripple Pokemon such as Heatran, and its ability to easily 2HKO Toxapex without any Calm Mind boosts. Alternatively, Flamethrower hits Steel-types that annoy Clefable like Excadrill, Mega Mawile, Melmetal, and Mega Scizor, but Clefable's easily walled by Heatran and Toxapex without Thunder. A Bold nature is preferred so Clefable can more easily check Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny and Mega Latias.

Calm Mind Clefable best fits on balance teams, as its defensive utility is very helpful there. Pokemon that struggle a lot with Kyurem and Mega Latias such as Heatran, Blissey, and Zapdos appreciate Clefable's ability to check them. Calm Mind Clefable can struggle quite a lot to beat Fire- and Steel-types such as Heatran, Volcarona, Mega Mawile, and Mega Scizor, and they can limit its opportunities to set up Calm Mind; as such, checks to them such as Toxapex, Heatran, Slowking, Landorus-T, and Garchomp work as excellent teammates. Spikes support from Ferrothorn is very important for Clefable, as it wears down Toxapex and Heatran, two of Clefable's most prominent answers.

Utility.description:
Clefable is an outstanding utility Pokemon due to its amazing defensive typing, decent bulk, and ability in Magic Guard, allowing it to check dangerous Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny, Kommo-o, Hawlucha, Garchomp, and Kyurem while not fearing passive damage. Stealth Rock is a great option for Clefable because it can cripple entry hazard removers such as Zapdos and Corviknight with its utility moves and be relatively unaffected by them in return. Calm Mind makes Clefable a much bigger threat and potential wincon while also allowing it to threaten Defoggers such as Zapdos and Tapu Fini more effectively to keep Stealth Rock up. Knock Off allows Clefable to cripple a vast majority of Pokemon, such as Zapdos, Ferrothorn, opposing Clefable, and Heatran. Alternatively, Thunder Wave provides speed control and still lets Clefable cripple Pokemon that want to switch in, such as Mega Scizor and Heatran. A Bold nature allows Clefable to more easily check Mega Lopunny and Garchomp, which it would otherwise struggle with, but special investment can be useful in checking Kyurem.

Clefable is a staple on balance teams due to its unrivalled utility and great role compression. Clefable can cripple Pokemon like Corviknight, Ferrothorn, Heatran, Toxapex, and Zapdos with Thunder Wave and Knock Off, supporting Pokemon like Volcarona, Rillaboom, Kartana, Mega Mawile, and Weavile. Although it has decent bulk, Clefable can be easily overwhelmed by Pokemon such as Heatran, Mega Mawile, and Mega Scizor, so checks such as Slowking, Heatran, and Zapdos are great teammates. Pokemon that heavily struggle versus Mega Lopunny and Garchomp such as Kyurem, Mega Mawile, and Heatran enjoy Clefable's ability to easily check them. Clefable appreciates Water-type checks such as Toxapex and Ferrothorn, as they allow it to more easily check Ash-Greninja, while Clefable's Dark-type resistance can be very helpful for the aforementioned Pokemon in keeping Ash-Greninja in check.

Unaware.description:
Unaware Clefable is a very important part of stall teams, as its Fairy typing alongside its large movepool allows it to support its team in many ways, mainly comfortably checking prominent setup sweepers such as Garchomp, opposing Clefable, Mega Gyarados, Hydreigon, Hawlucha, and Volcarona. Calm Mind allows Clefable to be a potential wincon for stall teams. Flamethrower allows Clefable to hit Pokemon that resist Moonblast such as Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight very hard. However, it can be replaced by Heal Bell, which makes Clefable very self sufficient and lets it support teammates such as Bulk Up Corviknight and Alomomola. Wish can also be considered, as Clefable's great defensive typing and decent bulk grant it opportunities to pass Wishes to another teammate. However, it's generally worse than Alomomola because its ability, bulk, and typing give it more opportunities to pass Wishes.

Unaware Clefable fits exclusively on stall teams, as its ability to shut down sweepers is very valuable and prevents these teams from being overwhelmed as easily. Mega Sableye and Corviknight are very important partners, as Unaware Clefable is vulnerable to both entry hazards and especially Toxic, which Mega Sableye and Corviknight are able to deter. Bulk Up Corviknight in particular is notable, as it can PP stall Toxapex's Haze with Pressure, allowing Calm Mind Clefable to more easily break past it late-game. Chansey and Alomomola are great partners for Clefable because they can free up more important moves for it; for example, Chansey can run Heal Bell for it and Alomomola can run Wish.

monotype.overview: Clefable is a great utility Pokemon, having access to decent bulk paired with Magic Guard as well as a good movepool that provides it with reliable recovery and the ability to set Stealth Rock. Magic Guard is especially useful, as it allows Clefable to serve as a status sponge for the rest of the team against Pokemon such as SubToxic Aegislash and Toxapex. It also means Clefable can come in freely against Spikes when going against types like Grass and Steel. Both these traits are very valuable due to Fairy teams commonly lacking entry hazard removal, making traditional teams susceptible to hazards like the aforementioned Spikes and Toxic Spikes. However, Clefable's bulk is not good enough to prevent it from being blown away by stronger wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Kyurem, Choice Specs Zapdos, and Choice Band Zeraora.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Leftovers can be used over Rocky Helmet, but that sacrifices Clefable's ability to threaten Celesteela outside of removing its recovery. Thunder Wave can be used over Knock Off to cripple various Pokemon, namely faster Pokemon and defensive walls such as Tapu Lele and Corviknight. Healing Wish can also be used over Knock Off in order to support an offensive teammate later on in the game. However, Knock Off's utility is generally a lot more valuable. Babiri Berry may be considered to take Scizor's Bullet Punch at +2 and Choice Band Excadrill's Iron Head, retaliating with Flamethrower. However, Babiri Berry's utility is situational, and Scizor's Bullet Punch can be neutralized by its teammate, Tapu Lele.

Checks and Counters

Wallbreakers Wallbreakers such as Choice Band Rillaboom, Choice Specs Zapdos, and Choice Specs Tapu Lele easily beat Clefable due to its middling bulk.

Stallbreakers: Stallbreakers such as Tapu Fini and Tornadus-T can break through Clefable by preventing it from using its utility moves or recovering with Soft-boiled.

Stealth Rock.description:
Clefable is a great Stealth Rock setter due to its good bulk, recovery, and Magic Guard, allowing it to set it on offensive threats like Choice Scarf Landorus-T or passive walls such as Toxapex and Ferrothorn. Moonblast is important for threatening Substitute Kyurem, Dragonite, Galarian Moltres, and Hydreigon in particular, keeping them from using Clefable as setup fodder. Knock Off cancels out passive recovery from various Pokemon like Celesteela, Dragalge, Toxapex, Aegislash, and Tyranitar by removing Leftovers, softening them up for later on in the game, as well as Heavy-Duty Boots users like Mandibuzz and Mantine so that they take damage from Clefable's Stealth Rock. It's also useful for removing Choice items like Excadrill's and Thundurus-T's Choice Scarf, allowing Pokemon like Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu to revenge kill them. Rocky Helmet in conjunction with Soft-Boiled chips down Celesteela, as it is forced to use Heavy Slam on Clefable in order to beat it. 16 Speed EVs let Clefable outspeed neutral-natured Celesteela so that Clefable can wear it down by using Soft-Boiled first and relying on Rocky Helmet recoil.

All offensive Pokemon on Fairy generally appreciate Clefable's ability to serve as a status sponge. Tapu Bulu and Tapu Koko are offensive teammates that Clefable can support by removing items like Thundurus-T's and Landorus-T's Choice Scarf, allowing them to revenge kill them. Stealth Rock is also great in the Electric matchup in particular, as Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu can OHKO Choice Specs Zapdos with Stone Edge after Stealth Rock damage, and it helps Tapu Koko pressure Flying more easily by chipping down faster checks like the aforementioned Choice Scarf users that try to switch in. In return, Tapu Bulu can provide Clefable with passive recovery with Grassy Terrain, and Tapu Koko can threaten Defoggers like Mantine and Corviknight that may try to remove Clefable's Stealth Rock with Thunderbolt, as Clefable usually cannot threaten them itself. Klefki forms a good hazard stacking core with Clefable and can support its subpar bulk with its dual screens. Mimikyu can check Pokemon such as Hatterene, Aegislash, and Thundurus-T that set up on Clefable due to its passiveness with Disguise. Tapu Lele can beat Poison-type Pokemon such as Toxapex and Dragalge for Clefable. Azumarill appreciates Stealth Rock, as it allows it to OHKO Celesteela with more ease after Belly Drum.

Calm Mind (Fairy).description:
Calm Mind Clefable functions as a bulky setup sweeper for Fairy teams due to its good coverage in Flamethrower and Thunderbolt, which lets it deal with Celesteela and Toxapex. Its ability in Magic Guard stops entry hazards and status from wearing it down. Calm Mind, in conjunction with Soft-Boiled, allows Clefable to accrue several boosts against Pokemon that cannot significantly damage it such as Ferrothorn, SubToxic Aegislash, and SubRoost Kyurem. Thunderbolt deals with Water- and Flying-types such as Mantine, Celesteela, and Volcanion, and it also wears down Haze and Roar users such as Toxapex and Heatran. Flamethrower deals with Steel- and Grass-types such as Ferrothorn and Rillaboom. Moonblast can be used to help deal with Dark- and Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Garchomp, and it also wears down Swampert, which can wall Clefable's coverage moves. Moonblast also allows Clefable to threaten Dragon teams, which do not mind Clefable's coverage moves. Life Orb turns Clefable into a fearsome threat, allowing it to consistently 2HKO Toxapex, Celesteela, and Drapion at +1. Magic Guard also nullifies its recoil. Alternatively, Leftovers makes Clefable harder for types such as Grass, Dark, and Water to handle due to its increased longevity. 16 Speed EVs let Clefable outspeed defensive variants of Celesteela, while the remaining EVs maximize its physical bulk to better deal with threats such as Choice Scarf Excadrill, Rillaboom, and Zeraora.

Klefki's dual screens make it an ideal partner for Clefable, as these allow Clefable to set up more easily, as well as staying in to damage threats such as Choice Band Excadrill and Rillaboom. Klefki also provides a Poison immunity to come in against threats such as Nihilego, debilitates Clefable answers such as Gengar and Mantine with Thunder Wave and Toxic, and sets Spikes to wear down the opposing team. Tapu Bulu and Clefable both wear down their shared checks in Toxapex, Celesteela, and Melmetal. Tapu Bulu also sets Grassy Terrain to improve Clefable's longevity, deals with Swampert, Clear Smog Gastrodon, and Regieleki for it, and pressures Heatran for Clefable not running Thunderbolt. This allows Clefable to sweep Steel teams late-game. Tapu Lele checks Poison-types like Nidoking and Dragalge, allows Clefable to deal with Scizor by setting Psychic Terrain, and deals with Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Kyurem, especially if Clefable doesn't have Moonblast. Clefable repays this by wearing down Steel-types such as Aegislash and Corviknight, which wall Tapu Lele. Tapu Koko pivots Clefable into passive Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, is a fast teammate that deals with Urshifu-R, Weavile, and Cinderace, and can deal with Water-types such as Mantine, Slowking, and Toxapex for Clefable not running Thunderbolt. Azumarill appreciates its checks in Mantine, Volcanion, and Ferrothorn being worn down, as this allows it to clean types such as Flying, Fire, and Steel late-game. In return, Azumarill deals with Alolan Marowak, Galarian Slowking, and Nidoking, which Clefable struggles against. Alternatively, Calm Mind Tapu Fini forms a special wallbreaking core with Clefable and relieves it from having to use Moonblast, as Tapu Fini deals with Dragon-, Ground-, and Fire-types such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Heatran. Mimikyu is a Swords Dance sweeper that deals with Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Spectrier, Gengar, and Hatterene. Alolan Ninetales appreciates Clefable's ability to take out Celesteela and Toxapex, as this allows Alolan Ninetales to clean Flying and Water teams late-game, and can also provide support with Grudge.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Kee Berry Sweeper.description:
• This Clefable aims to take advantage of opposing setup sweepers in order to augment its own stats and reverse sweep.

  • Moonlight is chosen to guarantee quick healing and for getting boosted healing in sun, which can be set by Clefable's own Max Flare. Be wary of its low PP and other weathers before committing to sweeping and relying on it for healing.

  • Kee Berry is used to grant Clefable a one-time boost of Defense and can be used in combination with Dynamax to ensure Clefable can survive hits such as Excadrill's Iron Head.

  • The given EV spread gives near maximum physical bulk and is used to survive an initial physical hit as well as possible before getting the +1 Defense boost from Kee Berry.

Trick Crippler.description:
• Clefable when equipped with Flame Orb or Lagging Tail can cripple various attackers, making them easy setup fodder for teammates.

  • Stealth Rock provides additional support, but can be sacrificed for Flamethrower coverage, in order to ensure Ferrothorn and Celesteela cannot switch in with impunity.

Items

  • Flame Orb allows Clefable to cripple physical attackers with Trick.

  • Lagging Tail and Full Incense are an extremely effective form of Speed control with Trick, with even fast Pokemon, and Pokemon under Trick Room being impacted by it.

  • Leftovers can also be opted for, and provides a decent all around Stealth Rock lead with two useful complementary attacks.

Utility.description: Clefable's Fairy typing, respectable bulk, and immunity to residual damage like Toxic make it a solid choice for either a defensive spinner or a Stealth Rock setter, finding many opportunities to come onto the field and matching up particularly well against common entry hazard setters like Seismitoad, Mudsdale, and Hippowdon as a spinner. Glare spreads paralysis, warding off wallbreakers like Gengar and Melmetal and providing speed control for slower wallbreakers such as Tyranitar and Buzzwole. Alternatively, Clefable's deep movepool allows it to run a vast array of other utility options; Teleport can bring the aforementioned wallbreakers in with ease, for example, matching up better against slower threats like Galarian Slowking and Ferrothorn, which Glare is less effective against. Knock Off is also a good option, removing items such as Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots to drastically reduce the longevity of Pokemon like Heatran and Zeraora. Trick in conjunction with Sticky Barb can be used in a similar manner, albeit only one time. Clefable can use both Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin on the same moveset for maximum role compression, although it loses any ability to deter aforementioned switch-ins like Gengar and Heatran in the process. The same holds true of both Aromatherapy and Wish, which are greatly appreciated by offensive tanks like Tornadus-T, Melmetal, and Heatran. VoltTurn cores with Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Aerodactyl greatly appreciate Rapid Spin Clefable only removing opposing hazards, while Spikes setters like Seismitoad can form a hazard-stacking core with Stealth Rock Clefable. Skarmory and Ferrothorn are also very notable hazard setters, as they can handle physical wallbreakers like Choice Band Tyranitar and Aerodactyl that punch through Clefable with ease. Similarly, Clefable struggles to take on strong special attackers like Keldeo and Rotom-H, so specially defensive teammates like Assault Vest Toxapex and Slowking are recommended.

Calm Mind.description: Calm Mind Clefable takes advantage of passive switch-ins like Corviknight, Gastrodon, and Ferrothorn lacking Grav Apple to accumulate multiple boosts, making itself a capable sweeper that can be difficult to take down. Rapid Spin offers entry hazard removal and bolsters Clefable's Speed stat, notably letting it outpace Choice Band Tyranitar after one boost and positive-natured base 95s like Obstagoon and Kyurem after two. Rapid Spin also invites in many hazard setters Clefable can boost against like Mudsdale and the aforementioned Gastrodon; since it pressured hazard setters, Calm Mind also makes it easier to keep hazards off the field. Glare is used to hinder threats like Fire Lash Cinderace and Nidoking that Clefable may force in after garnering boosts. An additional coverage move such as Flamethrower, Stored Power, or Thunder can be used instead to more immediately pressure Fairy-resistant walls such as Ferrothorn, Corviknight, and non-Assault Vest Toxapex, making Clefable a more independent sweeper but reducing its utility. 12 Speed EVs are used to outpace uninvested Tyranitar. Clefable pairs well with bulky Pokemon like Skarmory and Toxapex that benefit from its offensive presence, and in turn they can set hazards to wear down foes and switch into strong wallbreakers like Choice Band Tyranitar and Urshifu-R, that force Clefable out. Clefable is hard stopped by Toxapex carrying Haze or Clear Smog, and without Flamethrower it can't meaningfully damage offensive Fairy-resistant Pokemon like Melmetal and Excadrill, so teammates that can remove or weaken these threats such as offensive Rotom-H and Rocky Helmet Ferrothorn are greatly appreciated.

camomons.comments:
Other Options

Wish can be used in the last slot on Unaware Clefable in order to heal its teammates . Teleport can also be run on Unaware Clefable to provide pivoting to Clefable's teammates, allowing offensive wallbreakers to come in more safely. Clefable can choose to run an alternative EV spread of 252 HP / 120 Def / 136 Spe with a Bold nature in order to outspeed threats such as Conkeldurr, Rhyperior and Melmetal; however, this does hamper Clefable's ability to take physical hits somewhat.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Threats such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, Ground / Flying Mew, and Water / Ground Salamence are immune to Thunderbolt and can all hit Clefable super effectively with their strong physical Ground-type STAB attacks, potentially OHKOing it in the majority of cases. However, none of the aforementioned threats easily switch in into offensive Clefable's Fairy-type STAB.

Physical Attackers: Strong physical wallbreakers such as Landorus-T, Lycanroc-D, Urshifu, and Dracovish can all heavily threaten Clefable. Lycanroc-D and Urshifu in particular can usually switch into Unaware Clefable quite safely and threaten to heavily dent it in return, though both struggle to break offensive Clefable.

Specially Defensive Walls: Although they cannot do that much in return, walls such as opposing Unaware Clefable, Chansey, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can take on Magic Guard Clefable's boosted attacks and pivot into powerful breakers that can threaten it in return.

Poison- and Steel-Types: Poison- and Steel-types have ample opportunity to switch in via Unaware Clefable's Toxic or offensive Clefable's Moonblast. Those that resist Knock Off such as Steel / Fighting Melmetal, Dark / Poison Toxapex, and Dark / Poison Tornadus-T do particularly well against Unaware Clefable, while Poison / Electric Latias and Steel / Ground Melmetal are able to switch into offensive sets safely.

Opposing Calm Mind Sweepers: Calm Mind users such as Electric / Poison Latias, Cresselia, and Magearna can boost alongside Clefable and potentially outdamage it and beat it one-on-one.

Unaware Wall.description:
Clefable is an incredible specially defensive wall that can check a wide array of special attackers and setup threats, such as Volcarona and Tornadus-T, due to its nice bulk, ability in Unaware, and reliable recovery options. With Knock Off and Toxic, Clefable can cripple various opposing threats, and it utilizes an amazing defensive typing with only one weakness. Clefable can be used as a dedicated Stealth Rock setter, since it can annoy common Defog users such as Tornadus-T, Mew, and Salamence by statusing them and removing important items such as Heavy-Duty Boots via Knock Off. Seismic Toss is a more consistent damaging option that lets Clefable effectively wear down opposing threats that either resist Knock Off or are immune to Toxic such as Cresselia, Latias, and opposing Clefable. Aromatherapy is another option that enables Clefable to cure itself and its teammates from status, which can be crucial on more defensive teams. Black Sludge provides Clefable with passive recovery, which can enable it to better survive hits from stronger threats such as Fleur Cannon Magearna and Choice Specs Tapu Lele. Heavy-Duty Boots is an alternative item option that enables Clefable to switch in more proficiently without needing to take entry hazard damage.

Clefable appreciates teammates that can handle physically offensive threats such as Landorus-T, Pheromosa, and Lycanroc-D. Thus, partners such as Mew, Slowbro, and Landorus-T all make great choices. Mew and Landorus-T in particular can provide Clefable with entry hazard support, enabling it to wear down targets more quickly in tandem with Knock Off + Toxic. Offensive teammates such as Tornadus-T, Garchomp, and Rillaboom also pair well with Clefable, as Clefable can help wear down their checks and enable them to break through the opposing team more easily. Entry hazard removal is also crucial for Clefable due to its susceptibility to both Stealth Rock and Spikes if it does not run Heavy-Duty Boots. Partners such as Latias, Defog Mew, and Avalugg all pair well with Clefable in this regard.

Offensive Setup.description:
Offensive Clefable is geared to act as a wincon that can terrorize common defensive cores thanks to its incredible STAB coverage and ability to forego passive damage thanks to Magic Guard, which makes it difficult to stop once it begins to set up. Thunderbolt compliments Moonblast well by targeting threats that resist Fairy like Steel / Flying Mew, Water / Poison Latias, and Fire / Flying Tornadus-T. Flamethrower can be used as a secondary STAB option over Thunderbolt, enabling Clefable to target checks such as Ferrothorn and Steel / Ground Garchomp. Life Orb boosts Clefable's power without the drawback of recoil thanks to its ability. As Calm Mind already boosts Clefable's Special Defense, a Bold nature and investment in HP and Defense enable it to sponge as many physical moves as possible.

Thunderbolt Clefable struggles against specially defensive walls like Ferrothorn, Steel / Ground Kommo-o, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowking. Thus, partners such as Swords Dance Garchomp, Lycanroc-D, and Heracross all make amazing teammates. Flamethrower Clefable struggles with Steel / Ground Pokemon immune to Fire-type attacks such as Coalossal and Heatran; thus, partners that can threaten them out like Landorus, Pheromosa, and Water / Dragon Hydreigon are very valuable additions alongside it. Due to the more offensive nature of this set, backup defensive pivots such as Mew, Blissey, and Buzzwole are much appreciated to keep opposing wallbreakers such as Haxorus and Melmetal in check. Clefable also appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Ferrothorn, Kommo-o, and Landorus-T to help wear down switch-ins more easily.

ubers.overview: Clefable is a niche Fairy-type in Ubers that is immune to entry hazards and status thanks to Magic Guard. Its vast movepool gives it all the tools it needs to properly support its teammates; it can set Stealth Rock, stick around with Soft-Boiled, remove valuable items with Knock Off, and consistently checks Yveltal. However, its subpar base stats leave it in Xerneas's dust as a defensive Fairy-type, as it fails to check prominent physical attackers such as Groudon, Choice Band Marshadow, and offensive Zygarde. As such, it's almost exclusively used for its ability to compress Stealth Rock and Thunder Wave in one teamslot.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Rocky Helmet is a niche option in the item slot to punish Yveltal's contact moves, as it can potentially put it in range of Choice Specs Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage, but Leftovers recovery is usually much more appreciated. Trick, alongside Sticky Barb, can cripple a foe, but is usually not worth it.

Checks and Counters

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM pressures Clefable immensely, and it can potentially set up on it, and does not really mind losing its item.

Eternatus: Specially defensive Eternatus does not mind losing its item and can threaten Clefable with Sludge Bomb, while offensive variants can set up on it with Meteor Beam.

Strong Wallbreakers: Zekrom, Calyrex-S, Kyogre, and offensive Groudon can all muscle through Clefable's middling defenses.

Other Steel-types: Heatran and Zamazenta-C all beat Clefable one-on-one, but Heatran does not appreciate getting its item removed or getting paralyzed.

Defensive.description:
Running Stealth Rock on Clefable frees up a moveslot for Necrozma-DM, allowing it to run coverage options or a Dragon Dance set. Knock Off is very valuable in Ubers, as many Pokemon rely heavily on items such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers. Thunder Wave can be run instead so that Clefable can paralyze common switch-ins such as Necrozma-DM and Eternatus, as well as wallbreakers such as Calyrex-S and Ho-Oh. Heal Bell is another alternative that allows Clefable to remove pesky status from its teammates.

Clefable is found mostly on bulkier teams where its passivity isn't as detrimental. Ferrothorn is a fantastic partner, checking Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Kyogre while Clefable can take on Marshadow in exchange. Ferrothorn also provides Spikes to pair with Clefable's Stealth Rock, making a decent entry hazard setting core. Yveltal can take on Calyrex-S, which threatens to OHKO Clefable. In return, Clefable can repeatedly switch into Knock Off for Yveltal, ensuring that Yveltal can keep its item. Eternatus also appreciates Clefable acting as a solid Knock Off switch-in. Defensive Zygarde is a fantastic partner that can help Clefable deal with strong physical wallbreakers such as Choice Band Marshadow, Swords Dance Groudon, and offensive Ho-Oh. Clefable running Heal Bell can heal Zygarde from stray status conditions, allowing it to use Rest more liberally.

ou.overview: Clefable, blessed with being born in RBY, has access to an expansive toolbox of support options in addition to a good defensive typing and two excellent defensive abilities in Magic Guard and Unaware. Its wide movepool allows it to function as an entry hazard setter with Stealth Rock, spread status with Thunder Wave or Toxic, hinder opposing Pokemon with Knock Off, and even run an offensive set with coverage moves like Flamethrower and Thunderbolt. This versatility makes Clefable a great addition to most team archetypes, letting it support offensive teammates with utility sets, wall setup sweepers with Unaware, or act as a special attacking setup sweeper with an offensive Calm Mind set. However, despite all of the attributes that make Clefable such a great addition to many teams, it suffers from middling defensive stats and can get overwhelmed by particularly strong attackers, requiring other bulky teammates to be the ones primarily taking hits and potentially struggling against offensive teams.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Clefable can make use of Magic Guard to run a Trick + Sticky Barb set to effectively impair opposing Pokemon, especially opposing walls, but should be wary of accidentally taking a Choice item or Assault Vest with Trick, ruining its defensive sets. Toxic is an alternative to Thunder Wave that can put opposing Pokemon on a timer, but since Clefable's most common checks are immune to Toxic, Thunder Wave is generally more effective. Clefable has access to Wish and Teleport, but its middling bulk makes it a subpar Wish passer, and a Wish + Protect set eats into Clefable's already limited moveslots. Encore can be used to lock foes into a move, allowing Clefable to set up entry hazards or a teammate to safely switch in. Healing Wish can be used to give offensive teammates like Dragonite and Volcarona a second life. Clefable can run a specially defensive EV spread to easily check Dragapult and offensive Zapdos variants, but this comes at the cost of being more vulnerable to strong physical attackers.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: If not running Flamethrower or Thunderbolt, Clefable is easily checked by Steel-types like Melmetal, Excadrill, Scizor, and Kartana.

Poison-types: Poison-types like Galarian Slowking, Nidoking, and Nihilego easily switch into Clefable, although they generally don't like taking Knock Off.

Heatran: Between its Steel / Fire typing and Flash Fire, Heatran checks just about every Clefable variant, with specially defensive variants even taking very little damage from Thunderbolt, though it has to be careful of Thunder Wave and risks being PP stalled out of Magma Storms between their poor accuracy and the chance of full paralysis.

Utility.description:
Set Description

Clefable is an excellent utility Pokemon thanks to its access to a number of support moves combined with Magic Guard, which grants it incredible longevity when paired with Soft-Boiled's instant recovery, since it can't be worn down by passive damage. Moonblast allows it to threaten a number of common offensive threats, such as Dragapult, Weavile, and Urshifu-R. Knock Off helps Clefable's teammates make progress by removing items like Leftovers from Heatran and Melmetal and Assault Vest from Galarian Slowking, scaring away potential switch-ins that need their items to check certain threats. Clefable is also a good Stealth Rock setter, with decent matchups against a number of entry hazard removers like Tornadus-T that allow it to safely set up entry hazards. Thunder Wave can be run over either of these moves to hinder Clefable switch-ins like Melmetal and Heatran so its teammates can handle them more easily. Leftovers is used to allow Clefable to passively recover health, while Rocky Helmet can be run instead to punish physical attackers like Weavile and Buzzwole as well as Pokemon like Landorus-T and Corviknight using U-turn to pivot out against it.

Team Options

Clefable fits well on nearly any team structure, providing support for attackers on offensive teams and leveraging its good defensive typing and ability to switch into offensive threats on defensive teams, as well as offering its ability to act as a Knock Off absorber since it isn't as reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots as other walls. Utility Clefable is a generally passive Pokemon and struggles against walls like Slowbro and Blissey, so it pairs well with offensive teammates like Weavile and Choice Band Tyranitar that can remove them while benefitting from Clefable's ability to check Fighting-types and slow down opposing offensive Pokemon. Steel-types like Melmetal and Kartana easily threaten Clefable, so checks like Skarmory, Zapdos, and Ferrothorn are appreciated. Clefable is also walled by Poison-types like Galarian Slowking, so Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus-T are necessary to take care of them while providing additional offensive pressure against Steel-types. Clefable can be overwhelmed by powerful special attackers like Choice Specs Tapu Lele, Volcanion, and Blacephalon, so special checks like Blissey, Gastrodon, and Heatran are welcome teammates. Melmetal helps Clefable against a number of threats, including Calm Mind sweepers like Tapu Koko and opposing Clefable as well as Galarian Slowking and Nihilego. Clefable can form an entry hazard-stacking core with Skarmory or Ferrothorn, which complement the pressure of Clefable's Stealth Rock with Spikes.

Unaware.description:
Set Description

Clefable's combination of Calm Mind and Unaware gives it a pivotal role on stall teams that have a hard time dealing with common threats like Garchomp and Weavile. Unaware ignores foes' boosted stats from moves such as Swords Dance, which means Clefable can effectively check setup sweepers. Calm Mind should be set up on Pokémon that can not deal notable damage to Clefable such as Corviknight, Slowbro and opposing Clefable in order for Clefable to act as a threat. Clefable should heal regularly with Soft-Boiled when attempting to wall the set up sweepers it is meant to handle since even when fully invested Clefable has to respect critical hits and high rolls from opposing sweepers. Aromatherapy is often slotted to ensure Clefable can clear away status conditions like poison, paralysis and burns on itself while also removing status conditions from its teammates. Flamethrower is an alternative to Aromatherapy so Clefable can threaten Steel-types like Melmetal, Corviknight and Ferrothorn if that is more necessary than being a cleric. The choice between Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots ends up mattering quite a lot in the matchups Clefable is supposed to take on, as an example Triple Axel from Weavile is a roll to 2HKO Heavy Duty Boots Clefable, while an Unaware Clefable with Leftovers is 3HKOed by Triple Axel. The added longevity and resilience from Leftovers is often preferred for this reason. Depending on team structure, Clefable might be forced to run Heavy-Duty Boots to ensure it can avoid taking damage from entry hazards if the team's hazard removal is not reliable. Clefable should be used to check setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Dragonite, Swords Dance Garchomp, Swords Dance Weavile, and Dragon Dance Dragapult. Maximum investment in Defense and HP ensures it can reliably take hits from these Pokemon, heal, and fire off Moonblasts or start setting up Calm Mind boosts. 12 EVs in Speed allow Clefable to outspeed uninvested Tyranitar.

Team Options

This set is almost exclusively seen on stall teams that require a dedicated Unaware user to deal with setup sweepers such as the aforementioned Swords Dance Weavile and Garchomp, which stall teams otherwise struggle with. It also acts as a wincon for stall teams in longer games by being able to effectively set up Calm Mind. Corviknight is a good partner for Clefable, as it ends up checking threats that Clefable otherwise cannot handle such as Choice Band Rillaboom, Kartana, and Melmetal while also removing entry hazards with Defog. Another teammate that often ends up being paired with Unaware Clefable is Toxapex, which is a Regenerator user with Knock Off that can ensure Clefable can keep up its walling capabilities by removing items from threats such as Choice Band Kartana and Urshifu-R that could otherwise threaten to KO Clefable. Blissey can be paired with Unaware Clefable to check threats such as Choice Specs Volcanion, Dragapult, and Blacephalon that Unaware Clefable cannot switch into or effectively answer. Blissey can also use Heal Bell to give Clefable the option to run Flamethrower over Aromatherapy. Bulky Ground-types such as Gastrodon and specially defensive Hippowdon are good partners for Unaware Clefable since they are solid answers to the common stallbreaker Magma Storm Heatran, which could otherwise threaten to trap and KO Clefable.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Description

Since Magic Guard ignores the passive damage from entry hazards and damaging status effects, Clefable can effectively set up Calm Mind on passive Pokemon like Toxapex and Slowbro. The choice of coverage on Calm Mind Clefable depends on what it wants to beat. Thunderbolt chunks and threatens Water-types like the aforementioned Toxapex while also threatening Flying-types like Corviknight and Tornadus-T. Thunder is sometimes chosen over Thunderbolt due to the high chance of paralysis threatening checks such as Heatran and the fact it stills allows Clefable to hit the aforementioned Water- and Flying-types. Using Flamethrower means that Clefable no longer threatens Water-types but can deal significant damage to Steel-types such as Melmetal and Ferrothorn. The choice between Life Orb and Leftovers is significant, as without the power boost from Life Orb, even Thunder Clefable will struggle to break through Toxapex, which can switch in and use Haze to remove Calm Mind boosts. If Leftovers is preferred, it is generally better to drop Thunderbolt for Flamethrower and drop the Speed investment to maximize physical bulk. 60 Speed EVs allow Clefable to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, while maximum investment in HP and Defense with a Bold nature maximizes bulk against threats such as Weavile and Garchomp, allowing Clefable to set up on them effectively.

Team Options

Calm Mind Clefable is a flexible wincon that often goes on teams centered around stacking entry hazards.
