Physically defensive hazard setters like Ferrothorn and Skarmory complement Calm Mind Clefable, since they check Pokemon like Melmetal and Kartana that could otherwise threaten to KO it while also putting down Spikes, which will wear down its switch-ins like Heatran and Melmetal. Ferrothorn in particular pairs well with Clefable; Clefable checks physical attackers that Ferrothorn can't deal with reliably such as Buzzwole, while Ferrothorn takes pressure off of Clefable by checking Tapu Koko and Galarian Slowking without Flamethrower. Ground-types like Garchomp, Hippowdon, and Gastrodon are beneficial to Clefable, since they check threats such as Heatran and Victini. Hippowdon and Garchomp are also able to set Stealth Rock, wearing down Pokemon that switch into Calm Mind Clefable such as Galarian Slowking and Toxapex. Another Pokemon that pairs well with Clefable is Dragon Dance Dragonite, which checks threats like Rillaboom while also acting as another wincon that takes advantage of Spikes. Swords Dance Scizor is a good partner to Clefable because it can check threats like Tapu Lele while being a threatening sweeper in its own right. Calm Mind Clefable has a nasty tendency of being set up on by Volcarona, so offensive checks to Volcarona like Heatran and defensive checks like Toxapex are good partners to Clefable.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Wish can be used to let Clefable heal up teammates like Excadrill, Landorus-T, and Groudon. Teleport is another option to safely pivot in the likes of Blacephalon, Zygarde-10%, and Kyurem-W, and it can also be used alongside Wish to safely heal up its teammates. Encore can be used to deny setup opportunities as well as allow safe swap ins for teammates. Trick alongside crippling items like Choice Scarf and Sticky Barb can also be used to deal with opposing walls.

Checks and Counters

Strong Wallreakers: Powerful wallbreakers like Tapu Lele and Galarian Moltres can overwhelm Clefable. Furthermore, set up sweepers with Mold Breaker such as Zekrom and Pangoro can break through Unaware variants.

Steel-types: Clefable cannot do much against Steel-types like Necrozma-DM, Zamazenta-C, and Ferrothorn. They have to be careful to avoid switching into troublesome moves like Knock Off, Flamethrower, Trick, and Thunder Wave though.

Utility (Defense).description:
Clefable's good utility movepool and insane defensive profile make it an excellent addition to almost any Godly Gift team. Magic Guard lets it ignore opposing entry hazards as well as absorb status moves for its teammates. Notably, it has an incredibly wide movepool featuring amazing utility moves like Stealth Rock, Thunder Wave, and Aromatherapy. With a Defense donation and its fantastic defensive typing, it can switch into physical attackers like Zygarde-10%, Urshifu-R, and Zekrom. Thunder Wave cripples offensive threats like Galarian Slowking, Tapu Lele, and Mewtwo as they try to take advantage of Clefable and helps slow wallbreaking teammates get the jump on foes. Knock Off can displace items on the opposing team, notably on common switch-ins like Heatran, Necrozma-DM, and Ho-Oh. Aromatherapy can be run to remove status conditions from its team members. Leftovers is the preferred item to run to get more passive recovery; however, Rocky Helmet can be run to chip physical attackers like Urshifu-R, Weavile, and Yveltal.

Clefable is an amazing defensive staple on any team that can give it the required Defense stat. It pairs extremely well with high Defense gods like Necrozma-DM and Groudon; it can still make use of a lesser Defense donation like from Yveltal or Kyurem-W as well. Clefable's ability to annoy opposing walls with status, chip damage, and item removal makes it a great asset for offensive teammates. Thunder Wave variants pair up excellently with slower wallbreakers like Kyurem-W and Rillaboom, helping them break through faster checks. Aromatherapy is appreciated by teammates that stand to benefit from longer games, like Ho-Oh and Gastrodon. Psychic- and Fairy-types like Tapu Lele, Mewtwo, and Galarian Slowking appreciate it removing Leftovers and Assault Vest from Steel-types. Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon like Heatran, Galarian Slowking, and Necrozma-DM can pivot into and force out Clefable, so running answers to these Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Groudon is recommended. Special Walls like Assault Vest Tangrowth, Ho-Oh, and Slowbro are also good teammates to deal with special attackers.

Unaware (Defense, Special Defense).description:
Thanks to Unaware, Clefable can effectively check setup sweepers such as Kartana, Rayquaza, and Garchomp. Calm Mind lets it act as a wincon and offensively pressure the opposing team, while also letting it set up alongside and deal with special attackers like Yveltal and Volcarona. Utility options like Stealth Rock and Knock Off are viable alternatives to Calm Mind. Aromatherapy can be run to cure it and its teammates from status conditions, helping it outlast checks like Gastrodon and Ho-Oh that rely on Toxic to beat it. Flamethrower can be run to improve its sweeping potential and gives it a way to hit Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Corviknight; however, this means cleric support elsewhere on the team is needed. Heavy-Duty Boots should be ran to fix its vulnerability to entry hazards while allowing it to bluff Magic Guard. Leftovers can be run instead to help Clefable's role as a wincon. A specially defense spread can be utilized instead if Clefable receives a Special Defense donation.

Clefable is a natural fit on stall and bulkier teams, especially when being paired up with gods that have a high Defense stat like Giratina, Necrozma-DM, and Shuckle. Defoggers like Corviknight, Ho-Oh, and Tornadus-T makes for good teammates, as entry hazards annoy Clefable if it gets its Heavy-Duty Boots knocked off. Steel-types like Necrozma-DM and Kartana could prove troublesome for Clefable, so teammates to help against these like Corviknight, Ferrothorn, and Tornadus-T are greatly appreciated. Incredibly powerful special attackers like Mewtwo, Kyurem-W, and Galarian Moltres also prove troublesome for it, so specially defensive teammates like Gastrodon, Tyranitar, and Slowbro can help deal with these. Physical walls such as Buzzwole and Skarmory are mandatory alongside specially defensive variants. Cleric support from teammates like Vaporeon and Audino is appreciated to allow Clefable to drop Aromatherapy for a utility move.

Magic Guard Calm Mind (Def).description:
Clefable can effectively function as a Magic Guard sweeper with Calm Mind and a Defense donation from gods such as Zamazenta-C, Necrozma-DM, Giratina, and Shuckle, making it incredibly difficult to take down after a boost. The effective immunity to Toxic and Leech Seed granted by Magic Guard gives Clefable a niche over its Unaware counterpart, enabling it to avoid significant chip damage from Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Rotom-W, and Skarmory. Soft-Boiled gives Clefable a consistent form of recovery. Moonblast is a powerful STAB move that hits many targets for neutral and super effective damage, such as Rayquaza, Pheromosa, Landorus-T, Galarian Moltres, and Rotom-W. Encore can lock Pokemon such as Zamazenta-C, Galarian Moltres, and Ferrothorn into status moves, while Thunder Wave can effectively cripple the same targets. Aromatherapy fits better on stall teams that require a cleric to keep their teams healthy. Flamethrower is a final option that sacrifices extra utility for better offensive pressure against Steel-types like Necrozma-DM and Corviknight. The given EVs and nature are to maximize Clefable's physical bulk, but can be optimized depending on the god it is paired with. When paired with Shuckle, Clefable can go with maximum HP and Special Defense due to its already significantly high Defense stat. This set also works well in the Special Defense slot with Giratina and Shuckle as gods and maximum HP and Special Defense EVs to better take on Galarian Moltres and special Giratina-O.

Magic Guard Calm Mind Clefable fits best on bulky offense and stall teams that appreciate its longevity and ability to pressure opposing teams with its setup moves. Zamazenta-C and Necrozma-DM are good pairings for bulky offense, as they appreciate Clefable's ability to spread paralysis with Thunder Wave and pressure otherwise annoying Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and opposing Clefable. Giratina and Shuckle are the best gods for stall teams, donating hefty defenses and benefiting from Clefable's cleric ability and its immunity to entry hazards. Clefable struggles versus potent physical attackers such as opposing Necrozma-DM, Kartana, and Pangoro. Skarmory and physically defensive Landorus-T are partners that can check both of those and force them out with Whirlwind and Earthquake, respectively. Clefable also struggles to handle opposing special setup sweepers such as Galarian Slowking, so a dedicated special wall such as Gastrodon should be paired with it to handle those attackers.

cap.comments:
Other Options

Clefable can run Unaware over Magic Guard to counter a variety of setup sweepers such as Necturna, Dragonite, Garchomp, Weavile, and Cawmodore. However, it is usually outclassed by Arghonaut, which has phazing and better physical bulk, in this regard. Additionally, the Toxic and entry hazards immunity that Magic Guard provides is usually worth more than running Unaware. Clefable can run Calm Mind on its utility set if its team needs both Stealth Rock and a secondary win condition, but this set compromises on both sweeping power and utility. Also on its utility set, Clefable can run Sticky Barb along with Trick to cripple Heatran, Toxapex, Equilibra, and Corviknight. However, Trick lacks the consistency of Knock Off and can sometimes neuter Clefable if it receives an unwanted item, such as an Assault Vest from Galarian Slowking. Encore can be run on the utility set to reduce Clefable's tendency of being setup fodder while allowing it to essentially win against any opposing Calm Mind Clefable.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Melmetal, Scizor, Equilibra, and Ferrothorn are all good answers to Clefable, as they take little to no damage from Moonblast and force Clefable out with strong Steel-type STAB moves. Kartana does the same, but takes far more from Moonblast. None of these Pokemon enjoy switching into Flamethrower, however.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Heatran, Astrolotl, Volcanion, Victini, and Volcarona all can come in on Clefable's Moonblast and force it out. Heatran can trap, taunt, and KO Clefable before it gets the chance to setup; Astrolotl can spam Fire Lash until Clefable is forced to switch and is very difficult to wear down; Victini and Volcanion force Clefable out with their nuclear STAB options; and Volcarona can setup alongside Clefable and beat it one-on-one. However, all of these Pokemon must beware Knock Off.

Strong Wallbreakers: Urshifu-R, Weavile, Tapu Lele, and Rillaboom can overwhelm Clefable and not allow it to switch in due to their immense offensive strength. Rillaboom in particular is a threat, forcing Clefable out with a roll to OHKO with Wood Hammer.

Poison-types: Poison-types such as Toxapex, Venomicon, Venomicon-E, and Galarian Slowking take little from any of Clefable's options and can force it out. It should be noted that Galarian Slowking and Venomicon must be wary of Knock Off, and Galarian Slowking cannot beat Calm Mind Clefable in a one-on-one. Moreover, the former three must be careful of getting hit by Thunder from Calm Mind sets.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Clefable excels at providing a myriad of utility options to teams while acting as a solid defensive Pokemon due to its typing and bulk. Clefable is a great user of Stealth Rock, as it can take advantage of free turns versus passive Pokemon like Blissey, Toxapex, and Ferrothorn. Knock Off is the best option for the final slot to cripple Moonblast switch-ins such as Venomicon and Heatran, but Thunder Wave is an alternative choice to paralyze Pokemon less bothered by Knock Off like Venomicon-E, Toxapex, and Ferrothorn. The given EV spread allows Clefable to survive a +2 Earthquake from Garchomp, with the rest invested in Special Defense to better answer Dragapult. Alternatively, if Dragapult is already checked on a team, Clefable can run maximum investment in HP and Defense in order to check threats like Weavile and Pajantom better.

Corviknight and Toxapex are excellent teammates for Clefable, as they can switch in on the physical wallbreakers that Clefable cannot handle such as Weavile, Melmetal, and Urshifu-R. Along those lines, Astrolotl, Venomicon, and Earthquake Galarian Slowking make great teammates, as they can consistently switch in on defensive Heatran and force it out, though Astrolotl must be wary of Toxic. Pokemon such as Equilibra and Venomicon-E can take advantage of Clefable's passivity, so teammates like Slowbro and Zapdos are appreciated for being able to check these Pokemon. Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Equilibra, and Garchomp are helpful for threatening Heatran, weakening opposing Equilibra, and for pressuring defensive Poison-types such as Toxapex and Galarian Slowking; moreover, the former two Ground-types form reliable hazard cores with Clefable by providing Defog and Rapid Spin, respectively. Finally, if Clefable is running Thunder Wave, Hex Dragapult is an excellent teammate, capable of punishing the special walls that otherwise answer Clefable such as Toxapex and Heatran.

Calm Mind.description:
Due to Clefable's excellent defensive typing and good natural bulk, Clefable's Calm Mind set can quickly turn into an issue for the enemy team, with very little being able to meaningfully pressure it once it starts setting up. The final moveslot depends on the team. Flamethrower is used for hitting Equilibra, Melmetal, and Ferrothorn super effectively, while Thunder is mainly for Toxapex, which can otherwise use Haze, and Heatran. Knock Off can be run over a coverage move to cripple Pokemon like Heatran, Equilibra, and Galarian Slowking for itself and its teammates, though this decreases Clefable's sweeping potential. Similarly, Trick in conjunction with Sticky Barb can be used to further maim one of Clefable's checks, though this lacks the consistency of Knock Off. Life Orb is the preferred item, as it enables Clefable to be a strong late-game sweeper, but Leftovers is an option that allows Clefable to be a more effective wall before it sets up. 60 Speed EVs let Clefable outspeed uninvested Corviknight and slower Pokemon like Venomicon and Equilibra; however, one can put those EVs into Defense instead to be a sturdier defensive pivot.

Clefable appreciates teammates such as Astrolotl and Garchomp that can take care of Heatran, which otherwise hard walls sets running Flamethrower. It additionally needs teammates that can switch in on Venomicon-E's Gunk Shot and Melmetal's Double Iron Bash, which Ferrothorn and Zapdos do well. Clefable pairs nicely with Heatran, Equilibra, and Corviknight, which can come in on opposing Equilibra's Doom Desire. In return, Clefable is a solid answer to Zeraora. Heatran deserves special mention for being able to trap and KO Toxapex, which otherwise can Haze stall Clefable if it lacks Thunder. Furthermore, Heatran pairs well with Knock Off Clefable, as it will be able to remove Toxapex's Shed Shell. Finally, Clefable should be paired with a special wall like Assault Vest Tornadus-T or Colossoil to take on special attackers such as Tapu Lele and Blacephalon that threaten it before it sets up.

bdspou.overview: Defensive Clefable is a staple for bulkier teams, as it blanket checks a myriad of setup sweepers such as Feraligatr, Garchomp, and Azumarill courtesy of its ability Unaware. Furthermore, its amazing Fairy typing allows it to pivot into Dragon-type STAB moves from the aforementioned Garchomp, Latias, and Dragonite, forcing them out. With Thunder Wave to debilitate the likes of Heatran or Flamethrower to punish other Steel-types, Clefable isn't easy to safely pivot into. Its access to utility moves such as Wish, Aromatherapy, and Stealth Rock makes it extremely customizable to support a team's needs. Calm Mind also turns it into a solid wincon for slower teams and makes it overall less passive. However, Clefable's reliance on Wish + Protect to sustain itself long-term renders it extremely passive and easily exploitable by prominent threats such as Magnezone and Nidoking. Furthermore, its overall bulk is fairly mediocre, meaning strong unboosted attacks such as Choice Band Infernape's Flare Blitz and Choice Specs Latias's Psychic completely demolish it. Moreover, it is easily chipped down by entry hazards, which make it a shaky blanket check if the team lacks sufficient entry hazard removal. However, Clefable is hard to pass up on due to its success against a lot of prominent sweepers, and its minor issues are easily fixed by its partners, making it a top-tier choice on more balanced teams.
bdspou.comments:
Other Options

Moonlight might seem tempting as an immediate recovery option that doesn’t require Protect; however, its extremely limited PP makes it detrimental long-term. A Magic Guard set utilizing a Life Orb can turn Clefable into a potent attacker, making use of its amazing coverage options such as Focus Blast for Heatran, Ice Beam for Gliscor, and Thunderbolt for Skarmory. Despite that, being forced to run Moonlight for recovery makes Clefable much easier to overwhelm, and this set loses much of the defensive utility that Unaware brings over Magic Guard. Aromatherapy is an option if teams desperately need a cleric; however, it bothering Gliscor and having very specific usage make it a mediocre option. A set with Stored Power and Calm Mind or Cosmic Power can sweep unprepared teams, but it is extremely matchup dependent, as it is walled by Dark-types and easily pressured by status. Cosmic Power + Charge Beam is a similar option, but it forfeits a lot of Clefable's defensive capabilities and is extremely inconsistent.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Offensive Steel-types such as Magnezone, Heatran, and Lucario easily force Clefable out, but they are easily worn down and the latter three hate Thunder Wave. Clefable is normally unable to break past Scizor, but Scizor dislikes being paralyzed and Calm Mind sets can break past it in the long term. Further, all of these Steel-types bar Heatran fall to Flamethrower.

Residual Damage: Entry hazards easily put Clefable into range of being overwhelmed by the foes it is supposed to check. If Clefable gets statused, it becomes much easier to break through as well, as burn chip damage negates the passive Leftovers recovery, paralysis makes its Wish + Protect much more inconsistent, and Toxic prevents it from stonewalling setup sweepers.

Strong Attackers: Due to its mediocre bulk, Clefable can easily be broken through by powerful wallbreakers such as Choice Band Infernape, Life Orb Garchomp, and Choice Specs Latias.

Taunt / Trick / Whirlwind User: Due to Clefable's passiveness, it is easily shut down by Taunt from Pokemon like Heatran and Gliscor. Trick + Choice Scarf from the likes of Rotom-W also makes it much easier to take advantage of, and Choice Scarf prevents it from consistently healing. Lastly, phazing from the likes of Whirlwind Skarmory prevents Clefable from recovering properly.

Defensive.description:
Set Description

Wish and Protect provide Clefable reliable recovery that can also allow it to sustain its teammates for longer games. Calm Mind turns Clefable into a dangerous cleaner, especially against weakened teams late-game; if it uses Unaware, then it will have the edge against other Calm Mind users whose boosts get ignored. With Thunder Wave, Clefable can paralyze Heatran on the switch, supporting slower threats like offensive Scizor and Breloom that may be stymied by it. Aromatherapy is useful to relieve its team from the effects of status, and it is especially useful if Clefable is using Unaware because these variants hate getting worn down and being forced to use Wish. If another Pokemon cannot run Stealth Rock, then Clefable can set the entry hazard up itself with its useful defensive profile. Clefable also tends to lure in Steel-types like Scizor, which hate getting blasted by Flamethrower. A physically defensive set with Unaware is the standard, ensuring that threats that can boost their attack like Dragonite, Garchomp, and Feraligatr cannot make their way through it. However, a specially defensive Magic Guard set is more useful against special attackers like Starmie, Alakazam, and Latias. Specially defensive Clefable is not completely safe against the uncommon Life Orb Psyshock from Alakazam, which threatens to break through it, but it is not OHKOed and can cripple it with paralysis, which is favorable for the Clefable. Additionally, Magic Guard Clefable absorbs status like Rotom-W's Will-O-Wisp very nicely, and it completely ignores Spikes and Toxic Spikes.

Team Options

While physically defensive Clefable can stuff boosting physical sweepers, it is not perfect against all physical attackers; Life Orb Garchomp and Crawdaunt as well as Choice Band Azumarill and Weavile can still break through it. Therefore, pairing it with other defensive Pokemon that can handle the other attacks that Clefable cannot take is good; Rotom-W is an example that can take many of these foes' attacks. Steel-type attackers like Scizor and Lucario threaten out Clefable well, so checks to them like Heatran for the former and Garchomp for the latter are appreciated. Gliscor is an especially reliable Lucario check and can even soft-check bulky Swords Dance variants of Scizor. These Pokemon are also able to set up Stealth Rock, freeing Clefable from having to do so. Defensive Pokemon that lack reliable recovery, such as Rotom-W and Heatran, appreciate Clefable being able to heal them with Wish. Fast offensive Pokemon like Weavile, Garchomp, and Latias appreciate the fact that they can fall back on Clefable when being forced out by a Fighting- or Dragon-type; in exchange, these offensive Pokemon can revenge kill wallbreakers like Nidoking that give Clefable trouble. Unaware Clefable also dislikes entry hazards that wear it down; Defoggers like Gliscor, Latias, and Scizor and Rapid Spin Starmie can help with this. All of the Defoggers, especially Gliscor, are particularly good against Roserade, which switches into Clefable, threatens it out with STAB Sludge Bomb, and lays down Spikes and Toxic Spikes that cut into Unaware Clefable's longevity. Specially defensive Magic Guard Clefable gives up its ability to handle physical attackers, so teammates like Tangrowth and Skarmory that can do so are mandatory. Tangrowth is a better option against Water-types such as Crawdaunt and Azumarill, while Skarmory is superior against Weavile and Dragonite; both handle Garchomp equally well. In exchange, they can fall back on Clefable to take on Starmie and Latias that would destroy them.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Extrasensory hits Mareanie for super effective damage, but it is quite weak coming from Vulpix's low Special Attack. Encore can stop setup sweepers and take advantage of Water-types stalling out sun turns with Recover. Protect is useful for blocking Fake Out and First Impression, but it also wastes a valuable sun turn. Memento supports setup sweepers like Tyrunt. Will-O-Wisp can punish physical attackers like Onix and Mienfoo, but it is usually better to attack such foes.

Checks and Counters

Ponyta: Ponyta is not threatened by any of Vulpix's attacks and, with Flash Fire, it can even grow stronger by switching into a STAB move. It can also use Flame Charge to turn the tables on sun teams and hit them with its boosted Flare Blitz. Ponyta must beware Hypnosis, though.

Water-types: Staryu outspeeds non-Choice Scarf Vulpix, while Frillish and Mareanie have the bulk to switch in and use Recover to stall out sun turns. Staryu and Frillish must beware Energy Ball, though, and Staryu and Mareanie can be picked off by Eject Pack Overheat sets paired with Diglett.

Trappers: Most variants of Diglett can trap and remove non-Choice Scarf Vulpix, although they cannot comfortably switch in. Eviolite and Choice Scarf Diglett deserve special mention; Eviolite Diglett can take a hit and remove Vulpix reliably, while Choice Scarf Diglett outspeeds even Choice Scarf Vulpix and can threaten sun teams as a whole. Although less reliable, Trapinch has the bulk to take a hit from Vulpix and KO it back with Earthquake.

Onix: Onix takes Vulpix's STAB moves well, OHKOes it with Earthquake, and can force uncomfortable turns against non-Choice Scarf Vulpix by Speed tying it. Onix is OHKOed by Energy Ball, though, and can be beaten if it loses the Speed tie.

Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock limits Vulpix's longevity and makes it especially vulnerable to priority moves from foes like Mienfoo, Grookey, and Trapinch.

Sun Setter.description:
Vulpix is LC's only automatic sun setter and supports dangerous Fire-types like Charmander and Ponyta. Weather Ball is Vulpix's most reliable STAB move under sun. Overheat deals massive damage to any neutral target and can safely bring in fragile threats when paired with Eject Pack. Fire Blast is a notable option on non-Eject Pack sets to provide a consistent attack outside of sun. Energy Ball hits Water-types and Onix. Hypnosis can cripple important switch-ins like Mareanie and Frillish, but its accuracy makes it unreliable. Flame Charge is another option to take advantage of sacrifices and forced switches, especially to avoid being trapped by Diglett. Heat Rock is the best item for dedicated sun teams, while Eject Pack works best in tandem with a single Fire-type teammate.

Both Charmander and Ponyta become fearsome threats under Vulpix's sun and are the main reasons to run this set. Diglett supports sun offense by reliably setting Stealth Rock and trapping Mareanie, Staryu, and opposing trappers. Natu prevents Stealth Rock from being set up, which increases the longevity of Vulpix and its teammates. Timburr is a reliable entry hazard remover in the tier with its bulk and Defog. This set works well when paired with an Eject Button user that can pivot into attacks and give safe entry to Ponyta and Charmander; Trubbish is an option because its Sticky Hold guarantees that the item will work, even against Knock Off.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Vulpix is a fast, powerful threat that outspeeds most of the tier and works as a strong cleaner. Overheat is an extremely strong STAB move that can take out bulkier, unsuspecting switch-ins. Energy Ball hits Water-types and Onix. Fire Blast is a strong alternative STAB move that hits hard when against Koffing's Neutralizing Gas and outside of sun.

Diglett is an invaluable partner for its ability to trap Mareanie, Ponyta, and sometimes Staryu. Trapinch can guarantee the removal of Ponyta. Natu can deter Stealth Rock from being set and preserve valuable health for Vulpix, letting it survive priority moves like Grookey's Grassy Glide. Grookey threatens Water-types and Onix, and it can lure in Fire-weak checks like Foongus to pivot Vulpix in with U-turn.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Flamethrower is an alternative to Fire Blast that provides more accuracy and consistency, but it is significantly weaker. Substitute can be used to avoid status from foes like Pyukumku and Altaria, while Agility helps Ninetales clean better late-game; however, Ninetales generally prefers retaining Scorching Sands.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Water-types like Poliwrath and Cramorant can take Energy Ball and retaliate with a powerful Water-type STAB attack. However, they have difficulty checking Ninetales after Nasty Plot. Pyukumuku is notable, as it ignores Nasty Plot with Unaware and can stall Ninetales with Toxic + Recover.

Ground-types: Ground-types like Piloswine and Rhydon can threaten Ninetales with their STAB moves, but they should be wary of Energy Ball.

Revenge Killers: Foes such as Manectric and Choice Scarf Sawk can outspeed and revenge kill Ninetales. It is also susceptible to priority from Kangaskhan, Gurdurr, and Shiftry if it is weakened.

Status: Ninetales is vulnerable to being worn down by Toxic from foes like Pyukumuku and Miltank, while Thunder Wave from Qwilfish cripples its Speed and makes it much easier to revenge kill.

Dragon-types: Altaria and Appletun resist or are immune to Ninetales's moves and can threaten it with a strong attack or status.

Nasty Plot.description:
Ninetales is a notable sweeper thanks to its access to Nasty Plot, excellent coverage options, and good Speed tier. Nasty Plot lets Ninetales break through bulky walls such as Clefairy with its powerful Fire Blast and clean weakened teams. Energy Ball targets Water-types like Poliwrath and Cramorant and Ground-types like Rhydon, Piloswine, and Stunfisk. Scorching Sands is Ninetales's best move against Qwilfish and opposing Fire-types like Rapidash and Coalossal.

Ninetales fits on balance and offense teams as a mid- and late-game wallbreaker and revenge killer. Wallbreaking partners such as Rotom and Thwackey complement Ninetales; Rotom is able to threaten Water-types and safely bring in Ninetales with Volt Switch, while Thwackey is able to handle specially defensive walls like Pyukumuku and Miltank that wall Ninetales. In return, they benefit from its ability to handle Tangela. Grass-types like Tangela and Gourgeist-S are also good partners, handling problematic foes like Stunfisk and Piloswine. Knock Off absorbers such as Uxie, Cofagrigus, and Qwilfish are necessary to preserve Heavy-Duty Boots and prevent Ninetales from being worn down by entry hazards; Uxie and Cofagrigus can also take on revenge killers such as Kangaskhan and Choice Scarf Sawk, while Qwilfish can provide entry hazard support to wear down foes like Piloswine and Poliwrath. Cleaners such as Calm Mind Klinklang and Alcremie can take advantage of Ninetales's wallbreaking to set up and clean late-game.

Fire teams appreciate Ninetales's Drought ability to summon sun, boosting Fire-type moves for the team and weakening opposing Water-type attacks. A coveted move in Nasty Plot lets it shred apart opposing teams and take up the role of a wallbreaker too. Its access to a strong Grass-type move in Solar Beam, which charges in one turn when sun is up, lets it take care of Rock-, Water-, and Ground-types such as Rhyperior, Jellicent, and Gastrodon. With Nasty Plot and Extrasensory, Ninetales is also able to deal with Toxapex, which can otherwise stomach hits from it. Hypnosis is an option over Extrasensory to put to sleep troublesome Pokemon like Tyranitar and Toxapex on a predicted switch-in. Against defensive teams like Poison, Ninetales should focus on setting up with Nasty Plot to break through the opposition, while against offensive teams like hyper offense Ghost, Ninetales should focus on direct attacking due to the lack of a defensive backbone to tank hits. Maximum Special Attack investment lets Ninetales hit as hard as possible, and maximum Speed investment with a Timid nature allows it to outspeed slower Pokemon that could KO Ninetales, such as Indeedee and Obstagoon. Heat Rock maximizes the number of sun turns, increasing the damage of Fire-type moves for Ninetales and its teammates.

All of Ninetales's teammates enjoy its ability to set sun. Charizard appreciates Ninetales's wallbreaking ability that allows it to clean late-game, as well as providing sun to activate Solar Power. In return, Charizard can take care of threats like Dragapult and Tyranitar with Dragon Pulse and Focus Blast, respectively. Choice Band Arcanine forms a good wallbreaking core with Ninetales, weakening each other's checks and counters. Arcanine also appreciates Hypnosis support from Ninetales to further limit its checks like Hippowdon. Cinderace can swap Stealth Rock from its side of the field with Court Change and threaten common hazard setters like Tyranitar with High Jump Kick. Torkoal can provide Ninetales with essential Stealth Rock support to score easier KOs and keep opposing hazards away with Rapid Spin, as they would otherwise undermine Ninetales's potential as a wallbreaker. In addition, Torkoal can set sun against slower weather setters like Pelipper and Hippowdon. Rotom-H can provide Ninetales with Volt Switch and Defog support; additionally, they can run Nasty Plot sets together to overwhelm shared checks.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

A set utilizing Nasty Plot alongside Blizzard and Moonblast turns Alolan Ninetales into an offensive threat. However, it's typically not worth forgoing the defensive utility to run this set, as it still cannot break through threats like Mega Scizor, Heatran, and Galarian Slowking, and hail teams usually pack more than enough offensive pressure. A set dedicated to setting Aurora Veil can be used on hyper offense teams, as Alolan Ninetales can provide immediate dual screens support unlike other Pokemon, which have to set Light Screen and Reflect separately, but it is generally a much worse dual screens setter than Tapu Koko and Grimmsnarl, as it has no way to prevent Defog. Hypnosis is another option to punish switch-ins and provide opportunities for teammates to switch in for free, but it is highly inconsistent, and forgoing another support option is usually not worth it.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Alolan Ninetales is unable to threaten Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, Melmetal, and Corviknight out, and all of them either use it as setup fodder or threaten a heavy hit on whatever switches in. Ferrothorn can take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's passivity and set up entry hazards on it, while Corviknight can use it to generate momentum, bringing another Pokemon in for free.

Fire-types: Mega Charizard Y, Heatran, Volcarona, and others easily threaten Alolan Ninetales out with their STAB moves and use it as setup fodder due to its inability to hit them back. In particular, Mega Charizard Y is an extremely strong check, as it also replaces hail and prevents Alolan Ninetales from setting Aurora Veil.

Mega Tyranitar and Tyranitar Both Tyranitar and Mega Tyranitar have immense special bulk under Sand and underspeed Alolan Ninetales, so they will always win the weather war and threaten it out with a Stone Edge. If Alolan Ninetales switches out, Tyranitar can Pursuit trap it, cutting deeply into its HP.

Hail Setter.description:
Alolan Ninetales is the tier's only viable Hail setter, functioning as a strong support member on Hail teams while providing a solid resistance to Dark to help with Ash-Greninja. It can set hail throughout the game because of its respectable Speed tier that lets it outspeed the likes of Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Landorus-T and its good support movepool that consists of options such as Pain Split and Aurora Veil. However, Alolan Ninetales is extremely weak and has terrible bulk, which is further exacerbated by its horrid Stealth Rock weakness. Furthermore, its extreme passivity allows threats such as Mega Medicham and Heatran to switch in for free. Aurora Veil allows Alolan Ninetales to provide increased opportunities to switch in for teammates like Arctozolt, as well as let partners like Volcanion and Corviknight more comfortably check threats such as Heatran and Mega Medicham. Pain Split serves the dual purpose of providing Alolan Ninetales with a form of recovery to aid its poor longevity so that it can more consistently provide Hail support and wearing down bulkier teams due to its low HP stat. Encore prevents threats like Mega Latias and Clefable from taking advantage of its passivity, as well as letting teammates like Arctozolt, Volcanion, and Mega Diancie switch in unpunished. Freeze-Dry is a solid STAB option that allows Alolan Ninetales to threaten Ground- and Water-types and prevent the likes of Gastrodon, Pelipper, and Gliscor from completely taking advantage of it. It also allows you to win the weather war against Pelipper and generally pressure rain teams hard.

Alolan Ninetales works best on hail teams, so Arctozolt is its premier partner, as it can make use of the hail to annihilate unprepared teams. Arctozolt also appreciates Alolan Ninetales luring and weakening Gastrodon for it, as well as providing safer opportunities to switch in through Encore and Aurora Veil. Due to its susceptibility to being taken advantage of by Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Mega Scizor, strong Fire- and Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Volcanion, and Heatran are solid partners. Volcanion in particular checks Ash-Greninja together with Alolan Ninetales thanks to its immunity to Water. Finally, Alolan Ninetales's severe weakness to Stealth Rock basically mandates extremely strong entry hazard control. As such, Pokemon like Corviknight and Mega Diancie work really well with it.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Grudge is an option that lures and depletes the PP of threatening moves, namely Melmetal's Double Iron Bash, but its usefulness is very situational. Hypnosis is a similarly inconsistent option, but it can cripple an opposing wall or sweeper if it hits.

Aurora Veil (Ice).description:
Alolan Ninetales is a crucial Pokemon on Ice thanks to its great typing and utility in Snow Warning and Aurora Veil. Moonblast threatens Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon-types such as Galarian Zapdos, Crawdaunt, and Kyurem. Freeze-Dry hits Water-types like Swampert and Gastrodon. Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to punish passive walls, setup sweepers, and entry hazard setters like Corviknight, Tapu Fini, and Clefable. Light Clay is preferred to get maximum value from Aurora Veil, but Icy Rock can be run if using Arctozolt. A bulkier spread with maximum HP investment over Special Attack is an option to provide more opportunities to set up Aurora Veil.

All of Alolan Ninetales's teammates appreciate Aurora Veil and it checking dangerous Fighting-types such as Urshifu-R. Kyurem can check Fire-types that wall and scare out Alolan Ninetales like Heatran and Volcanion and threaten them with Earth Power. Dragon Dance Kyurem, in particular, appreciates Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil to ease setting up Substitute and Dragon Dance. Piloswine is a more passive Pokemon that can perform a similar role in checking Fire-types such as Volcarona and Heatran with help from Aurora Veil while also being able to set Stealth Rock. Cloyster can get rid of entry hazards for Alolan Ninetales while also chipping Steel-types such as Melmetal with Rocky Helmet and bringing it in safely with Teleport. Galarian Darmanitan and Weavile are offensive wallbreakers that can abuse the special bulky Pokemon that wall Alolan Ninetales, like Slowking and Aegislash. Arctozolt can use Alolan Ninetales's Hail to decimate offensive teams and common checks to Alolan Ninetales like Celesteela and Corviknight. Mamoswine is an option for a more offensive Stealth Rock setter that can help preserve offensive momentum.

Aurora Veil Setter (Fairy).description:
Alolan Ninetales's fast Aurora Veil allows Fairy teams to better take advantage of their setup sweepers. Freeze-Dry nails Water- and Ground-type Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Gastrodon, Seismitoad, and Pelipper, while Moonblast allows Alolan Ninetales to hit Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-type such as Sableye, Hydreigon, Kyurem-B, and Kommo-o hard. Encore enables Alolan Ninetales to lock setup sweepers such as Corviknight, Snorlax, and Centiskorch and defensive Pokemon like Toxapex and Hippowdon into inopportune moves. Light Clay and Snow Warning pair with Aurora Veil to maximize its duration and enable setup, enabling teammates such as Mimikyu to more easily take advantage of it. The given EVs and a Timid nature allow Alolan Ninetales to be as strong and fast as possible and take on Pokemon such as Cloyster and Toxapex. Alolan Ninetales should time when its sets Aurora Veil against other teams with access to weather, as it can easily be blocked if hail is overridden.

All of Alolan Ninetales teammates appreciate its ability to set up Aurora Veil, especially the setup sweepers. Calm Mind Hatterene, Swords Dance Mimikyu, Bulk Up Grimmsnarl, and Nasty Plot Togekiss are the team's setup sweepers that can take advantage of Aurora Veil, allowing them to tank hits with more ease and making setting up easier. Hatterene also can bounce back entry hazards for Alolan Ninetales thanks to Magic Bounce, which also allows it to keep up Aurora Veil against Defog users such as Galarian Weezing and Pelipper. Other teammates such as Gardevoir and Primarina appreciate the Aurora Veil, as it allows them to spam their attacks with little drawback. Gardevoir especially helps Alolan Ninetales, as it can take advantage of opposing weather teams thanks to Trace and its Choice Scarf to revenge kill their sweepers with ease, such as Excadrill and Barraskewda. Clefable is another support Pokemon available to Aurora Veil teams, being able to support them with Thunder Wave and Healing Wish or set up Stealth Rock, allowing its teammates to break through the foe's team with more ease. Stealth Rock also allows Alolan Ninetales to at least 2HKO all Pokemon in the Water matchup, such as taking out Toxapex with Freeze-Dry and OHKOing Cloyster with Moonblast. Pokemon such as Grimmsnarl can take on Pokemon that can beat Ninetales such as Jirachi and Gengar with Sucker Punch, and Togekiss can tank attacks from Choice Scarf users that take can OHKO Alolan Ninetales such as Duraludon and paralyze them with Thunder Wave. Lastly, Ribombee's Sticky Web allows Alolan Ninetales to outspeed Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion, Dracovish, and Duraludon.

doublesou.overview: Thanks to it being the fastest Pokemon with access to Snow Warning, Alolan Ninetales is the preferred weather setter on hail teams. Its high Speed is particularly important, as it allows Alolan Ninetales to set Aurora Veil before attackers such as Kyurem-B and Heatran can attack, making it significantly easier to set. Alolan Ninetales's Speed also allows to outspeed and threaten Landorus with Blizzard, which also deals a considerable amount of damage to Pokemon like Rillaboom and Naganadel. However, Alolan Ninetales lacks any significant defensive utility due to its poor defensive typing and meager bulk, neither of which are attributes that a Pokemon that needs to be switching in to reset the weather would want. Other weathers removing hail also significantly hurt Alolan Ninetales due to its heavy reliance on hail. On top of that, its mediocre Special Attack allows Heatran and Volcanion, among other Pokemon that resist its attacks, to come in with minimal risk. Due to these flaws, Alolan Ninetales is restricted to hail teams that can make up for its lackluster offense, with Landorus and Urshifu-R beating the Fire- and Steel-types that threaten Alolan Ninetales and Kyurem taking advantage of hail with its own Blizzard. Alolan Ninetales can also be used on certain setup spam teams, thanks to Aurora Veil allowing Pokemon such as Dragon Dance Kyurem-B and Shift Gear Genesect to set up more easily.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Icy Wind allows Alolan Ninetales to provide speed control for its teammates, a role it can perform quite well thanks to its high Speed. However, Icy Wind far worse than Encore and Moonblast across the board thanks to the prominence of Trick Room teams and it leaving Alolan Ninetales worse off against Kyurem-B and Urshifu-R.

Hail Setter.description:
• Blizzard is Alolan Ninetales's best attacking move and a strong spread move in itself, hitting common Pokemon like Rillaboom and Landorus.

  • Encore gives Alolan Ninetales the ability to punish Pokemon using Fake Out and Protect, while Moonblast allows it to OHKO Urshifu-R and deal a decent amount of damage to Kyurem-B.

  • Aurora Veil reduces the amount of damage Alolan Ninetales's teammates take, which can make attackers like Urshifu-R and Kyurem much harder to handle.

  • Protect can stall out Trick Room and Tailwind turns and allow a teammate to switch in to support Alolan Ninetales while keeping it safe.

  • Light Clay extends how long Aurora Veil is active, reducing how often Alolan Ninetales is required to set it in a game.

  • Snow Warning allows Aurora Veil to be used and makes Blizzard perfectly accurate for Alolan Ninetales and Kyurem.

  • A Timid nature is needed to outspeed Landorus and Urshifu-R so that Alolan Ninetales can either set Aurora Veil before they attack or offensively check them.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Blizzard can be used over Encore to enable Alolan Ninetales to nab an OHKO on Mega Pinsir; however, without Encore, it cannot force setup sweepers such as Bisharp and hazard settlers like Galarian Corsola to lock into uility moves. Heavy-Duty Boots is a niche option to avoid taking Stealth Rock damage. Choice Scarf is another option that enables Alolan Ninetales to outpace Mega Lopunny, Mega Gallade, and Choice Scarf Terrakion, but this means fewer turns of Aurora Veil and making it harder for setup sweepers like Alolan Sandslash and Cloyster to setup.

Checks and Counters

Ice

Steel-types: Alolan Ninetales has trouble dealing with Steel-types like Mega Scizor, Jirachi, and Excadrill due to resisting both of Alolan Ninetales's moves and can take care of it with Bullet Punch and Iron Head.

Super Effective Attacks: Fire-types like Mega Charizard X, Blacephalon, and Cinderace are able to tank any of Alolan Ninetales attacks and OHKO it. Mega Charizard Y and Torkoal can also prevent Aurora Veil from being set up thanks to Drought. Fast Rock-types like Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Diancie are able to OHKO Alolan Ninetales with their STAB attacks. Poison-types like Gengar are able to OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Sludge Wave.

Special Walls: Special Defensive walls such as Blissey and Empoleon can take any of Alolan Ninetales attacks, and take care of it with their attacks or using Toxic.

Stealth Rock: Alolan Ninetales is greatly hindered by Stealth Rock, which limits the times it can switch in to provide hail and Aurora Veil.

Revenge Killers: Fast Pokemon like Mega Lopunny and Mega Gallade along with Choice Scarf users like Greninja, Terrakion, and Excadrill can easily outpace and take care of Alolan Ninetales.

Aurora Veil (Ice).description:
Alolan Ninetales is a great asset to Ice-type teams due to summoning hail and using Aurora Veil to allow its teammates to take less damage from attacks. Alolan Ninetales's Fairy typing is good to threaten Fighting- and Dark-types like Keldeo and Mega Sableye with STAB Moonblast, and it has a great Speed tier to outpace Pokemon such as Keldeo and Terrakion. Freeze-Dry is used to hit Water-types such as Swampert, Pelipper, Mantine, and Gastrodon. Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to lock entry hazard settlers and setup sweepers like Galarian Corsola, Torkoal, and Bisharp into non-damaging moves. Light Clay is used to maintain Aurora Veil for eight turns, and Snow Warning is needed to summon hail. 252 Special Attack EVs make Alolan Ninetales hit as hard as possible. A Timid nature with 252 Speed EVs is vital for Alolan Ninetales to outpace Keldeo and Hydreigon.

All teammates appreciate Alolan Ninetales providing Aurora Veil to help take attacks and its Moonblast threatening Keldeo and Terrakion. Alolan Sandslash loves Alolan Ninetales summoning hail to enable Slush Rush, allowing it to outpace Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Diancie. Alolan Ninetales in return can take care of Landorus and Nidoking outside hail. Avalugg is a great wall that can come in on Excadrill's and Bisharp's attacks and take care of them with Body Press. It can also use Rapid Spin to get rid of entry hazards that prevent Alolan Ninetales from repeatedly coming in. Cloyster is a great partner, as it loves the support from Aurora Veil to safety set up and sweep and can take care of troublesome Rock- and Fire-types once it set up, like Mega Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Charizard Y, and Victini. Piloswine is also a great partner that can take care of Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y thanks to Thick Fat and provide Stealth Rock. Mamoswine is another option, as it can also provide Stealth Rock support, takes neutral damage from Fire- and Rock-type attacks and helps against Rock-, Fire-, Steel- and Poison-types like Tyranitar, Heatran, Magnezone, and Toxapex. Kyurem is a great wallbreaker; helps out Alolan Ninetales by taking care of troublesome Steel-types such Heatran, Excadrill, and Magnezone with Earth Power; and helps out in the Water-type matchup with Freeze-Dry to 2HKO Toxapex, which Alolan Ninetales has trouble beating. Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan is a great wallbreaker and a great way to take care of troubling Steel-types like Excadrill, Heatran, and Jirachi that threaten Alolan Ninetales out. Choice Scarf Weavile is a great check to a set-up Cloyster thanks to Foul Play and troublesome Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gengar, Blacephalon, Victini and Jirachi thanks to Knock Off and Pursuit. Knock Off is also useful to get rid of Heavy-Duty Boots from Blissey, Leftovers from Tyranitar, and Eviolite from Porygon2.

zu.overview: Wigglytuff's poor bulk for a defensive Pokemon means it is completely unviable within SS ZU. Wigglytuff is ultimately outclassed as a defensive Fairy-type by Alcremie, outclassed as a defensive Normal-type by Miltank, and outclassed both as a special wall and as a Wish pass user by Clefairy.

WishPort.description: Wigglytuff aims to wall special attackers and pass Wish through Wish + Teleport while dissuading switch-ins with Knock Off. However, despite its access to Knock Off, its lack of meaningful bulk means it isn't worth using in this role, as more often than not Wigglytuff needs to use Wish for itself; use Clefairy if you want a Wish pass user or special wall - otherwise use Alcremie or Miltank.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Despite Golbat's middling Special Attack, Nasty Plot sets are plausible thanks to its great bulk and typing providing setup opportunities. It has great coverage options in Giga Drain and Heat Wave for Rock-, Steel-, and Ice-types. Defog sets also find a place in Golbat's toolkit, seeing it perform as a defensive pivot with U-turn.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-type Pokemon such as Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio are immune to Toxic and resist Brave Bird, walling Golbat without Super Fang and hitting back hard with their attacks.

Electric-types: Electric-type Pokemon such as Rotom, Manectric, and Morpeko resist Brave Bird and threaten Golbat with their STAB attacks.

Rock-types: Rock-type Pokemon like Rhydon, Lycanroc-N, and Kabutops resist Brave Bird and threaten Golbat with their STAB attacks.

Ice-types: Ice-type Pokemon such as Articuno, Jynx, and Piloswine threaten Golbat with their super effective STAB attacks. Jynx, however, cannot switch into Brave Bird without the risk of being OHKOed.

Stallbreaker.description:
Thanks to its fantastic Eviolite-boosted bulk, defensive typing, and utility moves, Golbat functions as a great stallbreaker. Toxic, Taunt, and a Toxic immunity allow Golbat to easily shut down common passive walls such as Miltank and Altaria. Super Fang hits Steel-types, which are immune to Toxic, such as Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio. Brave Bird instead allows Golbat to hit Thwackey and Sawk harder, in addition to being able to KO Poison-types such as Skuntank and Silvally-Poison. The EV spread enables Golbat to outspeed Qwilfish, Cramorant, and Sawk.

Golbat is best used on stall and bulky offense teams looking for a Pokemon to help check Fighting- and Grass-types. Stealth Rock setters like Miltank, Rhydon, and Stunfisk all benefit from Golbat's presence to handle these types, with Rhydon and Stunfisk handling Electric-types and Miltank providing Heal Bell support. Late-game cleaners such as Thwackey, Sawk, and Rotom appreciate Super Fang wearing down walls. Steel-types such as Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio make great partners, covering Golbat's Rock, Psychic, and Ice weaknesses. As Golbat is reliant on Eviolite for its bulk, Pokemon that can take a Knock Off such as Gourgeist-XL and Silvally formes are appreciated. Entry hazard removers such as Articuno, Altaria, and Kabutops compensate for Eviolite barring Golbat from running Heavy-Duty Boots.

Physically Defensive.description: Vileplume's reliable bulk and good defensive typing allow it to act as a switch-in to common threats in RU such as Mimikyu and Raikou, while its ability Effect Spore lets it potentially punish contact moves, especially U-turn from the likes of Flygon and Heliolisk. Unfortunately, Vileplume can get worn down quickly and is often forced to use its recovery to remain healthy, which gives openings to Pokemon it invites in like Chandelure and common Flying-types such as Noivern and Togekiss. Strength Sap is Vileplume's main recovery move and allows it to lower the Attack stat of an opposing physical attacker. Corrosive Gas is used to remove important items such as Leftovers, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Choice items from Pokemon such as Registeel, Crobat, and Toxtricity. Alternatively, Sleep Powder can be used to put common switch-ins such as Crobat and Noivern to sleep, generating free turns for itself and its teammates. An alternative EV spread of 252 HP / 144 Def / 112 SpD can be used to avoid a 4HKO from Xurkitree's Thunderbolt. Vileplume is best suited for balance teams that need a check for prominent physical attackers such as Sharpedo and Mimikyu. Due to Vileplume's weakness to Fire-types, bulky Water-types such as Suicune and Milotic can be great teammates. In return, Vileplume can handle offensive Electric-types such as Xurkitree and Raikou. Since Vileplume often invites in Flying-types like Crobat and Tornadus, checks to these Pokemon such as Xurkitree and Raikou are good partners. Registeel and Steelix also make great teammates for Vileplume, since they are able to check offensive Psychic-types such as Gardevoir. Since Vileplume often switches into pivots, taking damage from entry hazards can quickly wear it down and limit its defensive capabilities, so entry hazard removal from Starmie or Crobat is important.

nu.overview: With its great typing, amazing bulk, and numerous utility options, Vileplume acts as a check to common Pokemon in the tier such as Silvally-Ground, Dhelmise, and Guzzlord. Its great Poison / Grass typing and reliable recovery options make it difficult for opposing teams to wear down. With Effect Spore, it has a chance to passively punish physical attackers and pivots. Vileplume's natural strength and unique combination of STAB moves in Giga Drain and Sludge Bomb make it difficult to switch into. Vileplume can also serve as a great tool against bulky Steel-types like Copperajah and Stakataka, as Corrosive Gas removes their held items and Sleep Powder puts them to sleep. However, Vileplume is slow and vulnerable to Psychic- and Fire-types as well as strong special attackers such as Choice Specs Guzzlord, Galarian Articuno, and Exploud. Vileplume is also easily worn down by entry hazards, and it has difficulty switching into strong physical wallbreakers like Golurk and Tyrantrum.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Leech Seed inflicts residual damage on opposing Pokemon and gives Vileplume an option for more recovery. While having less PP than Leech Seed, Synthesis gives Vileplume consistent recovery. Moonblast can put out some extra damage on Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon-types like Passimian and Guzzlord. Aromatherapy can be used if the team needs a cleric option. Growth can turn Vileplume into a wincon late-game at the cost of its utility in Corrosive Gas or Sleep Powder.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Psychic-types such as Starmie and Galarian Articuno threaten Vileplume with Psychic or Hurricane. They can force out Vileplume, but none of them want to get poisoned by Sludge Bomb.

Flying-types: Aerodactyl can dish out huge damage with Dual Wingbeat. Ninjask and Braviary resist Giga Drain, and Braviary also gains a Defiant boost from Strength Sap. However, all of them have to be wary about switching into Sludge Bomb and getting poisoned.

Fire-types: Salazzle and Swords Dance Talonflame can threaten out Vileplume with their strong STAB options, but switching into Corrosive Gas is problematic, as it removes their Heavy-Duty Boots.

Strong Wallbreakers: Choice Band users such as Tyrantrum and Golurk threaten Vileplume with Head Smash and Earthquake, respectively. Alolan Exeggutor, Guzzlord, and Exploud threaten Vileplume with their STAB moves and coverage.

Strength Sap Blockers: Xatu and Espeon can both block Vileplume's recovery from Strength Sap with Magic Bounce, limiting its ability to switch into Passimian and Silvally-Ground.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Strength Sap is one of Vileplume's biggest assets to check Pokemon like Copperajah and Stakataka. Corrosive Gas removes the item of common switch-ins like Escavalier, Copperajah, and Salazzle. Alternatively, Sleep Powder can be used to put common switch-ins to sleep, making it safer for Vileplume to switch out on them. Black Sludge gives Vileplume extra recovery, but running no item is better for checking Knock Off and Poltergeist users like Drapion and Golurk.

Vileplume is weak to Flying-types, so Steel- and Rock-types such as Stakataka, Copperajah, and Diancie that can check Talonflame and Braviary are appreciated. In return, Vileplume can check Rotom-C, Decidueye, and Vaporeon for them. Vileplume struggles against strong Psychic-types such as Starmie and Galarian Articuno; therefore, partners like Escavalier and Copperajah are great. Vileplume in return checks Fighting-types such as Passimian for them. Vileplume dislikes Fire-types like Salazzle, so Mantine and Vaporeon are great partners for it. Vileplume and Guzzlord form a great core, since they are able to wall physical and special attackers while canceling out each other's weaknesses; Vileplume helps with Fighting- and Fairy-types, and Guzzlord helps with Psychic-types. Offensive teammates like Silvally-Ground and Starmie both target Poison-types and Arcanine, which Vileplume has trouble with.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Lead Diglett is an option on hyper offense teams as a lead that can guarantee Stealth Rock and Memento. Choice Scarf Diglett outspeeds the entire metagame, including +2 Porygon, +1 Tyrunt, and +1 Ponyta, and can be used as a backstop against opposing Diglett and other fast threats with Final Gambit.

Checks and Counters

Grookey: Grookey only fears the rare Sludge Bomb and can punish Diglett's presence with its hard-hitting STAB moves, Knock Off, U-turn, and Swords Dance, all of which can grant momentum and force difficult predictions. Grassy Terrain also severely weakens Earthquake and can make trapping difficult.

Opposing Arena Trap Users: Opposing Diglett and Trapinch can take out Diglett before it traps its main target, and thus it must be deployed carefully when facing them to maximize its value.

Bulky Pokemon: Bulky threats like healthy Mienfoo, Porygon, and Staryu can take advantage of Diglett after a trap, tolerating its attacks to garner momentum and force hard predictions.

Air Balloon.description:
Air Balloon Diglett can guarantee the removal of dangerous threats and defensive stalwarts like Ponyta, Focus Sash Abra, and Mareanie while eluding opposing Arena Trap users with Air Balloon. Air Balloon also allows it to trap opposing Diglett. Final Gambit is a powerful option that sacrifices Diglett to guarantee KOs on low-health foes. Beat Up KOes Focus Sash Abra with five hits and hits Galarian Ponyta and Natu hard while Diglett's teammates are healthy. Rock Slide nails both Larvesta and Natu. Substitute can be used to more reliably trap Pawniard, while Sucker Punch provides priority to teams that lack it. Diglett can run Stealth Rock, but it will rarely find turns to set it up due to its frailty. Protect is a notable option that blocks Mienfoo's Fake Out and Trapinch's First Impression, letting Diglett preserve its Air Balloon.

Air Balloon Diglett works best with teammates that fear opposing Diglett like Ponyta and Abra without Shed Shell, and, against non-Air Balloon Diglett, it can punish the opponent for trapping one of these threats by counter-trapping their Diglett. Diglett removing important defensive Pokemon like Pawniard and Mareanie is also beneficial to Abra, Porygon, and Mienfoo. Mienfoo can force in targets like Mareanie and bring in Diglett safely to trap them with U-turn. Arena Trap means Diglett does not have traditional counters, but Grookey can heavily punish Diglett after it traps a foe, and Shed Shell Abra can evade Arena Trap. Bulky Poison-types like Koffing and Foongus, as well as Natu, can cover the Grookey matchup, while Frillish, Ferroseed, and Pawniard can slow down Abra.

Eviolite.description:
Eviolite Diglett trades the flexibility of Air Balloon and the power of Life Orb for bulk and reliability, as Eviolite lets it take a hit from foes like Mareanie, Pawniard, and non-Life Orb Abra and Diglett to secure a KO. Beat Up KOes Focus Sash Abra with five hits and threatens Galarian Ponyta and Natu while Diglett's teammates are healthy. Final Gambit trades Diglett for a KO or major damage against bulky foes like Ferroseed. Memento can aid setup sweepers, especially Dragon Dance Tyrunt. Rock Slide nails both Larvesta and Natu. Stealth Rock is an option for role compression, and Diglett's ability to trap its foes prevents Natu from blocking Stealth Rock. Earth Power helps Diglett trap foes like Mareanie and Ponyta while Grassy Terrain is active. The given investment in Special Defense helps Diglett more reliably trap threats like Abra.

Eviolite Diglett works well with teams that want to guarantee a KO against a foe that other sets cannot reliably defeat, including Pawniard for hard hitters like Abra, Porygon, and Calm Mind or Cosmic Power Natu. This set works in tandem with Salac Berry Magnemite, as it reliably sets Stealth Rock while being able to switch into Ferroseed's Giga Drain, letting it use Memento to secure Magnemite's trap and setup. This set is vulnerable to Grookey, which does heavy damage to Diglett and forces it out, and to opposing Arena Trap users, especially Trapinch. Bulky Poison-types like Koffing and Foongus, along with Natu, cover the matchup against Grookey, while Grookey itself or Staryu can take advantage of Trapinch.

Life Orb.description:
Life Orb Diglett accepts maximum frailty in return for maximum power, and its sheer strength allows it to trap a wide array of enemies without Eviolite, even including chipped Mienfoo and Foongus. Earthquake is very powerful with Life Orb, while Beat Up KOes Focus Sash Abra in four hits and threatens Galarian Ponyta, Natu, and Frillish while Diglett's teammates are healthy. Substitute allows Diglett to avoid Pawniard's Sucker Punch to reliably trap it. Rock Slide hits Natu and Larvesta, while Sucker Punch can KO Grookey and Choice Scarf users like Porygon and Vulpix at low health. Protect blocks Mienfoo's Fake Out and Trapinch's First Impression, and hitting Trapinch with Earthquake before fainting can be invaluable to limiting the threat it poses to the rest of the team. Sludge Bomb is notable for its ability to weaken Grookey, one of Diglett's better checks.

Life Orb Diglett can threaten almost any defensive core with its power, but teammates like Mienfoo, Porygon, Abra, and Natu especially benefit from its ability to remove Mareanie and Pawniard. This set can also support teams weaker against Mienfoo because Diglett can trap and remove it after Knock Off and chip damage. Trapinch and Air Balloon Diglett are the main roadblocks for this set, as they will always trap and KO Diglett after it gets its own KO. Grookey also punishes Diglett, but it must be wary of Sucker Punch when at low health. Grookey and Staryu can take advantage of Trapinch and Diglett, while Koffing, Foongus, and Natu check Grookey.

Special Focus Sash.description:
This set is specifically to trap Grookey. Diglett can use Earth Power over Earthquake to not be hampered by Grassy Terrain and remove key components of the opponent's team, such as Pawniard and Mareanie. Sludge Bomb OHKOes non-Eviolite Grookey and hits niche threats like Morelull. Final Gambit allows Diglett to heavily damage an enemy when it doesn't have to remove Grookey, such as Ferroseed, Porygon, or Staryu. Memento can aid setup sweepers, especially Dragon Dance Tyrunt. Protect lets Diglett keep Focus Sash intact through Stealth Rock if Grassy Terrain is active. It also blocks Mienfoo's Fake Out.

Pokemon weak to Grookey, such as Carvanha, Abra, Tyrunt, Shellos, and Staryu, greatly benefit from Diglett removing it. Grookey itself is a good teammate, as Grassy Terrain can offset Stealth Rock chip. Porygon and Abra benefit from Diglett removing opposing Steel-types, and Mienfoo benefits from the removal of Mareanie. When not facing Grookey, Final Gambit's guaranteed removal of weakened threats like Staryu and Trace Porygon helps out teammates such as Ponyta and Mudbray.

Focus Sash Trapper.description:
Dugtrio serves as a trapper for Ground-type teams with its excellent ability in Arena Trap. Thanks to it, Dugtrio can pick off weakened foes or eliminate problematic threats such as Dracovish and Weavile without allowing them to counteract. Earthquake is Dugtrio's primary and strongest attack. Stone Edge is mainly used to hit Flying-types such as Gyarados and Charizard. Reversal hits extremely hard when Focus Sash is consumed, allowing Dugtrio to do significant damage to Normal- and Ice-type Pokemon such as Obstagoon and Mamoswine. Sucker Punch allows Dugtrio to hit common Choice Scarf users such as Galarian Darmanitan and Dracovish, and common priority users such as Mamoswine. Screech can be used as an alternative to further complement its physical presence, allowing Dugtrio to trap foes more consistently by reducing their Defense. Focus Sash complements its ability Arena Trap, as it guarantees at least one Pokemon trapped from full HP. Dugtrio should seek trapping opportunities to pick off weakened foes or slower Pokemon that it can reliably beat.

Dugtrio needs to keep its Focus Sash intact in order to trap fast threats such as Weavile effectively, so Excadrill makes an excellent teammate for Dugtrio, as it can use Rapid Spin to remove entry hazards for Dugtrio. It can also handle Fairy-types such as Grimmsnarl and Ribombee that either use Dugtrio as setup fodder or simply easily KO it without fear of Reversal. Hippowdon makes another decent teammate for Dugtrio with its access to Sand Stream and Stealth Rock; the cumulated passive chip damage allows Dugtrio to trap more consistently throughout the match. With its great bulk, Hippowdon can also pivot for Dugtrio after it traps and removes a threat and a revenge killer is sent out by the opponent. Mamoswine is a good offensive teammate with nearly unresisted coverage that allows it to punch many holes in opposing teams; this allows Mamoswine and Dugtrio to complement each other excellently. Dugtrio can trap and eliminate Pokemon that were weakened by Mamoswine, while it also can be used to trap fast Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Dracovish to grant Mamoswine freedom. Seismitoad is a good defensive partner with access to Toxic, which can generate chip damage for Dugtrio for consistent trapping. With its ability in Water Absorb, it can also check Dracovish. Rhyperior makes a good teammate for Dugtrio, as it can handle the Flying-types that Dugtrio cannot trap and struggles against, most notably Corviknight.

ubers.overview: Dugtrio's sole purpose in Ubers is trapping Eternatus. With Special Defense investment, Dugtrio is able to take a Dynamax Cannon even after Stealth Rock, meaning it can easily dispatch Eternatus after coming in with a smart double switch, on a teammate's U-turn, or when Eternatus is forced to recover. Reliably removing Eternatus lets strong sweepers and wallbreakers such as Kyogre, Ho-Oh, and Marshadow wreak havoc. Additionally, your own Eternatus can increase the pressure of Toxic Spikes without opposing Eternatus to absorb it. Dugtrio's trapping ability also makes it generally useful for picking off weakened Pokemon, and it has some nifty utility options, such as Memento to give a party member a free turn to set up. However, Dugtrio is very weak and therefore struggles against more offensive builds, and it is generally outclassed by more powerful Choice Scarf users such as Calyrex-S and Galarian Darmanitan. It is extremely frail and relies on teammate support, double switches, and revenge killing to come on to the battlefield. As such, Dugtrio is an extremely niche pick that functions best on teams that are dedicated to sweeping once Eternatus is removed.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band can be used for greater power, and it makes targets such as Blissey and Cosmic Power Eternatus much easier to trap. However, the lessened Speed makes Dugtrio lose a lot of utility against offensive Pokemon, and it risks being outsped by its main target, Eternatus. Sucker Punch can be used for its priority, although it is generally not as useful as the moves listed above. The main target would be Choice Scarf Calyrex-S; however, as a Ghost-type, it cannot be trapped. Rock Slide can flinch and is more accurate than Stone Edge; however, Dugtrio generally needs all the power it can get.

Checks and Counters

Teams Without Eternatus: Dugtrio doesn't have a check in the traditional sense thanks to Arena Trap trapping foes. However, it is almost useless if there's no Eternatus for it to trap. Offensive teams in particular enjoy the opposing revenge killer being unable to significantly damage most of their sweepers.

Draco Meteor Eternatus: While rare, Eternatus that has Draco Meteor can OHKO Dugtrio. Dugtrio could still KO a weakened Eternatus or come in on one that has already used Draco Meteor, but Draco Meteor does severely limit its ability to trap Eternatus.

Cosmic Power Eternatus: If Eternatus has set up Cosmic Power, it will usually have the bulk to tank repeated Earthquakes from Dugtrio. However, Eternatus needs to make sure it has enough HP to do this. Also, if Eternatus is forced to use Recover by one of Dugtrio's teammates, it puts itself at risk of being trapped without being able to set up a Cosmic Power on the switch.

Trapper.description:
Earthquake always 2HKOes specially defensive Eternatus. Stone Edge hits Flying-type Pokemon like Yveltal and Ho-Oh for good damage and has good offensive synergy with Earthquake. Memento is a great move to allow a free turn of setup for one of Dugtrio's teammates. It can also be used in an emergency to stop a setup sweeper in its tracks. For the last moveslot, Toxic can be used to cripple a threat that Dugtrio can't do much damage to, such as Groudon or Zygarde. Beat Up is an interesting option to easily dispatch SubSeed Calyrex-S, which, while rare, can wreak havoc on an unprepared team. Stealth Rock can fit an entry hazard on teams that have a hard time fitting one. Locking into Stealth Rock is not a big concern thanks to Arena Trap preventing a setup sweeper from coming in. The given EVs allow Dugtrio to outspeed +1 positive nature base 90s, such as Zekrom, and always survive a Dynamax Cannon from an uninvested Eternatus after Stealth Rock.

Dugtrio needs teammates that thrive when Eternatus is gone. Kyogre is the most notable example, as Eternatus is the main answer to its powerful Water Spouts in the tier. Kyogre can significantly damage Eternatus on the switch, forcing it to either use Recover or attack; in either instance, Dugtrio can come in and KO Eternatus. A similar concept can be done with Pokemon such as Dracovish, Ho-Oh, and Marshadow. In general, hitting Eternatus with a strong attack to force it to use Recover is the best way to get Dugtrio on the field, as this prevents Cosmic Power sets setting up on Dugtrio switching in. Bulky teammates such as Buzzwole and Zarude provide nice defensive utility for your team, and both have the potential to sweep with Bulk Up once Eternatus has been eliminated. Toxic Spikes Eternatus makes for a fantastic partner, as the opposing team will have no way to absorb Toxic Spikes with their own Eternatus down. Additionally, Toxic Spikes can somewhat help with Dugtrio's weaknesses against offensive teams. Eternatus can also switch into Kyogre, which Dugtrio can attract. Dugtrio appreciates pivots to let it come into battle safely. U-turn users such as Yveltal and Corviknight and Teleport users such as Blissey can do this.

pu.overview: Alolan Dugtrio's high Speed, high Attack, and Sand Force ability make it a niche option on offensive sand teams. Given a free turn, Alolan Dugtrio massively threatens many tier staples such as Gigalith, Charizard, and Ribombee. However, Alolan Dugtrio's poor bulk limits its opportunities to switch into these targets, and its power, while great, may occasionally come up short against very bulky targets such as Doublade. Additionally, Alolan Dugtrio's very poor bulk makes it susceptible to priority revenge killers such as Thwackey as well as faster threats such as Cinccino and Choice Scarf Gallade.

Sand Wallbreaker.description: Earthquake is Alolan Dugtrio's strongest move and boasts immense power under sand, OHKOing offensive Jellicent and having a good chance to 2HKO Quagsire after Stealth Rock. Iron Head is a secondary STAB move that slams many Pokemon resistant or immune to Ground, such as Eldegoss and the aforementioned Ribombee. Sucker Punch is a good option to pick off faster Pokemon that would otherwise revenge kill Alolan Dugtrio, such as Cinccino and Lycanroc. Memento can be used to help a teammate such as Sandslash set up and potentially sweep. Rock Slide hits Flying-types such as Charizard and Levitate users such as Vikavolt. Gigalith is a mandatory partner for Alolan Dugtrio because it provides sand as well as Stealth Rock to help chip down some of Alolan Dugtrio's checks, such as Cinccino, into range for its attacks. Other Pokemon that pair well with it include Sand Rush sweepers such as Sandslash, as well as Doublade, since it can switch into physical attackers that may try to revenge kill Alolan Dugtrio.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Life Orb Alolan Dugtrio can run all four attacking moves if its team already has a Stealth Rock user, or use Memento, giving a setup opportunity to a teammate. Hone Claws is another option; however, the boost is rarely enough to allow Alolan Dugtrio to break or clean. Beat Up is another option to deal better with non-Choice Scarf Rotom, but it is usually not worth using, as it doesn't target anything else.

Checks and Counters

Physically Bulky Foes: Due to its average damage output, most walls including Poliwrath, Tangela, and Throh can take Alolan Dugtrio's Earthquake at full health and threaten it with huge damage.

Faster Attackers: Due to its abysmal bulk, faster threats like Choice Scarf Sawk and Alolan Persian don't have any problems OHKOing Alolan Dugtrio.

Priority Moves: Strong priorities like Thwackey's Grassy Glide, Gurdurr's Mach Punch, and Shiftry's Sucker Punch remove Alolan Dugtrio after minimal damage.

Flying-types and Levitate: Even if they have to watch out for Stone Edge and don't check it well if poisoned, most foes with a Ground immunity like Rotom and Cramorant can force Alolan Dugtrio out. Altaria is notable for being especially hard to deal with for Toxic sets due to Natural Cure.

Bulky Attackers: Alolan Dugtrio needs significant chip damage to knock out some attackers like Silvally-Dark and Rhydon, which can easily OHKO it with their STAB moves.

SubToxic.description:
Alolan Dugtrio is one of the fastest Pokemon in ZU, which allows it to easily set up a Substitute versus frailer foes it outspeeds and forces out like Rotom-S and Clefairy without Seismic Toss. The combination of Substitute and Toxic allows Alolan Dugtrio to progressively weaken its checks like Poliwrath, Tangela, and Altaria, putting them in range of one of its STAB moves. Protect is an alternative over Iron Head; while this makes it more passive versus Ground-resistant and immune foes like Tangela and Articuno, it lets Alolan Dugtrio recover more HP from Leftovers and, in conjunction with its incredible defensive typing, set more Substitutes. Protect also lets it rack up more Toxic damage and scout for faster attackers like Choice Scarf Sawk and Rotom. Tangling Hair can reduce the Speed of a threat and potentially let a teammate outspeed and revenge kill it.

This set fits well on bulky teams looking for a reliable revenge killer, as Alolan Dugtrio can revenge kill fast threats like Silvally formes and Rapidash. In return, bulky partners like Miltank, Altaria, and Tangela can sponge hits for Alolan Dugtrio, helping it rack up Toxic damage. Defensive pivots such as Uxie, Rotom-S, and Clefairy make for particularly great partners since they can bring Alolan Dugtrio in safely, which it normally cannot do without a slow pivot due to its abysmal bulk. Physical sweepers such as Galarian Rapidash, Silvally formes, and Swords Dance Qwilfish also appreciate Alolan Dugtrio weakening and crippling physical walls, opening the way for them to sweep.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
With its blazing Speed, Alolan Dugtrio outspeeds most Pokemon, which lets it act as a threatening fast glass cannon. Due to the number of switches it can force, Alolan Dugtrio can easily set up Stealth Rock versus threats like Klinklang, Alcremie, and Articuno. Sucker Punch lets Alolan Dugtrio revenge kill weakened foes like Thwackey and Choice Scarf Rotom. On the other hand, Stone Edge lets Alolan Dugtrio nail defensive Flying-types like Cramorant, Rotom-S, and Altaria that can handle its STAB moves. Life Orb significantly bolsters Alolan Dugtrio's power, allowing it to 2HKO Rhydon with Earthquake and OHKO Choice Scarf Rotom with Sucker Punch. Tangling Hair lets Alolan Dugtrio act as an emergency check to other fast sweepers, potentially offering a teammate a revenge kill opportunity.

Due to its average damage output and blistering Speed, Alolan Dugtrio functions as a mid- to late-game breaker, able to switch moves to remove threats. Therefore, wallbreakers that can weaken and cripple walls early-game like Black Belt Sawk, Thwackey, and Silvally formes work well. Pivots pair well with Alolan Dugtrio, providing it with much needed switch-in opportunities. Offensive pivots like Rotom and Silvally formes keep offensive momentum, whereas defensive ones such as Clefairy and Articuno are able to take hits for Alolan Dugtrio. Fighting checks like Rotom-S and Qwilfish are appreciated to switch into the likes of Sawk and Gurdurr; Qwilfish can also form a nice entry hazard core with its Spikes support, while Alolan Dugtrio provides an Electric immunity in return.

lc.overview: Meowth is a niche revenge killer with the combination of Technician-boosted Fake Out + Feint to handle Choice Scarf users like Vulpix, Porygon, and Mienfoo offensively. It can also check frail fast threats like Abra and Grookey. It also has a great matchup against hyper offense teams like sun, Spikes-stack, and dual screens due to its ability to waste turns and cripple frail sweepers. Meowth can threaten bulkier Pokemon such as Koffing and Staryu with Fake Out into Double-Edge, if these have been chipped or hit with Knock Off beforehand, allowing it to threaten bulky offense teams. However, Meowth is extremely frail and vulnerable to fainting if it cannot KO the foe, and priority users like Grookey can easily revenge kill it if they survive Feint.
