Against opponents like Aromatisse, Gardevoir, or Ninetales-Alola which may be using Encore and Disable together, you should alternate between Play Rough and Liquidation to secure the matchup. Specifically against Gardevoir, if put in a situation where Azumarill has a move disabled and Gardevoir can click Encore the next turn without the move failing, Azumarill should click Aqua Jet so that it cannot be forced to Struggle. However, against Salazzle, Azumarill should instead switch between Liquidation and Aqua Jet to avoid being forced to struggle. Against Sawk and non-Choice Band Crustle, prediction is required with using Aqua Jet and either Liquidation or Play Rough to avoid the foe's Counter OHKOing Azumarill.

Stall.description:
Set Description

This set stalls out would-be checks such as Celesteela and Grass types such as Rillaboom, Zarude, and some Tapu Bulu sets. Amnesia and Charm both weaken incoming attacks, eventually letting Azumarill chip foes down with Seismic Toss. Icy Wind can be used over Seismic Toss to beat Aggron and secure the matchup against all Tapu Bulu sets, and Rest provides recovery and removes status conditions, such as Entei's Toxic. Additionally, Sap Sipper gives Azumarill an immunity to incoming Grass-type attacks from foes like Rillaboom, Tapu Bulu, and Zarude, and it prevents Leech Seed users like Whimsicott from taking advantage of Azumarill's passivity.

EVs

The Defense investment allows Azumarill to survive a Poison Jab followed by a Charm-weakened Poison Jab from Choice Band Urshifu, as well as the best odds of defeating Galarian Darmanitan, since having maximum Defense EVs does not change the roll. The rest of the EVs are dumped into Special Defense for improved odds to beat Timid Porygon-Z and Choice Specs Spectrier. Minimizing Azumarill's Attack helps to lower confusion self-damage, which slightly improves the matchup against foes like Galarian Moltres.

Usage Tips

Against Tapu Fini, Azumarill should use Amnesia once and then repeatedly use Seismic Toss. This takes advantage of Tapu Fini's tendency to Iron Defense immediately against Azumarill. By boosting its Special Defense, Azumarill lowers the healing Tapu Fini gets from Draining Kiss, so it cannot outheal Azumarill's Seismic Toss. When facing Entei, you should continuously use Seismic Toss to beat it reliably. When using Icy Wind against Aggron, Azumarill should use Icy Wind turn 1. If Aggron uses Head Smash, Rest should be used until the foe faints from recoil damage. If Aggron uses any other move, Azumarill should use a combination of Charm and Rest to stall out Aggron's pp instead.

monotype.overview:
Fairy

Thanks to its ability in Huge Power and Aqua Jet, Azumarill can act as a powerful physical attacker for Fairy teams. It can run either a sweeping Belly Drum set or a Choice Band set to wallbreak. Azumarill can remove items and hit Pokemon like Aegislash and Slowbro with Knock Off. It can also damage Steel-types like Melmetal and Ferrothorn with Superpower. Due to its low stats and reliance on Aqua Jet, Azumarill gets revenge killed easily by any Pokemon that doesn't mind Aqua Jet, like Zarude or Tapu Lele. Its Speed leaves it slower than some defensive Pokemon like Rotom-W and Mew, letting them burn or cripple Azumarill.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Fairy

Azumarill can run a Jolly nature to outrun Pokemon like Adamant Azumarill and Rotom-W. Play Rough is an option with Choice Band too, since it hits Dragon- and Fighting-types like Kingdra and Keldeo, but it is usually outclassed by a move like Knock Off, which hits more important targets.

Checks and Counters

Fairy

Haze: Pokemon like Mantine can remove Azumarill's Attack boost from Belly Drum with Haze. Unlike other setup sweepers, Azumarill usually only has one chance to set up, since it costs half of Azumarill's health.

Status: All status conditions greatly hamper Azumarill's ability to make progress. A burn renders its attacks much weaker, paralysis lets Pokemon like Melmetal outrun it, and being poisoned forces Azumarill to take even more residual damage on top of entry hazards and often Belly Drum.

Revenge Killlers: Pokemon that can outspeed Azumarill and also survive or nullify Aqua Jet, like Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Bulu—which aren't OHKOed even at +6—are able to revenge kill Azumarill easily.

Psychic Terrain: Psychic Terrain from Azumarill's common teammate, Tapu Lele, prevents it from using Aqua Jet, a key part of its arsenal. This leaves it unable to KO Pokemon like Nihilego, Victini, and Nidoking.

Belly Drum (Fairy).description:
Belly Drum Azumarill is an effective sweeper with its STAB Aqua Jet, which lets it pick up KOs on threats like Thundurus-T, Nihilego, and Zeraora. Knock Off can OHKO targets that comfortably tank Aqua Jet, like Amoonguss, Aegislash, and Gastrodon, after a Belly Drum. It also has the added utility of removing items, like Toxapex's Black Sludge or Mantine's Heavy-Duty Boots. Substitute is used to avoid status conditions and set up on defensive Pokemon like Torkoal and defensive Aegislash when Azumarill is behind Light Screen. Brick Break can also be used, as it hits Pokemon like Melmetal for more damage. Play Rough is an option for targets that survive both Knock Off and Aqua Jet, like Hydreigon. 4 HP EVs allow Azumarill to trigger its Sitrus Berry after a Belly Drum every time. The Speed EVs allow it to outpace most defensive Pokemon like Aegislash and Celesteela. It is a good idea to set up Belly Drum with dual screens active or in front of a passive Pokemon, since Azumarill usually only gets once chance to use it. You also don't want to use Belly Drum if Tapu Lele's Psychic Terrain will still be active, since it prevents Aqua Jet from being used.

Klefki is an invaluable teammate because of its dual screens—allowing Azumarill to set up more easily, Spikes, and Steel typing providing a Poison immunity and resistance to Ice. Spikes support is incredibly important for Azumarill, allowing it to always OHKO Pokemon like Toxapex and Ferrothorn after a Belly Drum. Clefable's utility options in Stealth Rock and Knock Off cripples foes and makes it easier for Azumarill to sweep as well. Tapu Bulu is great because it can beat Electric-types like Rotom-W and Alolan Raichu. It can revenge kill threats like Zapdos and Thundurus-T with a Choice Scarf or break through defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Toxapex with Substitute + Swords Dance. Tapu Koko is a great offensive pivot that provides STAB Thunderbolt and Dazzling Gleam to hit troublesome Water- and Dragon-types like Mantine, Toxapex, Latios, and Kyurem for Azumarill. Tapu Lele can beat Poison- and Dragon-types like Nidoking, Hydreigon, and Latias with its STAB Psyshock and Moonblast. Nasty Plot Togekiss can remove troublesome Poison- and Grass-types like Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, Ferrothorn, and Rillaboom. Other dual screens sweepers like Bulk Up Grimmsnarl and Swords Dance Mimikyu can work together with Azumarill and break down the opposing team. Both are excellent in the Ghost or Psychic matchup with their STAB, super effective attacks and priority attacks.

Choice Band (Fairy).description:
Choice Band Azumarill's immediate power lets it act as an effective physical wallbreaker. Liquidation hits Pokemon like Hippowdon, Heatran, and Mandibuzz. Aqua Jet allows Azumarill to occasionally revenge kill Pokemon like Excadrill, Nihilego, and Victini. Knock Off can remove items like Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokemon, and it also beats the likes of Slowking and Aegislash. Superpower lets Azumarill deal hefty damage to Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Melmetal.

Klefki is an incredible teammate, providing dual screens and a switch-in to Ice-, Grass-, and Poison-type attacks, as well as Spikes, which Azumarill heavily appreciates to pick up KOs more easily. Clefable's Stealth Rock and Knock Off are equally helpful for Azumarill. It also has Magic Guard, letting it act as a status absorber for Azumarill. Its Rocky Helmet allows it to chip down Pokemon like Celesteela, making it easier for Azumarill to break past them. Tapu Koko's U-turn can help Azumarill find opportunities to break through the opposing team. Choice Band Azumarill and Tapu Koko form a good offensive core, as Azumarill can beat Ground-types that come in on Tapu Koko, like Hippowdon and Excadrill, and Tapu Koko beats troublesome Dragon-, Water-, and Flying-types, like Hydreigon, Mantine, and Corviknight. Tapu Lele and Azumarill can break many defensive cores together with their powerful attacks. Tapu Lele can handle Poison- and Dragon-types like Dragalge, Toxapex, and Latios, while Azumarill can beat targets like Ferrothorn, Aegislash, and Slowking. However, Tapu Lele's Psychic Surge can sometimes prevent Azumarill from using Aqua Jet. Tapu Bulu enjoys Azumarill revenge killing Pokemon like Volcarona and Choice Scarf Blacephalon. In return, Tapu Bulu can beat Electric-type Pokemon like Rotom-W and Tapu Koko. It also beats Water-types like Mantine and Seismitoad. Togekiss beats Grass's and Poison's defensive cores with Substitute + Nasty Plot, that Azumarill has trouble breaking through. Bulk Up Grimmsnarl and Swords Dance Mimikyu are other great dual screens attackers that help beat Ghost and Psychic.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Bad Bunny (Huge Power Wallbreaker).description:
• Azumarill is an uncommon but unique wallbreaker in Battle Stadium, with decent bulk, useful dual STAB coverage, and a great priority move to beat much of the metagame that doesn't resist its attacks.

  • Superpower gives Azumarill a way to beat Ferrothorn while providing Max Knuckle Attack boosts during Dynamax, whereas Bounce is used with Life Orb to help Azumarill become a surprise sweeper.

  • The given EVs allow Azumarill to have decent bulk while outspeeding uninvested Celesteela, and avoiding a Special Attack boost from Download Porygon2. The leftover 4 EVs can be put anywhere but Defense.

Items

  • Assault Vest makes Azumarill quite bulky, especially while Dynamaxed.

  • Choice Band makes Azumarill an effective hit and run attacker.

  • Life Orb, while compromising Azumarill's bulk, is the most effective wall-breaking tool for it, making Azumarill a good Dynamax attacker.

bdspou.overview: Azumarill graces BDSP OU as either a terrifying, hard-to-scout Belly Drum sweeper or a strong wallbreaker with Choice Band. Huge Power, STAB priority in Aqua Jet, and a rarely-resisted STAB combination back up its offense, while its Water / Fairy typing helps it switch into prominent Dragon-types and some offensive threats. Azumarill is generally a strong option for hyper offense and standard offense teams, since Aqua Jet is handy in the priority-heavy BDSP OU metagame, and it switches into offensive foes such as Feraligatr, Weavile, and Infernape to quickly wreak havoc. However, it needs support to stay healthy —especially if using Belly Drum— and to handle certain threats. Its low Speed leaves it vulnerable defensively despite its decent bulk and Aqua Jet, and it needs help to pressure the common Breloom and Rotom-Wash, which massively threaten it in return. Azumarill's main set, Belly Drum + Sitrus Berry, also struggles to beat Unaware Clefable, a common defensive glue Pokemon that it can't 2HKO. Still, Azumarill usually only needs one window of opportunity to either sweep or put a dent in the opposition.
bdspou.comments:
Other Options

Belly Drum Azumarill can run an alternative EV spread of 92 HP / 252 Atk / 164 Spe with an Adamant nature. This spread improves its bulk while still outspeeding defensive Skarmory. Facade is a niche alternative to Superpower for Choice Band Azumarill that allows it to still be functional if it is burned.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Defensive Tangrowth can switch into Choice Band Azumarill, but it has to scout Azumarill's set, since Belly Drum lets Play Rough OHKO it. Breloom falls to Play Rough but resists Aqua Jet and outspeeds Azumarill, letting it revenge kill Azumarill with Seed Bomb or Bullet Seed. It can also use Spore and then set up. Shaymin forces Azumarill out with Seed Flare and can stomach +6 Aqua Jet; however, it cannot switch into Choice Band Play Rough unless it has Defense investment.

Rotom-W: Rotom-W can cripple Azumarill with Will-O-Wisp, resists Aqua Jet, and easily threatens massive damage with Volt Switch or Thunderbolt. While Rotom-W doesn't like to take a Play Rough on the switch, Azumarill can only outspeed even uninvested Rotom-W with a suboptimal Jolly nature.

Bulky Water-type Pokemon: Quagsire with Unaware can avoid 2HKOs from Belly Drum Azumarill and stall it out with Toxic barring Waterfall flinches, but it does struggle against the Choice Band set, which cleanly 2HKOes it. Empoleon can phaze Belly Drum Azumarill one time, but it fares much better against the Choice Band set, as it can take all its attacks besides Superpower. Milotic naturally outspeeds Azumarill and wipes out its Belly Drum boost with Haze. Milotic struggles against the Choice Band set, though, since Play Rough 2HKOes unless Marvel Scale is active. Azumarill, regardless of the set, fears a Scald burn when facing bulky Water-types in general.

Revenge Killers: Most offensive threats can damage Belly Drum Azumarill enough that it either can't set up or enters KO range for most priority moves. Azumarill's most notable revenge killers are Latias, and Starmie, which can safely take a +6 Aqua Jet, even with chip damage, and OHKO Azumarill. Focus Sash Alakazam can also check Azumarill in a pinch, being able to deal with the Choice Band set with two Psychic hits, provided Azumarill isn't locked into Aqua Jet.

Faster Priority: Lucario, Dragonite, and offensive Scizor can pick off weakened Azumarill with priority before it can use Aqua Jet. Choice Band Dragonite can even take a Play Rough from Choice Band Azumarill, 2HKOing in return with Extreme Speed.

Belly Drum.description:
This set is designed for Azumarill to clean up late-game or heavily cripple the opposition. Once set-up Aqua Jet is its go-to move for most situations thanks to its priority. Sitrus Berry helps Azumarill beat priority revenge killers and take a hit while setting up. Mystic Water is an alternative to strengthen Aqua Jet and give a small chance to 2HKO Unaware Clefable with Waterfall. Azumarill can set up against a Latias Choiced locked into Draco Meteor or Surf, or on a Garchomp locked into Outrage. After setting up, Azumarill does need to worry about phazers like full-health Skarmory and maximally physically defensive Empoleon, but it can blow past chipped Skarmory and other Empoleon sets.

Azumarill works best on hyper offense teams, where it can immediately threaten a sweep after a turn of setup. This set does get checked by Unaware Clefable, which is a common blanket check for the numerous setup sweepers in the tier, so a teammate like Lucario that can deal with it is great. Azumarill will need teammates that can handle Shaymin and Breloom, since both can take an Aqua Jet at +6 and threaten it with an OHKO. The most important tip with using this set is to, before sweeping, use teammates to wear down or take out Pokemon that avoid the OHKO from +6 Aqua Jet. For example, Choice Scarf users such as Infernape can wear down Starmie, and Latias with U-Turn. Scizor's U-Turn threatens to OHKO those threats and can get Azumarill into the game safely without losing momentum. Alakazam and Weavile both threaten Starmie, and Latias with their superior Speed. Garchomp is another great teammate for Azumarill to provide Stealth Rock and also deal with Magnezone, which outspeeds Azumarill and threatens it before Belly Drum. Azelf, and suicide lead Skarmory support Azumarill and its hyper offense teammates with dual screens and entry hazards. Focus Sash Alakazam, Breloom, and Dragonite are notable late-game cleaners that appreciate Azumarill's wallbreaking ability, which makes their roles easier.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band makes Azumarill a potent immediate wallbreaker with very few switch-ins, which forces frightening predictions. Even Slowbro has a modest chance to get 2HKOed by Play Rough after Stealth Rock. The most notable difference from Belly Drum Azumarill is that this set beats the premier Unaware users of the tier: Clefable and Quagsire. Choice Band Azumarill's fourth move of choice is Superpower, which can take out Steel-types such as Empoleon, Lucario, and Magnezone on the switch.

Choice Band Azumarill struggles against bulky Grass-types. Weavile can handle Shaymin and Tangrowth alongside Starmie, and Latias. Infernape can pivot Azumarill in with U-Turn alongside beating the Grass-types of the tier. Garchomp switches into Volt Switch and Electric-type moves in general, along with providing Stealth Rock for offense teams. Scizor pivots Azumarill in and tends to invite in Heatran and Infernape, which Azumarill performs well against. Rotom-W and Gliscor are notable defensive pivots that Azumarill works well with thanks to their Will-O-Wisp support and Electric immunity, respectively. Focus Sash Alakazam appreciates Choice Band Azumarill bulldozing the opposition and weakening its checks so it can clean up.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Fairy

Azumarill can opt to run Sitrus Berry if a different teammate like Tapu Bulu runs a Z-Crystal. However, Normalium Z is the more reliable way to ensure it successfully uses Belly Drum. Azumarill can also chose to run Brick Break in lieu of Play Rough, as it better deals with Steel-type Pokemon, namely Melmetal, which otherwise withstands any of Azumarill's attacks even after Belly Drum. Substitute may be used over Play Rough in order to let Azumarill set up on Pokemon that rely on status moves to deal with it, like Torkoal and Mega Sableye, but Play Rough is generally preferred due to it hitting useful targets. Return along with a Jolly nature can be used to better deal with Galarian Weezing and Mega Venusaur, significantly improving the Poison-type matchup.

Checks and Counters

Fairy

Water-resistant Pokemon: Pokemon that resist Azumarill's Aqua Jet such as Latios and Serperior can withstand Aqua Jet even after Belly Drum and KO Azumarill with their STAB moves or super effective coverage options. Even many walls that resist Water, like Mega Venusaur, Celebi, and Rotom-W, can outspeed Azumarill and KO it with super effective STAB moves before Azumarill can use Knock Off or Play Rough.

Haze Users and Phazers: Mantine can outspeed Azumarill and remove its boosts with Haze, while Azumarill fails to reliably set up Belly Drum against Toxapex, as it removes the move's boosts with Haze and proceeds to easily deal with unboosted Azumarill. In the same vein, Azumarill fails to reliably set up against phazers like Hippowdon and Skarmory.

Status: All status conditions significantly hinder Azumarill's ability to act as a reliable offensive threat. Burn makes it significantly weaker, paralysis prevents it from outspeeding threats like Porygon2 it otherwise would, and poison puts it on a timer, wearing it down quickly in conjunction with Belly Drum's health drop.

Psychic Terrain: Due to Azumarill's below average Speed stat, it heavily relies on Aqua Jet. As a result, Tapu Lele's Psychic Terrain can hamper Azumarill greatly and make it much more easily revenge killed.

Belly Drum (Fairy).description:
An amazing Attack stat thanks to Huge Power, access to priority in Aqua Jet and Belly Drum to further take advantage of its amazing Attack stat, and a decent typing cement Azumarill as an effective physical attacker that helps greatly in matchups such as Fire, Ground, and Steel. Aqua Jet allows it to deal with faster threats like Volcarona and Mamoswine, making up for its subpar Speed stat. Knock Off hits Psychic- and Ghost-types like Jirachi and Aegislash for super effective damage, and it's able to OHKO Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Celesteela and bulky walls like Toxapex with minor or no chip damage after Belly Drum. Play Rough is a stronger STAB option that deals with Dragon- and Dark-types such as Kommo-o and Mandibuzz. Maximum Speed EVs make Azumarill as fast as possible, outspeeding threats such as Dragalge and Melmetal. Normalium Z is Azumarill's preferred item, as it nullifies chip damage taken prior to using Belly Drum while also preventing Azumarill from being crippled by Knock Off, as opposed to Sitrus Berry. The added perk of Normalium Z is that Azumarill can use Belly Drum without it to use Z-Belly Drum later, either recovering its HP back to full if it didn't switch out.

Klefki pairs up exceptionally well with Azumarill. Klefki acts as a much needed Poison immunity and provides dual screens support and Spikes support, the former allowing Azumarill to set up more easily and the latter chipping down foes for it. Tapu Koko helps greatly in the Flying- and Water-type matchups, while Mega Diancie is able to bounce off entry hazards as well as status moves directed at Azumarill. Mega Diancie can also provide Stealth Rock support, which helps it further improve the Fire- and Flying-type matchups, and aid in matchups like Poison, Steel, and Electric thanks to a wide range of coverage options in Psychic, Mystical Fire, and Earth Power. Tapu Bulu is a great asset in the Water-, Electric- and Ground-type matchups. Tapu Lele is not only a great wallbreaker when equipped with a Choice Specs, but also a great help against Poison-types such as Mega Venusaur and Galarian Weezing that threaten Azumarill. Mimikyu helps greatly in the Ghost- and Psychic-type matchups, dealing with Pokemon like Aegislash and Tapu Lele. Lastly, Togekiss synergizes well with Azumarill, as it deals with Grass-types troublesome to Azumarill, like Mega Venusaur and Ferrothorn, while Azumarill in return deals with Rock-type threats to Togekiss.

zu.overview: Sudowoodo is unviable in SS ZU because it is entirely outclassed defensively by Rhydon, which has higher stats in almost every category, a better typing, and access to support moves in Toxic and Roar. Offensively, Lycanroc-N outclasses Sudowoodo with its ability to handle Steel-types like Klinklang with Close Combat, access to Swords Dance, and higher Speed while also having Sucker Punch for faster foes.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description: Sudowoodo attempts to act as a threatening entry hazard setter with its 150-Base Power Rock-type STAB move in Head Smash, solid coverage with Wood Hammer, and Sucker Punch to make up for its abysmal Speed. Unfortunately, Rhydon entirely outclasses it defensively with better stats across the board after Eviolite, a better typing to deny Volt Switch users like Rotom, and better support moves in Toxic and Roar to cripple switch-ins and deny setup. Lycanroc-N outclasses Sudowoodo offensively with better coverage moves like Close Combat and Iron Tail, a higher Speed stat, and access to Swords Dance.

Rain Setter.description:
Politoed enables a powerful but matchup-reliant archetype in rain due to being the only Drizzle Pokemon in the tier. However, outside of setting rain, Politoed is a generally underwhelming Pokemon that can’t provide much help to rain teams itself and often becomes a momentum sink due to its passiveness. Encore allows it to deal with bulkier threats that would wall it otherwise and discourage Pokemon from setting up on it. Toxic can break down walls in tandem with Encore, particularly bulky Water-types that pose a threat to rain teams like Milotic. Hypnosis trades some effectiveness against passive builds for the potential to shut down common roadblocks to rain teams like Gastrodon and Assault Vest Reuniclus, and maintain utility against more offensive teams looking to take advantage of Politoed’s passivity. Ice Beam chips Grass-types like Celebi, 3HKOes Dragalge, and OHKOes Noivern with the Special Attack investment. Perish Song forces bulky setup sweepers out, allowing Politoed to check Pokemon like Suicune, Snorlax, and Reuniclus. Finally, Rest allows Politoed to continue setting rain when severely weakened and in long matches against passive teams. Non-Ice Beam variants can invest the 76 Special Attack EVs into Defense, as they do nothing significant with Scald. 56 Speed EVs let Politoed outrun Alolan Marowak, but 92 Speed EVs can be ran for Milotic, which Encore + Toxic variants can beat.

Politoed’s only niche is setting rain, so Pokemon that take advantage of it are necessary. Swift Swim Pokemon like Kingdra, Ludicolo, and Kabutops can offensively pressure the opponent and sweep once they are weakened. Electric-types of your own like Raikou and Heliolisk are able to run Thunder and Weather Ball as coverage and check Electric- or Water-types. Tornadus also enjoys fully accurate Hurricane and Weather Ball coverage. Toxicroak appreciates the Dry Skin recovery and can switch into Milotic with impunity. Steel-types like Metagross and Steelix can provide good defensive utility for rain teams and appreciate Fire-type moves being weakened under rain. Finally, entry hazard setters such as Klefki and Roserade can help pressure bulkier cores that threaten rain such as Suicune + Assault Vest Reuniclus, as well as synergizing with the surprising amount of switches Politoed can force from defensive Pokemon.

doublesou.overview: Politoed is one of the primary rain setters due to Drizzle alongside decent defensive typing and stats, although it has lackluster offensive presence. It can often survive long enough to set rain multiple times, maintaining weather control. Attackers like Urshifu-R, Zapdos, Kingdra, and Tornadus take advantage of rain, and Helping Hand boosts their strength even further. Scald burns and support moves such as Icy Wind and Encore give Politoed further utility value beyond setting rain. A major drawback Politoed faces is matching up poorly against a plethora of common Pokemon, such as Rillaboom, Tapu Fini, Kyurem-B, Amoonguss, and Dragapult, among others. The aforementioned teammates, along with others like Genesect and Tsareena, can help this, though. Politoed's relative passivity can also clash with the typically fast-paced nature of rain teams. Therefore, it faces competition from Pelipper as a rain setter, which has Hurricane to deal with troublesome Grass-types and Tailwind, making it more offensively suited than Politoed.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Toxic and Hypnosis are notable support options but require terrain control to be truly effective, as they otherwise struggle against teams with Tapu Fini. Ice Beam trades the utility of Icy Wind for damage, helping Politoed against Grass- and Dragon-types, but it still struggles against the likes of Rillaboom and Kyurem-B. Sitrus Berry complements Politoed's natural bulk, but it is usually inferior to Eject Button or Damp Rock for maintaining rain. Hydro Pump is an offensive option even stronger than Weather Ball, although the imperfect accuracy makes it difficult to justify. Perish Song offers an alternative win condition for when the opponent has only two Pokemon left, but it does little otherwise.

Rain Setter.description:
• Scald is Politoed's primary attack, doing reasonable damage while boosted by rain and offering utility in the form of potential burns. Weather Ball has more raw power at the cost of utility and being incredibly reliant on rain, for instance guaranteeing the OHKO on Landorus.

  • Helping Hand mitigates Politoed's limited offensive presence by allowing it to boost a stronger teammate's attack instead. It also lets Politoed make a move before Eject Button forces it out.

  • Politoed's third moveslot is quite flexible, and which option is best can differ depending on the exact team. Icy Wind provides speed control for teammates, while Encore can lock a foe into a move like Fake Out or Protect, punish setup such as Dragon Dance from Kyurem-B, or disrupt Trick Room users.

  • Protect allows Politoed to stall out a turn, wasting turns of opposing Tailwind or Trick Room, or keeping it safe while a teammate is brought out to be assisted with Helping Hand.

  • Eject Button helps Politoed get off the field after its job of setting rain is done, allowing more offensive teammates to switch in and benefit while saving Politoed to set rain again later. Alternatively, Damp Rock extends the duration of rain, reducing the need to set it an additional time.

  • The given EV spread patches up Politoed's more vulnerable physical bulk to ensure it can survive almost any single attack. This further helps Politoed fulfill its duty of maintaining rain throughout the match.

uu.overview: Quagsire possesses a unique niche in the UU metagame with its ability in Unaware, which lets it stop setup sweepers such as Nasty Plot Thundurus-T, Swords Dance Scizor, and Dragon Dance Salamence in their tracks. A Water / Ground typing allows Quagsire to act as a Volt Switch absorber while also checking Pokemon such as Rotom-H and Lycanroc-D. As such, these attributes make Quagsire a staple on stall teams. However, Quagsire's 4x weakness to Grass makes it unable to check Pokemon such as Nihilego, Gyarados and pivot Thundurus-T, as they commonly carry Grass-type coverage. Quagsire's bulk only goes so far, as very strong wallbreakers such as Crawdaunt and Azumarill can break through it with minimal effort. Finally, Quagsire's poor special bulk leaves it unable to take on special attackers well, leaving it vulnerable to Pokemon such as Keldeo.
uu.comments:
Other Options

A Curse set turns Quagsire into a bulky sweeper, but it will need many boosts before it can cause serious damage and is even more vulnerable to Grass-types. Additionally, it must drop Scald from its moveset, making Quagsire much more passive.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type Moves: Grass-types like Zarude, Amoonguss, and Tangrowth resist any attack Quagsire throws at them and proceed to force it out, with the former two being able to bypass Toxic through Jungle Healing or its typing. Pokemon that can lure in Quagsire and KO it with a coverage move, such as Gyarados, Azelf, and Nihilego, are also threats to Quagsire.

Strong Wallbreakers: Quagsire's bulk is only decent; extremely strong attacks coming from the likes of Conkeldurr, Keldeo, Diggersby, and Necrozma will easily overwhelm it.

Residual Damage: Status such as Toxic and burn hinder Quagsire, as it has to use Recover more often. Chip damage from Spikes can also wear down Quagsire for wallbreakers like Keldeo to KO it more easily.

Unaware Wall.description:
Scald has a good chance to burn threats such as Scizor and Tapu Bulu. Earthquake hits Pokemon such as Raikou, Jirachi, and Nihilego. Toxic cripples Pokemon attemping to set up on Quagsire like Thundurus-T as well as defensive walls like Slowking and Tangrowth. Haze is an option to stop setup sweepers such as Galarian Slowbro and Celesteela in their tracks. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option to avoid damage from Spikes and Toxic Spikes; however, Quagsire is already resistant to Stealth Rock, and the passive recovery brought by Leftovers is generally much more appreciated. The given EV spread allows Quagsire to take on special attackers such as Rotom-W more comfortably while maximizing its physical bulk.

Quagsire fits best on stall teams, stopping setup sweepers with Unaware. Amoonguss and Tangrowth are excellent partners for Quagsire, as they check Grass-types such as Tapu Bulu and Zarude. Additionally, these Pokemon are able to check wallbreakers that Quagsire struggles with, such as Conkeldurr and Keldeo. Chansey forms a solid defensive core with Quagsire, being able to check special attackers such as Nihilego and Thundurus-T, while Quagsire checks physical threats for it in return. Chansey's Heal Bell also allows it to cure status that easily wear down Quagsire. Umbreon can provide Wish support and counter Gyarados for Quagsire. Salamence can help provide Defog support to remove Spikes for Quagsire. Ditto can provide offensive support and deter wallbreakers like Diggersby and Crawdaunt that Quagsire can't deal with properly.

Quagsire is a reliable wall thanks to its typing and access to Unaware, as it can deal with many physical threats and setup sweepers including Mimikyu, Flygon, and Cloyster. Since it has Unaware, it can afford to be passive and purely focus on not getting KOed, which is different from the playstyles of other bulky Water-types like Gastrodon and Milotic. Toxic hits Flying-types and other walls such as Togekiss or Porygon2, ensuring they do not take advantage of Quagisre's lack of offensive presence. Scald is used to threaten Pokemon such as Steelix and Bronzong and attempt to burn physical attackers such as Mimikyu, Flygon, and Cloyster. Despite being immune to stat changes itself, Quagsire can run Haze in order to beat Stored Power Reuniclus, which can otherwise set up and beat Quagsire one-on-one. Ice Beam can also be run in order to give Grass-types such as Celebi and Roserade a harder time switching in. Curse can be used to turn Quagsire into a late-game sweeper; however, it often struggles due to how vulnerable it is to special attacks. Heavy-Duty Boots are used to ensure entry hazards do not cripple it, which is often crucial since Quagsire's natural bulk isn't good enough to take multiple hits at lower percents. Running Haze over Toxic can also be effective, as Toxic isn't often necessary against what Quagsire checks.

Quagsire is primarily used on stall teams because it allows them to not be overwhelmed by setup sweepers. Umbreon is a great partner for Quagsire, as it can tank the special hits that it can't, such as Toxtricity's Boomburst or Chandelure's Shadow Ball. Umbreon also often runs Heal Bell, which helps Quagsire clear any status it might receive from the likes of Metagross, Bronzong, or Raikou. Due to Quagsire's middling bulk, it often cannot deal with stronger wallbreakers of the tier such as Bewear and Guts Heracross; Galarian Weezing is a great choice of teammate, as it can wall these threats. Lucario and Pangoro can both 2HKO Quagsire with Close Combat, so having a Flying-type such as Crobat, Talonflame, or Xatu on the team to eliminate this weakness is helpful. Flying-types also help Quagsire by dealing with Grass-types such as Roserade and Celebi. Registeel also makes for a great partner as it too can wall the aforementioned Grass-types.

pu.overview: Quagsire is seen on stall teams and sometimes balance teams thanks to its support moves, Unaware, and reliable recovery. With Unaware, Quagsire is able to counter many setup sweepers such as Sandslash, Silvally-Ghost, Charizard, and Sandaconda. Additionally, it fulfills a lot of role compression for said teams thanks to its wonderful defensive typing providing an Electric immunity to foes like Togedemaru and Rotom and making it an excellent switch-in to Aggron. However, Quagsire's 4x weaknesses to Grass-types and Freeze-Dry leave it unable to check certain Pokemon such as mixed Silvally formes as well as Perrserker. Furthermore, Quagsire fails to halt incredibly strong wallbreakers like Life Orb Gallade and Choice Band Sawk in their tracks due to them comfortably 2HKOing it. Lastly, Quagsire has poor Special Defense, which makes it struggle against common special wallbreakers like Vikavolt, Choice Specs Mesprit, and Whimsicott.

Unaware Wall.description: Scald is essential for Quagsire, as it burns Grass-types that can switch into its STAB moves like Shiftry and Gourgeist-S. Toxic wears down switch-ins like Whimsicott, Ribombee, and Vikavolt. Curse is another option to provide stall teams with a bulky setup sweeper. Haze is also a good option to prevent setup opportunities from foes like Ribombee and Silvally-Fairy. Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred for its ability to nullify entry hazards, since Quagsire's bulk isn't largely impressive to begin with. Taking 48 EVs from Defense and putting them in Special Defense allows Quagsire to switch into Quiver Dance Ribombee, although it makes it easier to overwhelm on the physical side. Weezing is an outstanding partner for Quagsire, as it provides a Toxic immunity and a switch-in to Grass-types like Trevenant. Audino provides cleric support and appreciates Quagsire's abilities to handle setup sweepers that take advantage of its passiveness, like Sandaconda. Charizard or Articuno makes for a fine Defogger to pair with Quagsire, as entry hazards can severely cripple Quagsire's longevity if it loses its Heavy-Duty Boots.

nu.overview: Quagsire finds success thanks to its great defensive typing, solid defensive stats, reliable recovery, and very useful ability in Unaware. It is used mostly on stall and balance teams to wall a variety of threats such as Salazzle, Aerodactyl, Tyrantrum, and Drapion while offering fantastic role compression. Quagsire doesn't only stare down offensive threats, though, as it can pester many defensive Pokemon with moves like Encore, Toxic, and Yawn. While Quagsire is typically the go-to option to take on setup sweepers, its below-average stats leave it struggling to deal with strong wallbreakers such as Tauros, Choice Band Passimian, and Golurk. Quagsire also has to fear Grass-type coverage such as Power Whip from Copperajah and powerful Grass-types such as Rotom-C and Tsareena, which can come in on Quagsire very easily and force it out.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots can help Quagsire pivot into threats, especially when facing Toxic Spikes, but the loss of Leftovers can make a lot of matchups more difficult than they need to be. Quagsire can viably run a Curse set, potentially even with Ice Punch or Avalanche to snipe incoming Grass-types, although special wallbreakers are far too common, and the set's initial damage output is far too low to be worth it in most cases. There are many other utility moves Quagsire can use, such as Yawn, Haze, and Infestation, but the ones listed in the main set are most useful overall.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type Coverage: Vileplume, Tsareena, Rotom-C, and Decidueye are all fairly common Grass-types that easily threaten an OHKO on Quagsire. Grass-type coverage like Power Whip from Copperajah and Grass Knot from Heliolisk also destroys Quagsire.

Special Wallbreakers: Special wallbreakers that don't rely on setting up can cleave through Quagsire quite easily; Exploud, Sylveon, and Vanilluxe are all capable of coming in on Quagsire and threatening a near OHKO.

Passive Damage: Despite its great defensive typing and ability, Quagsire's stats often leave much to be desired, meaning that entry hazards, status, and item removal can leave it overwhelmed by Pokemon it's meant to check. Some examples of Pokemon that do this effectively are Drapion with Knock Off, Salazzle with Toxic, and Spikers.

Strong Physical Wallbreakers: Pokemon that can muscle past Quagsire with raw power such as Passimian and Choice Band Golurk can be problematic if it is the sole physical wall on a team.

Mixed Wall.description:
Set Details

Earthquake and Toxic synergize perfectly with each other, as the Poison- and Steel-types immune to Toxic are often weak to Earthquake, which allows Quagsire to exert some offensive pressure even as a defensive Pokemon. Protect can be used in favor of Scald to rack up as much poison damage as possible, which is extremely helpful in whittling down threats such as Rotom-C and Decidueye. 68 Special Defense EVs allow it to deal with Salazzle and Choice Scarf Heliolisk more effectively.

Quagsire pairs best with other walls often found on stall teams, which may fall in the face of common stallbreakers such as Tyrantrum, Salazzle, and Drapion. Guzzlord and Escavalier take on Grass-types very nicely for Quagsire and also help make up for its poor Special Defense. Rocky Helmet Xatu and Effect Spore Vileplume can punish powerful wallbreakers like Passimian and Tauros that can overwhelm Quagsire and can switch into Toxic aimed at it. They appreciate Quagsire's Rock and Fire resistances, respectively, while providing additional partners that resist Grass.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This set is for one of the final Battle Stadium Singles metagames for this generation. If you feel there is anything wrong or missing, please post in this thread.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Haze not only lets Quagsire avoid being setup fodder for Stored Power users like Espeon and Reuniclus, but also reliably beats Kyurem-B and Zekrom. A specially defensive spread alongside a Special Defense donation can be used to check special attackers like Galarian Slowking and Galarian Moltres instead, although Quagsire is generally outclassed by Gastrodon in this regard.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Without any investment or donation, Quagsire's special bulk is rather mediocre, which makes it easily overwhelmed by threats such as Mewtwo and Choice Specs users like Blacephalon and Tapu Lele.

Grass-type Pokemon and Coverage Moves: Kartana, Rillaboom, and Dhelmise OHKO Quagsire with their Grass-type attacks. Other foes like Volcarona, Nihilego, and Choice Specs Tapu Koko can often KO Quagsire with their Grass-type coverage. However, none of them like taking either an Earthquake, Scald burn, or Toxic.

Select Setup Sweepers: Dragon Dance Kyurem-B, Swords Dance Pangoro, and Calm Mind Espeon and Reuniclus can easily break through Quagsire with Teravolt, Mold Breaker, and Stored Power, respectively; the latter two are also effectively immune to Toxic because of their abilities. That being said, Kyurem-B and Pangoro have to be wary of a potential Scald burn.

Taunt: Tapu Fini, Mewtwo, Tornadus-T, and Yveltal can prevent Quagsire from recovering HP and using Toxic, making it easier to take down. They also don't mind any of Quagsire's attacks.

Toxic: Some Pokemon like Landorus-T, Rotom-W, and Rotom-H that would otherwise be walled by Quagsire may carry Toxic, crippling it in the long-term.

Unaware Wall (Defense).description:
Quagsire's remarkable defensive typing and Unaware make it a highly valuable piece on very defensive teams. After a high Defense donation, it can wall setup users like Swords Dance Rayquaza, Weavile, and Garchomp and other physically offensive Pokemon like Choice Band Victini and Zeraora. Its Ground typing stops Volt Switch from Pokemon like Rotom-W, Zeraora, and Rotom-H, which helps to prevent the defensive teams Quagsire fits into from being overwhelmed by VoltTurn strategies. Earthquake immediately threatens foes like Galarian Slowking, Volcanion, Victini, and Heatran. Scald prevents physical attackers like Rillaboom, Kartana, Zygarde-10%, and Kyurem-B from safely switching in by threatening a burn. Toxic further spreads passive damage by crippling Pokemon like Ho-Oh, Mewtwo, and Volcarona. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Quagsire from being overwhelmed by entry hazards, which significantly cut into its walling capabilities. However, Leftovers is a viable alternative if Quagsire's team has sufficient entry hazard removal.

Quagsire's defensive qualities and generally passive nature make it a perfect fit for stall teams where Giratina is its Defense donator. Tyranitar and Corviknight can compensate for Quagsire's poor special bulk; the former deals with Yveltal, Galarian Moltres, and Blacephalon, while the latter deals with Tapu Lele and some Mewtwo sets. Corviknight and Skarmory can check problematic Grass-types like Kartana and Rillaboom; they also provide Defog support so Quagsire is less reliant on its Heavy-Duty Boots and can switch into Knock Off users like Landorus-T and Weavile. Skarmory also deals with Swords Dance + Mold Breaker Pangoro, which is one of few setup sweepers able to break through Quagsire. Quagsire checks threatening Electric- and Fire-types like Zeraora, Dracozolt, Rotom-H, and Victini for Skarmory and Corviknight and stops Zamazenta-C, Zygarde-10%, and Excadrill for Tyranitar. Toxic from Gastrodon and Landorus-T cripple Quagsire, so teammates that can switch into them like Amoonguss, Corviknight, Skarmory, and Magic Bounce Xatu are appreciated; Amoonguss, in particular, also absorbs Toxic Spikes. Stored Power users like Espeon and Reuniclus can easily muscle past Quagsire, so Pokemon that can phaze them out like Dragon Tail Giratina and Whirlwind Hippowdon, respectively, make for great partners.

Unaware Wall.description:
Owing to its invaluable ability Unaware and its stellar defensive typing, Quagsire is the most reliable Zacian-C check in the game, as well as being adept at checking Necrozma-DM and Swords Dance Arceus formes and capable of taking on Dragon Tail Zygarde-C. Earthquake allows Quagsire to defeat Zacian-C, 2HKOing it while also damaging Primal Groudon and Necrozma-DM. Scald can be used over Earthquake for a chance to permanently cripple the aforementioned threats barring Primal Groudon, but it is less effective at forcing them out. Haze prevents Necrozma-DM from setting up on Quagsire and breaking through it with Sunsteel Strike while also providing a win condition versus Baton Pass teams and preventing Zygarde-C from freely setting up. Toxic allows Quagsire to cripple switch-ins such as Ho-Oh and support Arceus formes while chipping away at offensive Pokemon such as Mega Rayquaza, Xerneas, and Yveltal that may try to take advantage of Quagsire's passive nature. Leftovers provides passive recovery and is important to help prevent Play Rough or Close Combat Zacian-C from breaking through Quagsire, which it can with minimal chip. Shed Shell on the other hand eases the matchup versus Mega Gengar and Gothitelle, but in general the stall teams Quagsire features on cannot handle these threats regardless.

Quagsire fits best on stall teams that in particular require an extremely reliable Zacian-C switch-ins. Due to Quagsire's low overall bulk, it is vulnerable to many wallbreakers. Lugia and support Arceus formes are good partners in order to help combat physical wallbreakers such as Primal Groudon, Mega Rayquaza,and Ultra Necrozma, whereas Chansey can check special ones such as Yveltal, Xerneas, Primal, Kyogre, Calm Mind Arceus formes, and Eternatus. Tyranitar is also a good partner, as it aids in checking Yveltal and Eternatus while potentially trapping Mega Gengar. Cleric support from the aformentioned Chansey and Diancie is also vital, as with just small amounts of chip damage, Zacian-C can break through Quagsire. Entry hazard removal is especially important, as Quagsire must be able to switch into Zacian-C reliably, and so Defoggers such as Ho-Oh, support Arceus formes, and Giratina are vital, and Magic Bounce users such as Mega Diancie and Mega Sableye are especially helpful for also countering Ferrothorn, which otherwise takes advantage of Quagsire.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Curse is useful in some situations, but Quagsire's standard moves are hard to forgo, and the omnipresence of Toxic in AG makes this set very unreliable.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Common special attackers like Kyogre, Eternatus, Calyrex-S, Xerneas, Yveltal, and Kyurem-W can threaten Quagsire and force it to switch out.

Strong Wallbreakers: Due to Quagsire's mediocre natural bulk, it fails to beat strong wallbreakers such as Life Orb Groudon, Marshadow, and Urshifu-S.

Toxic: Toxic is common in AG and seen on both passive walls and offensive Pokemon. If Quagsire is badly poisoned, it struggles to check Zacian-C.

Physically Defensive.description:
Quagsire is a mediocre physical wall in AG that fits on stall and bulky balance builds. It is outclassed by physical walls such as defensive Zygarde-C, Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Lunala due to its average defense stats and passive nature. However, Quagsire holds a niche as the only Zacian-C counter in AG. Additionally, it also checks Coil and Dragon Dance variants of Glare Zygarde and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Earthquake allows Quagsire to directly damage Zacian-C and chip other switch-ins such as Eternatus, Kyogre, and Necrozma-DM. Scald can be used to fish for burns against Toxic-immune Pokemon such as Eternatus, Necrozma-DM, and Ferrothorn. Haze is an alternative that allows Quagsire to act as an emergency check to setup sweepers such as Geomancy Xerneas, Dragon Dance Zekrom, and Swords Dance Groudon. Recover provides longevity throughout the game. Toxic threatens and prevents strong breakers such as Kyogre, Calyrex-S, Xerneas, and Yveltal from switching in for free. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Quagsire from being chipped down by entry hazards and lets it remain fully healthy to switch into Zacian-C, while Rocky Helmet can be used on teams with strong entry hazard control to wear down and pressure Zacian-C and prevent Quagsire from being too passive.

Quagsire needs a lot of support and is vulnerable to almost every special attacker. Thus, it must be paired with solid specially defensive walls such as Eternatus, Ferrothorn, Blissey, and Kyurem-W. Due to Quagsire's poor natural bulk, checks to naturally strong physical wallbreakers such as Marshadow, Groudon, and Zekrom are also appreciated, so teammates like Lunala, Eternatus, and Zygarde-C are solid options. Offensive Pokemon like Xerneas, Kyogre, and other setup sweepers can take advantage of Quagsire's passive nature and set up on it; Ditto is an excellent teammate to punish the aforementioned Pokemon.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

An alternative EV spread of 252 HP / 80 Def / 176 Spe gives Espeon more bulk while still maintaining enough Speed investment for base 100 Speed Pokemon such as Victini; however, not being able to outspeed Kartana, Blacephalon, and Nihilego can make Espeon more prone to being revenge killed once screens expire.

Checks and Counters

Necrozma-DM: Its exceptional bulk and typing mean it can withstand Espeon's boosted attacks easily. Unlike other specially defensive Steel-types, Necrozma-DM can make use of Swords Dance and Dragon Dance to beat Espeon before it accumulates enough boosts.

Dark-types: A Speed-donated Pangoro, Tyranitar, and Bisharp can outspeed and threaten Espeon with their dangerous STAB attacks. Tyranitar and Bisharp also possess the special bulk and defensive typing, respectively, to withstand Espeon's Dazzling Gleam if necessary, with the former also reducing Morning Sun's recovery with sand. However, none of the aforementioned Dark-types can OHKO Espeon from full without prior chip, especially if Reflect is up. Alolan Persian and Choice Band Weavile are naturally faster than Espeon and can OHKO it with Beat Up, with the former even able to do so through Reflect.

Strong Wallbreakers: Even with a Defense donation and Electric Seed's boost, Espeon is still pressured by strong and fast wallbreakers like Choice Band Pheromosa. Choice Band Victini resists Espeon's attacks and can severely damage it afterward. Prior to boosting, strong attackers like Blacephalon, Yveltal, and Rayquaza can KO Espeon, especially as unboosted Stored Power and Dazzling Gleam do pitiful damage in return, although Rayquaza suffers from Dragon Ascent's Special Defense drop. They can't reliably deal with Espeon if Reflect and Light Screen are up, however.

Haze and Clear Smog: Clear Smog Gastrodon and Haze Quagsire can remove all of Espeon's boosts easily and thus stop it from sweeping. Moreover, Haze's high PP makes it harder to PP stall with Calm Mind.

Trick: Because Trick bypasses Magic Bounce, Espeon can be crippled with a Choice item by foes like Blacephalon, Tapu Fini, and Calyrex-I, preventing it from fully setting up.

Calm Mind (Defense).description:
With a Defense donation, Espeon turns into a potent bulky setup sweeper. The combination of Calm Mind and the Defense boost from Electric Seed makes it hard to revenge kill and simultaneously strengthens Stored Power, especially with Morning Sun recovery to give it more setup opportunities. Stored Power also allows Espeon to muscle past Unaware users like non-Haze Quagsire and Clefable, making it an excellent slot on hyper offense teams. Electric Seed's Defense boost lets Espeon withstand attacks from common offensive threats like Rillaboom, Zeraora, and Zamazenta-C, and with the item's consumption, take on Knock Off and Poltergeist users like Weavile, Yveltal, and Dhelmise more easily. Espeon's naturally high Speed tier means it can even outspeed foes like Blacephalon, Urshifu-R, and Rayquaza, preventing it from being revenge killed easily. Dazzling Gleam provides crucial coverage to hit Dark-types like Galarian Moltres, Yveltal, and Tyranitar. Magic Bounce prevents any attempts of stopping it with Taunt, Toxic, Thunder Wave, and Roar from Pokemon like Heatran, Ho-Oh, Rotom-W, and Giratina, respectively. This is especially useful, as even without any coverage to hit Steel-types super effectively, Espeon can safely set up on the likes of specially defensive Necrozma-DM, Heatran, and Ferrothorn due to their passive nature and Espeon's effective immunity to their status moves.

Calm Mind Espeon excels the most on hyper offense teams. Tapu Koko is a mandatory partner, as it provides dual screens for Espeon to set up more easily, brings it in safely with U-turn, and helps activate its Electric Seed with Electric Surge. Espeon pairs well with most gods used on hyper offense teams, but offensive gods that can donate a high Defense stat like Necrozma-DM and Groudon are notably great partners. In particular, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM is also a potent setup sweeper itself that appreciates Espeon's ability to muscle past Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Offensive teammates like Volcarona and Double Dance Galarian Moltres can keep up the pressure against the opposing team for Espeon to sweep much more easily.

Support.description:
Umbreon is a sturdy wall in the metagame thanks to its great defenses and good typing, allowing it to easily withstand attacks from common Pokemon such as Groudon, Venusaur, and Dragapult. Foul Play takes advantage of the high Attack stats of Restricted Pokemon and deals very acceptable damage to them, such as on Groudon and Calyrex-I. Snarl allows Umbreon to slow down strong specially attacking threats such as Calyrex-S and Kyogre. Yawn makes Umbreon demand respect unlike most other defensive Pokemon, as sleep is generally an oppressive mechanic and can also completely shut down Dynamax for at least a turn, forcing the Pokemon to switch out in order to prevent it and wasting their Dynamax. Moonlight semi-reliably heals 2/3 of Umbreon's HP under sun, which is fantastic for a defensive Pokemon that is usually paired with Groudon. Moonlight can prove to help Umbreon win against Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Kyogre under sun due to being able to play a very long game with them, 2HKOing the former and slowly chipping the latter down. Helping Hand allows Umbreon to bypass its lack of offensive presence by powering up an ally such as Groudon. Protect helps Umbreon stall opposing Dynamax turns more effectively. Sitrus Berry allows Umbreon to heal off a good amount of damage immediately, while Leftovers allows it to play the slow game when healing alongside Protect or Moonlight. The EV spread allows Umbreon to always survive Modest Kyogre's Water Spout under rain and Brave Calyrex-I's Max Hailstorm.

Umbreon appreciates partners such as Groudon that can set sun, helping Umbreon heal a substantial amount with Moonlight, and Umbreon in turn gives Groudon room to set up with Swords Dance via Yawn and can shoot its damage up even higher with Helping Hand. Charizard is another good Umbreon partner that also loves being in the sun. It offsets Umbreon's weakness to Zacian-C and both Urshifu formes with its G-Max Wildfire and Max Airstream, respectively. Grimmsnarl makes Umbreon even more problematic by bolstering its bulk via dual screens support and serves as a secondary check to both Urshifu formes.

uu.overview: Umbreon's stellar mixed bulk and Dark typing make it a strong pick on defensive teams, checking threats like Excadrill, Gyarados, Salamence, and Swords Dance + Knock Off Scizor. It provides fantastic team utility as a Wish passer, getting plenty of opportunities to heal up its teammates versus Pokemon like Azelf and Salamence. While unable to pressure some defensive Pokemon such as Amoonguss, Celesteela, and Teleport Chansey at all, Umbreon can freely use them to pass Wish, and Foul Play + Toxic greatly punishes many offensive checks switching in and prevents Umbreon from being too passive. However, it can offer a lot of opportunities to dangerous Fairy- and Fighting-types like Primarina, Cobalion, and Conkeldurr that can greatly threaten bulkier teams. Umbreon also struggles versus some of the stronger special attackers in the tier like Thundurus-T and Meteor Beam Nihilego, and chip damage can bring it into 2HKO range of Pokemon it checks like Mamoswine and Nidoking.
uu.comments:
Other Options

A Calm nature is an option to prevent Nidoking from 2HKOing Umbreon after Stealth Rock. This, however, makes Umbreon unable to check Mamoswine and more damaged by Pokemon like Excadrill and Dragon Dance Gyarados. Heal Bell is an option that lets Umbreon clear status from itself and its teammates. However, dropping Toxic for it makes Umbreon noticeably more passive and invites offensive Pokemon in, giving it far fewer opportunities to safely pass Wish. Therefore, it should only be used on teams with absolutely no better options against status.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Fighting-types like Cobalion, Keldeo, and Conkeldurr are some of the biggest threats to Umbreon. Conkeldurr can be deterred by Umbreon stalling for burn damage, but Drain Punch variants can easily regain their HP versus Umbreon's teammates, forming a long-term threat. Cobalion's Toxic immunity and ability in Justified let it safely switch into Umbreon as well.

Fairy-types: Defensive Primarina variants can easily wall Umbreon and sponge Toxic while pressuring its teammates. For non-defensive sets, Umbreon can outspeed and poison Substitute + Calm Mind variants or scout Choice Specs variants, but the former sets up for free if not immediately poisoned, and the latter poses a serious threat to Umbreon's teammates. Hatterene can easily set up on Umbreon, bouncing back Toxic. While Togekiss cannot beat Umbreon without Heal Bell due to Inner Focus, Heal Bell + Nasty Plot variants can set up provided they have enough Heal Bell PP remaining.

Dark-types: Crawdaunt is a huge threat to Umbreon thanks to its titanic damage output and resistance to Foul Play. Zarude's resistance to Foul Play and ability to sponge Toxic with Jungle Healing make it a great pivot into Umbreon; however, it cannot easily beat Umbreon itself unless Umbreon has wasted a lot of PP, and Zarude must be careful to not waste too much Jungle Healing PP if it needs check a teammate like Slowking. Choice Specs Hydreigon can easily overwhelm Umbreon if it switches into Draco Meteor.

Chip Damage: Pokemon such as Mamoswine and Nidoking can easily get the edge versus Umbreon if it has been chipped by entry hazards, lost its Leftovers to Knock Off from a Pokemon like Nihilego or Mamoswine itself, or statused. While Umbreon still avoids being 2HKOed by Life Orb Mamoswine without its Leftovers, Stealth Rock makes the 2HKO decently likely. Modest Nidoking can 2HKO Bold Umbreon with Stealth Rock up, forcing it to waste passive turns on Protect, which can be easily predicted.

Physically Defensive.description:
Foul Play lets Umbreon do considerable damage to physical attackers, being particularly key to checking Dragon Dance users like Gyarados and Salamence. Toxic lets Umbreon punish special attackers like Salamence and Moltres for using Roost against it and most of the broader metagame effectively. Wish alongside Protect keeps Umbreon and its teammates healthy. Protect is also useful to scout Choice-locked Pokemon, like Primarina and Keldeo, and absorb attacks from Pokemon like Cobalion and Conkeldurr paired with Future Sight from Slowking. Inner Focus lets Umbreon avoid flinches from Pokemon it checks, like Mamoswine, Gyarados, and Jirachi, and check non-Heal Bell variants of Togekiss. Maximum Defense investment with a Bold nature lets Umbreon avoid the 2HKO from Mamoswine's Earthquake after Stealth Rock while improving its matchup versus Pokemon like Excadrill.

Umbreon predominantly fits on balance, semi-stall, and stall teams as a fantastic check to threatening Pokemon like Azelf and Gyarados, as well as key team support through Wish. Hippowdon and Skarmory can check threats like Conkeldurr and Tapu Bulu for Umbreon. Skarmory can also provide an additional Excadrill check, Spikes support, and an Azumarill check. Slowking can check Keldeo and Primarina for Umbreon, while Umbreon checks Zarude and Hydreigon for it. Cleric support is vital, as Umbreon gets easily statused by Pokemon it checks like Hippowdon. Togekiss is a great option that can help check Hydreigon and provide an extra wincon with Nasty Plot versus the bulkier teams Umbreon struggles to make progress against, as well as checking Conkeldurr. Chansey is another fantastic option that can counter Primarina, Hydreigon, and Nidoking, while Articuno can also provide simultaneous Heal Bell and Defog support alongside Pressure, beating and PP stalling entry hazard setters like Hippowdon and Skarmory. Quagsire is a superb teammate on stall teams, dealing with Calm Mind Galarian Slowbro, Belly Drum Azumarill, and Nasty Plot Thundurus-T. Nihilego can check Hydreigon and Thundurus-T for Umbreon while providing Stealth Rock and Knock Off support against Pokemon like Excadrill and Scizor.

ru.overview: Umbreon's high special bulk and defensive typing make it a great check for common special threats such as Xurkitree, Chandelure, and Nidoqueen. Wish and Heal Bell enable it to stay healthy over the course of the battle and support its teammates. Foul Play allows Umbreon to better deal with various threats such as Golurk, Flygon, and Nasty Plot Celebi, while its ability Synchronize makes it difficult for Pokemon such as Raikou, Gastrodon, and Milotic to weaken it with status moves. However, Umbreon's weaknesses to Fighting and Fairy leave it vulnerable to common threats such as Lucario, Heracross, and Gardevoir. In addition, its passive nature, increased by its two-turn recovery, makes it easy for many Pokemon such as Reuniclus, Togekiss, and the aforementioned Lucario to take advantage of it.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Moonlight instead of either Protect, Wish, or Heal Bell gives Umbreon a one-turn recovery, but it does not have many PP and supporting teammates is one of the main reasons to use Umbreon. A physically defensive set can better check threats such as Metagross, Flygon, and Golisopod. However, many teams prefer the specially defensive variant, since it counters more important Pokemon. 180 EVs can be invested into Speed to outspeed Adamant Golurk. However, this makes Umbreon worse against special attackers such Nidoqueen and Chandelure. Inner Focus with Toxic is an option to better deal with Togekiss, but it has less use outside of this matchup.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Pokemon like Bewear and Pangoro can take huge advantage of Umbreon, but they dislike Toxic. Heracross, Lucario, and Toxicroak take good damage from Foul Play but pressure Umbreon with their Fighting-type moves. Stakataka, Reuniclus, and Sharpedo often run Fighting-type coverage that can break through Umbreon.

Fairy-types: Barring sets with Toxic, Togekiss and Diancie easily set up on Umbreon. Klefki has nothing to fear from Umbreon, can set up Spikes freely, and pressures it with Toxic. Mimikyu can safely set up once due to Disguise and OHKO Umbreon with a boosted Play Rough. Although Gardevoir takes good damage from Foul Play, it 2HKOes Umbreon with Moonblast.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Calm Mind Suicune, Reuniclus, and Curse Snorlax easily use Umbreon as setup fodder, since they take little from Foul Play and negate Toxic through Magic Guard, Rest, or Substitute.

Physical Attackers: Strong physical attackers such as Choice Band Flygon and Metagross overwhelm or break through Umbreon, but most of them take a lot from Foul Play.

Taunt and Trick: Taunt and Trick users such as Noivern, Crobat, Gardevoir, and Chandelure restrict Umbreon to one move, allowing them to better deal with it.

Toxic-immune Pokemon: Pokemon that are immune to Toxic such as Registeel, Nidoqueen, and Steelix cripple Umbreon with their own Toxic and cannot be statused in return.

Defensive.description:
Foul Play hits many physical attackers that try to take advantage of Umbreon such as Metagross, Golurk, and Flygon. Protect enables Umbreon to heal from Wish safely and scout Choice-locked Pokemon such as Gardevoir, Chandelure, and Heracross. If the team already has a cleric, Toxic is a good option over Heal Bell to punish common counters such as Togekiss, Incineroar, and Suicune. Since Umbreon is affected by every entry hazard, Heavy-Duty Boots gives it more switch-in opportunities and makes it less dependent on entry hazard control. Alternatively, Leftovers is a good choice for some passive recovery if the team has reliable entry hazard control.

Balance, semi-stall, and stall teams appreciate Umbreon's defensive qualities to check threatening Pokemon such as Polteageist, Chandelure, and Nidoqueen. Defensive Pokemon without reliable recovery such as Registeel, Stakataka, Bronzong, and Diancie appreciate Umbreon's Wish support. In return, they check Togekiss and either check troublesome Fairy-types or take the role of cleric to relieve Umbreon. Since Fighting-types such as Heracross, Bewear, and Pangoro heavily pressure Umbreon, checks to them such as Crobat, Dhelmise, and Galarian Weezing are very important. These Pokemon also give reliable entry hazard control if Umbreon runs Leftovers. On more defensive teams, Quagsire is a good choice to keep setup sweepers such as Reuniclus, Lucario, and Suicune in check, while Choice Scarf Ditto is a reliable offensive check to them. Reuniclus and Suicune are great setup sweepers on more semi-stalling teams and appreciate Umbreon's ability to check Ghost-types and keep them healthy with Heal Bell and Wish. Physical walls such as Gastrodon, Vileplume, and Galarian Weezing check troublesome physical threats such as Pangoro, Stakataka, and Sharpedo, which can overwhelm Umbreon.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This set is for a new and developing metagame. If you have any questions about the set, feel free to ask any in the Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Discussion thread.

KINGSLAYER (Defensive Support).description:
• With its good bulk, Yawn, and STAB Foul Play, Umbreon has a small niche as an answer to both Calyrex-S and Calyrex-I.

  • Foul Play provides consistent damage, puts heavy pressure on Calyrex-S thanks to its quadruple weakness, and can do decent damage to Zacian-C trying to come in.

  • Snarl is less useful against Calyrex-I, but it can completely shut down Calyrex-S, as well as annoying most special threats thanks to the Special Attack drop.

  • Moonlight can be used in place of Wish for instant, though inconsistent, recovery.

  • Though Umbreon should only Dynamax in the most dire of situations, a Careful nature will make Max Darkness slightly stronger.

Items

  • Leftovers is the most sensible item, granting Umbreon consistent passive recovery, lessening the need to use Wish and Protect.

  • Sitrus Berry is an alternative to Leftovers, providing Umbreon with a quick burst of health after taking some damage.

  • Utility Umbrella can allow Umbreon to better stand up to Kyogre, and it also enables more consistent recovery if using Moonlight. However, even with Utility Umbrella, Umbreon should not be relied on as a Kyogre answer.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpD with Calm - This spread maximizes Umbreon’s special bulk, allowing it to consistently check Calyrex-S.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with Bold - This spread allows Umbreon to better take physical attacks but severely hinders its consistency against Calyrex-S and other special threats.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Regenerator allows Umbreon to spend more time Wish passing but makes it very prone to becoming setup fodder. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead of Leftovers to make Umbreon less reliant on entry hazard removal, but the loss of recovery makes it difficult to check offensive foes as easily. Moonlight is an option that gives immediate recovery, but doesn't have much PP.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Pixilate and Magic Guard Tapu Koko can switch into Umbreon and KO it after minimal chip damage; however, the former must be wary of Toxic before its Flame Orb activates. Other Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Togekiss threaten Umbreon with their respective Fairy STAB attacks, with the former OHKOing it with Sheer Force-boosted Moonblast. Just like Pixilate Tapu Koko, neither of them want to switch into Toxic.

Trick Users: Umbreon struggles to provide much defensive utility if it is tricked a Choice item by Pokemon like Tapu Fini, Mew, and Azelf, so Foul Play and Protect should be used strategically to prevent this from happening.

Offensive pressure: While Umbreon is able to win one-on-ones against certain setup sweepers, these sequences can cost a lot of PP, leaving it without many tools to further serve as a physical wall. Notable examples are common wallbreakers like Adaptability Zygarde-10% and setup sweepers like Talonflame which are happy to repeatedly attack Umbreon and force it to use up Wish PP.

Unaware Wall.description:
Umbreon is a decent Wish passer and cleric that checks various setup sweepers like Cosmic Power Mew and Tapu Bulu for its teammates. Unaware + Foul Play gives Umbreon a way to reliably win the one-on-one against common Swords Dance users like Dhelmise, Garchomp, and Talonflame; most notably, it can even beat Belly Drum Kommo-o. Wish + Protect is Umbreon's main form of recovery and makes it able to scout Choice-locked foes like Azelf, Terrakion, and Barraskewda before switching to a check. While most teams prefer Heal Bell support, especially since there are few viable clerics, Toxic is good at weakening defensive foes like Regenerator Swampert and Tapu Fini. Leftovers gives passive recovery and has good synergy with Protect. Maximum Defense investment is recommended to more easily tank physical attacks like Drain Punch, Close Combat, and Earthquake from Kommo-o, Tapu Bulu, and Garchomp, respectively.

Umbreon's lack of pivoting move and defensive utility past its niche land it exclusively on semi-stall and stall teams. Pokemon without reliable recovery options like Sheer Force Tapu Lele, Galarian Zapdos, and Swords Dance users like Garchomp and Dhelmise are wallbreakers who greatly benefit from Umbreon's Wish passing and status relief. Regenerator Kommo-o sets Stealth Rock, switches into U-turn, and tanks powerful attacks from Pokemon like Barraskewda and Terrakion, while Umbreon covers for its weakness to Psychic-type attacks from users like Psychic Surge Azelf and Alakazam. Other common defensive Pokemon like Corviknight, Chansey, and Ferrothorn give Defog support, check special attackers, and set entry hazards, respectively, while Umbreon ensures that they don't become setup fodder. Since Umbreon matches up poorly into the most common specially attacking threats like Tapu Lele and Primal Weather users, Jirachi and Chansey are coveted teammates. Nidoqueen pairs exceptionally well with Umbreon by covering for its weakness to Pokemon like Terrakion and Tapu Koko; it also pressures foes with Toxic Spikes. Because Umbreon is prone to being PP stalled out of Wish, it also relies on the aforementioned defensive Pokemon to help it wall and chip foes. Regenerator Doublade and Runerigus are niche but synergistic partners that check particularly strong Fighting-types like Tough Claws Galarian Zapdos and Adaptability Terrakion to relieve pressure on Umbreon.

uu.overview: Slowking's useful resistances, excellent ability in Regenerator, and superb natural bulk make it one of the best defensive pivots in the metagame. These traits, combined with Teleport, allow Slowking to consistently force progress against many teams by allowing wallbreakers such as Thundurus-T and Zygarde-10% to enter the field safely. Due to its incredible bulk and typing, Slowking can easily come in on threats like Keldeo, Cobalion, Celesteela, Excadrill, and Nihilego and then pivot to a revenge killer with Teleport. However, as a result of its somewhat below average physical defense, Slowking is unable to consistently wall strong physical attackers such as Conkeldurr and Swords Dance Excadrill. Slowking also gets forced out by threats such as Zarude, Hydreigon, and Thundurus-T quite easily due to its initial passivity and can get overwhelmed by status from Pokemon it checks like Toxic from Moltres and Sludge Bomb poisons from Nihilego. Slowking's typing also holds it back, as it is weak to U-turn as well as Knock Off. Slowking competes with Chansey for the role of a defensive pivot, as Chansey isn't weak to foes such as Hydreigon. Slowking also competes with Primarina, which has a better defensive typing and a better matchup against Hydreigon.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Slowking can opt to run Trick over Teleport while running a Choice Scarf in order to cripple would be switch-ins like Zarude. Counter is another option over Teleport that can punish Pokemon like Zarude and reflect damage from U-turn users. Thunder Wave cripples common answers such as Hydreigon as well as Meteor Beam Celesteela while still punishing Keldeo. However, running it instead of Psyshic STAB leaves Slowking vulnerable to Primarina and Conkeldurr. Running Thunder Wave over Teleport is also fine, as long as the team has enough pivot support. This can open some doors for teammates like Conkeldurr and SubToxic Jirachi, as Conkeldurr is faster than paralyzed Hydreigon and Zarude, and Jirachi outspeeds revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Choice Scarf Zarude if they are paralyzed. A Trick Room + Teleport Slowking set can be used as a teammate for slow wallbreakers like Alolan Marowak and Conkeldurr on semi-Trick Room teams.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Zarude and Hydreigon wall Slowking due to their Psychic immunity and Scald resistance. Zarude is an especially good answer to Slowking, as it can heal off Scald burns via Jungle Healing.

Grass-types: Tapu Bulu and Tangrowth threaten Slowking immensely with their supereffective attacks. In particular, Tapu Bulu can OHKO Slowking or use it as setup fodder, but it should be wary of Scald. Amoonguss threatens Slowking with Spore and Sludge Bomb poisons, but it can be worn down by Psychic if it is not running Synthesis.

Electric-types and Electric-type Coverage: Electric-types like Thundurus-T and Raikou heavily pressure and force out Slowking. Electric-type coverage like Thunderbolt on Starmie and Thunder on Reuniclus keep Slowking from switching into them.

Status: Status forces Slowking to use Slack Off more often. Chansey is difficult for Slowking to overcome, as it can cripple Slowking with Toxic and shrug off Scald burns with Natural Cure. Slowking is also vulnerable to status from Pokemon it checks, such as Toxic poison from Excadrill and Moltres, Sludge Bomb poisons from Nihilego, and Scald burns from Primarina.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Scald reduces Slowking's passivity, burning switch-ins like Hydreigon and Tangrowth. Psychic threatens foes such as Amoonguss as they switch in. Additionally, Psychic discourages Conkeldurr from staying in to use Knock Off. Future Sight can be used instead to support Slowking's wallbreaking teammates. In addition to being an excellent pivot move, Teleport works well with Future Sight to bring in an offensive teammate such as Conkeldurr to capitalize on Future Sight absorbers, which are mainly Dark-types. Psyshock can be used over Psychic or Future Sight to prevent Slowking from becoming setup fodder for Calm Mind + Substitute Primarina and Meteor Beam Nihilego, though it makes Slowking more vulnerable to Conkeldurr. Colbur Berry allows Slowking to avoid an OHKO from Conkeldurr's Knock Off, improve its matchup against Mamoswine, and give it the ability to pivot against Hydreigon with Teleport. However, Heavy-Duty Boots can instead be used to keep Slowking from getting worn down by Spikes and Stealth Rock. 0 Speed IVs let Slowking underspeed opposing Slowking and gain momentum with a slower Teleport. 56 Special Defense EVs with a Sassy nature improve Slowking's matchup against foes such as Primarina and Moltres; however, it should be noted that this worsens Slowking's matchup against Zygarde-10%.

Slowking fits best on bulky offense, VoltTurn, and balance teams that appreciate its ability to tank special attacks and pivot in strong wallbreakers. Frail wallbreakers such as Zygarde-10% and Thundurus-T appreciate Slowking's ability to safely pivot them onto the field via Teleport. These teammates also enjoy Future Sight pressuring Amoonguss and Nihilego. Slowking forms an excellent defensive core with Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Tangrowth, which appreciate its ability to switch into Fire-type attacks and check Poison-types such as Tentacruel. In return, they can come in on Grass- and Electric-types like Tapu Bulu, Zarude, and Thundurus-T that force out Slowking. Slowking forms a strong pivot core with Moltres, with Moltres pressuring Grass-types such as Tangrowth and Tapu Bulu and Slowking checking foes such as Keldeo. Slowking appreciates entry hazard control from teammates such as Excadrill, Mandibuzz, and Rotom-H. Skarmory is also a good teammate for Slowking, as it checks Zarude easily and helps against Mamoswine, Conkeldurr, and Scizor. Its Whirlwind also synergizes with Future Sight, heavily damaging shared checks like Thundurus-T or outright KOing Fighting-types. Hippowdon acts as a switch-in to Rotom-H, Raikou, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon for Slowking.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind enables Slowking to become a dangerous offensive threat and set up on common Pokemon such as Nihilego and Moltres while retaining its longevity. After a boost, it is able to survive moves such as Dark Pulse from Choice Specs Hydreigon and stomach attacks such as Nidoking's Thunderbolt and Salamence’s Hurricane. Scald helps Slowking threaten switch-ins such as Hydreigon and enemy Slowking with burns. Psyshock helps against Chansey, opposing Slowking, Calm Mind Primarina, and Galarian Slowbro. Colbur Berry improves Slowking's matchup against Conkeldurr and Mamoswine, though it still has watch out for Facade from the former if it's below 66% HP.

Calm Mind Slowking fits best on balance, semi-stall, and stall teams as a wincon that maintains crucial defensive utility against Pokemon such as Mamoswine and Azelf. Nihilego and Chansey are useful Stealth Rock setters that check Thundurus-T and Hydreigon. Nihilego is more offensively potent and provides Knock Off support, whereas Chansey has more longevity and can also provide cleric support instead of setting Stealth Rock.
