Skarmory also struggles to fit all of its good utility moves and thus is often extremely passive, relying on Rocky Helmet and Body Press to deal any damage. Skarmory's Flying typing is a double-edged sword, making it neutral to Fighting and immune to Ground but a target for Electric coverage such as Zekrom's Bolt Strike and Xerneas's Thunder. It also faces stiff competition from other defensive Steel-types. Necrozma-DM checks Xerneas much better, Ferrothorn is a less passive Spikes setter and answers Kyogre, and Corviknight can be used as a Defogger.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

If need be, Skarmory can run Stealth Rock. However, seeing how common other Stealth Rock setters are in the metagame and how difficult it is for Skarmory to find space, it's usually omitted. Defog seems good initially, but Skarmory then competes with Corviknight, which can also Pressure stall the opposition's Stealth Rock PP to come out on top long-term. Moreover, Defog clashes with Spikes. Iron Defense allows Skarmory to hit for significantly more damage with Body Press and counter physical setup sweepers such as Groudon and Necrozma-DM. However, Skarmory's meager base 70 Speed and difficulty finding a move to drop means it's situational at best. Taunt and Toxic can be used in tandem to maximize Skarmory's utility, but running only status moves on a Pokemon this slow means Taunt forces Struggle.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Almost any special attacker can overwhelm Skarmory, so threats such as Xerneas, Calyrex-S, and Kyogre can threaten it out with just their presence. None of them enjoy Toxic, however.

Zekrom: Zekrom's Teravolt allows it to bypass Skarmory's Sturdy and OHKO with Life Orb Bolt Strike, but it doesn't enjoy the residual damage it takes from Toxic or entry hazards.

Fire-type Attacks: Ho-Oh, Groudon, and Raquaza can use Fire-type moves to OHKO Skarmory, with the former two carrying a status move to pressure Skarmory's teammates and the latter having a myriad of attacks to break through cores.

Eternatus: Eternatus isn't bothered by any of Skarmory's options and can comfortably fire off its strong special attacks to 2HKO it.

Taunt: Skarmory's reliance on status moves makes it a perfect Taunt target for the likes of Yveltal and Mewtwo. They risk taking Toxic on the switch, though.

Defensive Spikes.description:
Roost provides reliable recovery to Skarmory, allowing it to consistently check physical attackers. Whirlwind phazes physical setup sweepers, even if they're behind a Substitute. Swords Dance users such as Groudon and Necrozma-DM are prime targets for Whirlwind. Combined with Spikes, it can rack up damage on grounded foes lacking Heavy-Duty Boots. Toxic lets Skarmory punish entry hazard removers such as Yveltal. It also damages common offensive switch-ins such as Ho-Oh and Kyogre. Body Press uses Skarmory's enormous Defense stat, nailing the likes of Yveltal after it uses Roost and Ferrothorn for significant damage. It also is useful in not making Skarmory complete fodder after Taunt. Rocky Helmet provides some much appreciated damage to most physical attackers and helps with Skarmory's passivity.

Skarmory struggles with special attackers like Kyogre and Calyrex-S, so teammates such as Eternatus and Blissey are very appreciated. Stealth Rock setters form an entry hazard setting core with Skarmory. Tyranitar can set Stealth Rock and switch into Ho-Oh and Calyrex-S. Tangrowth and Groudon also pair up nicely, being able to take on some of the physical attackers that Skarmory cannot handle, namely Zygarde and Zekrom. Knock Off users such as Yveltal and Necrozma-DM can remove Heavy-Duty Boots, allowing Skarmory's Spikes to put in more work. Despite being a Steel-type, Skarmory can lose to Geomancy Xerneas. Bulky Ho-Oh and other Steel-types such as Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn can effectively deal with Xerneas. Xerneas itself can either run a Geomancy set to beat Zygarde and Zekrom and benefit from Spikes or a defensive set with Aromatherapy in case Skarmory gets statused.

ou.overview: Skarmory's impressive physical bulk and great defensive typing allow it to blanket check most physical attackers in the tier, including Landorus-T, Garchomp, Rillaboom, Kartana, and Weavile. Skarmory differentiates itself from other physical walls by being one of the only viable Spikes setters in the tier, easily setting it because of the many switches it forces against the Pokemon it walls. This prevents it from being completely passive despite its poor offensive stats. Iron Defense in conjunction with Body Press can also turn it into a late-game wincon. However, Skarmory's terrible special bulk leaves it vulnerable to almost every special attack, including even resisted attacks from strong wallbreakers like Tapu Lele and Dragapult. Skarmory faces competition from Ferrothorn and Mew as a Spikes setter, which have access to Knock Off and better special bulk to check Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Kyurem, as well as Corviknight and Buzzwole as a physically defensive wall, which have U-turn and actual offensive presence, respectively. Skarmory does, however, have access to reliable recovery and can consistently check Ground-types unlike Ferrothorn, as well as access to Spikes unlike Corviknight and Buzzwole.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Whirlwind can be used in the third moveslot to phaze setup sweepers and Pokemon that Skarmory does not want to face, like Tapu Koko, Magnezone, and Volcarona, if they try to switch into it. The switches it forces can wear down the opposing team in conjunction with Spikes. A Shed Shell allows Skarmory to escape Magnezone's Magnet Pull, which can annoy teams that rely on it to trap Skarmory to support Pokemon like Rillaboom and Kartana. However, Rocky Helmet is valuable, especially against U-turn users Skarmory can't punish without it, and Shed Shell can easily be removed by Knock Off if it pivots into one of the aforementioned Pokemon.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types and Electric-type Coverage: Tapu Koko and Zapdos do not mind anything except Toxic from Skarmory and can switch in and force it out, or remove Spikes with Defog in Zapdos's case. Zeraora dislikes switching into Body Press, leaving it reliant on pivots to switch in, but it also forces Skarmory out and can set up on it with Bulk Up. Magnezone is of particular note, as it traps Skarmory with Magnet Pull, though it must be wary of Body Press on the switch, and faster variants of Skarmory can outspeed and KO Magnezone with Body Press if it is weakened. Melmetal can potentially force in Skarmory and use Thunder Punch to weaken it.

Fire-types and Fire-type Coverage: Volcarona and Victini can switch into Skarmory safely if it does not carry Toxic, and the former can use Skarmory as setup fodder if it does not carry Whirlwind. Heatran cannot switch in safely in fear of Body Press but can force Skarmory out. Garchomp, which Skarmory usually walls, occasionally uses a mixed set with Fire Blast in order to lure in and KO it. Galarian Slowking usually uses Flamethrower on its Assault Vest set.

Special Attackers: Due to Skarmory's low special bulk, almost every special attacker, like Hydreigon, Tapu Lele, and Tornadus-T, is capable of threatening it out, though the former two take considerable damage from Body Press should they switch directly in. Pivots like Landorus-T that Skarmory wants to switch into can use U-turn to bring one of these special attackers safely in against it.

Defensive Spikes.description:
Body Press is the preferred attacking move, as it deals significant damage to most of the physical attackers Skarmory wants to check like Kartana, Excadrill, and Rillaboom, and it punishes Magnezone attempting to switch in and trap Skarmory. Iron Defense allows Skarmory to match boosts from setup sweepers like Swords Dance Weavile and Garchomp. Be careful when facing Kartana, however, as Sacred Sword bypasses Defense boosts. Iron Defense also boosts the power of Body Press, making Skarmory less passive and potentially able to sweep late-game if faster special attackers are removed. Toxic is an alternative to cripple some Pokemon that can otherwise switch into Skarmory like Zapdos, Volcarona, Tapu Koko, and Slowking, and it allows Skarmory to more consistently keep its Spikes up; it quickly puts most Defog users, with the exception of Corviknight, on a timer. However, it lets physical setup attackers overwhelm Skarmory in the short term. Rocky Helmet allows Skarmory to wear down physical attackers that make contact like Urshifu-R and Weavile. It is also particularly useful for deterring U-turn to gain momentum from the likes of Rillaboom, Landorus-T, and Urshifu-R, forcing progress against them. At the cost of considerable bulk, 176 Speed EVs can be used to outspeed Modest Magnezone so that Skarmory can 2HKO it with Body Press if it is weakened or caught on the switch.

Many offensive Pokemon can benefit from Skarmory's Spikes punishing the switches they force and wearing down checks, like Bisharp, Weavile, Zeraora, and Dragapult. Bisharp and Weavile are particularly notable for their powerful Knock Offs, which can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes to wear them down further with Spikes, and the former can deter Defog thanks to Defiant while utilizing Assurance to take advantage of Spikes. Ground-types like Landorus-T, Hippowdon, and Garchomp can check Electric-types for Skarmory. Skarmory usually draws in special attackers, making special walls that can check them for it ideal teammates. For example, Blissey is a good check to Dragapult and Hydreigon, Slowking checks Heatran and Tapu Lele, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowking covers Kyurem and Tapu Koko. Skarmory's Spikes prevents U-turn users like Dragapult and Tapu Koko from freely using them for momentum, especially when paired with Knock Off support. Skarmory can also check most of the strong physical attackers that can beat them, like Rillaboom and Landorus-T. Skarmory is especially valuable to sand teams, as it can check Pokemon that they are usually weak to like Rillaboom and Excadrill, forming a solid defensive core with either specially defensive Tyranitar or Hippowdon, the two viable sand setters.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used over Iron Defense in order to wear down physical setup sweepers like Rillaboom and put common switch-ins like Tapu Koko, Zapdos, and Gastrodon on a timer, but Skarmory loses the ability to make Body Press stronger and now loses to Mega Mawile and Swords Dance Rillaboom. Shed Shell can be used to switch out against Magnezone but is not worthwhile due to its relatively high opportunity cost in exchange for fixing one matchup. A faster Skarmory spread of 252 HP / 72 Def / 184 Spe with a Bold nature allows it to outpace Magnezone and OHKO it after one Iron Defense with the cost of having less bulk.

Checks and Counters

Strong Special Attacks: Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Mega Charizard Y, and Heatran can easily take care of Skarmory with their super effective attacks, and other strong special attackers like Greninja and Hydreigon can also easily take care of it. Magnezone is especially dangerous for Skarmory, as it can trap it and take care of it with Thunderbolt or gain momentum by using Volt Switch on it.

Ghost-types: Ghost-types like Gengar and Aegislash are immune to Body Press and therefore use Skarmory as setup fodder.

Taunt: Taunt shuts down Skarmory, as it cannot set up with Iron Defense, use Roost, or put down Spikes.

Defensive.description:
With its sky-high Defense, solid defensive typing, and ability to lay Spikes, Skarmory makes a fantastic fit on balance and stall teams. Iron Defense allows Skarmory to handle Swords Dance Mega Mawile, Garchomp, Mega Garchomp, and Rillaboom better, and it makes Body Press hit harder. Spikes helps wear down the opposing team and makes it easier for Skarmory’s teammates to sweep. Rocky Helmet is used to get off damage against physical attackers like Mega Lopunny, Mega Mawile, Rillaboom, and Mega Swampert. Leftovers can be used over Rocky Helmet to give Skarmory passive recovery. 96 Speed EVs allow Skarmory to outpace Mega Mawile, allowing it to use Roost before the latter can hit it with Thunder Punch.

Skarmory best fits on stall and balance teams. All teammates love Skarmory coming in on strong physical attacks from Weavile and Mega Lopunny and providing Spikes to wear down the opposing team. Chansey and Blissey are solid teammates for Skarmory, as they can come in on strong special attacks from Magnezone, Greninja, and Tapu Koko that Skarmory cannot tank, and in return, Skarmory can come in on Mega Lopunny and Mega Mawile's attacks for them. Clefable can check dangerous setup sweepers that threaten Skarmory like Mega Heracross and Mega Latias thanks to Unaware. Mega Sableye is great to pair with Skarmory due to Magic Bounce preventing Stealth Rock from wearing it down and Will-O-Wisp making physical attackers like Garchomp, Mega Scizor, and Kartana easier to handle. Alomomola can provide Wish support while also coming in on attacks from Mega Scizor, Mega Charizard X, and Victini that Skarmory struggles with, while in return Skarmory can come in on strong attacks from Rillaboom and Garchomp for it. Gastrodon is great to have a Manaphy check for the team, and it can also take care of Heatran, Magnezone, Manaphy, and Tapu Koko for Skarmory. Both Calm Mind Clefable and Reuniclus on balance teams love Skarmory for its Spikes support, which makes it easier for these two to set up and sweep. Ditto can revenge kill setup sweepers that Skamory cannot handle, such as Mega Heracross and Mega Charizard X, and trap and OHKO Magnezone with Hidden Power Ground.

monotype.overview:
Steel

Skarmory's typing allows it to easily find itself a spot in Steel teams for providing the much-needed Ground immunity and Fighting neutrality. Skarmory has access to Spikes, making it the primary setter for its team while freeing up Ferrothorn to run more utility options such as Thunder Wave and Stealth Rock. Its high Defense stat and great typing allow Skarmory to check various physically offensive Pokemon such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Urshifu-R with the help of Roost, Rocky Helmet, and Toxic. Moreover, having access to Roost and Toxic sets Skarmory apart from its competitors in Celesteela and Corviknight. Skarmory is an easy target for Electric-types such as Zapdos and Zeraora, which can grab momentum against Skarmory with their respective coverage. Furthermore, Skarmory can be trapped and eliminated by Magnezone, which enables a safer win route for Bulk Up Zeraora, and it is also vulnerable to Fire-type attacks from Pokemon such as Victini, Blacephalon, and Volcarona, which all pose a threat to it. Skarmory's Special Defense is low, making it weak to common special attackers in the tier such as Blacephalon, Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Kyurem. Being unable to touch any Ghost-type Pokemon outside of Toxic causes Skarmory to lose momentum heavily, especially against Substitute users such as non-Choice Specs Aegislash, Dragapult, and Spectrier, which all force it out.

Flying

Often appearing on balance teams, Skarmory's incredible Defense stat allows it to check many physical attackers such as Melmetal and Bisharp for its teammates. Due to its excellent typing, Skarmory can provide a key neutrality to Ice-type attacks, allowing it to check powerful Ice-types such as Mamoswine and Weavile. Skarmory's access to Spikes, Whirlwind, and Roost allows it to carve out a niche for itself on Flying teams. As a result of its low HP and Special Defense, Skarmory is unable to tank resisted hits from special attackers such as Choice Specs Kyurem and Choice Specs Tapu Lele and can be worn down by walls using special attacking moves like Scald from Toxapex. Skarmory faces competition from Corviknight and Celesteela, as they both share the same typing. Corviknight and Celesteela can tank both physical and special attacks, while Skarmory is relegated to tanking physical attacks.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Steel

In offensive structures, using Skarmory as a suicide lead with both Spikes and Stealth Rock paired with a Custap Berry allows it to set up entry hazards for its offensive teammates at the beginning of the game and apply pressure more easily.

Flying

224 HP EVs allow Skarmory to always be at full HP after two turns of Leftovers recovery after Stealth Rock damage, thus enabling it to use Sturdy. However, this spread reduces Skarmory's overall physical bulk and makes it easier to KO.

Checks and Counters

Steel

Ghost-types: Skarmory's only attacking move is Body Press, which is blocked by every Ghost-type Pokemon in the metagame and causes Skarmory to be forced out, especially if it's lacking Whirlwind.

Electric-types: Electric-types can all force out Skarmory with their respective STAB moves. Zapdos and Rotom-W can remove Spikes with Defog, while Magnezone threatens Skarmory with trapping. However, Magnezone must be careful to not take a hit from Body Press on the switch.

Fire-types: Skarmory has no way of handling offensive Fire-types such as Blacephalon, Volcarona, and Heatran, and these Pokemon can easily take advantage of Skarmory. However, the former two need to be careful about Toxic and the latter must be aware of Body Press.

Special Attackers: Special attackers such as Hydreigon, Kyurem, Dragapult, Gengar, and Spectrier can easily break through Skarmory due to its low Special Defense.

Taunt: Fast Taunt users such as Tornadus-T, Tapu Fini, and Heatran can block Skarmory from using Spikes, Whirlwind, and Roost.

Flying

Hatterene: While preventing Skarmory from setting Spikes with Magic Bounce, Hatterene can also use Skarmory as setup fodder.

Special Attackers: Due to Skarmory's low HP and Special Defense, it is 2HKOed from resisted special attacks from foes such as Choice Specs Tapu Lele.

Taunt: Foes such as Mandibuzz and Bulk Up Corviknight are able to inflict Taunt on Skarmory, preventing it from not only setting Spikes but also healing itself via Roost.

Physically Defensive (Steel).description:
Skarmory serves as the primary Spikes setter for its team, allowing offensive teammates such as Bisharp and Excadrill to wallbreak more consistently throughout the game. Body Press synergizes well with Skarmory's bulk and is especially helpful in the mirror matchup against Pokemon such as Bisharp, Ferrothorn, Melmetal, and Heatran on the switch, as well against Dark-types such as Weavile, Tyranitar, and Hydreigon. Roost helps Skarmory to stay healthy throughout the match against foes such as Urshifu-R, Excadrill, and Tyranitar. Whirlwind is used to prevent setup from Pokemon such as Garchomp and Dragapult while also generating passive chip damage if Spikes were set beforehand. Toxic can be used over Whirlwind to cripple Pokemon such as Mandibuzz and Mantine. Rocky Helmet complements Skarmory's physical bulk and typing excellently, as contact move users such as Urshifu-R and Weavile as well as U-turn and Flip Turn users such as Landorus-T, Scizor, Swampert, and Barraskewda will all be worn down by it. Sturdy allows Skarmory to set Spikes or use Toxic on a foe that can knock it out from full health if necessary. Furthermore, Sturdy allows Skarmory to deal damage against troublesome Pokemon that threaten Steel teams, such as Hydreigon. An Impish nature and maximum HP and Defense investment make Skarmory as tanky as possible against the aforementioned physical threats such as Urshifu-R, Excadrill, and Landorus-T.

Having access to Spikes makes Skarmory a valuable teammate, as it allows its offensive teammates such as Excadrill, Aegislash, Melmetal, and Bisharp to have an easier time against common walls such as Toxapex, Porygon2, and Ferrothorn. Ferrothorn is one of the best teammates for Skarmory, as the duo form an effective entry hazard-stacking core with Ferrothorn's Stealth Rock. Furthermore, Skarmory can make up for Ferrothorn's weakness to Fighting, while Ferrothorn takes care of Electric-types such as Tapu Koko and Rotom-W for Skarmory and provides a resistance to Water. Heatran provides the much-needed Fire immunity against Pokemon like Blacephalon and Hydreigon, while Skarmory can take on Ground-type attacks such as Earthquake from Garchomp and Excadrill. Furthermore, Heatran's common moves in Toxic and Magma Storm can deal immense chip damage when combined with Skarmory's Spikes. Excadrill takes care of Electric-types such as Tapu Koko and Zeraora if it is holding a Choice Scarf and can remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin to preserve Skarmory's Sturdy. Aegislash makes a good partner for Skarmory, as it relieves the pressure from Skarmory to handle Fighting-type attacks. This is especially important against Choice-locked foes such as Urshifu-R, which will have to avoid being heavily punished by Skarmory's Rocky Helmet. Furthermore, Aegislash helps greatly against Psychic-types such as Hatterene and Tapu Lele, which Skarmory generally struggle against. Bisharp's ability in Defiant also deters Defog from Pokemon such as Mantine and Zapdos, and its typing allows it to shine against Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Galarian Slowking, Slowking, Galarian Corsola, and Spectrier.

Defensive Spikes (Flying).description:
Toxic allows Skarmory to punish opposing Defoggers such as Rotom-W and Heavy-Duty Boots Zapdos as they try to switch into it. Whirlwind can be used over it to phaze opposing setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Dragon Dance Dragapult. In conjunction with Skarmory's bulk it can be used to shuffle opposing teams, slowly damaging them via Spikes. Body Press uses Skarmory's enormous Defense stat to hit threats such as Galarian Darmanitan and Tyranitar. Roost provides Skarmory with reliable recovery, allowing it to preserve Sturdy as well as consistently providing an answer to foes such as Cloyster and Excadrill. Rocky Helmet punishes physical attackers as well as pivots that use Flip Turn and U-turn by taking a chunk of their HP. Leftovers allows Skarmory to gain passive recovery, which it in turn gives it more chances to use its ability Sturdy. Sturdy is Skarmory's best ability, as it can allow Skarmory to survive attacks from foes such as Heliolisk and Volcarona when at full HP, and it can proceed to OHKO the former with Body Press. Maximum HP and Defense investment with a Bold nature allows Skarmory to be as bulky as possible, as well as boosting the power of Body Press.

Mantine is an excellent teammate for Skarmory, as its superb Special Defense allows it to wall special attackers such as Volcarona, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and Hydreigon. In return, Skarmory is able to handle foes like Dragonite and Dragapult. Skarmory appreciates the presence of Landorus-T to OHKO threats such as Tapu Koko and Zapdos. Landorus-T can also switch in on foes such as Zapdos after it has been Choice-locked into Thunderbolt. Skarmory then reciprocates this by acting as a switch-in to physical attackers such as Mamoswine that would otherwise OHKO Landorus-T with Icicle Crash. Defensive Zapdos can provide a key neutrality to Electric-type attacks as well as act as a special wall, taking attacks from foes such as Tapu Koko under Electric Terrain. Moreover, it can run a Toxic + Substitute set to wear down opposing walls such as Mandibuzz that Skarmory would find hard to deal with. Skarmory can then assist Zapdos by taking on potent physical attackers such as Swords Dance Terrakion that Zapdos would otherwise fall to. Zapdos can also run a Choice Specs set that appreciates Skarmory's ability to wear down foes such as Slowking with Spikes. Teammates such as Choice Band Galarian Zapdos and Galarian Moltres appreciate the presence of Spikes on the field, with the former potentially OHKOing foes such as Slowbro, Slowking, and Mew and the latter becoming a much more potent sweeper, being able to guarantee an OHKO on foes such as Slowking. In return, Galarian Zapdos is able to prevent foes from removing Spikes via Defog carelessly due to Defiant. Galarian Moltres is able to check the fearsome Spectrier that would otherwise OHKO Skarmory after it has been inflicted with a status condition. Thundurus-T and Dragonite are also good teammates for Skarmory, as both are helped by Spikes chipping away at their respective checks, and the former can absorb Electric-type attacks for it. Knock Off users such as Tornadus-T allow teammates to take advantage of Skarmory's entry hazards, as it can force foes that normally run Heavy-Duty Boots such as Victini and Cinderace to switchin less often. Moreover, Tornadus-T can use Taunt on opposing Defog users such as Mantine and Corviknight to prevent them from ridding the field of Skarmory's Spikes.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This set is for a new and developing metagame. If you have any questions about the set, feel free to ask any in the Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Discussion thread.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Skarmory has a wide range of other status options available. Toxic allows it to punish switch-ins directly and rack up even more residual damage. Skarmory can also set Stealth Rock, but the limited distribution of Spikes makes Skarmory's access to that move more valuable. Taunt is an option to prevent setup and Defog, but Skarmory's low Speed makes it an unreliable option. Skarmory can also forgo Body Press or Brave Bird to run four utility moves, but this makes it exceedingly passive, except as a dedicated lead with Custap Berry where Roost is not needed. Skarmory can opt to replace its held item with a Shed Shell to escape Magnezone, but must still be careful when facing Knock Off users like Kartana and Necrozma-DM. Skarmory can also run a specially defensive set, but this set is generally outclassed by Corviknight.

Checks and Counters

Fire- and Electric-types: Even physical Fire- and Electric-types like Victini, Zeraora, and Dracozolt can reliably 2HKO Skarmory with their super effective STAB moves.

Taunt: Skarmory is vulnerable to Taunt, as it cannot recover, phaze, or set Spikes in front of Taunt users like Yveltal and Alolan Persian.

Pivots: Physical pivots like Landorus-T can draw Skarmory in and pivot to a special attacker that forces it out. Especially with Stealth Rock up, this can wear down Skarmory by denying it a chance to recover. Pivots are especially dangerous when paired with Magnezone.

Zygarde-10%: Thanks to Thousand Arrows, Zygarde is one of the few physical Ground-types that Skarmory cannot reliably check.

Strong Special Attackers: Even with augmented HP, Skarmory has poor special bulk and it can be 2HKOed by most special attackers such as Mewtwo and Galarian Molres.

Physical Wall (HP).description:
Skarmory is the most reliable Spiker in the metagame and one of the sturdiest physical walls. With its amazing defensive typing, access to reliable recovery, and sky-high Defense, it is the perfect candidate for the HP teamslot. Skarmory is able to comfortably wall most physical threats, including Dhelmise, Bisharp, Excadrill, and Weavile. Body Press works off of its high Defense stat and threatens many of the Pokemon it walls, like Excadrill, but Brave Bird is an option for better neutral coverage and the ability to hit Ghost-types, especially Dhelmise, at the cost of taking recoil. Spikes punishes switch-ins and takes advantage of the free turns Skarmory generates. Iron Defense allows Skarmory to check setup sweepers as well, boosting alongside them while also powering up Body Press; Whirlwind is another option in the last moveslot to phaze set-up foes that Skarmory cannot KO. Rocky Helmet lets Skarmory punish physical attackers even more heavily, especially pivots that can otherwise wear down Skarmory, while Leftovers provides extra recovery. Maximum Defense investment is required to check the high-powered attackers common in Godly Gift and has the nice side effect of also powering up Body Press.

Skarmory is a good option for stall and balance teams looking for a catch-all physical wall. Since most Uber Pokemon have a high base HP, Skarmory can work with a wide range of Gods, but some of the best fits are Giratina, Yveltal, and Kyurem-W. Wallbreakers like Victini and Zeraora appreciate Skarmory's Spikes, which help wear down their checks, and its ability to switch into would-be revenge killers that force them out, such as Landorus-T. Since Skarmory's Special Defense is poor, it appreciates bulky teammates like RegenVest Tangrowth and Gastrodon to sponge special hits aimed at it. Due to its Electric and Fire weaknesses, Skarmory is unable to wall Victini, Zeraora, and Dracozolt; reliable switch-ins to these foes like Hippowdown and Quagsire make good partners, especially since Skarmory covers their Grass weaknesses.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Intimidate allows Skarmory to check Galarian Zapdos and Tough Claws Zarude better, but is otherwise not as useful as Dauntless Shield.

Checks and Counters

Specially Offensive Pokemon: Skarmory has a middling Special Defense stat, so even neutral special attacks and even some resisted ones from strong offensive threats can 2HKO it. Examples include Sheer Force Tapu Lele and Latios. Tapu Koko and Zapdos deserve a special mention thanks to their Electric STAB attacks.

Fire-type Pokemon: If Skarmory doesn't have Flash Fire, Fire-type attacks from Heatran and Choice Band Cinderace can OHKO it.

Strong Physical Wallbreakers: If opting out of Dauntless Shield, strong physical wallbreakers like Barraskewda and Terrakion can 2HKO Skarmory on the switch.

Physically Defensive.description:
Skarmory sets itself apart from Corviknight thanks to its access to utility moves like Whirlwind, Toxic and especially Spikes. Body Press takes advantage of its high Defense stat, which is notably higher than Corviknight's, and can 2HKO Heatran and Zarude as well as OHKO Terrakion. Brave Bird is an alternative that hits foes such as Dhelmise, Tapu Bulu, and Galarian Zapdos harder. Skarmory usually finds ample opportunities to set multiple layers of Spikes throughout a game to wear down the opposing team. Roost helps Skarmory stay healthy to continuously check threats like Zarude and Garchomp. Whirlwind prevents setup sweepers from exploiting Skarmory's passivity and also synergizes well with Spikes. Iron Defense is an option on Body Press sets that still checks setup sweepers and also makes Skarmory less passive. Another option is Toxic, which helps wear down both passive foes like Mandibuzz and setup sweepers like Dhelmise. Leftovers gives Skarmory extra recovery, while Rocky Helmet is an option that punishes contact moves. Skarmory can run several different abilities. Dauntless Shield maximizes Skarmory's defensive capabilities and Body Press damage. Wandering Spirit, especially combined with Rocky Helmet, deters U-turn and Flip Turn from Regenerator pivots such as Swampert and Landorus-T, and also lets Skarmory serve as an emergency check to sweepers that heavily rely on their ability such Magic Guard Talonflame and Triage Tapu Lele. Flash Fire negates one of its weakness and allows it to surprise dangerous Fire-type such as Volcarona and Desolate Land Heatran with Brave Bird and Body Press, respectively. It also allows Skarmory to check the plethora of physical Fire-types like Talonflame and Cinderace that can be hard to account for otherwise.

Skarmory's ability to set Spikes make it a better fit on stall teams compared to Corviknight, in particular entry hazard stack teams. Powerful offensive threats like Tapu Lele and Terrakion appreciate Spikes to nab more KOs. Offensive threats with a pivot move like Tapu Koko and Barraskewda can also rack up Spikes damage while still keeping offensive momentum by forcing additional switches. Heatran can set entry hazards alongside Skarmory, threaten to eliminate entry hazard removers with Magma Storm and Taunt. In return, Skarmory can cover for Heatran's weakness to Ground, and Dauntless Shield variants can also handle dangerous Fighting-types like Terrakion. Many Ground-type Pokemon also make for good partners, as they can take on Electric attacks and set Stealth Rock. Swampert and Garchomp are notable partners thanks to their resistance to Fire. Special walls are needed, as Skarmory invites many special attackers in when it set Spikes. Blissey forms the famous SkarmBliss core, taking on dangerous special threats like Zapdos and Sheer Force Tapu Lele while regaining momentum with Teleport while Skarmory handles strong physical attacks that Blissey struggles against. Pixilate Tapu Koko is one of the most dangerous physical threats that Skarmory can't properly handle regardless of its ability choice, so it's vital to have a teammate that answers it such as Ferrothorn or Nidoqueen. Without Dauntless Shield, strong physical wallbreakers like Terrakion can 2HKO Skarmory, which partners like Mew and Palossand can deal with. Physical Fire-types such as Cinderace and Talonflame also pose a threat should it forgo Flash Fire, making Zapdos and the aforementioned Swampert great teammates.

bdspou.overview: Skarmory's excellent defensive typing and impressive physical bulk give it an important role in BDSP OU as a check to some of the tier's most common physical attackers like Breloom and Weavile. It is a great Spiker due to its ridiculous physical bulk, longevity, and its ability to beat common Defoggers like Gliscor and Scizor. Whirlwind further cements Skarmory as an excellent defensive centerpiece against the onslaught of physical sweepers common to the tier like Lucario and Feraligatr. Skarmory is not even limited to a defensive role; it also fits on common hyper offense structures as a dedicated lead due to its access to the combination of Spikes, Stealth Rock, and Taunt, ensuring that it can get up as many entry hazards as it can while denying opposing entry hazards. Despite its strength as a wall, Skarmory can be taken advantage of by special attackers like Latias and Starmie; Starmie can even spin its Spikes away. Skarmory is often forced to Whirlwind setup sweepers like Garchomp, leaving it weakened. It is weak to common coverage types in Electric and Fire, and it is extremely vulnerable to the ever-present Magnezone if its Shed Shell is removed. Furthermore, its face stiff competition as a suicide lead from Azelf, which boasts higher Speed and Explosion.
bdspou.comments:
Other Options

Skarmory can run Defog over Spikes on its defensive set, but this is generally better accomplished by Gliscor, and the value Spikes provides is usually greater. Taunt can be run of the defensive set to prevent Scizor, Blissey, and Clefable from recovering and, in Scizor's case, removing Skarmory's Spikes; however, Taunt is hard to justify over any of Skarmory's other moves. Stealth Rock is an option over Brave Bird on the defensive set to layer even more entry hazards, but this leaves Skarmory helpless in the face of Tangrowth and Celebi.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Though Skarmory usually runs Shed Shell to evade Magnezone's Magnet Pull, it often switches into Knock Off users like Tangrowth and Gliscor; once Shed Shell has been removed or if Skarmory is running a different item, Magnezone is free to trap and KO it. Outside of Magnezone, Pokemon like Raikou, Rotom-W, and Rotom-C pressure Skarmory while maintaining momentum with STAB Volt Switch. Raikou can set up with Calm Mind and Substitute on Skarmory, while Rotom-W can similarly set up with Nasty Plot.

Fire-types and Fire-type Coverage: Fire-types like Infernape and Heatran force Skarmory out with their strong STAB moves. Heatran is particularly good at pressuring Skarmory, as it does not mind switching into Brave Bird and can punish it with a Flame Body burn. Fire-type coverage from Pokemon like Nidoking, Dragonite, and Garchomp is similarly scary. Azelf commonly runs Flamethrower and, more importantly, Taunt, which shuts down lead Skarmory.

Strong Special Attackers: Pokemon like Latias, Alakazam, Starmie, and Togekiss not only commonly carry super effective coverage, but can simply power through Skarmory due to its middling special bulk. Latias and Starmie deserve special mention for being able to remove Skarmory's Spikes with Defog and Rapid Spin.

Crawdaunt: Crawdaunt is the rare physical attacker that has the necessary strength to outright 2HKO Skarmory, making it a particularly dangerous foe if Skarmory is a team's only physically defensive wall.

Defensive Spikes.description:
Skarmory can use its impressive physical bulk to set up Spikes in the face of common Defoggers like Scizor and Gliscor. Despite incurring recoil, Brave Bird is Skarmory's best option for pressuring Tangrowth and Breloom. Whirlwind is incredibly helpful at preventing common physical setup sweepers like Feraligatr, Cloyster, Dragonite, and Lucario from boosting past Skarmory; it also racks up chip damage from Spikes. Shed Shell is the preferred item, as it lets Skarmory escape Magnezone's Magnet Pull, which many teams rely on to handle Skarmory. However, if Magnezone is not a concern, Leftovers improves Skarmory's matchup into hard-hitting physical attackers like Lucario. Sturdy importantly lets Skarmory always live one hit from full, ensuring that it can always revenge kill or phaze a sweeper that has gotten out of hand if Skarmory is healthy.

Skarmory fits best on balance or stall teams that appreciate its ability to wall a number of common physical Pokemon. Stacking Stealth Rock with Skarmory's Spikes is an effective strategy to whittle way the health of Pokemon like Heatran that threaten Skarmory. Blissey and Gliscor can both set Stealth Rock; Blissey can easily switch into the special attacks that forces Skarmory out, while Gliscor can deal with Fire- and Electric-types like Infernape and Heatran that pressure Skarmory. Gliscor, along with Tangrowth, are excellent Knock Off absorbers, a quality that Skarmory greatly appreciates, as losing its Shed Shell leaves it completely helpless against Magnezone. Tangrowth can also effectively switch into Crawdaunt, which is one of the rare physical attackers with enough strength to overpower Skarmory. Skarmory is especially devastating when paired with a VoltTurn core, which forces Spikes damage onto foes repeatedly by pivoting, making teammates like Rotom-W and Scizor are great options. Clefable is a good partner for dealing with special setup sweepers like Alakazam and Latias that Skarmory cannot effectively phaze. Similarly, on stall teams, Quagsire is a good option for dealing with the few physical setup sweepers, namely Lucario and Dragonite, that are capable of powering through Skarmory. Starmie is an excellent partner for removing just the opponent's entry hazards with Rapid Spin and switching into Heatran; Starmie is particularly valuable in mirror matchups, allowing Skarmory to trade Spikes with opposing Skarmory without seriously hindering its own team.

Suicide Lead.description:
The basis for this set is fairly straightforward: set up as many entry hazards as possible before Skarmory gets KOed. Taunt helps prevent opposing entry hazards from going up and stops slower Defog users like Scizor and Gliscor from removing Skarmory's own entry hazards. Brave Bird is a particularly helpful tool for generating momentum; if the opponent lets Skarmory set up all of its entry hazards, Skarmory can simply KO itself with Brave Bird recoil to safely get in a teammate. A Custap Berry, in conjunction with Sturdy, ensures that Skarmory can usually get up at least two layers of entry hazards before getting KOed.

Suicide lead Skarmory fits best on hyper offense teams that appreciate it getting up entry hazards early while preventing foes from doing the same. Setup sweepers like Lucario, Feraligatr, and Breloom appreciate Skarmory's entry hazards chipping foes into range of their boosted attacks. Lucario, in particular, needs Stealth Rock up to OHKO Latias with +2 Extreme Speed and Tangrowth and Skarmory with +2 Close Combat, while Skarmory's ability to deny opposing entry hazards benefits Breloom by keeping its Focus Sash intact. Focus Sash Alakazam can be troublesome, as Magic Guard preserves its Focus Sash; accordingly, teammates like Choice Scarf Garchomp and Weavile are excellent choices for pressuring it. Skarmory is unable to block faser foes like Azelf and Roserade from setting up entry hazards, so Rapid Spin support from Starmie can be potentially helpful if denying opposing entry hazards is key, such as when using Dragonite and Focus Sash Breloom.

Rain Sweeper.description:
Kingdra's all-around good stats and access to Swift Swim make it an excellent choice on rain teams. Hurricane is used so that Kingdra can beat Grass-type Pokemon like Roserade without Draco Meteor Special Attack drops. Hydro Pump's main use over the more accurate Surf is to 2HKO even dedicated special walls like Registeel, Umbreon, and Assault Vest Reuniclus in rain; Surf is already powerful enough to OHKO most offensive Pokemon it hits neutrally. Flip Turn can be used instead to grab momentum off of Kingdra's checks and ease prediction for Choice Specs sets. Life Orb is the preferred item because it boosts power without locking Kingdra into one move; however, Choice Specs gives Kingdra the best chance to 2HKO bulky Water-types like Suicune and Milotic with Draco Meteor while also avoiding Life Orb's chip damage. Kingdra can opt for a Timid nature in order to outpace Choice Specs Gardevoir, which copies its Swift Swim with Trace, and improve its matchups against the likes of Togekiss and Chandelure out of rain.

Kingdra must always be supported by Drizzle from Politoed to activate Swift Swim. Without Drizzle support, Kingdra is outclassed by other offensive Water-type Pokemon like Starmie. Kingdra works best when used alongside other rain sweepers. Kabutops, Omastar, and Ludicolo can weaken bulky Water-type Pokemon like Milotic and Suicune. Toxicroak walls the aforementioned bulky Water-types and can also switch into First Impression attempts from Golisopod, making it an especially good Kingdra partner. In a similar vein, Tornadus benefits from Kingdra's Flip Turn to come in safely and break down bulky Water-type Pokemon.

CritDra.description: This set was added after the analysis was uploaded.

nu.overview: Kingdra has insane late-game potential thanks to how strong its Sniper-boosted critical hits are. The amount of Pokemon in NU that can contend with Kingdra's Water + Dragon coverage is low, and the amount that can meaningfully threaten Kingdra in return is even lower. Kingdra suffers, though, from taking multiple turns to fully set up, which gives the opponent a bit of time to prevent it from taking the game over. Additionally, many of the Pokemon it'd like to set up against, namely Vaporeon, Talonflame, and Arcanine, commonly run Toxic, which severely compromises its ability to clean late-game. Lastly, despite being one of the few offensive checks to Inteleon and Starmie, Kingdra offers very little defensively compared to other Water- and Dragon-types like Vaporeon, Alolan Exeggutor, and Guzzlord, meaning it requires a good amount of defensive teambuilding support.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs sets possess immense power, can provide pivot support with Flip Turn, and fit well on rain teams, but both Inteleon and Starmie are better dedicated wallbreakers, and rain teams aren't very consistent.

Checks and Counters

Sylveon: Bulky Sylveon variants can stomach a critical hit from Surf and retaliate with Moonblast or Hyper Voice, the latter having a decent chance to OHKO Kingdra and bypassing Substitute. Even offensive variants can easily survive an attack from Kingdra and OHKO in return.

Bulky Water-types: Despite being setup fodder for Kingdra, Vaporeon and Mantine can cripple it with Toxic and stall out turns and Draco Meteors by spamming their recovery moves.

Offensive Pressure: Kingdra isn't very strong nor fast before it boosts, and its bulk isn't very great; therefore, Pokemon like Rotom-C, Decidueye, and Silvally-Ghost can give it issues because Kingdra can't OHKO them without a critical hit, is slower than them without an Agility boost, and takes significant damage from their attacks, making it hard to safely set up when faced with such foes. Additionally, priority users like Choice Band Sneasel and Toxicroak can revenge kill Kingdra regardless of if it uses Agility.

Critical Hit-immune Foes: Shell Armor Escavalier counters Kingdra because of its bulk and can remove Kingdra's Scope Lens with Knock Off. Battle Armor Drapion is a much shakier answer, since Draco Meteor KOes it after Stealth Rock, but it can also weaken Kingdra's damage output with Knock Off.

CritDra.description:
Set Details

The combination of Focus Energy and Scope Lens ensures Kingdra can always critically hit, letting it ignore the Special Attack drops from Draco Meteor. Alongside Agility, this severely limits overall counterplay to Kingdra once it sets up. Alternatively, Kingdra can use Substitute to avoid Toxics from Vaporeon, guaranteeing that Kingdra wins one-on-one. A Modest nature is used to guarantee an OHKO on Drapion after Stealth Rock and because Timid isn't necessary thanks to Agility.

Because Kingdra has very few answers after boosting, much of the support it requires is related to easing setup. Dual screens from Xatu is one way to do this, making it harder for powerful attackers like Toxicroak and Heliolisk to take Kingdra out. Similarly, pivots like Talonflame and Arcanine that draw in Water-types help provide Kingdra with good setup opportunities. Sylveon is one of the few foes that Kingdra can't OHKO even with a critical hit; teammates like Scrafty and Passimian that can force damage onto it and push it into OHKO range are helpful as a result. Entry hazard support also works to force chip damage onto Pokemon that can stomach a hit, with Pokemon like Diancie, Copperajah, and Garbodor being good hazard setters.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Life Orb lets Kingdra switch moves, but it comes with the drawbacks of less power and recoil. Flip Turn allows Kingdra to take advantage of common switch-ins like Toxapex, pivoting to teammates that can handle it like Barraskewda. Ice Beam is an option over Hurricane so that Kingdra can hit Flying-types like Galarian Moltres super effectively. However, it is less powerful than Hurricane against other targets. Kingdra can also run a Timid nature to outpace Regieleki, Choice Scarf Weavile, and Adamant Dragon Dance Dragapult at +1. However, if Kingdra is not running a Modest nature, it loses the ability to potentially 2HKO Ferrothorn under rain. Mystic Water and Dragon Fang are also options to allow Kingdra to switch moves and hit hard, and unlike Life Orb they don't reveal its item.

Swift Swim (Water).description:
Kingdra is a decent Swift Swim user for Water teams utilizing rain, as it helps in various matchups such as Electric, Grass, and especially Dragon. Draco Meteor threatens bulky walls such as Dragalge and Amoonguss. Dragon Pulse is used to deal with foes that resist Water such as Kyurem, as well as other foes like Galarian Slowking. Hydro Pump allows Kingdra to 3HKO Galarian Slowking and gives it a chance to 2HKO Ferrothron under rain. Hurricane can be run over Hydro Pump to let Kingdra hit Grass-types such as Tapu Bulu super effectively. Maximum Speed investment allows Kingdra to outspeed threats like Choice Scarf Latios and Choice Scarf Thundurus-T.

As Kingdra relies on Swift Swim to do its job, Pelipper is an amazing teammate for it. If Kingdra opts to run Hurricane, Pelipper can run a defensive set with Heavy-Duty Boots rather than a Choice Specs set. Barraskewda can break down walls like Galarian Slowking, as well as threats such as Regieleki and Alolan Raichu in Electric Terrain when rain is active. Urshifu-R is also an option, as it can pressure shared checks like Mantine and Galarian Moltres. It also ravages Ferrothorn and Kyurem, foes that would otherwise pose a huge threat to the team. Eject Button Toxapex supports Kingdra by crippling foes like Porygon2 and Chansey with Toxic and Knock Off. It also walls revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Dragapult. Slowking allows Kingdra to enter the field safely through Teleport, as well as providing Future Sight support to help wear down foes like Galarian Slowking. Swampert provides Stealth Rock support and can pivot Kingdra in via Flip Turn. It can also phaze Substitute Kyurem by using Roar. Late-game sweepers such as Crawdaunt, Cloyster, and Keldeo can be run alongside Kingdra, as they appreciate the holes Kingdra can punch in many teams. They also are able to deal with foes such as Chansey and Ferrothorn, which give Kingdra trouble. Volcanion is also an excellent teammate, as it can switch into and defeat Fairy-types like Tapu Fini, as well as Grass-types such as Ferrothorn.

doublesou.overview: While Kingdra does stand out as the best Swift Swim attacker in SS DOU, it still leaves a lot to be desired. Its Speed in rain gives it a notable amount of utility, as it can pin down faster, frailer foes while it breaks the opposing team with strong rain-boosted Muddy Waters. In particular, Kingdra excels in using its offensive presence to give its teammates space and clean up weakened teams. However, it has multiple awkward matchups in the metagame, including against DOU's top threats in Rillaboom, Tapu Fini, and Kyurem-B, and its average Special Attack stat can at times feel lacking, which is a major downside, as it offers no utility outside of purely attacking. Kingdra, in particular, faces stiff competition as a Water-type attacker in rain from Urshifu-R, which boasts noticeably better power output and coverage, an improved matchup against Trick Room, more relevant utility in the ability to force trades with Unseen Fist, and most importantly a non-reliance on rain to be effective; while Kingdra does offer blazing Speed and a better match-up against fast Dragon-types in Dragapult and Naganadel, its Speed is also easily compensated for by the rain archetype's many Tailwind-setting Flying-type options in Tornadus and Zapdos, and its need for Speed also leaves it much more vulnerable in the face of opposing speed control. Kingdra's reliance on keeping its rain setter available, as it is very lacking as an attacker without it, on top of its other flaws, ultimately makes it quite awkward to run on rain teams.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs is an option in order to amplify Kingdra's damage output even further, taking advantage of the fact that it only really needs its Water-type STAB moves to do its job while also niftily avoiding Life Orb's recoi. However, the set's inability to switch moves and run Protect viably can also leave it quite punishable, especially with Fake Out and other priority moves being particularly awkward to play against. Substitute is an option over one of Kingdra's coverage moves in order to block Fake Outs and Grassy Glide from Rillaboom, though losing one of its coverage moves can also make breaking through teams more difficult.

Swift Swim Attacker.description:
• Muddy Water is Kingdra's primary attacking option, as it hits both foes with significant rain-boosted damage.

  • Hurricane is Kingdra's best option to hit Grass-type switch-ins such as Rillaboom and Amoonguss for super effective damage, and it is also nifty for sniping Urshifu-R.

  • Draco Meteor is used to decimate Dragon-types that may otherwise be able to stomach a rain-boosted Water-type attack and hit back hard such as Kyurem-B, Dragapult, and Naganadel, though be wary, as it also weakens Kingdra considerably, squandering the already limited turns of rain.

  • Hydro Pump is an option over either coverage move to decimate neutral targets such as Zeraora, Necrozma, and Metagross, which otherwise easily survive a Muddy Water, at the cost of being worse against either Grass-types and Rillaboom or Dragon-types.

  • Protect lets Kingdra be safe for a turn, which is handy for giving teammates time to position around it and stalling out threatening field conditions such as opposing Tailwind and Trick Room.

  • Life Orb in conjunction with the given EV investment and Modest nature is geared towards maximizing Kingdra's offensive presence, with Swift Swim letting it outrun practically the entire metagame under rain, getting the jump on Zeraora and Dragapult as well as Choice Scarf users such as Genesect and Galarian Zapdos.

Trick Room Support.description:
Porygon2 is the metagame's best Trick Room setter with its incredible bulk, mere one weakness, and ability to keep top-tier Pokemon at bay, such as Calyrex-S and Landorus-T. Trick Room is invaluable speed control for almost any team, and Porygon2 sets Trick Room reliably thanks to its immense bulk. Recover gives Porygon2 longevity, letting it stall out Dynamax turns and potentially help it serve as a late-game wincon, outlasting foes. Eerie Impulse is immensely useful to impede the metagame's various special attackers such as Calyrex-S, Rotom-H, and Kyogre. Tri Attack is oftentimes less critical than Porygon2's other options, but its the best option versus Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Incineroar that aren't vulnerable to Porygon2's coverage or Eerie Impulse. Ice Beam makes Porygon2 one of the best checks to one of the metagame's most potent threats, Landorus-T, and it also deals decent damage to the likes of Groudon and Venusaur. Foul Play allows Porygon2 to threaten a 2HKO onto Calyrex-S and hit boosted Weakness Policy users such as Solgaleo, Calyrex-I, and Metagross quite hard. Download is good because it gives Porygon2 a Special Attack boost pretty often, considering common Pokemon such as Incineroar, both Urshifu formes, and Landorus-T have higher Defense stats. Trace should only be run if Porygon2 chooses Eerie Impulse and Foul Play as its last two moves. Trace will be more advantageous than disadvantageous most of the time, mainly due to the potential of copying Intimidate from users such as Incineroar and Landorus-T. Thunderbolt is an option for Porygon2's third moveslot, giving Porygon2 BoltBeam coverage with Ice Beam and allowing it to more immediately threaten the likes of Charizard, Blastoise, and Kyogre, and unlike Eerie Impulse, its not shut down by Taunt. However, its overall less useful then Eerie Impulse. Note that when running Thunderbolt, Porygon2 should elect for a Modest nature to best make use of its BoltBeam coverage. Icy Wind is alternative speed control over Trick Room, though oftentimes Trick Room is simply going to be more valuable. Shadow Ball has the advantage over Foul Play of being able to OHKO Calyrex-S after a Download boost, but it's worse versus boosted Weakness Policy users. Ally Switch is an option over one of the last two moveslots, giving Porygon2 the ability to redirect attacks from its teammates, though its incredibly difficult to justify Ally Switch due to it taking a valuable slot. A physically defensive EV spread is preferred for Porygon2 to better set Trick Room in the face of powerful physical attackers such as Urshifu-S and Zacian-C, and the given EVs allow Porygon2 to survive Adamant Zacian-C's Close Combat with the remainder thrown into Special Defense. A specially defensive EV spread such as 252 HP / 144 Def / 112 SpD with a Sassy nature is also a good option, which allows Porygon2 to live extremely powerful special attacks such as Calyrex-S's Helping Hand- and Life Orb-boosted Max Mindstorm and Kyogre's Mystic Water-boosted 150 BP Max Geyser. A Modest nature with some Special Attack investment can make Porygon2 notably more threatening with a Download boost, though this of course compromises its bulk.

Porygon2 makes a great fit on sun teams with either Torkoal or Groudon alongside Venusaur because they greatly appreciate its role compression as a check to Landorus-T with Ice Beam, as well as Calyrex-S and Rotom-H with Eerie Impulse. Furthermore, the combination of Porygon2 with the aforementioned Pokemon is quite flexible between Porygon2's ability to set Trick Room or swap into a Drought setter to activate Venusaur's Chlorophyll, which has the threat of both Dynamax and Sleep Powder at its disposal. Incineroar pairs extremely well with Porygon2 with its Fake Out capable of helping it set Trick Room. Other good Restricted Pokemon to pair with Porygon2 are Kyogre and Zacian-C, the former being a heavy hitter that can benefit greatly from Trick Room and the latter appreciating its ability to check Landorus-T.

Offensive Support.description:
Contradictory to Porygon2's massive bulk with Eviolite, it can run a more niche, albeit effective offensive set. Download and Analytic activate fairly consistently, and alongside Special Attack investment and occasionally Dynamax Porygon2 can be a threat in of itself. Tri Attack is simply a consistent STAB move, whereas Hyper Beam gives Porygon2 the strongest possible Max Strike, though it's less flexible outside of Dynamax and Porygon2 tends to stay on the field for a long time. Shadow Ball threatens Calyrex-S, one of the metagame's most dangerous Pokemon. Ice Beam on the other hand lethally threatens Landorus-T and deals good damage to the likes of Groudon and Venusaur. Running either Trick Room or Icy Wind is invaluable for speed control and should be used respectively of which would benefit your team more. Recover is incredibly useful, granting Porygon2 longevity and allowing it to serve as a late-game wincon by outlasting foes and stalling out Dynamax turns. Alternatively, Ally Switch allows Porygon2 to redirect attacks from its partners, but this gives up Recover's longevity. Thunderbolt is a coverage option that slams the likes of Charizard, Tapu Fini, and Blastoise fairly hard, though its difficult to justify over Porygon2's generally more important coverage options. Download should be used if Porygon2 has Trick Room, and it should instead have Analytic instead when running Icy Wind, as Analytic will not consistently activate under Trick Room.

Porygon2 is generally seen on compositions with Zacian-C, Gigantamax Lapras, and sometimes Grimmsnarl. Offensive Porygon2 compromises its bulk, so dual screens setters such as the aforementioned Gigantamax Lapras and Grimmsnarl are good partners. The former has a great Landorus-T matchup, freeing Porygon2 from running Ice Beam, while the latter also packs other useful support moves like Fake Tears to help Porygon2. Note that Lapras and Grimmsnarl can be run together, but Grimmsnarl should not be running dual screens when doing so.

ubers.overview: Porygon2 is a necessary setter on Trick Room teams, providing great defensive utility against Calyrex-S to the otherwise frail playstyle. Thanks to Eviolite and access to Recover, Porygon2 has the ability to set Trick Room reliably and can use Teleport to safely bring in its teammates. Unfortunately, Trick Room is an inherently unreliable playstyle, and by extension Porygon2's niche is extremely limited. Porygon2 is also extremely susceptible to Knock Off, Trick, and Taunt and as such is often forced out by the ever-prevalent Yveltal.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Ice Beam is an option to let Porygon2 check Zygarde, but it is otherwise completely outclassed by Foul Play. Thunder Wave provides some nice utility, but has poor synergy with Trick Room. Trace can be run to potentially reset a favorable weather condition or copy an ability such as Intimidate from Landorus-T, but it is extremely situational.

Checks and Counters

Yveltal: Yveltal can remove Porygon2's Eviolite with Knock Off and shut its utility down with Taunt without being threatened by any of Porygon2's moves.

Phazers: Zygarde-C, Ho-Oh, and Kyogre can all utilize a phazing move to disrupt Porygon2's Trick Room or Teleport attempts, making it extremely difficult for it to accomplish its goal.

Item Disruption: Knock Off and Trick can both be detrimental to Porygon2, especially so when it receives a Choice item from the likes of Calyrex-S and Calyrex-I.

Taunt: Aerodactyl, Mewtwo, and Grimmsnarl can shut down Porygon2's utility with Taunt, stopping it from setting Trick Room and pivoting with Teleport.

Trick Room Setter.description:
Trick Room is a potent tool against offensive teams and teams lacking proper defensive cores such as Yveltal, Necrozma-DM, and Eternatus. Teleport pairs up nicely with Trick Room, enabling Porygon2's slow teammates to shine. Analytic-boosted Foul Play will almost always OHKO Calyrex-S and disincentivizes offensive Necrozma-DM and Groudon from setting up. A physically defensive set is preferred over specially defensive to better check Psyshock Calyrex-S.

Porygon2 is exclusively seen on dedicated Trick Room teams. Other Trick Room setters such as Hatterene, Necrozma-DM, and Calyrex-I are great partners to keep Trick Room active for as long as possible. Slow and powerful wallbreakers that can take advantage of Trick Room such as Dracovish and Melmetal appreciate Porygon2. Despite not being very slow, Choice Specs Kyogre fits the Trick Room playstyle quite nicely, further enabling Dracovish's wallbreaking potential and being a sturdy check to Necrozma-DM and Zygarde, while also being a fierce wallbreaker in its own right.

Specially Defensive.description:
Porygon2 can function decently as a defensive pivot thanks to its great support movepool, Eviolite-boosted bulk, and amazing ability. Teleport allows Porygon2 to reliably get in powerful wallbreakers while sparing them from taking direct damage. Ice Beam is generally the preferred attacking move because it OHKOes Noivern and Flygon, while also 2HKOing Roserade and Golurk. Tri Attack is a decent alternative that does more to the likes of Xurkitree, Raikou, and Starmie. Toxic cripples the likes of Milotic, Rhyperior, and Raikou, mitigating their long-term impact against Porygon2's teammates. Foul Play is an attacking option to hit Metagross and Alolan Marowak, while also letting Porygon2 check Polteageist much easier. A specially defensive spread allows Eviolite Porygon2 to blanket check many dangerous special attackers, such as Xurkitree, Toxtricity, and Roserade. Some Defense investment can be used to make Porygon2 a better pivot into the likes of Dhelmise and Flygon should its team need it. Trace allows Porygon2 to copy great abilities, like Regenerator from Reuniclus and Punk Rock from Toxtricity.

Porygon2 pairs very well with most offensive Pokemon, as it's able to absorb damage and switch them in safely with Teleport. Toxtricity, Pangoro, Golurk, and Heracross are powerful wallbreakers that enjoy having Porygon2 to fall back on when they're forced out by certain special attackers, such as Noivern. Pokemon such as Dhelmise and Starmie can remove entry hazards, which otherwise hamper Porygon2's ability to pivot and forces it to use Recover more often. A pivoting core can also be powerful, especially with the likes of Flygon, Incineroar, and Raikou, as it can keep Porygon2 in favorable situations. Powerful Fighting-types such as Heracross, Pangoro, and Lucario can take advantage of Porygon2's inability to generally threaten them. The aforementioned Togekiss and Galarian Weezing fare well against Heracross and Pangoro, while Jellicent can handle Lucario. In turn, Porygon2 can easily handle most Toxtricity variants and other Electric types. Togekiss can even provide Defog and Heal Bell support, while Galarian Weezing can handle most Knock Off users.

Physically Defensive.description:
Porygon2 is a great physically defensive option available to Normal teams with the ability to utilize Teleport and check Dragon Dance Dragapult, Mimikyu, and Jirachi, which would all otherwise prove very threatening for Normal. Recover provides Porygon2 with a reliable form of healing for it to continually switch into attacks from Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Excadrill and Mimikyu. Foul Play acts both as a countermeasure for Pokemon like Scizor and Azumarill that would otherwise use Porygon2 as setup bait and as an attacking move to hit other powerful physical threats like Alolan Marowak and Excadrill. Ice Beam gives Porygon2 good coverage to deal with Dragon threats like Hydreigon and Noivern more easily as well as certain other offensive threats like Diggersby and Hawlucha. Toxic allows Porygon2 to wear down defensive Pokemon like Mandibuzz and Gastrodon that may otherwise attempt to switch in. Teleport is another option to be considered, as it allows Porygon2 to bring in frail offensive Normal-type threats like Diggersby, Heliolisk, and Indeedee-M safely and create momentum. Discharge can be an option to run over Toxic as good coverage for hitting Flying- and Water-type threats like Corviknight and Pelipper with a sizable chance to paralyze notable threats for Normal teams such as Calm Mind Keldeo and Bulk Up Urshifu-R, which would otherwise use Porygon2 as setup fodder. Trace is generally the preferred ability due to the potential of copying abilities like Natural Cure from Chansey, Regenerator from Toxapex and Amoonguss, and Intimidate from Krookodile, all of which increase Porygon2's survivability. Maximum investment in HP and Defense with a Bold nature is used to have Porygon2 perform its best as a physical wall against threats like Excadrill and Scizor.

Most if not all Pokemon on Normal appreciate Porygon2's ability to deal with physical threats. Blissey in particular forms an excellent defensive core with Porygon2 due to being especially weak to offensive physical threats. Porygon2 in return appreciates Blissey's role as a special wall to help deal with strong special threats that itself cannot hold off like Kingdra in rain and Volcarona. If Porygon2 is running Teleport, frail offensive threats like Diggersby and Indeedee-M appreciate its ability to bring them in safely without leaving them open to attacks and status moves. Braviary helps Porygon2 deal with hard-hitting threats that have Fighting-type coverage like Heracross and Rillaboom. Porygon2 is especially susceptible to all forms of entry hazards, particularly Toxic Spikes, due to their ability to quickly wear down Porygon2 and reduce its ability of switching into attacks reliably. As a result, Porygon2 along with the entire Normal team appreciates Braviary's ability of keeping hazards off through the use of Defog. Ditto makes for a good partner due to its ability to punish offensive setup sweepers that may use Porygon2 as setup fodder like Belly Drum Azumarill, Swords Dance Excadrill, and Bulk Up Urshifu-S. Ditto and Porygon2 also work well together due to their ability to PP stall Poison and Water teams by copying Regenerator from Pokemon such as Toxapex and Amoonguss. Heliolisk provides Porygon2 with an easier time against Water due to its great ability in Dry Skin for absorbing powerful Water-type attacks from wallbreakers like Dracovish. Bewear appreciates Porygon2's ability to mitigate its low Speed by paralyzing faster Pokemon like Hydreigon and Kyurem with Discharge. Porygon2 in return gains a partner to help deal with Steel- types like Corviknight and Ferrothorn that it would otherwise have a hard time dealing with.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: A+ Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are fantastic in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame, and can sweep, support, or wall significant portions of the metagame. These Pokemon require less support than most others to be used effectively and have few flaws that can easily be overlooked when compared to their positive traits.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Defensive.description:
• With recovery, BoltBeam coverage, and impressive defensive stats, Porygon2 is one of the best walls in the metagame.

  • Porygon2 has a highly contested final moveslot. Offensively, Tri Attack is a reliable STAB attack that does good damage to most switch-ins. Foul Play allows Porygon2 to punish Pokemon that boost their Attack stat, such as Mimikyu. Although seemingly odd, Giga Impact allows Porygon2 to effectively take advantage of an Attack boost from Download, surprising Calm Mind setters like Tapu Fini and Raikou with a boosted Max Strike after Dynamaxing.

  • For final support options, Trick Room is a highly effective way to support slow sweepers such as Glastrier, Celesteela, and Rhyperior. Substitute protects Porygon2 from status such as Leech Seed and Sleep. Thunder Wave is a more consistent option for paralysis spreading than Discharge.

  • Download gives Porygon2 a decent offensive presence, making it the prefered option. Trace is a usable alternative for punishing Intimidate Pokemon such as Landorus-T, and copying other useful abilities such as Beast Boost.

EV Spreads

  • 244 HP / 252 Def / 12 SpD with Bold: This spread allows Porygon2 to be an effective physical wall, useful against a wide variety of threats such as Landorus-T and Dragapult.

  • 244 HP / 12 Def / 252 SpD with Calm: This spread makes Porygon2 a great special wall, making it a good check against threats such as Zapdos and Galarian Moltres.

  • 244 HP / 232 Def / 32 Spe with Bold: Defensive Thunder Wave Porygon2 should use this spread to outspeed base 100 Speed Pokemon after paralysis.

  • 244 HP / 232 SpD / 32 Spe with Calm: Specially defensive Thunder Wave Porygon2 should use this spread to outspeed base 100 Speed Pokemon after paralysis.

  • 244 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Def / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Relaxed: Physically defensive Porygon2 with Giga Impact should use this spread for dealing good damage with a boosted Max Strike.

  • 244 HP / 4 Atk / 4 Def /252 SpD / 4 Spe with Sassy: Specially defensive Porygon2 with Giga Impact should use this spread to deal good damage with Max Strike.

Offensive.description:
• Thanks to Download, Porygon2 is a very effective bulky offensive threat.

  • Tri Attack is a great offensive option due to being a reliable STAB that hits most Pokemon neutrally. Alternately, Giga Impact makes Porygon2 a shockingly good mixed Dynamax sweeper that punishes Calm Mind Pokemon such as Raikou and Tapu Fini. Hyper Beam is a decent alternate option for a strong Max Strike while Dynamaxed as well.

  • Trick Room is an incredible support option that not only makes bulky sweepers such as Glastrier and Rhyperior much more deadly, but Porygon2 itself is fully capable of sweeping under it. Speed Swap is an interesting alternative that severely punishes fast Pokemon that stay in against Porygon2.

  • Porygon2 has many combinations of Attacks to consider, depending on the make-up of your team. When using Giga Impact, Porygon2 should always pair it with Ice Beam so it doesn't lose to Landorus-T. Porygon2 can function without a Normal-type STAB since boltbeam coverage hits so many Pokemon hard, but it does make it a more passive Pokemon. A Normal STAB and Thunderbolt offers good coverage, but can be annoyed by Dragapult who resists that combination.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Porygon2 can run Unaware and act as a physical wall with Foul Play, however it's outclassed by Mandibuzz due to its reliance on Eviolite. Unaware on its Trick Room set helps it punish physical setup Pokemon, however usually Porygon2 wants to pivot out as fast as possible to avoid wasting Trick Room turns. Magic Coat is an option to prevent Taunt, Roar, and Whirlwind from blocking Trick Room, but is heavily predicition reliant and generally leaves Porygon2 extremely passive.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-type Wallbreakers: Terrakion and Galarian Zapdos threaten to OHKO Porygon2, which either stops it from using Trick Room or Teleport safely.

Taunt: Taunt from Tapu Koko, Heatran, and Kommo-o prevents Porygon2 from doing its job, especially since they also take little from Foul Play.

*Offensive Substitute Users: Most Trick Room staples don't carry moves that can go through Substitute, preventing Porygon2 from pivoting into them, especially if they are threatened by the Substitute user. Substitute can also stall out valuable Trick Room turns. Examples of Substitute users include Mamoswine, Kommo-o and Chandelure.

Phazing Moves: Dragon Tail from Kommo-o and Whirlwind from Hippowdon go before Trick Room and thus denies Porygon2's ability to set it.

Trick Room Setter.description:
Porygon2 finds a place on Trick Room teams thanks to its rare combination of Trick Room and Teleport alongside its great bulk when boosted by Eviolite; additionally, it is one of the few Trick Room setters not weak to Ghost and Dark. Trick Room allows its teammates like Alolan Marowak and Conkeldurr to take advantage of their low Speed to create holes in the opposing team. Teleport is necessary to bring its partners in without taking any damage. Recover helps Porygon2 stay healthy to set Trick Room multiple times per game. Foul Play prevents foes such as Garchomp and Chandelure from taking advantage of it with setup moves or making it a complete sitting duck with Taunt, although Ice Beam is an option that hits Mandibuzz and Kommo-o harder. Regenerator mitigates some damage dealt while Porygon2 sets Trick Room. Maximum Special Defense investment is preferred for Porygon2 to better take special hits and pivot out, as strong Fighting-type wallbreakers in Terrakion and Galarian Zapdos still OHKO physically defensive variants.

Slow but powerful wallbreakers like Stakataka, Conkeldurr, and Galarian Slowking appreciate the free switch in Porygon2 provides for them. Alolan Marowak discourages Fighting-type moves from targeting Porygon2 and resists most common priority moves that can negate Trick Room like Horn Leech from Tapu Bulu and Draining Kiss from Togekiss, making it a particularly great partner. Since strong Fighting-type moves, especially Close Combat from the likes of Terrakion and Galarian Zapdos, can prevent Porygon2 from doing its job, Trick Room setters that resist Fighting such as Cresselia and Slowbro are necessary to ensure Trick Room can be reliably set up. Furthermore, Porygon2 is vulnerable to Taunt and these teammates can carry Oblivious or Mental Herb. Diancie is also a good partner thanks to its immunity to Dragon Tail and ability to set Stealth Rock.

doublesou.overview: Porygon2 manages to stand out as a reliable Trick Room setter and threatening late-game wincon thanks to its Eviolite-boosted defenses, access to Recover, and single weakness in Fighting. Download can allow it to provide some offensive pressure with its good coverage in Thunderbolt and Ice Beam should it get a Special Attack boost. Porygon2 is appreciated on semi-Trick Room teams. On these teams, Rillaboom provides Fake Out support and checks Urshifu-R, while Volcanion and Diancie benefit from Trick Room, with Diancie being a secondary setter. However, if lacking a Download boost, Porygon2 can find itself being ignored due providing subpar offensive pressure. Porygon2 also has to be cautious of Knock Off from Incineroar and Toxic from Blastoise, which can severely cripple it. Despite having one weakness, Porygon2 can be OHKOed by Life Orb Urshifu-R and overwhelmed by combinations of strong attacks from Pokemon like Zygarde and Heatran.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Icy Wind Porygon2 fits on more offensive teams that do not need Trick Room support. It can also use Ally Switch to cause the opponent to pay attention to it or make unnecessary reads, which can rectify its passivity problem. However, running Ally Switch means you need to give up either valuable coverage or pressure with Toxic.

Trick Room.description:
• Ice Beam is a good coverage option that allows Porygon2 to hit foes such as Rillaboom, Zygarde, and Dragapult. In combination with Thunderbolt, it can hit the entire tier for at least neutral damage.

  • Thunderbolt enables Porygon2 to pressure Tapu Fini, Volcanion, and Urshifu-R with super effective damage, while Toxic puts bulky walls like Assault Vest Kyurem-B and Porygon2, and setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Kyurem-B and Calm Mind Tapu Fini outside of Misty Terrain, on a timer.

  • Recover enables Porygon2 to stay healthy and consistently set up Trick Room, making it difficult to remove late-game once its main checks have been removed, such as Urshifu-R and Heatran.

  • Trick Room makes Porygon2 an excellent form of speed control, as it can turn the tables against faster threats such as Urshifu-R and deters setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Kyurem-B from setting up. Allies in Volcanion and Diancie benefit greatly from Trick Room support, as they then underspeed the majority of the metagame.

  • Download can often boost Porygon2's Special Attack due to the prevalence of Zygarde and Urshifu-R, which greatly improves its special moves, allowing it to OHKO Urshifu-R, Zygarde, and Dragapult at +1.

  • The given EV spread allows Porygon2 to OHKO Zygarde and Dragapult at +1, as well as making Choice Band Zygarde's Thousand Arrows into a 4HKO and Modest Charcoal Heatran only able to 3HKO.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Normal

Porygon2 can run Toxic over Hidden Power Fire or Teleport to pose an even bigger threat versus Water-, Flying-, and Ground-type teams by crippling Slowking, Zapdos, and Gastrodon, respectively. However, losing either standard move isn't desired. With Trace, Foul Play can be used over Discharge as a way to broadly check setup sweepers, but Discharge's coverage and paralysis chance are greatly appreciated, and the sweepers it checks can be dealt with Ditto or Porygon2's other moves.

Checks and Counters

Normal

Status: Toxic poison puts Porygon2 on a timer, greatly reducing its overall effectiveness as a wall. Burns, while much less of an issue, still hamper Porygon2's defensive capabilities by taking away its health continuously due to its lack of passive recovery.

Knock Off and Trick: Knock Off users like Bisharp and Mega Sableye remove Porygon2's Eviolite, diminishing its sky-high bulk and making it much more vulnerable. In addition to doing that, Trick from Choice-locked Pokemon like Latios and Blacephalon also locks Porygon2 into a single move, turning it into a liability.

Stallbreakers: Stallbreakers like Taunt Mew and SubToxic Zapdos can easily beat Porygon2 by either disabling its Recover or PP stalling it.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Although Porygon2's insane bulk on both sides lets it take on most wallbreakers, extremely powerful ones like Choice Band Victini and Choice Specs Tapu Lele easily shred it by scoring clean 2HKOes with their STAB moves.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types like Terrakion and Mega Gallade are able to easily take down Porygon2 by virtue of their STAB super effective attacks. However, Porygon2 is able to take a hit from most and retaliate with paralysis from Discharge.

Setup Sweepers: Certain setup sweepers like Mega Latias and Mega Gallade use Porygon2 as setup fodder, easily powering through it once they rack up a few boosts.

The Duck (Normal).description:
Porygon2 is the premier physically defensive wall available for Normal teams due to its combination of stellar bulk, reliable recovery, and a movepool that's able to keep important threats in check. Recover is Porygon2's go-to move, allowing it to stay healthy and provide its utility throughout the match. Ice Beam works as Porygon2's main attack, keeping key Ice-weak targets like Dragonite, Gliscor, and Landorus-T at bay. Discharge has a decent chance to cripple the opposition with paralysis while dealing good damage to Pokemon such as Pelipper, Celesteela, and Gyarados. It also forms the BoltBeam coverage alongside Ice Beam, which is capable of heavily denting Flying teams.
