Trapper-weak attackers like Ponyta and Abra benefit from Trapinch trapping and deterring Diglett and opposing Trapinch, and Ponyta also enjoys the removal of Onix. Natu and Koffing appreciate Trapinch as a safety net against Tyrunt and, in return, both check Grookey. Foongus enjoys the removal of Steel-types while checking Grookey and Water-types for Trapinch. Fighting-types and Poison-types appreciate Trapinch removing Abra.

ru.overview: Flygon's sheer versatility, excellent defensive typing and ability, and offensive potential make it one of RU's best offensive Electric-immune Pokemon, a top contender that can fit on many different teams. Dragon Dance Flygon is an immense threat that can set up against common Pokemon like Raikou. A Choice Band set gives more immediate wallbreaking power, but it is easier to play around due to both of its STAB options having immunities. When it comes to support, Flygon is one of the best Defoggers in the tier thanks to its favorable matchup against most prevalent entry hazard setters like Rhyperior and Metagross. Choice Scarf Flygon can proudly claim to be the tier's fastest Choice Scarf user and is a reliable revenge killer. Flygon excels as a pivot and almost always carries U-turn if lacking Dragon Dance. However, its average base Attack stat leaves it struggling to break through common defensive Pokemon like Gastrodon and Milotic, even when boosted. Flygon's typing also gives it an exploitable weakness to Ice-type coverage.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Throat Chop is an option to hit Bronzong and comes with the bonus of blocking Sylveon's Hyper Voice, but it has no other use, and it takes up a moveslot over Outrage. Flygon has an expansive special movepool and a passable Special Attack stat, but both fully special and mixed sets tend to struggle to push past Togekiss. A bulky Dragon Dance set with Roost can take advantage of Flygon's great defensive typing to accumulate multiple boosts, but it struggles to break through bulky Water-types even more than fully offensive sets already do. Scale Shot is an alternative STAB option over Outrage that boosts Flygon's Speed, which is especially useful on Choice Band sets to both wallbreak and clean up late-game, but its inconsistent power makes it a less desirable choice.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Water-types such as Milotic, Gastrodon, and Suicune are bulky enough to take even boosted attacks from Flygon and can KO back with Ice Beam, but they are 2HKOed by Choice Band Outrage on the switch and don't enjoy Toxic. Vaporeon has Heal Bell to heal off Toxic but struggles to reliably check Dragon Dance sets without Ice Beam. Unaware Quagsire hard counters Dragon Dance Flygon and can win against Choice Band sets with Curse.

Fairy-types: Togekiss can comfortably take on defensive and Choice Scarf Flygon, especially if it's carrying Heal Bell, but it struggles greatly with Dragon Dance and Choice Band sets. Rarer bulky Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Levitate Galarian Weezing can take on any set with relative ease. Gardevoir can copy Levitate with Trace, making it immune to both of Flygon's STAB moves, and has a good chance to survive even a +1 Life Orb-boosted Stone Edge. Mimikyu can safely revenge kill Dragon Dance Flygon thanks to Disguise, but other sets can break its Disguise scot-free with U-turn. Slurpuff can use Flygon as fodder to set up Belly Drum.

Priority Users: Golisopod can revenge kill Flygon with First Impression after it's been weakened a bit. Other priority users like Lucario, Toxicroak, and Entei can also revenge kill Flygon but need it to be even more weakened beforehand.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Pokemon such as Calm Mind Reuniclus, Vileplume, and Porygon2 have enough physical bulk to win the matchup against any of Flygon's sets, but they can't directly switch into its Choice Band set.

Bronzong: Bronzong completely walls Flygon because Levitate nullifies Earthquake and it resists Flygon's other moves. However, Bronzong can get worn down by repeatedly switching into U-turn, especially from Choice Band sets.

Dragon Dance.description:
After a Dragon Dance, Flygon outspeeds the majority of the metagame and every single Choice Scarf user besides opposing Flygon. Stone Edge is necessary to stand a chance of breaking through the most common Fairy-type Togekiss and also OHKOes Flying-types like Noivern and Crobat, saving Flygon from having to lock itself into Outrage. Life Orb is the preferred item to guarantee the OHKO on maximum HP Togekiss with +1 Stone Edge, but a Lum Berry can be used instead to set up on Pokemon like Raikou without being crippled by Toxic or a Scald burn. An Adamant nature can be used alongside Lum Berry to OHKO offensive Togekiss with boosted Stone Edge, but it sacrifices the Speed tie after a boost with opposing Choice Scarf Flygon.

Bulky Water-types such as Gastrodon and Milotic are major roadblocks for Flygon's sweeps, as they can take one hit and KO back with Ice Beam. Pokemon such as Raikou, Metagross, and Incineroar can put them on a timer with Toxic, making them easier to wear down into range of Flygon's boosted attacks. Grass-types like Roserade and Celebi can switch into Water-types while also making up for Flygon struggling to check Electric-types such as Raikou and Xurkitree. Roserade also provides Spikes support to whittle down Flygon's checks and counters. Celebi, on the other hand, appreciates Flygon removing Togekiss and can provide free switches with U-turn. Strong priority users like Golisopod and Lucario need to be dealt with before Flygon can attempt a sweep. Togekiss can check Golisopod while softening up the opposing team for Flygon with its Nasty Plot set or provide valuable support with Heal Bell and Wish. Crobat and Talonflame can help against Lucario, while also providing free switches with U-turn on Steel- and Rock-types that Flygon can force out and set up on. Chandelure, Golisopod, and Incineroar take care of Bronzong, which completely walls Flygon.

Defog.description:
Flygon can reliably remove entry hazards set by Pokemon like Metagross, Stakataka, and Roserade with Defog. Toxic cripples Pokemon Flygon otherwise can't touch like Togekiss, Noivern, and opposing Flygon. U-turn can be used instead to generate momentum against its switch-ins, which more offensive teams especially appreciate. Leftovers negates the damage from Stealth Rock and helps Flygon stay healthy throughout the match. Flygon can also forgo holding an item to nullify Poltergeist, which lets it soft check Pokemon like Golurk. 224 Speed EVs alongside a Jolly nature are used to outspeed Mimikyu, and the Attack EVs ensure the OHKO on Chandelure with Earthquake. The EV spread is quite customizable but should have a minimum of 80 Attack and 120 Speed EVs to outspeed and always OHKO Xurkitree with Earthquake.

Grass-types such as Roserade, Vileplume, and Celebi can switch in on bulky Water-types and also help Flygon deal with Electric-types like Xurkitree and Raikou, which carry Dazzling Gleam and Toxic, respectively. Pokemon such as Raikou, Metagross, and Incineroar commonly run Toxic, which hinders Flygon's ability to check them; cleric support from Togekiss, Diancie, or Umbreon can remedy this. Steel-types such as Metagross, Registeel, and Bronzong can take on Fairy-types such as Togekiss and Gardevoir. Flygon is unable to check Volcanion, unlike other Dragon-types like Noivern—Assault Vest Reuniclus, Gastrodon, and Starmie can patch up this weakness. Pokemon such as Noivern, Calm Mind Reuniclus, and Golisopod enjoy Flygon putting the likes of Togekiss, Gastrodon, and Milotic on a timer with Toxic. Toxic-less Flygon invites Pokemon such as Togekiss and Noivern in for free, which Pokemon like Xurkitree, Rhyperior, and Metagross can take advantage of off of Flygon's U-turn. Entry hazards often significantly limit Assault Vest Reuniclus, Suicune, and Heracross, so they appreciate Flygon as a Defogger.

Choice Scarf.description:
U-turn keeps up momentum and can provide free switches to teammates. Stone Edge hits Togekiss for decent damage. Outrage is Flygon's strongest STAB move to clean late-game and KOes Pokemon like Noivern and opposing Flygon. Toxic can be used instead to cripple switch-ins like Togekiss, Gastrodon, and Milotic. Defog is an option on offense teams in real need of emergency entry hazard removal, but Choice Scarf Flygon is generally a poor Defogger, as it's too weak to truly threaten standard entry hazard setters and it lacks longevity. 20 Special Defense EVs ensure that Flygon survives a Dazzling Gleam from Xurkitree.

Choice Scarf Flygon is a great glue for any team looking for an Electric- and Ground-immune Choice Scarf user. Bulky Water-types such as Gastrodon and Milotic can take any hit with ease and KO back with Ice Beam, so Pokemon such as Xurkitree, Starmie, and Calm Mind Reuniclus make great partners, taking advantage of them after Flygon's U-turn provides them with free entry. Grass-types such as Roserade, Vileplume, and Celebi can switch in on bulky Water-types and similarly appreciate Flygon providing free switches with U-turn. Wallbreakers like Xurkitree, Toxicroak, and Chandelure appreciate Flygon pivoting them in on Pokemon such as Togekiss, Bronzong, and Gastrodon. Steel-types such as Metagross, Registeel, and Bronzong can take on Fairy-types such as Togekiss, Gardevoir, and Sylveon. Gardevoir can be especially troublesome, as its access to Trace and Fairy typing mean it gets a free switch if Flygon locks into Earthquake or Outrage.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Flygon turns the tables on conventional switch-ins like Gastrodon and Milotic by 2HKOing them with Outrage. Stone Edge 2HKOes maximum HP Togekiss and has a good chance to OHKO Togekiss variants that don't have HP investment. U-turn takes advantage of its switch-ins like Bronzong by providing free switches to teammates, and it's a risk-free option against teams with multiple Pokemon immune to its STAB moves. First Impression, on the other hand, is a decently strong priority move and allows Choice Band Flygon to act as a revenge killer. It can also be used over Outrage or Stone Edge, but dropping either is generally not worth it.

Pokemon that tend to struggle with bulky Water-types like Gastrodon and Milotic, such as Metagross, Entei, and Sharpedo, appreciate Choice Band Flygon's ability to surprise and 2HKO them on the switch. However, while Flygon can 2HKO most bulky Water-types, it can't beat them one-on-one, so it appreciates Grass-types such as Roserade, Vileplume, and Celebi as teammates. In return, they appreciate Flygon pivoting them safely in against bulky Water-types with U-turn. Pivots such as Crobat, Xurkitree, and Tornadus are crucial, as they can position Flygon into favorable matchups to punch as many holes in the opposing team as possible. Steel-types such as Metagross, Stakataka, and Bronzong can take on Fairy-types like Togekiss and Gardevoir. Future Sight support from Assault Vest Reuniclus can ease the need to predict correctly, as Flygon can more safely lock itself into any move knowing that the incoming Pokemon will have to also take a Future Sight.

Defog.description: Speed investment allows it to outspeed base 90 Speed Pokemon such as Roserade and Lucario.

pu.overview: Altaria works well as a role compressor in PU thanks to its part-Dragon typing, fair bulk, and reliable recovery, which allow it to check even the most popular special attackers in the metagame, like Jellicent and Charizard. With access to both Defog and Heal Bell, Altaria can act well as entry hazard control and a cleric all in one. However, its typing leaves it weak to STAB and coverage moves from common Stealth Rock setters like Gigalith and Mesprit with Dazzling Gleam. It also tends to be quite passive, as it has neither pivot moves to gain momentum for its team nor a threatening offensive presence. On top of that, it's also easily overwhelmed due to its unimpressive stats, especially after its Heavy-Duty Boots has been removed.

Defog.description: Hurricane synergizes amazingly with Defog due to the latter lowering the foe's evasion, making Hurricane land more often. Flamethrower gets rid of Steel-types like Togedemaru, Ferroseed, and Perrserker while also hitting Grass-types like Eldegoss and Tangela. Toxic helps handle walls that neither Altaria nor its teammates can take care of easily, which may include Audino, Aromatisse, and Regirock. It especially helps against entry hazard setters like the aforementioned Regirock and Gigalith, as they have no reliable recovery, meaning Altaria wins in the long run. Even though hazard setters may have Toxic themselves, Heal Bell allows Altaria to get rid of it and act as a cleric for its entire team. Heavy-Duty Boots allows it to come in and out without worrying about Stealth Rock, letting it Defog and check Pokemon without having to constantly use Roost. The EVs critically allow Altaria to outspeed Modest Jellicent while still making it as specially bulky as possible. Altaria fits best on bulky offense or balance teams that have reliable checks to common hazard setters, so Pokemon such as Jellicent, Quagsire, Palossand, and Trevenant make for good partners. Notably, Aggron benefits from Altaria clearing hazards and bringing in Fairy- and Steel-types, as it takes care of them with Heavy Slam and Earthquake, respectively. Aggron also takes care of Pokemon like Ribombee, Glastrier, and Regirock so Altaria has an easier time on the field. A notable alternative set for Altaria is a Fire Spin plus Perish Song set. Even though it's quite gimmicky, relies on Fire Spin's imperfect accuracy, and needs the foe to lack a pivot move, it works well at taking care of foes.

zu.comments:
Other Options

The combination of Fire Spin and Perish Song lets Altaria trap and take out walls such as Musharna and Pyukumuku; however, this set lacks the utility of Defog and only traps a limited number of Pokemon. Draco Meteor is Altaria's strongest move, but it is less consistent than Hurricane and Dual Wingbeat due to the Special Attack drop. Heal Bell can be used on stall teams lacking a cleric.

Checks and Counters

Ice-types and Ice-type Coverage: Altaria's 4x weakness to Ice makes it extremely vulnerable to any Ice-type attacks. Altaria is threatened by Ice-types such as Abomasnow, Froslass, and Jynx, but it also has to watch out for Ice coverage from Poliwrath.

Rock-types: Rock-types such as Kabutops and Rhydon threaten Altaria with Stone Edge and can safely set up Stealth Rock versus Altaria.

Dragon-types: Due to its weakness to Dragon, powerful Dragon-type wallbreakers like Flapple and Appletun can break through Altaria with their STAB moves, even if they can't switch into Altaria's Hurricane.

Fairy-types: Fairy-types such as Clefairy and Alcremie pressure Altaria with their super effective STAB move, and they aren't pressured by Toxic thanks to Magic Guard and Aromatherapy, respectively. They can even take advantage of Altaria to set up with Calm Mind.

Setup Sweepers: While Altaria's bulk is great, it gets easily overwhelmed by strong attackers that can set up such as Silvally-Dark, Rotom-S, and Shiftry.

Physical Wall.description:
Altaria is a premier wall in ZU thanks to its ability to reliably answer powerful physical and special attackers such as Thwackey, Ninetales, Tangela, and Sawk. Toxic allows Altaria to put foes on a timer, letting it comfortably use Defog against entry hazard setters such as Piloswine and Miltank. Hurricane is Altaria's strongest STAB move, letting it threaten foes such as Qwilfish, Gurdurr, and Thwackey. Earthquake is an alternative that targets Toxic-immune foes such as Skuntank and Klinklang, while allowing Altaria to take on Fire-types more easily. The given EV spread allows Altaria to outspeed Adamant Piloswine and Jolly Rhydon and avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Thievul while maximizing its physical bulk.

Altaria is an excellent pick for balance and stall teams looking for a Defogger and a check to Fire-types. Offensive Fire-types like Rapidash and Ninetales can take advantage of Altaria's checks such as Clefairy, Rhydon, and Froslass while benefitting from Altaria walling opposing Fire- and Water-types. These two are also checks to Ice-types, and additional checks such as Piloswine, Poliwrath, and Miltank make for great partners, handling Altaria's biggest weakness. Other walls such as Pyukumuku, Rhydon, and Miltank appreciate Altaria's ability to absorb status for them; in return, they can handle threats that Altaria struggles with such as Jynx and Flapple. Choice Scarf users such as Sawk and Rotom can revenge kill the threats that can muscle through Altaria.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon

Facade can be used on the Dragon Dance set over Return due to Mega Altaria frequently getting status ailments, but without status, it is weaker than Return and usually not worthwhile.

Checks and Counters

Dragon

Steel-types: Steel-types like Jirachi and Excadrill can outpace Mega Altaria and take care of it with Iron Head. Pokemon like Celesteela, Aegislash, and Ferrothorn can tank any attacks from Mega Altaria and take care of it with their attacks. Mega Scizor is also a problem because it can take care of boosted Mega Altaria with Bullet Punch.

Poison-types: Poison-types such as Mega Venusaur and Galarian Weezing can take a boosted attack from Mega Altaria and KO it with Sludge Bomb or hinder it with Will-O-Wisp.

Phazers and Haze: Phazers and Haze users like Skarmory and Toxapex can get rid of Mega Altaria's boosts.

Fairy-types: Mega Diancie, Mimikyu, and Tapu Lele can outpace a unboosted Mega Altaria and OHKO it with their STAB attacks.

Ditto: Ditto is able to copy Mega Altaria's boosts and reverse sweep.

Dragon Dance (Dragon).description:
Mega Altaria is a fearsome setup sweeper thanks to its good bulk and Roost enabling it to set up with Dragon Dance, and its ability Pixilate makes it dominate Dark and Dragon matchups. It also gives Dragon-type teams a much needed Dragon immunity for mirror matchups. After Dragon Dance, Mega Altaria can outpace and take care of Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and non-Choice Scarf Greninja. Earthquake is used to hit Pokemon like Alolan Muk, Toxapex, and Heatran.

Teammates like Latias, Latios, and Hydreigon love Mega Altaria for threatening Dark and Fighting-types like Mega Sableye, Hydreigon, and Terrakion. Garchomp is a much needed partner to take care of Steel-types like Excadrill and Mega Scizor. It also takes care of Poison-types like Toxapex and provides Stealth Rock support. Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Kommo-o are vital to handle Steel-types that Mega Altaria cannot beat like Celesteela, Jirachi, and Skarmory. Dragonite can help with walls such as Blissey and Celesteela if running Choice Band or can use Dragon Dance to take care of Pokemon like Heatran and Mega Venusaur. Mega Altaria has trouble with Poison-types like Toxapex and Mega Venusaur, so it loves partners like Latios and Latias, which can also provide Defog support to get rid of troublesome entry hazards. Zygarde-10% and Duraludon greatly help against Fairy teams, taking care of Mega Diancie and Tapu Lele, which unboosted Mega Altaria struggles against.

Bulky Dragon Dance (Dragon).description:
Dragon Dance is able to turn Dark, Fighting, and Dragon matchups in Mega Altaria's favor while outpacing threats like Greninja and Keldeo after one Dragon Dance. Refresh is the preferred move in the last slot that allows Mega Altaria to freely set up on Pokemon that run status-inducing moves like Mega Sableye, Blissey, Porygon2, and Klefki. Heal Bell can be ran over Refresh to heal teammates' status as well. Natural Cure lets Altaria absorb status for teammates before Mega Evolving. 252 HP EVs allow Mega Altaria to set up on Porygon2 and Latias, while 16 Defense EVs allows Mega Altaria to be as bulky as possible. 240 EVs in Speed outpace Diggersby and Adamant Choice Band Dracovish.

All teammates love Mega Altaria for coming in on Dragon-type attacks, taking care of Mega Sableye and the defensive core of Blissey and Porygon2, and using Heal Bell. Mega Altaria loves Garchomp for taking care of Steel-types like Excadrill and Mega Scizor. Garchomp can also provide Stealth Rock support to make Mega Altaria able to sweep better. Pokemon like Hydreigon and Kommo-o to take care of Steel-types like Celesteela, Melmetal, and Jirachi. Mega Altaria has trouble with Poison-types like Mega Venusaur and Nidoking, so Latias and Kyurem are great partners. Mega Altaria has trouble with strong and fast Fairy-types like Mega Diancie and Tapu Koko, so Choice Scarf Duraludon and Dragalge can take care of them. Latios and Latias are great Defog users, while Latias can also use Healing Wish. Dragalge is good to provide Mega Altaria with Toxic Spikes, improving the Fairy matchup and making it easier for Mega Altaria to sweep.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Fire Blast can be run over Roost to lure in and break through Skarmory, Ferrothorn, and Mega Scizor; however, this trades away most of Mega Altaria's defensive utility for a mediocre sweeper set that's relatively easy to revenge kill and wear down, making this only a worthwhile option on hyper offense teams. Heal Bell or Refresh over Earthquake allows Mega Altaria to care much less about status, although the coverage loss is often not worth it. Other STAB options such as Facade and Body Slam can be used over Frustration, with the former letting Mega Altaria take advantage of being statused, and the latter spreading paralysis, although these are much more situational and inconsistent, making them less useful overall. Lastly, a bulky special attacking set utilizing Hyper Voice, Flamethrower, and a utility move could hone in on Mega Altaria's unique defensive capabilities but gets worn down incredibly easily and doesn't make much progress.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Mega Scizor and Skarmory hard wall Mega Altaria, taking negligible damage from both its attacks and healing up safely, and they can take advantage of it by either using Swords Dance or laying down Spikes. Other Steel-types such as Melmetal and Ferrothorn are also solid checks, but they are prone to being worn down by entry hazards and repeated Earthquakes.

Status Effects: Status completely neutralizes Mega Altaria. Poison and burn sink its longevity and damage output, and, although less detrimental than the former two, paralysis makes it much easier to revenge kill and reduces its setup opportunities. The rare Facade, Heal Bell, and Refresh make Mega Altaria much more resilient to status.

Faster Pokemon: Due to its middling Speed tier even at +1, Mega Altaria is still outsped and forced out by a plethora of faster Pokemon such as Weavile, Protean Greninja, Kartana, and common Choice Scarf users like Tapu Lele and Landorus-T after a boost. However, none of these Pokemon can safely switch in.

Fairy-types: Clefable can take unboosted hits from Mega Altaria and pressure it out with Moonblast and Thunder Wave, although it falters to two boosted Frustrations. Mega Mawile and Tapu Fini can take a boosted attack and retaliate if healthy but are unable to switch in safely. Other Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie and Tapu Koko outspeed it after a Dragon Dance and force it out if brought in safely, but they can't switch in on their own due to their frailty.

Bulky Dragon Dance.description:
Mega Altaria can be a potent wincon and also sports excellent defensive utility. Mega Altaria's solid natural bulk, Roost, and solid resistances make it a great check to Ash-Greninja, Zapdos, and non-Ice Beam Mega Latias, setting up freely on them. However, its average Speed tier and relatively poor damage output without multiple boosts make it mediocre in practice. Frustration is Mega Altaria's best attacking move, its already solid Base Power further bolstered by Pixilate and STAB, denting even resistant foes like Ferrothorn and Corviknight hard when boosted. Earthquake allows Mega Altaria to pressure Steel- and Poison-types, which resist Fairy, such as Toxapex, Heatran, and Melmetal. The given EV spread allows Mega Altaria to 2HKO defensive Clefable at +1, survive two Mega Lopunny Frustrations—allowing Mega Altaria to set up on it—and outspeed Pokemon such as Tapu Lele and Kyurem after a Dragon Dance. The remaining EVs are placed in Special Defense to take hits from Zapdos, Mega Charizard Y, and Ash-Greninja better.

Mega Altaria fits on bulky teams that can wear down its checks like Ferrothorn, Melmetal, and Mega Scizor to facilitate a late-game sweep. Pokemon such as Rotom-W, Toxapex, Ferrothorn, Slowbro, and Landorus-T all appreciate Mega Altaria's unique defensive utility; it either secondarily checks or outright handles threats like Ash-Greninja, Heatran, Mega Charizard Y, and Zapdos that force them out. In return, these Pokemon provide a solid defensive backbone against Steel- and Ice-types such as Mega Scizor, Melmetal, and Weavile. Entry hazards such as Spikes from Greninja and the aforementioned Ferrothorn enormously benefit Mega Altaria, as they help wear down its checks into range of its boosted attacks. Pokemon such as Heatran and Fightinium Z Kartana work extremely well with Mega Altaria, as they force out, pressure, and force damage on the Steel-types that check it. Magnezone in particular deserves a special mention, as it can instantly trap and remove pesky Steel-types such as Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn, paving the way for a Mega Altaria sweep. Volcarona with Psychic, Electrium Z Rotom-W, and Groundium Z Greninja bait in and remove Toxapex, which Mega Altaria can struggle to break through.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Lunatone has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Skuntank, Thievul, and Morpeko outspeed an unboosted Lunatone and threaten it with their STAB attacks.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio can switch into Lunatone's STAB attacks and threaten it out with their own. They need to be careful of Earth Power, however.

Priority users: Priority users such as Thwackey, Shiftry, and Qwilfish can revenge kill Lunatone with Grassy Glide, Sucker Punch, and Aqua Jet, respectively.

Choice Scarf users. Fast Choice Scarf users such as Gourgest-S and Alolan Persian can outspeed and revenge kill Lunatone even after a Rock Polish.

Meteor Beam.description:
Thanks to STAB Meteor Beam, Lunatone shines in ZU as a niche wallbreaker, boosting its Special Attack and muscling past any neutral foe in a single turn. Psyshock hits Pokemon such as Sawk and Qwilfish, and is its main STAB move once Power Herb has been used. Earth Power is the coverage move of choice, hitting Steel-types Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio, as well as Dark-types in Skuntank and Morpeko. Rock Polish allows Lunatone to outspeed common Choice Scarf users Sawk and Rotom and perform as a late-game cleaner. Stealth Rock is an option since Lunatone forces out common Defoggers like Articuno and Altaria.

Lunatone fits well on offense builds, benefiting teams that are centered around stacking entry hazards by threatening common Defog users such as Articuno and Altaria. Pokemon that appreciate Klinklang and Rapidash being weakened such as Alcremie, Jynx, and Thwackey benefit from Lunatone's presence. As Lunatone relies on Rock Polish to outpace offensive threats and is weak to common attacking types in the meta, pivots such as Thwackey, Articuno, and Type: Null are appreciated to bring it in safety and provide setup opportunities. Checks to Grass- and Water-types are much needed, so Pokemon such as Tangela, Appletun, and Articuno, respectively, work well. Dark-types such as Skuntank and Silvally-Dark are also great partners, resisting opposing Dark- and Ghost-type attacks that threaten Lunatone.

zu.overview: Solrock fails to be an effective physical wall and Stealth Rock setter due to its terrible stats and weakness-laden typing, meaning that even with full HP and Defense investment it often can't switch into common physically offensive threats like Sawk, Klinklang, and Qwilfish; as a result it is outclassed by the myriad of other excellent options like Palossand, Rhydon, and Miltank.

Physical Wall.description: Physically defensive Solrock aims to spread burn and set Stealth Rock while staying healthy with Morning Sun, chipping already statused switchins with Rock Slide, and punishing contact moves with Rocky Helmet. It ultimately isn't effective at this due to it being weak to common coverage and prone to getting 2HKOed, making it a liability for its team. Use Palossand, Rhydon, or Miltank instead.

zu.overview: Even with a decent typing and coverage options, Whiscash is a poor mixed attacker because it is too slow and not strong enough to threaten the opposition. This leads to it getting consistently walled by threats like Miltank and Alcremie. Other mixed attackers like Silvally-Poison and Silvally-Fighting have higher Speed and better coverage options to justify running, making them more consistent than Whiscash.

Mixed Attacker.description: Whiscash can threaten core Pokemon like both Stunfisk formes, Qwilfish, and Articuno with its decent coverage options. However, mixed attackers like Silvally-Poison and Silvally-Fighting can perform these roles but better due to their higher Speed and better coverage options, making them superior options to run over Whiscash.

uu.overview: Sporting a high Attack stat, Adaptability, and high-Base Power moves, Crawdaunt is an extremely powerful wallbreaker in UU capable of KOing even the bulkiest walls. Water + Dark is a deadly STAB combination that feasts on common defensive Pokemon like Hippowdon, Slowking, and Scizor, with resists to this combo like Primarina and Keldeo still taking massive damage from its Choice Band-boosted attacks. Access to a strong priority move in Aqua Jet allows Crawdaunt to bypass its low Speed and pick off targets such as Azelf and Thundurus-T, while Close Combat crushes Hydreigon and Zarude attempting to switch in. However, Crawdaunt is extremely slow, being outsped and KOed by common threats such as Cobalion and Keldeo. This, combined with its poor bulk and weaknesses to common typings, leaves it with limited opportunities to switch in and forces Crawdaunt to rely on pivots to facilitate its wallbreaking attempts.Crawdaunt faces competition as a Water-type wallbreaker from Keldeo, Primarina, and Azumarill, all of which sport superior defensive utility. However, Crawdaunt's STAB Knock Off is a relevant advantage that lets it break the likes of Amoonguss and Tangrowth more easily.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance with a Life Orb turns Crawdaunt into a terrifying wallbreaker, OHKOing physically defensive Tangrowth and Skarmory at +2. However, Crawdaunt's poor bulk and low Speed give it little chances to set up before being forced out, making Choice Band's immediate power preferred on most teams. Liquidation can be used over Crabhammer due to its better accuracy, but it's much weaker, failing to 2HKO foes like maximum HP Primarina.

Checks and Counters

Faster Water-resistant threats: Due to its low Speed, Crawdaunt is forced out by anything faster that can take a boosted Aqua Jet like Gyarados, Hydreigon, Rotom-W, and Salamence.

Grass-types: Both Amoonguss and Tangrowth can take a hit from Knock Off, though they have to be careful switching into it if they have their item at risk of being 2HKOed. Tapu Bulu resists Crawdaunt's STAB combination, allowing it to pivot into it multiple times and threaten to OHKO back. Zarude outspeeds Crawdaunt and resists a boosted Aqua Jet, allowing it to revenge kill Crawdaunt with ease.

Fighting-types: Though it would prefer to not switch in, Keldeo resists Crawdaunt's STAB combination and can OHKO it back. Conkeldurr is able to revenge kill Crawdaunt with Mach Punch. Cobalion takes Aqua Jet well and KOes Crawdaunt in return.

Choice Band.description:
Crabhammer and Knock Off cover the majority of the tier, destroying common Pokemon like Hippowdon, Celesteela, and Slowking. Aqua Jet allows Crawdaunt to threaten frailer faster foes like Azelf, Thundurus-T, and Choice Scarf Diggersby. Close Combat destroys Hydreigon and Zarude attempting to switch into Crawdaunt. Lash Out is an option to crush defensive Salamence attempting to switch into Crabhammer while being a solid alternative STAB to Knock Off.

Crawdaunt is intended to be used as an early- or mid-game wallbreaker on more offensive teams, tearing open defensive cores to allow its teammates to clean late-game. Pivots are essential to give Crawdaunt as many wallbreaking attempts as possible. Slowking is not only one of Crawdaunt's favorite targets, but an amazing teammate as well, defensively checking Keldeo and Noivern while also giving Crawdaunt safe entry with Teleport. Slowking also can provide Future Sight support to help Crawdaunt KO Pokemon like Salamence and Amoonguss that attempt to switch into it. Noivern, Choice Scarf Hydreigon, and Choice Scarf Diggersby can revenge kill faster threats like Cobalion, Zarude, and Raikou for Crawdaunt as well as bring it in against Hippowdon with U-turn. Scizor can bring in Crawdaunt with U-turn against threats like Celesteela as well as wear down Tangrowth and Salamence with Knock Off. It also answers Zarude. Entry hazard support is essential in wearing down bulky Pokemon due to Crawdaunt's inability to take a hit if it fails to KO its target. Nidoqueen and Hippowdon can provide Stealth Rock support for Crawdaunt, with the former checking foes like Thundurus-T and Hydreigon and the latter threatening Grass- and Fairy-types like Tangrowth, Tapu Bulu, and Primarina. Entry hazard removal from Pokemon like Tentacruel and Salamence keep Crawdaunt from being worn down by entry hazards, boosting its longevity. Defensive Grass-types like Amoonguss and Assault Vest Tangrowth can defensively answer revenge killers to Crawdaunt like Primarina, Thundurus-T, and Keldeo. Pokemon that can spread paralysis such as Nihilego and Togekiss can help Crawdaunt bypass its low Speed. Late-game cleaners like Zygarde-10% and Swords Dance Cobalion appreciate Crawdaunt's wallbreaking and can finish off weakened foes like Skarmory while also keeping faster threats like Hydreigon and Zarude in check throughout a game.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Dance can be used instead of Swords Dance to give Crawdaunt a chance to improve its middling Speed, but this set is largely outclassed, as you lose out on the extreme wallbreaking power Swords Dance provides, and the Speed isn’t enough to help it sweep without multiple boosts. Even then it is prone to revenge killing due to its pitiful bulk.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Bulky Grass-types such as Tangrowth, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Venusaur can switch into Crawdaunt’s moves with relative ease and force it out, and offensive Grass-Types such as Rillaboom, Kartana, and Serperior can all revenge kill Crawdaunt. Tapu Bulu is an exceptionally good check, as it is resistant to both of Crawdaunt’s STAB moves, has reliable recovery, and can run a Z-Crystal to negate the damage increase from Knock Off, while still outspeeding it with minimal investment to KO it.

Faster Pokemon: Generally the best way to deal with Crawdaunt is by forcing it out with a faster check such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, or Kyurem, as Crawdaunt lacks consistent defensive counterplay that don’t get shredded by its spammable STAB moves.

Hydreigon: Hydreigon is one of the few Pokemon that can switch into both of Crawdaunt‘s STAB moves and heal them off while also forcing Crawdaunt out.

Bulky Water-types: Pokemon such as Mega Gyarados and Tapu Fini can both switch into Crawdaunt‘s STAB moves and threaten it out with a burn or outright KO it; however, Tapu Fini hates losing its Leftovers, as it is its main form of recovery.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Crawdaunt is a potent wallbreaker, demolishing slower teams with Swords Dance and Adaptability while revenge killing faster Pokemon with a boosted Aqua Jet, as most teams lack a defensive answer to its power and STAB moves. It even eviscerates defensive Pokemon like Clefable, specially defensive Toxapex, and Ferrothorn. However, its middling Speed and bulk limit its switch-in opportunities. Knock Off is Crawdaunt’s most spammable move, letting it cripple switch-ins by removing their items and KOing the bulky Grass-types that attempt to tank a boosted hit. Crabhammer nets KOs on Dark-resistant Pokemon such as Clefable and Mega Tyranitar. Aqua Jet lets Crawdaunt pick off weakened foes, clean late-game, and revenge kill Pokemon like Volcarona and Mega Diancie that would otherwise end a sweep. Waterium Z is the preferred item, as it gives Crawdaunt a one-time nuke on many of its usual switch-ins and almost always KOes a neutral target, while Life Orb is a secondary option to pull off ridiculous feats such as OHKOing physically defensive Tangrowth and Toxapex after a boost.

Crawdaunt fits on bulky offense teams that can safely bring it in multiple times throughout the match; it therefore appreciates slow pivoting from the likes of Corviknight, Slowbro, and Slowking. Reliable speed control such as Mega Lopunny complement this further by helping to deal with faster teams, while Crawdaunt shreds through bulkier teams for them. As Crawdaunt is prone to being revenge killed by even resisted and neutral hits due to its pitiful defences, a strong defensive core to fall back on complements it perfectly. Specifically, checks to offensive Grass-types such as Rillaboom, Kartana, and Serperior such as Corviknight and Zapdos deny these Pokemon a free boost or KO each time it comes in. Lastly, other wallbreakers such as Rillaboom and Tapu Koko work with it amazingly, softening up the opponent’s team early on for Crawdaunt to clean late-game.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Crawdaunt is one of the hardest Pokemon to switch into in the tier due to its enormous, Adaptability-boosted immediate power and nearly unresisted STAB combination. However, its middling Speed and bulk limit its ability to switch in. Aqua Jet is Crawdaunt’s main way of damaging faster foes that threaten to revenge kill it such as Mega Lopunny, Zeraora, and Tapu Koko, doing over half to all three of them. Knock Off synergizes well with Crabhammer due to most of the tier’s Dark-resistant Pokemon fearing Crabhammer, which is also Crawdaunt's hardest hitting move. Crunch is the usual fourth option for Choice Band Crawdaunt, as it provides a secondary STAB option if the target has already lost its item or uses a Mega Stone or Z-Crystal. Close Combat is an extremely niche option and is used for nailing Hydreigon, which can switch in to scout Crawdaunt’s move, and Ferrothorn.

Crawdaunt fits perfectly on VoltTurn teams that can repeatedly bring it in to further pressure the opponent. A good defensive core that focuses on bringing Crawdaunt in is a must, with Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Corviknight, Slowbro, and Slowking as Crawdaunt is extremely susceptible to being revenge killed and is a huge momentum sink after getting a KO. Other than that, fast threats pair well with Crawdaunt such as Tapu Koko and Mega Lopunny, helping Crawdaunt pressure and soften up offensive teams for it to clean.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

A set with Swords Dance and Life Orb or Muscle Band can be used to snowball through slower teams such as Poison and Steel teams, as Crawdaunt's STAB moves KO walls such as Toxapex and Ferrothorn at +2 after minimal chip damage, while Aqua Jet takes on faster threats such as Nidoking and Excadrill.

Choice Band (Dark).description:
With a high base Attack stat in conjunction with a phenomenal ability in Adaptability, Choice Band Crawdaunt serves as a hard-hitting wallbreaker for Dark teams. Knock Off is Crawdaunt's most powerful and most spammable Dark-type STAB move, allowing it to remove items from targets. Crabhammer is the strongest Water-type STAB move backed by Adaptability, cleanly OHKOing the likes of physically defensive Hippowdon and 2HKOing physically defensive Mandibuzz and defensive Corviknight. Aqua Jet makes up for Crawdaunt's low Speed and additionally allows it to pick off weakened or frail Pokemon such as Alolan Raichu, Gardevoir, Galarian Darmanitan, and Zeraora. Close Combat serves as a stronger means of hitting Ferrothorn as well as threatens Normal teams, as no Normal-type can switch into it. Alternatively, Crunch allows Crawdaunt to maintain the 2HKO on an itemless Toxapex. Crawdaunt should be brought into the battle to wallbreak with pivoting moves such as U-turn or through double switches, as it cannot switch into attacks due to its lackluster bulk. Maximum Attack investment in conjunction with an Adamant nature while holding a Choice Band allows Crawdaunt to hit as hard as possible. Maximum Speed investment allows Crawdaunt to outspeed defensive Rotom-W and defensive Mandibuzz.

Tyranitar is able to provide Stealth Rock support, which wears the opposing team down and allows Crawdaunt to wallbreak more easily. Tyranitar can also cripple threats such as Mew, Gardevoir, and Indeedee-M with Thunder Wave, allowing Crawdaunt to outspeed them and making up for its lackluster Speed tier. Mandibuzz can switch into Pokemon such as Flygon, Virizion, and Excadrill that threaten Crawdaunt greatly, Defog away entry hazards such as Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web that hinder Crawdaunt, and allow Crawdaunt to safely get into the battle with U-turn. Weavile and Bisharp appreciate Crawdaunt's wallbreaking abilities, as they all share similar checks. Weavile is able to beat Dragon-types such as Kommo-o and Noivern, while Bisharp is able to defeat Fairy-types such as Galarian Weezing and Hatterene. Additionally, Crawdaunt is able to wallbreak and punch holes through teams early-game, allowing Bisharp to sweep late-game. Dual screens Grimmsnarl makes up for Crawdaunt's poor bulk, allowing it to take hits more easily, while Bulk Up Grimmsnarl appreciates Crawdaunt's wallbreaking capabilities weakening Pokemon like Toxapex and allowing it to sweep more easily. Drapion is able to threaten Fairy-types such as Primarina, Togekiss, and Whimsicott, which all threaten Crawdaunt, in addition to providing Toxic Spikes support for Crawdaunt to wallbreak more easily. Incineroar is able to switch into Grass- and Fairy-type attacks and can provide Crawdaunt with a slow U-turn to enter the battle safely.

Choice Band (Water).description:
Crawdaunt is an incredible wallbreaker that fits on both balance and rain teams and can break through teams of many types such as Poison, Water, and Psychic. Knock Off is its most spammable move and can 2HKO walls like Toxapex and Slowbro, which can annoy rain sweepers, as well as removing important items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite. Crabhammer offers more power and threatens Dark-resistant walls like Galarian Weezing, Mandibuzz, and Clefable. Close Combat is a good coverage move for Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Melmetal. Crunch can be used instead to guarantee high, reliable damage after Knock Off removes a foe's item. It's especially helpful against bulky archetypes such as Poison and Water stall teams, notably 2HKOing Toxapex and Amoonguss even after they lose their items. Aqua Jet helps Crawdaunt compensate for its low Speed, pick off weakened foes, and potentially OHKO Gengar, Nihilego, Thundurus-T, and Choice Specs Tapu Koko after Stealth Rock in rain. An Adamant nature with maximum Speed EVs is enough to outpace slower Pokemon like Clefable, Swampert, uninvested Rotom-W, and Mantine.

Pokemon such as Slowking, Slowbro, and Rotom-W that can pivot Crawdaunt into annoying walls are great teammates; Slowbro and Slowking can also provide Future Sight support, which helps Crawdaunt break through Poison teams, especially if it isn't running Crunch. Swampert provides an immunity to Electric, Stealth Rock support, and Flip Turn to pivot Crawdaunt in safely. Toxapex can check Grass-, Fairy- and Fighting-types, such as Tapu Bulu, Clefable, and Terrakion, and carry Eject Button on rain teams to pivot Crawdaunt in against slower threats. Pelipper is a reliable Defog user and activates rain, which can allow Crawdaunt to spam Aqua Jet and Crabhammer, 2HKOing Pokemon such as Amoonguss. Urshifu-R can overwhelm Steel-types if Crawdaunt is lacking Close Combat, threaten Ice-types such as Kyurem, and use U-turn to avoid losing momentum by bringing Crawdaunt into Psychic-types such as Slowbro. As Crawdaunt is slow, faster teammates such as Barraskewda and Choice Scarf Tapu Fini can clean up teams late-game.

pu.overview: Claydol's unique qualities, movepool, and typing allow it to function as an interesting form of role compression on teams. It has access to Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin, making it a solid choice for either a Stealth Rock setter or a defensive spinner, although it cannot threaten most Ghost-types. Its typing and Levitate give it important resistances to Poison-, Psychic-, and Rock-type moves, letting it pivot into these moves from Pokemon such as Weezing, Mesprit, and Aggron, as well as two important immunities to Electric and Ground; these make it a stop to Volt Switch pivots and Pokemon locked into Earthquake in a pinch, as it fares badly against most of them otherwise. However, Claydol is very passive, heavily relying on Toxic to maintain a presence. It is forced to choose between two STAB moves that are exploitable, meaning it can struggle against foes such as Golbat and Togedemaru depending on the move it chooses. Its typing is also a double-edged sword, with weaknesses to Grass, Dark, Water, and Bug, making it easy to exploit by Pokemon such as Gourgeist and Absol, and many of the Pokemon it would like to check can run these moves. Claydol also lacks recovery if it forgoes Leftovers, meaning it can be hard to check what it wants to over a long match.

Defensive.description: Psychic has solid neutral coverage as Claydol's STAB move, letting it chip Flying-types such as Archeops and Charizard, but makes it harder to threaten Dark-types. Scorching Sands can be chosen as its STAB move due to its ability to spread burns and hit Dark-types, but it loses to Pokemon such as Golbat and Weezing. Teleport allows Claydol to gain momentum against Pokemon it forces out such as Choice-locked Togedemaru. Alternatively, Protect and Leftovers give Claydol more recovery, increase Toxic damage, and scout opposing Choice-locked Pokemon. However, this gives it a worse matchup against Knock Off users such as Absol and Gallade due to the lack of Colbur Berry. The Speed investment is to guarantee outspeeding fully invested base 80s after a Rapid Spin, such as Gallade and Mesprit, crippling them with a Toxic before they can respond. Claydol likes to have defensive support from Pokemon that can handle special attackers like Rotom, Charizard, and Basculin. Lanturn can take hits from all of them and cripple them with Toxic, and Assault Vest Lanturn specifically can soak up general special hits for Claydol. Ferroseed is another option, functioning as a Toxic sponge that can also check Grass- and Water-types. In return, Claydol can reduce the chip damage Lanturn takes with Rapid Spin and deal with Ground-types such as Sandaconda for both of them. Claydol often best fits on more defensive teams due to its lack of recovery, supportive capabilities, and lacking offensive presence; as such, it appreciates the cleric and Wish support Pokemon such as Aromatisse and Audino can give it.

monotype.overview:
Grass

Cradily is a great support option for Grass teams because of its utility options in Stealth Rock and Toxic, part-Rock typing that provides neutrality to Flying- and Fire-type attacks, and ability in Storm Drain to absorb Water-type attacks. Its part-Rock typing in conjunction with its high Special Defense and reliable recovery betters its ability to take on special attackers like Volcarona, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T. It forms a great defensive core with Amoonguss and Ferrothorn, with all covering each others' weaknesses fairly well. However, Cradily's typing leaves it susceptible to threats like Fighting-, Steel-, and Ice-types like Terrakion, Scizor, Galarian Darmanitan, and Glastrier. Its poor offensive stats give setup sweepers like Excadrill, Rillaboom, and Dragapult opportunities to set up with ease.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Grass

Earthquake is an option over Toxic to hit Poison- and Steel-types like Dragalge, Nidoking, Heatran, and Magnezone, but be aware of Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain being active. Heavy-Duty Boots is another effective way to keep Cradily healthy, since Grass normally doesn't run entry hazard removal.

Checks and Counters

Grass

Poison-types: Poison-types like Galarian Weezing and Toxapex are immune to Toxic and aren't bothered by Cradily's Rock Blast. They can also hinder its recovery with Will-O-Wisp or Toxic.

Status: Cradily should be cautious of status, particularly Toxic and burns, because the former limits it as a reliable defensive switch-in and the latter halves the damage of Rock Blast.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Celesteela, Excadrill, and Aegislash can easily take Rock Blast repeatedly, are immune to Toxic, and can KO Cradily with their Steel-type attacks. Setup sweepers like Bisharp and Scizor can additionally set up. However, Earthquake can deal with Pokemon like Heatran and Magnezone.

Wallbreakers: Physical wallbreakers like Choice Band Zeraora and Choice Band Rillaboom can OHKO Cradily with their STAB attacks or super effective coverage moves, while special wallbreakers like Choice Specs Hydreigon can heavily dent Cradily.

Specially Defensive (Grass).description:
Rock Blast hits Flying-, Ice-, Bug-, and Fire-types like Zapdos, Alolan Ninetales, Araquanid, and Volcarona and helps with Pokemon that commonly set up Substitute like Galarian Moltres, Hydreigon, and Kyurem. Kyurem, in particular, can stall out other Rock-type STAB moves due to Pressure. Toxic allows Cradily to cripple potential switch-ins, bulkier Pokemon like Hippowdon, Mandibuzz, and Porygon2 that can recover off damage from Rock Blast, and setup sweepers like Hydreigon that may try using it as setup bait. Cradily can reliably stall foes with Toxic thanks to Recover. Storm Drain allows Cradily to pivot into Water-type attacks and prevents Scald burns from Pokemon like Toxapex. Maximum Special Defense and HP investment along with a Careful nature gives Cradily the best matchup against special attackers like Volcarona and Kyurem.

All of Cradily's teammates appreciate its ability to set up Stealth Rock, which allows sweepers like Rillaboom and Zarude to secure KOs mid- or late-game and hampers threatening Fire- and Flying-types. Rillaboom and Zarude can take care of Steel-types like Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Bisharp with their Fighting-type attacks, while Cradily can get rid of threats like Volcarona and Togekiss with Rock Blast. Choice Band Rillaboom can break past defensive cores that threaten Cradily such as Toxapex + Pelipper and Galarian Slowking + Slowbro. Rillaboom also sets Grassy Terrain for Cradily, giving it passive recovery, and is able to get rid of Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Zapdos and Mantine with Knock Off, resulting in Stealth Rock wearing down teams more effectively. Bulk Up Zarude can pressure defensive Pokemon like Toxapex and Blissey, which easily wall Cradily or threaten it with Toxic, and KO Psychic- and Ghost-types like Victini and Dragapult. Ferrothorn forms a defensive core with Cradily, setting Spikes and dealing with Ice- and Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales, Cloyster, and Tapu Lele with Gyro Ball. Its part-Steel typing gives a neutrality against Bug-type attacks and allows it to pivot into Toxic. Ferrothorn also deals with physical attackers like Excadrill for Cradily, while Cradily deals with special attackers like Nidoking in return. Amoonguss absorbs Toxic Spikes that could hinder Cradily's recovery, spreads status ailments with Spore, Stun Spore, and poison from Sludge Bomb, and switches into Fighting-type attacks from Terrakion and Keldeo that could OHKO Cradily. Celebi and Whimsicott can also deal with Fighting-types that threaten Cradily with Psychic and Moonblast, respectively. Whimsicott also helps in the Dark- and Dragon-type matchups, as it can KO Pokemon like Hydreigon, Kyurem, and Dragapult with Moonblast and provides an immunity to Dragon. Rotom-C can get rid of Flying-types like Skarmory, Celesteela, and Taunt Mandibuzz with Thunderbolt, which Cradily fails to do much against, and break through defensive cores that overpower Cradily with Nasty Plot. Choice Scarf Rotom-C can also revenge kill faster Pokemon like Garchomp and Alolan Ninetales and bring Cradily safely into the field with Volt Switch.

zu.overview: Armaldo may look appealing to use thanks to its high Attack and access to Knock Off and Rapid Spin. However, its horrific Speed, lack of reliable recovery, and many defensive weaknesses make it a poor utility Pokemon. It is outclassed by other utility Pokemon like Kabutops and Coalossal, since both of them have better typings and movepools to use.

Offensive Utility.description: Armaldo attempts to keep up Stealth Rock and either threaten the opposition with Knock Off or clear entry hazards on its side with Rapid Spin. Unfortunately, its awful Speed, poor defensive profile, and lack of reliable recovery make it a bad utility Pokemon. Kabutops and Coalossal outperform it due to their superior typings and movepools.

ru.overview: Milotic is a solid all-purpose bulky Water-type in the RU tier. This is thanks to a great combination of mixed defenses, good movepool, decent Speed as a defensive Pokemon, and an ability that actually gives it a benefit from being hit by status moves. Flip Turn even allows Milotic to be used on faster-paced teams, as it becomes a bulky Pokemon that can actually build or maintain momentum. Milotic's ability to check powerful threats like Flygon, Rhyperior, Noivern, and Metagross is very welcome on many teams. However, Milotic finds itself in a tier where Electric- and Grass-types, such as Raikou, Heliolisk, Celebi, and Roserade, are incredibly potent. While Milotic's ability to take hits of all kinds is relatively uncommon for defensive Pokemon, it does mean that extremely powerful wallbreakers, such as Lucario and Heracross, can use their powerful STAB moves to brute force their way past Milotic.
ru.comments:
Other Options

A Competitive set can be a Defog deterrent on Spikes stacking teams, as the common Defoggers do not generally fare well against a Milotic with boosted Ice Beam. Marvel Scale might make Flame Orb strategies look appealing, but the constant chip damage forces Milotic to use Recover way too often.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: RU is not short on Electric-types, and all of them can simply push past Milotic's defenses with powerful STAB moves. Raikou and Xurkitree aren't scared of Scald nor hindered too badly by a potential Toxic, as they rarely stay in long. Toxtricity is more vulnerable to Flip Turns as it switches in due to its much lower Speed, but similarly threatens out Milotic if it safely switches in and is immune to Toxic. Heliolisk is perhaps the worst enemy of Milotic thanks to Dry Skin even cutting off Milotic's ability to pivot out with Flip Turn as Heliolisk switches in.

Grass-types: Celebi, Roserade, and Decidueye easily handle Milotic. Celebi's Natural Cure can make Toxic and Scald burns a non-factor for it, while Roserade's Natural Cure and secondary Poison typing work similarly. Both can utilize their powerful Grass-type STAB moves to eliminate Milotic. To make matters worse, Celebi can set up Nasty Plot, while Roserade can litter the field with Spikes to undermine Milotic's bulk later on.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Milotic's good but not spectacular mixed bulk means that very powerful wallbreakers can push past it. Guts Heracross, Swords Dance Lucario, and Nasty Plot Togekiss are all strong enough to overcome Milotic with powerful neutral STAB moves.

Defensive.description:
Milotic's great typing and mixed defenses allow it to take both physical and special hits quite well. Flip Turn generally is preferred to generate and maintain momentum as a defensive Pokemon, something that is generally uncommon. This is especially helpful on faster-paced teams that would rather have Milotic stay a step ahead of threats like Raikou and Roserade. Ice Beam prevents Grass-types from switching into Milotic as freely, discouraging Roserade from using Spikes freely. It also OHKOs Noivern and Flygon. Toxic is able to cripple defensive Pokemon such as Gastrodon and opposing Milotic, which can help Milotic's more offensive teammates push past them. It also is great for chipping away at common switch-ins like Raikou and Xurkitree. Haze is a great alternative that allows Milotic to stall out Substitute + Protect variants of Suicune lacking Toxic as well as prevent Calm Mind Reuniclus and Cosmic Power Metagross from taking advantage of Milotic's low damage output. On more defensive teams, Haze is a solid option over Flip Turn or Ice Beam, as these teams generally don't care as much about momentum as they do about covering as many offensive threats as possible. Milotic's 88 Speed EVs enable it to outpace Adamant Incineroar and Bewear.

As Milotic is a defensive Pokemon that can maintain momentum, it can work on faster-paced teams that appreciate having it as a defensive backbone when they're forced out by certain Pokemon. Xurkitree and Raikou are powerful Electric-types that can threaten the majority of the tier and appreciate Milotic being able to bring them in safely. VoltTurn cores with the likes of Flygon, Incineroar, Xurkitree, and Heliolisk are also powerful on more offensive teams that aim to maintain momentum. Roserade is a great check to most Electric-types, can spare Milotic from Toxic from bulky Water-types, and litter the field with Spikes to amplify the effects of Flip Turn. In return, Milotic is able to check offensive Steel-types and multiple Fire-types. Registeel is able to set up Stealth Rock, check Gardevoir and most Electric- and Grass-types, and appreciates Milotic being able to switch into most Fire- and Ground-types looking to take on Registeel. Crobat and Togekiss are able to take on the likes of Heracross and Pangoro for Milotic. Crobat can even handle Roserade and clear the field of entry hazards, which can force Milotic to use Recover more often that it would like.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Milotic can run Ice Beam instead of Scald to more reliably damage targets weak to it, such as Garchomp and Zygarde-10%. Instead of Assault Vest, it can also run Heavy-Duty Boots to stop entry hazards from wearing it down or Leftovers to gain passive recovery but becomes far less capable of switching into strong special attacks.

Checks and Counters

Physical Attackers: Milotic's middling Defense stat leaves it vulnerable to strong physical hits from attackers like Galarian Zapdos and Terrakion.

Grass-types: Common offensive Grass-types like Zarude, Dhelmise, and Rillaboom easily threaten Milotic with powerful STAB moves.

Passive Damage: Because Milotic typically relies on Regenerator as its only form of HP recovery, it can be easily chipped down through entry hazards and statuses like Toxic.

Heatran: Desolate Land Heatran takes negligible damage from Milotic's coverage options and completely blocks Scald, and Toxic can be used to wear Milotic down while avoiding triggering Mirror Coat.

RegenVest.description:
RegenVest and naturally high Special Defense make Milotic a reliable check to certain primal weather users like Desolate Land Volcanion and Primordial Sea Inteleon, as well as a generic specially defensive switch-in. Dragon Tail can be used to phaze out opposing setup sweepers like Volcarona and Cosmic Power Mew. Scald is a great STAB option that also threatens to burn typical Regenerator switch-ins like Swampert and Jirachi and Water-resistant foes like Swampert and Toxapex, as well as generally deterring physical attackers from switching in. Mirror Coat takes advantage of Milotic's high special bulk to survive even super effective special attacks and deal huge damage back to opposing special attackers and is especially useful against aggressive special attackers like Tapu Koko and Zapdos. Running minimum Speed allows Milotic to underspeed certain pivots such as Careful Corviknight and RegenVest Jirachi.

Milotic fits well on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its ability to take special hits and maintain momentum through Flip Turn. Offensive Pokemon such as Galarian Zapdos, Barraskewda, and Talonflame benefit from Milotic switching into powerful special attacks and pivoting them in safely. Milotic's Defense is fairly average, so it appreciates teammates like Intimidate Corviknight that can check physically offensive threats like Zarude. Teammates like Tapu Fini that can take Knock Off are also helpful to allow Milotic to preserve its Assault Vest. It also pairs well with entry hazard removers like Mandibuzz and Dhelmise to minimize the amount of chip damage it takes while pivoting. Milotic struggles to check opposing Heatran, as it is immune to Flip Turn and can retaliate with Toxic, making teammates like specially defensive Garchomp valued partners.

Defensive Pivot.description: This spread avoids being 2HKOed by Nidoqueen's Thunderbolt and outspeeds Adamant Golurk. Haze can be run if the team really needs it, but Milotic is much more useful with any of the other options given.

pu.overview: Absol is a good wallbreaker in the PU metagame thanks to a sky-high Attack stat, a spammable STAB option in Knock Off, and options to boost its Attack in Choice Band and Swords Dance. Access to priority in Sucker Punch, which is especially potent with Swords Dance, makes it harder to revenge kill. Its wide coverage options to hit standard Dark-type checks, like Iron Tail and Close Combat for Silvally-Fairy and Regirock, and an extremely strong STAB Knock Off are its main draws over Sneasel. Unfortunately, Absol's poor bulk, few resistances, and weaknesses to common Fighting- and Bug-type moves in the tier leave it with little defensive utility. This means Absol struggles to get in, and due to its middling Speed tier as well as Sucker Punch potentially being worked around, it often gets forced out.

Choice Band.description: The fourth move of choice depends on what Absol wants to deal with. Iron Tail takes care of bulky Fairy-types such as Aromatisse and Silvally-Fairy; however, Psycho Cut lets it 2HKO Weezing after Stealth Rock and does significant damage to Fighting-types like Poliwrath. Justified is run in order to punish Knock Offs from Pokemon such as Audino; however, Super Luck means Psycho Cut will critically hit half of the time. A Jolly nature is chosen to ensure Absol can outspeed Pokemon like Modest Magmortar, but an Adamant nature hits harder. Absol has trouble getting onto the field, so slow pivots such as Uxie can remedy this issue. They also help by baiting in Absol's prey, foes such as Rotom and Palossand, making it even easier for Absol to take something down. Fighting-types such as Gurdurr and Gallade appreciate Absol's ability to weaken Poison- and Fairy-types with its coverage, making it easier for them to sweep. Absol appreciates Fighting-type checks and Pokemon that can pivot into U-turn, such as Aromatisse and Weezing, as they can punish these Pokemon that Absol dislikes.

Swords Dance.description: Iron Tail takes out Fairy-types such as Aromatisse, while Close Combat takes care of Rock-types such as Regirock and Dark-types such as Shiftry. Play Rough can be used as a middle ground to hit Fighting-types such as Gurdurr and Poliwrath on a switch-in while hitting Fairy-types harder than Close Combat, but lacks the higher power of Iron Tail or Close Combat. Life Orb is preferred, but Black Glasses gives better longevity and the ability to bluff a Choice Band set. Justified is run to punish Knock Offs from Pokemon like Uxie. However, Super Luck, when used with Psycho Cut, results in a critical hit half of the time. Sticky Webs support is heavily appreciated due to Absol's middling Speed tier, so setters like Ribombee and Vikavolt are great partners for it. Vikavolt also breaks through physical walls such as Regirock. On bulkier teams, slow pivots such as Lanturn can help Swords Dance Absol wallbreak or sweep a team by slowly wearing down its checks whilst providing setup opportunities. Hazard setters such as Palossand also help Swords Dance Absol by moving many faster threats into the range of a boosted Sucker Punch, like Silvally-Fairy. Offensive sweepers such as Quiver Dance Ribombee appreciate Absol's wallbreaking, as it makes it easier for them to clean late-game.

nu.overview: Absol is an effective wallbreaker because it's incredibly strong and has great coverage; very little can safely switch into it. Furthermore, unlike other wallbreakers with a somewhat average Speed tier, Absol's access to Sucker Punch gives it extra security against frail revenge killers like Salazzle, Heliolisk, and Starmie. Defensively, though, Absol offers very little despite its typing being passable; it just lacks the bulk to make use of its resistances to Ghost and Dark as much as its main competition in Guzzlord, which is much bulkier and has an even better defensive typing. As a result, Absol also struggles getting into battle without aggressive play and pivot support, limiting the amount of chances it has to wallbreak. Absol also can have a rough time dealing with foes like Diancie, Sylveon, and Mudsdale if it lacks the proper coverage move or chance to set up.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Psycho Cut has good synergy with Super Luck and targets Toxicroak as well as other Fighting-types that may try pivoting into Knock Off, although Iron Tail is a vastly superior option if you desire more coverage. Focus Sash on dual screens teams works to guarantee Absol a Swords Dance boost. Choice Band sets cannot switch between moves but have great raw power and lack the constant chip damage of Life Orb.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Toxicroak is one of the better offensive checks to Absol because it resists Dark and Fighting and easily dispatches Absol with Drain Punch. Other Fighting-types like Scrafty and Passimian can deal with Absol too, but they're much more vulnerable to Close Combat.

Physical Walls: Mudsdale has the raw bulk to take multiple attacks from Absol and beat it one-on-one with Earthquake. Vileplume is a shakier answer, needing to be at full health to contend with Absol, but can take two Knock Offs and recover health back with Strength Sap. Arcanine detests losing its Heavy-Duty Boots, but its bulk combined with Intimidate lets it easily wall Absol.

Fairy-types: Sylveon and Diancie are both good Knock Off switch-ins that threaten to KO Absol with their STAB attacks. Iron Tail heavily pressures both, though, and even Swords Dance Absol variants can still heavily dent Diancie with Close Combat.

Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Absol has perfect coverage if it opts for Iron Tail; without it, Fairy-types like Diancie and Sylveon can generally answer it throughout a game. However, Swords Dance is still a great alternative that gives Absol more late-game potential and can severely limit offensive answers to it with the threat of +2 Sucker Punch. Do note, though, that because of how fragile Absol is, Iron Tail's miss chance is even more punishing and it's very hard to find good setup opportunities with Swords Dance. A Jolly nature is usually advised so Absol always outpaces Decidueye and Adamant Toxicroak, but Adamant lets it always OHKO Heliolisk with Sucker Punch and lowers the amount of chip damage necessary to secure a KO against other revenge killers like Salazzle.

Because of Absol's poor defenses, it greatly appreciates the support of pivots to get it in safely. Xatu, Talonflame, and Rotom-C are some of the best available; Xatu's slow Teleport is particularly nice for guaranteeing safe entry, and Talonflame can help handle Sylveon for Absol. Additionally, Rotom-C is great at getting Absol in against Dhelmise and Guzzlord. Absol's ability to force damage onto Fairy-types works well alongside late-game cleaners like Ninjask and Choice Scarf Passimian, with all of these options also supplying Absol with pivot support. If using Swords Dance, consider running Absol on a hyper offense dual screens team with Xatu or Espeon to provide it with safer setup opportunities.

zu.overview: Glalie is not viable in SS ZU due to it being entirely outclassed by Froslass, which performs the same role of a suicide lead but has better Speed, superior support moves, and a typing to deny Rapid Spin. Glalie is easier to take advantage of with its mediocre Speed and being forced to use Explosion to remove itself after setting Spikes.

Suicide Lead.description: Glalie attempts to act as a suicide lead with access to Spikes while using Taunt and Explosion to keep its entry hazards from being removed. However, it is entirely outclassed by Froslass, which performs this role much better with its faster Speed stat, access to Destiny Bond, and Ghost typing to thwart Rapid Spin users like Crygonal.

zu.overview: Walrein is not a very good Pokemon in SS ZU. Its seemingly decent bulk is undercut by its poor defensive typing, mediocre damage output, and lack of reliable recovery options. It could make use out of Swords Dance, but the aforementioned defensive issues combined with rather poor Speed make setting up rather difficult. Plus, Qwilfish does such a set way better thanks to its better defensive typing and Aqua Jet, and Froslass is a better physically attacking Ice-type due to its much greater Speed and being more immediately threatening.

Swords Dance.description: This set attempts to make use out of Walrein's decent coverage and Swords Dance, but setting up is made rather difficult with Walrein's bad defensive typing and poor Speed. Qwilfish is a much better user of Swords Dance thanks to its much better typing, great defensive ability in Intimidate to aid in setting up, and Aqua Jet for priority, while Froslass is better as a physically offensive Ice-type due to its much better Speed tier and much more immediate power.

zu.overview: While the combination of Head Smash and Rock Head alongside a good offensive movepool might seem enticing, Relicanth is a poor attacker due to its low Speed and mediocre Attack. Despite having weaker Rock-type STAB attacks, Kabutops and Rhydon outclass it due to the former having way more utility with Knock Off, Rapid Spin, and Flip Turn, and the latter having much better power and bulk. Relicanth also struggles to break through bulky Pokemon like Tangela and Palossand even with Toxic, making it even more difficult to justify running.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description: Relicanth attempts to set up Stealth Rock before using the combination of Head Smash and Rock Head to wallbreak as much as it can before getting KOed. However, Relicanth's oft-lacking power makes it difficult to justify running over Kabutops and Rhydon, with the former's additional utility and the latter's bulk and power being far stronger positives than what Relicanth can offer.

uu.overview: Salamence is a very versatile defensive and offensive presence. Its typing, natural bulk, and Intimidate allow it to check common threats such as Excadrill, Zarude, Scizor, and Conkeldurr. It's also a solid Defogger, matching up well against entry hazard setters such as Excadrill, Skarmory, and Cobalion. Salamence can utilize its solid Special Attack, decent Speed tier, and powerful moves like Hurricane and Draco Meteor as a strong special attacker, or it can sweep teams with Dragon Dance and Moxie. That, coupled with coverage in Flamethrower and Earthquake, makes Salamence difficult to predict and revenge kill. However, its reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots means Salamence does not appreciate Knock Off from Pokemon it’s supposed to check, such as Tangrowth and Scizor. Bulky Fairy-types like Hatterene and Primarina can easily take a hit and KO Salamence, while many other threats like Keldeo, Gyarados, and Nidoking carry Ice-type coverage. Offensive threats such as Thundurus-T and Nihilego outspeed it, and Dragon Dance sets are also vulnerable to revenge killers with priority such as Mamoswine and Lycanroc-D. Salamence also faces fierce competition from Hydreigon; Hydreigon's higher Special Attack stat alongside Dark-type STAB moves lets it better deal with popular defensive stalwarts such as Slowking, and it has greater item versatility by virtue of its neutrality to Stealth Rock. However, Salamence has a far better matchup against Pokemon such as Conkeldurr and Scizor, and it's able to outspeed and revenge kill opposing Hydreigon.
uu.comments:
Other Options

An Intimidate Dragon Dance set using Roost over Outrage can work on Magneton teams to check problematic answers to Excadrill such as Zarude while remaining offensively potent, but this set fails to get past Hippowdon. Fire Blast over Flamethrower on the special attacking set gives Salamence more power against Steel-types like Celesteela; however, it is less reliable and the additional power is often unneeded. Lum Berry can give Salamence more room to set up on Pokemon like Swampert and Tangrowth, but it doesn't carry as much consistent utility as Life Orb. Choice Scarf alongside Moxie can give Salamence surprising sweeping potential, as it doesn't require a setup turn to outspeed targets such as Keldeo and revenge kills sweepers such as Gyarados. Choice Specs improves Salamence's wallbreaking ability and can lure Hippowdon in to nail it with Hydro Pump.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Pokemon such as Azumarill, Togekiss, Primarina, and Hatterene take advantage of Salamence's lack of coverage for them, having the bulk to take a hit and either set up or KO Salamence.

Rock-types: Without Draco Meteor, special Salamence struggles to relieve Stealth Rock pressure from Nihilego, though it must be wary of Earthquake. Lycanroc-D can OHKO offensive variants of Salamence with -1 Stone Edge after minimal chip damage and easily revenge kill it with Accelerock, though Lycanroc-D cannot switch into Salamence safely.

Walls: Pokemon like Chansey and Slowking can handle special Salamence with their massive special bulk and use it for momentum with Teleport. However, the two cannot reliably tank hits from Dragon Dance sets. Umbreon and Mandibuzz have the natural bulk to survive Salamence's special attacks and take advantage of Dragon Dance sets with Foul Play. Celesteela is an especially detrimental defensive threat because it completely walls Dragon Dance sets without Fire Blast. Hippowdon can take hits from both physical and special sets and cripple Defog Salamence with Toxic.

Mamoswine: Mamoswine is the most consistent revenge killer against Salamence, as Ice Shard OHKOes any set.

Special Attacker.description:
Draco Meteor helps Salamence revenge kill Hydreigon and deals solid damage to neutral targets like Swampert, Rotom-W, and Rotom-H. Hurricane 2HKOes Assault Vest Tangrowth and has a significant chance to OHKO Amoonguss after Stealth Rock. It also prevents Slowking from switching into Salamence. Defog can be used over either STAB move, though this sacrifices neutral coverage against Pokemon like Nihilego and Azumarill. Flamethrower is solid coverage against Pokemon such as Scizor and Skarmory and can finish off weakened targets such as Tangrowth and Conkeldurr without risking a Hurricane miss. Roost alongside Heavy-Duty Boots makes Salamence harder to wear down by threats like Scizor and Zarude. Intimidate makes Salamence a more reliable switch-in to threats such as Conkeldurr, Scizor, and Excadrill while making them easier to pivot around.

This set fits on bulky offense and balance teams for its wallbreaking capabilities against Pokemon like Amoonguss and important defensive utility against other foes like Scizor. Swampert, Nidoqueen, and Excadrill are able to break through Salamence's checks like Nihilego, provide Stealth Rock support to soften up defensive Pokemon such as Celesteela, and capitalize on support against Tangrowth. Excadrill also pressures Hatterene and Togekiss and provides Rapid Spin support so Salamence can drop Defog. Scizor and Mamoswine takes advantage of Salamence removing potential roadblocks such as Amoonguss and Skarmory, and they threaten Stealth Rock setters Salamence has troubles against like Chansey and Nihilego. Zarude, Slowking, and Cobalion are effective pivots to safely bring Salamence into foes such as Hydreigon and Tangrowth. Slowking in particular provides slow pivoting with Teleport so Salamence can safely enter on Grass-types, as well as providing a stronger backbone against Conkeldurr with Colbur Berry. Rotom-W also acts as a pivot to bring Salamence in on Tangrowth and can check Mamoswine and Celesteela. Azelf can handle faster Pokemon such as Nihilego and Lycanroc-D. Defensive partners like Amoonguss and Hippowdon handle threats like Primarina and Nihilego.

Dragon Dance.description:
At +1 Speed, Salamence outspeeds revenge killers like Azelf, Thundurus-T, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. At +2 Speed, it blows past even faster revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Zarude. +1 Outrage destroys many neutral targets like Rotom-W, Rotom-W, and Swampert, though there is always the risk of Fairy-types like Azumarill and Primarina revenge killing Salamence. +1 Dual Wingbeat OHKOes targets such as Conkeldurr, Zarude, and Amoonguss after Stealth Rock. Dual Wingbeat also has the benefit of hitting Keldeo through Substitute, though risking a burn from Scald is not ideal. Earthquake OHKOes Cobalion and Jirachi at +2. Fire Blast can be used instead to lure in and break through Skarmory and increase Salamence's chances for a Moxie sweep. Life Orb can be used to OHKO Pokemon such as bulky Moltres with +1 Outrage and Primarina with +2 Dual Wingbeat. It can also be used alongside a Naive nature to ensure that Fire Blast OHKOes Skarmory after Stealth Rock. However, Salamence's Stealth Rock weakness and Life Orb recoil will quickly put it into range for Lycanroc-D's Accelerock. Moxie helps Salamence get multiple boosts to KO bulky targets like Hippowdon and makes it more difficult to revenge kill.

This set fits on offense and hyper offense teams as a wallbreaker or late-game cleaner with Moxie. Excadrill is an excellent lead that sets Stealth Rock to wear down bulky Pokemon such as Rotom-W and provides Rapid Spin. Sticky Web from Ribombee lets Salamence outspeed foes such as Nihilego. Celesteela walls this set, so early-game wallbreakers such as Nasty Plot Thundurus-T and Azelf are decent options. They also appreciate Salamence's ability to threaten Chansey. Other teammates that overwhelm physically bulky Pokemon such as Quagsire and Skarmory, such as Gyarados and Autotomize Celesteela, are valuable assets to this set. They also heavily benefit Salamence by overwhelming checks like Amoonguss and Primarina. Pivots such as Diggersby and Zarude can position Salamence to set up on Pokemon like Tangrowth. Zarude also blanks Hippowdon and Rotom-W for Salamence. Mamoswine is a consistent revenge killer against Salamence, so teammates that take it on such as Slowking and Scizor are appreciated. Magneton is able to trap and remove Skarmory, Celesteela, and Scizor for Salamence. It also wipes out Primarina and Togekiss.

Defensive.description:
