Priority Moves: Both Choice Band Azumarill's Aqua Jet and Scizor's Bullet Punch OHKO Mamoswine after Stealth Rock damage.

Status: Burn from Galarian Corsola, Spectrier, or Scald stops Mamoswine from dealing meaningful damage.

Choice Band (Ground).description:
Icicle Crash deals with Grass-, Flying-, and Dragon-types, allowing Mamoswine to significantly damage walls such as Amoonguss, Celesteela, and Kommo-o. Icicle Spear can be considered instead to break the Substitutes of Kyurem and Galarian Moltres, but it is less consistent than Icicle Crash. Earthquake deals with Steel- and Water-types that resist Icicle Crash such as Aegislash and Toxapex. Superpower heavily dents Pokemon that are not bothered by the first two moves, such as Porygon2, Cloyster, Air Balloon Heatran, and Ferrothorn. Knock Off may be considered over Superpower to cripple physical walls such as Slowbro, Galarian Corsola, and Rotom-W. Ice Shard allows Mamoswine to revenge kill weakened threats such as Hydreigon, Galarian Moltres, and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu. It also lets it clean up Flying and Dragon teams late-game when their walls have been sufficiently chipped. A Choice Band allows Mamoswine to OHKO walls such as Amoonguss, Zapdos, and Toxapex with the appropriate STAB move. An Adamant nature lets Ice Shard better pick off threats such as Thundurus-T, Galarian Moltres, and Tapu Bulu. Thick Fat allows Mamoswine to check SubRoost Kyurem and remove Ice-types such as Galarian Darmanitan in a pinch.

Excadrill is a good teammate to eliminate fast threats Mamoswine struggles with such as Zeraora, Volcarona, and Blacephalon when used on sand teams, or it can provide Rapid Spin support and clean late-game on weather-less teams once Mamoswine has chipped opposing walls. Gastrodon provides a Water immunity, can spread Toxic to wear down the opposing team, and can take special attacks aimed at Mamoswine. Alternatively, Seismitoad may be considered as the Water-immune partner, as it can check Azumarill, which usually poses a huge threat for Ground teams. Landorus-T provides Gravity support to allow Mamoswine to break through checks such as Rotom-W and Celesteela that can normally wall it. Swords Dance Garchomp can work alongside Mamoswine to break through their shared checks such as Slowbro and Kyurem when facing Psychic and Dragon teams. Nidoking deals with physical walls such as Slowbro and Ferrothorn that Mamoswine struggles with. Hippowdon can take physical attacks from Zeraora and Victini aimed at Mamoswine and can set sand and Stealth Rock to chip the opposing team further.

Choice Band (Ice).description:
Mamoswine is an effective wallbreaker on Ice teams, as it helps pressure Fire-, Rock-, and Steel-types such as Torkoal, Tyranitar, and Heatran. Earthquake makes it a dangerous threat for Poison and Electric teams, and Icicle Crash hits Ground-immune targets like Celesteela, Zapdos, and Mantine. Ice Shard provides priority and aids in revenge killing the likes of Agility Galarian Moltres, Choice Scarf Galarian Zapdos, and Choice Scarf Thundurus-T. Superpower grants Mamoswine the ability to break past bulky Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Porygon2. Heavy Slam can be used to reliably defeat setup sweepers such as Hatterene and Clefable. Knock Off is a great utility option that allows Mamoswine to get rid of important items such as Eviolite from Chansey, Porygon2, and Piloswine as well as recovery items from Ferrothorn and Slowbro. An Adamant nature lets Mamoswine better revenge kill the aforementioned targets of Ice Shard.

Kyurem appreciates Mamoswine breaking through Steel-types such as Aegislash and Melmetal, as they are able to tank Kyurem's Earth Powers quite easily. In return, Kyurem checks Rotom-W and Slowbro and is capable of PP stalling Ferrothorn's Gyro Ball and Corviknight's Body Press with Pressure. Arctozolt not only helps Mamoswine break down defensive cores used by Poison and Flying teams, but also threatens Water-types such as Pelipper, Volcanion, and Toxapex. Cloyster values Mamoswines immunity to Electric-type moves from Tapu Koko, Zapdos, and Alolan Raichu, while also setting Spikes to support Mamoswine's wallbreaking by providing chip damage against foes. Aurora Veil Alolan Ninetales allows Mamoswine to tank more hits and wallbreak for a prolonged period of time; Alolan Ninetales also checks threats such as Urshifu-R and Kommo-o. Galarian Darmanitan can use Flare Blitz to KO Ferrothorn for non-Superpower Mamoswine and also lures Ground-immune Steel-types like Corviknight and Celesteela. Mamoswine wears down bulky teams so that Weavile can sweep in the late-game, while Weavile's Speed is great for dealing with faster threats such as Volcarona, Spectrier, and Blacephalon.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Stealth Rock Setter.description:
• Mamoswine is an effective early game setter of Stealth Rock with Focus Sash, thanks to its good coverage and access to priority in Ice Shard.

  • Icicle Spear is the prefered Ice-type STAB, since it breaks through Focus Sash and Mimikyu's Disguise.

  • Oblivious blocks the effects of Intimidate and Taunt, making it Mamoswine's best ability.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Substitute is an option over Toxic in the last moveslot to ease prediction, but the lack of significant bulk forces Mamoswine to run Leftovers, for more longevity and a Jolly nature to outspeed Mew and Tapu Fini. Water Absorb can also be paired with this to take advantage of Substitute against Barraskewda and Swampert, but otherwise reduces damage output even further. Mamoswine can use High Horsepower when paired with a Grassy Surge user like Dhelmise, although this increases the likelihood of residual chip. A Sheer Force Life Orb set allows Mamoswine to use Freeze Dry, Ice Beam, and Earth Power to beat its normal checks like Swampert, Corviknight, and Dauntless Shield Mew, but is generally weaker against neutral targets.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Physical Walls: Bulky Physical walls like Dauntless Shield Mew and Intimidate Corviknight can reliably switch into Mamoswine and recover any lost health.

Residual Damage: Stealth Rock and other entry hazards can severely limit how many attacks Mamoswine can get off, especially Life Orb variants. Mamoswine also fears poison and burn as they severely limit its longevity.

Bulky Water-Types: Bulky Water-types like Swampert and Tapu Fini can switch into Mamoswine's Ice-type attacks with relative ease before pivoting out and healing with Regenerator or even threaten a KO with their own attacks. However, Earthquake can 2HKO them, but this requires correct prediction to avoid excessive residual chip.

Revenge Killers: Revenge killers like Azelf and Terrakion OHKO Mamoswine and force it out. Azelf is particularly troublesome as it stops Mamoswine from using Ice Shard thanks to Psychic Surge.

Zarude and Tapu Bulu: Grassy Glide in Grassy Terrain from Zarude outpaces Mamoswine and can immediately OHKO. Tapu Bulu also OHKOes Mamoswine when outside of Psychic Terrain with Triage Horn Leech.

Adaptability Wallbreaker.description:
Mamoswine is a good wallbreaker thanks to its high Attack and functionally unresisted STAB move combination. It can 2HKO almost every Pokemon without Intimidate or Dauntless Shield, such as Tapu Fini, Swampert, and Ferrothorn. Earthquake is the main STAB attack, allowing it to hit Steel- and Poison-types like Heatran and Toxapex for super effective damage, while Icicle Crash hits Ground-, Dragon- and Flying-types such as Landorus-T and Zapdos. Ice Shard is a useful Ice-type priority attack that allows it to revenge kill a plethora of Pokemon like Zygarde-10% and Landorus-T, as well as weakened faster threats like Tapu Koko and Talonflame. Toxic poisons Dauntless Shield Mew and bulky Water-types like Swampert and Tapu Fini to wear them down over the course of the game, while Knock Off removes important items from its checks, notably Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots, to weaken them more easily. Stealth Rock is an alternative as Mamoswine can reliably keep them up against Defoggers it can 2HKO like Tapu Fini and Moltres. Choice Band is the preferred option due to its lack of recoil and ability to guarantee the 2HKO on Tapu Fini, but it requires Mamoswine to rely on predictions, while Life Orb allows more flexibility at the cost of struggling to break bulkier walls without extensive team support. An Adamant nature allows Mamoswine to hit as hard as possible while still allowing it to outspeed fast defensive Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Mew.

Mamoswine can break through special walls like Blissey and Jirachi with ease for special attackers such as Azelf and Zapdos. It can also break down Water-and Dragon-types like Tapu Fini and Silvally-Dragon for Cinderace, Talonflame, and other Fire-types; in return, these Fire-types can deal with Intimidate Corviknight, which would otherwise prevent Mamoswine from making progress. Dauntless Shield Mew is also another common check, so physical pivots like Cinderace and Barraskewda can help Mamoswine beat it. Special attackers such as Azelf and Volcarona force out Mamoswine, so Zapdos and Assault Vest Swampert are appreciated to tank their attacks. Revenge killers such as Cinderace and Terrakion threaten Mamoswine, so answers like Swampert, Zapdos, and Dauntless Shield Mew are all greatly appreciated. Zarude and Tapu Bulu also force out Mamoswine, so checks like Dauntless Shield Mandibuzz and Corviknight help in these matchups. Due to its mediocre bulk, Mamoswine likes coming in via pivots; as such, it appreciates partners like Corviknight and Mew that can slow pivot for it. Tapu Koko is also a great partner as it can outspeed and pivot on special walls that Mamoswine forces out like Blissey and Jirachi, along with being able to lure in Swampert and KO it with Grass Knot.

bdspou.overview: Mamoswine is a great wallbreaker in BDSP OU due to its excellent STAB combination and an insane Attack stat that makes it nearly unwallable. It makes great use of Life Orb, as its huge Attack stat and unique Ice-type priority move in Ice Shard allow it to finish off Dragon-types and can also be useful for chipping down neutral targets into KO range for other attacks. It can also make use of Substitute to ease prediction, with the drawback of less damage output. Unfortunately, while Mamoswine's typing is advantageous offensively, it's lacking defensively with no defensive utility outside of Thick Fat and an Electric immunity. Mamoswine is unable to capitalize off of this, as it can't consistently come in on Volt Switch from common Electric-types such as Rotom-W, while fellow Ground-type wallbreaker Garchomp can. Mamoswine's STAB moves, while good, can easily be played around. Combined with a mediocre Speed stat, this makes Mamoswine very prediction-reliant without Substitute compared to other, more reliable wallbreakers such as Crawdaunt, Azumarill, Infernape, Garchomp, and Breloom. Mamoswine's weaknesses also leave it vulnerable to common priority such as Aqua Jet, Mach Punch, and Bullet Punch from Crawdaunt, Azumarill, Infernape, and Scizor. Mamoswine also has great competition in the form of Garchomp, as the latter is often used over Mamoswine because of its higher consistency and better defenses. However, although Mamoswine possesses a great deal of weaknesses, its strength more than makes up for the effort needed, as Mamoswine's STAB combination makes switching into it effectively very tough, as most switch-ins get 2HKOed.
bdspou.comments:
Other Options

Mamoswine is capable of becoming a Stealth Rock lead that can counter some of the lead metagame with Focus Sash and Oblivious; however, it's usually better to run the wallbreaker set, as it offers more power and can still be used as a Stealth Rock setter. Mamoswine can use Choice Band, as it's very powerful. However, it's often dismissed in favour of Life Orb, as they have similar damage output. Mamoswine can also use Choice Scarf to get rid of its speed issue; however, not getting to switch up Mamoswine's moves isn't ideal, and not getting a big damage boost makes it inferior to Choice Band, which is already unviable. Mamoswine can switch Freeze-Dry for Icicle Spear to OHKO Dragonite, even with Multiscale intact, as well as SubPunch Breloom; however, its inconsistency makes it less useful than Icicle Crash.

Checks and Counters

Rotom-W: Rotom-W is one of the only counters to Mamoswine. It doesn't get affected by Earthquake and Icicle Crash bounces right off it, while it can OHKO Mamoswine back with Hydro Pump and even burn Mamoswine with Will-O-Wisp if it needs to. However, Rotom-W must be wary of switching in on Freeze-Dry, as with Stealth Rock chip, it can 2HKO Rotom-W, making it unable to switch in again.

Skarmory: Skarmory is one of the only walls to Mamoswine, as it doesn't take too much damage from Icicle Crash while having reliable recovery in Roost. However, although Icicle Crash doesn't do enough damage to 2HKO Skarmory outright, a deadly flinch chance means that Mamoswine might be able to break through with enough flinches and luck.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Slowbro, Gastrodon, and Milotic all tank non-Choice Band Mamoswine's hits and can either possibly OHKO or burn Mamoswine. Gastrodon needs to be wary of Freeze-Dry, as it's a 4x super effective move. Slowbro and Milotic can both shrug off Freeze-Dry, however.

Faster Pokemon and Priority: While faster Pokemon like Starmie, Lucario, Alakazam, and Infernape can't switch into Mamoswine's attacks, all of them outspeed Mamoswine and are able to OHKO it. Priority users such as Crawdaunt and Scizor can also 2HKO Mamoswine, with the former being able to OHKO it after Stealth Rock chip.

Residual Damage: As Mamoswine usually runs Life Orb, it will get worn down with entry hazards damage, as Mamoswine will typically switch out a lot of times. Substitute Mamoswine doesn't have this issue, however, as it has Leftovers to heal itself back up.

Life Orb Attacker.description:
Earthquake and Icicle Crash are very strong STAB moves that can take care of many slower Pokemon such as Togekiss, Heatran, and Magnezone. Ice Shard is useful for revenge killing Dragon-type threats such as Latias, Garchomp, and Dragonite while also being useful to revenge kill other Ice-weak targets such as Breloom, Gliscor, and Shaymin. Freeze-Dry is useful to deal major damage to Rotom-W on the switch in, usually making it unable to check Mamoswine again alongside Stealth Rock chip, and it is also useful for dealing with Quagsire. Stealth Rock provides good role compression, as Mamoswine can beat common Defoggers such as Gliscor and Latias. Life Orb is the preferred item, as it boosts Mamoswine's wallbreaking potential by a decent amount, although it has the drawback of recoil. Never-Melt Ice is a strong alternative, as it retains the power boost for Ice-type moves but doesn't have the drawback of recoil. Jolly is the preferred nature, as it outspeeds Jolly Feraligatr and Breloom, but an Adamant nature can be used, as Mamoswine still outspeeds threats such as Modest Heatran and bulky Gliscor while boosting priority damage. A Naive nature can be used to strengthen Freeze-Dry without much compromise.

Mamoswine fits best on offensive teams, as it is able to guarantee damage on Scizor and Clefable, which can be capitalized on by Pokemon such as Feraligatr, Breloom, and Latias. Mamoswine appreciates pivots that help it get onto the battlefield such as Scizor and Rotom-W. Mamoswine capitalizes on entry hazards; as such, Stealth Rock from Garchomp or Heatran and Spikes from Roserade or Skarmory help it break more easily. Mamoswine appreciates Latias healing it back to full health with Healing Wish, as Life Orb recoil is a big weakness that Mamoswine has to deal with. Grass-types such as Rotom-C and Shaymin can cover for Mamoswine's Water weakness relatively well. Sweepers such as Feraligatr, Azumarill, Lucario, and offensive Scizor also appreciate Freeze-Dry Mamoswine, as it is able to lure in and KO Rotom-W and Slowbro, which are often their greatest counters. Rapid Spin support from Starmie can also help reduce the amount of residual damage Mamoswine takes, and in return, Starmie can force out Skarmory while removing the Spikes it sets up.

Substitute.description:
Mamoswine being extremely prediction-reliant is ultimately one of its biggest downfalls; however, Mamoswine can circumvent this issue by using Substitute to provide a layer of defense to fall back on, as well as an immunity to status conditions. Ice Shard is useful if a foe survives a hit, as this set lacks power. Icicle Crash and Earthquake are a beautiful offensive pairing, as the majority of the metagame will be 2HKOed. Leftovers is usually the item of choice, as it will help Mamoswine heal off Substitute's recoil, but Never-Melt Ice is also useful if it needs the extra firepower. Adamant is Mamoswine's preferred nature, as it allows it to gain a bit power back from not having Life Orb. However, a Jolly nature is also an option to outspeed Jolly Feraligatr and Breloom.

Substitute Mamoswine is best paired with Pokemon that can eliminate its most common counter, Rotom-W. Pokemon such as Breloom, Latias, Tangrowth, and Shaymin can do the job. Additionally, Pokemon that can get rid of entry hazards such as Latias, Gliscor, Scizor, and Starmie make Mamoswine's job a lot easier. Late-game cleaners such as Life Orb Scizor, Choice Band Dragonite, Swords Dance Lucario, and Feraligatr also benefit immensely from Mamoswine's wallbreaking potential. Mamoswine also appreciates Latias healing it back to full HP with Healing Wish.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

A Jolly nature allows Mamoswine to outspeed offensive Heatran, but it doesn't outspeed anything else significant because Mamoswine can already KO foes like Nidoking with Ice Shard, and it has less breaking power without Adamant. Choice Scarf turns Mamoswine into a decent revenge killer that can outspeed the likes of Tapu Koko, Zeraora, and Barraskewda without rain, but it loses a ton of extra damage output without Choice Band, making it more difficult to wallbreak.

Checks and Counters

Ground

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive walls such as Mega Slowbro, Skarmory, and Swampert are able to take attacks from Mamoswine and wear it down with Scald, Body Press, or Flip Turn, respectively. However, Swampert's lack of reliable recovery means that it can easily be pressured by Mamoswine's teammates.

Status: Burn significantly reduces Mamoswine's damage output, leaving it unable to function as a wallbreaker. Toxic consistently wears Mamoswine down, making it difficult for it to stay in the field for a long time.

Water-types: Offensive Water-types such as Mega Swampert, Urshifu-R, and Mega Gyarados can outspeed Mamoswine and KO it with their STAB moves. Bulky Water-types such as Tapu Fini, Slowbro, Swampert, and Suicune are able to tank attacks from Mamoswine and 2HKO it with Scald, with Tapu Fini and Suicune outspeeding Mamoswine as well.

Rotom-W: Rotom-W is one of the most consistent checks to Mamoswine, being immune to its Earthquake due to Levitate and resisting its Icicle Crash. Rotom-W is able to either KO Mamoswine with a powerful Hydro Pump or cripple it or another teammate with Will-O-Wisp or Toxic.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types like Heracross, Mega Gallade, Terrakion, and Kommo-o after a boost can all outspeed Mamoswine and KO it with their STAB moves.

Revenge Killers: Mamoswine sits at a mediocre Speed tier for an offensive Pokemon, making it outsped and KOed by a myriad of powerful revenge killers such as Mega Lopunny, Keldeo, Tapu Lele, Blacephalon, and Rillaboom due to Grassy Glide.

Choice Band (Ground).description:
Mamoswine's good Attack stat and daunting STAB combination make it an excellent wallbreaker that can help against types like Flying and Dragon, which are otherwise poor matchups for Ground teams. Icicle Crash allows it to get rid of Mandibuzz, Tapu Bulu, and Dragonite. Ice Shard provides useful priority for fast threats like Landorus, Hydreigon, Latias, and Latios, especially if they are weakened. Superpower is a useful move for targeting Ferrothorn and Porygon2; however, Knock Off gets rid of items like Eviolite, Leftovers, and Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Galarian Corsola, Porygon2, Celesteela, and Blissey. An Adamant nature paired with a Choice Band maximizes Mamoswine's damage output, letting it pick off weakened threats with Ice Shard better and have a better chance of KOing a weakened Celesteela or Corviknight. Thick Fat is the preferred ability to give Ground teams a useful resistance to Ice-type attacks. Generally, Mamoswine should be used to wallbreak types like Flying, Poison, and Dragon early-game, and it can clean weakened teams with Ice Shard late-game.

Hippowdon is a great partner, as it tanks hits for Mamoswine due to its good bulk, can phaze out threatening foes like Mega Scizor and Mega Gallade with Whirlwind, and provide Stealth Rock and Sand Stream support, which gives Mamoswine an easier time sweeping late-game by racking chip damage on foes. Landorus is an essential wallbreaker, as it can not only break through physically defensive foes like Slowbro and Mega Sableye for Mamoswine, but utilize Gravity in order to make Mamoswine's Earthquake useful against threats like Celesteela, Rotom-W, and Corviknight. Gastrodon and Seismitoad can absorb Water-type attacks for Mamoswine; Gastrodon has access to reliable recovery, and Seismitoad can outspeed and threaten Azumarill as well as use its higher physical bulk to take attacks from Pokemon like Barraskewda more easily. Excadrill is a dangerous sweeper under Hippowdon's sand due to Sand Rush, which allows it to outspeed fast threats like Mega Lopunny and Terrakion for Mamoswine, and it provides Rapid Spin support while breaking past physically defensive foes like Mega Sableye, Porygon2, and Avalugg with Steelium Z and Swords Dance. Garchomp can break through most walls due to Swords Dance and Dragonium Z while weakening Celesteela with Fire Fang and providing a useful neutrality to Water- and Grass-type attacks. Mega Garchomp can destroy foes like Celesteela and Ferrothorn with Fire Blast while living an Aqua Jet from +6 Azumarill and threatening it back with a Sand Force-boosted Earthquake. Mega Steelix is a powerful bulky sweeper with Curse that can also live a hit from +6 Azumarill's Aqua Jet and threaten it back with Heavy Slam, and it also threatens other foes like Tapu Bulu and Rillaboom.

ru.overview: Although Porygon-Z has the offensive capacity to function decently in RU, it provides very little else compared to its competition, which makes it difficult to justify on a team. In terms of pure wallbreaking power, it is outclassed by Indeedee and Toxtricity, while boosting sets are too frail to reliably set up. Choice Scarf sets face competition from the myriad of revenge killing options in the tier such as Choice Scarf Flygon, Golisopod, and Choice Scarf Gardevoir, all of which provide significantly more utility and defensive presence to a team. Furthermore, the ubiquity of Ghost- and Steel-types in the tier forces it to rely on prediction and makes it unable to take advantage of its greatest strength in Adaptability-boosted Tri Attack.

Choice Scarf.description: Porygon-Z's Adaptability-boosted Tri Attack makes it an adequate revenge killer and cleaner, and it can make progress against both offensive and defensive teams through its coverage moves or Trick. However, it offers no defensive utility at all and cannot switch into most attacks, requiring significant team support to consider using over other revenge killers like Flygon.

1v1.comments:
Other Options

Porygon-Z can utilize a set with Chople Berry for Zeraora and Fighting-types like both Urshifu formes. This set runs an EV spread of 88 Def / 252 SpA / 168 Spe with a Modest nature and the moves Hyper Beam, Uproar, Agility, and Nasty Plot or Icy Wind. 88 Defense EVs allow Porygon-Z to survive a Plasma Fists from Choice Band Zeraora and use Agility turn 1 to outspeed and OHKO with Hyper Beam. Icy Wind can help out versus Sawk to break Sturdy and then KO with Hyper Beam.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Description

Choice Specs-boosted Hyper Beam is able to OHKO many top-tier Pokemon like Aromatisse, Cresselia, and Assault Vest Arcanine. Uproar can be beneficial against Whimsicott and Pressure Entei, which try to stall Porygon-Z out with Substitute. Thunderbolt beats Corviknight, and Ice Beam hits Garchomp and Dragapult. Trick + Recover + Nasty Plot allows Porygon-Z to shut down stall Pokemon like Chansey. Dark Pulse helps beat non-Assault Vest Metagross and is an option to hit Spectrier.

EVs

252 Speed EVs are used to outspeed Tapu Fini, Dracovish, Kommo-o, and some other Porygon-Z. An alternate EV spread of 68 Def / 184 SpA / 252 Spe reliably beats Garchomp with Ice Beam, as the 68 Defense EVs prevent the KO from Custap Berry Garchomp's Outrage.

Usage Tips

Hyper Beam is usually the best choice versus a neutral target like Azumarill or Cresselia, as it will do more damage than super effective coverage moves thanks to Adaptability. If Entei's Pressure is not revealed on turn 1, Porygon-Z should click Hyper Beam over Uproar, since Entei is using Inner Focus with Assault Vest instead of Substitute.

For coverage moves like Thunderbolt, Ice Beam, and Dark Pulse, it's best to use them on Pokemon like Celesteela and Spectrier, as they either resist or are immune to Hyper Beam. Nasty Plot Porygon-Z can use Trick and set up until Hyper Beam OHKOes Chansey.

Custap Berry.description:
Set Description

This Porygon-Z set aims to surprise Pokemon like Galarian Darmanitan, Naganadel, and opposing Porygon-Z by using Endure + Custap Berry. Hyper Beam deals an extreme amount of damage to Pokemon like Rillaboom, Tapu Fini, and Volcanion. Nasty Plot enables Porygon-Z to set up against stall Pokemon like Chansey and better damage foes like Sylveon and Primarina. Uproar helps versus Substitute users like Whimsicott and stall Entei, while Thunderbolt is helpful against Corviknight and Celesteela. Ice Beam hits Garchomp and Naganadel.

EVs

The defensive investment allows Porygon-Z to survive a Fake Out into Grassy Glide from Life Orb Rillaboom. The HP in specific lets it reliably beat Timid Choice Specs Tapu Fini. 216 Speed EVs are for base 85 Speed Pokemon without a boosting nature, such as Rillaboom, Cresselia, and Tapu Fini.

Usage Tips

Endure is the best move on turn 1 versus threats that can OHKO Porygon-Z like Galarian Darmanitan, Choice item Urshifu-S and Urshifu-R, and also Naganadel. Then, while in Custap Berry range, it can OHKO back with Hyper Beam or Ice Beam. If running Uproar, it should be used against Pokemon like Whimsicott turn 1 to bypass their Substitute and KO them before they can stall.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Description

Choice Scarf Porygon-Z outspeeds fast threats like Zeraora and also other, slower Choice Scarf users in Dracozolt and Togekiss, OHKOing them with Hyper Beam. Trick + Recover effectively shuts down the likes of Chansey and Galarian Corsola. Dark Pulse hits Ghost-types like Spectrier and Galarian Corsola, while Ice Beam can be beneficial for Landorus-T especially with Assault Vest, and Garchomp.

EVs

This set runs maximum Speed investment to outspeed Zeraora and base 80 Speed or less Choice Scarf users like Togekiss, Dracozolt, and Dracovish. Maximum Special Attack allows it to get better KO odds versus Volcanion and stall Zapdos. A Modest nature improves its chances versus Maranga Berry Zapdos; however, it will not outspeed Choice Scarf Togekiss and Zeraora.

Usage Tips

Dark Pulse hits Ghost-types like Spectrier and Galarian Corsola for supereffective damage and Ice Beam helps versus Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus. Using Trick + Recover and repeatedly clicking Hyper Beam wins versus Chansey.

Life Orb.description:
Set Description

This set has most of the same monstrous wallbreaking power that Porygon-Z is known for, but with the freedom to switch between its STAB attacks and utility options. Nasty Plot allows it to counter Mirror Coat users like Gastrodon and Assault Vest Swampert. Uproar secures the win versus Pressure stall Pokemon like Substitute + Protect Zapdos, Entei, Corviknight, and SubSeed users like Whimsicott. Substitute overwhelms hard stall Pokemon like Unaware Pyukumuku. Recover can increase Porygon-Z's longevity versus Pokemon like Seismic Toss Chansey, and Dark Pulse lets it hit Spectrier.

EVs

92 Special Defense EVs allow Porygon-Z to survive an Overheat from Choice Scarf Volcanion and OHKO back. With 176 Speed EVs, it outspeeds neutral-natured base 80 Speed Pokemon like Regidrago and Togekiss.

Usage Tips

Substitute should be used turn 1 versus Gastrodon to avoid moves like Mirror Coat and Clear Smog, then Nasty Plot on turn 2 lets Porygon-Z OHKO with Hyper Beam. However, if Gastrodon uses Amnesia turn 1, then Nasty Plot should be repeated until Porygon-Z reaches +6 and then Uproar is an OHKO or 2HKO, even after Chilan Berry. This same strategy should be used for Corviknight, as Nasty Plot boosted Hyper Beam OHKOes. However, if they use Substitute too, Nasty Plot should be used twice so that Uproar will at worst 2HKO.Substitute is the best move on turn 1 versus Pyukumuku to stop Mirror Coat then Uproar can be used for a 2HKO. Recover helps versus stall Pokemon like Seismic Toss Chansey, as Porygon-Z can boost up with Nasty Plot and heal off the damage to KO with Hyper Beam.

Rocky Helmet.description:
Set Description

This set punishes slower physical attackers that normally check Porygon-Z like Aggron, Rhyperior, and Metagross through Reflect + Rocky Helmet, chipping down their health until they are in Hyper Beam KO range. Nasty Plot can help versus some stall Pokemon or just bolster Hyper Beam's damage even more, while Recover helps Porygon-Z outlast its foes.

EVs

64 Defense EVs are so that Porygon-Z can survive three Choice Band Aggron Heavy Slams after Reflect, and the 188 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed Metagross. Maximum Special Attack is for the best Hyper Beam damage versus the aforementioned Pokemon.

Usage Tips

Reflect versus slower physical threats, like Aggron and Metagross, allows Porygon-Z to tank their hits and then use Recover until they are chipped down from Rocky Helmet. Hyper Beam should be used when it will OHKO the foe. Nasty Plot can reduce the turns needed to stall out foes like Aggron while also lowering the chances that Porygon-Z falls to a critical hit. It can also help Hyper Beam eventually OHKO versus stall Pokemon like Chansey, with Recover helping Porygon-Z set up.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B- Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Special Wallbreaker.description:
• Porygon-Z's high base Special Attack coupled with Adaptability and great coverage allows it to break down or outright sweep a variety of slower opposing team compositions.

  • Tri Attack or Uproar can be used as an alternative STAB options to Hyper Beam that do not have cooldown, whereas Thunderbolt provides solid coverage against the likes of Celesteela and Water-types such as Tapu Fini and Gyarados.

  • Nasty Plot allows Porygon-Z to boost its Special Attack to nearly unwallable levels, whereas Trick allows it to cripple passive walls and regain move flexibility.

Items

  • Chopple Berry lets Porygon-Z survive Fighting-type Attacks while Dynamaxed, particularly useful against Cinderace and Urshifu-R.

  • Life Orb lets Porygon-Z deal massive damage even without a Nasty Plot boost.

  • Choice Scarf patches up Porygon-Z's Speed stat, letting it outspeed key threats such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Dracovish.

zu.overview: Dusknoir may look enticing to use due to its decent Attack backed up with high-Base Power moves. However, Dusknoir can only set up a Substitute against overly passive teams, which is not helped by its average bulk and low Speed. Most importantly, Dusknoir is grossly outperformed as an attacker by Gourgeist formes and Trevenant due to its lower Speed and lack of a secondary STAB option.

Substitute + 3 Attacks.description: Dusknoir attempts to exploit walls like Miltank and Articuno through Substitute and fire off as many attacks it can before going down. However, Dusknoir is usually too slow and defensively vulnerable to pull it off reliably. Gourgeist formes and Trevenant are much better options as offensive Ghost-types, with both of them sporting better Speed, additional Grass-type STAB moves, and additional utility with Trick. To make matters worse, Dusknoir's strongest STAB move relies on foes having an item, making it even harder to fit on a team when Knock Off users are common.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Froslass's Spikes set can take advantage of a variety of options, thanks to its utility movepool. Toxic and Will-O-Wisp cripple switch-ins and physical attackers alike. However, having to give up Taunt or an attacking option makes it difficult to fit. Physical attacks can be ran on its Spikes set, but it has bad synergy with Knock Off, which you want to use to remove Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Faster Pokemon: Froslass's poor bulk and weakness-laden typing leaves it vulnerable to opposing revenge killers. Choice Scarf users like Rotom, Sawk, and Gourgeist-Small have super effective coverage for it. Outside of that, priority users like Kangaskhan and Thwackey do a good job of handling Froslass. While Alolan Persian doesn't use priority, it's one of the few Pokemon faster than Froslass.

Water-type Pokemon: Though repeated Ghost-type attacks can threaten it, Poliwrath's physical bulk and typing lets it serve as a great check to Froslass, actively punishing its Triple Axel with Rocky Helmet. For similar reasons on top of having Intimidate, Qwilfish is a great switch-in to Triple Axel, but is more vulnerable to Poltergeist and special attacking sets. While it is relegated to stall teams, Pyukumuku can completely blank Froslass if it doesn't get afflicted by Taunt or Trick.

Steel-type Pokemon: While it can struggle to take multiple Ghost-type attacks, Klinklang has the bulk and typing to handle Froslass's Ice-type attacks, while using Gear Grind to KO it. Despite its frailty, Alolan Dugtrio is as fast as Froslass and has Sucker Punch.

Dark-type Pokemon: Dark-types like Alolan Persian and Silvally-Dark resist Froslass's Ghost-type attacks and immediately threaten it with their own STAB moves. However, they must be wary to not switch into its powerful Ice-type attacks.

Miltank: With its immunity to Ghost, and with Thick Fat variants resisting its Ice-type STAB, Miltank can completely blank Froslass and wear it down via Toxic. However, if Froslass uses Taunt, Miltank is unable to touch it.

Choice Band.description:
Possessing a blistering Speed stat and a ruthless dual STAB combination, Froslass is a strong Choice Band wallbreaker. With both of its powerful STAB attacks, Froslass has amazing neutral coverage that defensive cores can have trouble handling. Switcheroo cripples the few defensive counters to Froslass, which include Miltank and defensive Poliwrath. Ice Shard is great against offensive teams, revenge killing faster threats like Thwackey, Lilligant, and Alolan Dugtrio after some chip. Either of the latter two moves can be replaced by Spikes, as Froslass can easily set multiple layers thanks to the free turns it generates forcing switches.

Choice Band Froslass generally fits well on offensive builds, but it must be noted that Poltergeist has negative synergy with Knock Off users. Due to its poor defenses, Froslass appreciates VoltTurn users who can safely bring it onto the field. Offensive pivots like Morpeko and Silvally formes can lure in Pokemon like Palossand and Altaria, respectively, bringing Froslass in safely to immediately threaten them. Defensive pivots including Articuno and Clefairy, which are able to take a hit and pivot out, so Froslass comes in unharmed. With its amazing ability to weaken walls and revenge kill wallbreakers, Froslass leaves ample opportunity for sweepers like Klinklang, Galarian Rapidash, and Silvally-Dark to set up. If bulkier teams intend on using Froslass, keeping it healthy through entry hazard removers like Morpeko and Coalossal is essential. Knock Off absorbers like Alcremie and Miltank also play important roles in giving Froslass backup when it's in danger.

Offensive Spikes Setter.description:
Froslass is a premier Spikes setter thanks to having one of the fastest Taunts in the metagame alongside a great STAB combination. It threatens common entry hazard removers like Altaria and Rotom and can use Taunt to block removal from other Pokemon like Articuno and Silvally-Poison. This also shuts down passive Pokemon like Miltank and Pyukumuku, which makes Froslass a solid stallbreaker. Froslass is also a capable revenge killer, as it outpaces the majority of the unboosted metagame, including threats like Jynx, Thievul, and Sawk.

Spikes Froslass's combination of Speed and offensive utility makes it a great fit for offensive builds. Offensive Knock Off users like Thwackey, Sawk, and Kabutops make opposing Pokemon vulnerable to Froslass's Spikes. These wallbreakers also directly benefit from Spikes, as it can put foes in greater range of KOs. Other wallbreakers that love Spikes include Galarian Rapidash and the Silvally formes. These Pokemon also threaten Froslass checks like Alolan Persian and Miltank. Morpeko is a particularly nice partner, removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin and threatening Froslass checks like Poliwrath and Choice Scarf Rotom. Pivots love the extra chip damage from Spikes, so VoltTurn users like Silvally-Fighting, Manectric, and Flapple can both safely bring in Froslass and further damage walls like Qwilfish and Palossand.

Suicide Lead.description:
With just about every great utility move needed and a great Speed tier, Froslass is a great suicide lead that facilitates setup sweepers. Froslass runs Focus Sash to guarantee at least one layer of Spikes. Froslass's Ghost typing and access to Taunt lets it easily shut Defog and Rapid Spin users alike. Destiny Bond lets it take down a foe with it, making it especially useful for bringing down wallbreakers like Klinklang and Silvally-Dark. It also pairs well with Taunt, forcing foes to attack it. Avalanche is its preferred attacking move, as its negative priority gives it a greater opportunity to take advantage of Destiny Bond. However, Icy Wind is also a solid option, as its ability to lower Speed makes taking advantage of the foe easier for its teammates. If Icy Wind is used, Froslass needs to instead run a Timid Nature with Special Attack investment.

Froslass's suicide lead set will exclusively be seen on hyper offense teams looking for a reliable Spikes setter who can quickly provide momentum. The pressure put on from Spikes makes it easier for setup sweepers to secure KOs, so partners like Klinklang, Silvally-Poison, and Crustle love Froslass. Knock Off users like Thwackey, Gurdurr, and Uxie are able to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the opposing side, making Spikes even more dangerous. Because entry hazard removers like Altaria and Articuno are inclined to enter the field with Spikes up, wallbreakers like Lycanroc-Midnight and Sawk immediately threaten these Defog users.

pu.overview: Froslass makes for a capable wallbreaker thanks to its usable Attack and great Speed tier combined with its unique typing. It also has access to utility moves such as Trick and Spikes, allowing it to cripple and overwhelm its answers; it can even run a dedicated Spikes set, although it becomes much weaker without a boosting item. However, its below average Attack often leaves it over-reliant on its own Spikes to get past defensive behemoths like Regirock, while its typing and bulk leave it easily revenge killed by faster threats such as Lycanroc, Choice Scarf Togedemaru, and Sneasel as well as priority moves like Sucker Punch and Accelrock.

Choice Band.description: Triple Axel is a strong, albeit unreliable, STAB move. Icicle Crash is an option, as it's more reliable despite being weaker; it also avoids Rough Skin and Flame Body from the likes of Druddigon and Coalossal. Trick allows Froslass to cripple its answers such as Aromatisse, while Ice Shard allows it to revenge kill foes like Ribombee. Despite seeming odd on a set using a Choice item, Spikes lets Froslass take advantage of the many Pokemon it forces out. Froslass's subpar bulk means it appreciates being brought in via partners like Galarian Articuno, which also acts as a Defog deterrent and appreciates the Spikes Froslass sets. Pokemon like Quiver Dance Ribombee and Dragon Dance Charizard have an easier time cleaning late-game after Froslass has weakened down walls such as Regirock, Aromatisse, and Wishiwashi.

Spikes.description: Froslass's great Speed and typing make it a potent Spikes setter, as it's capable of pressuring common spinners such as Sandslash. Taunt prevents Pokemon like Mareanie from recovering and also allows Froslass to keep its Spikes on the field against Defog users like Silvally-Fairy. Wallbreakers like Magmortar and Archeops greatly appreciate the Spikes Froslass sets, as it gives them an easier time breaking through Gigalith and Regirock, respectively. Pokemon like Regirock, Weezing, and Lanturn can switch into threats such as Lycanroc, Aggron, and Togedemaru that force out Froslass, respectively.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ghost

Froslass can run dual screens with Light Clay to make setup easier for teammates, but the Spikes support is useful in more instances. Ice Beam and Triple Axel can be considered over Icy Wind for the Flying matchup since Spikes is useless there. Ice Beam OHKOes Landorus-T, while Triple Axel does huge damage to Galarian Moltres.

Suicide Lead (Ghost).description:
Froslass's high speed makes it a particularly effective user of Spikes, always getting at least one layer up when teams lack a faster Pokémon. Spikes allows Froslass to pressure opposing teams by punishing switching, and wearing down opposing Pokemon. Taunt ensures that Defog users like Rotom-H, Volcanion and Corviknight, will not be able remove the Spikes, as well as blocking entry hazards and status from the likes of Ferrothorn and Toxapex. Icy Wind offers Froslass valuable speed control, ensuring that setup sweepers like Volcarona can't use it as setup fodder, and also allows Froslass to bring down faster targets with Destiny Bond the following turn. Destiny Bond also pairs well with Taunt, since Taunt forces foes to attack Froslass directly. Will-O-Wisp is also an option as it cripples Pokemon like Bisharp and Tyranitar that could play around Destiny Bond. Cursed Body can potentially cripple Choice-Locked Pokemon like Weavile and Zarude, giving its teammates the opportunity to set up.

Offensive Pokemon like Gengar, Dragapult, Spectrier, Mimikyu, and Blacephalon appreciate the Froslass’s Spikes support, which allows them to KO foes more easily. For example, Gengar can benefit from Spikes wearing away at Specially Defensive Tyranitar to the point that Focus Blast can KO it. Blacephalon and Spectrier benefit from Spikes wearing their checks like Drapion and Heatran allowing them to sweep Poison and Steel teams late-game. Spectrier also appreciates Will-O-Wisp Froslass spreading burns in the opposing teams if running Hex. Dragapult, Mimikyu, and Aegislash appreciate Spikes support to overwhelm physically defensive Pokémon such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Hippowdon. Aegislash deals with Clefable and Hatterene which are unaffected by Spikes. Runerigus forms an entry hazard-stacking core with Froslass, with the former providing Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes

Suicide Lead (Ice).description:
Froslass is able to make a great suicide lead thanks to its high Speed stat and is great for its access to entry hazards, Taunt, and Destiny Bond. Spikes are great to pressure switch-ins and get chip damage on the opponent's Pokemon. Taunt enable Froslass to shut down other Pokemon from getting up Stealth Rock, Toxic Spikes, or Spikes. Destiny Bond can be used to take down a Pokemon with it. Shadow Ball allows Froslass to 2HKO Hatterene that would otherwise bounce Spikes back. Froslass should be used as a lead most of the time to get up Spikes and try to take a Pokemon down with it with Destiny Bond. It can also be saved for later in the game to stop common Rapid Spin users such as Excadrill from getting rid of Spikes thanks to its Ghost typing.

Stealth Rock setters such as Mamoswine and Piloswine work great with Froslass to form an entry hazard-stacking duo to pressure Pokemon from being able to switch in and out, as well as making it easier for Cloyster and Weavile to sweep. Wallbreakers and setup sweepers such as Mamoswine, Kyurem-B and Cloyster appreciate Froslass's Spikes to chip down the opposing team and make them easier to get rid of. However, Froslass will struggle to set up Spikes later in the game if there are entry hazards down that can break its Focus Sash, so partners such as Avalugg and Galarian Mr. Mime go well with it. Froslass also struggles against Pokemon that can attack and KO it with priority moves like Aegislash, so partners such as Galarian Darmanitan and Lapras are needed, as they can take care of it.

ubers.overview: Froslass is one of the premier entry hazard setters and dedicated leads in the tier. By virtue of its base 110 Speed and access to useful utility moves like Spikes, Taunt, and Destiny Bond, Froslass distinguishes itself as a more viable option than other Spikes setters like Mew and Cloyster. Icy Wind also allows it to slow down faster threats and prevent them from using Defog via Taunt or potentially trade with them via Destiny Bond. However, Froslass’s rather low bulk leaves it vulnerable to being easily KOed. Additionally, Froslass has difficulty defeating common Sticky Web setters on hyper offense teams like Slurpuff and Mental Herb Shuckle. Furthermore, although base 110 Speed is adequate, Calyrex-S outspeeds and can use Substitute in front of Froslass and proceed to cause problems to the hyper offense teams it is commonly utilized on.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Other status moves like Thunder Wave and Will-O-Wisp can be run over Destiny Bond or Icy Wind if a particular team benefits from it. However in most cases, this is suboptimal. Poltergeist can be used over Icy Wind or Shadow Ball as an option for a stronger attacking move. In this case, a Jolly nature should be utilized instead.

Checks and Counters

Faster Offensive Threats: Faster offensive threats like Calyrex-S and Weavile can outspeed Froslass and KO it, threatening to sweep the hyper offense teams it is commonly featured on.

Ho-Oh: Thanks to Sacred Fire, Ho-Oh has a 50% chance of burning Froslass, negating its ability to potentially trade via Destiny Bond, and proceed to remove the entry hazards Froslass has set up with Defog.

Status Moves: Status moves like Toxic and Will-O-Wisp can bypass Focus Sash and make Froslass susceptible to being KOed before it gets to lay more than one layer of Spikes. Alternatively, Thunder Wave greatly reduces Froslass's overall effectiveness at setting up entry hazards and trading with a problematic foe.

Anti-Entry Hazard Pokemon: Faster users of Taunt such as Aerodactyl can completely prevent Froslass from setting up Spikes. Magic Coat leads like Slurpuff force mind games and can potentially bounce back Froslass's entry hazards and Taunt, putting its teammates in an extremely disadvantageous position. Furthermore, Magic Bounce users like Xatu can prevent Froslass from setting up Spikes, although it can 2HKO Xatu with Icy Wind.

Suicide Lead.description:
Taunt prevents slower Defoggers from removing Spikes, while Destiny Bond is used in conjunction with Taunt to potentially force a trade with an opposing threat. Finally, the attacking move of choice comes down to personal preference. In most cases, the speed control that Icy Wind provides offers more benefit and utility to the hyper offense teams that Froslass is commonly run on. However, Shadow Ball can be used over Icy Wind if Magic Bounce users like Xatu are a concern or if Substitute variants of Calyrex-S pose an issue to the team Froslass is being utilized on. Cursed Body could prove situationally useful, especially when facing Choice-locked foes. Maximum Speed EVs and a Timid nature are utilized to guarantee that Froslass outspeeds as many threats as possible while almost always setting up at least one layer of Spikes.

As Froslass is commonly featured on hyper offense teams, potential team options include offensive threats like Meteor Beam Eternatus and Zekrom, which pressure and overwhelm the Defoggers commonly found in the tier. Yveltal is another great partner to pair with Froslass, as it has access to Taunt, which can prevent slower Defoggers from removing any entry hazards Froslass set up. Additionally, Froslass can be paired with another entry hazard setter like Slurpuff or a screens setter like Grimmsnarl or Regieleki to form a utility core that allows a variety of setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Geomancy Xerneas, Dragon Dance Zekrom, and Double Dance Groudon to sweep more easily. Air Balloon can be run on any of the aforementioned sweepers if the matchup against Sticky Web teams is a concern. Furthermore, it should be noted that Froslass struggles against leads on Sticky Web teams such as Slurpuff and Mental Herb Shuckle. Thus, pairing Froslass with a fast Rapid Spin user like Pheromosa or Regieleki would greatly benefit the removal of entry hazards and facilitate a potential sweep from one of Froslass's teammates.

nu.overview: Froslass makes for a great dedicated lead because of its high Speed stat and access to the coveted Spikes. On top of that, its support movepool can enable it to cripple the opposing team with status moves like Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave, shut down opposing leads with Taunt and Icy Wind, or even take down a Pokemon with Destiny Bond. Even though Froslass is a strong lead option, it is quite linear in what it can do because of its terrible bulk and defensive typing, which make it quite difficult to hit the field in the middle of a game. Teams that can shrug off Froslass's status spam with reliable entry hazard control and cleric support often result in Froslass accomplishing nothing, essentially forcing the user to play a 5v6 game.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Although Froslass has low Attack, its great offensive typing and high-Base Power moves can make it quite threatening as a Choice Band user, with Poltergeist, Triple Axel, priority in Ice Shard, and Switcheroo to cripple defensive walls. However, Choice Band Froslass is thoroughly outclassed by Sneasel, as it lacks Knock Off and is slower and weaker.

Checks and Counters

Faster Offensive Threats: Although Froslass can cripple faster Pokemon such as Aerodactyl, Salazzle, and Talonflame with Thunder Wave, these Pokemon will still beat it one-on-one, or at least trade on a Destiny Bond, meaning Froslass only gets one layer of Spikes up.

Reliable Entry Hazard Control: Froslass is quite passive besides it setting up Spikes and using status moves; teams with reliable entry hazard control from Pokemon such as Defog Rotom-C and Rapid Spin Tsareena are able to minimize Froslass's role in setting hazards.

Anti Leads: Kabutops and Aerodactyl are other common suicide leads and carry Rock Blast, limiting Froslass to one or zero layers of Spikes.

Dedicated Lead.description:
Set Details

With a Focus Sash, Froslass can consistently set up at least two layers of Spikes against the majority of the metagame. Taunt prevents opposing entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale and Duraludon from attempting to trade hazards. Icy Wind and Thunder Wave slow down and cripple faster Pokemon such as Aerodactyl and Salazzle; this lets Froslass set up another layer of Spikes or use Destiny Bond to take them out next turn. Will-O-Wisp similarly cripples offensive threats, hitting targets such as Drapion and Copperajah, which would otherwise easily shrug off Froslass's moves. Will-O-Wisp even allows Froslass to tank a Rock Blast from Stakataka, which would normally KO Froslass through its Focus Sash.

Focus Sash users such as Aerodactyl and Salazzle greatly appreciate Froslass's ability to reliably prevent opposing entry hazards from going up with Taunt so as to keep their Focus Sash intact. Common hyper offense staples like Silvally-Ground, Decidueye, and Omastar appreciate the Spikes support to soften up their checks while applying enough pressure to make it difficult for the opponent to safely remove Spikes. Additionally, Pokemon that deter the use of Defog such as Defiant Passimian and Braviary as well as spinblockers like Dhelmise and the aforementioned Decidueye further help keep Spikes up.

pu.overview: Rotom is a quite versatile Pokemon thanks to its solid typing both offensively and defensively, great Speed, and decent movepool. These traits allow it to perform well as either a Choice Scarf user or a Defogger. Electric / Ghost is a near unresisted typing, barring Shiftry, which can be pivoted out against with Volt Switch. Defensively, Rotom resists or is immune to various common attacks from Pokemon such as Archeops and Sandaconda, although has to watch out for common coverage moves such as Knock Off. Rotom's Speed allows it to outspeed threatening breakers such as Nasty Plot Mesprit and for its Choice Scarf set to outspeed other common Choice Scarf users like Mesprit. There are other Electric- and Ghost-types that give it competition as a Choice Scarf user, such as Togedemaru with its valuable Steel typing, and Haunter with its higher Special Attack alongside support moves such as Destiny Bond; both also have higher speed than Rotom. However, Rotom's unique type combination and access to both Trick and Volt Switch make it a great option over the other two.

Choice Scarf.description: Choice Scarf allows Rotom to utilize its solid Speed to outspeed various other Choice Scarf users, such as Kabutops and Mesprit, as well as gain momentum with Volt Switch. While Trick is run to cripple specially defensive Pokemon that may try to switch in on Rotom, such as Lanturn and Gigalith, it can also be used to potentially put a stop to bulky setup Pokemon such as Uxie. Rotom is best used as a revenge killer or brought in by slow pivots such as defensive Mesprit and defensive Silvally-Fairy, which furthermore form a solid VoltTurn core with it. Wallbreakers such as Gallade benefit from being brought in through Rotom's Volt Switch.

Defog.description: Rotom can serve as a solid Defog user with its good matchup against various entry hazard setters such as Mesprit and Sandslash. Furthermore, it is able to cripple various other hazard setters such as Gigalith and Druddigon with Will-O-Wisp. Will-O-Wisp also powers up Hex, which should only be run alongside it. Thunderbolt is an option for the last slot if you want to give Rotom more of an offensive presence, although Pain Split is an option to increase Rotom's longevity that pairs well with its low HP stat. Colbur Berry allows for Rotom to better check Fighting-types and other Knock Off users, such as Sawk, but Heavy-Duty Boots is a secondary option so it can take no damage from Stealth Rock. While Rotom does have a nice defensive typing, it is recommended to not switch it into attacks too many times, as it is easily worn down with its only okay bulk, especially without Pain Split. Pokemon that are easily worn down by entry hazards, such as Gallade and Sandaconda, appreciate Rotom's hazard removal.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used over Will-O-Wisp to better cripple defensive walls like Miltank and Coalossal at the expense of not punishing physical attackers as hard. Discharge is an alternative to Thunderbolt on sets with Hex. Rotom can forgo Special Attack investment and run a more bulky set with maximum HP investment to better check physical Ground- and Fighting-types like Piloswine and Sawk.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Silvally-Dark and Alolan Persian are faster than non-Choice Scarf Rotom and can revenge kill it easily. Skuntank can use Rotom as setup fodder if it has locked itself into Shadow Ball. Shiftry and Morpeko resist Rotom's STAB attacks but must be wary of switching into Will-O-Wisp or being pivoted upon, as they are quite frail.

Electric-immune Pokemon: Rhydon, Piloswine, Stunfisk, and Manectric can safely switch into Rotom's Electric-type attacks, especially if it has a Choice item. However, Rhydon and Piloswine dislike Will-O-Wisp and Trick, and all of the aforementioned Pokemon do not enjoy switching into Choice Specs Shadow Ball.

Specially Bulky Pokemon: Despite Rotom having a decent Special Attack stat, it struggles to break past Pokemon with solid special bulk, as they can take a hit and retaliate. Throh can threaten Rotom immediately with Knock Off. Specially defensive walls such as Clefairy, Appletun, and Cryogonal are great long-term checks, as they have reliable recovery; Clefairy can also pivot into a revenge killer, while the latter two threaten Rotom immediately.

Faster Threats: Non-Choice Scarf Rotom is very susceptible to being revenge killed by Choice Scarf users such as Sawk and Gourgeist-S. Faster Pokemon such as Rapidash and Froslass threaten Rotom. Pokemon with priority moves such as Thwackey and Kangaskhan can also threaten to revenge kill Rotom after some prior chip damage.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf improves Rotom's revenge killing capabilities at the cost of some wallbreaking power; it outpaces foes like Froslass, Silvally-Poison, and Choice Scarf Sawk. Volt Switch can be used to pick off weakened foes while also keeping momentum against potential switch-ins. Trick can be used once there isn't a need for Rotom's revenge killing purposes and punishes passive walls like Galarian Stunfisk and Articuno. Thunderbolt makes for a great cleaning move, as it is a stronger Electric-type STAB move that doesn't force Rotom out. Alternatively, Will-O-Wisp cripples opposing targets, namely physical Ground-types like Rhydon, Piloswine, and Galarian Stunfisk, while Defog is useful on teams that cannot fit entry hazard removal elsewhere.

Rotom enjoys the luxury of being able to use Volt Switch as often as possible, so having a entry hazard remover such as Articuno, Altaria, or Coalossal is a good idea. Pairing Rotom with Pokemon that can deal with Ground-types like Poliwrath and Gourgeist-S is also recommended to achieve this goal. Rotom also benefits greatly from entry hazard support, as it wants to use Volt Switch often to force out common Pokemon like Qwilfish and Articuno and wear down common switch-ins such as Throh and Clefairy. Good examples of entry hazard setters include Miltank, Qwilfish, and Rhydon. Physically offensive threats such as Sawk, Rapidash, and Silvally-Dark benefit from Rotom's ability to bring them in safely after forcing out their checks. Rotom is great on VoltTurn cores and works well with other pivots such as Articuno, Silvally formes, and Thwackey.

Utility.description:
With great status moves and Volt Switch, Rotom is a great offensive pivot that offers solid utility. Defog is great on teams that need entry hazard control, while Pain Split provides Rotom with a form of recovery. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers and Ground-types such as Rhydon, Kangaskhan, Thwackey, and Piloswine, and it also boosts the power of Hex. Colbur Berry prevents Rotom from being KOed by Sawk's Knock Off, which gives Rotom a chance to cripple it with a burn, while Heavy-Duty Boots allows Rotom to avoid taking Stealth Rock damage when pivoting. Sitrus Berry can be used for more general increased longevity and is preferred over Leftovers due to the constant pivoting.

Rotom is best used on bulky offense and balance teams that benefit from its ability to disrupt opposing teams and offer support with Defog. Pokemon such as Kangaskhan, Thwackey, and Sawk that appreciate Rotom's ability to bring them in safely; and in return, they can make up for Rotom's lack of immediate power, as it is reliant on spreading burns in order to maximize its power. Offensive threats such as Rapidash, Ninetales, and Skuntank appreciate Rotom's ability to lure in Ground-types and cripple them with burns. Rapidash and Ninetales also benefit from Defog and Rotom forcing out Water-types like Poliwrath and Cramorant. Skuntank helps Rotom by checking faster Ghost-types such as Gourgeist-S and Choice Scarf Rotom and Dark-types like Shiftry and Thievul. Other status inducers like Thunder Wave Qwilfish and utility Rapidash pair well with Hex.

Choice Specs.description:
Rotom is one of the most threatening special attackers in ZU due to the lack of Pokemon that resist its STAB combination. Choice Specs further facilitates Rotom's wallbreaking power by letting it nab 2HKOs on most walls, while its solid Speed allows it to revenge kill a weakened Skuntank or Klinklang. Volt Switch lets Rotom gain momentum on Water- and Flying-types and get out of bad matchups against threats such as Throh and Appletun. Trick can be used not only to immediately cripple the aforementioned specially defensive walls but also to punish Ground-types that may attempt to block its Volt Switch attempts, such as Stunfisk and Piloswine.

Rotom is susceptible to being revenge killed by faster Dark-types like Alolan Persian and Silvally-Dark if it is locked into Shadow Ball; therefore, it is imperative to pair Rotom with Fighting- or Fairy-types such as Sawk, Gurdurr, Alcremie, and Clefairy. The aforementioned Fighting-types also benefit from Rotom's ability to break past physical walls such as Tangela and Uxie and can deal with Normal-types like Kangaskhan and Miltank so Rotom can use Shadow Ball more freely. Pivots such as Thwackey and Silvally formes make for great partners, as they can bring Rotom in safely and form a solid VoltTurn core. Tangela and Appletun can switch into Ground-types like Stunfisk and Rhydon should Rotom lock into an Electric-type move.

Nasty Plot.description:
Nasty Plot Rotom is a great wallbreaker on offensive teams. With a single boost, Rotom OHKOes physical walls such as Tangela and Poliwrath and has a chance to 2HKO specially defensive walls such as Clefairy and Articuno. Substitute lets Rotom block status attempts from Altaria and Miltank and set up on them freely.

Thwackey can lure in Flying-types and bring in Rotom safely so it can freely set up with Nasty Plot. In return, Rotom can break past physical walls such as Tangela, Poliwrath, and Altaria, which Thwackey struggles with. Late-game cleaners such Alcremie benefit greatly from Rotom's ability to weaken special walls such as Galarian Stunfisk and Articuno. Teleport Clefairy is a great defensive pivot that can absorb Dark-type attacks from revenge killers like Silvally-Dark and Choice Scarf Sawk. Rotom also appreciates having Knock Off users like Shiftry and Alolan Persian to weaken special walls such as Throh and Clefairy.

uu.overview: Rotom-H's unique typing generates a solid offensive and defensive profile that grants it a good place in the metagame. As an Electric-type pivot, it distinguishes itself from Rotom-W and Thundurus-T thanks to its ability to immediately threaten and wipe out common Grass-type walls like Amoonguss and Tangrowth. Its typing also gives it the resistances to check Pokemon like Celesteela, Moltres, Scizor, Mamoswine. However, Rotom-H lacks reliable recovery, meaning it can get overwhelmed when trying to check multiple foes like Thundurus-T + Mamoswine. Pokemon it wants to switch into like Scizor and Tangrowth can remove its Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, and most entry hazard setters, including Swampert, Hippowdon, Excadrill, and Nihilego, can beat it, though Swampert and Hippowdon fear Toxic. It's also outsped and KOed by various common threats such as Keldeo, Hydreigon, and Zygarde-10%. Rotom-W gives Rotom-H massive competition due to its ability to immediately threaten Ground-types like Hippowdon and Nidoking, allowing it to have a nearly unblockable Volt Switch.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Nasty Plot + Pain Split turns Rotom-H into a dangerous wallbreaker with the longevity needed to still check Scizor and Tangrowth, breaking through traditional checks like Hippowdon while targeting Fire-resistant Pokemon like Slowking. However, Rotom-H has an only average Speed tier and is subject to being overwhelmed by common Pokemon like Keldeo, Nihilego, and Hydreigon. Defog can be used against Pokemon Rotom-H forces out like Amoonguss, Jirachi, Celesteela, and Moltres, but Rotom-H loses to common Stealth Rock setters like Hippowdon and Nihilego. Furthermore, it must forego Pain Split, leaving it with limited longevity taking on Pokemon it should check like Scizor and Mamowswine. Choice Scarf + Trick cripples common Rotom-H answers like Chansey and Swampert and revenge kills +1 Gyarados. However, Trick sacrifices another valuable moveslot, and using Choice Scarf hampers Rotom-H's longevity by leaving it vulnerable to Stealth Rock.

Checks and Counters

Chansey: Chansey walls Rotom-H with its enormous special bulk, wears it down with Toxic, and keeps itself healthy with Soft-Boiled, but it has to be wary of Pain Split due to the huge amount of HP Rotom-H receives.

Rock-types: Lycanroc-D and Nihilego outspeed and OHKO Rotom-H, the latter of which being a reliable switch-in. Rhyperior can take Overheat with relative ease and OHKO back with Stone Edge. Nihilego and Rhyperior can also set Stealth Rock in front of Rotom-H.

Ground-types: Swampert, Hippowdon, and Nidoqueen all block Volt Switch and can threaten Rotom-H with massive damage or status, although the former two hate Toxic while the latter doesn't like taking Overheat. Zygarde-10% and Excadrill are both notable for outspeeding and OHKOing Rotom-H by getting past Levitate, the former using Thousand Arrows and the latter utilizing Mold Breaker Earthquake.

Water-types: Keldeo, Starmie, and Tentacruel all outspeed and threaten Rotom-H. Rotom-W, Slowking, and Primarina take Volt Switch well and threaten Rotom-H back with super effective damage. Crawduant and Azumarill can pick off Rotom-H with priority Aqua Jet.

Knock Off: Rotom-H hates Knock Off, as it loses its Heavy-Duty Boots and becomes susceptible to Stealth Rock. Pokemon Rotom-H normally would check like Mamoswine, Scizor, and Tangrowth can heavily hinder it, allowing them to overcome Rotom-H in the long-term as it takes additional damage from Stealth Rock.

Pivot.description:
Overheat and Volt Switch have good synergy, letting Rotom-H hit hard and then pivot. Toxic cripples most defensive answers to Rotom-H, such as Swampert, Hydreigon, and Hippowdon. Pain Split serves as Rotom-H's only recovery tool, taking advantage of checks that can consistently recover their HP such as Salamence and Chansey. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Rotom-H get onto the field safely and pivot more frequently. 152 Speed EVs let Rotom-H outspeed Modest Nidoking and nail it with a powerful Overheat, with the remaining EVs in HP and Defense to better check Scizor.

Rotom-H fits on bulky offense, VoltTurn, and balance teams that appreciate its ability to form a VoltTurn cores with Pokemon like Scizor and break through common foes like Amoonguss and Scizor. Additional pivots are essential teammates for Rotom-H; Scizor covers Rotom-H's weakness to Rock-types like Nihilego and Lycanroc-D, brings Rotom-H in against Skarmory and Celesteela with U-turn, and counters Hippowdon and Chansey. Slowking is a slow pivot that can switch into offensive checks like Keldeo and Nihilego for Rotom-H. Additionally, Amoonguss, Tangrowth and Zarude make for great partners, destroying Water-, Rock-, and Ground-types like Keldeo, Lycanroc-D, Zygarde-10%, and Hippowdon that trouble Rotom-H. In return, Rotom-H takes care of Steel- and Flying-types like Celesteela, Scizor, and Moltres. Krookodile is another useful teammate, as Rotom-H brings it in safely against foes like Nihilego and Chansey. Rotom-H also pressures Skarmory for Krookodile, and together they deal with Thundurus-T. Togekiss counters Hydreigon and Salamence for Rotom-H and can remove status with Heal Bell. Wallbreakers that are frail or slow, like Thundurus-T, Zygarde-10%, and Primarina, appreciate Rotom-H bringing them in safely against Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Salamence.

Nasty Plot.description: A very good offensive typing in tandem with Nasty Plot makes Rotom-H a good wallbreaker, as it is easily able to break through common defensive Pokemon like Clefable, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight. It is mostly used on balance and bulky offensive teams looking for a reliable progress maker or Togekiss check. Clefable and Blissey are particularly good partners, as they are often able to deal with common threats to Rotom-H, such as Dragapult and Hydreigon.

Substitute + Nasty Plot (Electric).description:
Rotom-H is a good option on Electric teams because of its ability to hit Grass- and Steel-type Pokemon such as Celebi, Vileplume, and Ferrothorn for super effective damage with Overheat. Being able to take down Steel-type Pokemon is especially important, as Overheat in the Steel matchup can be otherwise hard due to its defensive core as well as revenge killers in Excadrill. Nasty Plot and Substitute in conjunction with its good Special Attack and decent Speed allows Rotom-H to serve as a setup sweeper and wallbreaker, being great against Steel teams as well as other types like Grass, Ice, and Psychic. Nasty Plot helps Rotom-H break past bulkier Pokemon such as Mew, Galarian Corsola, and Celebi as well as OHKO offensive Pokemon such as Gardevoir, Hatterene, and Kyurem-B with a boosted Overheat. Substitute allows Rotom-H to set up on more passive defensive Pokemon, mainly Ferrothorn, Celebi and Appletun, or forced switches. Against Steel, Rotom-H should look to set up Substitute against Ferrothorn in order to beat more Pokemon with Overheat. Substitute is also good because it enables Rotom-H to set up in front of Bisharp's Sucker Punch and force Aegislash to change to Blade forme to take it on, allowing Rotom-H to deal with these Pokemon more consistently especially against Steel teams. Thunderbolt hits Pokemon such as Toxapex and Corviknight for super effective damage while OHKOing Pokemon such as Indeedee and Gengar after a Nasty Plot boost without having to rely on Overheat along with its Special Attack drops. Maximum Speed combined with a Timid nature allows Rotom-H to outspeed Pokemon like Indeedee-F, Mamoswine, and Diggersby as well as other Pokemon like Choice Scarf Duraludon if Sticky Web is set.

The entirety of Electric teams appreciates Rotom-H's ability to beat Steel teams effectively. Galvantula and Vikavolt set Sticky Web for Rotom-H, allowing it to outspeed Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Duraludon, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, and Salazzle. Alolan Raichu is a good revenge killer under Electric Terrain, being able to take on Pokemon such as Seismitoad, Terrakion, and Choice Scarf Excadrill, which check Rotom-H. The latter is extremely important, as it can beat Rotom-H with Earthquake if it is not behind a Substitute. Pincurchin sets Spikes and Toxic Spikes, wearing down the opposing team for Rotom-H, and can slow down Pokemon like Gengar with Thunder Wave and give Rotom-H setup opportunities with Memento. Zeraora is a great physical wallbreaker, being able to take on special walls like Snorlax and Tyranitar with its high Attack paired with Choice Band as well as Dragon-type Pokemon like Dragapult, Hydreigon, and Dracovish with Play Rough. In return, Rotom-H can break past a lot of the Pokemon Zeraora struggles with such as Galarian Corsola, Torkoal, and Vileplume with Nasty Plot. Toxtricity is another special sweeper with Shift Gear that works together with Rotom-H to take on types like Psychic, Grass, Fairy, Ice, and Poison. Morpeko can break dual screens using Psychic Fangs to help Rotom-H wallbreak and bring Rotom-H in safely using Parting Shot. It can also beat Pokemon like Gastrodon and Seismitoad with Seed Bomb for Rotom-H.

Nasty Plot.description:
Rotom-H's strong matchups into sun threats like Venusaur and Charizard, as well as Zacian-C, give it a strong niche. Overheat is Rotom-H's strongest STAB move and, when Dynamaxed, becomes Max Flare, which sets sun, powering up Overheat and reducing the power of opposing Water-types like Kyogre and Tapu Fini. Nasty Plot allows Rotom-H to OHKO Pokemon like Landorus-T, Groudon, and Thundurus with boosted Max Flare, and it also compensates for Overheat's Special Attack drop. Ally Switch allows Rotom-H to redirect attacks like Zacian's Behemoth Blade or Venusaur's Sleep Powder to itself. Safety Goggles gives Rotom-H protection against Venusaur's and Amoonguss's powder moves, while Sitrus Berry provides some recovery; however, protection against Venusaur's Sleep Powder is usually preferred .

Rotom-H fits best on Zacian-C teams that appreciate its ability to check sun threats like Venusaur and Charizard, as well as opposing Zacian-C. Landorus-T checks Coalossal for Rotom-H while Rotom-H checks opposing Ice-types like Calyrex-I. Both Landorus-T and Rotom check many of the same things like Venusaur, Charizard, and Zacian, giving it them flexibility and insurance against these threats. Rillaboom checks Water-types like Kyogre and appreciates Rotom-H's ability to check Zacian-C, Charizard, and Calyrex-I. Prankster Pokemon like Grimmsnarl and Thundurus reduce the damage Rotom-H takes from opponents with dual screens support and Eerie Impulse, and can provide it with speed control in the form of Scary Face and Thunder Wave. Gastrodon can protect Rotom-H from opposing Water-types such as Blastoise and Lapras with Storm Drain and check Landorus-T while Rotom-H checks common Grass-types like Venusaur and Rillaboom for it.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B+ Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Choice.description:
• Rotom-H sports a fantastic defensive typing, and serves as a premier offensive pivot with good defensive upside.

  • Rotom-H often choses Trick and Will-O-Wisp as defensive move options to cripple defensive walls or physical Dynamax sweepers at the expensive of offensive coverage

  • Alternatively, Rotom-H can also opt between Thunderbolt or Dark Pulse as offensive move selections over Will-O-Wisp, which can be somewhat awkward with choice lock. Thunderbolt gives Rotom-H a repeatable Electric-type STAB that doesn't force it to switch, and Dark Pulse helps it get important coverage against various Pokemon that resist both of its STAB types, such as Dragapult.

Items

  • Choice Scarf allows Rotom-H to outspeed major threats, such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Dracovish. It also punishes defensive Pokemon more with Trick.

  • Choice Specs gives Rotom-H much more power.

EV spreads

  • 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe Timid: This spread maximizes speed and power for Choice Scarf.

  • 68 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 12 SpD / 172 Spe Modest: This spread gives Rotom-H some bulk while maximizing Special Attack and outspeeding Adamant Choice Band Dracovish and slower variants of Zapdos.

Bulky Baking Oven.description:
• Rotom-H without a choice item can seamlessly play both a potent Dynamax role and a useful supporting role in one set.

  • Nasty Plot in combination with Electric STAB options allow it to check all variants of Zapdos, but can be replaced by Volt Switch if equipping an Assault Vest.

  • For the last slot, Rotom-H can use Dark Pulse to hit many targets that resist its dual STAB, and can also gain access to Max Darkness, dropping foes' Special Defense. It can also opt for running Will-O-Wisp to gain the upper hand against physical attackers.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry gives Rotom-H a quick burst of recovery that can turn potential 2HKOs into 3HKOs, with th most notable one being turning Zapdos's Life Orb Max Lightning into a 3HKO after Stealth Rock against maximum HP Rotom-H.

  • Assault Vest gives Rotom-H plenty of special bulk to better check special threats, and it works particulary well with Dynamax.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD Modest: This spread forgoes Speed investment to maximize Rotom-H's HP.

  • 68 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 12 SpD / 172 Spe Modest: This spread gives Rotom-H bulk, maximizes Special Attack, and outspeeds Adamant Choice Band Dracovish and slower variants of Zapdos.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used to wear down bulky Pokemon such as Gastrodon, Ho-Oh, and Giratina over time, as well as check Volcarona, but Will-O-Wisp is generally preferred. Thunder Wave is also an option to aid slower wallbreakers, but makes it a worse check to Rillaboom.

Checks and Counters

Gastrodon: Gastrodon resists Overheat and is immune to Volt Switch, and it does not care much about getting burned. Only Toxic Rotom-H can threaten it.

Dragon-Types: Giratina and Kyurem-W are able to consistently switch into Rotom-H without fearing its STAB moves or common status options. Kyurem-W can also threaten Rotom-H with Turboblaze Earth Power.

Knock Off: Rotom-H's reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots for longevity leaves it an easy target for Knock Off from the likes of Tangrowth, Rillaboom, and Zeraora.

Toxic Users: Toxic from Pokemon like Landorus-T and Heatran completely cripples Rotom-H and wears it down considerably, leaving it vulnerable to the Pokemon it's supposed to check.

Pivot (HP).description:
Rotom-H's unique set of resistances and good bulk make it a potent specially defensive pivot, as it can switch into top special attackers like Tapu Koko and Heatran. Rotom-H excels at bringing teammates such as Tapu Lele and Zygarde-10% in safely with Volt Switch, as it threatens common Ground-types such as Landorus-T with Will-O-Wisp.
