Overheat, in addition to being Rotom-H's strongest attack, provides coverage against the numerous Grass- and Steel-types in the metagame like Tangrowth and Necrozma-DM. Will-O-Wisp also helps check Rayquaza and Rillaboom, which its excellent typing allows it to check without significant Defense investment. Pain Split allows Rotom-H to stay healthy, which is useful in longer games. It can also opt for Defog, since it matches up well into common entry hazard setters such as Landorus-T, Ferrothorn, and Necrozma-DM.

Rotom-H fits best on bulky offense teams that have high HP gods, such as Yveltal, Mewtwo, and Kyurem-W. Yveltal is an especially good partner since it appreciates Rotom-H checking Tapu Koko. Other pivoting teammates like Tapu Koko, Landorus-T, and the aforementioned Yveltal form potent VoltTurn cores with Rotom-H. Strong wallbreakers such as Weavile, Tapu Lele, and Zygarde-10% appreciate Rotom-H bringing them onto the field safely. Grass-types such as Dhelmise and Rillaboom make excellent partners, as they threaten Rotom-H's number one enemy, Gastrodon. Knock Off severely threatens Rotom-H because of its reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots to not get worn down by Stealth Rock, so Knock Off switch-ins such as Buzzwole and Clefable make for great teammates. Finally, other special walls such as Tangrowth and Slowbro help cover special attackers that don't fear Rotom-H, like Kyurem-W and Volcanion.

uu.overview: Rotom-W is a potent pivot thanks to its Electric / Water typing and access to Levitate, giving it a rare Flying resistance to check Celesteela and Crobat as well as letting it take on other dangerous threats such as Scizor, Hippowdon, and Mamoswine. Hydro Pump brilliantly complements Volt Switch, wiping out Ground-types like Hippowdon and Excadrill that attempt to block Volt Switch, giving it nearly unblockable momentum. Its utility moves can also greatly aid its team with certain roles; Will-O-Wisp can let it punish Amoonguss and Scizor, while Defog lets it remove entry hazards thanks to its strong matchup against common entry hazard setters like Skarmory and Hippowdon. Choice Scarf sets can also provide great role compression to a team, providing insurance against +1 Gyarados and +2 Celesteela and an entry hazard remover in one slot. However, Rotom-W's low HP and reliance on Leftovers and Pain Split for recovery limit its role as a pivot due to its susceptibility to Stealth Rock, leaving it vulnerable to Knock Off users like Scizor and Mamoswine. Status from Pokemon that it is supposed to check like Hippowdon and defensive Celesteela also poses issues. It also faces competition from Primarina and Slowking, which can check Hydreigon, Azelf, and Cobalion, foes that Rotom-W cannot. When using Rotom-W, one also has to to have additional reinforcements against Excadrill and Zygarde-10%, making it difficult to build with.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Rocky Helmet can be used to punish contact moves like Diggersby's Body Slam and U-turn, while Rindo Berry lets it safely check a +2 Gyarados. However, losing out on the passive recovery of Leftovers makes them hard to justify. Toxic can be used to punish Tangrowth further than Will-O-Wisp, but it is often not worth it over that or Defog, since it leaves Rotom-W unable to touch Amoonguss at all. A Nasty Plot set with Pain Split can exploit bulkier teams and annoy its checks with Discharge paralysis, but it can't hit Grass-types and is greatly outclassed by Thundurus-T as a Nasty Plot user due to the latter's much higher Speed, greater power, and better coverage.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type coverage: Tangrowth and Amoonguss stonewall Rotom-W completely, but they don't appreciate Will-O-Wisp, and must be careful of Trick on Choice Scarf variants; however, they can give it a detrimental item like Assault Vest or Black Sludge. Zarude outspeeds it and can pivot in and out freely, since it does not care about Will-O-Wisp thanks to Jungle Healing. Rotom-W also doesn't appreciate additional Grass-type coverage like Power Whip from Gyarados and Energy Ball from Azelf.

Certain Ground-types: Excadrill and Zygarde-10% can ignore Rotom-W's Levitate with Mold Breaker Earthquake and Thousand Arrows, though they do not want to directly switch into it. Swampert is neutral to Hydro Pump, can fire back with Toxic, and is able to freely pivot out thanks to Flip Turn. Seismitoad and Gastrodon can check Rotom-W better thanks to their Water immunity.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Hydreigon can freely switch in and fire off powerful Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteors and Dark Pulses, as well as absorb Trick from Rotom-W. It does, however, get chipped down by Will-O-Wisp. Rotom-W is also unable to switch into many offensive Pokemon like Lycanroc-D, Azelf, and even other Water-types like Keldeo and Primarina.

Pivot.description:
Volt Switch lets Rotom-W pivot out against checks like Amoonguss and Tangrowth and bring in Scizor and Salamence, while Hydro Pump lets it nail Volt Switch blockers like Hippowdon, Excadrill, and Thundurus-T. Pain Split can be used on Chansey and the aforementioned Grass-types for some good recovery thanks to their massive HP, though Rotom-W must watch out for Toxic from Chansey. Will-O-Wisp cripples the likes of Cobalion, Scizor, and Dragon Dance Salamence, as well as hampering Amooguss's longevity. Defog can be used to capitalize on Rotom-W's solid matchup against entry hazard setters like Skarmory and Hippowdon, though dropping Will-O-Wisp leaves it susceptible to bulky Swords Dance Scizor and unable to meaningfully damage Grass-types. 88 Speed EVs let Rotom-W outspeed Adamant maximum Speed Scizor, with the rest invested into HP and Defense to check physical threats like Mamoswine and Salamence, but it can run a specially defensive spread with a Calm nature to better handle Primarina and Nidoqueen. Rotom-W can run more Speed to outpace Nidoking, but the relatively empty Speed tier in between is not worth the loss in bulk.

Rotom-W best fits on balance and bulky offense teams as an effective defensive pivot against deadly foes like Mamoswine and Meteor Beam Celesteela. Rotom-W forms a good VoltTurn core with other pivots such as Scizor and Zarude, since they are all able to pivot around and come in on each other's checks often. Scizor can come in on Tangrowth and opposing Zarude, while Zarude can come in on Zygarde-10%, and both appreciate Skarmory and Celesteela being handled by Rotom-W. Entry hazards from Hippowdon, Nihilego, and Nidoqueen can be especially deadly due to how many times Rotom-W and its teammates can force out its foes. Since Rotom-W can't handle foes like Cobalion, Excadrill, and Zygarde-10%, which other defensive Water-types usually check, Amoonguss and Tangrowth can greatly benefit it. They can also work in tandem to check Keldeo and Primarina so Rotom-W doesn't get overwhelmed as easily. Wallbreakers like Mamoswine and Choice Specs Hydreigon also appreciate the pivoting Rotom-W offers, bringing them in on Tangrowth and Amoonguss. Checks to both Chansey and Hydreigon are important, and Cobalion, Conkeldurr, and Togekiss help out in this regard. The latter can also provide Heal Bell support to help sustain Rotom-W's longevity.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf lets Rotom-W outspeed many faster threats like Keldeo, +2 Celesteela, and +1 Gyarados as well as pivot out against otherwise faster checks like Zarude. Defog gives it emergency entry hazard control against Excadrill while still reliably beating every other entry hazard setter. However, Pain Split can be used over Defog if the team already has a form of entry hazard removal, letting Rotom-W retain its longevity against checks like Chansey and Tangrowth. Trick cripples Chansey, Slowking, and Amoonguss and can be used once Rotom-W's revenge killing role is no longer needed, such as if Gyarados and Lycanroc-D are removed.

Choice Scarf Rotom-W fits on balance teams that appreciate some form of speed and entry hazard control in one slot that can cripple bulky Pokemon like Chansey and Amoonguss with Trick. Cobalion appreciates Rotom-W outspeeding Azelf, Zygarde-10%, and Choice Scarf Diggersby and handling Ground- and Fire-type moves coming its way. Cobalion can be brought in on Grass-types like Amoonguss and Zarude while also absorbing Knock Off for Rotom-W. Excadrill and Salamence can act as hazard control in place of Rotom-W to let it run Pain Split to aid its longevity. The latter also counters Zarude. Amoonguss and Tangrowth can act as primary checks to Keldeo and Primarina while also handling Zarude and Zygarde-10%. Nihilego provides Stealth Rock support and pressures Thundurus-T well. Trick cripples foes such as non-Choice item Hydreigon to help out a partner like Hex Chandelure. Chansey clears status with Aromatherapy and counters Hydreigon and Nidoqueen.

ubers.overview: Rotom-W uses Levitate and its solid typing to be a nice defensive answer to strong Pokemon like Groudon and Necrozma-DM. Its main draw over other physically defensive Pokemon, like Giratina, is Volt Switch; this makes it far less passive and enables wallbreaking teammates, as it pivots on walls like Eternatus and Ferrothorn, which resist its STAB moves. Its typing is important for its Ice resistance, as not many Pokemon outside of Necrozma-DM can stand up to Icicle Crash and Triple Axel from Galarian Darmanitan and Weavile, and unlike Necrozma-DM, Rotom-W can take Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire with ease. Rotom-W has low overall bulk and below average attacking stats, though, making it fairly exploitable for any Pokemon its typing and ability don't allow it to counter.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Rotom-W can run Trick with a Choice Scarf to remove the threat of walls like Eternatus and Ferrothorn. Trick would most often be used instead of Hydro Pump, which leaves Rotom-W unable to touch a Zygarde behind Substitute and makes chipping Groudon difficult.

Checks and Counters

Eternatus: Eternatus walls both STAB moves from Rotom-W and is able to recover off burn damage, but it can be used as bait for Volt Switch to bring in another offensive threat.

Ferrothorn: Ferrothorn can use Rotom-W to set up entry hazards, as it has no reliable way to damage Ferrothorn. Long-term damage from Will-O-Wisp and Volt Switch can add up, though.

Passive Damage: While immune to Spikes, Rotom-W is heavily hindered if Stealth Rock stays up or if it gets poisoned.

Knock Off: Pokemon that Rotom-W can normally check like Necrozma-DM can carry Knock Off to limit it heavily, since landing it makes Rotom-W rely solely on Pain Split for recovery. Rotom-W doesn't get to use its Ice resistance as much as desired against Weavile, since it fears Knock Off.

Zygarde-C: Zygarde-C rarely has its Substitute broken by Hydro Pump from Rotom-W, even with minimal HP investment, allowing it to set up freely most of the time. Thousand Arrows also negates Levitate, Rotom-W's only way of checking most Ground-types. Zygarde can freely set up on Rotom-W lacking Hydro Pump even before transformation.

Giratina: Giratina ignores everything Rotom-W tries to do, healing off status with Rest and taking almost no damage from Volt Switch thanks to Leftovers.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Rotom-W's ability to check Pokemon comes mainly from its typing and ability, meaning strong Pokemon that can break past its average bulk are very threatening. Calyrex-S, Choice item Kyogre, Zekrom, and Xerneas can all take advantage of it to force progress by wallbreaking.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Rotom-W uses Volt Switch and Will-O-Wisp to damage walls like Eternatus and Ferrothorn over time. These moves are the main draws of the set and are crucial for Rotom-W as a wall to make up for its lack of offensive stats. Pain Split is necessary for recovery and is a great help in the Ubers tier, where many Pokemon like Eternatus have very high natural HP stats, letting it reliably heal off most damage. Forcing Eternatus to recover off the resulting chip damage is important for momentum, allowing in partners that can exploit a free turn off a Volt Switch like Weavile to come in. Hydro Pump is helpful for dealing with Zygarde trying to set up Substitute before becoming Zygarde-C, as well as chipping Groudon, which takes no damage from burn over time if holding Leftovers. Alternatively, Defog can reliably clear entry hazards against the tier's best Stealth Rock setters, Necrozma-DM and Groudon, allowing for Stealth Rock-weak Pokemon like Galarian Darmanitan and Rayquaza to shine as partners. However, it makes Rotom-W even more passive.

One of Rotom-W's biggest weaknesses is status, with Toxic on Groudon or Necrozma-DM limiting how much it can pivot. It is important to pair Rotom-W with a cleric, such as Calyrex-S, Xerneas, or Blissey, to alleviate this weakness. Xerneas in particular is a good pivot into Dragon-types like Zygarde, and it adds a great Knock Off switch-in so Rotom-W can keep its Leftovers. Baiting in Ferrothorn and Eternatus and using Volt Switch is a fantastic way to get in strong wallbreakers like Galarian Darmanitan and Choice Specs Calyrex-S, which can take advantage of these Pokemon. Kyogre is another strong partner, as it appreciates the chip damage Rotom-W deals to its checks, which lets break through them with Choice Specs- or Calm Mind-boosted attacks more easily.

ou.overview: Rotom-Wash has a smorgasbord of qualities that give it a unique role in the OU metagame. An amazing defensive typing, Levitate removing a key Ground weakness, numerous status inflicting moves in Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave, and Toxic, pivoting in Volt Switch, and a form of recovery in Pain Split all allow it to function as an optimal defensive pivot. Unlike other Electric-types that struggle with Ground-types like Zeraora, Tapu Koko, and Magnezone, Rotom-Wash is able to safely switch into them without fear thanks to Levitate. This synergizes well with its access to STAB Hydro Pump, giving it the ability to wash them away without difficulty. Rotom-Wash doesn't just have to capitalize on its defensive prowess; it can also use its impressive STAB combination and its access to Nasty Plot to become a bulky setup sweeper that can still switch in on Pokemon like Melmetal, Landorus-T, and Weavile. Despite this, Rotom-Wash does have some notable flaws. Its recovery is limited to Pain Split, which is entirely dependent on the HP of its opponent, and Leftovers, which gets removed by Knock Off from Pokemon it commonly checks like Landorus-T, Weavile, and Tornadus-T. Rotom-Wash also faces steep competition from Slowbro, another physically defensive bulky Water-type pivot, with Slowbro having access to more reliable recovery options such as Regenerator and Slack Off instead of Pain Split and Leftovers, access to Future Sight to offensively support its teammates, better physical bulk, and slow pivoting with Teleport to bring frailer teammates in safely.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Rotom-Wash is able to slot in Defog over Pain Split because its typing and ability allow it to safely use Defog on Heatran and Landorus-T, giving it a valuable niche over other common Defoggers. Unfortunately, this comes at the cost of a status move, since it needs Pain Split for recovery; this massively limits its ability to check threats like Garchomp and Weavile. Rotom-Wash can opt for a Choice Scarf set with Trick to punish common specially defensive switch-ins such as Ferrothorn and Blissey, running maximum Speed investment in order to outspeed Pokemon like Tornadus-T, +1 Speed Dragonite, and Choice Scarf Tapu Fini. However, Rotom-Wash really appreciates the additional bulk that it has to forego in order to invest in Speed, so it won't be able to take as many attacks. Another hindrance is that Choice Scarf Rotom-Wash is slower than other common Choice Scarf Pokemon in the tier like Tapu Lele, Kartana, and Blacephalon, making it much easier to revenge kill compared to the previous threats mentioned.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Offensive Grass-types like Kartana and Rillaboom can stomach Rotom-Wash's attacks and threaten it out but fear Will-O-Wisp. Ferrothorn is a defensive Grass-type that can repeatedly stomach any of Rotom-Wash's attacks and restore all the chip damage taken through Leftovers and Leech Seed recovery, but it also strongly dislikes Will-O-Wisp neutering its attacking moves, preventing it from inflicting meaningful damage on the threats it wants to check.

Dragon-types: Depending on Rotom-Wash's status condition of choice, offensive Dragon-types are able to switch in safely and set up on it. If running Thunder Wave, Garchomp can come in and threaten it with Swords Dance + Scale Shot. If running Will-O-Wisp, Choice Specs Dragapult can come in and fire off Shadow Balls and Draco Meteors without consequence.

Special Walls: Blissey, Galarian Slowking, Gastrodon, and Ferrothorn are all Pokemon that have excellent special bulk, allowing them to easily switch into Rotom-Wash even when severely chipped. However, Ferrothorn is prone to getting its Leftovers recovery nullified by Will-O-Wisp, and Gastrodon's longevity is greatly squandered by Toxic.

Strong Attackers: Physical attackers like Urshifu-R and Blaziken can overwhelm Rotom-Wash with Close Combat, and Choice Band Tyranitar mauls it with both of its STAB options. Special attackers like Dragapult, Tapu Lele, and Blacephalon can 2HKO it with strong neutral hits.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Set Description

Hydro Pump is Rotom-Wash's main way of cleaning Ground-types like Landorus-T and Excadrill that are immune to Volt Switch and can prevent it from grabbing momentum. Will-O-Wisp lets Rotom-Wash cripple hard-hitting physical attackers like Melmetal, Weavile, and Garchomp and nullifies Ferrothorn's Leftovers recovery and weakens its attacks. Thunder Wave is able to slow down fast offensive threats like Dragapult, Volcarona, and Tapu Lele. Toxic whittles down defensive walls that can outlast Rotom-Wash like Gastrodon and Zapdos. Pain Split and Leftovers serve as Rotom-Wash's semi-reliable forms of recovery, helping it check offensive threats like Garchomp and Heatran and take Stealth Rock chip damage more easily. 132 Speed EVs allow Rotom-Wash to outspeed positive Speed nature Aegislash and neutral Speed nature Volcanion and Bisharp, while the defensive investment allows Rotom-Wash to survive Close Combat from Urshifu-R after taking Stealth Rock damage.

Team Options

Rotom-Wash fits best on VoltTurn balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to maintain and generate momentum against multiple different threats like Heatran, Landorus-T, Tornadus-T, Weavile, and Sand Rush Excadrill. Corviknight is an amazing teammate for it on teams like this, since both of them work in tandem with their respective pivoting moves. Corviknight can patch up its matchups against Grass-type wallbreakers like Kartana and Rillaboom, while Rotom-Wash takes on Fire-types like Heatran and Victini for it. Dragapult is an offensive pivot that is able to lure in Pokemon like Tapu Fini, Heatran, Landorus-T, and Tyranitar in for Rotom-Wash, and Rotom-Wash can lure in Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Ferrothorn for it. Landorus-T is another pivot that works well with Rotom-Wash, since it appreciates Rotom-Wash being able to switch into Weavile's Ice-type STAB moves as well as checking Tornadus-T, which is able to heavily chip Landorus-T with Hurricane or remove its item, and Volcanion for it. Landorus-T is also able to threaten out Galarian Slowking, one of Rotom-Wash's best checks, and can check Dragapult and Tapu Koko for it. Melmetal appreciates Rotom-Wash threatening the likes of Corviknight and Slowbro, while Melmetal can check powerful attackers like Tapu Lele and Choice Band Tyranitar that can overwhelm Rotom-Wash. Tornadus-T is another great teammate for Rotom-Wash, being able to take on threats such as Rillaboom and Kartana that force out Rotom-Wash. It also alleviates the pressure off of Tornadus-T to check Ground-types like Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Excadrill. Clefable is a nice teammate, too, since it can help check threats like Weavile and Urshifu-R that can overwhelm Rotom-Wash and has utility in Stealth Rock, Knock Off, and Trick + Sticky Barb, which can gradually wear down opposing Rotom-Wash checks such as Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking. Heatran fits well with Rotom-Wash because it checks threats such as Dragapult and Tapu Lele while also possessing Stealth Rock. In return, Rotom-Wash is able to check Ground- and Water-types like Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Slowking.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Description

With Nasty Plot, Rotom-Wash becomes a potent bulky setup sweeper that can utilize its solid STAB combination that is difficult to wall outside of Gastrodon as well as Dragon- and Grass-types; this allows it to quickly snowball against teams once these answers are out of the picture. Discharge is preferred over Thunderbolt due to its higher paralysis chance, letting Rotom-Wash punish answers like Dragapult, Rillaboom, Ferrothorn, and Galarian Slowking if they dare come in and try to force it out. Pain Split is Rotom-Wash's primary method of recovery in conjunction with Leftovers, making it difficult to wear down, especially after accumulating enough boosts. The given EV spread alongside a Timid nature allows Rotom-Wash to be as fast and bulky as possible and outspeed Timid Heatran and Nidoking.

Team Options

Nasty Plot Rotom-Wash finds its place on bulky offense and balance teams, which appreciate its role as a mid- or late-game sweeper and can give it the support it needs to fulfill its task. As Rotom-Wash has no way of dealing with Storm Drain Gastrodon, Grass-types like Ferrothorn, Kartana, and Rillaboom are superb partners for it; these Grass-types also provide Knock Off support to remove crucial items like Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T. Ferrothorn lays down Spikes, and the latter two Grass-types help deal with Urshifu-R, which threatens to overwhelm Rotom-Wash with heavy damage. In return, Rotom-Wash deals with Heatran and Flying-types like Tornadus-T and Corviknight. Pivots like Landorus-T, Tornadus-T, Corviknight, and Dragapult are beneficial, as they can safely get Rotom-Wash in with U-turn, helping it pave the way for a sweep. These pivots also aid Rotom-Wash in other ways: Landorus-T and Tornadus-T provide Knock Off support to remove important items like Leftovers from Clefable and Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Zapdos, helping Rotom-Wash break through them with its boosted attacks; Tornadus-T and Corviknight can reliably answer Grass-types like Rillaboom, Ferrothorn, and Kartana, all of which easily threaten Rotom-Wash; and Dragapult threatens the aforementioned Grass-types with its powerful special attacks and lures in Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Heatran for Rotom-Wash to pressure. Choice Band Tyranitar is a solid offensive partner, as it can force through Pokemon that can answer Rotom-Wash like Dragapult, Blissey, and Galarian Slowking. It also enjoys Rotom-Wash potentially paralyzing foes with Discharge, compensating for its low Speed. Clefable is a fantastic partner for Rotom-Wash, since it benefits from Fire- and Steel-types like Heatran, Melmetal, and Excadrill being forced out and handles threats like Weavile and Urshifu-R in return. Clefable can also help pave the way for Rotom-Wash's late-game sweep by dipping into its solid utility movepool: Knock Off deprives Pokemon like Ferrothorn of their Leftovers, paralysis from Thunder Wave cripples faster targets like Dragapult, and cleric support with Aromatherapy cures Rotom-Wash of any status ailments. Specially defensive Garchomp spreads Toxic poison to cripple Pokemon like Gastrodon and Rillaboom that can put Rotom-Wash's sweep to a screeching halt, and it also possesses Stealth Rock. Other Pokemon that can answer the aforementioned Grass-types, like Heatran, Dragonite, and Melmetal, are also solid partners. Heatran sets up Stealth Rock, solidly answers powerful special attackers like Tapu Lele and Dragapult, and can trap and forcibly remove special walls like Blissey and Galarian Slowking with Magma Storm while using Taunt to stop the former from healing itself. Dragonite benefits from physically bulky Pokemon like Corviknight and Slowbro being weakened or removed so that it can set up with Dragon Dance without them getting in the way. Melmetal handles wallbreakers like Choice Band Tyranitar and can punish Gastrodon with Toxic if it dares come in and threaten both it and Rotom-Wash.

Status Utility (Electric).description:
Rotom-W serves as the primary defensive Pokemon on Electric-type teams, taking advantage of its part Water typing to take on threatening Pokemon like Barraskewda and Galarian Darmanitan. In addition, its ability Levitate enables Rotom-W to act as the primary check to Ground-types. Will-O-Wisp is good for burning physical attackers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu while Toxic is important for allowing Rotom-W to beat Pokemon such as Seismitoad and Gastrodon that would wall it otherwise, making it even better against Ground teams. Volt Switch enables Rotom-W to act as a slow pivot for the team in order to bring in teammates safely.

Due to Levitate and Volt Switch, nearly every Electric-type Pokemon greatly benefits from Rotom-W's presence on a team. Specifically, Toxtricity and Zeraora greatly appreciate Rotom-W's ability to serve as a defensive pivot by using Volt Switch to bring them in safely. Rotom-W also pairs well with Vikavolt, which provides a secondary Ground-type immunity. Heliolisk can also pair well with Rotom-W due to its immunity to Water-type attacks, which also relieves the pressure from Rotom-W to deal with strong Water-type Pokemon. In addition, Heliolisk's coverage moves also helps deal with Ground-types, further relieving pressure from Rotom-W.

Nasty Plot + Substitute (Water).description:
Rotom-W is a decent setup sweeper on Water teams thanks to its access to Nasty Plot in tandem with Substitute. Substitute allows Rotom-W to set up on more passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Pelipper, Mandibuzz, and Jellicent, posing a huge threat to types such as Water, Ghost, and Dark. Thunderbolt and Hydro Pump are Rotom-W's STAB moves, with Hydro Pump being especially strong under rain. Thunderbolt hits everything on Water bar Seismitoad and the uncommon Gastrodon, and Hydro Pump beats them both if they are Swift Swim and Sticky Hold, respectively. Dark Pulse is an alternative option over Hydro Pump in order to hit Pokemon such as Celebi, Seismitoad, and Ferrothorn. Generally, Rotom-W should try to look for opportunities to punch holes in the opposition early- to mid-game for other sweepers like Barraskewda and Seismitoad to sweep late-game, since Rotom-W won't be sweeping by itself most of the time. A Timid nature along with maximum Speed investment is used to outspeed Pokemon such as Gyarados and Togekiss that can be problematic to deal with otherwise.

Pelipper's Drizzle is great for boosting Rotom-W's Hydro Pump, and Pelipper can bring in Rotom-W safely with U-turn. Keldeo primarily is an amazing partner for Rotom-W because it can beat Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Hydreigon that would otherwise be problematic, while Keldeo appreciates Rotom-W's ability to beat Flying-type Pokemon such as Togekiss and Corviknight for it. Other offensive Pokemon like Seismitoad, Barraskewda, and Choice Scarf Dracovish appreciate Rotom-W's role as a early- to mid-game wallbreaker in order to sweep teams late-game. Rotom-W also appreciates said Pokemon to beat Pokemon that it can't, such as Ferrothorn, while outspeeding faster Pokemon such as Indeedee, Hydreigon, and Dragapult. Toxapex is a good partner for Rotom-W because of its access to Toxic Spikes, which helps with types such as Normal, Psychic, and Fairy. Toxapex is also great as a defensive pivot, being able to switch into attacks such as Ferrothorn's Power Whip for Rotom-W. Araquanid is a good partner for Rotom-W because of its ability to set Sticky Web and slow down faster Pokemon such as Mew, Indeedee, and Choice Scarf Gardevoir for it to outspeed. It can also threaten Celebi with Leech Life.

Defensive Defog (Water).description:
Rotom-W's good bulk coupled with its defensive typing and access to Volt Switch makes it a good defensive pivot and Defog user on Water teams. Defog prevents the team from being overwhelmed with entry hazards, especially Spikes and Sticky Web; Levitate is especially great with Defog, as it allows Rotom-W to avoid all hazards bar Stealth Rock. Spikes is obnoxious to deal with because it chips almost all of Rotom-W's teammates down, and Sticky Web slows down offensive Pokemon such as Barraskewda, Dracovish, Keldeo, and Seismitoad, making sweeping relatively harder. Will-O-Wisp is used to cripple physical attackers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu, while Thunder Wave can be used to slow down faster Pokemon such as Gardevoir, Duraludon and Dragapult for the team. Volt Switch should be used liberally to grab momentum, whether against Pokemon Rotom-W can't outright beat such as Reuniclus and Snorlax, faster Pokemon, or forced switches. Rotom-W should generally look for opportunities to pivot into resisted attacks such as Seismitoad's Hydro Pump and Togekiss's Air Slash so it can use Defog safety and grab momentum. However, it does lack a form of reliable recovery, so be careful when switching it into stronger attacks and preserve its HP.

The entire Water team appreciates Rotom-W's ability to remove hazards. Pokemon such as Pelipper and Toxapex in particular hate getting chipped by Stealth Rock and Spikes, as it limits their ability to switch in and do their job well. Offensive Pokemon such as Keldeo, Crawdaunt, Dracovish, Barraskewda, and Cloyster also hate taking chip damage and struggle with Sticky Web, as they rely on their Speed stats to consistently threaten the opposing team. Rotom-W can also pivot into stronger attacks for the aforementioned offensive Pokemon and can use Volt Switch in order to grab momentum, giving them a safe switch. In return, many of these offensive Pokemon can use the safe switch in to beat Pokemon that Rotom-W can't such as Ferrothorn, Indeedee, Hydreigon, and Dragapult. Rotom-W appreciates Pokemon such as Dracovish, Pelipper, Seismitoad, and Mantine, as they are able to threaten Celebi for it. Toxapex is a good defensive Pokemon that pairs well with Rotom-W because of its ability to absorb status from Pokemon such as Drapion and Mandibuzz, and it can pivot into stronger attacks such as Roserade's Leaf Storm and Lucario's Focus Blast for Rotom-W. It can also use Haze to prevent setup sweepers such as Hydreigon and Reuniclus from getting out of hand.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: A- Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are fantastic in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame, and can sweep, support, or wall significant portions of the metagame. These Pokemon require less support than most others to be used effectively and have few flaws that can easily be overlooked when compared to their positive traits.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Choice Attacker.description:
• With access to Volt Switch and Trick, Rotom-W makes for a great choiced pivot in the metagame.

  • Thunderbolt gives Rotom-W an Electric-type STAB it can stay in with without Dynamaxing, but Dark Pulse lets Rotom-W deal good damage to Dragapult switch-ins, and is the most damage it can do against Naganadel switch-ins.

Items

  • Choice Specs gives Rotom-W a much needed power boost.

  • Choice Scarf is still a good option to let Rotom-W outspeed important threats such as Landorus-T and Dragapult.

EV Spreads

  • 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread maximizes Rotom-W's power and speed. Modest is prefered for damage output, but Timid does outspeed Modest Galarian Moltres.

  • 92 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 12 SpD / 148 Spe with Modest: This is a slightly bulkier spread that ensures Choice Specs Rotom-W outspeeds Timid Celesteela.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD with Modest: This spread maximizes power and bulk for Choice Specs Rotom-W.

Bulky.description:
• Rotom-Wash's typing is a good fit for a bulky attacker. Discharge gives Rotom-W a higher chance to paralyze foes, while Thunderbolt offers more power and can be a better fit with Will-O-Wisp.

  • Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-W to effectively cripple physical attackers.

  • If using Assault Vest, Dark Pulse is the most damage Rotom-W can do to Dragapult and Naganadel.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry gives Rotom-W a quick burst of recovery, which is important against powerful foes such as Cinderace.

  • Assault Vest gives Rotom-W a lot of special bulk, especially if it Dynamaxes.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 92 SpA / 12 SpD / 148 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Rotom-W to outspeed Timid Celesteela, while offering good bulk and decent power.

  • 252 HP / 108 Def / 148 Spe with Bold: This spread maximizes Rotom-W's physical bulk while still outspeeding Timid Celesteela.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Bold: This spread gives Rotom-W the maximum physical defense possible.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD with Modest: This spread maximizes Rotom-W's bulk and power.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Rotom-W makes a shockingly good user of Nasty Plot, with high base power moves and good coverage.

  • Dark Pulse ensures that Dragapult and Naganadel don't wall Rotom-W, and is an excellent fit while Dynamaxed with Max Darkness lowering foes' Special Defense.

  • Volt Switch lets Rotom-W be a good pivot when it can't set up Nasty Plot.

  • Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-W to cripple physical attackers, and act more as a general bulky set if setting up Nasty Plot doesn't make sense.

  • Substitute lets Rotom-W set up on common status users such as Swampert, Celesteela, and Hippowdon that lack Whirlwind.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry gives Rotom-W a quick burst of recovery.

  • Leftovers is a good option if using Substitute, gradually letting Rotom-W regain its health back against passive Pokemon.

  • Chesto Berry + Rest can also be an effective option against Hippowdon leads.

EV Spreads

  • 92 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 12 SpD / 148 Spe with Modest: This spread allows Rotom-W to outspeed Timid Celesteela, while maximizing its power.

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 92 SpA / 12 SpD / 148 Spe with Modest: This spread makes Rotom-W more like its bulky set, while still giving it enough power to be a threat with Nasty Plot.

  • 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread maximizes Rotom-W's Speed and power. Modest is still prefered for damage output, but Timid does allow Rotom-W to outspeed Modest Galarian Moltres.

Defensive.description: Rotom-W serves as a premier defensive pivot thanks to its high Defense, typing, and Levitate allowing it to check strong Pokemon like Excadrill and Tornadus-T. Volt Switch allows Rotom-W to safely pivot out of threats like Rillaboom and Buzzwole and bring in teammates to pressure them. Scald deters switch-ins like Zeraora and Dracozolt by threatening them with burn. Roost gives Rotom-W consistent recovery, while Strength Sap better checks setup sweepers like Excadrill and Salamence, though it becomes less effective with repeated uses. Rotom-W's last move is flexible based on preference and team composition; Toxic wears down other defensive Pokemon and threatening setup sweepers, while Apple Acid hits Seismitoad and weakens opposing special walls with Special Defense drops. Defog lets Rotom-W serve as an entry hazard remover and has good matchups against many common entry hazard setters. 56 Speed EVs outspeeds Adamant Tyranitar and pivots safely out of strong moves such as Head Smash. More Speed EVs can be invested to outspeed threats like Buzzwole and Heatran, but this comes at the cost of cutting further into its bulk. Offensive Pokemon like Gengar, Weavile, and Keldeo appreciate Rotom-W's ability both to take physical hits and bring them in safely. Rotom-W struggles with special walls like Blissey and appreciates physically offensive teammates that can remove them, such as Aerodactyl and Terrakion, as well as teammates such as Corviknight that can switch into Grass-types like Rillaboom.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

A more specially defensive spread can be used to check Heatran better but it worsens the matchup significantly against Pokemon like Gliscor and Mega Swampert. Waterium Z is a niche option on Rotom-W to consistently eliminate Gliscor and Heatran, threaten a KO on weakened foes, and consistently check Weavile, but the lost Leftovers recovery can add up a lot with Stealth Rock long term. A Choice Scarf set can also be run with Trick, which has a lot of surprise factor, but losing Leftovers hurts and Rotom-W is a subpar Choice Scarf user. Rocky Helmet garners chip damage on the likes of Landorus-T and Corviknight, but it's generally not worth using over Leftovers. Lastly, Thunder Wave is another option that can be run instead of Will-O-Wisp, letting Rotom-W slow foes for the rest of your team to generate momentum easily and drastically punish Pokemon like Serperior for getting too greedy, but this lets Pokemon such as Mega Scizor set up on it.

Checks and Counters

Grass-Types: Tangrowth, Amoonguss, and Ferrothorn can safely pivot in on Rotom-W and and freely set up entry hazards, or chip it down with their STAB moves. Rillaboom, Kartana, and Tapu Bulu have to be cautious when coming in on it to avoid getting burnt, but they otherwise threaten it back out. Serperior can always come in on it, only fearing the rare Thunder Wave, and set up a Substitute and wreak havoc. However, Rotom-W can safely pivot out of these Pokemon with Volt Switch on a predicted switch, maintaining momentum.

Specially Offensive Dragon-types: Dragon-types such as Kyurem, Hydreigon, and Mega Latias can come in and set up for free on Rotom-W due to them resisting both of its STAB moves and not fearing a burn. These Pokemon do, however, fear a Thunder Wave if they hard switch in, and a burn can pressure Kyurem a lot in the long term.

Residual Damage: Due to Rotom-W’s lack of reliable recovery, residual damage in the form of Stealth Rock, status and sand can add up a lot in the long term, reducing it’s reliability as a pivot and a check to Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Melmetal.

Bulky Pivot.description:
Due to its amazing defensive typing, Levitate, and the ability to check a multitude of threats such as Mega Swampert, Mega Scizor, Landorus-T and Gliscor, Rotom-W is a great pivot on offensive teams. Volt Switch lets Rotom-W generate momentum freely on the Grass- and Dragon-types that it lures in, and it can also pivot freely because Hydro Pump deters Ground-types that could block its Volt Switch. Pain Split gives Rotom-W longevity together with Leftovers, although unreliably. Defog is another option over Pain Split for role compression, as it also has a good matchup against two of the best Stealth Rock setters in the tier, Heatran and Landorus-T. However losing out on the recovery is generally not worth it for an otherwise subpar Defogger, since Rotom-W is threatened greatly by Toxic in the long term and loses to common Stealth Rock setters such as Garchomp, Clefable, and Mega Diancie. Will-O-Wisp prevents Pokemon such as Mega Scizor from using Rotom-W as setup bait. The given EV spread allows it to outspeed Tyranitar, specially defensive Heatran, and Aegislash.

Strong wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham, Ash-Greninja, Heatran, and Mega Mawile all appreciate Rotom-W’s ability to bring them in safely, and Mega Mawile especially loves Rotom-W luring in Grass-types such as Tangrowth and Rillaboom that it can use as setup fodder. Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Tangrowth, and Corviknight all appreciate the Fire resistance Rotom-W provides, and they can check Grass-types like Serperior, Rillaboom, and Kartana for it in return. Landorus-T and Jirachi also form a potent VoltTurn core with Rotom-W that can be difficult to stop and exerts immense pressure, as Rotom-W threatens Skarmory, Corviknight, and defensive Landorus-T for its partners. Garchomp is also a notable partner, as it appreciates Rotom-W bringing it in safely and threatening Tapu Fini, Skarmory, and Corviknight for it, in addition to providing an extra defensive measure for opposing Heatran. Lastly, Heatran and Tangrowth both appreciate Rotom-W’s ability to check threats such as Flyinium Z Landorus-T and, in the case of Heatran, Mega Swampert. In return, Heatran and Tangrowth check Rillaboom and Serperior for Rotom-W.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be run to wear down bulkier foes like Gastrodon, Tangrowth, Ho-Oh, and Lunala over time, but Rotom-W generally appreciates its other status spreading moves more. A specially defensive EV spread can be run to better check foes like Heatran, Volcarona, and Kyogre; however, Rotom-W is generally better off being physically defensive thanks to the plethora of major physical threats it can check. Choice Scarf Rotom-W can be an excellent revenge killer alongside slower gods, and it can also cripple slower foes with Trick. However, running Speed investment dramatically reduces Rotom-W's bulk, and there are generally better options for Choice Scarf users.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Grass-types like Kartana, Ferrothorn, and Tangrowth can safely sponge any of Rotom-W's moves and can hit it back super effectively; however, they do dislike getting burned.

Wallbreakers: Powerful wallbreakers like Galarian Moltres, Zekrom, and Tapu Lele are potentially able to overpower Rotom-W. However, it can punish them with status and they cannot safely switch in.

Chip Damage: Stealth Rock severely burdens Rotom-W, as it gets worn down as it repeatedly switches in. Furthermore, Toxic from foes like Heatran, Giratina, and Gastrodon will wear down Rotom-W over time.

Dragon-types: Dragon-types like Hydreigon, Zygarde-10%, and both Kyurem formes resist Rotom-W's STAB attacks and can overpower it, but they must be cautious about switching into status moves or Volt Switch.

Defensive Pivot (HP).description:
Rotom-W is one of the best defensive Pokemon in the metagame thanks to its great defensive stats, useful resistances, and plethora of moves that make it incredibly annoying to switch into. Thunder Wave cripples threats such as Yveltal, Volcarona, and Tapu Lele, while Will-O-Wisp ruins physical attackers such as Rayquaza, Necrozma-DM, and Bisharp. Volt Switch lets Rotom-W generate momentum on special walls like Ferrothorn, Tangrowth, and Giratina for free. Pain Split gives it a form of recovery, which can help in longer games. Defog is another option, as Rotom-W beats common entry hazard setters like Necrozma-DM, Landorus-T, and Heatran. Leftovers is the preferred item to give Rotom-W a form of passive recovery.

Rotom-W fits best on bulky offense teams. It's best paired up with gods with high HP stats like Yveltal, Kyurem-W, and Ho-Oh. Other pivoting teammates like the aforementioned Yveltal, as well as Landorus-T, Zeraora, and Tapu Koko, are highly valued as they're able to keep up the momentum alongside Rotom-W. Powerful wallbreakers like Tapu Lele, Kartana, and Rayquaza also appreciate Rotom-W's pivoting and ability to spread status. Grass-types like Kartana, Ferrothorn, and Tangrowth are annoying for it, so pairing it up with Grass checks like Tornadus-T, Heatran, and Galarian Slowking make for good partnerships. Will-O-Wisp variants are vulnerable against special attackers like Mewtwo, Nidoking, and Tapu Lele, making specially defensive walls such as Galarian Slowking, Tangrowth, and Necrozma-DM fantastic teammates.

Defensive.description:
Hydro Pump is used to hit Ground-types like Garchomp, Gliscor, and Mamoswine that attempt to block Volt Switch. Will-O-Wisp lets Rotom-W cripple physical attackers like Azumarill, Feraligatr, and Scizor. Thunder Wave debilitates Pokemon that rely on their high Speed like Weavile and Alakazam, making them easier to revenge kill. Protect can be used to scout Choice item users like Azumarill while also being able to rack up extra Will-O-Wisp damage and gain more recovery from Leftovers. Alternatively, Discharge can be used for a second Electric STAB that has a nasty 30% paralysis rate, and a higher base power that allows it to KO threats like Belly Drum Azumarill. However, it indirectly inhibits Will-O-Wisp, as if Discharge paralyzes a strong physical attacker like Scizor or Tyranitar, it can prove to be a liability. Both Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave can be run at the same time to give Rotom-W more flexibility in terms of spreading status, but this is not generally recommended. 8 Speed EVs allow Rotom-W to outspeed Adamant Crawdaunt.

This set fits on bulky offense and balance teams where it acts as a slow pivot, safely bringing in strong offensive teammates while checking Heatran, Mamoswine, and Feraligatr. Heatran is a good partner, dealing with Pokemon that check Rotom-W like Tangrowth and Clefable while also providing Stealth Rock support. In return, Heatran appreciates Rotom-W's ability to beat Water- and Ground-types like Slowbro, Mamoswine, and Gliscor. Scizor can check Latias while appreciating Rotom-W checking Heatran and forming a VoltTurn core. Strong offensive Pokemon like Alakazam, Breloom, and Garchomp are able to take advantage of the offensive momentum Rotom-W generates while also appreciating Rotom-W's ability to chip foes, softening them up for the late-game.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Electric

Toxic can be used over Will-O-Wisp to cripple Rotom-W's checks such as Gastrodon, Seismitoad, and Kommo-o, putting them on a timer during a match. However, this restricts Rotom-W's ability to cripple physical attackers like Tapu Bulu and Rillaboom. Rotom-W can run a physically defensive set if Choice Specs Zapdos is used in order to live an Earthquake from Mold Breaker Excadrill at full health and KO it with Hydro Pump.

Checks and Counters

Electric

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Rillaboom, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Venusaur can pose huge threats to Rotom-W, as they resist both of its STAB moves and threaten it back with their STAB moves. However, physical Grass-types don't appreciate being burned by Will-O-Wisp on the switch.

Dragon-types: Dragon-types such as Mega Altaria, Kommo-o, and Hydreigon can easily threaten Rotom-W, as they also resist both of its STAB moves and can set up on it with ease. Mega Altaria can also circumvent status moves like Will-O-Wisp due to Refresh, which allows it to easily set up with Dragon Dance.

Specially Defensive Walls: Specially defensive walls such as Blissey, Celebi, and Alolan Muk can tank numerous hits from Rotom-W and threaten it with their moves, forcing it out as a result.

Stallbreakers: Stallbreakers such as Bulk Up Zarude and Kommo-o are large threats to Rotom-W, as they can take both of its STAB moves with ease and freely set up on it without worrying about status moves due to Taunt.

Residual Damage: Residual damage such as burn, Toxic, and Stealth Rock can take advantage of Rotom-W's lack of reliable recovery, which negatively impacts its longevity during a match. Burn notably cancels out Rotom-W's Leftovers recovery.

Mold Breaker Excadrill: Excadrill's access to Mold Breaker lets it ignore Levitate and completely break through Rotom-W with Earthquake. However, it's unable to come in on a Hydro Pump or Will-O-Wisp. However, physically defensive variants of Rotom-W can live an Earthquake from Excadrill at full health and KO it with Hydro Pump.

Gastrodon and Seismitoad: Gastrodon and Seismitoad can easily switch in on Rotom-W's Hydro Pump due to their access to Storm Drain and Water Absorb, respectively, while blocking its Volt Switch due to their Ground typing. Gastrodon can then cripple Rotom-W with Toxic, while Seismitoad can weaken Rotom-W with Grass Knot. However, both are put on a timer by Toxic if Rotom-W is running it, which limits their ability to switch in freely.

Defensive Pivot (Electric).description:
Rotom-W is a great defensive pivot for Electric teams thanks to its good bulk, Water typing, and Levitate, which combine to let it handle threats like Sand Rush Excadrill, Mamoswine, and Gliscor while threatening them with a powerful STAB Hydro Pump. Additionally, its Water typing means it can check Fire- and Water-types such as Blacephalon, Victini, and Urshifu-R that are otherwise difficult to deal with for Electric teams. Volt Switch can bring in offensive teammates like Tapu Koko, Regieleki, and Zeraora safely in a match. It also works very well in tandem with Hydro Pump, as Rotom-W can pressure numerous Ground-types and prevent them from blocking Volt Switch. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers like Mega Gallade, Weavile, and Garchomp, and it is especially effective against switch-ins like Tapu Bulu and Rillaboom. Pain Split is helpful if Rotom-W is weakened, healing off of high-HP foes such as Blissey. Alternatively, Defog may be used to let Rotom-W act as an entry hazard remover on teams should Zapdos lack Defog. Leftovers gives Rotom-W a form of recovery outside of Pain Split, making it weakened less easily. 44 Speed EVs are used in order to outspeed Jolly Azumarill, while 252 HP and 212 Special Defense EVs along with a Calm nature make Rotom-W more effective against special attackers such as Blacephalon, Greninja, and Choice Specs Pelipper.

All teammates benefit from Rotom-W's typing allowing it to notably check Ground-, Fire-, and Water-types such as Sand Rush Excadrill, Mamoswine, Blacephalon, and Urshifu-R, as Electric teams otherwise have limited defensive checks to these Pokemon. Zapdos forms an excellent defensive core with Rotom-W, as Zapdos can deal with Grass-types that give Rotom-W trouble such as Tapu Bulu, Rillaboom, and Ferrothorn. Additionally, Zapdos can take on Mold Breaker Excadrill, which is very problematic for Rotom-W and the rest of Electric teams. Choice Specs Zapdos can also be used to break through additional Grass-types like Mega Venusaur and Cradily with a powerful STAB Hurricane. Tapu Koko and Play Rough Zeraora can deal with numerous Dragon-types that Rotom-W heavily struggles against such as Kommo-o, Mega Latias, and Hydreigon. Additionally, Tapu Koko can pressure troublesome Ground-types for Rotom-W like Gastrodon, Seismitoad, and Swampert with Grass Knot. Zeraora pressures specially defensive walls such as Blissey and Galarian Slowking for Rotom-W. Alolan Raichu can take on threats like Mega Venusaur due to its Psychic typing while utilizing Grass Knot in order to defeat Ground-types that give Rotom-W trouble, such as Gastrodon, Seismitoad, and Swampert. Regieleki appreciates Rotom-W's ability to eliminate most Ground-types with Hydro Pump, giving it a great opportunity to break through the opposing team with its powerful Electric-type moves. Alolan Golem and Magnezone can trap and eliminate Steel-types such as Mold Breaker Excadrill and Ferrothorn, with both often being immune to Excadrill's Earthquake due to Air Balloon.

Offensive Pivot.description: Rotom-F is not viable in PU, but this is considered its most effective moveset.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Thunder Wave and Toxic are valid replacements for Will-O-Wisp, but the former is punished by switching into Ground-types, which already don’t fear Rotom-S's other moves, and the latter allows switch-ins such as Galarian Stunfisk to come in more easily. Discharge can used as Rotom-S's Electric-type STAB move to paralyze offensive switch-ins but leaves it worse off versus bulkier Pokemon. Rotom-S can be a team's Choice Scarf user, but its weakness to Stealth Rock, vulnerability to common priority moves such as Ice Shard, and direct competition with Rotom make it suboptimal for that role.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Ground-types: Ground-types such as Piloswine, Galarian Stunfisk, and Rhydon block Rotom-S's Volt Switch and Thunderbolt and take little from Air Slash. All of them, however, don’t appreciate taking a Will-O-Wisp on the switch.

Revenge Killers: Faster attackers with moves to hit Rotom-S hard such as Froslass, Kangaskhan, and Silvally formes are able to pressure it out with ease.

Toxic: Taking Toxic from users such as Altaria, Alolan Persian, and Miltank cripples Rotom-S due to its unreliable recovery.

Knock Off: Knock Off users like Sawk, Thwackey, and Gurdurr are difficult for Rotom-S to consistently switch into. Entry hazard setters with access to Knock Off such as Uxie and Clefairy also make it hard for Rotom-S to consistently remove entry hazards throughout a game.

Defog.description:
Rotom-S is a good entry hazard remover in the metagame due to its ability to pivot with Volt Switch and excellent defensive typing that lets it wall and threaten common Pokemon such as Qwilfish and Sawk. Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-S to cripple physical attackers such as Kangaskhan, Silvally formes, and Rhydon on the switch, while Pain Split gives greater but unreliable longevity. 252 Speed EVs let Rotom-S outspeed relevant Pokemon such as Cramorant, Qwilfish, and non-Choice Scarf Sawk. Investing in Special Attack over HP allows it to pressure common walls like Altaria and Piloswine, which is also viable.

Rotom-S fits on balance and offense teams as an entry hazard remover and pivot. Common VoltTurn teammates like Silvally-Dark, Alolan Persian, and Uxie can form a pivot core with Rotom-S to safely bring in wallbreakers such as Jynx and Shiftry. Toxic cripples Rotom-S, so Toxic-immune partners such as Qwilfish and Clefairy are greatly appreciated; Rotom-S in turn provides them with a switch-in to Ground-type attacks. Knock Off hinders Rotom-S's ability to remove entry hazards, so Knock Off absorbers such as Silvally formes, Qwilfish, and Skuntank help immensely. Rotom-S is unable to deal with hard-hitting wallbreakers such as Kangaskhan, Silvally formes, and Rapidash, so strong revenge killers such as Froslass, Alolan Persian, and Choice Scarf Sawk are all great teammates.

Nasty Plot.description:
Rotom-S's decent Speed along with an excellent offensive typing give it a niche as a stallbreaker and cleaner with Nasty Plot. Substitute allows Rotom-S to avoid crippling status from passive Pokemon such as Clefairy and Altaria, which, in conjunction with its STAB Thunderbolt, lets it beat the only Unaware user in the tier in Pyukumuku. Pain Split, on the other hand, gives Rotom-S more longevity against weak attackers without status such as Galarian Stunfisk and Uxie.

Rotom-S fits on offensive teams for its stallbreaking and cleaning capabilities. Teammates such as Silvally formes, Kangaskhan, and Alolan Dugtrio appreciate Rotom-S dealing with bulky Pokemon such as Pyukumuku, Tangela, and Altaria. Faster offensive Pokemon such as Kangaskhan, Rapidash, and Silvally formes are able to threaten Rotom-S, so switch-ins such as Tangela, Poliwrath, and Galarian Stunfisk and fast attackers like Alolan Persian, Alolan Dugtrio, and Choice Scarf Sawk are vital for it. Ground-type Pokemon such as Piloswine and Rhydon are able to stomach an unboosted attack from Rotom-S, so switch-ins such as Tangela and Miltank are appreciated.

ru.overview: Rotom-C serves as a great pivot, largely due to its fantastic offensive typing, as its Leaf Storm can threaten common Volt Switch blockers such as Gastrodon, Flygon, and Steelix. Rotom-C also possesses many key resistances that halt opposing Electric-types, such as Xurkitree or Raikou from sweeping. Along with good natural typing, Levitate provides additional defensive utility. Along with Rotom-C's defensive utility, it can become a dangerous wallbreaker with Nasty Plot, threatening even the bulkiest special walls such as Registeel and Umbreon. Despite this, it can face competition from other Electric-types, as it lacks the raw power of Xurkitree and the natural Speed of Raikou. Choice Scarf Rotom-C blitzes by most other Choice Scarf users, such as Gardevoir, Heracross, and Chandelure; however, Flygon, the most common one, can outspeed and give it trouble. Rotom-C can also sometimes be awkward to fit on a team, as it is an Electric-type that does not resist Flying-type attacks from Crobat and Togekiss.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Rotom-C can run a utility set that relies on status moves such as Will-O-Wisp, Pain Split, and Defog; it should also be paired with Volt Switch and Leaf Storm to retain its excellent pivoting capabilities. This set switches well into a variety of Pokemon, such as Metagross, Raikou, and Starmie. The issue with this set is its lack of reliable recovery, being outclassed by other Pokemon and it only checking a small pool of Pokemon. Shadow Ball is an option to cover Celebi and Dhelmise but doesn't hit much else and Rotom-C can already indirectly deal with them with Volt Switch to bring in a teammate. Substitute can be used on Nasty Plot sets, but spending HP often isn't worth it against more passive teams. Most Nasty Plot Rotom-C checks can break through Substitute easily too. Choice Specs can give Rotom-C the extra power it might lack but is overall inferior to Xurkitree.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Rotom-C is completely walled by the many Grass-types in the tier, such as Celebi, Roserade, Dhelmise, Vileplume, and Tsareena. It can only hope to cripple the defensive ones like physically defensive Roserade, Eldegoss, and Ferroseed with Trick.

Special Walls: Despite being able to Trick them a Choice Scarf or set up with Nasty Plot, Rotom-C can still struggle to break through special walls like Registeel, Guzzlord, and Bronzong, as it is vulnerable to Toxic.

Ground-types: Ground-types, primarily those neutral to Leaf Storm such as Flygon, Steelix, and Nidoqueen, block its Volt Switch, which disrupts its otherwise seamless pivoting; this is crucial for Choice Scarf sets. Although Flygon still takes a hefty chunk from Rotom-C's Leaf Storm, it can heal off most of it with Roost and can pivot on it with U-turn, which does a large amount of damage.

Faster Threats and Priority: Although Choice Scarf Rotom-C outspeeds a large portion of the meta, including base 80 and 85 Speed Choice Scarf Users like Chandelure, Gardevoir, and Heracross, faster Choice Scarf users such as Flygon and Indeedee-M can threaten it with U-turn and Expanding Force, respectively. Golisopod's First Impression also forces out Rotom-C while Lucario, Mimikyu, and Entei can pick it off after a little chip.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Rotom-C is able to outspeed most unboosted Pokemon, such as Crobat and Noivern, allowing it to safely pivot on them. Trick allows Rotom-C to shut down defensive Pokemon, such as Registeel and Umbreon, as it removes their Leftovers and limits their defensive utility. Thunderbolt is a consistent attack that is useful for cleaning, but it also gives Rotom-C the extra power to OHKO offensive Crobat and Tornadus, and it is necessary when facing Togekiss, as Volt Switch doesn't force it out. If a team needs entry hazard removal, however, Defog can be run over Thunderbolt, but it is not preferred.

Flygon is Rotom-C's most common partner, as it can threaten the bulky Steel-types that it cannot, as well as create a VoltTurn core that can be difficult to manage for the opposing team. Flygon also covers up Rotom-C's Fire weakness, which can be taken advantage of by Chandelure and Salazzle. In return, Rotom-C takes down the bulky Water- and Flying-types Flygon struggles with. Rotom-C's fantastic pivoting can also be taken advantage of by strong wallbreakers, such as Pangoro and Heracross, which also help with Steel-types. Unlike other Electric-types, Rotom-C has a difficult time switching into Togekiss, so having Rock-types such as Rhyperior, Aerodactyl, and Diancie are recommended for balance teams. Stealth Rock can chip Rotom-C down over time, which can be a problem in longer games. Hazard removers such as Starmie, Crobat, and the aforementioned Flygon help with this setback.

Nasty Plot.description:
Nasty Plot allows Rotom-C to break past would-be checks such as bulky Nidoqueen and Umbreon if it lacks Toxic. Due to its average Speed, Rotom-C is easy to revenge kill from the likes of Entei, Choice Scarf Heracross, and Salazzle. Grass-types such as Roserade, Vileplume, Celebi, and other special walls such as Assault Vest Reuniclus and Guzzlord are difficult to break through. Pain Split gives Rotom-C the option of recovery, which allows it to take an extra hit to support its setup and overall longevity. Volt Switch can be run to pivot on its checks, but it is not the primary focus of the set.

Pokemon that can take advantage of Grass-types, such as Roserade, Vileplume, and Celebi, should be paired with Nasty Plot Rotom-C. Metagross or Incineroar can both accomplish this role, as well as faster options such as Crobat, Noivern, and Tornadus. Rotom-C also lacks Speed, which makes fast Flying-types even more helpful; other fast Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Choice Scarf Flygon also complement it well. Due to Rotom-C's Grass typing, U-turn from Flygon, Noivern, and Crobat can do serious damage, which makes it difficult to sweep with Rotom-C. Rocky Helmet users, such as Gastrodon and Klefki, are good partners to punish the aforementioned U-turn users. Having fast cleaners like Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Sharpedo, and Choice Scarf Heracross can clean weakened teams, as well as give teams the Speed it lacks.

nu.overview: The biggest benefit to using Rotom-C is its nearly unblockable Volt Switch. Rotom-C's Speed and STAB Leaf Storm prevent Ground-types from reliably denying it from generating momentum, and, although plenty of Pokemon take negligible damage from its attacks, they cannot prevent it from freely pivoting and bringing in terrifying wallbreakers. It's also the best Choice Scarf user in the tier, revenge killing key Pokemon like Talonflame and Starmie, still pivoting very effectively, and providing a source of entry hazard removal. Add Nasty Plot into the mix, and you've got a Pokemon with great use at every stage of the game, be it pivoting and slowly chipping away at checks early- and mid-game or cleaning teams with boosted attacks late-game. Despite all of this, there are still solid defensive stops to Rotom-C like Vileplume and Guzzlord that prevent it from easily sweeping teams and lower the impact of repeated Volt Switches. Additionally, because Rotom-C's Speed tier isn't all that impressive, aggressive double switches into faster revenge killers like Drapion and Salazzle can keep it from continuously generating momentum with Volt Switch. Choice Scarf sets also struggle with this, especially against Protect users like Vaporeon.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Going itemless is an option for blocking Poltergeist from Golurk and Decidueye, although both commonly carry super effective coverage for Rotom-C. These two item options also let Rotom-C more effectively bluff a Choice Scarf set, potentially letting it scare out faster threats like Starmie and Talonflame. Choice Specs sets are fairly potent wallbreakers that make Volt Switch slightly more punishing to switch into and can just get by with Rotom-C's limited coverage. However, they are much less effective at ensuring Rotom-C can generate constant momentum with Volt Switch. Nasty Plot sets can use Substitute + Discharge to exploit foes like Vaporeon that can't break Substitute and cripple checks like Alolan Exeggutor, but Volt Switch pivoting is too good to drop. Foul Play helps against Decidueye and Dhelmise but is otherwise hard to justify.

Checks and Counters

Dragon-types: Alolan Exeggutor and Guzzlord can withstand Rotom-C's boosted attacks, take negligible damage from Volt Switch, and have ways to punish whatever Rotom-C brings in with Volt Switch, be it Alolan Exeggutor's Teleport or Guzzlord's Knock Off.

Grass-types: Grass-types like Decidueye and Vileplume have solid special bulk and typing, letting them easily wall Rotom-C. Additionally, Vileplume and Dhelmise can keep themselves healthy despite repeated Volt Switches thanks to their recovery moves, making them much harder to wear down over time.

Faster Attackers: Rotom-C's Speed still leaves it vulnerable to a plethora of faster attackers, including Talonflame, Salazzle, and Drapion, all of which can revenge kill it and potentially prevent it from using Volt Switch through aggressive play.

Special Walls: Generic special walls like Copperajah and Sylveon are bulky enough to withstand a few hits from Rotom-C, but they're much more prone to being worn down by Volt Switch.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

The combination of Trick and Defog makes Rotom-C an incredible source of utility and gives it even more room to cripple checks to it like Guzzlord, Alolan Exeggutor, and Vileplume. Alternatively, Nasty Plot gives it great late-game potential. If you wish to have a more consistent attack to lock into, Thunderbolt is a good alternative that does more damage to Salazzle and can't miss versus Water-types like Starmie. 8 HP EVs prevent Talonflame from 2HKOing Rotom-C with Brave Bird.

Pokemon like Salazzle, Starmie, and Guzzlord benefit from Rotom-C crippling shared checks like Snorlax and Vileplume with Trick. Similarly, wallbreakers like Golurk and Swords Dance Toxicroak appreciate being safely brought in against foes like Snorlax and Decidueye that they match up well into. Golurk can also help against Copperajah, and Toxicroak easily deals with Vaporeon, which otherwise easily scouts Rotom-C with Protect. Setup Grass-types like Decidueye and opposing Rotom-C can take advantage of Rotom-C locking into Leaf Storm, so checks to them like Assault Vest Copperajah, Drapion, and Guzzlord are necessary teammates.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Pain Split lets Rotom-C make better use of its ability to switch into foes like Vaporeon and Mantine, and it can also be used to weaken checks like Copperajah and Guzzlord that have high HP stats. Thunderbolt can be run instead so Rotom-C has a spammable Electric-type attack after it boosts, but it's usually not necessary.

Rotom-C needs Dragon- and Grass-types weakened or removed before it can sweep with Nasty Plot, so pair it with wallbreakers like Choice Specs Sylveon, Assault Vest Copperajah, and Toxicroak. Conversely, Rotom-C is great at repeatedly taking advantage of bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Mantine, and Quagsire; offensive Fire- and Water-types like Salazzle, Starmie, and Inteleon appreciate this, and in return, they can help wear down bulky Dragon-types like Guzzlord. Rotom-C struggles with being easily revenge killed by faster threats like Flare Blitz Talonflame, Drapion, and Ninjask if it attempts to set up too early; make sure to pair it with checks like Vaporeon, Mudsdale, and Diancie.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Pain Split gives a good boost in longevity, helping Rotom-C continuously pivot and remove entry hazards throughout a battle. Alternatively, Will-O-Wisp lets Rotom-C more quickly wear down checks to it like non-Rest Guzzlord, Decidueye, and Vileplume. Offensive investment makes Rotom-C's Volt Switch more cumbersome for special walls like Copperajah and Sylveon to switch into, but opting for more bulk, especially alongside Will-O-Wisp, gives it more leeway around physical attackers like Guzzlord and Dhelmise.

Rotom-C commonly draws in Dragon- and Grass-types, so wallbreakers like Glastrier and Assault Vest Copperajah work well here; in addition, they appreciate Rotom-C safely bringing them in with Volt Switch, since their low Speed often leaves them vulnerable to taking hits first from the foe. Since Rotom-C is one of NU's most consistent pivots, it pairs well with other pivots like Talonflame, Silvally-Ground, and Passimian. Talonflame also switches into U-turns from foes like Ninjask, and it can bring Rotom-C in against Diancie. Rotom-C is poor at keeping Stealth Rock off the field against Copperajah; strong physical wallbreakers like Passimian, Golurk, and Guzzlord help mitigate this issue.

Nasty Plot + Substitute (Electric).description:
Rotom-C is a good option on Electric teams because its Grass typing along with its access to a powerful STAB move in Leaf Storm makes it a reliable answer to the many Ground-type Pokemon that Electric teams dislike dealing with. Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Seismitoad, and Gastrodon are all easily set up on by Rotom-C, and other Pokemon such as Mamoswine and Excadrill have trouble revenge killing it due to Substitute. Nasty Plot allows Rotom-C to serve as a setup sweeper by beating Pokemon such as Hatterene, Bisharp, and Excadrill after a boost, while Substitute also allows it to set up on status users such as Seismitoad, Pokemon that are unable to deal significant damage to Rotom-C such as Toxapex, and forced switches, as well as helping against Bisharp's Sucker Punch. Thunderbolt is valuable coverage that hits Pokemon such as Corviknight and Toxapex for super effective damage, as well as Pokemon like Aegislash, Bisharp, Jirachi, Salazzle, and Galarian Weezing neutrally. Leaf Storm is Rotom-C's stronger STAB attack that hits the aforementioned Ground-type Pokemon and can beat bulkier Pokemon, such as Mew, Hatterene, and Gardevoir, with a Nasty Plot boost. Although its bulk is not the best, Rotom-C can serve as an answer to certain offensive Pokemon using its typing, such as Barraskewda and Seismitoad under rain, but shouldn't set up on other hard-hitting offensive Pokemon such as Indeedee and Dragapult that threaten to OHKO or heavily dent it.

The entirety of Electric appreciates Rotom-C's ability to serve as a reliable answer to Ground-type Pokemon, seeing as Electric teams struggle immensely against them otherwise. In return, Sticky Web setters such as Galvantula and Vikavolt are good partners for Rotom-C, as they patch up its middling Speed and allow it to outspeed Pokemon such as Choice Specs Indeedee, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Choice Specs Gengar, and Mimikyu, paving the way for it to sweep. Choice Band Zeraora is a fantastic wallbreaker that can take on faster Pokemon such as Hydreigon, Cinderace, and Dragapult and forms an offensive core with Rotom-C. Zeraora's ability to wallbreak early-game and beat Dragon- and Steel-type Pokemon with Play Rough, Plasma Fists, and Close Combat is fantastic for Rotom-C to sweep weakened teams or vice versa. Toxtricity is another special attacker that can beat Grass-type Pokemon such as Whimsicott, Vileplume, and Roserade for Rotom-C. Alolan Raichu is a powerful wallbreaker that can outspeed and beat threats such as Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan, Choice Scarf Gengar, and Choice Scarf Excadrill for Rotom-C under Electric Terrain. Pincurchin can set up Spikes and Toxic Spikes as well as use Memento to weaken the opponent and bring Rotom-C in for it to set up and sweep. Morpeko is amazing against Psychic and Ghost teams and can bring Rotom-C in with Parting Shot while the stat drops help it set up. Morpeko can also break screens, which limit Rotom-C’s sweeping potential, with Psychic Fangs.

Nasty Plot (Grass).description:
Rotom-C's useful Electric typing, access to Nasty Plot, good Special Attack, and average Speed stat allow it to help out greatly with Flying-types and become a fearsome setup sweeper. Nasty Plot allows Rotom-C to net OHKOs against bulkier Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex and Corviknight. Use Substitute on passive Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Toxapex to avoid status and set up with Nasty Plot. Thunderbolt makes Rotom-C able to take on Flying-types such as Corviknight and Mandibuzz. Dark Pulse is used for neutral damage and greatly helping with Ferrothorn, Seismitoad, and Excadrill and Ghost- and Psychic-types like Aegislash and Celebi. Maximum HP makes it easier for Rotom-C to keep its Substitute while setting up on Ferrothorn, while maximum Speed with a Timid nature allows Rotom-C to outpace Togekiss.

Rotom-C's teammates appreciate its ability to be able to threaten Flying-types such as Pelipper and Corviknight. Rotom-C loves entry hazard setters such as Ferrothorn and Roserade to sweep more easily mid- to late-game and in particular likes Ferrothorn thanks to its Steel typing allowing it to come in on Ice-type attacks. Appletun forms a good defensive core with Ferrothorn because its Dragon typing and Thick Fat makes it able to come in on Fire-type attacks from Pokemon like Dragapult and Charizard. Virizion makes a great partner due to its ability to take on Charizard and Centiskorch with Stone Edge, OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Smart Strike and Steel-type Pokemon like Excadrill. Leech Seed users such as Ferrothorn, Appletun, and Whimsicott are good partners for Rotom-C, as they wear down opposing Pokemon for it while helping it set up by providing it with more passive recovery. Whimsicott can be used for its Substitute + Leech Seed to chip Pokemon down and make it easier for Rotom-C to clean up. Whimsicott's Fairy typing and access to Moonblast also help greatly in the Dragon- and the Dark-type matchup with pressuring and taking care of Hydreigon and Grimmsnarl. Whimsicott can also use Heat Rock and Sunny Day to make Venusaur and Celebi turn into dangerous sweepers that greatly help in the Steel-type matchup, taking care of Pokemon that Rotom-C has trouble with such as Duraludon with Growth-boosted Weather Ball or Nasty Plot-boosted Earth Power.

pu.overview: Uxie's position in the metagame stems from the viability of Grassy Terrain hyper offense, which allows it to serve as a consistent sweeper with a Grassy Seed. Thanks to Stored Power and Draining Kiss, it can boost past Steel-types like Togedemaru and Aggron and get past Dark-types like Sneasel and Absol, all of which are common Psychic-type checks. Compared to competition like Swoobat and Comfey, it combines the STAB Stored Power and Toxic Spikes immunity of the former, the latter's ability to hit Dark-types super effectively, and its own formidable initial bulk, which surpasses both of theirs. With that and a solid Speed tier, it is difficult to take down, even with common offensive Pokemon like Charizard and Archeops. However, it is solely found on Grassy Terrain teams, as otherwise, it is too vulnerable to having its setup interrupted before it can sweep. It also can't deal with anti-setup options like Taunt and Encore from Pokemon like Jellicent and Sableye, and it must choose between Substitute and Rest in dealing with moves like Toxic, each of which has its own downsides. It lacks immediate power to force foes out, so even with Grassy Seed, it can be overwhelmed before it becomes a threat. Finally, some wallbreakers, such as Vikavolt and Silvally-Ghost, can use super effective STAB moves break past +1 Uxie with little support.

Grassy Seed Sweeper.description: Draining Kiss is used to hit Dark-types while gaining HP as a side benefit. Rest is the more chosen fourth move, allowing Uxie to beat Pokemon that rely on Toxic or chipping down setup sweepers to beat it, like Gigalith and Charizard. However, Rest leaves it open for offensive Pokemon like Doublade and Sandslash to take advantage of. Substitute can be used over Rest to still protect Uxie against status, as well as Leech Seed from Ferroseed, while leaving it less passive, but this lowers its limited HP pool. Remember that Uxie cannot viably run Leftovers, as it needs Grassy Seed, and it doesn't recover HP from Grassy Terrain due to Levitate. Thwackey is a mandatory partner for Uxie, as it is the only viable Grassy Terrian setter in the tier. It can also bring Uxie in with U-turn, giving Uxie an easier time to set up. Partners like Thievul and Hitmonlee, which fit well on Grassy Terrain teams, can force out Uxie's switch-ins like Gigalith and Aggron.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Uxie can run an Assault Vest set to handle special attackers such as Jynx, Exeggutor, and Manectric at the expense of switching into Sawk, Rhydon, and Gurdurr. Its lack of reliable recovery and bad matchup against common special attackers like Rotom and Skuntank mean it struggles to fit into most teams. Leftovers is an alternative to Colbur Berry on Uxie's defensive set, improving its longevity. However, this makes Uxie vulnerable to Knock Off. Thunder Wave is a viable alternative to Knock Off on defensive Uxie that debilitates faster attackers such as Thievul and Silvally formes, letting Uxie's teammates take them on more easily. Defensive Uxie can also run Choice Scarf with Trick and 64 Speed EVs, letting it outspeed up to Alolan Persian and debilitate a potential entry hazard remover like Articuno or Coalossal. However, Uxie can get a harmful item like Skuntank's Black Sludge or Rotom's Choice Specs, or even become setup fodder for Silvally formes due to their Trick immunity. Memento is an alternative for the defensive pivot set, blocking Defog and bringing in a teammate more safely than U-turn, but Uxie often can't fit it. Encore can be used to punish Pokemon that otherwise freely set up on Uxie like Galarian Rapidash and Ninetales.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Uxie is threatened by attackers such as Rotom and Gourgeist-S. However, most of them take great damage from Knock Off and STAB moves, meaning Uxie can pressure them on the switch.

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Thievul, Silvally-Dark, and Skuntank threaten Uxie with their super effective STAB moves, block Future Sight, and can sponge boosted Draining Kiss. However, several of them, including Liepard and Morpeko, take heavy damage from U-turn, and Colbur Berry Uxie can afford to take a hit.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Defensive sweepers such as Alcremie and Spiritomb easily set up on the weak Uxie. Most of them can also beat Uxie in a setup war.

Wallbreakers and Stallbreakers: Wallbreakers such as Thwackey and Froslass can use Uxie's passivity to threaten its whole team with their powerful moves. However, they dislike losing their items to Knock Off. Faster Taunt users such as Alolan Persian can shut down Uxie's utility and take advantage of it with Toxic.

Steel-types: Setup Uxie has a very hard time breaking through Steel-types such as Klinklang due to its low damage output. They can easily break Uxie's Substitute and remove Uxie before it is boosted enough.

Haze Articuno and Unaware Pyukumuku: Haze Articuno and Unaware Pyukumuku can wall most setup Uxie. However, Pyukumuku has to be wary of Stored Power's increased Base Power.

Nasty Plot.description:
Uxie can act as a terrifying late-game cleaner with its Nasty Plot set. Substitute lets it avoid status such as Toxic from Articuno and Altaria, dodge Knock Off from Tangela and Clefairy, and sponge hits from weak attackers like Clefairy lacking Seismic Toss and Stunfisk. Psyshock is preferred over Psychic as a STAB move to get around special walls like Articuno and Clefairy more easily. Draining Kiss lets Uxie break through Dark-types like Thievul and Morpeko after a boost and provides coveted recovery.

Uxie is a great late-game cleaner for bulkier teams that can weaken its checks over time. Therefore, entry hazard support, especially Spikes from setters such as Coalossal and Qwilfish, is invaluable. Knock Off support is similarly valuable for removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers, the latter being the only form of recovery of Steel-types that check Uxie like Klinklang. Toxic users such as Altaria and Rapidash cripple the likes of Haze Articuno, Alcremie, and Musharna to help Uxie break through them.
