Special wallbreakers such as Exeggutor, Rotom, and Jynx can soften opposing special walls in order to let Liepard clean late game. Checks to Fighting-types such as Uxie, Qwilfish, and Altaria take on Sawk and Gurdurr, which force Liepard out. Likewise, checks to Fairy-types like Klinklang, Silvally-Poison, and Rapidash are great partners that handle Alcremie and Clefairy. Checks to Dark-types such as Alcremie, Gurdurr, and Sawk are also appreciated, as Silvally-Dark and Skuntank can take on Liepard. Kangaskhan is a threat because of Fake Out outprioritizing Copycat, letting it easily revenge kill a weakened Liepard; therefore, checks like Uxie, Tangela, and Cofagrigus are appreciated.

All-out Attacker.description:
With excellent Speed, STAB Knock Off, and great coverage choices, Liepard makes for a potent all-out attacker. U-turn pivots from switch-ins like Poliwrath, Tangela, and Alolan Persian. Prankster Copycat revenge kills naturally faster Pokemon and Choice Scarf Pokemon locked into certain moves, like Froslass, Alolan Dugtrio, and Choice Scarf Sawk and Rotom. Sucker Punch alongside Life Orb provides more consistent priority. Gunk Shot targets Alcremie and Tangela, while Play Rough hits incoming Fighting-types like Sawk, Throh, and Gurdurr. If Liepard chooses not to run Copycat, then Limber should be chosen to avoid paralysis from Stunfisk.

Liepard fits well on VoltTurn teams, being able to use Prankster Copycat to copy slow Volt Switches and U-turns. Pivots like Articuno, Thwackey, and Choice Scarf Rotom can work with it to wear down the opposition. Liepard's Knock Off helps cripple entry hazard removers like Articuno and Cryogonal, allowing Stealth Rock setters like Palossand and Rhydon to keep up hazards more consistently. While some of Liepard's checks, like Gurdurr and Tangela, hate losing their items to Knock Off and getting pivoted on by U-turn, Liepard can still struggle to break through them by itself. Special attackers, like Jynx and mixed Silvally-Poison, can ease its need for prediction and give it switch-ins to fall back on. Spikes setters like Qwilfish and Froslass can make Liepard increasingly difficult to switch into.

zu.overview: Musharna is unviable in SS ZU because it is outclassed by other Calm Mind users such as Alcremie and Galarian Rapidash due to their better abilities and defensive typing.

Calm Mind.description: Musharna acts as an late-game cleaner with its great bulk and access to Calm Mind, Heal Bell, and reliable recovery. It does have some use on Electric Terrain teams when it runs Electric Seed, since consuming its item can help it avoid or better take hits from strong moves like Poltergeist and Knock Off, but even then it is outclassed entirely by Uxie. However, Musharna is almost never worth using over Alcremie and Galarian Rapidash because they have better defensive typings for the tier, which allows them to run useful items like Leftovers. They also have great abilities to avoid Taunt and Encore in Alcremie's case and Toxic in Galarian Rapidash's case.

zu.comments:
Other Options

A utility set with Heavy-Duty Boots, Roost, and Defog is feasible, as this set gives Unfezant reliable recovery and allows it to be an offensive entry hazard remover. However, the listed sets more naturally play to Unfezant's strengths, and this set struggles even more against hazard setters like Coalossal, Rhydon, and Qwilfish due to its reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Rock- and Steel-types: Rhydon, Coalossal, and Klinklang resist Unfezant's STAB moves, fear none of its coverage, and threaten OHKOs or significant damage with their STAB moves. Rhydon and Coalossal can also set or remove entry hazards, and Coalossal's Flame Body deters Unfezant from pivoting or attacking. However, Pawniard and Klinklang can be worn down by the Choice Band set and fail to reliably switch in later on.

Stealth Rock: Unfezant’s weakness to Stealth Rock and recoil from Brave Bird quickly wear it down, causing it to faint rather quickly.

Electric-types: Electric-types like Rotom formes and Stunfisk can stomach a hit from both Unfezant sets and threaten to OHKO in return with their super effective STAB moves. Stunfisk also has Static to discourage Unfezant from pivoting with U-turn. However, Rotom must be aware of Night Slash from the Choice Band set.

Faster Offensive Threats: While none of them can safely switch in, Pokemon like Jynx, Rapidash, and Choice Scarf Sawk and Rotom can KO Choice Band Unfezant with minimal to no prior chip damage due to its mediocre bulk. However, they must also be aware of Choice Scarf sets, which they can't check.

Choice Band.description:
Unfezant is a powerful wallbreaker, able to devastate teams without sturdy Flying-resistant Pokemon such as Rhydon or Coalossal with Choice Band-boosted STAB Brave Bird. U-turn enables Unfezant to pivot out against Stunfisk, Piloswine, and Klinklang, keeping momentum and chipping them. Quick Attack finishes off weakened faster foes like Jynx and Accelgor. Night Slash lets Unfezant OHKO Rotom. Facade instead becomes a very powerful STAB move if Unfezant gets statused. Super Luck gives it better chances to break through Double Dance Alcremie if it has gained a Defense boost prior.

Unfezant fits well in offensive teams due to its great power, good Speed tier, and mediocre bulk. It struggles to break past sturdy Flying-resistant Pokemon like Klinklang and Coalossal and could potentially lose momentum against them. Water- and Electric-types pair particularly well, as Pokemon like Silvally-Water, Rotom, and Raichu can force them out with their STAB or coverage moves and bring Unfezant in safely with their pivot moves. In return, Unfezant can form a VoltTurn core with them and force out Grass-types such as Tangela and Gourgeist-S, which pressure them. Spikes users, such as Qwilfish and Coalossal, wear down its checks, many of which lack reliable recovery. Entry hazard control from the likes of Coalossal, Rotom, and Hattrem can ameliorate its Stealth Rock weakness. Special wallbreakers like Rotom, Exeggutor, and Jynx can overwhelm physical walls like Rhydon, Pyukumuku, and Miltank that Unfezant has difficulty breaking through. Other Flying-type wallbreakers, like Silvally-Flying and Rotom-S, can overwhelm their checks with repeated STAB Flying-type moves and coverage options.

Choice Scarf.description:
Unfezant also carves itself a niche on offensive teams as a fantastic revenge killer. It notably outspeeds and OHKOes two of the most prominent opposing Choice Scarf users, Rotom and Sawk, with Night Slash and Brave Bird, respectively. While Unfezant's main attack is its powerful STAB Brave Bird, it can also use U-turn to pivot out of unfavorable matchups such as Klinklang, Miltank, Rhydon, and Galarian Stunfisk. Facade provides Unfezant with a strong secondary STAB option once it becomes inflicted by status, as tends to happen, usually by a stray Toxic or Static paralyzation. Super Luck synergizes well with Night Slash and is useful for breaking through certain bulky setup sweepers like Acid Armor Alcremie and Kee Berry Uxie.

Choice Scarf Unfezant fits best on bulky offense teams that can wear down the opposing team so it can clean up. Unfezant can create a VoltTurn core with teammates such as Kabutops and Rotom that collectively weakens its checks. Unfezant could also create a Flying-type spam core with Silvally-Flying, which notably nails Rhydon and Coalossal with Surf. Unfezant also appreciates offensive teammates such as Rapidash and Poliwrath that can help combat Flying-resistant foes. Hattrem is a common sight on Flying-type spam teams, bouncing back Stealth Rock and nailing Rock-types or Steel-types with either Giga Drain or Mystical Fire. Because of Brave Bird recoil and Stealth Rock, as well as Unfezant's tendency to switch in multiple times per game, entry hazard removal from teammates such as Defog Rotom and Gurdurr is much appreciated.

pu.overview: Gigalith’s excellent natural bulk in tandem with Sand Stream allows it to act as one of PU’s most widely useful Pokemon. Its typing allows it to resist common threats such as Galarian Articuno, Ribombee, and Charizard, and with base 135 Attack, it is by no means passive. However, Gigalith has no means of recovery outside of Leftovers and is prone to being worn down. Its pure Rock typing can be a detriment at times, as Pokemon such as Eldegoss can come in on it for free and proceed to remove Gigalith’s hazards while threatening it out with its STAB moves.

Specially Defensive.description: Stone Edge can be run over Rock Blast for more immediate damage, but its low PP and accuracy make it unreliable at times. Earthquake prevents Pokemon like Togedemaru and Aggron from taking advantage of Gigalith. Protect is used to scout for Choice-locked Pokemon such as Trevenant and Togedemaru, as well as to gain additional Leftovers recovery and rack up residual Sandstorm damage. Toxic can be run to cripple Pokemon such as Whimsicott and punish safe switch-ins such as Regirock and Palossand, which would otherwise come in on it for free. Sand Rush users like Sandslash and Lycanroc can more easily break through or sweep opposing teams with Gigalith's sand supporting them. Gigalith should be paired with team members that can deal with Water-, Grass-, or Fighting-types, such as Lanturn, Ferroseed, and Weezing. Lanturn is also able to support Gigalith with Heal Bell, allowing it to better check Pokemon like Charizard that commonly run Toxic, while Ferroseed can cripple switch-ins like Charizard with Knock Off while giving Gigalith switch-in opportunities. Other teammates such as Doublade and Whimsicott appreciate Gigalith’s ability to handle Fire- and Flying-types, and Whimsicott also deals with the Water- and Ground-types that give Gigalith trouble.

nu.overview: Gigalith is the sole viable sand setter, enabling Sand Rush users like Sandslash and Lycanroc and racking up chip damage against defensive staples like Xatu, Sylveon, and Talonflame, as well as the opponent's team in general. Gigalith's great all-around defensive stats allow it multiple opportunities to set up sand. Furthermore, it can check Salazzle and Talonflame while having utility with moves like Stealth Rock and Toxic. However, its abysmal Speed usually means it must take a hit before moving. When combined with damage on the switch, status, and no reliable recovery, Gigalith can be worn down deceptively quickly, especially since it's weak to STAB or coverage moves from Pokemon such as Toxicroak, Exploud, and Diancie. Gigalith is also difficult to teambuild around due to almost exclusively fitting on dedicated sand teams, and these teams demand extensive support to execute a successful sweep.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Heavy Slam can punish defensive Sylveon for trying to stall out sand turns and heavily damage other Fairy-types like Diancie and Comfey. Explosion deals huge damage to most neutral targets and can keep up momentum for sand builds at the cost of sacrificing Gigalith.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Fighting-types like Scrafty, Passimian, Gallade, and Toxicroak can massively damage Gigalith with their STAB moves and force it out. However, Toxicroak can be OHKOed by Earthquake after taking damage from Stealth Rock and sand.

Water-types: Vaporeon does not take much damage from any of Gigalith's attacks and can use it to pass Wish to its teammates, fish for burns with Scald, or remove status with Heal Bell. More offensive Water-types, like Starmie and Kingdra, can avoid the 2HKO from any of its attacks and use it as a chance to start wallbreaking or set up; however, the combination of Toxic poison and sand damage severely limits their sweeping potential.

Grass-types: Vileplume's immunity to Toxic and great defensive stats mean it can easily recover from any of Gigalith's attacks via Strength Sap, whittle it down with Giga Drain, or even use it as setup fodder. Tsareena and Dhelmise can easily use Rapid Spin against it, while Decidueye can set up Swords Dance on it, but all of them dislike taking Toxic upon switching in.

Ground-types: Mudsdale and Palossand can cripple Gigalith with Toxic and set up Stealth Rock freely, while offensive Ground-types, like Golurk, Silvally-Ground, and Rhydon, can switch in on any of Gigalith's moves and fire off a powerful attack. None of them appreciate taking Toxic, however.

Residual Damage: Although Gigalith does not mind paralysis due to its already terrible Speed, its longevity is severely hampered by poison and burn, with the latter also hurting its ability to damage Xatu as it switches in. Stealth Rock and Spikes wear it down even more quickly.

Specially Defensive.description:
Set Description

Toxic wears down foes like Vaporeon, Exploud, and Rotom-C and prevents them from taking advantage of Gigalith. Earthquake provides super effective coverage against foes like Toxicroak, Heliolisk, and Copperajah. A specially defensive EV spread alongside Leftovers is recommended to more effectively check Salazzle, Sylveon, and Exploud over the course of a game. Leftovers helps Gigalith get worn down less quickly, but Smooth Rock gives more setup chances for Sand Rush sweepers like Lycanroc and Sandslash.

Gigalith synergizes well with Lycanroc and Sandslash, letting both use Sand Rush to wallbreak or sweep. Pokemon like Rotom-C, Alolan Exeggutor, and Xatu help cover Gigalith's weaknesses to Water, Grass, and Fighting and can pivot. In turn, Gigalith can address Rotom-C's struggles against Poison- and Fire-types and sponge weak neutral or resisted special hits, like Xatu's Psychic and all of Salazzle's moves. Starmie provides Rapid Spin support and an additional switch-in to Water- and Fighting-type attacks.

pu.overview: Swoobat's niche simply comes from its ability, Simple. Using Calm Mind, it can snowball through teams more quickly faster than other setup sweepers such as Sandaconda and Uxie can. After Grassy Seed activation and one Calm Mind, Stored Power 2HKOes Audino, and another Calm Mind sees Gigalith, the tier's best special wall, KOed after Stealth Rock. Thanks to Calm Mind's Special Defense boosts, faster special attackers like Whimsicott and Ribombee struggle to revenge kill it, although Whimsicott can bother Swoobat with Encore. With Heat Wave, set-up Swoobat can also tear through Steel-types like Ferroseed and Doublade, which are usually solid checks to Psychic-types. Another boon for Swoobat is its great Speed tier, which makes it harder for tier staples like Charizard and Archeops to revenge kill. However, it relies on Grassy Seed to be effective, restricting it to Grassy Terrain teams. Despite Grassy Seed activation giving Swoobat Defense and denying Knock Off's damage boost, its physical bulk is overall poor, with a weakness to Stealth Rock alongside common Dark- and Rock-type moves not helping it. Finally, Swoobat can't fit both Heat Wave and Substitute on the same set, which means either it relies on teammates to remove Steel-types so it can sweep, or it becomes unable to set up on more passive Pokemon like Audino without fearing Toxic.

Simple Sweeper.description: Swoobat sets up Calm Mind most efficiently on slower defensive Pokemon that lack a status move, such as Sandslash and Eldegoss. Roost gives Swoobat reliable recovery, ensuring that random chip damage doesn't faze it, and lets it avoid super effective damage from slower Rock-types like Regirock and Aggron. Substitute protects Swoobat against common methods of incapacitating setup sweepers, like Trick + a Choice item or Toxic. Heat Wave targets Steel-types directly, OHKOing Togedemaru and Ferroseed after a Calm Mind. The given EV spread ensures a Gyro Ball from Ferroseed cannot break Swoobat's Substitute after Grassy Seed and it maximizes Speed for Lycanroc. Thwackey is absolutely mandatory on teams with Swoobat, as no other viable Pokemon can automatically set Grassy Terrain. On these Grassy Terrain teams, Grassy Seed + Unburden Thievul and Hitmonlee make great partners; both of them can also thrash Steel-types like Togedemaru and Aggron. Some entry hazard removers such as Coalossal can easily fit on Grassy Terrain teams and often remove Stealth Rock for Swoobat.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Taunt can be used over Roost to prevent Swoobat from getting hit with status, Haze, or forced out by Roar. Articuno and Rhydon are the most common users of these moves. Substitute can also be used to dodge status and makes Swoobat harder to revenge kill.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Silvally-Dark, Skunktank, and Morpeko can threaten Swoobat with their STAB attacks and are immune to Stored Power. Sableye and Liepard are notable threats, as they can Encore Swoobat into Calm Mind thanks to Prankster.

Haze and Phazers: Articuno and Cryogonal can Haze Swoobat, eliminating all of Swoobat's stat boosts. Rhydon and Articuno can also phaze out Swoobat with Roar.

Faster Threats: Choice Scarf Rotom, Manectric, and Kabutops outspeed Swoobat and can threaten Swoobat with their STAB attacks. Rotom and Manectric can also cripple Swoobat with Trick and Switcheroo respectively.

Terrain Sweeper.description:
Swoobat is a devastating sweeper in Terrain thanks to its great Speed tier and fantastic ability in Simple. Electric Seed boosts Swoobat's Defense significantly on switch-in, giving it much more physical bulk to ease setup, lessening its weakness to Knock Off, and providing it with an immunity to Poltergeist. Calm Mind boosts Swoobat's Special Attack and Special Defense, turning Stored Power into a destructive 140 Base Power move after a single use and Electric Seed's activation. Air Slash hits foes that resist or are immune to Psychic such as Uxie, Skuntank, and Silvally-Dark, while Heat Wave targets Klinklang, which resists both of Swoobat's STAB moves. Roost keeps Swoobat healthy, making it harder to revenge kill and giving it opportunities to set up multiple Calm Minds. The EV spread maximizes Swoobat's bulk and Speed, allowing it to always live Thunderbolt from Choice Scarf Rotom at +2 Special Defense after Stealth Rock damage.

Pincurchin is a mandatory teammate, as it provides Electric Terrain to trigger Swoobat's Electric Seed. It can also assist with Spikes support and provides a free turn of setup with Memento. Other beneficiaries of Electric Terrain such as Drifblim, Uxie, and Thievul make great partners, helping in wearing down shared checks, making it easier for Swoobat to sweep. Raichu and Manectric can also assist Swoobat by wallbreaking with boosted Rising Voltage and providing an immunity to Electric for the team. Pokemon that can pressure Dark- and Steel-types for Swoobat such as Sawk and Gurdurr also work well as teammates.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Drilbur can opt to run a bulkier spread of 116 HP / 76 Atk / 196 Def / 120 Spe with an Impish Nature to better counter Pokemon like Tyrunt. Another option is replacing Rock Slide with Rock Tomb, exchanging some power for speed control. Alternatively, moves like Poison Jab to hit Grookey and Morelull on the switch, Toxic to cripple Shellos and Cosmic Power Natu, and Swords Dance to potentially sweep can be used instead.

Checks and Counters

Grookey: Grookey can switch in safely against Drilbur unless it is running the rare Poison Jab. Once it is in, Grookey threatens a KO with priority Grassy Glide and can punish a switch with U-turn.

Water-types: Drilbur does poorly into most Water-types. Frillish can easily tank Drilbur's attacks, can block Rapid Spin, and can do huge damage back. Carvanha and Staryu both outpace Drilbur and KO it easily, and Shellos can set up on it for free unless Drilbur is carrying the niche Toxic.

Fast Utility.description:
Drilbur is a useful role-compression choice in Little Cup, able to both set and remove entry hazards. Mold Breaker means that, unlike other Stealth Rock users, Drilbur does not have to fear Natu's Magic Bounce. Furthermore, having the rare Rapid Spin makes Drilbur one of the most efficient entry hazard removers in the tier and lets it boost its Speed for late-game cleaning. High Horsepower is slightly weaker and less accurate than Earthquake, but allows Drilbur to work better with Grookey. Rock Slide hits Flying- and Bug-types such as Natu and Larvesta. Finally, its Ground typing makes it a comfortable switch-in to Poison-types like Koffing, eating any of its attacks and forcing it out.

Drilbur makes a fantastic partner for Ferroseed, as they form a potent hazard stacking core with Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Rapid Spin; additionally, Ferroseed checks the Water-types that threaten Drilbur. Fighting-types like Mienfoo and Iron Fist Timburr also greatly appreciate having Drilbur on their side, as it counters Koffing and can reliably set Stealth Rock to cripple Larvesta. Drilbur struggles against Grass-type Pokemon, meaning it has high synergy with Fire- and Poison-types like Larvesta and Koffing, which also appreciate Drilbur removing entry hazards. It also struggles against Water-types, making Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Magnemite and Grookey good choices for teammates.

Entry Hazard Lead.description:
The combination of Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin with Mold Breaker allows Drilbur to set up Stealth Rock against Hattrem, the tier's premier Magic Bounce user. Focus Sash allows Drilbur to take a hit against faster foes and guarantee that Stealth Rock goes up before it faints. Toxic hits bulky Pokemon like Vullaby and Wartortle, as well as Ghost-types like Galarian Corsola that may attempt to spinblock against Drilbur; Galarian Corsola can also set up Stealth Rock itself after switching in.

Drilbur pairs well with dual screens setters such as Electabuzz and Morgrem, as it can lead on hyper offense teams and set up Stealth Rock. Electabuzz, in particular, is able to set up screens and threaten the Vullaby or Wartortle that may want to remove Stealth Rock. Setup sweepers that appreciate support from screens such as Shell Smash Wartortle, Swords Dance Thwackey, and Bulk Up Raboot are good partners. Sticky Web hyper offense teams can also use Drilbur as their main lead. In these teams, both Charjabug and Cutiefly can set up Sticky Web. Moreover, naturally slow but bulky and offensively potent Pokemon like Machoke, Choice Band Piloswine, and Choice Specs Lampent can adequately take advantage of Sticky Web. Overall, hyper offensive teams built around Grassy Terrain can also benefit from Drilbur. Thwackey can set up the Grassy Terrain and then Pokemon such as Bulk Up Raboot, Swirlix, Woobat, and Thwackey itself can take advantage of it with Grassy Seed, boosting their defenses and Acrobatics damage in the case of both Raboot and Thwackey. Nonetheless, Drilbur has some issues in trying to get Stealth Rock up against fast Taunt users such as Electabuzz, Galarian Linoone, and Thwackey, with Electabuzz and Galarian Linoone switching out afterwards and Thwackey threatening it. Wartortle is the perfect counter to Drilbur, as it can deny Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin and break Focus Sash. Piloswine and Thwackey can also limit Drilbur's utility with their respective STAB attacks, though they need first to break Focus Sash. Pokemon such as Electabuzz can switch in against Wartortle and gain momentum. Shell Smash Wartortle and Bulk Up Raboot can also take advantage of Piloswine and Thwackey, respectively, using them as setup fodder.

uu.overview: Excadrill has valuable role compression in UU as an Electric-immune entry hazard remover and potential Stealth Rock setter. It has the typing to check many threatening foes like Nihilego, Togekiss, Jirachi, and Galarian Slowbro. Mold Breaker allows Excadrill to bypass abilities like Levitate from Rotom-W and Magic Bounce from Hatterene to KO them or set Stealth Rock. Excadrill can also utilize a suicide lead set on hyper offense teams to pave the way for dangerous sweepers like Celesteela and Thundurus-T. Excadrill can also be a potent late-game cleaner with a Swords Dance + Rapid Spin set, boosting up to break through walls like Chansey and Amoonguss and clean through weakened teams. However, Excadrill is extremely vulnerable to the tier's Water-, Grass-, and Fighting-type Pokemon like Keldeo, Zarude, and Conkeldurr, all of which can easily take advantage of it due to their higher Speed or access to priority. Excadrill struggles to bypass common threats like Skarmory, Hippowdon, Moltres, and Celesteela. Skarmory and Hippowdon are especially troublesome, as Excadrill struggles to keep entry hazards removed against the most prevalent setters in the tier. Furthermore, Excadrill's defensive stats are lackluster without investment, which hinders its role as a Steel-type when checking threats like Hatterene and Hydreigon.
uu.comments:
Other Options

On Hippowdon teams, Excadrill can use Sand Rush over Mold Breaker to be the fastest threat in the tier, though sand isn't a prominent archetype in UU and Excadrill fails to beat Celesteela and Skarmory anyway. Choice Scarf allows Excadrill to revenge kill threats like Azelf and be the fastest entry hazard remover in the tier, but it is typically undesirable to be locked into any of its moves. Sand Force alongside Choice Band on Sand teams turns Excadrill into a very dangerous wallbreaker, but like Choice Scarf this set struggles because Excadrill hates being locked into any of its moves. Assault Vest lets Excadrill better tank hits from Hydreigon and Galarian Slowbro, though it misses out on the passive recovery Leftovers provides.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Skarmory, Celesteela, and Moltres resist Excadrill's STAB combination, with the former two also being immune to Toxic. However, Moltres dislikes getting hit with Rock Tomb from suicide lead variants. Thundurus-T outspeeds Excadrill and nails it with Focus Blast. Salamence can switch into Excadrill and lower its Attack with Intimidate.

Water-types: Bulky Water-types like Swampert and Slowking can take a hit from Excadrill and retaliate with a super effective attack. Gyarados can use variants without Toxic as setup fodder. Azumarill and Keldeo can revenge kill Excadrill easily.

Grass-types: Tangrowth's massive physical bulk allows it to wall most Excadrill variants, though it has to be careful when taking on Swords Dance sets, as they can break through it with an Iron Head flinch, and Tangrowth needs chip damage to KO Excadrill back. Zarude's natural bulk lets it pivot into Excadrill; it does not fear Toxic because of Jungle Healing and forces it out due to its higher Speed. Dhelmise can block Rapid Spin attempts from Excadrill and threaten it back with heavy damage.

Fighting-types: Cobalion and Keldeo outspeed and force out Excadrill. Conkeldurr has enough physical bulk to take an Earthquake and recover its health with Drain Punch or OHKO Excadrill with Mach Punch if at full health.

Faster Threats: Faster threats like Krookodile, Zygarde-10%, Hydreigon, and Lycanroc-D all outspeed and threaten Excadrill. However, none of these Pokemon want to switch into it, barring Krookodile, which can in a pinch.

Utility.description:
Earthquake and Iron Head provide fantastic coverage for Excadrill, slamming common threats like Galarian Slowbro, Nihilego, and Mamoswine. Rapid Spin lets Excadrill clear entry hazards thanks to matching up well against other entry hazard setters like Nihilego and Chansey. Toxic burdens defensive checks like Tangrowth, Slowking, and Hippowdon, allowing Excadrill or a teammate to get past them in the long-term. However, Toxic is useless against certain answers like Skarmory. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be run for more role compression thanks to Excadrill pressuring entry hazard control like Rotom-W and Hatterene and being able to set up Stealth Rock against Pokemon like Nihilego and Jirachi thanks to its typing. Moreover, finding another Pokemon to run Stealth Rock can strain teambuilding, though Excadrill becomes unable to cripple and wear down threats like Hippowdon. Magnet Rise is an option over Iron Head to completely shut down Hippowdon from setting up Stealth Rock, being immune to Earthquake and punishing it with Toxic, though Excadrill's offensive capabilities become more limited. Mold Breaker bypasses Levitate from Rotom-W, Rotom-H, and Hydreigon, allowing Excadrill to severely damage them with Earthquake while also allowing Excadrill to circumvent Hatterene's Magic Bounce. Maximum Attack investment lets Excadrill threaten Amoonguss and Primarina as much as possible, though maximum investment in Special Defense in an option to better check threats like Hatterene, Rotom-W, and Galarian Slowbro via directly switching in.

Excadrill both removing and setting entry hazards gives it a place on many bulky offense and balance teams. Thundurus-T is a great partner that can remove Flying-types like Skarmory, Celesteela, and Moltres that hinder Excadrill. Grass-types like Tangrowth and Amoonguss can switch into Water- and Grass-types like Azumarill and Zarude for Excadrill. They also scare out Hippowdon. Fighting-type checks like Salamence and Slowking provide great support against threats like Cobalion and Conkeldurr, with Salamence also beating Grass-types like Zarude and Tangrowth as well as helping Excadrill keep entry hazards off the field thanks to it beating entry hazard setters it struggles with like Skarmory and Swampert. Salamence also beats bulky variants of Swords Dance Scizor. Other entry hazard setters like Nihilego and Cobalion can cover setting Stealth Rock for Excadrill, freeing up a moveslot to run Toxic. Fast offensive threats like Zygarde-10%, Azelf, and Salazzle appreciate Excadrill's support and can deal with faster threats like Thundurus-T and Hydreigon. The latter two also check Amoonguss, Tangrowth, and Skarmory.

Suicide Lead.description:
Excadrill is a great suicide lead for hyper offense teams thanks to Mold Breaker, allowing it to set up Stealth Rock against Hatterene and pressure Rotom-W with Earthquake. Rapid Spin supports its team against opposing Stealth Rock setters like Nihilego and Swampert. Excadrill also keeps Sticky Web off the field thanks to its amazing matchup against Ribombee, which normally hinders many hyper offense teams. Rock Tomb heavily damages Thundurus-T and Moltres and slows down faster threats like Zarude for its teammates to set up on. Steel Beam is an option that allows Excadrill to retain momentum after setting up Stealth Rock, preventing Defoggers like Salamence from removing Stealth Rock. A Focus Sash guarantees Excadrill can survive a hit and get up Stealth Rock before fainting.

This Excadrill set fits best on hyper offense teams, allowing teammates to come in and sweep after setting up Stealth Rock. Deadly setup sweepers like Thundurus-T, Gyarados, and Celesteela all appreciate entry hazard support wearing down checks like Chansey, Skarmory, and Nihilego. Thundurus-T takes advantage of the Flying-types Excadrill lets in like Skarmory and Celesteela, while the latter two also appreciate Excadrill removing opposing Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin, preventing chip damage so they can sweep more easily. Rapid Spin support also allows Gyarados to run items like Mystic Water instead of Heavy-Duty Boots. Spikes leads like Scolipede can form an entry hazard stacking core with Excadrill.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance boosts Excadrill's Attack to sky-high levels, letting it overwhelm the sturdiest of physical walls like Tangrowth and Amoonguss with its STAB moves if Stealth Rock is up. In conjunction with Mold Breaker, it can break through Quagsire's Unaware. Rapid Spin lets Excadrill compress entry hazard removal alongside boosting its Speed, making it a dangerous late-game threat, as faster threats like Zygarde-10% can no longer revenge kill it. Rock Slide is an option to slam Moltres, which otherwise counters this set, and hit Thundurus-T and Celesteela, but it only should be used if the team can fit entry hazard removal elsewhere. Leftovers makes Excadrill harder to wear down, further facilitating its sweeping attempts.

Excadrill best fits on offensive teams that give it ample opportunities to wallbreak. Pivot support from Zarude, Thundurus-T, and Slowking can bring Excadrill in safely to set up against their checks like Togekiss and Chansey. Notably, Slowking is a slow pivot, providing Excadrill with a free switch with Teleport. Slowking and Thundurus-T are also great at taking advantage of Celesteela and Skarmory, both of which wall Excadrill. Amoonguss and Tangrowth can provide a key defensive backbone for Excadrill, taking on threats like Conkeldurr, Hippowdon, and Azumarill. Entry hazard support from Nihilego and Swampert is key in helping Excadrill break through physical walls like Tangrowth and Amoonguss. Early-game wallbreakers like Hydreigon and Conkeldurr can weaken walls like Celesteela and Moltres for it to cleanly sweep late-game. Other Steel-types like Celesteela and Jirachi can make up for Excadrill's frailty by checking threats it normally would like Hydreigon and Hatterene.

ubers.overview: Excadrill is a unique utility Pokemon that combines the ability to set Stealth Rock and remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Thanks to Sand Rush, Excadrill outspeeds nearly the entire metagame and can use its powerful Earthquake to also serve as a potent revenge killer or Swords Dance sweeper. However, lead Excadrill can almost never set Stealth Rock again if they are cleared, heavily diminishing its value as opposed to bulky entry hazards setters such as Necrozma-DM that can come in several times in a battle. This means that lead Excadrill is limited to hyper offense teams that can punish Defoggers. When not being used as a lead, its mediocre bulk means that careful switching is needed to get it into battle. Furthermore, the limited duration of sand means that it usually can only stay in for a few turns before needing to switch out. Running Sand Rush Excadrill means that you are also required to use Tyranitar on your team, which constrains teambuilding.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Steel Beam can be used on the lead set to prevent Defoggers that are slower than Excadrill from using Defog while maintaining momentum.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Ghost-types can block Excadrill's Rapid Spin. Lunala can easily remove Excadrill's entry hazards with Defog, but it's vulnerable to Toxic. Giratina goes one step further by curing itself from Toxic poison with Rest. Choice Scarf Calyrex-S can use Trick on Excadrill to let a teammate easily clear its Stealth Rock and can revenge kill it even under sand.

Bulky Grass-types: Tangrowth walls Sand Rush Excadrill, KOes it with Earthquake, and can punish Rapid Spin with Rocky Helmet, though it needs to be wary of Toxic. Zarude can also defeat Excadrill through Bulk Up and Power Whip, and it can cure Toxic poison with Jungle Healing. Physically defensive Ferrothorn can take it out with Body Press.

Bulky Ground-types: Groudon, Landorus-T, and Zygarde-C can all withstand a boosted hit from Excadrill and take it out with a Ground-type move. Defensive Zygarde-C is an especially good check to Sand Rush Excadrill, as it can use Rest to remove Toxic poison.

Skarmory and Corviknight: Skarmory and Corviknight can withstand all of Excadrill's attacks while taking it out with Body Press. Rocky Helmet whittles down Excadrill if it tries to spin, letting Skarmory keep Spikes up against it. Corviknight's Pressure allows it to stall out Stealth Rock's PP with Defog.

Resetting Weather: Kyogre and Groudon can mitigate Excadrill's sweeping capability by changing the weather and can take it out with their STAB moves, though they have to be careful of switching into Earthquake, especially if they're slower.

Taunt: Taunt prevents lead Excadrill from using Stealth Rock, though it can punish Taunt users such as Yveltal and Aerodactyl with Rock Tomb.

Entry Hazard Lead.description:
Stealth Rock provides invaluable chip damage throughout a game, while Rapid Spin allows Excadrill to clear entry hazards against other leads, improving matchups against other hyper offense leads such as Aerodactyl, Mew, and Shuckle. Keep in mind that Slurpuff can bounce back Stealth Rock with Magic Coat and prevent Excadrill from spinning with Yawn, Froslass can block Rapid Spin and create a guessing game with Taunt while always being able to set a layer of Spikes, and Cloyster can clear Excadrill's hazards while easily taking it out with Icicle Spear after a Shell Smash. The Speed boost also allows Excadrill to threaten Eternatus with Earthquake if it uses Toxic Spikes on the first turn while also dissuading fast threats such as Calyrex-S from coming in. Be careful about spinning on Ferrothorn and Rocky Helmet Necrozma-DM, as hazards are not cleared if Excadrill faints from recoil. Rock Tomb 2HKOes Ho-Oh, preventing it from using Defog, while also deterring sweepers from setting up in front of Excadrill. Furthermore, the Speed drop allows a teammate to outspeed the foe, deterring setup such as Geomancy from Xerneas. Earthquake allows Excadrill to dent other leads such as Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and Ferrothorn while preventing it from being used as setup fodder by Substitute users such as Zekrom and Zygarde-C, whereas Toxic allows Excadrill to pressure bulky Pokemon such as Yveltal with passive damage. Focus Sash guarantees it can take a hit to set Stealth Rock, and Mold Breaker allows Excadrill to ignore the rare Magic Bounce and and hit Giratina-O through Levitate. A Jolly nature is used to outspeed maximum Speed Necrozma-DM.

Excadrill fits on hyper offensive teams that appreciate its ability to reliably set Stealth Rock while keeping them off your side. Powerful sweepers such as Xerneas, Calyrex-S, Groudon and Zekrom that can punish Defoggers and appreciate walls being chipped are therefore a perfect match. It struggles to spin against Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S, so Yveltal is recommended to both threaten them and prevent Defog with Taunt. Excadrill also often fails to prevent Stealth Rock from Rocky Helmet Necrozma-DM, which can be pressured with Pokemon such as Kyogre, Groudon, and Calyrex-S.

Sand Rush.description:
Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed most of the metagame under sand. Rock Slide is vital coverage for Flying-types such as Yveltal and Ho-Oh, while Rapid Spin allows Excadrill to remove entry hazards in a pinch. The Speed boost can also be useful to continue attacking after sand ends. Swords Dance turns Excadrill into a powerful sweeper, though it is limited by sand turns. Alternatively, Toxic allows Excadrill to perform a more support-oriented revenge killing role, letting it cripple Pokemon such as Yveltal, Zygarde-C, Landorus-T, and Lugia. Life Orb allows Excadrill to consistently OHKO threats such as physically defensive Necrozma-DM and specially defensive Yveltal and 2HKO untransformed or offensive Zygarde-C at +2, as well as having a good chance at OHKOing Eternatus and Ho-Oh with slight chip damage without any boosts. On the other hand, Leftovers allows it to play a more slower-paced game and avoid being stalled into defeating itself with recoil by foes such as Tangrowth and Zygarde-C. Though a Jolly nature is preferred to outspeed maximum Speed Necrozma-DM outside sand as well as Adamant Sand Rush Excadrill under sand, Adamant can be used for extra power.

Tyranitar is a mandatory teammate to provide Sand Stream support. It also sets Stealth Rock to help Excadrill pick up KOs and checks both Calyrex-S and Lunala, which can revenge kill and wall Excadrill, respectively. As Excadrill is prone to having its weather replaced by Groudon and Kyogre, Pokemon that can deal with them such as Lunala and Eternatus, respectively, are helpful partners. Pokemon that appreciate Steel-types and Eternatus removed such as Xerneas and Kyogre can benefit from its support. Excadrill can also lure certain walls such as Landorus-T into being poisoned, which helps other Pokemon such as Marshadow KO them.

ou.overview: Excadrill is a strong sand sweeper thanks to its incredible ability in Sand Rush that allows it to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame under sand, great Ground / Steel typing that aids it offensively and defensively, and access to Swords Dance and Rapid Spin, with the latter helping Excadrill sweep when sand is not set up. Rock Slide also gives Excadrill incredible coverage, enabling it to hit checks like Zapdos and Pelipper. However, as Pokemon like Slowbro and Buzzwole possess the physical bulk to take its moves even after a Swords Dance and threaten it back with their STAB moves, while Pokemon like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Rotom-W can stonewall Excadrill due to their defensive typings. Moreover, even though Excadrill possesses an incredible defensive typing, its lackluster bulk hampers it severely, leaving it weak to a wide variety of Pokemon.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Excadrill can opt for a Choice Band with Earthquake, Iron Head, Rock Slide, and Rapid Spin, which lets it 2HKO Zapdos outright and 2HKO Ferrothorn and Slowbro after slight chip damage; however, it doesn't appreciate being Choice-locked. Excadrill can also function as a suicide lead, holding a Focus Sash with a moveset of Earthquake, Rapid Spin, Steel Beam, and Stealth Rock, though Landorus-T and Mew typically function better as suicide leads. Excadrill can use Mold Breaker to ignore Levitate on Rotom-W, Unaware on Quagsire, and Multiscale on Dragonite, though it is very niche otherwise. This set is usually specially defensive to check Fairy-types like Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele more effectively, but it is not recommended due to its severe lack of longevity.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Slowbro can tank hits from Excadrill even after a Swords Dance and can threaten it with Scald or Body Press. Rotom-W is immune to Earthquake, resists Iron Head, and doesn't mind taking Rock Slide while threatening to OHKO Excadrill with Hydro Pump.

Bulky Ground-types: Landorus-T takes hits from Excadrill reasonably well thanks to Intimidate, Hippowdon's great natural bulk lets it eat hits from Excadrill, and both of them can threaten it with Earthquake in retaliation.

Faster Threats: Threats like Dragapult, Blacephalon, Garchomp, and Urshifu-R all outspeed Excadrill outside of sand and can OHKO it.

Priority Moves: Choice Band Urshifu-R can OHKO Excadrill with Aqua Jet after slight chip damage, Rillaboom can OHKO it with Grassy Glide either at +2 or with a Choice Band, and Weavile can take out Excadrill with Ice Shard if it is at very low HP.

Non-Ground-weak Steel-types: Corviknight and Skarmory are immune to Earthquake and don't take much damage from Rock Slide. In addition, they can also threaten Excadrill with Body Press. Ferrothorn can use Leech Seed on Excadrill and use attacking moves like Power Whip and Body Press to deal good damage, though it struggles to switch in on +2 Excadrill. Air Balloon Heatran is immune to Earthquake, takes little damage from Excadrill's other moves, and can OHKO it with Magma Storm.

Sand Sweeper.description:
Set Description

Thanks to its high Attack stat further bolstered by Swords Dance, solid offensive typing, and access to Sand Rush, Excadrill functions as an extremely dangerous sand sweeper. Swords Dance enables Excadrill to sweep entire teams, allowing it to OHKO Dragapult, Melmetal, and Urshifu-R at +2 with Earthquake. Iron Head, on top of being a STAB move, OHKOes Weavile and Tapu Lele while 2HKOing Clefable, whereas Rock Slide hits Zapdos and Pelipper while OHKOing Volcarona. Rapid Spin lets Excadrill remove entry hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes, which is particularly notable due to the lack of spinblockers that can stomach Earthquake in the tier, its ability to not activate Defiant from Defog punishers such as Galarian Zapdos and Bisharp, and the moveset flexibility it provides to teammates like Zapdos and Tornadus-T. Rapid Spin also boosts its Speed, letting it sweep without sand and outspeed Zeraora and Dragapult at +1 in conjunction with a Jolly nature. Leftovers heals off chip damage from hazards, allowing Excadrill to take hits from the likes of Dragapult and Weavile in a pinch while checking Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Zapdos without Heat Wave more effectively, whereas Air Balloon lets it set up on Ground-types like specially defensive Garchomp, opposing Excadrill, and Hippowdon in addition to making it immune to Spikes.

Team Options

Excadrill is mainly used on sand teams due to its ability Sand Rush, letting it sweep much more easily and provide valuable speed control for sand teams. Tyranitar is an exemplary teammate for Excadrill, as it reliably sets up sand with Sand Stream and can support it in a variety of ways depending on its set; Choice Band variants help pressure stall teams that depend on Corviknight or Skarmory to stave off Excadrill while pressuring shared checks like Buzzwole against other structures, while specially defensive sets help wear down checks like Corviknight, Skarmory, Rotom-W, and Buzzwole with Stealth Rock and status from Thunder Wave or Toxic. Alternatively, Hippowdon is another solid sand setter, allowing Excadrill to fit on bulkier archetypes due to it being a bulky Ground-type with reliable recovery and access to Stealth Rock. Ferrothorn pairs extremely well with Excadrill, as it is a Steel-type that can check threats like Weavile and Tapu Lele, compensating for Excadrill's inability to reliably check those threats due to its lack of bulk. Ferrothorn also provides entry hazard support with Stealth Rock or Spikes, and it can remove items from the likes of Corviknight, Skarmory, and Buzzwole with Knock Off while being one of the better checks in the tier to Rotom-W. Clefable's Magic Guard ability makes it immune to sand chip damage and a good switch-in to Scald users like Slowbro and Gastrodon while also being another option to set Stealth Rock; in return, Excadrill threatens checks to Clefable like Galarian Slowking and Melmetal. Zapdos threatens checks like Slowbro, Buzzwole, Corviknight, and Skarmory for Excadrill, takes hits from Grass-types like Kartana and Rillaboom and can wear down bulky Ground-types that can trade with Excadrill in a pinch, such as Landorus-T, Hippowdon, and Garchomp; in exchange, Excadrill threatens Weavile and Tapu Lele, and its Rapid Spin allows Zapdos to run moves like Heat Wave and Toxic instead of Defog. Tornadus-T aids Excadrill by removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from checks like Zapdos, Rotom-W, and Landorus-T, while Excadrill can use Rapid Spin to remove Stealth Rock that Tornadus-T despises without Heavy-Duty Boots, letting it run Assault Vest or Nasty Plot sets. Tapu Lele threatens Rotom-W and Buzzwole, prevents Excadrill from being hit by Weavile's Ice Shard and Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet, offers Future Sight support, and is a solid form of speed control outside of sand if running a Choice Scarf set. In return, Excadrill threatens checks to Tapu Lele such as Heatran and Galarian Slowking. Urshifu-R threatens Landorus-T and Ferrothorn as well as being able to revenge kill Blaziken with Aqua Jet, which can easily tear through sand teams, while Excadrill can threaten Urshifu-R's checks like Clefable and Toxapex. Moreover, they can wear down Slowbro, Corviknight, and Skarmory together.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Steelium Z is a niche option that can push more damage onto Pokemon like Tapu Fini, Gliscor, physically defensive Tangrowth, and Landorus-T, but these targets can be pressured by Normalium Z anyway while also causing headaches for Zapdos and Rotom-W. Air Balloon reverses the matchup against Ground-types such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Gliscor. However, these matchups aren't worth being stonewalled by Tangrowth, Slowbro, and Zapdos. A specially defensive set can be used to check a myriad of Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele while providing Rapid Spin, but it is easy to wear down and overwhelm. On the Stealth Rock Lead set, Steel Beam may seem like a nice option over Rock Tomb to perform more as a suicide lead, but due to it needing Excadrill to be at a lower HP to effectively work, it is rather undesirable, and it still struggles to keep Stealth Rock up versus Corviknight. Toxic is another option that can cripple bulky switch-ins like Tangrowth and Zapdos, but both it and Steel Beam come at the cost of losing Rock Tomb, which opens up a lot of faster Pokemon to be less threatened by Excadrill.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Corviknight, Zapdos, and Mega Charizard Y are immune to Excadrill's Earthquake and take its Iron Head decently well, while they can all retaliate with super effective coverage. Mega Charizard Y can also remove potential sand, causing Excadrill to be slower than it. However, the former must be wary of Substitute variants if it lacks Body Press, and the latter two are shattered by +2 Normalium Z.

Faster Pokemon: When unboosted by sand or Rapid Spin, Excadrill sits are at a poor Speed tier. As a result, faster Pokemon like Garchomp, Ash-Greninja, and Mega Lopunny are capable of revenge killing it. Ash-Greninja in particular has a powerful Water Shuriken to dispatch of Excadrill even when its boosted. However, none of these Pokemon can switch into Excadrill directly and cannot beat it if its Speed is boosted.

Grass-types: Physically defensive Tangrowth is incredibly difficult for Excadrill to break if it has used its Z-Move, and Tangrowth can wear Excadrill down with Rocky Helmet and Giga Drain or neutralize it with Sleep Powder. However, Tangrowth can be crippled by Toxic long-term. Rillaboom, while unable to switch in directly, deals heavy damage to Excadrill with a priority Grassy Glide. Even if Rillaboom is taken out, Excadrill may have to contend with Grassy Terrain weakening its Earthquake.

Exploiting Focus Sash: Fake Out users like Mega Medicham and Mega Lopunny are able to break Excadrill's Focus Sash without Excadrill being able to do anything and can immediately OHKO it in the following turn. Water Shuriken from Greninja can be troublesome, as it lets Greninja transform into Ash-Greninja and it denies Stealth Rock, provided it gets enough hits. On a similar note, Weavile's Triple Axel bypasses Focus Sash and KOes Excadrill before it can do anything.

Sand Rush Sweeper.description:
Excadrill is a cornerstone on sand teams, serving as a capable wallbreaker and sweeper for the archetype thanks to its high Attack, access to Swords Dance, and doubled Speed under sand. Additionally, its solid bulk and fantastic defensive typing give it many opportunities to set up against the likes of Clefable, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Koko. Swords Dance alongside a Z-Move lets Excadrill clean up weakened defensive Pokemon like Slowbro, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Fini. Giga Impact gives it access to Breakneck Blitz, allowing Excadrill to break through common Pokemon like Zapdos as well as chipped Slowbro and Tangrowth after a boost. Rapid Spin can be used if Excadrill's team can't fit Defog elsewhere and gives Excadrill the ability to limit Stealth Rock Clefable, patch up its Speed without the need for sand, and remove entry hazards for Pokemon weak to them like Mega Charizard Y. Toxic can be used in the fourth slot to wear down Slowbro, Tangrowth, Landorus-T, and Zapdos, especially alongside sand damage. Substitute is an option to use non-Body Press Corviknight as setup fodder. Leftovers allows for Excadrill to take advantage of its solid defensive typing, giving it easier setup on Pokemon like Clefable and Tapu Koko. However, forgoing Normalium Z can be detrimental against teams carrying Slowbro, Zapdos, and Tangrowth. Jolly is the preferred nature to Speed tie with opposing Excadrill, but if adequate Excadrill counterplay is on your team, Adamant can be used for its higher power, which is notable for dispatching Slowbro and Tangrowth a bit easier.

Excadrill necessitates sand to function properly, so either Tyranitar or Mega Tyranitar are mandatory alongside it. Mega Tyranitar is also a great Stealth Rock setter, chipping Excadrill's answers into the range of its attacks. Both Tyranitar formes are also notable for being able to beat Zapdos one-on-one for Excadrill and having Pursuit to cripple Mega Latias. Corviknight effortlessly walls Excadrill, so teammates that can deal with it, such as Zapdos and Magnezone, make excellent teammates. Both are also notable for tearing open physically defensive Tangrowth, which would otherwise halt Excadrill's sweep. Swords Dance and Choice Band Kartana sets are also capable of forcing damage onto Corviknight and Zapdos, causing them to falter at checking Excadrill. Faster Pokemon like Ash-Greninja and Mega Lopunny can exploit Excadrill's mediocre Speed outside of sand, with Ash-Greninja revenge killing it even under sand with Water Shuriken, so partners such as Toxapex, Slowbro, and Corviknight are needed to help remedy this issue. Ferrothorn and Ash-Greninja are notable partners for their ability to set Spikes, allowing Excadrill to pressure Pokemon that would otherwise check it like Tangrowth. Calm Mind Clefable and Reuniclus are solid partners for Excadrill, as they appreciate Excadrill dismantling Steel-types that can halt their sweep. They also provide a solid defensive backbone which Excadrill can fall back on once sand has run out.

Stealth Rock Lead.description:
Lead Excadrill serves as an important member on hyper offense teams to set up Stealth Rock, as well as keep opposing entry hazards off the field for Pokemon like Volcarona and Gyarados. Adding onto the fact that there are not many Electric-type immunities featured on hyper offense, Excadrill's inclusion is all the more important. However, even with this advantage, it still finds itself outclassed by Mew and Landorus-T due to it being unable to prevent Pokemon like Corviknight and Tapu Fini from using Defog and it not having a good defensive typing like the other two do. Setting up Stealth Rock is Excadrill's main role, and when paired with Mold Breaker, it can even set up Stealth Rock against Magic Bounce users like Mega Diancie and Mega Sableye. Mold Breaker also lets Excadrill's Earthquake hit Levitate users like Hydreigon, Rotom-W, and Mega Latias, letting Excadrill not be complete setup fodder against them. Rapid Spin defines Excadrill's niche over other entry hazard leads like Landorus-T and Mew, letting it keep hazards off the field before it gets KOed. Rock Tomb can slow down faster Stealth Rock users like Garchomp and Landorus-T so that Excadrill can use Rapid Spin before they KO it. It can also slow down setup Pokemon that might try to take advantage of Excadrill like Mega Gyarados and Thundurus-T. Focus Sash is chosen as the item so that Excadrill is usually able to get up Stealth Rock before getting KOed.

Lead Excadrill exclusively fits on hyper offense teams and, as such, has teammates that are commonly found there. Pokemon that appreciate Excadrill's ability to keep entry hazards off the field such as Gyarados and non-Heavy-Duty Boots variants of Volcarona, Weavile, and Thundurus-T serve as great teammates to pair with it. Excadrill can also function on Sticky Web teams to provide Stealth Rock when the Sticky Web setter is Ribombee while also giving the team a form of entry hazard removal, which Shuckle cannot do. Additionally, due to the nature of hyper offense being rather slow at first, Tapu Koko is especially threatening to the archetype, making Excadrill an important teammate because it resists or is immune to both of Tapu Koko's STAB moves. Pokemon like Weavile and Greninja who have multi-hit moves are also invited in by Excadrill, so it appreciates partners like Mega Gyarados, Mega Scizor, and Kommo-o that can pivot into these Pokemon.

monotype.overview:
Ground

Sand Rush alongside its phenomenal Attack stat allows Excadrill to become a potent revenge killer for Ground teams, taking on threats such as Zarude, Keldeo, Barraskewda, and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu under sand. Excadrill's decent natural bulk allows it to live attacks such as unboosted Galarian Moltres's Fiery Wrath, Choice Specs Dragapult's Shadow Ball, and Hydreigon's Flamethrower. Excadrill's part-Steel typing allows it to take neutral damage from Ice- and Grass-type attacks such as Weavile's Ice Shard and Tapu Koko's Grass Knot and resist Dragon- and Psychic-type attacks such as Latias's Draco Meteor and Psychic. It also has Rapid Spin, which allows Excadrill to clear entry hazards off the field; this gives Ground teams their only and reliable form of entry hazard removal. However, Excadrill relies on sand to outpace most offensive threats such as Choice Specs Zapdos, Victini, Tapu Lele, Blacephalon, and Nidoking, leaving it easily revenge killed outside of sand.

Steel

Excadrill is an effective revenge killer and late-game cleaner for Steel teams, making it extremely valuable in the Electric, Poison, Psychic, and Fire matchups. Its ability, Mold Breaker, is extremely useful, as it allows Excadrill to spam Earthquake without being bothered by Levitate users like Rotom-W and Galarian Weezing. However, Excadrill is slower than most Choice Scarf users and gets forced out by those that carry super effective coverage such as Blacephalon, Tapu Lele, and Galarian Darmanitan. Furthermore, Excadrill struggles to deal with physical walls such as Slowbro and Galarian Corsola, which means that it needs support from teammates like Aegislash and Bisharp to break down certain defensive cores.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Swords Dance + Rapid Spin can be used on both Sand Rush and Mold Breaker Excadrill. It allows Excadrill to act as a sweeper outside of sand thanks to Rapid Spin allowing it to outspeed Pokemon such as Kyurem. Mold Breaker can be used to target Levitate users such as Rotom-W, Hydreigon, and Latios with Earthquake. A Choice Scarf set can be used on sand less Ground teams to allow Excadrill to act as a revenge killer without the boost from sand or Rapid Spin and take on threats such as Choice Specs Tapu Lele. Shadow Claw can be used to take on Psychic teams, allowing Excadrill to 2HKO Pokemon such as physically defensive Bronzong.

Steel

An Occa Berry or Chople Berry may be used over Leftovers on the Swords Dance set to survive a Fire- or Fighting-type move, allowing Excadrill to lure in and KO Pokemon like Zapdos, Blacephalon, Zeraora, and Thundurus-T, but the lack of Leftovers recovery hurts Excadrill's longevity in other matchups. Shed Shell may also be used over Leftovers to prevent Excadrill from getting trapped by Magnet Rise Air Balloon Magnezone, but it is useless in other matchups. Using these items over Leftovers also allows Excadrill to bluff a Choice Scarf set, which can be favorable in Psychic and Electric matchups, as its Choice Scarf set threatens to outspeed and KO Victini and Zeraora.

Checks and Counters

Ground

Ground-immune and -resistant Pokemon: Pokemon that are immune to or resist Earthquake present a problem to Excadrill. However, Pokemon like Landorus-T, Galarian Moltres, and Zarude have to watch out for its other STAB and coverage moves in Iron Head, Rock Slide, and X-Scissor, respectively. The only Pokemon that truly wall all of Excadrill's coverage are Celesteela, Corviknight, and Skarmory; the former can wall its attacks and wear it down with Leech Seed + Protect, and the latter two can threaten it with Body Press in return.

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive walls such as Rotom-W, Porygon2, Galarian Corsola, and Hippowdon can easily take all of Excadrill's attacks and either cripple it with status or threaten it with their STAB attacks.

Revenge Killers: Revenge killers such as Spectrier, Garchomp, Cinderace, and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu outspeed and revenge kill Excadrill outside of sand. Dragon Dance Dragapult also only needs one Dragon Dance to outpace Excadrill in sand, and Choice Scarf Weavile outspeeds Adamant Excadrill in sand.

Status: Being burnt severely hinders Excadrill's performance as a wallbreaker, as it can no longer break past defensive Pokemon such as Mandibuzz and Amoonguss or OHKO offensive threats such as Choice Specs Zapdos, even after Stealth Rock. Whimsicott and Zapdos can paralyze Excadrill with Stun Spore and Static respectively, preventing it from outspeeding threats such as Zarude and Zeraora.

Steel

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive Pokemon such as Slowbro, Celesteela, and Hippowdon take minimal damage from Excadrill's attacks and threaten it with their own super effective attacks.

Choice Scarf Users: Faster Choice Scarf users such as Victini, Zarude, and Landorus-T outspeed Excadrill and can OHKO it.

Magnezone: Excadrill has to be wary of getting trapped and KOed by Magnezone in Electric matchups as Excadrill may be forced to lock into Rock Slide to KO Zapdos. Magnezone can even hold an Air Balloon to render Excadrill's Earthquake ineffective. However, Magnezone is less threatening if Excadrill is using a Swords Dance set.

Status: Burn from Galarian Corsola and Scald users like Slowbro severely reduces Excadrill's offensive potential.

Sand Rush (Ground).description:
Earthquake allows Excadrill to take on most Pokemon that are weak or not resistant to Ground-type attacks such as Zeraora, Victini, Ferrothorn, Garchomp, Urshifu-R, and Dragapult. Iron Head targets Ice- and Fairy-types such as Avalugg, Alolan Ninetales, Tapu Bulu, and Tapu Lele. X-Scissor is used to take on Zarude and Celebi while also dealing with other Dark- and Psychic-types such as Hydreigon and Slowbro. Rock Slide targets Flying-types such as Zapdos, Galarian Moltres, and Mantine. Sand Rush allows Excadrill to outspeed threats such as Blacephalon, Zeraora, Zarude, and Choice Specs Dragapult under sand. Maximum Speed investment allows Excadrill to outspeed threats such as Tapu Bulu, Adamant Diggersby, and Choice Specs Pelipper. An Adamant nature paired with a Choice Band allows Excadrill to OHKO threats such as Keldeo after Stealth Rock and 2HKO Slowbro with X-Scissor. A Jolly nature can be used to outspeed threats such as +1 Adamant Dragapult and Choice Scarf Weavile in sand. Excadrill should be safely brought in to take advantage of the sand with methods such as Eject Button Hippowdon or by bringing it on resisted attacks such as Latias's Draco Meteor.

All of Excadrill's teammates appreciate its ability to take on Ice-, Psychic-, and Fairy-types, clear entry hazards with Rapid Spin, and act as a revenge killer in sand against threats such as Barraskewda, Choice Specs Dragapult, and Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu. Hippowdon is a mandatory partner for Excadrill, as it sets sand and Stealth Rock, as well as being able to bring in Excadrill safely with Eject Button. Hippowdon can also take on physical threats such as Dragon Dance Dragapult, Zeraora, and Bisharp for Excadrill. Gastrodon and Seismitoad offer Excadrill an immunity to Water-type attacks such as Mantine's Scald and Barraskewda's Waterfall. Gastrodon offers a more defensive presence thanks to Recover, while Seismitoad checks Azumarill, which would otherwise beat Excadrill. Swords Dance Garchomp wears down shared checks like Celesteela with Fire Fang, takes on Mantine with Stone Edge, and can become dangerous setup sweeper with Scale Shot, which makes handling Pokemon like Spectrier much easier. Landorus-T provides a Ground immunity, allowing it to switch into Hippowdon's Earthquake; it is also a great revenge killer that can take on weakened threats such as Zeraora, Spectrier, and Urshifu-R with its Choice Scarf set. Gravity Landorus-T can threaten Pokemon such as Skarmory, Celesteela, and Corviknight for Excadrill, as well as taking on Steel teams in their entirety if it carries Bulk Up and Substitute. Nidoking can beat Steel-types such as Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Celesteela with Earth Power + Flamethrower or Flying-types such as Mantine, Pelipper, Corviknight, and Dragonite with Thunderbolt + Ice Beam. Mamoswine is a great late-game cleaner that can pick off weakened threats such as Garchomp, Dragapult, and Hydreigon with Ice Shard while also being able to remove items such as Slowking's Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off.

Choice Scarf (Steel).description:
Earthquake deals with Fire- and Steel-types, allowing Excadrill to remove threats such as Victini and Heatran. Rock Slide allows Excadrill to threaten Flying-types such as Zapdos and Crobat that switch into Earthquake. Rapid Spin allows Excadrill to remove only the opponent's entry hazards, which synergizes with Steel's tendency to stack entry hazards. Iron Head deals with Fairy- and Ice-types such as Tapu Bulu and Kyurem. Toxic may be used to punish defensive Pokemon like Mew and Slowbro. A Choice Scarf allows Excadrill to outspeed a majority of the metagame and remove threats like Zeraora, Dragapult, and Victini.

Ferrothorn is a good teammate, as it covers Excadrill's weaknesses to Ground and Water by checking Hippowdon and Kingdra and it sets up entry hazards to chip foes. Aegislash provides a Fighting immunity and can punish physically defensive walls such as Slowbro and Mantine with Toxic. Heatran offers a Fire immunity and can trap and remove bulky walls such as Mew and Porygon2 that Excadrill struggles with. Celesteela provides a Ground immunity and threatens Grass- and Steel-types such as Amoonguss and Ferrothorn. Alternatively, Corviknight or Skarmory could be considered as the Ground-immune partner, as they both threaten Fighting-types such as Galarian Zapdos and Kommo-o. Melmetal heavily damages bulky walls such as Amoonguss and Toxapex, which allows Excadrill to clean Psychic and Poison teams late-game. Jirachi threatens physical walls such as Slowbro, Amoonguss, and Celesteela for Excadrill and can wear down Poison and Water teams with its Choice Specs set. Bisharp deals with faster, frailer Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Victini and Blacephalon with Sucker Punch and can break down walls such as Slowbro and Porygon2 with its Swords Dance set.

Swords Dance (Steel).description:
With Swords Dance, Excadrill becomes an effective late-game sweeper for Steel teams, allowing it to break through walls such as Toxapex, Slowbro, and Zapdos, which improves the matchup of Steel teams against Poison, Psychic, and Electric teams. Earthquake deals with Poison- and Steel-types, allowing Excadrill to OHKO bulky Pokemon such as Toxapex and Melmetal after a Swords Dance. Rock Slide allows Excadrill to OHKO threats such as Thundurus-T, Zapdos, and Crobat after a Swords Dance. Iron Head may be considered instead, as it allows Excadrill to clean late-game in the Fairy and Dragon matchup and hit common switch-ins such as Landorus-T harder. Rock Blast can be considered to break the Substitutes of Kyurem and Galarian Moltres, but it is less consistent than Rock Slide. Rapid Spin allows Excadrill to boost its Speed, pick off weakened Pokemon, and take advantage of forced switches, allowing it to outspeed would-be answers such as Victini, Zeraora, and Gengar. Leftovers prolongs Excadrill's longevity, allowing it to set up and threaten opposing teams multiple times in a match.

Ferrothorn checks threats such as Tapu Fini and Hippowdon for Excadrill and sets up entry hazards to chip the opposing team. Specially defensive Aegislash can tank weak special attacks from physically defensive walls such as Slowbro and Porygon2 and punish them with Toxic while also providing a Fighting immunity. Heatran provides a switch-in to Fire-type attacks and can utilize a Choice Scarf set to make up for Excadrill's reduced Speed, allowing it to outspeed and KO threats such as Choice Scarf Tapu Bulu and Victini. Celesteela, Corviknight, and Skarmory provide a Ground immunity and utility in the form of Leech Seed, pivoting, and entry hazards, respectively. Choice Scarf Magnezone can trap and KO opposing Steel-types such as Celesteela, Corviknight, and Skarmory and Water-types such as Urshifu-R and Keldeo, all of which Excadrill struggles with.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Offensive Support.description:
• With Mold Breaker and an excellent typing, Excadrill has the tools to deal with major threats, such as Mimikyu and Rotom-W.

  • Rock Tomb is essential for providing Speed control.

  • If using Focus Sash, Excadrill is a good choice for setting up Stealth Rock.

  • Horn Drill gives Excadrill a 30% chance to bust through defensive Pokemon that would otherwise wall it, such as Celesteela.

  • Swords Dance lets Excadrill take advantage of more passive threats, such as Cresselia. If using Assault Vest, Brick Break is a reasonable replacement while Dynamaxed thanks to Max Knuckle, and has the bonus of breaking Reflect and Light Screen otherwise.

Items

  • Focus Sash lets Excadrill focus on supporting the team to its fullest extent, without worrying about getting OHKOed.

  • Assault Vest is the item of choice if Excadrill plans on Dynamaxing, making it a surprisingly bulky Pokemon. It also lets Excadrill handle Nihilego far better than it would otherwise.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: This maximizes Excadrill's Speed and power, letting it outspeed Pokemon in a similar speed bracket such as Dragonite and Gyarados.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Adamant: While this spread no longer allows Excadrill to outspeed Dragonite and Gyarados consistently, it does allow Excadrill to KO Dynamax Nihilego with Rock Tomb + Earthquake under Grassy Terrain.

  • 244 HP / 116 Atk / 148 Spe with Adamant: This spread is a good fit for bulkier Assault Vest sets, allowing Excadrill to OHKO Dynamax Naganadel with Max Quake, while still outspeeding them after one use of Rock Tomb.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Excadrill's decent Speed tier and access to Mold Breaker make it a good choice for Choice Scarf revenge killing, outspeeding major threats such as Mimikyu, Pheromosa, and Dragapult.

  • Horn Drill is Excadrill's best hope at breaking past defensive Pokemon such as Cresselia and Tapu Fini, with a 30% chance of OHKOing them as long as they aren't Dynamaxed.

  • Rock Slide is Excadrill's most powerful option for coverage against Flying-types. Rock Tomb is a weaker alternative that does provide Speed control in a pinch.

Sand Sweeper.description:
• When it comes to Sand Stream sweeping, no Pokemon does the job better than Excadrill, who fully takes advantage of Dynamax to both set up the sand, and Max Moves to increase its bulk.

  • Rock Slide's chance to flinch makes it a good choice for a Rock-type attack outside of Dynamax, but Rock Blast deserves special mention for blasting through Disguise and Focus Sash.

  • Swords Dance makes Excadrill less reliant on Dynamax to sweep, and lets Excadrill deal massive damage to defensive Pokemon such as Tapu Fini and Cresselia.

  • Brick Break allows Excadrill to boost its Attack while Dynamaxed via Max Knuckle, in addition to breaking Reflect and Light Screen outside of it.

  • While Excadrill is fully capable of setting up sand on its own thanks to Dynamax, consider pairing Excadrill with Hippowdon or Tyranitar to ease reliance on Max Rockfall in certain match-ups.

Items

  • Weakness Policy takes full advantage of Excadrill's Dynamax capabilities, especially since its two Max Move STABs boost its defensive stats.

  • Focus Sash gels well with setting up Swords Dance at unexpected times, opening up new late-game sweeping opportunities.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: This EV spread makes Excadrill as fast as possible, outspeeding key threats under Sandstorm such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Cinderace.

  • 196 Atk / 140 SpD / 172 Spe with Jolly: This EV spread gives Excadrill enough Special Defense to survive Choice Specs Rotom-W's Hydro Pump while Dynamaxed, while still outspeeding up to Choice Scarf Naganadel under Sandstorm.

Excadrill is one of the most threatening sweepers in STABmons, pressuring many defensive cores and outpacing offensive Pokemon like Zeraora, Cinderace, and Terrakion when sand is active. Earthquake and Thousand Waves are usually interchangeable, with Earthquake having more power but Thousand Waves trapping opponents and generating momentum. Additionally, Thousand Waves is not weakened by Grassy Terrain from Rillaboom. Sunsteel Strike lets Excadrill beat Fairy-types and wear down Ground-resistant Pokemon, and Rapid Spin clears entry hazards. Swords Dance makes Excadrill a powerful sweeper in sand, while Shore Up allows Excadrill to take on a more supportive role with Rapid Spin. A Jolly nature lets Excadrill revenge kill Pokemon like Nidoking and Mamoswine outside of sand, but an Adamant Nature provides Excadrill with a ton of power to let it break walls like Buzzwole after just a bit of prior damage. Leftovers is the preferred item to provide passive recovery and offset chip damage from stray hits and Rocky Helmet. Alternatively, Metal Coat makes Sunsteel Strike even more threatening against walls after chip damage. Tyranitar or Hippowdon are mandatory teammates to provide sand. Excadrill requires partners like Rotom-W, Thundurus-T, and Crawdaunt that can deal with both bulky Water- and Ground-types like Slowbro and Hippowdon and its biggest checks, Corviknight, Celesteela, and Skarmory. Dracozolt helps Excadrill overwhelm Ground-types while beating Steel- and Flying-types, making it a staple on sand teams. Defensive Water-types like Toxapex and Slowbro can also help as pivots into Ground- and Flying-types while generating momentum for Excadrill with Flip Turn and Teleport, respectively.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

A dedicated lead set with Stealth Rock, Rock Tomb, Rapid Spin, and Steel Beam is possible; however, it still struggles to keep Stealth Rock up against Pokemon such as Corviknight and Giratina. High Horsepower is an option if Rillaboom is run on the same team to prevent reduced Earthquake damage.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Skarmory and Corviknight are the hardest counters to Excadrill, as they are immune to Toxic, resist its STAB moves, can threaten it with Body Press, and remove its Stealth Rock with Defog. Physically defensive Yveltal and Mandibuzz can also beat Excadrill thanks to Foul Play, and Landorus-T is neutral to Rock Slide and weakens Excadrill's attacks with Intimidate. However, they fear Toxic wearing them down.

Weather Control: Rayquaza and Groudon can nullify sand, then outspeed and easily OHKO Excadrill.

Physically bulky Pokemon: Pokemon with great physical bulk like Tangrowth, Buzzwole, and Slowking can easily take a boosted hit from Excadrill. The former can then retaliate with Earthquake, Focus Blast, or cripple it with Stun Spore, while the latter two can hit it super effectively with their STAB attacks. Pyukumuku and Quagsire can ignore all boosts Excadrill acquires and heal off all damage done. However, all of these Pokemon can get worn down by Toxic and sand damage.

Sand Rush (Defense, Special Defense, Spe.description:
Sand Rush Excadrill is a dangerous sweeper under sand thanks to its high Attack and offensive typing. Earthquake is its main attack, OHKOing numerous offensive Pokemon such as Zeraora and Heatran. Rock Slide hits Pokemon that are immune to Ground, notably Ho-Oh and Yveltal. Swords Dance further boosts Excadrill's Attack, allowing it to break through sturdy physical walls such as Magic Guard Clefable and Ferrothorn. Iron Head is its secondary STAB option that hits some Pokemon like Kyurem and Landorus-T harder, and its flinch chance can be useful to take down foes Excadrill struggles with otherwise, like Landorus-T, Unaware Clefable, and Tangrowth. Rapid Spin instead gives it some utility by removing entry hazards while also giving it the potential to sweep outside of sand. Leftovers is the preferred item to increase Excadrill's longevity and utilize its great defensive typing; however, Life Orb can be used to increase its damage output at the cost of being more prone to getting worn down. Sand Rush lets Excadrill outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, even fast Choice Scarf users like Kartana. An Adamant nature maximizes its damage output, but Jolly is an option to outspeed Pheromosa and its Speed receiver outside of sand at +1 Speed.

Excadrill's already great Attack and decent Speed make it flexible with what slot it can fit into. A sand setter is mandatory for Excadrill; Tyranitar is preferred, as it can act as a reliable switch-in to dangerous Pokemon like Yveltal, Kyurem-W, and Galarian Moltres once sand runs out, and it also provides Stealth Rock to chip Excadrill's checks and counters and can lure Landorus-T and KO it with Ice Beam. Dracozolt is another sand staple that can break physical walls that trouble Excadrill, especially Skarmory, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn. Together, they wear down Landorus-T for the other to break through. Magnezone can trap and eliminate these two Pokemon, which makes it a great teammate, although it does not provide much defensive utility. Sand cores are very susceptible to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, so the rest of the team should focus on shoring up these weaknesses. Ho-Oh is immune to Ground, checks Tangrowth, and also provides great Attack for Dracozolt, Defense or Special Defense for Excadrill, and Speed for Tyranitar. Similarly, Rotom-W can handle Ground-type Pokemon and check other weather setters that would otherwise be problematic. Tangrowth and Buzzwole deal with Zygarde-10%, which can bypass Ho-Oh and Rotom-W's Ground immunities with Thousand Arrows. Clefable can switch in on Close Combat from Buzzwole and Zeraora and is also immune to sand chip damage thanks to Magic Guard.

Specially Defensive (Special Defense).description:
Specially defensive Excadrill is a good form of role compression, capable of setting Stealth Rock, clearing entry hazards, and checking prominent metagame threats, in particular, Tapu Koko. Earthquake is its primary STAB attack, hitting Alolan Raichu and Tapu Koko hard and can also discourage specially offensive Fire-types like Heatran and Volcanion from switching in. Rapid Spin removes entry hazards, and Excadrill's natural resistance to them means it can often switch in multiple times even without recovery. Toxic cripples switchins such as Tangrowth and Landorus-T. Stealth Rock complements Excadrill's ability to support its teammates and compress roles. Alternatively, if another teammate already has Stealth Rock, Excadrill can opt for Iron Head to better deal with Kyurem-W and Fairy-types like Clefable and Tapu Lele. Leftovers is Excadrill's only form of recovery, but Heavy-Duty Boots is also an option on more offensive teams if Spikes is a particular concern. Mold Breaker helps Excadrill threaten Rotom formes with Earthquake by bypassing Levitate and also eases prediction for Stealth Rock and Toxic by going through Magic Bounce. 32 Speed EVs allow it to outpace Modest Magnezone and Victini after V-Create.

Specially defensive Excadrill fits best on offense teams as a utility Pokemon that serves as a Tapu Koko counter. It benefits from any Special Defense boost; however, gods with high Special Defense like Ho-Oh and Zamazenta ease its ability to take hits.
