Since Excadrill takes the Special Defense slot while still being weak to prominent special threats such as Volcanion, Slowking and Kyurem-W are helpful to shore up this weakness. Offensive threats enjoy Excadrill's ability to clear entry hazards and potentially land a Toxic on Landorus-T while still keeping entry hazards on the foe's side for them to more easily wallbreak. This is especially beneficial to those that tend to switch out repeatedly throughout a game like Victini and Rayquaza. Conversely, they threaten Skarmory, Ho-Oh, and Corviknight, which Excadrill struggles to take on. Rotom-W checks Rayquaza and Zamazenta-C, which would otherwise easily break Excadrill due to its low Defense.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance is an option to take advantage of passive walls that cannot meaningfully threaten Excadrill like Chansey and Ferrothorn. While Regenerator is Excadrill's most consistent set, it can consider immunity abilities like Water Absorb and Bulletproof to better check certain key threats like Zapdos and Tapu Lele; this does leave it without reliable recovery. Excadrill can also run a Pressure + Protect set to stall out dangerous attacks, as several key threats like Terrakion and Zapdos rely on one move to reliably beat it.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Excadrill is heavily threatened by Barraskewda and Inteleon, as they can easily OHKO it and also pivot out against it.

Ground-types: Pokemon like Garchomp and Swampert can set Stealth Rock while threatening to heavily damage Excadrill with Earthquake, preventing it from using Rapid Spin reliably.

Fire- and Fighting-types: Excadrill can't reliably switch into Fire-types like Cinderace and Heatran and Fighting-types like Terrakion; however, all of these threats fear Earthquake or Rock Slide.

Dhelmise: Dhelmise does not fear any of Excadrill's common attacks and can block its attempts to spin.

Defensive Regenerator.description:
Defensive Excadrill is one of the few reliable spinners in the metagame and, thanks to its excellent typing, can also switch into all common variants of Tapu Koko. Regenerator lets it come in multiple times per game to clear entry hazards, supporting offensive and entry hazard-setting teammates alike by clearing hazards on its side only. Earthquake provides reliable damage and OHKOes Tapu Koko, which Excadrill is often tasked with checking. Iron Head is a secondary STAB move that helps against Tapu Lele, but Rock Slide is an option to beat Defog Moltres and catch Talonflame on the switch. Toxic is also an option to poison Excadrill's common switch-ins like Tapu Fini and Garchomp. Stealth Rock makes Excadrill an all-in-one entry hazard control package and allows it to force chip damage onto Tapu Koko. Rocky Helmet is the preferred item to further chip Pixilate Tapu Koko and opposing pivots. The given EV spread outspeeds Modest Tapu Lele, avoids the 2HKO from Pixilate Tapu Koko's Facade, and avoids the 3HKO from Tapu Koko's Dazzling Gleam.

Excadrill works well on hazard-stack balance and bulky offense teams thanks to its good longevity and Rapid Spin. It pairs especially well with Spikes Ferrothorn, Skarmory, and Mew, especially since it also bears the burden of checking Tapu Koko for them. While Excadrill has decent bulk, it can easily be overwhelmed by powerful wallbreakers like Zarude and Inteleon, making solid checks like Chansey and Intimidate Skarmory excellent teammates. It also can't check strong Fire-, Fighting-, and Water-types due to its typing, necessitating teammates like Toxapex and Tapu Fini. Thanks to Excadrill keeping entry hazards off the field without removing opposing hazards, it pairs well with powerful offensive teammates like Garchomp and Zarude, which appreciate the extra chip damage; additionally, Excadrill can reliably switch into Tapu Koko, one of their more prominent revenge killers. Excadrill has a poor matchup against several common entry hazard setters, especially Garchomp and Skarmory, so a secondary entry hazard remover like Defog Corviknight can be valuable.

doublesou.overview: Sand Rush and high Attack make Excadrill a fast and strong attacker when sand is active. Its excellent STAB combination hits almost the entire tier for at least neutral damage. Excadrill finds itself on some variations of sand teams as the primary attacker, matching up well against all of Incineroar, Diancie, Kyurem-B, Naganadel, and Steel-types. Tyranitar is a mandatory partner to set sand, and Incineroar and Zapdos are common teammates, as they take on Water- and Grass-types that threaten Excadrill and provide Fake Out, Parting Shot, and Tailwind to maximize its offensive capabilities. Unfortunately, Excadrill has many noticeable flaws that keep it from being too common in Doubles. It can't rely on its strong, spread Earthquake due to the dominance of Rillaboom and Grassy Terrain, and it struggles against Rillaboom itself, along with many other common Pokemon in Tapu Fini, Urshifu-R, Amoonguss, and Zygarde. Furthermore, Excadrill hates opposing speed control, notably getting outsped and OHKOed by Urshifu-R and Landorus when opposing Tailwind is up, even when sand is active. Likewise, it also has a hard time against Volcanion and Incineroar in Trick Room. Lastly, Excadrill competes against Dracovish and Dracozolt as the primary sand beneficiary on sand teams, as they offer much higher single-target damage. Overall, Excadrill is an suboptimal option on an already niche style of play and, therefore, not the most common Pokemon in the tier.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Excadrill can utilize Swords Dance to boost its Attack to monstrous levels and help counteract Intimidate, but it leaves Excadrill exposed for a turn. Rock Slide is an option to hit non-grounded Pokemon such as Zapdos, but its pool of targets is quite limited. Excadrill can set and remove entry hazards with Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin, but it is not the most reliable at doing either, and Excadrill would rather be attacking with any free turns it can generate.

Sand Attacker.description:
• High Horsepower and Iron Head are Excadrill's primary STAB options and hit Pokemon such as Incineroar, Diancie, Naganadel, and Kyurem-B for super effective damage.

  • Earthquake is a spread option that can be used when Grassy Terrain is not active, but you must be wary of hurting Excadrill's partner. Substitute lets Excadrill block Intimidate and Fake Out, as well as gaining momentum against more passive counterplay.

  • Protect keeps Excadrill safe and lets its partner gain a stronger position.

  • With Sand Rush, Excadrill notably outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame when sand is active, even without a Jolly nature.

Hazard Lead.description:
Excadrill is a decent entry hazard lead in the metagame thanks to its ability to set Stealth Rock against Magic Bounce Pokemon. It also has great utility moves in Rapid Spin and Rock Tomb to aid it in the matchup versus other common leads like Deoxys-S and Smeargle. Rock Tomb lowers the Speed of opposing lead Pokemon that Excadrill or its teammates would otherwise be slower than, and it also prevents sweepers like Dynamaxed Yveltal, Mega Rayquaza, and Xerneas from KOing Excadrill with Speed boosts under their belt. A high Attack stat and Earthquake ensure that Excadrill isn't passive setup bait, letting it threaten common entry hazard setters such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Ferrothorn as well as potentially OHKO Zacian-C; this forces them to KO Excadrill, which allows its teammates to safely enter the field and take advantage of the Stealth Rock that it has laid. Toxic is also a viable option over Earthquake to pressure Pokemon such as Dragon Dance Zygarde-C, support Arceus formes without Refresh, and other Pokemon that try to set up on Excadrill. Rapid Spin removes entry hazards set by other lead Pokemon such as Deoxys-S, Primal Groudon, and Smeargle and provides Excadrill with a Speed boost to outspeed and threaten faster Pokemon. A Jolly nature is used to outspeed Smeargle, support Arceus formes, Modest Yveltal and Xerneas, and, after one Speed boost from Rapid Spin, Jolly Zacian-C. Focus Sash is the chosen item, as it guarantees that Excadrill will survive any one non-multi-hit move from faster Pokemon, which improves the chance of it getting Stealth Rock up.

Excadrill fits best on hyper offense teams due to the fact that other playstyles generally do not appreciate a dedicated suicide lead. Beating lead Substitute Zacian-C is essential for offense, as otherwise, said foe will most likely outspeed and KO or severely damage the rest of Excadrill's team, preventing safe setup in most cases. Entry hazard-sensitive Pokemon such as Mega Rayquaza, Lunala, and Yveltal really appreciate Excadrill's ability to get rid of entry hazards. Other sweepers such as Zacian-C, Xerneas, and Dragon Dance Zygarde-C are also great teammates for Excadrill. Pokemon that can block Excadrill's Rapid Spin like Ferrothorn and Ghost-types like Lunala can be problematic, so teammates that can take advantage of them such as Zacian-C and Yveltal are also appreciated.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Steel

Leftovers or Focus Sash may be used on Swords Dance Excadrill to improve its longevity and or better ensure at least one KO, but both lower its ability to threaten Flying-types.

Choice Scarf (Steel).description:
Excadrill is Steel's go-to revenge killer with its excellent Ground- and Rock-type coverage, which makes it a solid wincon against Fire, Electric, and Poison teams. Earthquake works well with Excadrill's ability, Mold Breaker, allowing it to threaten Rotom-W and Galarian Weezing. Rock Blast may be used over Rock Slide to get past Substitutes from Kyurem and Dragonite's Multiscale, but the damage is highly inconsistent. Toxic allows Excadrill to put Mega Sableye, a huge roadblock for Steel teams, on a timer due to Mold Breaker, in addition to punishing common switch-ins such as Landorus-T, Slowbro, and Porygon2. Rapid Spin removes entry hazards without clearing the hazards Steel teams stack. A Choice Scarf with a Jolly nature lets Excadrill outspeed threats such as unboosted Volcarona, Victini, and Zeraora and boosted Kommo-o.

Ferrothorn provides Excadrill with a switch-in to Water-types like Mega Swampert and Slowbro, and it helps Excadrill break through defensive cores with Stealth Rock and Spikes support. Corviknight, Skarmory, or Celesteela provides Excadrill with a Ground immunity. Corviknight can give it a safe switch-in with U-turn and threaten Fighting-types with Brave Bird, Skarmory can set entry hazards so that Excadrill can force progress against bulkier teams, and Celesteela threatens Grass-types like Ferrothorn, Rillaboom, and Zarude with Flamethrower. In return, Excadrill provides an Electric immunity and can take on threats such as Choice Band Zeraora and Tapu Koko. Aegislash and Heatran provide a Fighting and Fire immunity, respectively, and can switch into most special attacks aimed at Excadrill. Heatran, in particular, can nullify Fire-type moves from Choice Scarf Blacephalon, which outspeeds Excadrill and poses a huge threat to Steel teams. Wallbreakers such as Bisharp, Mega Scizor, and Choice Specs Aegislash can pressure physical walls such as Porygon2, Slowbro, and Mega Venusaur, which helps Excadrill clean opposing Normal, Psychic, and Poison teams late-game.

Swords Dance (Steel).description:
With Swords Dance, Excadrill becomes a threatening sweeper and late-game cleaner, as it can break through bulky Pokemon such as Toxapex, Melmetal, and Mandibuzz. Rock Slide deals with Flying-types that switch into Excadrill such as Crobat, Zapdos, and Mega Charizard Y. Rapid Spin boosts Excadrill's Speed, letting it take advantage of forced switches and outspeed checks such as Gengar, Zeraora, and Mega Charizard Y. Rockium Z allows Excadrill to bypass checks in Celesteela and Mandibuzz, as well as ensuring the OHKO on both Mega Charizard X and Mega Charizard Y.

Ferrothorn can take on Water- and Ground-type moves from Urshifu-R and Mega Swampert aimed at Excadrill, and it also sets entry hazards to help Excadrill break down the opposing team. Aegislash provides a Fighting immunity and can weaken checks such as Slowbro and Mantine with Toxic. Heatran provides a Fire immunity and can check threats like Victini and Volcarona, which Swords Dance Excadrill cannot due to not running Choice Scarf. Corviknight and Skarmory provide a Ground immunity and can check Fighting-types such as Terrakion. Alternatively, Celesteela may be used as the Ground-immune partner, as it can handle offensive threats such as Rillaboom and Mega Diancie that Excadrill struggles with. These Ground-immune teammates also lure in Electric-types such as Tapu Koko and Magnezone, which Excadrill can set up on. Choice Scarf Magnezone forms a good wallbreaking core with Excadrill, as it removes Steel-types like Skarmory and Ferrothorn that Excadrill struggles with, as well as removing threats like Keldeo and Urshifu-R. Jirachi and Mega Scizor benefit from Excadrill's wallbreaking abilities, as they can clean late-game against Poison and Flying teams and Dragon and Fighting teams, respectively.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Steel Beam can be used on the suicide lead set to maintain momentum and stop Defog users slower than it, but is difficult to fit.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Excadrill relies on its teammates to pressure troublesome Ghost-types such as Lunala, Calyrex-S, and Marshadow, as they can prevent Rapid Spin from being used. Giratina can completely shut down Excadrill by removing Stealth Rock with Defog, absorbing Toxic with Rest, crippling it with Will-O-Wisp, and tanking any hit from it with ease.

Entry Hazard Removal: Excadrill's ability to set Stealth Rock becomes completely diminished once Pokemon carrying Defog such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal can KO it off the field and attempt to remove it. However, offensive teammates such as Kyogre, Calyrex-S, and Yveltal can take advantage of the turn used for Defog and force them out or set up on them.

Entry Hazard Lead.description:
Excadrill provides good utility to hyper offense teams in AG as a lead due to the potent combination of Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin. Stealth Rock deals residual damage to most foes attempting to switch in, and Rapid Spin prevents opposing entry hazard setters such as Necrozma-DM, Ferrothorn, Eternatus, and Tyranitar from keeping entry hazards up against Excadrill. Additionally, Rapid Spin is occasionally useful for gaining a Speed boost after being used, deterring naturally faster Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Zacian-C from attempting to switch in. Rock Tomb is great for 2HKOing Ho-Oh, which is able to switch into Stealth Rock with Heavy-Duty Boots and remove it with Defog, while also lowering the foe's Speed so a teammate is able to outspeed it, preventing sweepers such as Geomancy Xerneas and Dragon Dance Zygarde-C from gaining Speed boosts on Excadrill. Wallbreakers such as Kyogre and Yveltal also appreciate being able to take advantage of slower Pokemon on the field. Earthquake can OHKO Zacian-C after a Defense drop from Close Combat or chip damage from Rapid Spin or Rock Tomb while preventing Substitute users like Zygarde-C and Zekrom from using Excadrill as complete setup fodder. Toxic punishes Yveltal, which can use Defog against Excadrill. Focus Sash allows Excadrill to withstand powerful attacks such as Kyogre's Water Spout and Marshadow's Close Combat and almost always guarantees it gets to set Stealth Rock.

Excadrill should only be used on hyper offense, where Pokemon such as Xerneas, Zacian-C, Calyrex-S, Rayquaza, and Groudon appreciate its ability to both set and remove entry hazards. Excadrill generally struggles against Ghost-types such as Lunala, Giratina, and Calyrex-S as they are able to block Rapid Spin, so Yveltal is a great partner for it. Excadrill dislikes using Rapid Spin against Rocky Helmet Necrozma-DM, so Kyogre, Calyrex-S, Yveltal, and Groudon can pressure it extremely well. Excadrill should be led with in most matches so it can immediately set Stealth Rock, deter opposing entry hazards, and maximize its teammates' offensive potential.

pu.overview: Cleric support is often at the heart of defensive teams, and a good representative of this role is Audino. Not only can it cure status, but it also passes hefty Wishes and sponges damage thanks to Wish and Regenerator. This extensive recovery makes Audino a solid check to notable special threats like Charizard, Galarian Articuno, and Haunter. Audino has less luck versus setup special attackers like Ribombee and Meteor Beam Archeops, though, as it fails to deter their setup. Its passivity is even more notable versus physical sweepers and stallbreakers like Gallade and Centiskorch, since it lacks Defense investment.

Cleric.description: Knock Off is better than a STAB attack for Audino, as it better threatens the targets it checks like Charizard and Galarian Articuno, and item removal also deters the likes of Doublade and Choice Specs Jellicent from switching in. Heavy-Duty Boots ensures Audino maximizes the recovery netted from Regenerator, allowing it to scout attacks more safely. Hell Bell can be swapped for Toxic so that Audino is less passive against foes like Sandslash, although the team will need another cleric like Ribombee or Eldegoss given Audino's own vulnerability to Toxic. Walls like Gigalith, Regirock, and Aggron all lack reliable recovery, making them viable receivers for Wish—or Heal Bell if they opt for Rest. Their Stealth Rock support works great with Audino's Knock Off removing opposing Heavy-Duty Boots, and they also function as counters to Ribombee. Fighting-type checks like Weezing and Silvally-Fairy are always warranted as switch-ins for Gallade. Eldegoss and Tangela offer natural synergy by forming a Regenerator core, with either blanket checking physical attackers for Audino. Other physical walls such as Quagsire and Weezing are also good partners. Quagsire stands out, as it can completely quash most setup sweepers.

ubers.overview: The combination of Regenerator, decent physical bulk, and useful support moves such as Wish, Knock Off, and Heal Bell makes Audino a decent niche option on balance teams. It checks the prominent Calyrex-S as well as physical Yveltal, and it also enables dangerous setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Groudon and Dragon Dance Zekrom. However, its lack of useful resistances and general passivity leave Audino threatened by staples of the tier such as Kyogre, Marshadow, Zygarde-C, and Zekrom. Also, despite its good matchup against Calyrex-S, Audino can easily be crippled by Trick or beaten by Focus Sash variants if it has to switch in on them, and thus it requires additional teammates to handle Calyrex-S.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Status moves such as Thunder Wave and Toxic can be used over Heal Bell or Protect to cripple threats like Yveltal, Zekrom, Kyogre, and Eternatus on the switch, but Heal Bell is usually far more valuable and not having Protect to use Wish safely can lead to dangerous scenarios against wallbreakers like Choice Specs Kyogre and offensive Eternatus.

Checks and Counters

Eternatus: Thanks to its high Special Attack, great bulk, and excellent ability in Pressure, Eternatus put immense pressure on Audino. In particular, Sludge Bomb Eternatus can forces Audino to spam Heal Bell, taking advantage of its low PP amount. On top of that, Eternatus usually doesn't care much about losing its item.

Special Wallbreakers: Special attackers such as Kyogre, the aforementioned Eternatus, and specially offensive Yveltal threaten Audino with their STAB moves. While Yveltal does not appreciate being hit by Knock Off, Calm Mind Kyogre and Cosmic Power Eternatus can use Audino as setup fodder.

Substitute Users: Substitute users such as Zygarde-C, Kyogre, and Xerneas can use Audino as setup fodder.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Pheromosa, Marshadow, Buzzwole, and Zamazenta-C threaten Audino thanks to their STAB moves. While Choice Band Marshadow and Pheromosa do not like being hit by Knock Off, the latter three can still use Audino as setup fodder with Bulk Up and Howl.

Setup Sweepers: Audino cannot threaten most setup sweepers at all, which include Dragon Dance Zekrom, Swords Dance Groudon, and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM.

Support.description:
Wish is a great option to keep both Audino and its teammates healthy. Protect is a classic option alongside Wish, and it also allows Audino to scout Choice item foes such as Choice Band Marshadow and Choice Specs Kyogre. Heal Bell lets Audino cure status. Knock Off cripples common threats such as Yveltal, Calyrex-S, Ho-Oh, and Lunala, removing precious items such as Heavy-Duty Boots, and Audino will always 2HKO Calyrex-S with Knock Off. Heavy-Duty Boots maximizes Regenerator's net recovery and makes Audino a better pivot.

The extreme passivity of Audino must be addressed by its teammates; powerful wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Groudon, Zekrom, and Choice Specs Kyogre are all good options that love both cleric and Wish support that Audino provides. The former two also act as great offensive checks to Taunt Yveltal, which Audino struggles against. Yveltal and Marshadow also pair well with Audino, as they form an extremely effective core against Calyrex-S, while Audino provides Wish and cleric support. Necrozma-DM can set Stealth Rock and appreciates Audino's ability to both check Calyrex-S and cripple common switch-in such as Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Lunala with Knock Off, leaving them susceptible to Stealth Rock.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Bulk Up with 156 Special Defense EVs turns Timburr into a dangerous wincon, but it still struggles to break through Poison-types. Running an EV spread of 196 Atk / 236 Def / 76 Spe with an Adamant nature improves Timburr's matchup against foes like Mienfoo, and it still outspeeds Frillish and Trace Porygon. Defog can be ran on teams that appreciate Timburr's ability to remove entry hazards.

Checks and Counters

Koffing: Koffing takes little from Timburr's attacks and can beat it one-versus-one. However, Timburr can wear it down, especially when paired with Mienfoo or Grookey.

Mareanie: Mareanie completely walls Timburr lacking Thunder Punch and outlasts it with Recover and Regenerator. Thunder Punch and Bulk Up sets can muscle through it, though.

Abra: Abra outspeeds Timburr, OHKOes it with Psychic, and can shrug off Mach Punch. It cannot safely switch in on Timburr's other attacks, however.

Foongus: Foongus shrugs off Timburr's Fighting-type attacks and can cripple it with Spore. However, Timburr can lure it in and then 2HKO it with Ice Punch.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Timburr is a niche pick thanks to its great bulk and access to moves like Mach Punch. Mach Punch picks off dangerous threats like Porygon, Carvanha, and Vullaby. Ice Punch allows Timburr to beat Foongus and hit Vullaby for super effective damage; alternatively, Thunder Punch can be ran with 156 Speed to allow Timburr to break past Mareanie.

Timburr is an inferior choice to Mienfoo for most teams due to the latter's more powerful STAB move in High Jump Kick, much greater survivability, and pivot move in U-turn; however, some hyper offense teams appreciate Timburr's greater bulk and role compression with Mach Punch. Entry hazard-stacking teams featuring Dwebble and multiple wallbreakers are some examples. Timburr can also be used together with Mienfoo in a Fighting spam core. Steel-types like Pawniard and Ferroseed are important teammates to check Psychic-types. Grookey shares checks like Koffing and Foongus with Timburr, and Grookey can work in tandem with it to break through these checks. Special attackers like Abra, Porygon, and Staryu appreciate Timburr handling Steel-types. Diglett can threaten Poison-types, especially Mareanie if Timburr is lacking Thunder Punch.

Bulk Up.description:
Bulk Up enhances Gurdurr's already solid offensive capabilities and allows it to function as a mid- to late-game sweeper, with Drain Punch keeping Gurdurr healthy and allowing it to garner boosts against physical attackers like Raboot and Piloswine. Knock Off is Gurdurr's best coverage move, hitting Fighting-resistant Pokemon like Galarian Corsola and Hattrem for massive damage while also making it easier to break through other Pokemon like Clefairy and Mareanie by removing their Eviolite. Mach Punch rounds off the set, helping to take out weakened faster attackers like Electabuzz and Rufflet. Ice Punch can be used over either of the last two moves, reducing Gurdurr's offensive utility but in turn giving it a way to more immediately damage Roselia and still hit neutral targets for respectable damage. The Speed investment allows Gurdurr to outpace uninvested Piloswine and Hattrem, although this can be invested into bulk if preferred.

Gurdurr can struggle to get past physically defensive walls like Tangela, Clefairy, and Galarian Corsola; other physical attackers like Galarian Linoone, Raboot, and Piloswine can assist in breaking down these shared answers while the latter two also greatly benefit from Gurdurr removing foe's items. Similarly, special attackers like Roselia and Duosion can increase Gurdurr's breaking potential with Spikes and Future Sight support, respectively, and can switch into the aforementioned walls with ease. Hattrem is also a notable teammate, as it can wall Mareanie and prevent Galarian Corsola from healing with Strength Sap.

Defog.description:
As a Defog user, Gurdurr has a solid matchup against common entry hazard setters like Piloswine and Ferroseed. It also finds opportunities to Defog as a bulky offensive threat, forcing out physical attackers unable to trade hits with it like Raboot and Galarian Linoone. Knock Off further increases its utility by crippling switch-ins. Toxic shores up Gurdurr's otherwise poor matchup into Galarian Corsola, but Ice Punch and High Horsepower are alternatives that help against Poison-type entry hazard setters in Roselia, Koffing, and Mareanie. The defensive investment allows Gurdurr to take two hits from Choice Band Raboot's High Jump Kick after Stealth Rock while also avoiding a 3HKO from Piloswine and other variants of Raboot, with the rest invested into Attack to increase Gurdurr's damage output.

Gurdurr's best teammates will vary depending on the fourth slot chosen; when using Toxic, Gurdurr will have a difficult time against the aforementioned Poison-types, so Pokemon that can pressure these or use them as setup fodder like Lampent, Ferroseed, and Duosion are fantastic partners. On the other hand, Pokemon that can assist in pressuring Galarian Corsola like Hattrem and Roselia are very desirable when foregoing Toxic, with the latter in particular being useful for absorbing Toxic Spikes, which Gurdurr has a difficult time clearing.

Flame Orb.description:
Guts-boosted Gurdurr is a force to be reckoned with; it trades Eviolite and Drain Punch for the power and coverage of Close Combat and Facade, allowing it to 2HKO physically defensive walls like Clefairy, Mareanie, and Slowpoke with ease. Mach Punch rounds off the set by finishing off weakened faster attackers like Raboot and Electabuzz. Unfortunately, Gurdurr still struggles to break through certain physically defensive walls like Tangela and Koffing, and without Eviolite, Gurdurr becomes much more vulnerable to faster Pokemon like Electabuzz and Raboot.

Charjabug is an excellent teammate for providing Gurdurr with Sticky Web support, slowing down wallbreakers like Lampent that would otherwise force Gurdurr out and using a slow Volt Switch to bring Gurdurr in safely and activate its Flame Orb. Other slow pivots like Slowpoke and Clefairy similarly are very useful and further support Gurdurr with moves like Future Sight, Thunder Wave, and Healing Wish to augment its offensive potential. Offensive pivots are similarly useful, with Electabuzz luring in specially defensive Pokemon like Duosion for Gurdurr to burst through and Thwackey providing passive recovery with Grassy Terrain and benefitting from Gurdurr breaking down shared checks like Roselia and Koffing.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Defog is an option to turn Gurdurr into an entry hazard remover that poses good matchups against common entry hazard setters like Piloswine and Rhydon, but it generally has difficulty fitting the move. Stone Edge targets foes like Rotom-S, Altaria, and Articuno.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Although they do not appreciate Knock Off removing their Heavy-Duty Boots, Flying-types such as Rotom-S, Altaria, and Cramorant can threaten to KO Gurdurr.

Physical Walls: Physical walls such as Altaria and Tangela are able to take hits from Gurdurr and pressure it with their STAB attacks. However, they should be wary of Knock Off. Alcremie is a notable foe that is able to take Gurdurr's STAB options and Knock Off and pressure it with its Fairy-type moves.

Chip Damage and Knock Off: It is easy to cripple and wear down Gurdurr, as it is reliant on Drain Punch recovery and Eviolite to check its foes.

Bulk Up.description:
Gurdurr is a notable tank in ZU thanks to its good bulk and access to decent recovery through Drain Punch. This recovery lets Gurdurr more consistently set up, letting it accumulate multiple boosts. Gurdurr can utilize Bulk Up mid- or late-game against passive foes like Stunfisk and Coalossal. Knock Off cripples switch-ins such as Tangela, Altaria, and Rotom-S. Mach Punch allows Gurdurr to revenge kill foes such as Shiftry and Kangaskhan. 252 HP and 60 Defense EVs ensure that Gurdurr will only be 3HKOed by Kangaskhan's Double-Edge. Guts lets Gurdurr absorb Will-O-Wisp from Rapidash and Toxic from Pyukumuku to empower its attacks.

Gurdurr fits on both bulky offense and balance teams due to its solid bulk and ability to generate pressure with both Bulk Up and Mach Punch. Gurdurr appreciates strong offensive support from its teammates to keep initiative throughout the battle, as it is otherwise prone to being worn down by common VoltTurn cores. Wallbreakers such as Rapidash, Silvally formes, and Thievul can threaten physical walls such as Tangela, Gourgeist-XL, and Qwilfish, enabling Gurdurr to better threaten them late-game. Pokemon such as Rotom and Exeggutor benefit from Gurdurr revenge killing foes such as Silvally-Dark and Shiftry with Mach Punch; in return, they can threaten Flying-types such as Rotom-S and Cramorant that trouble it.

uu.overview: Guts Conkeldurr is one of UU's most devastating wallbreakers. Once burned by Flame Orb, it can evade status from defensive staples like Amoonguss and Chansey. Knock Off and Ice Punch or Facade offer virtually perfect coverage alongside its powerful Drain Punch or Close Combat, allowing it to dismantle defensive cores like Chansey and Quagsire. STAB Mach Punch is also a great tool, functioning as a strong priority attack that can threaten faster Pokemon like Excadrill, Mamoswine, and Hydreigon. Conkeldurr is a bit weighed down by its proneness to being worn down from Flame Orb, however. This is made a larger problem by its poor Speed, which allows the tier's many faster threats like Keldeo and Salamence to overwhelm it, as well as its iffy defensive typing, which doesn't give it many notable resistances and leaves it open to Pokemon like Moltres, Togekiss, Primarina, and Salamence. Moreover, sand chip from Hippowdon wears down Conkeldurr. Conkeldurr also faces competition from Fighting-types like Keldeo, who offers comparable power in addition to greater Speed and an additional Water-typing.
uu.comments:
Other Options

A Bulk Up set with investment in Special Defense can function as a solid bulky sweeper that can absorb status. Conkeldurr could hold Assault Vest to more easily switch into Scald from Pokemon like Raikou and Quagsire while also checking special attackers such as Nihilego. However, this often prevents it from being able to maximize its offensive potential, and it is still quite prone to being worn down.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Defensive Salamence is a particularly good check to Conkeldurr because of its ability to always take a hit from full HP thanks to Intimidate, allowing it to switch into Conkeldurr and threaten it with Dual Wingbeat. Skarmory's massive physical bulk lets it switch into a weaker attack from Conkeldurr and nail it with Brave Bird. Togekiss and Crobat can also be a solid checks, 4x resisting Conkeldurr's STAB moves and revenge killing it. Moltres resists Mach Punch and can power through Conkeldurr with Hurricane.

Psychic-types: Slowking and Galarian Slowbro can take Knock Off from full HP while severely damaging Conkeldurr with STAB Psychic-type attacks. Necrozma and Azelf outspeed and pressure Conkeldurr with their powerful attacks.

Fairy-types: Although it takes hefty damage from Facade, bulky Primarina can restore its health as it dents Conkeldurr with Draining Kiss, while its Choice Specs sets can outrun and OHKO it outright. Azumarill outspeeds Conkeldurr, resists Mach Punch, and can KO it with Play Rough. Hatterene can trade with Conkeldurr and restore health with Draining Kiss.

Faster Pokemon: Conkeldurr's low Speed and Flame Orb use leave it quite vulnerable to being overwhelmed by faster Pokemon like Tapu Bulu, Nidoking, Keldeo, and Thundurus-T.

Guts Wallbreaker.description:
Drain Punch can be used as Conkeldurr's primary STAB move, giving it more longevity and a safe attacking option. However, Close Combat is also an option for its massive damage output, crushing defensive staples like Celesteela and Skarmory. Facade heavily damages various Pokemon that resist its STAB attacks, including Nidoqueen, Amoonguss, and Primarina. Ice Punch KOes Conkeldurr's most common counter in defensive Salamence while hitting threats like Hippowdon and Tangrowth super effectively. However, Conkeldurr becomes walled by Primarina. Knock Off nails foes such as Galarian Slowbro, Chandelure, and Slowking. It also removes items from switch-ins like Salamence, Togekiss, and Moltres, crippling them heavily. Mach Punch is a strong priority move that can pressure faster foes like Hydreigon, Excadrill, and Zarude while picking off weakened threats in general. An Adamant nature is preferred in order to maximize Conkeldurr's wallbreaking potential.

Conkeldurr generally fits well on more offensively oriented builds. Some balance teams appreciate the offensive pressure it offers, too. Due to Conkeldurr's tendency to wearing itself down, it appreciates Grassy Terrain support from Tapu Bulu for passive recovery. Tapu Bulu also checks faster threats to Conkeldurr like Primarina and Azumarill. Conkeldurr struggles to break through physical walls like Tangrowth and Hippowdon in the short term, so teammates who can threaten these like Moltres and Zarude are appreciated. Entry hazard setters like Nihilego and Swampert can wear down checks like Skarmory with Stealth Rock for Conkeldurr to muscle through easier. Nihilego can also check many revenge killers to Conkeldurr like Togekiss, Salamence, and Crobat. Slow pivots like Chansey, Slowking, and Mandibuzz can help bring Conkeldurr into play against threats like Excadrill, Zarude, and Lycanroc-D. Slowking can also provide Future Sight support to further amplify Conkeldurr's wallbreaking power. Late-game cleaners like Thundurus-T and Scizor are able to clean up after Conkeldurr softens up the opposing team. In return, it can pressure Flying-types like Togekiss and Salamence. Faster teammates like Choice Scarf Hydreigon can revenge kill threats to Conkeldurr like Azelf and Salamence.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Conkeldurr can use Thunder Punch or Ice Punch to hit Flying-types or Poison Jab to threaten Fairy-types. Tinted Lens can be run to deal more damage to switch-ins, and Tough Claws can be used to increase Conkeldurr's overall offensive power, though opting for one of these means that Conkeldurr can no longer act as a revenge killer as it underspeeds nearly the entire metagame.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Conkeldurr's Special Defense is vulnerable to hits from special attackers like Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko.

Passive Damage: Even with Drain Punch, Conkeldurr can be quickly worn down by the combination of entry hazards and Life Orb recoil.

Psychic Surge: Psychic Surge users like Azelf hinder Conkeldurr, as Psychic Terrain blocks Triage's priority and prevents Conkeldurr from using it to recover HP.

Fast Fighting-Resistant Pokemon: Pokemon like Zapdos and Talonflame heavily threaten Conkeldurr, as they easily outspeed it and aren't threatened by Drain Punch.

Fairy-types: Conkeldurr is unable to meaningfully damage most Fairy-types and is threatened in return by the likes of Togekiss, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Koko.

Triage.description:
Boasting excellent Attack and STAB Drain Punch, Conkeldurr is a powerful Triage cleaner. It also has respectable physical bulk, allowing it to set up with Bulk Up and have good survivability when combined with Drain Punch's recovery. Knock Off can be used to punish Psychic-types switching into Conkeldurr as well as cripple opposing Pokemon by removing Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots, making them easier to wear down. Earthquake is a powerful coverage move that OHKOes Tapu Koko and 2HKOes Toxapex.

Conkeldurr fits well on balance and bulky offense teams that benefit from its revenge killing abilities. Teammates like Tapu Koko and Jirachi that struggle with opposing Steel-types appreciate Conkeldurr's ability to remove them. Due to its below average Special Defense, Conkeldurr benefits from teammates like Blissey and Ferrothorn that can take special hits. Conkeldurr's ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots makes it a great teammate for entry hazard setters like Mew and Skarmory. Conkeldurr is also vulnerable to chip damage from entry hazards itself, so entry hazard removers like Corviknight and Excadrill help to keep it from getting worn down. Conkeldurr is extremely weak to Psychic Surge users like Azelf, as they block Drain Punch entirely, so teammates like Mandibuzz and RegenVest Jirachi are strongly encouraged. Conkeldurr also struggles against Togekiss and Tapu Fini, so teammates like Tapu Koko are helpful to KO them. Zapdos and Galarian Zapdos are also fast, powerful threats that resist Drain Punch, so fast offensive Pokemon like Zygarde-10% are helpful teammates. Despite its great Attack, Drain Punch's relatively low Base Power means it misses several key KOs, making powerful wallbreakers like Sheer Force Tapu Lele exellent teammates.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

With Sludge Bomb, 100 Special Attack EVs could be opted instead to guarantee a 2HKO on Tanglea after Stealth Rock damage. RestTalk sets offer recovery so that Palpitoad can wall throughout the game; they tend to be less worthwhile as Palpitoad sacrifices two vallauble supportive moves for this recovery. Specially defensive spreads are able to wall Electabuzz more consistently.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Any offensive Grass-type like Tangela, Thwackey, and Roselia can outspeed and OHKO Palpioad. Furthermore, they make for good switch-ins agaianst it, with Roselia especially being unfazed by its status attempts.

Setup Sweepers: Rufflet, Gurdurr, Duosion, and Clefairy are examples of sweepers that are bulky enough to setup and break Palpitoad, and have work arounds or immunities to Toxic. Lampent has potential coverage in Energy Ball to targets Palpitoad as well.

Magic Bounce: Hattrem prevents Palpitoad from setting up Stealth Rock, and may even opt for Giga Drain to be immensely threatening to Palpitoad.

Residual Damage: Palpitoad lacks reliable recovery, and will be worn down from status, U-turn, and Knock Off. Attackers like Electabuzz and Raboot have a decent chance of sweeping by wearing down Palpitoad.

Stealth Rock.description:
Palpitoad's well-rounded stats and great Water / Ground typing help it fit on teams as a viable physical wall. It can set up Stealth Rock early-game and threaten other entry hazard users like Piloswine and Koffing with its STAB attacks. Earth Power can nail common physical attackers like Klang and Raboot that Palpitoad has no problem switching into. Scald has a chance to burn physical attackers like Thwackey and Fraxure that may switch in on Palpitoad and can also wear down defensive Pokemon that lack recovery like Hattrem and Charjabug. On the other hand, Sludge Bomb nails Grass-types like Tangela and Thwackey; the latter otherwise could Substitute safely on Palpitoad. Toxic is great for crippling walls that shrug off Palpitoad's attacks like Galarian Corsola and Togetic.

Palpitoad is a good check to some physical attackers, but its lack of recovery and immediate firepower makes it vulnerable to multiple foes. Palpitoad should avoid setting up Stealth Rock if Magic Bounce users are on the opposing team, as Hattrem especially can shrug off Palpitoad's attacks and threatens back with Giga Drain. Try pairing it with Dark- and Steel-types like Galarian Linoone and Klang to help with these situations. Palpitoad also struggles against other entry hazard setters like Ferroseed and Roselia, so having anti-entry hazard Pokemon like Hattrem and Vullaby is worthwhile. Additionally, being 4x weak to Grass-type attacks is dangerous, which walls like Ferroseed, Roselia, Vullaby, and Charjabug can all help patch; in return, Palpitoad functions as a Fire-type switch-in for these three. As Palpitoad worries about strong special wallbreakers like Abra, special walls like Galarian Corsola and Klang can help make a defensive backbone for the rest of the team. Palpitoad is also susceptible to being worn down from status, Knock Off, and multiple physical attacks. Try to either have other physical walls with reliable recovery and support with Wish and Heal Bell from users like Clefairy.

uu.overview: Seismitoad separates itself from other Ground-type Stealth Rock setters thanks to its additional Water typing and access to Water Absorb, which allows it to completely counter Rotom-W and discourage powerful threats like Choice Specs Keldeo from clicking Hydro Pump. Seismitoad's typing also allows it to check common Pokemon like Celesteela and Darmanitan. Seismitoad has a positive matchup against some of the entry hazard removers of the tier, such as Rotom-W, Salamence, and Excadrill, through potent utility moves like Toxic and Knock Off. However, Seismitoad's lack of reliable recovery outside of Leftovers makes it vulnerable to status effects and Knock Off. Seismitoad's crippling weakness to Grass-types gives Pokemon like Amoonguss and Zarude free entry and bad matchups against threats that carry Grass-type coverage moves such as Nihilego and Gyarados. Seismitoad also faces massive competition from Swampert, who shares the same typing, is bulkier, and has Flip Turn to not be a momentum sink. However, Seismitoad's access to Knock Off gives it an important niche over Swampert on bulkier teams that need the role compression. Seismitoad also has to compete with other Stealth Rock setters such as Hippowdon and Cobalion, which offer greater offensive presence.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Seismitoad can run an offensive Stealth Rock set on rain teams that enjoy its immunity to Electric-type attacks. With moves like Hydro Pump, Earth Power, and Sludge Wave, it can tear through many teams. However, even with a Life Orb and a rain boost, 85 Special Attack may not cut it at times. Rain teams generally prefer Kingdra as a wallbreaker as well due to its better typing. A physical Seismitoad on rain teams can open the door for teammates like Kingdra by blowing through Chansey, Salamence, and Swampert with Earthquake, Ice Punch, and Power Whip, respectively, though this gives Seismitoad a worse matchup against Skarmory and Tangrowth. Seismitoad can run more offensive EV spreads on its traditional Stealth Rock set with good coverage options such as Sludge Wave. However, this considerably cuts into Seismitoad's bulk, which is often less than ideal.

Checks and Counters

Grass-type Pokemon and Coverage Moves: Seismitoad's defensive set often invites in Pokemon like Tangrowth and Amoonguss, which are difficult to outlast due to Regenerator. Zarude has Jungle Healing to remove status, making it a complete counter to Seismitoad. Dhelmise can force Seismitoad out as it removes Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin. This weakness to Grass also means that Pokemon such as Gyarados, Thundurus-T, and Nihilego can threaten Seismitoad with coverage moves like Power Whip and Grass Knot.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Offensive threats like Azelf, Hydreigon, Diggersby, and Conkeldurr greatly hinder Seismitoad's ability to act as a defensive wall because of their powerful secondary STAB attacks, taking advantage of its passivity and lack of recovery. However, they do not appreciate switching into Seismitoad due to its STAB moves or fear of status.

Toxic: Seismitoad greatly fears Toxic from common Pokemon like Chansey and Swampert, including Pokemon it would normally check like Celesteela, Salamence, and Cobalion, as its already limited longevity becomes worsened.

Defensive Stealth Rock.description:
Seismitoad can use Stealth Rock after pivoting into Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Celesteela. Scald gives Seismitoad a chance to burn switch-ins such as Tapu Bulu and Amoonguss as well as offensive Pokemon like Scizor. Toxic makes Seismitoad less passive against the likes of Tangrowth and Slowking switching in. It also helps Seismitoad outlast other Defoggers such as Salamence and Rotom-W as well as threaten other foes like Keldeo. Knock Off is useful for removing items from Defoggers like Salamence, Mandibuzz, and Rotom-W, making it tougher for them to remove Stealth Rock. 64 Speed EVs enable Seismitoad to outspeed Adamant Azumarill.

Seismitoad fits best on balance and semi-stall teams that appreciate its defensive qualities and Stealth Rock and Knock Off support. Grass-types like Amoonguss and Tangrowth act as secondary checks to Water-types such as Primarina, Keldeo, and Azumarill, for Seismitoad struggles to check then by itself. They also as good Knock Off sponges for Seismitoad to maintain Leftovers. Tapu Bulu also counters the aforementioned Water-types and provides Grassy Terrain support to increase Seismitoad's longevity. Salamence and Skarmory help take on Grass-types like Zarude and Tangrowth, with the latter also providing Spikes to complement Seismitoad's Stealth Rock. Salamence also can keep Seismitoad from being worn down by Spikes with Defog. Umbreon and Jirachi can sustain Seismitoad with Wish, with the former checking wallbreakers like Mamoswine, Azelf, and Nidoqueen that can overwhelm Seismitoad. Togekiss can similarly play the role of a cleric and assist in pressuring Grass-types like Zarude and Tapu Bulu while forming a solid backbone against Keldeo. In exchange, Seismitoad helps in wearing down Rotom-W and Rotom-H. Chansey also acts as a cleric with Aromatherapy and walls dangerous wallbreakers like Hydreigon, Thundurus-T, and Azelf with ease.

Defensive Pivot.description: Seismitoad is an incredibly effective pivot thanks to its fantastic bulk which lets it check physical attackers like Zeraora and Tyranitar. Furthermore, its fantastic typing lets it handle the likes of Heatran and Dracozolt, and thanks to Water Absorb, it's also a fantastic check to Water-types like Rotom-W, Keldeo, and Urshifu-R. Seismitoad's excellent defensive profile gives a plethora of opportunities to set up entry hazards, which is why Spikes is preferred over Stealth Rock. However, Stealth Rock is an option if the team already has another Spikes setter. Shore Up allows Seismitoad to stay healthy throughout a game, so that it can check Pokemon like Cinderace and Zeraora long-term. Thousand Waves allows Seismitoad to trap Pokemon such as Toxapex and Tyranitar. Toxic is an alternative to Thousand Waves that punishes switch-ins like Rotom-W, Tornadus-T, and opposing Seismitoad, allowing partners like Heatran, Keldeo, and Aerodactyl to potentially break through them. Rocky Helmet can be used to further spread chip damage onto Pokemon such as Zeraora, Cinderace, and Buzzwole, while Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Seismitoad from being pressured by entry hazards while switching in on wallbreakers. Wallbreakers like Cinderace and Aerodactyl pressure Pokemon that want to switch into Seismitoad's Flip Turn, like Ferrothorn and Tornadus-T. 0 Speed IVs and EVs and a Relaxed nature can be used for a slower Flip Turn, underspeeding Pokemon like Clefable to better bring in wallbreakers like Aerodactyl.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Toxic may be used over anything but Power Whip to pressure Mantine and Slowbro, and Poison Jab makes Seismitoad a Tapu Bulu lure. Scald is also an option to threaten switch-ins such as Tapu Bulu and cripple Pokemon expecting a setup opportunity like Garchomp and Scizor. Assault Vest may be used over Leftovers to handle special attackers such as Kingdra, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Fini better, but the lack of Leftovers recovery lessens Seismitoad's ability to check threats such as Urshifu-R and Azumarill in the long run.

Offensive (Ground).description:
Seismitoad's ability to outspeed and remove threats such as Belly Drum Azumarill and Crawdaunt gives it a niche as a Water-immune Pokemon for Ground teams. Compared to its main competition, Gastrodon, Seismitoad trades longevity and walling potential for utility, Speed, and offensive presence. Substitute takes advantage of foes locked into a Water-type move such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Choice Band Barraskewda, as well as passive, status-reliant Pokemon such as Rotom-W and Toxapex. Power Whip deals heavy damage to Water-types, notably KOing Azumarill after it has used Belly Drum, Crawdaunt after Stealth Rock damage, and Urshifu-R after a Close Combat Defense drop. Power Whip also deters Calm Mind Tapu Fini and Keldeo from using Seismitoad as setup fodder. Earthquake threatens Poison- and Steel-types such as Toxapex, Dragalge, and Magnezone. Knock Off deals with Ghost-types and removes items from switch-ins such as Tapu Bulu, Zapdos, and Zarude. 104 Speed EVs with an Adamant nature allow Seismitoad to beat Adamant Crawdaunt and Adamant Azumarill, while the defensive investment lets it survive Close Combat from Choice Band Urshifu-R.

Status, especially Toxic, hinders Seismitoad's ability to pivot against predicted Water-type moves from Urshifu-R and Kingdra. This makes Nidoking an excellent teammate, as it absorbs Toxic Spikes. Nidoking also deals with Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Celesteela and threatens Kommo-o, Tapu Bulu, and Corviknight, which commonly use Seismitoad as setup fodder. Seismitoad's offensive presence makes it a great fit for sand teams, as Choice Band Sand Rush Excadrill appreciates Seismitoad's ability to remove Azumarill and Rotom-W, and in return outspeeds and removes threats such as Kyurem, Zarude, Tapu Bulu, and Tapu Lele. Landorus-T provides a Ground-type immunity and can take Grass-type attacks from Zarude and Choice Specs Jirachi. Mamoswine deals with Flying- and Grass-types such as Galarian Moltres, Zapdos, and Tapu Bulu. It also switches into Freeze-Dry from Alolan Ninetales and Kyurem. In return, Seismitoad switches into Scald from Slowbro and Toxapex. Swords Dance Garchomp pressures Dragon- and Flying-types such as Kyurem, Dragonite, and Corviknight as well.

Swift Swim (Water).description:
Seismitoad is the premier Stealth Rock setter for Swift Swim teams while also providing an Electric-type immunity for the team. Hydro Pump is hard to switch into under rain, and Earth Power is strong Ground-type STAB move for Seismitoad to use. Focus Blast allows Seismitoad to 2HKO Ferrothorn. Grass Knot will enable Seismitoad to take on opposing rain teams with more ease as well as Water-immune Pokemon such as Gastrodon and opposing Seimsitoad, with Hydro Pump being able to take on Ground teams in the rain easily. However, Ferrothorn is harder to break past for the team without Focus Blast. Seismitoad's EV spread allows it to take advantage of the rain to its best ability by being as strong and as fast as possible.

Barraskewda and Gyarados appreciate Seismitoad's ability to set up Stealth Rock as well as help them break past physical walls such as Ferrothorn by wearing them down. Gyarados is also a check to Choice Scarf Gardevoir on rain teams, which poses a considerable threat to Swift Swim Water teams through outspeeding every Pokemon on the type by obtaining Swift Swim through Trace. Furthermore, Barraskewda can take on faster Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion and Gengar under rain. Other wallbreakers such as Keldeo are appreciated as partners as they break down shared checks with Seismitoad and can beat faster Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Indeedee outside of rain. Toxapex is a good partner for Seismitoad as a result of its Grass neutrality as well as its ability to weaken the opposing team by spreading status.

Physical Sweeper.description:
• Sporting a solid typing, colorful coverage, and access to Swift Swim, Seismitoad is a potent rain sweeper that can threaten many common Pokemon in the Series 12 format.

  • Seismitoad's spammable STAB combination allows it to set its own rain with Max Geyser and boost its Special Defense with Max Quake while Dynamaxed, making it more difficult to revenge kill.

  • Power Whip is necessary coverage to break past Water-immune Pokemon and other bulky Water-types, such as Kyogre, Quagsire, and Tapu Fini, with Life Orb-boosted Max Overgrowth OHKOing all three.

  • Brick Break is Seismitoad's best option for a physical Max Knuckle, further preventing Ferrothorn and physically defensive Porygon2 from walling it. Brick Break also allows Seismitoad to remove opposing Light Screen and Reflect for its team.

  • Bounce is Seismitoad's only option for Max Airstream, but the Speed boost can be crucial if rain runs out the following turn, and it heavily damages most Grass-type switch-ins. Notably, it is the only listed move that can damage Shedinja while Seismitoad is Dynamaxed.

  • Ice Punch is Seismitoad's only way to hit Dragonite and defensive Zygarde-C for meaningful damage, maintains coverage against Grass-types, and is its strongest option against Landorus-T outside of rain.

  • At the cost of a coverage option, Seismitoad can set Stealth Rock if its team lacks a setter. Due to its ability to threaten a sweep under rain, Seismitoad can find opportunities to set up Stealth Rock on predicted switches to checks like Ferrothorn, Lapras, and Shedinja.

  • Toxic may seem strange on such an offensive Pokemon, but it supports Seismitoad's team by crippling a potentially troublesome wall, and Seismitoad's threat level tends to draw walls in. Additionally, if Seismitoad forgoes Bounce, Toxic is its only option to defeat Heavy-Duty Boots Shedinja.

  • Kyogre is one of Seismitoad's best teammates, as it can summon rain with Drizzle to kickstart a Seismitoad sweep, and together they can wear down their shared checks.

  • While Seimitoad's power under rain and many coverage options make it difficult to keep in check, it still needs to be wary of Grass- and bulky Water-types. Zapdos makes for a standout partner, threatening them with its accurate STAB Hurricane and Thunder under rain. Urshifu-S pressures the likes of Ferrothorn, Shedinja, and Porygon2, which give Seismitoad trouble.

Items

  • Life Orb is the best item to enable a Seismitoad sweep, granting it high damage output while Dynamaxed despite an only average Attack stat.

  • Choice Band makes Seismitoad worse at Dynamax sweeping, in exchange for OHKOing maximum HP Zacian-C and havng a 70% chance of OHKOing maximum HP Kyogre with Power Whip.

  • However, if Life Orb is already being used by another Pokemon, other viable options include Mystic Water, Rindo Berry, and Expert Belt. Do note that Seismitoad needs either a Life Orb or Expert Belt to OHKO Kyogre with Max Overgrowth.

EV Spreads

  • 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Adamant: Under rain, this EV spread lets Seismitoad outspeed the entire unboosted metagame bar Regieleki, as well as +1 positive-natured base 100s.

  • 116 HP / 252 Atk / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread gives Seismitoad a good chance of surviving a Play Rough from Jolly Zacian-C while still outspeeding Pheromosa and Calyrex-S under rain.

  • 52 HP / 252 Atk / 204 Spe with Adamant: If Seismitoad is holding a Rindo Berry, this EV spread will allow it to survive a Grassy Glide from Choice Band Rillaboom under Dynamax.

Specially Defensive Support.description:
• With its serviceable bulk, great defensive typing, and coveted Water Absorb ability, Seismitoad can act as one of the sturdiest Kyogre switch-ins around while blanket checking the metagame's many Water-types. While it competes with Gastrodon, which sports higher special bulk and access to Recover, Seismitoad's unique utility movepool and access to Grass-type coverage make it less predictable.

  • Stealth Rock is the primary advantage Seismitoad has over many other Water-immune Pokemon, freeing up its teammates to run more offensive sets.

  • Seismitoad's access to Toxic, very valuable and rare for a non-Poison type, is key to put foes on a timer.

  • If holding a Light Ball, Fling becomes a one-time paralysis-inducing move, which can be a nasty surprise for offensive switch-ins that don't mind Toxic but hate the Speed drop from paralysis.

  • If holding Leftovers, Protect allows Seismitoad to restore a bit of additional HP per turn, as well as scouting for potentially devastating Grass-type coverage.

  • Power Whip is an option for more security against bulkier Kyogre variants, particularly those with Substitute + Calm Mind. In general, carrying Grass-type coverage makes Seismitoad a much better check to many threatening Water-types, such as Tapu Fini, Quagsire, and Rotom-W.

  • Rest when paired with Chesto Berry, lets Seismitoad stick around much longer.

Items

  • Light Ball makes Fling a one-time paralysis-inducing move.

  • Leftovers provides Seismitoad with passive recovery each turn, and it synergizes especially well with Protect. Aguav Berry is an alternate healing option.

  • Chesto Berry is required when running Rest, to avoid losing serious momentum while asleep.

EV Spreads

  • The listed 4 Speed EVs allow Fling Seismitoad to outpace paralyzed Cinderace.

  • 212 HP / 4 Atk / 92 Def / 196 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: This EV spread allows Seismitoad to avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, avoid the OHKO from its Play Rough, and survive a Choice Band-boosted Wicked Blow from Urshifu-S.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: This spread maximizes Seismitoad's special bulk, letting it take on Kyogre as well as possible.

  • 228 HP / 4 Atk / 76 Def / 196 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: This spread allows Seismitoad to always survive Timid Life Orb Yveltal's Max Darkness and almost always survive Adamant Zacian-C's Play Rough.

Specially-based Sweeper.description:
• Despite its lower Special Attack stat, Seismitoad can run a specially-based set worth consideration, as Hydro Pump actually outdamages Liquidation against neutral targets, and the ability to catch opponents off guard with a mixed set has tremendous value in a best-of-one format.

  • A Ground-type STAB move lets Seismitoad deal good damage against Zacian-C, with Earthquake doing more against Kyogre and Tyranitar, while Earth Power is less vulnerable to Attack drops via Intimidate or burn.

  • Power Whip nets crucial coverage against Water-immune Pokemon and bulky Water-types. Grass Knot is a feasible alternative, sporting much higher damage against physically-bulky targets like Quagsire. It is significantly weaker against Kyogre and Gastrodon than Power Whip, though, and will fail if the target is Dynamaxed.

  • Focus Blast is Seismitoad's only way of hitting Ferrothorn for significant damage, netting a 2HKO against specially defensive variants outside of Dynamax.

  • Sludge Bomb allows Seismitoad to boost its Special Attack with Max Ooze while Dynamaxed, and it's Seismitoad's strongest option against Rillaboom.

  • Seismitoad can set Stealth Rock if there's not already a setter on its team, but it won't be able to surmount Grass-types.

  • While Toxic may seem out of place on a set designed for sweeping, it is Seismitoad's only shot at beating Chansey, specially defensive Porygon2, and Shedinja, and it can put other troublesome walls on a timer for its team.

Items

  • Life Orb is the best item to enable a Seismitoad sweep, granting it high damage output while Dynamaxed despite its only average attacking stats.

  • However, if Life Orb is already being used by another Pokemon on the team, other viable options include Mystic Water, Assault Vest, and Expert Belt.

EV Spreads

  • 4 Atk / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Mild: Under rain, Seismitoad will outspeed the entire unboosted metagame bar Regieleki, as well as +1 positive-natured base 100s. A Mild nature is preferred over Rash to always survive a Max Geyser from Modest Kyogre while Dynamaxed.

  • A special-only set with a Modest nature can be run if opting for Grass Knot, though such a set struggles even more to break past many of the metagame's special walls.

Stealth Rock.description: Speed investment outspeeds Alolan Marowak.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Throh can run a wallbreaker set with Flame Orb and Facade; however, it lacks a spammable powerful STAB move, since it is limited to Superpower and Storm Throw. Additionally, Sawk and Silvally-Fighting are usually preferred for their higher Speed tiers and better wallbreaking capabilities. Throh can also attempt to use a Bulk Up set with either Mold Breaker or Guts, with the former giving it the ability to ignore Pyukumuku's Unaware; however, Gurdurr is better at this role due to having Drain Punch for recovery and Mach Punch for priority. A physically defensive set is more effective at checking the likes of Silvally formes, Sawk, and Kangaskhan, but Throh struggles to absorb status without a specially defensive spread.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Pokemon like Spiritomb, Rotom, and Gourgeist-XL are immune to Throh's STAB moves and can sponge Knock Off. Spiritomb can set up on Throh, while Rotom and Gourgeist-XL annoy it with status. However, Rotom should be careful switching into Knock Off.

Flying-types: Flying-types like Altaria, Rotom-S, and Cramorant resist Throh's STAB moves and can retaliate back with their super effective STAB moves. However, they despise losing their valuable Heavy-Duty Boots to Knock Off.

Fairy-types: Fairy-types like Alcremie, Galarian Rapidash, and Shiinotic resist Throh's moves and can threaten it with their super effective STAB moves. Although Clefairy cannot break through Throh, it can cripple Throh with Knock Off or pivot with Teleport into a check.

Physical Wallbreakers: Even if Throh's physical bulk is far from lacking, its reliance on Rest lets it often get overwhelmed by physical wallbreakers like Froslass, Silvally formes, and Sawk.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types like Uxie, Swoobat, and Musharna resist Throh's STAB moves, don't take much from Knock Off, and threaten it with their STAB moves or Future Sight. Jynx can also break past Throh, but it cannot safely switch into Throh's attacks.

Special Wall.description:
Throh is a very bulky special wall that works especially well on Spikes-stacking teams. Circle Throw lets it phaze switch-ins, which pairs well with entry hazard support. Knock Off cripples checks like Altaria, Alcremie, and Tangela, hits Ghost-types like Rotom and Gourgeist-S, and removes Heavy-Duty Boots, which is appreciated on entry hazard-stacking teams. Rest is Throh's only form of recovery; thanks to Sleep Talk and Guts, Throh acts as a status absorber and lacks passivity while asleep. The given EV spread lets Throh outspeed uninvested base 50 Speed Pokemon such as Piloswine.

Throh appreciates entry hazard support a lot, especially Spikes from setters such as Qwilfish and Coalossal. Spinblockers like Rotom and Gourgeist formes and fast Taunt users like Alolan Persian, Golbat, and Qwilfish can keep up these entry hazards. Rapid Spin users such as Kabutops and Morpeko also make for great partners. Additionally, most of them help handle physical attackers Throh struggles to beat such as Sawk and Silvally-Poison. Despite being a good special wall, Throh appreciates being paired with Pokemon that can handle Volt Switch like Stunfisk and Manectric; they prevent it from getting chipped by Electric-types like Rotom, Manectric, and Raichu and losing momentum.

pu.overview: Among the myriad of Fighting-types in PU, Sawk tries to stand out thanks to its above average Speed tier that allows it to overcome certain threats of the tier such as Gallade, Mesprit, and Magmortar. Sawk also has very good coverage, its movepool including moves like Knock Off, Poison Jab, Stone Edge, and Earthquake which, coupled with its access to Mold Breaker allow it to defeat the most common switch-ins to other Fighting-types, such as Weezing, Charizard, and Whimsicott. Sawk is very frail though, but this problem can be handled thanks to its ability Sturdy, allowing it to survive a hit from full HP and retaliate, making it a dangerous threat to offensive archetypes. However, it has no real defensive utility, and nothing in its movepool pushes it over the edge, so Fighting-types such as Poliwrath and Gallade are often preferred over it.

Choice Attacker.description: This set makes switching into Sawk's Close Combat a really difficult task that only a few pokemon such as Aromatisse, Uxie, and Weezing can afford to accomplish. But Sawk's coverage makes up for that problem: Earthquake, paired with its ability Mold Breaker allows it to beat Weezing with Earthquake and eases prediction against Rotom, while Knock Off is good for getting rid of items, as well as hitting Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Mesprit, Doublade, and Gourgeist-S. Poison Jab rounds off the set, hitting Fairy-types such as Aromatisse and Ribombee super effectively. Sawk greatly appreciates teammates that are capable of bringing it in against Pokemon like Gigalith, Regirock, and Aggron with pivoting moves, such as Archeops and Togedemaru. Cleaners such as Ribombee really appreciate Sawk's ability to get rid of their counters such as Regirock, Gigalith, and Weezing, and Ribombee can also set up Sticky Web, making Sawk a lot harder to revenge kill. However, if Sticky Web is not set up, Sawk is rather easy to revenge kill and needs a strong defensive core to back it up. Therefore, hazard setters like Weezing and Gigalith also make for good partners, improving Sawk’s wallbreaking potential.

Sturdy Boots.description: This set makes good use of Sawk's Sturdy ability and Heavy-Duty Boots keeping it intact. Knock Off is its main coverage option, allowing it to deal good damage to Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Jellicent and Mesprit. Knock Off can also make Sawk a lot harder to revenge kill by getting rid of Choice Scarf from Pokémon such as Mesprit. Poison Jab hits Fairy-types such as Silvally-Fairy and Ribombee super effectively, and Earthquake deals good damage to Neutralizing Gas Weezing and Lanturn. This Sawk set works particularly well on offensive teams thanks to its ability to stop sweeps, as it is able to revenge kill a lot of threats such as Lycanroc and Ribombee. Cleaners such as Ribombee and Silvally-Ghost really appreciate Sawk's ability to wear down their checks such as Sandaconda and Weezing.

zu.comments:
Other Options

An Adamant nature can be run on its non-Choice Scarf sets to have a better chance to 2HKO Tangela lacking its Eviolite, however a Jolly nature is usually preferred to outspeed the likes of Timid Skuntank and Modest Thievul.

Poison Jab lets Sawk 2HKO Alcremie and Clefairy, but this requires giving up one of its other coverage moves, which generally isn't preferred because they target more Pokemon.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Spiritomb, Gourgeist-XL, and Sableye can switch into any of Sawk's attacks with ease. Spiritomb can also set up on Sawk with Calm Mind.

Physical Walls: Tangela, Uxie, and Altaria can switch into Sawk and either cripple it with status or deal significant damage. However, Tangela and Altaria must be careful of switching into Knock Off and Stone Edge, respectively, as Choice Band and Black Belt Sawk can 2HKO Tangela lacking Eviolite and can KO Altaria with some prior chip damage. While Qwilfish must be wary of switching into Earthquake, it can easily switch into Close Combat and wear Sawk down with its Rocky Helmet.

Faster Threats: Rotom, Jynx, and Froslass can revenge kill Sawk once it's slightly worn down; however, none of them can directly switch into Sawk's attacks.

Choice Scarf.description:
With a solid Speed tier and its incredibly high attacking power, Sawk makes for an excellent revenge killer that fits well on offense and balance teams. Choice Scarf allows Sawk to threaten foes such as Alolan Persian, Kangaskhan, and Froslass. Knock Off targets Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Rotom, Gourgeist-S, and Uxie while also crippling common switch-ins such as Alcremie, Clefairy, and Tangela. Earthquake hits Poison-types such as Silvally-Poison, Qwilfish, and Skuntank. Stone Edge lets Sawk deal with Flying-types such as Rotom-S, Altaria, and Golbat. Mold Breaker allows Sawk to hit Levitate users such as Uxie and Rotom with Earthquake. Alternatively, Inner Focus allows Sawk to beat Qwilfish with Earthquake, as Inner Focus nullifies its Intimidate, and not flinch from Kangaskhan's Fake Out. However, don't expect to get free turns from Kangaskhan trying to flinch you, as the opponent should notice the absent Mold Breaker activation message.

While Sawk has super effective coverage for Pokemon that resist or are immune to Close Combat, it still needs physical walls such as Uxie, Tangela, and Altaria to be weakened in order to KO them and successfully clean. Therefore, special attackers such as Skuntank, Rotom, and Jynx that can deal with them make for great partners. Entry hazard setters such as Rhydon, Piloswine, and Qwilfish help to wear down Sawk's common switch-ins, as most do not have access to reliable recovery. Pivots such as Uxie, Rotom-S, and Alolan Persian circumvent Sawk's mediocre bulk by safely bringing it onto the field, with the former also having access to Future Sight, which dissuades Poison-types from switching in.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Sawk forgoes Choice Scarf's increase in Speed for more wallbreaking power, letting Close Combat net 2HKOs on neutral physical walls like Pyukumuku and Gurdurr. Knock Off pressures Ghost- and Psychic-types like Rotom and Uxie while also crippling common switch-ins such as Tangela; Close Combat threatens a 2HKO on Tangela once its Eviolite has been removed. Earthquake punishes Poison-types like Qwilfish and Silvally-Poison, while Stone Edge nails Flying-types such as Rotom-S and Altaria.

Choice Band Sawk is vulnerable to being revenge killed by faster Flying- and Psychic-types such as Rotom-S and Jynx, so switch-ins such as Rhydon and Articuno are appreciated. These Pokemon also have the added benefit of providing entry hazards to help wear down its switch-ins. Special setup sweepers such as Ninetales and Alcremie benefit greatly from Sawk's ability to break past specially defensive walls such as Coalossal and Miltank. Sawk also appreciates the removal of Ghost-types, so pairing it with Dark-types like Skuntank, Shiftry, and Alolan Persian is a good idea. Future Sight Uxie is a great partner, as it punishes the physical walls such as Tangela and Altaria that switch in on Sawk and can also pivot Sawk in safely with U-turn. Sawk can also weaken the aforementioned walls into the KO range of physical cleaners like Rapidash and Swords Dance Silvally formes.

All-Out Attacker.description:
With its all-out attacker set, Sawk can bluff a Choice item and surprise its foe with a powerful Black Belt-boosted Close Combat or a super effective coverage move. Knock Off targets Ghost- and Psychic-types like Rotom, Froslass, and Exeggutor, while also crippling checks like Altaria and Tangela. Stone Edge handles Flying-types like Altaria, Rotom-S, and Articuno, whereas Poison Jab deals significant damage to Fairy-types like Alcremie, Clefairy, and Galarian Rapidash. Earthquake lets Sawk break Poison-types like Qwilfish and Silvally-Poison. Black Belt 2HKOes Tangela lacking Eviolite with Close Combat after Stealth Rock. Mold Breaker lets Sawk use Earthquake on Levitate users like Rotom and Uxie, while Inner Focus makes it immune to Qwilfish's Intimidate and prevents Kangaskhan from chipping it down with Fake Out.

All-out attacking Sawk can cripple and weaken physical walls like Tangela, Poliwrath, and Altaria to open a way for physical sweepers like Swords Dance Lycanroc-N, Shift Gear Klinklang, and Thwackey. Pivots like Rotom, Clefairy, and Alolan Persian can bring Sawk safely on to the field. Entry hazard setters like Froslass, Piloswine, and Rhydon can force out Sawk's checks like Altaria, Alcremie, and Silvally-Poison and help Sawk wallbreak, while Sawk can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from its checks with Knock Off to make entry hazards more effective against them.

Spikes Setter.description: Venipede's ability to outspeed common entry hazard removers and match up well against common leads, such as Mienfoo and Abra, give it a niche in LC as a Spikes setter on hyper offense. Pin Missile and Endeavor further let Venipede weaken foes for its teammates. The EVs allow Venipede to outspeed the unboosted metagame at +1 Speed while also surviving some powerful attacks, such as Natu's Psychic. Strong attackers like Abra, Carvanha, and Ponyta benefit from Spikes wearing down their checks such as Ferroseed and Mareanie. Partners such as Pawniard and Staryu, which can pressure Natu, are also very useful to have.

Suicide Lead.description:
Scolipede is able to get Spikes up easily for hyper offense teams with its Speed and can keep them up with its coverage and Endeavor. Poison Jab notably hits Hatterene hard while also hitting neutral targets like Azelf, Hydreigon, and Thundurus-T for solid damage. Earthquake dissuades Cobalion from setting up on Scolipede and nails Rapid Spin users like Tentacruel and Excadrill. Endeavor is useful against bulkier Pokemon such as Chansey, as well as Defog users like Salamence. Speed Boost stops lead Excadrill from spinning away Spikes and outspeeding Scolipede afterwards. It also lets Scolipede set multiple layers of Spikes against Choice Scarf users like Diggersby and Hydreigon. Focus Sash ensures Scolipede can get at least one layer of Spikes and can bring foes down to low HP with Endeavor.

Scolipede is only used on hyper offense and pairs nicely with Stealth Rock setters like Taunt Krookodile and Meteor Beam Necrozma, forming a double entry hazard-stacking core to enable sweepers like Gyarados and Salamence. Krookodile and Necrozma can pressure entry hazard removers like Salamence and Dhelmise better than Scolipede can. Sweepers like Salamence, Scizor, and Azelf all appreciate entry hazards to muscle past foes such as Primarina and Chansey. While Scolipede can keep up some offensive pressure, it is still setup bait for Pokemon like Scizor, Celesteela, and Salamence, making checks to them such as Gyarados, Nihilego, and Azumarill respectively solid partners. Taunt Gyarados, Polteageist, and Thundurus-T can all set up on Skarmory, who may try to set up Spikes against Scolipede since it cannot threaten it.

Memento.description: Cottonee has good support moves and Prankster, which allows it to provide opportunities for setup sweepers on hyper offense teams with Memento. Cottonee's typing lets it check some of the biggest issues for hyper offense teams in Mienfoo and Grookey. It also enables Grookey by luring and crippling Ferroseed and Koffing with Knock Off. Encore and Defog give Cottonee a bit more flexibility by allowing it to provide additional setup opportunities for teammates and help teammates such as Tyrunt switch in safely. Cottonee pairs well with Memento Diglett as a secondary Memento user; together, they can provide setup opportunities for multiple setup sweepers. The best teammate for Cottonee is a setup sweeper whose setup it facilitates, like Swords Dance Grookey and Tyrunt.

pu.overview: Whimsicott is a very versatile Pokemon; its good offensive Fairy typing and immaculate Speed tier let it revenge kill Pokemon such as Swords Dance Gallade, and it has a defensive presence with its great typing, Prankster, and ability to annoy opposing Pokemon with status moves. It is difficult to play around due to the unpredictability that comes with the great variety of sets it can run and its Speed. However, Whimsicott lacks the Special Attack and coverage to deal much damage. This makes it rely on utility and status moves to disrupt foes. It also lacks great defensive stats to constantly check threats such as Regirock.

Offensive.description: U-turn is used to get Whimsicott out of bad matchups, especially after using Switcheroo, when its power is lower. Psychic hits Poison-types very hard, doing massive amounts of damage to Weezing and Garbodor, while being a reliable way to hit Fire-types neutrally. Hurricane hits Fire-types harder, 2HKOing Centiskorch and usually 2HKOing offensive Charizard, but is much less reliable than Psychic. Switcheroo is used to disrupt defensive cores, as Whimsicott can force in a Pokemon such as Charizard or Togedemaru that would otherwise wall it and limit the Pokemon's counterplay by giving it Choice Specs. Pixie Plate is an alternative to Choice Specs that sacrifices strength for flexibility, making prediction less of a factor. Whimsicott offensively pairs well with Pokemon that break Fire- and Steel-types, most notably Fighting-type Pokemon that can run Rock-type coverage such as Gurdurr and Sawk. Defensively, it appreciates support from Steel-types such as Aggron and Togedemaru to switch into Poison-, Flying-, and Ice-type moves, as well as a bulky Water-types such as Jellicent and Lanturn to handle Fire- and Steel-types. With U-turn, Whimsicott can form a solid VoltTurn core with the latter partner.

Utility.description: Knock Off allows Whimsicott to remove important items such as Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from defensive Pokemon such as Audino and Charizard, making them much less effective at checking offensive threats, while Prankster Encore deals with offensive Pokemon such as Silvally-Ghost and Frosmoth by locking them into a setup move. U-turn is a crucial move for this set, allowing Whimsicott to let wallbreakers such as Lycanroc and Aggron in on its answers like Charizard and Togedemaru, respectively. Stun Spore provides speed control against fast Pokemon such as Ribombee on the switch so that Pokemon such as Gallade can sweep much more easily. Leech Seed gives Whimsicott a form of recovery, allowing it to exploit defensive Pokemon to increase its longevity. Whimsicott pairs very well with Pokemon that like its usual Steel-, Fire-, and Flying-type switch-ins crippled, such as Frosmoth.

SubSeed.description: This set uses Prankster to its fullest potential, catching opposing Pokemon with a Leech Seed and then using Substitute before they can act. The combination of Leftovers and Leech Seed recovery almost makes up for the HP loss of using Substitute every turn, slowly draining the opposing Pokemon's HP until it's in range of a Moonblast.
