Psychic can be used to annoy Poison-types that can easily break its Substitute, while Knock Off is used to disrupt defensive Pokemon with recovery that can stall Leech Seed. Encore can be used to prevent setup Pokemon such as Ribombee from taking advantage of this set's passive nature while also stalling out the recovery of defensive Pokemon such as Wishiwashi. This set struggles most against Grass-types such as Tangela and Ferroseed, and Whimsicott must be wary of moves such as Dual Wingbeat from Archeops that both break its Substitute and damage it. Defensively, Whimsicott needs Pokemon such as Aggron and Galarian Stunfisk that can tank hits from Pokemon that can get past its Substitute, and these teammates can also benefit from the passive recovery that Leech Seed gives them. It also benefits from Flying- and Fire-types such as Charizard and Magmortar that deal with the Grass-types it struggles against.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Grass

Whimsicott can run a Substitute + Leech Seed set, but this set is generally inconsistent due to the opponent's ability to simply switch out. Choice Band and Choice Specs can be run on Whimsicott to cripple walls like Celesteela and Toxapex with Switcheroo and break past foes like Gengar and Galarian Moltres more easily. Infiltrator Whimsicott can get past Kyurem and Hydreigon's substitutes, but this isn't recommended; without Prankster + Encore, Whimsicott cannot lock Speed-boosting sweepers like Volcarona and Dragonite into their setup moves. U-turn can also be run on the utility set over Knock Off or Encore to preserve momentum. Whimsicott can run Sunny Day with Chlorophyll Venusaur as a partner, but this doesn't follow the ideal Grass team structure.

Utility (Grass).description:
The utility provided by Stun Spore, Knock Off, and Encore makes Whimsicott a staple on Grass teams. Stun Spore functions as speed control, paralyzing fast, threatening foes such as Tornadus-T and Choice Scarf Heatran. Encore punishes setup sweepers like Volcarona, Scizor, and Dragonite and status moves from threats like SubRoost Kyurem. Knock Off provides a huge amount of utility, allowing Whimsicott to remove key items from foes like Dragalge, Toxapex, and Celesteela. Moonblast threatens Dark-types that are immune to Prankster, such as Hydreigon and Zarude; it also threatens Dragon- and Fighting-types like Kyurem, Kommo-o, and Bewear. The given EV spread allows Whimsicott to outspeed Choice Specs Gengar and Latios in order to remove their items. The rest of Whimsicott's EVs are spread over Special Attack and HP to make Moonblast as powerful as possible while helping Whimsicott's decent natural bulk. Whimsicott can also opt for an EV spread of 208 HP / 92 SpA / 208 Spe in order to switch into Bulk Up Corviknight's Brave Bird. Heavy-Duty Boots is the preferred item, as Grass teams often lack entry hazard control; however, Pixie Plate can be used to boost the power of Whimsicott's Moonblast, giving it a greater offensive presence.

All of Whimsicott's teammates appreciate its ability to prevent setup sweepers like Volcarona, Clefable, and SubRoost Kyurem from brutalizing the team. Choice Band Rillaboom is a phenomenal teammate for Whimsicott, as it can deal with walls like Toxapex for Whimsicott. In return, Whimsicott can take on Dark- and Dragon-type Pokemon for Rillaboom, such as Galarian Moltres and Kommo-o. Bulk Up Zarude is an excellent teammate for Whimsicott, as Whimsicott can Encore foes like Volcarona which can lead to setup opportunities. Whimsicott can also paralyze foes like Spectrier and Choice Scarf Gengar, allowing Zarude to OHKO them with Darkest Lariat. Ferrothorn not only checks terrifying Ice-types like Weavile and Kyurem for Whimsicott, but it provides Spikes support to make it easier for Whimsicott to defeat foes like Cobalion. Cradily checks special attackers, such as Nidoking, Galarian Slowking, and Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and sets Stealth Rock to wear down foes like Galarian Zapdos so that Whimsicott can KO them. Amoonguss is also a good teammate, as it can absorb Toxic Spikes for the team; it also provides the team with a physical wall capable of dealing with Tapu Bulu and Dragapult.

Sunny Day (Grass).description:
Whimsicott is a staple on Grass teams that rely on the sun, as it is one of the best setters thanks to Prankster and can pivot into its teammates to take advantage of sun with Memento and U-turn. Sunny Day sets up the sun for teammates such as Venusaur, Shiftry, and Celebi to take advantage of. Moonblast allows Whimsicott to nail Dragon-type Pokemon such as Kommo-o and Hydreigon. U-turn allows it to bring in its teammates to take advantage of the sun. Encore prevents Whimsicott from becoming setup bait for sweepers such as Bulk Up Corviknight. Memento does the same thing as U-turn; however, it allows Whimsicott to safely bring in a setup sweeper such as Venusaur with a free opportunity to set up. Heat Rock increases the number of sun turns and Prankster gives Sunny Day and Memento priority. Whimsicott should set up sun multiple times throughout the match, and when it's time for a teammate to sweep or Whimsicott is low on health, it should reset the sun and then give it a setup opportunity with Memento.

Teammates that take advantage of the sun such as Venusaur, Celebi, and Shiftry appreciate Whimsicott's ability to set it up, and all of its teammates appreciate its ability to take on Dragon-type Pokemon thanks to Moonblast. Thanks to the sun, Venusaur and Shiftry's Speed is doubled with Chlorophyll, allowing them to fire off attacks faster and become revenge killers. Weather Ball users such as Venusaur and Celebi especially appreciate the sun, as it makes the move Fire type to nail Steel-type Pokemon such as Corviknight and Ferrothorn. Choice Scarf Virizion acts as a revenge killer that takes on threats such as Choice Scarf Charizard and Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan for the team. It also provides a way to take on the most common hail and sand setters in Alolan Ninetales and Tyranitar thanks to its coverage in Smart Strike and Close Combat. Alongside Whimsicott, Ferrothorn makes up the support for weather-based Grass teams as the team's way of setting entry hazards, allowing the teams sweepers to more easily muscle through the opposing team.

vgc2022.overview: Whimsicott's Prankster Tailwind and lightning-fast playstyle make it a perfect choice for hyper offense teams, particularly those featuring Calyrex-S as a Restricted Pokemon. Due to the combination of Prankster and its high base Speed of 116, Whimsicott is the most reliable Tailwind setter in the metagame, making it a crucial pick for those that rely on moving first. It also comes armed with a bevy of support moves which allow it to fill all kinds of niches that very specific teams or cores may require, like fast Taunt, Sunny Day, or even the dreaded Switcheroo + Eject Button combo to disrupt opposing Dynamax users. Its Fairy-type attacks also pressure Dark-types like Yveltal and Grimmsnarl that are often used to counter Calyrex-S. However, Whimsicott does have glaring flaws; first and foremost, fast Tailwind is utterly ruined if the opponent is able to set up Trick Room. It also has to worry about being stopped in its tracks by Fake Out. Whimsicott's offensive presence is generally middling, so it relies on the power of partners like Calyrex-S, Kyogre, Kartana, and Regieleki to deal damage, often supported by its Helping Hand. This is a double-edged sword, however, as if its partner goes down during the turn, both it and its partner's efforts are effectively wasted.
vgc2022.comments:
Other Options

Coba Berry is helpful for allowing Whimsicott to survive a Max Airstream if your team's Focus Sash is already taken; however, this makes Whimsicott much easier to KO. Encore is useful for locking opponents into unfavorable moves like Protect and Trick Room, but optimal conditions don't always come up for it to be used, and it can be blocked by Psychic Terrain. Sunny Day can be used in its last moveslot to help check Kyogre, but Protect is generally more useful. Other speed control options like Trick Room and Cotton Spore can also turn the tables in Tailwind mirror matches.

Prankster Support.description:
• Moonblast is Whimsicott's best option for single-target damage, but spread Dazzling Gleam allows Whimsicott to put more damage on the board as a whole. Energy Ball can be used on Kyogre teams as a means to hit Gastrodon.

  • Prankster Tailwind is nearly guaranteed to go up, making Whimsicott a vital component of hyper offense teams where speed is everything.

  • Helping Hand is a universally beneficial way for Whimsicott to boost its ally's offensive pressure instead of relying on its relatively weak Fairy coverage.

  • Taunt can disrupt the opponent's attempts to counter Whimsicott such as Trick Room and opposing Tailwind.

  • Focus Sash preserves Whimsicott for a future Tailwind or Helping Hand support, as its middling defenses leave it OHKOed by the majority of the metagame's attacks otherwise.

Utility.description:
Being the fastest Prankster Pokemon in the game with a deep supportive movepool, Whimsicott establishes itself as one of the best utility Pokemon in the current metagame. Prankster allows Whimsicott to have a priority Tailwind, allowing it to boost its team's Speed against faster restricted Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Calyrex-S, while gen 8’s dynamic speed mechanics make Tailwind users like Whimsicott very potent. Moonblast is able to deal good damage to Fairy-weak Pokemon such as Urshifu-S. Taunt allows Whimsicott to prevent Trick Room from Porygon2 and Mimikyu as well as Venusaur's Sleep Powder, Amoonguss's Spore, and Rotom-H's Will-O-Wisp. Helping Hand allows Whimsicott to still play a supportive role while facing common Fake Out Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom while also making up for Whimsicott's lack of offensive presence. Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to take a move which it wouldn't be able to. Alternatively, the combination of Switcheroo and Eject Button can be run to get rid of your opponent's Dynamax if properly timed.

Whimsicott usually plays a supportive role on the team enabling common partners like Calyrex-S, Thundurus,and Charizard to excel with its supportive moves. Whimsicott is able to provide Tailwind and Cotton Spore for Calyrex-S while also keeping Dark-types such as Urshifu-S in check. Thundurus is able to take care of Incineroar for Whimsicott while Whimscott provides Helping Hand. Charizard and Whimsicott synergize well due to Whimsicott providing Charizard with Sunny Day and Fake Tears while Charizard keeps Zacian-C in check for Whimsicott.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Prankster Support.description:
• This Whimsicott functions to help hyper offensive or setup sweeper-centered builds set up against faster foes.

  • Tailwind is used to boost Speed while sacrificing Whimsicott, allowing the incoming Pokemon to take advantage of the Speed boost.

  • Alternatively, Switcheroo in combination with Lagging Tail makes the foe setup fodder for certain sweepers that can take advantage of slowed Pokemon to rack up boosts.

  • Memento allows Whimsicott to freely pivot against opposing Pokemon after setting up speed control. Memento finds usefulness in guaranteeing one turn of Dynamax stalling, avoiding opposing boosts from secondary effects of Max Moves or Moxie, and also neutering Dynamax sweepers via attacking stat drops.

  • Moonblast is Whimsicott's primary STAB move, hitting Dark types, which are not affected by Prankster, hard. Energy Ball also makes a decent STAB, letting Whimsicott deal serious damage to Tapu Fini and Rotom-W.

  • Taunt prevents Whimsicott from being Taunted itself as well as shuts down more passive Pokemon such as Swampert and Hippowdon. Charm stifles physical Pokemon without needing to sacrifice Whimsicott via Memento.

Items

  • Focus Sash lets Whimsicott survive even powerful attacks, ensuring it can support your offensive Pokemon.

  • Lagging Tail should only be used with Switcheroo.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: This is used with attacking sets and Focus Sash to give Whimsicott the ability to hit hard when using Moonblast or Energy Ball. Timid is an alternate option for outspeeding Garchomp.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with a Bold nature: This maximizes physical bulk in order to get off a Switcheroo or Fling followed by Memento without getting OHKOed and should be used for all non-attacking variants.

Cotton Guard Stall.description:
• This Whimsicott takes advantage of Prankster to set up Cotton Guard, allowing it to stop even would-be physical checks, such as Metagross, that may try to switch in.

  • Prankster Substitute + Leech Seed serves as its main method of defeating opposing Pokemon, stalling them out while passively sapping HP through Leech Seed and healing through Leftovers.

  • While it might be possible to run a no-attack variant of this version of Whimsicott, Moonblast is strongly recommended in order to hit Dark-types, which are unaffected by Prankster, and to ensure that Whimsicott is not complete Taunt bait.

  • The given EV spread maximizes physical bulk in order to Leech Seed stall most effectively and take minimal damage from physical threats immediately after a Cotton Guard boost.

doublesou.overview: Whimsicott has a usable niche as a decent support Pokemon, but it's seriously lacking in every other department. Its Prankster ability lets it to make excellent use of its wide support movepool, which includes moves like Fake Tears, Encore and Taunt, but most notably Tailwind. Prankster Tailwind is a great tool, as it immediately enables many strong attackers, and it can even be consistently set while opposing speed control is up, which is invaluable to the Hyper Offense teams Whimsicott is usually found on. Pokemon like Heatran, Urshifu-R, Zygarde, and Landorus especially appreciate Whimsicott's support, and the latter two can threaten the Fire-types, like Incineroar, that Whimsicott hates. Heatran and Landorus further benefit from Fake Tears. Whimiscott also has limited defensive utility, as its typing allows it to switch in on the likes of Rillaboom, Zygarde, and Urshifu-R, although its poor defenses make this risky. This same bad bulk, alongside its overall poor typing, means Whimsicott has trouble setting Tailwind multiple times, as it struggles to stay in for multiple turns or switch back in after leaving the field. Whimsicott also has difficulty against teams with Psychic Terrain or Tsareena, both of which negate most of its support movepool, bar Tailwind. Finally, Whimsicott faces competition from other Tailwind setters such as Naganadel and Mew. The former possesses powerful offensive pressure, and the latter has a massive support movepool, which includes Fake Out, and fantastic bulk, which makes setting Tailwind multiple times a cinch.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Memento cripples attackers until they switch and provides momentum, which can be invaluable on hyper offense teams. However, it doesn't provide as much utility as Whimsicott's other moves while also sacrificing it on use.

Prankster Support.description:
• Prankster Tailwind is Whimiscott's main niche, allowing it to instantly provide speed control for a teammate like Urshifu-R, Zygarde, or Heatran.

  • Taunt can be used to prevent status moves like Tailwind and Trick Room from opposing Pokemon, while Encore lock the foe into an unfavorable move, like Protect, Fake Out, or Tailwind. Both greatly benefit from Prankster's priority.

  • Moonblast allows Whimiscott to decently check Zygarde and Urshifu-R while also providing chip damage for its team.

  • Fake Tears further supports special attackers such as Heatran and Landorus by helping them break through bulkier Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Porygon2.

  • Protect allows Whimiscott to block Fake Out and preserve its Focus Sash.

  • Focus Sash guarantees Whimsicott can take a hit, which can allow it to get a support move off after setting Tailwind or a second Tailwind later.

  • A Timid nature allows Whimsicott to Speed tie with other Whimsicott, in addition to outspeeding Landorus. 252 HP EVs can be used if Moonblast isn't used.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Lilligant can utilize Choice Specs to dish out strong Petal Dances without the fear of confusion due to Own Tempo. Choice Specs Lilligant also has a free moveslot for Healing Wish, one of the best support moves in the game. However, Lilligant still struggles to break through the same Grass-resistant Pokemon it did before and cannot incapacitate them with sleep.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Articuno and Altaria counter Lilligant due to their superb special bulk and, in Altaria’s case, its 4x resistance to Grass and Natural Cure. Other Flying-types such as Silvally-Flying and Rotom-S still fair quite well, although they are more prone to being overwhelmed by Lilligant due to their lack of longevity and, in the case of Silvally-Flying, its lack of Heavy-Duty Boots.

Fire- and Poison-types: Fire- and Poison-types such as Rapidash, Ninetales, and Silvally-Poison resist both Giga Drain and Pollen Puff. However, Lilligant is able to overwhelm them with a few Quiver Dance boots.

Klinklang: Klinklang also resists all of Lilligant’s attacks and is an excellent sleep absorber on Choice sets that utilize Sleep Talk as a fourth move. Klinklang doesn’t have any reliable recovery options, so it must be kept reasonably healthy to reliably check Lilligant.

Sap Sipper: Sap Sipper Miltank and Bouffalant are immune to Lilligant’s Grass moves and can either put Lilligant on a timer with Toxic or outright KO it.

Revenge Killers: Lilligant is slower than most Choice Scarf users such as Manectric, Gourgeist-S, and Jynx after a Quiver Dance and is prone to being easily revenge killed.

Quiver Dance.description:
Lilligant is a niche Quiver Dance sweeper that capitalizes on Sleep Powder generating one or two free turns to boost and break through the opposing team. Pollen Puff nails opposing Grass-types such as Appletun, Exeggutor, and Tangela. Life Orb gives Lilligant more firepower, which it desperately needs; however, Leftovers provides Lilligant with passive recovery, which can help it acquire Quiver Dance boosts against more passive foes such as Galarian Stunfisk. While this set isn't intended to take advantage of Chlorophyll, Lilligant provides some counterplay versus opposing sun sweepers, notably Shiftry.

Fighting-types such as Sawk and Gurdurr do a fantastic job of scaring out Klinklang, one of Lilligant's biggest checks, and can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Flying-types such as Articuno and Altaria. Similarly, Ice-types such as Jynx and Froslass force out opposing Flying-types and can help Lilligant chip away at Klinklang and Fire-types like Rapidash and Ninetales. Both examples of offensive partners, however, result in overlapping weaknesses, limiting Lilligant's use to only offensive teams. Entry hazard setters such as Uxie, Qwilfish, and Froslass can provide Lilligant with the necessary chip damage needed to whittle down foes it struggles against. Pokemon such as Silvally-Dark and Choice Scarf Kabutops can also offensively pressure common Defog users for Lilligant.

pu.overview: With a solid Speed tier, Adaptability, and a STAB pivoting move in Flip Turn, Basculin secures its niche as a decent pivot in the tier. A Choice Scarf Basculin can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, as well as some boosted Pokemon like Choice Scarf Mesprit and +1 Silvally-Ghost. Its decent offensive stats allow it to hit hard physically while packing a solid Ice Beam for a few physical walls, like Tangela. However, Basculin lacks ways around common Water-resistant foes like Jellicent and Eldegoss, forcing it to pivot out most times. It is also frail, limiting its ability to come in on Pokemon it would otherwise force out, like Charizard and Gigalith. Since it pivots so much, it is prone to racking up chip damage from entry hazards, Iron Barbs, and Rocky Helmet. Finally, despite having a good Speed tier, it cannot deal with Unburden + Grassy Seed users like Thievul and Hitmonlee, so it pales in comparison to Choice Scarf Ribombee on that front.

Choice Scarf.description: Crunch lets Basculin hit Jellicent super effectively, which is especially useful against Water Absorb variants, since they keep it from simply pivoting out. Superpower hits Ferroseed harder than anything else Basculin has, Ice Beam outdamages the recovery from Tangela's Regenerator—even with a Jolly nature—and Aqua Jet picks off faster foes like +1 Ninjask. Basculin struggles heavily with Water-resistant Pokemon and physically defensive walls, but it preys upon common special walls like Audino and Gigalith: partners like Galarian Articuno and Vikavolt pair well with Basculin, as they can come in on Basculin's checks, and Basculin can force out the special walls that check them. They also appreciate Basculin bringing them in with Flip Turn, forming a solid offensive pivoting core with it. Entry hazard setters like Sandslash can help Basculin wear down switch-ins like Tangela and Ferroseed, as they do not run Heavy-Duty Boots; this also helps Basculin clean late-game. Entry hazard removers like Eldegoss and the aforementioned Sandslash are equally important, as Basculin is constantly taking damage from entry hazards otherwise.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

Krokorok can also carry Toxic on its sets to better wear down switch-ins like Tangela and Gurdurr.

Checks and Counters

Gurdurr: Gurdurr counters both Krokorok set by being able to switch in repeatedly and OHKOing it with STAB attacks. Furthermore, Gurdurr can remove Stealth Rock through Defog.

Grass-types: Thwackey and Tangela have no trouble switching into Krokorok and OHKOing it with their STAB attacks.

Physical Walls: Clefairy, Machoke, and Charjabug can usually switch into Krokorok multiple times and block its progress.

Special Wallbreakers: Lead Krokorok relies on Intimidate and its moderate Speed to secure Stealth Rock, so faster special attackers like Focus Blast Electabuzz, fast Tangela, and Lampent can take it out. However, none can switch into Krokorok and greatly fear the Choice Scarf set.

Revenge Killers: Pokemon like Choice Scarf Raboot and Shell Smash Wartortle are able to revenge kill Krokorok with strong coverage.

KrokoRocks (Stealth Rock Lead).description:
Krokorok provides Stealth Rock and early momentum as a lead. Hattrem is ineffective as a form of entry hazard prevention due to it fearing a STAB Knock Off, while Taunt targets Defog users like Vullaby and Togetic. Taunt also prevents opposing entry hazards such as Stealth Rock from Galarian Corsola and Piloswine, Sticky Web from Charjabug, Toxic Spikes from Koffing, and Spikes from Ferroseed. Intimidate along with Krokorok's defensive investment allows it to survive an attack followed by priority when up against Piloswine and Machoke. The remaining Speed investment and a Jolly nature let Krokorok outspeed Modest Roselia along with other slower attackers like Lampent and Marshtomp.

Use Krokorok as a lead and supplement it with offensive teammates that preserve the momentum it gains early-game. Sweepers like Thwackey and Lampent appreciate Stealth Rock pressuring Vullaby, as well as Knock Off both weakening Marshtomp, Piloswine, and Galarian Corsola. Roselia is particularly potent as a partner, not only for providing additional entry hazard pressure with Spikes, but also for checking threats to Krokorok like Thwackey, Tangela, Wartortle. Faster attackers like Raboot and Thwackey revenge kill Krokorok and are immune to entry hazard damage with Magic Guard and Heavy-Duty Boots, respectively. It is best then to pair Krokorok with cleaners like Klang, Wartortle, and Fraxure to deal with them, as well as forms of speed control such as Hattrem and Charjabug. To help preserve Krokorok, pick teammates that resist Ice or are immune to Fighting like Klang, Galarian Corsola, and Lampent; the two Ghost-types are additionally compatible as spinblockers.

Choice Scarf.description:
Krokorok differentiates itself from other offensive Ground-types like Piloswine by being the only one with enough Speed to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame with Choice Scarf. It's a good revenge killer and lead on offensive teams that checks Raboot, Electabuzz, and Metang with Earthquake and sets up Stealth Rock when they switch out. Knock Off removes Eviolite from Earthquake switch-ins like Tangela, Clefairy, and Gurdurr. Stone Edge hits Flying-type and Defog users like Vullaby, Rufflet, and Togetic, which usually can sustain Knock Off.

Choice Scarf Krokorok can fulfill different roles depending on what is needed, whether it is to sweep, revenge kill, or set entry hazards. Krokorok will, however, find itself commonly forced out by locking itself in the wrong move or by being unable to get through common physical walls like Tangela and Gurdurr, making special wallbreakers such as Electabuzz, Roselia, and Lampent great partners. Krokorok is also quite frail, making pivots like Thwackey and Electabuzz great partners, and they can also force out Water-types like Wartortle and encourage Steel-types like Klang or Metang to switch in. These partners are also checked by Grass-types, so having Flying- and Fire-types like Vullaby, Raboot, and Lampent is greatly appreciated. Krokorok is also greatly pressured by priority users like Piloswine, making physically defensive walls like Tangela, Machoke, and Galarian Corsola pivotal.

uu.overview: Krookodile's solid offensive potential and utility options in Taunt and Knock Off make it a decent Stealth Rock setter in UU. Few Pokemon resist the combination of Earthquake and Knock Off, denting the likes of Nihilego, Galarian Slowbro, and even neutral targets like Primarina and Amoonguss. Intimidate lets Krookodile switch into resisted and neutral hits such as Lycanroc-D's Stone Edge without getting too worn down while also prevents late-game sweeps from Pokemon like Scizor. Moves like Stealth Rock and Taunt let Krookodile take on common Defoggers like Mandibuzz and Moltres while having Knock Off to ruin their longevity. However, Krookodile is quite frail, still being threatened by physical attackers like Cobalion, Scizor, and Zygarde-10% even after Intimidate, and its special bulk leaves it vulnerable to special attackers like Hydreigon and Salamence. Weaknesses to common types like Grass, Water, and Fighting hinder its defensive utility and leave it helpless against common Pokemon like Tangrowth, Primarina, and Keldeo. Coverage from Electric-types like Thundurus-T's Focus Blast prevents Krookodile from checking them despite its Electric immunity. Excadrill gives Krookodile immense competition as a utility Ground-type on teams, sporting a better defensive typing, having access to Rapid Spin, and being able to hit hard without investment in Attack. Hippowdon's access to reliable recovery and greater bulk also give Krookodile heavy competition as a Stealth Rock setter.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band allows Krookodile to be a powerful wallbreaker, using its near unresisted STAB combination to threaten Pokemon like Excadrill and Amoonguss. However, this set faces competition from Zygarde-10% who is faster and has a more spammable attack in Thousand Arrows. Krookodile can also run a Choice Scarf set to be a decent revenge killer to the likes of Azelf and Raikou, but this set faces competition from other Choice Scarf users like Diggersby and Hydreigon due to them being stronger and having access to U-turn. Krookodile can opt for a more offensive Choice Scarf set with Moxie, letting it accumulate Attack boosts as it KOes enemies. However, the utility that Intimidate offers is more worth it to weaken Pokemon like Zygarde-10%, and Krookodile can't break past Grass-types and Hippowdon without enough boosts. Rindo Berry is an option to survive +1 Nihilego's Grass Knot and OHKO back with Earthquake.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Amoonguss and Tangrowth check Krookodile very well and are only bothered by Knock Off. Both cause big damage with Giga Drain and incapacitate a team member with Spore or Sleep Powder. Zarude and Tapu Bulu can also switch into Krookodile's STAB moves and can recover with Jungle Healing or Horn Leech.

Water-types: Rotom-W is immune to Ground and can nail Krookdoile with Hydro Pump. Krookodile also can't take any Water-type hits from Azumarill, Primarina, and Keldeo, but they don't like to switch in directly into its moves. Swampert and Slowking can take hits from Krookodile and threaten it back.

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Keldeo, Cobalion, and Conkeldurr also threaten Krookodile greatly, with the former two outspeeding and KOing it. Meanwhile, Conkeldurr has the bulk to take an Earthquake and recover its health with Drain Punch or just pick off Krookodile with Mach Punch. Fighting-type coverage like Focus Blast on Thundurus-T and Close Combat from Lycanroc-D keep Krookodile from taking them on.

Strong Wallbreakers: Despite its ability and good defensive typing, Krookodile has subpar bulk and lacks reliable recovery, meaning it gets worn down quite quickly switching into Pokemon such as Excadrill and Zygarde-10%. Pokemon like Hydreigon and Nidoking hurt it very badly with even resisted special STAB moves due to its bad special bulk.

Physical walls: Hippowdon and Skarmory are unfazed by any of Krookodile's attacks and can wear it down with status or outright KO it.

Stealth Rock.description:
Knock Off is useful for checks like Amoonguss, Swampert, and Celesteela, crippling them for Krookodile's teammates. Stealth Rock wears down Pokemon like Celesteela and Tangrowth for teammates like Thundurus-T and Primarina, and Krookodile matches well against entry hazard removers like Excadrill and Moltres. Toxic allows Krookodile to cripple checks such as Tangrowth and Tapu Bulu. Taunt prevents Stealth Rock and Defog from Pokemon like Excadrill, Swampert, Rotom-W, and Moltres. It also can deny recovery from Hippowdon and defensive Salamence. Leftovers offsets entry hazard damage and gives Krookodile longevity to keep threats like Nihilego and Excadrill in check more easily. Rocky Helmet lets Krookodile wear down Scizor and fully counter suicide lead Excadrill. Chople Berry lets Krookodile take Lycanroc-D's Close Combat and KO back with Earthquake. It also helps Krookodile take Thundurus-T's Focus Blast to then weaken or KO it. On hyper offense teams, Life Orb can be used to amplify Krookodile's offensive presence and let it pressure Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Rotom-W more easily. The given EV spread allows Krookodile to outspeed Excadrill while minimizing Earthquake's ability to 2HKO it while also allowing Krookodile to always survive an unboosted Close Combat from Cobalion.

Krookodile's role compression and item versatility let it perform on both hyper offense and bulky offense teams that appreciate its Knock Off and Stealth Rock support. Spikes setters like Scolipede on hyper offense teams and Skarmory on bulky offense teams form entry hazard stacking cores with Krookodile, appreciating Krookodile's ability to stop Defog with Taunt. Skarmory, namely Iron Defense variants, also help take on Zarude, Azumarill, and Conkeldurr. Setup sweepers such as Thundurus-T and Necrozma work well with Krookodile, as it can set Stealth Rock up and weaken their checks such as Tangrowth and Primarina. Special attackers like Azelf and Nihilego appreciate Krookodile denting and crippling their checks in Chansey and Celesteela with Knock Off, paving their way to sweep. In return, they compensate for Krookodile's lower Speed tier and remove Pokemon like Conkeldurr, Zarude, and Tapu Bulu. Amoonguss can check Pokemonn like Primarina and Zarude for Krookodile, and together they can keep Lycanroc-D in check. Salamence forms a double Intimidate core with Krookodile, weakening Pokemon like Zarude and stopping setup sweepers like Gyarados from getting out of control. Krookodile is vulnerable against Fairy-types such as Azumarill and Togekiss so partners like Scizor, Rotom-W, and Tentacruel are valuable.

Stealth Rock Lead (Dark).description:
Krookodile is a valuable lead for hyper offensive Dark teams thanks to the massive utility options it has to offer for its teammates, notably Stealth Rock and Taunt. Taunt is used to shut down Defoggers such as Mandibuzz and Mantine as well as slower entry hazard setters such as Ferrothorn, Hippowdon, Toxapex, and Skarmory. Knock Off has the benefit of removing items from bulky threats such as Porygon2, Mandibuzz, and Blissey, making them easier to deal with. Earthquake lets it threaten Pokemon such as Torkoal, Klefki, and Cobalion. It also discourages fast sweepers like Volcarona and Scolipede from safely setting up on it and beating the majority of the team. Intimidate is a fantastic ability, as it weakens problematic foes like Terrakion and Zeraora, which can handle Dark-type teams easily with their STAB and coverage moves. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows it to outspeed slower foes such as Lucario, Kommo-o, and Rotom-C. Focus Sash lets Krookodile set Stealth Rock without getting OHKOed by powerful attacks such as Moonblast from Jirachi or Focus Blast from Alakazam. It's recommended to lead with Krookodile at the start of match, so it can set up Stealth Rock more efficiently with its Focus Sash intact. Magic Bounce users such as Xatu and Hatterene should also be dealt with before attempting to set up Stealth Rock.

Setup sweepers and wallbreakers such as Dragon Dance Tyranitar, Bulk Up Urshifu-S, Hydreigon, and Bisharp appreciate Krookodile's entry hazard support to wear down the opposing team and its ability Intimidate. Taunt is especially useful because it prevents most Pokemon from setting up entry hazards and defensive threats like Toxapex and Corviknight from fully recovering their health. Bisharp can also handle a huge threat in Hatterene, which deflects Stealth Rock with Magic Bounce. Urshifu-S appreciates Stealth Rock damage on opponents, since it can specifically OHKO Zeraora with Sucker Punch and Hatterene with Wicked Blow after a Bulk Up boost. Drapion's part-Poison typing is very useful, as it can set Toxic Spikes and form a hazard-stacking core with Krookodile. Zarude is helpful against troublesome Water-types such as Keldeo and Primarina, as they are both able to use Substitute and force Krookodile to damage them. Krookodile cannot prevent faster leads such as Ribombee, Galvantula, and Cobalion from setting up entry hazards, so Mandibuzz getting rid of them with Defog is appreciated.

uu.overview: Darmanitan is a great wallbreaker and revenge killer on sun teams, with its sun-boosted Flare Blitz being extremely difficult to switch into. Under sun, even the sturdiest of Water-types like Slowking and RestTalk Primarina cannot switch in without risking a 2HKO. Its coverage moves also hit most Fire-resistant Pokemon for good damage, with Rock Slide hitting Moltres and Rotom-H, while Earthquake OHKOes Nihilego and lets Darmanitan revenge kill Tentacruel. Both coverage moves also don't have recoil damage. Darmanitan can be difficult to revenge kill, as it resists Scizor's Bullet Punch and many faster threats are unable to switch in safely. However, its poor bulk and Stealth Rock weakness severely limit its entry points, and it is still forced out by revenge killers such as Lycanroc-D, Azumarill, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon once they are in. Flare Blitz, its main STAB attack, has substantial recoil damage that racks up over time, which reduces Darmanitan's overall longevity. It also struggles to break past Fire-resistant Pokemon with recovery if it lacks sun support, like Primarina and Salamence. Darmanitan faces competition as a Choice Scarf user with Diggersby, which has better longevity due to its Stealth Rock resistance and lack of recoil damage.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Trick is an option to debilitate defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Chansey, and Primarina. However, it sacrifices the Speed boost from Choice Scarf, so it should only be used when Choice Scarf is no longer necessary, and has to replace a coverage move. Choice Band can further increase Darmanitan's power, but it becomes more vulnerable to revenge killers like Nihilego and Cobalion, and the additional power is mostly unnecessary. Heavy-Duty Boots grants Darmanitan more longevity, letting it fit on different team archetypes, but the loss of Speed and inability to avoid recoil from being forced into using Flare Blitz prevents it from fulfilling an offensive pivot role that well compared to other options like Azelf.

Checks and Counters

Chip Damage: Due to not commonly running Heavy-Duty Boots, Darmanitan takes substantial entry hazard damage upon switching in. With that and Flare Blitz recoil, Darmanitan gets worn down very quickly. Hippowdon's summoned sand also wears down Darmanitan and removes sun.

Dragon-types: Dragon-types such as Salamence, Hydreigon, and Zygarde-10% all present problems for Darmanitan. Defensive Salamence is the best counter available, resisting Flare Blitz and also lowering Darmanitan's Attack with Intimidate. Salamence can also use Roost to heal any damage that Darmanitan inflicts. Zygarde-10% and Choice Scarf Hydreigon revenge kills Darmanitan, and they can potentially predict Darmanitan switching out to wallbreak.

Water-types: Water-types such as Primarina, Slowking, Swampert, and Rotom-W are solid checks that can tank a hit and heavily damage Darmanitan with their STAB moves. However, if sun is active, they might struggle to switch in on Flare Blitz. Keldeo acts as an offensive check, but it doesn't like to directly switch in, and Azumarill can revenge kill Darmanitan with Aqua Jet.

Choice Scarf.description:
With a Sheer Force boost and STAB, Flare Blitz hits most Pokemon very hard, OHKOing threats such as Scizor, Azelf, Amoonguss, and Celesteela. U-turn allows Darmanitan to take advantage of the switches it forces and pivot out on Pokemon that aren't 2HKOed by Flare Blitz, like Primarina and Slowking. Rock Slide hits Flying-types such as Salamence and Moltres, and Earthquake OHKOes Nihilego while also hitting Cobalion, Zygarde-10%, and Excadrill without incurring recoil. Choice Scarf ensures that Darmanitan can outspeed Pokemon such as Azelf, Zygarde-10%, and Crobat.

Darmanitan best fits on sun teams, which appreciate its revenge killing while strengthening its nuclear Flare Blitz. Torkoal is the cornerstone of sun teams, providing Stealth Rock, Rapid Spin, and sun. Venusaur sets up on foes that threaten Darmanitan, such as Keldeo and Primarina lacking Psychic. In exchange, Darmanitan can break through Celesteela and trade with Noivern, as well as pivoting out of bad matchups like Primarina and Keldeo to give Venusaur setup opportunities. Defensive Celesteela checks Hydreigon and Excadrill, while Darmanitan breaks through Celesteela checks like Chansey. Hatterene checks Dragon-types such as Salamence and Hydreigon, provides Magic Bounce support, and can heal Darmanitan's chip damage from Stealth Rock with Healing Wish. Swampert and Chansey are great pivots that can bring in Darmanitan safely against Excadrill and Krookodile, with Swampert checking Rotom-W and Chansey checking Hydreigon. Skarmory can provide Spikes support, which is valuable in providing chip damage for Darmanitan. It also handles many physical attackers that threaten Darmanitan, such as Diggersby and Hippowdon, well.

Choice Band.description:
Set Description

Galarian Darmanitan uses its great Attack, decent Speed tier, Gorilla Tactics, and Choice Band to OHKO as many opponents as possible before they can move. Either Icicle Crash or Ice Punch can be used; Ice Punch has perfect accuracy, but Icicle Crash has more power, notably securing matchups against Bulk Up Zarude, Rocky Helmet Aromatisse, and physically bulky Tapu Lele. Icicle Crash also has a 30% flinch chance, allowing Galarian Darmanitan to potentially beat Sturdy users and bulkier threats like Crustle and Aromatisse. Giga Impact OHKOes many bulkier Pokemon such as Sylveon and Primarina and even has a chance to OHKO physically defensive Tapu Fini. Flare Blitz does massive damage to Steel-types, notably OHKOing Registeel and non-Occa Berry Celesteela, and also helps Galarian Darmanitan defeat slower Volcarona sets. The last move is usually one of Superpower, Earthquake, or Iron Head. Superpower helps against Tyranitar, Air Balloon Heatran, bulky Kyurem and Chansey, Earthquake beats some Arcanine and Sitrus Berry Volcanion more reliably, and Iron Head reliably beats Aromatisse.

EVs

Adamant is usually preferred, as it performs better versus bulkier Pokemon, like Tapu Fini and Aromatisse. The 4 Special Defense EVs block Pokemon with the ability Download, most notably Porygon2, from getting +1 Special Attack.

On bulkier spreads, Giga Impact is less valuable, since it lacks the necessary Attack investment to OHKO Tapu Fini. However, it is still valuable versus Sylveon and Primarina.

An alternative spread of 88 Atk / 244 Def / 176 Spe outspeeds Rillaboom and survives Celesteela's uninvested Heavy Slam and Life Orb Rillaboom's Fake Out + Grassy Glide.

An alternative spread of 8 HP / 116 Atk / 132 SpD / 252 Spe survives Choice Scarf Togekiss's Fire Blast and Choice Specs Tapu Fini's Hydro Pump so that it can KO them with Icicle Crash and two Earthquakes, respectively.

Usage Tips

If Galarian Darmanitan does not have Iron Head, it should use Icicle Crash or Ice Punch against Aromatisse, rather than Giga Impact. Even though Giga Impact has a chance to OHKO, it has better odds to 2HKO with Ice Punch or Icicle Crash + Struggle. Galarian Darmanitan is 2HKOed by Moonblast and Rocky Helmet damage from Aromatisse, which means that if Aromatisse dodges or survives Giga Impact turn 1 and uses Trick Room, it can use Moonblast, disable Giga Impact as it recharges, and use Moonblast again to KO Galarian Darmanitan.

With the defensive spread, use Icicle Crash or Ice Punch versus Celesteela instead of Flare Blitz. This ensures that Celesteela will not KO Galarian Darmanitan afterwards, and the Ice-type moves 2HKO most Celesteela.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Description

Icicle Crash is Galarian Darmanitan's strongest STAB option. Superpower beats non-Chople variants of Porygon-Z, Urshifu-S, and Kyurem. Earthquake is for Nihilego, Entei, and Zeraora. The last move is more variable, depending on the needs of the team; Flare Blitz for a better Celesteela and Metagross matchup, Thrash for Choice Scarf Tapu Fini, Rock Slide for Volcarona, or Lash Out for Spectrier.

EVs

Galarian Darmanitan runs maximum Speed and a Speed-boosting nature to outspeed Choice Scarf Porygon-Z and Pheromosa. The leftover 4 EVs are put into Special Defense so Download users like Porygon2 get an Attack boost instead of a Special Attack boost.

An Adamant nature instead of a Jolly nature helps versus Heatran, but loses out on Timid Choice Scarf Kyurem and Porygon-Z, as well as other Galarian Darmanitan.

An alternative spread of 160 Atk / 112 Def / 236 Spe and an Adamant nature allows Galarian Darmanitan to survive Jolly Garchomp's Stone Edge and Adamant Garchomp's Outrage, so this spread is fairly reliable versus Choice Scarf and Custap Berry Garchomp.

If using Thrash, consider an EV spread of 4 HP / 144 Atk / 104 SpD / 252 Spe to survive Choice Specs Tapu Fini's Hydro Pump.

Usage Tips

In nearly every matchup, use the move that does the most damage to come out on top.

Zen Mode.description:
Set Description

Icicle Crash and, after activating Zen Mode, Flare Blitz are Galarian Darmanitan's strongest STAB options. In most matchups, Zen Mode is triggered when Galarian Darmanitan uses Endure on an attack that would otherwise OHKO it, activating both Zen Mode and the Salac Berry. To round out this set, Galarian Darmanitan-Z can use Encore to lock opponents into non-damaging moves, such as Endure. Reversal is another option, which can defeat Kyurem and Heatran.

EVs

Adamant is the preferred nature, as base 135 Speed and at +1 Speed outspeeds all relevant threats.

Usage Tips

When Galarian Darmanitan-Z can outspeed and OHKO an opponent, such as Venusaur and Ferrothorn, Galarian Darmanitan should just attack turn 1. Other matchups, where Darmanitan is outsped and OHKOed, like versus Pheromosa and Kartana, Galarian Darmanitan should use Endure, activate the Salac Berry, and OHKO the next turn.

Note that Galarian Darmanitan-Z is much weaker without Gorilla Tactics, so it does not KO bulkier Pokemon that it normally expects to like Regidrago.

Choice Scarf (Ice).description:
Galarian Darmanitan's tremendous Attack stat bolstered by its ability Gorilla Tactics, along with its decent Speed and coverage options, allows it to serve as an effective sweeper and revenge killer. Icicle Crash allows it to beat Ground- and Dragon-types like Hippowdon and Dragapult. Flare Blitz provides great coverage for Bug- and Steel-types like Frosmoth and Corviknight. U-turn is a solid option for safely bringing in a teammate on a predicted switch. Superpower allows Galarian Darmanitan to OHKO defensive Pokemon like Tyranitar and Snorlax. However, Earthquake serves as great coverage for Aegislash, Toxapex, and Chandelure. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows Galarian Darmanitan to Speed tie with opposing Choice Scarf users like Drapion.

With its great Speed tier and offensive presence, Galarian Darmanitan has the flexibility to function as a late-game sweeper or wallbreaker while also being able to provide its team momentum with U-turn. Entry hazard removers such as Avalugg and Galarian Mr. Mime serve as helpful teammates for keeping Galarian Darmanitan healthy throughout a match. Vanilluxe offers Aurora Veil support to bolster Galarian Darmanitan's survivability, especially against Choice Scarf users that outspeed it such as Gengar as well as priority users like Bisharp and Aegislash, while also being able to break through defensive Water-types like Rotom-W and Toxapex with Freeze-Dry. Piloswine and Mamoswine support Galarian Darmanitan with Stealth Rock, allowing defensive checks such as Galarian Corsola and Rotom-W to be slowly worn down into KO range.

Choice Band (Ice).description:
By virtue of the stacked boosts from Choice Band and Gorilla Tactics onto its already amazing Attack stat, Galarian Darmanitan is an obscenely powerful wallbreaker. Icicle Crash is able to destroy walls that don't resist it, like Clefable, and even frailer Ice-resistant Pokemon on the switch-in, such as Crawdaunt. Fire Punch and Flare Blitz serve as coverage to nail Steel- and Ice-types that resist Icicle Crash; the former one is preferred, as it already OHKOes Corviknight and Ferrothorn without recoil damage. However, the latter scores KOs versus Levitate Bronzong, +1 Corviknight, Mamoswine, and Aegislash after contact with King's Shield. Earthquake nails Toxapex and Torkoal and is Galarian Darmanitan's best way to damage Snorlax. U-turn takes advantage of the number of switches Galarian Darmanitan forces, generating momentum for the team while hitting reasonably hard. A Jolly nature is vital to outrun Kommo-o and tie with other base 95 Speed Pokemon such as Indeedee.

Because this Galarian Darmanitan forgoes the Speed boost from Choice Scarf, it becomes vulnerable to faster Pokemon like Hydreigon and Dragapult. Other Choice Scarf revenge killers that can beat them, like Weavile and Galarian Mr. Mime, are, thus, great partners. Entry hazards are also an issue for Galarian Darmanitan, since they reduce its lifespan greatly, especially if it's running Flare Blitz; therefore, Rapid Spin users such as the aforementioned Galarian Mr. Mime and Avalugg are mandatory teammates. Alolan Ninetales provides Aurora Veil support for Galarian Darmanitan, making it more useful against offensive teams by taking hits better and KOing faster, frailer enemies back. Swords Dance Weavile and Cloyster appreciate Galarian Darmanitan's capability to break walls for a late-game sweep. Froslass, Mamoswine, and Piloswine can lay down Spikes and Stealth Rock, respectively, softening defensive Pokemon like Toxapex for Galarian Darmanitan.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Gorilla Tactics.description:
• Galarian Darmanitan has the highest Attack stat in the format after accounting for Gorilla Tactics, allowing it to hit incredibly hard with relatively high speed without taking an additional penalty from a Choice item.

  • Earthquake is highly recommended, as it's Galarian Darmanitan's best attack against Tapu Fini.

  • U-turn allows Galarian Darmanitan to do substantial chip damage while not locking itself into an attack. Superpower is Galarian Darmanitan's best attack against Rotom-W.

Items

  • Choice Scarf makes Galarian Darmanitan into a good revenge killer, outspeeding prominent foes such as Dragapult and Landorus-T with a Jolly nature.

  • Choice Band makes Galarian Darmanitan more effecitve as a wall breaker, making Earthquake deal over 50% to Bold Tapu Fini.

GORILLA WARFARE.description:
• With its sky high Attack stat and the in-built Choice Band of Gorilla Tactics, Galarian Darmanitan boasts the highest natural raw Attack in the game.

  • Flare Blitz provides valuable coverage against Steel-Types like Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn.

  • Earthquake hits Rock-Types for heavy damage and provides a way to threaten foes like Zacian-C without the recoil of Flare Blitz.

  • U-turn makes Galarian Darmanitan a great pivot, doing heavy damage to most targets while maintaining a switch advantage.

  • Stone Edge and Rock Slide can be used to heavily pressure Ho-Oh.

  • Superpower is great for breaking through Tyranitar, Chansey, and Blissey with minimal stress. Should you choose to Dynamax Galarian Darmanitan, you can use Max Knuckle to take its Attack to unmatched levels.

  • It is worth noting that when Dynamaxed, Galarian Darmanitan will lose its Gorilla Tactics boost, so Dynamax should only be used when it is necessary to switch moves

Items

  • Choice Scarf helps patch up Galarian Darmanitan’s somewhat disappointing Speed stat, allowing it to threaten the likes of Eternatus more easily.

  • Focus Sash can let Galarian Darmanitan get around its abysmal bulk, ensuring it gets an attack off as a lead and potentially letting you preserve it for later in the game. If hazards are not in play, Focus Sash Galarian Darmanitan can also be used to threaten big damage on Max Airstream users, such as Yveltal.

  • Choice Band takes Galarian Darmanitan’s offense to new heights, letting it perform absurd feats such as OHKOing fully defensive Toxapex with Earthquake, alongside making its Icicle Crash all but impossible to safely switch into.

Zen Mode.description:
• By using Zen Mode, Galarian Darmanitan gains the ability to switch moves, potentially securing a surprise KO. Zen Mode also increases Darmanitan-G’s Attack and Speed even further once activated. The Speed boost makes it quite fast, and it can surprise previously-faster targets with a devastating second attack.

  • Flare Blitz is valuable coverage against Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, additionally, the recoil from Flare Blitz can potentially activate Zen Mode, boosting its offenses and giving it STAB on Flare Blitz.

  • Earthquake hits Rock-types such as Tyranitar for heavy damage while also threatening the odd Heatran.

  • With Yawn, Galarian Darmanitan can support its team in the event it is walled while still being a potent offensive threat. Yawn is also somewhat unexpected on Galarian Darmanitan, since opponents must respect the more common Gorilla Tactics set.

  • Stone Edge can be used to heavily pressure Ho-Oh.

  • Superpower provides super effective coverage against Chansey, Blissey, and Tyranitar, as well as giving Galarian Darmanitan access to Max Knuckle.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf can be used to outspeed faster Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Zarude, Garchomp, and Tornadus-T; however, being Choice-locked makes it easier to play around and is generally outclassed by other Choice Scarf users like Azelf and Latios.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Slowbro, Toxapex, Tapu Fini, and Vaporeon have the physical bulk to withstand any attacks from Galarian Darmanitan. Toxapex's Prankster-boosted Haze can also reliably remove its Belly Drum + Salac Berry boosts. However, Tapu Fini has to be wary of +6 Earthquake.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: If Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan is not running Fire Punch, Dauntless Shield Skarmory can wall it reliably and proceed to phaze it. However, not running Earthquake makes it walled by Tapu Fini. Dauntless Shield Mew and Hippowdown are not 2HKOed by any attacks on the Magic + Guard Life Orb set, letting them retaliate with Will-O-Wisp or Earthquake, respectively.

Unaware: Belly Drum variants can't break through common Unaware users like Chansey, Blissey, and Mew, the latter of which threatens an OHKO in return with Foul Play.

Revenge Killers: Due to Galarian Darmanitan's average Speed tier, faster Pokemon like Garchomp, Inteleon, Terrakion, and Zygarde-10% can outspeed and threaten it with an OHKO. Even with its blazing Speed from Zen Mode and Salac Berry, priority moves like Triage Kommo-o's Drain Punch, Barraskewda's Aqua Jet, and Zygarde-10%'s Extreme Speed can still pick it off easily, given its Substitute is not up.

Magic Guard + Life Orb.description:
Great Attack and wide offensive movepool make Galarian Darmanitan a formidable wallbreaker. Icicle Crash threatens common foes like Garchomp, Kommo-o, Mandibuzz, and Landorus-T and has great neutral coverage in a metagame where offensive Ice-types are rare. Flare Blitz complements Icicle Crash by hitting non-Flash Fire Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Corviknight, and Skarmory, as well as Jirachi and Doublade. U-turn lets Galarian Darmanitan act as a pivot—which works exceptionally well with Magic Guard to avoid entry hazard damage—to safely bring in teammates that can deal with its switch-ins like Tapu Fini and Dauntless Shield Mew, even providing a strong hit for the latter. Earthquake provides important coverage for Toxapex, while Superpower covers other Steel-types like Flash Fire Ferrothorn. Magic Guard also provides solid longevity by letting Galarian Darmanitan avoid Life Orb and Flare Blitz recoil, as well as Rocky Helmet from users like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn. A Jolly nature is used to outspeed and OHKO Adamant Galarian Zapdos and, after minor chip damage, Modest Tapu Lele.

Galarian Darmanitan fits mostly on offense and bulky offense teams. Defensive pivots like Corviknight and RegenVest Jirachi and Landorus-T make for great teammates, as they can bring it in safely on foes like Ferrothorn and opposing Landorus-T. They can also switch into threats that can revenge kill it reliably like Terrakion, Tapu Lele, and Volcarona, respectively. Offensive pivots like Zarude and Tapu Koko are also great options, as they form a potent VoltTurn core with Galarian Darmanitan; they pressure bulky Water-types and Dauntless Shield Mew, while Galarian Darmanitan threatens some of their best checks like Mandibuzz and RegenVest Landorus-T, respectively. Late-game cleaners like Swords Dance Talonflame and Choice Scarf Azelf appreciate Galarian Darmanitan pressuring Mandibuzz and Corviknight for them. A sturdy Fire-resistant or -immune teammate like Slowbro or Primordial Sea Zapdos is necessary to switch into fast Fire-type threats like Cinderace and Talonflame. Offensive teammates that can compensate for Galarian Darmanitan's average Speed like Choice Scarf Azelf and Choice Band Zarude are great partners, as they can revenge kill faster threats like Terrakion and Barraskewda, respectively.

Zen Mode.description:
Thanks to Belly Drum and a high Speed stat post-transformation, Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan becomes a threatening cleaner when it is able to set up. Once Zen Mode is activated, its newfound Speed tier alongside Salac Berry allows it to outspeed the unboosted metagame, outpacing fast foes like Regieleki, Choice Scarf Azelf and Latios, and Surge Surfer Xurkitree. After Belly Drum, Icicle Crash threatens to OHKO prominent physically bulky Pokemon like Swampert, Flash Fire Ferrothorn and Corviknight, and Dauntless Shield Hippowdon. Even with Belly Drum and Ice Punch's reliability, Icicle Crash is still preferred to ignore debilitating Rocky Helmet from foes like Kommo-o and Hippowdon, and most importantly, guarantee the 2HKO on Unaware Mandibuzz, which ignores its Belly Drum boost. Boosted Fire Punch cleanly OHKOes physically defensive Steel-types like Dauntless Shield Skarmory and Corviknight, as well as Jirachi and Doublade. Earthquake is a fine alternative to also hit the latter two alongside Heatran, Volcanion, and Toxapex and is Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan's strongest attack to hit other bulky Water-types like Tapu Fini and Vaporeon. Substitute lets it safely activate Zen Mode and Salac Berry, takes advantage of passive foes like Mew and Ferrothorn by blocking their status moves, and prevents it from being revenge killed by priority attacks like Triage Kommo's Drain Punch and Barraskewda's Aqua Jet.

Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan fits exclusively on hyper offense teams that appreciate its high offensive presence. Since it will, at best, get one chance to sweep, it needs pristine conditions to get both Belly Drum and the Salac Berry activation safely. Dual screens support from teammates like Regieleki and Tapu Koko are near-mandatory, as they allow Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan to set up much more easily. They can also help alleviate its Stealth Rock weakness: Regieleki's Rapid Spin removes them, while Tapu Koko's Taunt can shut down attempts of setting them up from foes like Ferrothorn and Heatran. Galvanize Kommo-o is an amazing partner that can wallbreak early-game and lure in and potentially KO Prankster Toxapex and Dauntless Shield Skarmory for Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan, especially if it is not running the right coverage move. Setup sweepers like Triage Tapu Bulu and Swords Dance Dhelmise appreciate Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan threatening Unaware Mandibuzz, Dauntless Shield Kommo-o, and physically defensive Corviknight and Skarmory for them; moreover, they help pressure bulky Water-types like Tapu Fini, Slowbro, and Vaporeon for it in return. Psychic Surge Azelf provides Psychic Terrain to prevent Zen Mode Galarian Darmanitan from being revenge killed by priority attacks, especially as it tends to be at low health after setting up.

ubers.overview: Galarian Darmanitan is a terrifying physical attacker with the ability to decimate unprepared teams with good prediction. Its solid Speed and ability in Gorilla Tactics make it a great Choice Scarf user in Ubers, getting the jump on +1 base 90 Speed Pokemon such as Zekrom and opposing Choice Scarf users like Kyogre and Landorus-T. Ice is an excellent offensive type in Ubers, hitting most Dragon-types super effectively and granting Galarian Darmanitan plenty of targets. Sadly, its complete lack of bulk combined with its Stealth Rock weakness gives it no defensive utility at all, limiting its entry to double switches and slow pivots. Galarian Darmanitan is a Pokemon that necessitates correct predictions and good positioning thanks to Gorilla Tactics, which makes it harder to use than most Pokemon in the metagame.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Fire Punch is an option on Belly Drum sets, as it allows Galarian Darmanitan to KO certain targets it otherwise can't such as Shedinja and Calyrex-I.

Checks and Counters

Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf Calyrex-S can outspeed and OHKO either set with Astral Barrage, and priority users such as Yveltal, Urshifu-S, and Marshadow can KO Galarian Darmanitan after Stealth Rock damage.

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Kyogre can stomach Galarian Darmanitan's hits and force it out.

Pivots: Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Necrozma-DM can scout Galarian Darmanitan's set and respond from there by doubling back to the appropriate check or phazing it.

Choice Scarf.description:
U-turn preserves momentum against switch-ins that Galarian Darmanitan cannot handle on its own. Icicle Crash hits many common Pokemon such as Zygarde-C, Groudon, and Zekrom super effectively while also hitting Xerneas for neutral damage. Flare Blitz is its best coverage option for Steel-types such as Necrozma-DM, Zamazenta-C, Magearna, and Ferrothorn, as well as Calyrex-I. Rock Slide deals with Ho-Oh trying to scout what move it's using, opening a potentially massive hole in the opposing team. Alternatively, Earthquake hits bulky Water-types like Kyogre and other Pokemon like Heatran and Rocky Helmet Necrozma-DM. A Jolly nature with Choice Scarf is crucial to outpace every base 90 Speed Pokemon at +1, such as Choice Scarf Kyogre and Dragon Dance Zekrom, as well as faster Pokemon such as Calyrex-S.

Entry hazard control from Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Lunala allows Galarian Darmanitan to use U-turn undisturbed by entry hazards and gives it more chances to come in and wreak havoc. Pivots such as U-turn Yveltal, Urshifu-S, and Landorus-T are another great aid to Galarian Darmanitan. Xerneas appreciates the pressure Galarian Darmanitan puts on its checks such as Necrozma-DM and Ho-Oh, and Marshadow appreciates the entry points Galarian Darmanitan provides and can revenge kill Choice Scarf Calyrex-S for it. Finally, hazard setters such as Ferrothorn, Necrozma-DM, and Landorus-T help Galarian Darmanitan apply greater offensive pressure.

Choice Band.description:
When equipped with a Choice Band, Galarian Darmanitan becomes one of the most fearsome Pokemon in the metagame to switch into. Nothing in the metagame can safely switch in without fear of being OHKOed or 2HKOed. For example, Galarian Darmanitan's most common check, Necrozma-DM, is easily OHKOed by Flare Blitz after Stealth Rock with a Jolly nature, or without Stealth Rock with an Adamant nature. Icicle Crash becomes immensely strong, easily 2HKOing defensive Xerneas and Ho-Oh. Earthquake hits Toxapex and Heatran, which otherwise wall this set, as well as 2HKOing defensive Kyogre. U-turn can be used to pivot against foes like Lunala, while Rock Slide OHKOes Ho-Oh. Jolly is preferred for outspeeding base 90 Speed Pokemon with maximum Speed investment like Zekrom as well as most Xerneas and Yveltal variants without fear of being slower. Adamant does provide some notable OHKOs, such as the aforementioned one on Necrozma-DM, as well as guaranteeing that Icicle Crash and Earthquake take out defensive Groudon and Toxapex, respectively, but it heavily relies on paralysis support.

The main flaw of this set is that it is extremely hard to bring into battle. Galarian Darmanitan is weak to Stealth Rock and vulnerable to all other entry hazards, and it has low defensive stats and a lack of resistances. Critically, without the Speed of Choice Scarf, Galarian Darmanitan can't always take advantage of opportunities to gain momentum from options like Yveltal's U-turn. Thunder Wave Ho-Oh is an excellent teammate for its ability to paralyze Eternatus, letting Yveltal's U-turn bring Galarian Darmanitan in more easily. Furthermore, Ho-Oh is great at preventing Necrozma-DM from keeping Stealth Rock up. Xerneas appreciates that Galarian Darmanitan can OHKO Necrozma-DM, with Geomancy and Choice Scarf sets in particular being able to sweep much more easily. Cosmic Power Eternatus also enjoys Necrozma-DM being gone, and it can take advantage of Kyogre. Eject Pack Eternatus, U-turn Landorus-T, and Teleport Blissey or Solgaleo are additional options that can provide momentum to bring Galarian Darmanitan in safely.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Galarian Darmanitan has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Ice

Physically Defensive Walls: While Galarian Darmanitan has amazing damage output, it struggles to get past extremely bulky physical walls such as Galarian Corsola, Mega Slowbro, and Porygon2, especially if it's running Choice Scarf. As a result, they are able to wear it down with their status or attacking moves. However, Choice Band variants of Galarian Darmanitan can 2HKO these walls.

Rotom-W: Rotom-W is an extremely effective check to Galarian Darmanitan; it resists both Icicle Crash and Flare Blitz, is immune to Earthquake due to Levitate, and threatens to wear it down with Hydro Pump or cripple it with Will-O-Wisp.

Status: Burn greatly hinders Galarian Darmanitan's wallbreaking. Paralysis leaves it more easily revenge killed, and Toxic puts it on a timer; both problems are worsened by its fragility and vulnerability to entry hazards.

Priority Moves: Offensive Pokemon carrying priority moves like Rillaboom, Bisharp, and Dragonite can take advantage of Galarian Darmanitan's middling bulk. However, Pokemon carrying weaker priority moves like Zygarde-10% need it to be heavily chipped before attempting to KO it.

Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan can be promptly OHKOed by faster Choice Scarf users like Blacephalon, Terrakion, Latias, and Nihilego. Choice Band Galarian Darmanitan is outsped and OHKOed by a plethora of offensive threats like Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, Mega Aerodactyl, and Hydreigon, so it must be extremely wary of them.

Choice Scarf (Ice).description:
Galarian Darmanitan is one of the best revenge killers on Ice teams due to its amazing coverage moves and generally high Attack stat boosted by Gorilla Tactics, which make it a decent wallbreaker as well. Flare Blitz lets Galarian Darmanitan KO Steel-types such as Celesteela, Aegislash, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight, which are massive threats to Ice teams. Earthquake provides good coverage against Toxapex, Heatran, and Torkoal, which otherwise completely wall Galarian Darmanitan. Earthquake is also useful for SubToxic Aegislash, as it doesn't activate King's Shield, unlike Flare Blitz. U-turn safely brings in a teammate to deal with a check to Galarian Darmanitan like Rotom-W or Galarian Corsola. Maximum Speed investment along with a Jolly nature allows Galarian Darmanitan to outspeed foes like Mega Aerodactyl, Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and Choice Scarf Excadrill. Galarian Darmanitan should be used to clean weakened teams late-game once bulky walls such as Porygon2 and Swampert are severely weakened or removed. Due to its poor bulk and vulnerability to entry hazards, notably Stealth Rock, it should avoid switching in excessively.

Alolan Ninetales is useful in order to deal with bulky Water-types that pressure Galarian Darmanitan such as Tapu Fini, Rotom-W, and Mega Slowbro with Freeze-Dry, as well as Fighting-types like Keldeo. Additionally, it provides valuable support with Aurora Veil. Avalugg is an extremely useful defensive teammate to deal with physical threats that outspeed Galarian Darmanitan such as Choice Scarf Weavile, Mega Swampert in rain, and Barraskewda in rain. It also removes entry hazards for it with Rapid Spin. Defensive Cloyster can also remove entry hazards and provides Spikes and Toxic Spikes support. Choice Specs Kyurem deals with physically defensive walls such as Porygon2, Galarian Corsola, and Swampert for Galarian Darmanitan due to its power and amazing coverage. Mamoswine is a good offensive partner with Galarian Darmanitan, crippling its usual checks like Galarian Corsola and Porygon2 with Knock Off while acting as a secondary way to deal with Steel teams. It also appreciates Galarian Darmanitan forcing out Steel-types like Celesteela, Ferrothorn, and Skarmory, which Mamoswine needs chip damage on to successfully KO. Piloswine can be used instead as a great wall to deal with Fire-types like Choice Scarf Blacephalon and Volcarona thanks to the combination of Thick Fat and Eviolite. It also provides Stealth Rock support for Galarian Darmanitan while dealing with other special attackers like Tapu Koko, Nihilego, and Alolan Raichu. Choice Scarf Weavile can greatly help in the Ghost and Psychic matchups, dealing with faster Choice Scarf users like Latias, Jirachi, and Blacephalon.

Choice Band (Ice).description:
Choice Band Galarian Darmanitan is one of the most lethal wallbreakers on Ice teams due to its Gorilla Tactics-boosted Attack, allowing it to easily break through types with defensive cores such as Dark, Normal, and Poison. Flare Blitz OHKOes troublesome Steel-types like Celesteela, Aegislash, Ferrothorn, and Skarmory after Stealth Rock damage. Earthquake lets Galarian Darmanitan deal with key targets such as Heatran, Toxapex, and Torkoal. U-turn is useful to bring in teammates safely while maintaining offensive momentum. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature lets Galarian Darmanitan outspeed foes such as Mega Garchomp, Nidoking, and unboosted Kommo-o. Galarian Darmanitan should be used as an early-game wallbreaker to take advantage of types with defensive Pokemon, like Dark, Normal, Poison, and punch holes in the opposing team.

Alolan Ninetales is a great teammate to deal with troublesome Fighting-types such as Mega Gallade, Keldeo, and Urshifu-R for Galarian Darmanitan, as well as Dark-types that outspeed it such as Hydreigon and Choice Scarf Weavile, while providing Aurora Veil support. Avalugg is an amazing defensive partner, as it deals with physical attackers that outspeed and KO Galarian Darmanitan like Zeraora, Mega Aerodactyl, and Mega Swampert while also providing Rapid Spin support. Piloswine is an excellent specially defensive wall that can deal with special Fire-types like Volcarona and Blacephalon due to Thick Fat and Eviolite. It also provides Stealth Rock support and deals with additional special attackers that outspeed and threaten Galarian Darmanitan like Latios, Hydreigon, and Thundurus-T. Choice Specs Kyurem can defeat extremely bulky physical walls for Galarian Darmanitan like Galarian Corsola and Porygon2, easing pressure off of it. It also breaks through bulky Water-types like Swampert, Mega Slowbro, and Rotom-W with Freeze-Dry. Choice Scarf Weavile deals with threatening Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gengar, Latias, and Latios.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Galarian Darmanitan can also use a devastatingly strong Choice Band set, limiting its switch-ins to an extremely small handful of Pokemon, but the loss in Speed is very noticeable. Superpower is a decent coverage option to hit Ferrothorn hard without the recoil as well as giving the option of Max Knuckle, but the drops in Attack and Defense make it more committal and less consistent than other options.

Checks and Counters

Kyogre: Defensive Kyogre resists both Icicle Crash and Flare Blitz while not taking much damage from any other coverage move. Repeated U-turns can easily chip it down, and healing damage with Rest leaves it vulnerable, but it is still one of the sturdiest walls to Galarian Darmanitan.

Necrozma-DM: While it doesn't appreciate Flare Blitz, Necrozma-DM can shrug off any other hit and even has a chance to live two Choice Scarf Flare Blitzes. It also accumulates chip damage by switching in with Rocky Helmet.

Chip Damage: Rocky Helmet on Necrozma-DM and Skarmory, Stealth Rock, other hazards, and Flare Blitz recoil can very easily wear down Galarian Darmanitan, especially because it can't stick around for long without switching.

Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf Calyrex-S as well as Geomancy-boosted Xerneas can outspeed and OHKO Galarian Darmanitan, while priority from Pokemon such as Marshadow and Yveltal exploit its low defensive stats to threaten it.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan is a solidly fast and incredibly strong revenge killer in AG. Icicle Crash can take out neutral Pokemon such as Marshadow and Calyrex-S when chipped while also threatening Eternatus, Zygarde, and Yveltal. U-turn is an easy to spam pivoting option that lets Galarian Darmanitan chip down walls that resist its main coverage, like Kyogre and Necrozma-DM, while creating a more favorable position for its team. Flare Blitz OHKOes Zacian-C, a prime target, while also dealing solid damage to Ferrothorn, Necrozma-DM, and Skarmory. Rock Slide OHKOes defensive Ho-Oh, which can pivot into Galarian Darmanitan and scout what it's locked into otherwise. Earthquake nails Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Eternatus in one move while also hitting Steel-types without the recoil drawback of Flare Blitz. A Jolly nature with maximum Speed and its Choice Scarf allow Galarian Darmanitan to outrun and revenge kill Pokemon such as Zacian-C, +1 Zekrom and Reshiram, and Calyrex-S.

With Galarian Darmanitan's ability to bait in and pressure Necrozma-DM, force out Ground- and Dragon-types, and pivot with U-turn, it is an excellent offensive partner for Zacian-C. Similarly, Zacian-C helps Galarian Darmanitan by pressuring checks to it such as defensive Kyogre and Toxapex with Wild Charge. Zekrom also threatens defensive Water-types and can take advantage of U-turn switch-ins to set up a Dragon Dance. Since Galarian Darmanitan also lacks any kind of defensive utility, common walls such as specially defensive Yveltal, Eternatus, and Zygarde-C also help by switching into wallbreakers it can't OHKO. Specially defensive Yveltal can also safely bring in Galarian Darmanitan with U-turn and provide Defog support, mitigating its weakness to entry hazards. Defensive Necrozma-DM is able to switch into and threaten out Xerneas and Zacian-C, Pokemon that Galarian Darmanitan can't switch into and can only pressure when locked into the right move.

zu.overview: Maractus is an unviable choice in SS ZU because it is entirely outclassed as a defensive Spikes setter by Roselia, which has much better bulk with Eviolite and a better typing for the tier both offensively and defensively.

Specially Defensive.description: Maractus attempts to support its teammates with Spikes and Knock Off while trying to help ward off special attackers. Unfortunately, it isn't quite capable of taking on the tier's top Pokemon, unlike Roselia, which can with its better bulk and typing, and Eviolite furthering its defensive prowess.

Entry Hazard Setter.description: Dwebble finds a solid niche in LC as an entry hazard setter on hyper offense thanks to having access to both Stealth Rock and Spikes. The combination of Knock Off and Rock Blast gives Dwebble a great matchup against Natu, the tier's most common entry hazard prevention, and makes it hard for Natu to reliably deny its entry hazards. Knock Off gives more utility to Dwebble, crippling lead Pokemon such as Mienfoo and spinners such as Staryu and Drilbur. Counter can be used surprise foes such as Mienfoo, but it is hard to fit. Weak Armor prevents spinners from reliably Dwebble's entry removing hazards. Offensive Pokemon such as Abra, Carvanha and Ponyta as well as setup sweepers like Tyrunt and Agility Porygon, appreciate hazard support from Dwebble to help overwhelm their checks such as Ferroseed and Staryu. Grookey threatens Staryu and can revenge kill weakened foes with Grassy Glide.

Shell Smash.description: With Shell Smash, Dwebble can become a scary offensive presence fast due to its decent STAB combination and access to Sturdy, giving it easier setup opportunities. However, as a setup sweeper, Dwebble is generally outclassed by Tyrunt, and it struggles against Grookey. Earthquake has great synergy with Rock Blast, providing perfect neutral coverage while also targeting Rock-resistant foes like Pawniard and Onix. Knock Off can remove an item from opposing Ferroseed. Entry hazard setters like Ferroseed and Pawniard are helpful, as they can wear down foes for Dwebble to clean late-game. Memento Diglett can assist Dwebble by letting it more easily set up against a foe of its choice. Pivots like Mienfoo and Natu provide Dwebble safe switch-in opportunities. The latter can also thwart entry hazards, helping maintain Dwebble's Sturdy.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

Rock Tomb over Stone Edge with a Jolly nature is beneficial for getting an edge against faster Taunt users like Electabuzz and Galarian Linoone, as Dwebble chips them down and outspeeds afterwards, but it comes at the cost of losing a strong STAB attack. Weak Armor with Focus Sash provides more Speed so that Dwebble has a better matchup against some leads like Electabuzz and Raboot, but the lack of an Eviolite combined with the Defense drop makes Dwebble less reliable for setting entry hazards against Pokemon like Clefairy and Piloswine.

Checks and Counters

Gurdurr: By resisting both of Dwebble's attacks, using Defog to clear entry hazards, and stopping Shell Smash sweeps with Mach Punch, Gurdurr is a consistent counter to Dwebble. Dwebble's best bet is to be paired with sweepers that require Gurdurr's Eviolite removed to sweep, or else it will be squandered versus it.

Special Attackers: Dwebble's special bulk is unsalvageable, and practically any offensive special attacker can 2HKO it.

Water-types: Wartortle stomachs Dwebble's attacks while hitting back hard, and after Sturdy activates, it uses Rapid Spin to remove any entry hazards. Mareanie and Marshtomp threaten with Scald, but they may lose their Eviolite in the process.

Bulky Leads: Bulkier Pokemon like Tangela and Gabite are able to take on Dwebble, although they could be annoyed by Knock Off and are unable to prevent Dwebble's first entry hazard attempt. Piloswine and Thwackey apply here as well, and they also have strong priority to punish Shell Smash.

Entry Hazard Setter.description:
Dwebble can set entry hazards and apply pressure against Defog users and Magic Bounce Pokemon, namely Vullaby and Hattrem. It can set both Stealth Rock and Spikes for early-game pressure against other common leads like Piloswine, Clefairy, and Charjabug. Shell Smash gives Dwebble an opportunity to put a large dent into the opposing team while outspeeding faster special attackers like Electabuzz and Gastly.

Use Dwebble as a lead to set entry hazards immediately or boost with Shell Smash for early momentum. Entry hazards are usually more worthwhile when Dwebble faces Electabuzz, as its strong Volt Switch into a priority user like Gurdurr or Thwackey would invalidate its wallbreaking attempts.
