Physical Wallbreakers: Mimikyu, Zygarde-10%, Groudon, Rayquaza, and Calyrex-I can overwhelm Reuniclus easily even if it has a high Defense donation; Assault Vest variants are even more vulnerable to them.

Anti-Setup Measures: Unaware + Haze Quagsire, which can stomach all boosted attacks except for Stored Power, Clear Smog Gastrodon, and phazers like Ho-Oh and Giratina have the bulk to take on Reuniclus's attacks and reliably remove its Calm Mind boosts. Taunt from Pokemon like Tornadus-T, Mewtwo, Yveltal, and Tapu Fini can prevent Reuniclus from healing and boosting. Trick from Choice item users like Mewtwo and Tapu Fini can permanently cripple Reuniclus, preventing it from further setting up.

Chip Damage: Since Assault Vest variants rely solely on Regenerator to stay healthy, Reuniclus can get overwhelmed quickly by repeated hits from even the special attackers it's supposed to check, especially if entry hazards and status get into the mix. Special attackers like Tapu Koko and Tornadus-T often carry U-turn, which, in tandem with their normal attacks, outdamages Reuniclus's recovery from Regenerator.

Assault Vest (Any).description:
Thanks to Regenerator and remarkable natural bulk augmented by Assault Vest, Reuniclus is an amazing special sponge that checks dangerous threats like Nihilego and Psychic-types like Galarian Slowking and Choice Specs Tapu Lele. It can even switch into and scout other Choice Specs users like Kyurem-W and Tapu Koko, shrugging most of the damage off with Regenerator as it switches out to the appropriate teammate. Psyshock is Reuniclus's most reliable attack and used over Psychic to hit foes like Galarian Slowking, Nihilego, and specially defensive Gastrodon harder. Aside from complementing Psyshock to hit physically bulky Pokemon like Zamazenta-C, Urshifu-R, and Tangrowth, Future Sight's delayed damage lets Reuniclus support its wallbreaking teammates like Urshifu-R and Kartana by providing an extra push to their attacks. Knock Off damages the Psychic-types Reuniclus is tasked to check while removing their Life Orb and Choice Specs, making them easier to handle; Knock Off can also cripple common defensive foes like Ferrothorn, Heatran, Slowking, and Tornadus-T. Focus Blast prevents Dark- and Steel-types like Pangoro, Weavile, Alolan Persian, Zamazenta-C, and Kartana from taking advantage of Reuniclus.

Assault Vest Reuniclus fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate the defensive capabilities and utility it provides; it is also an excellent candidate for taking a dump stat on stall teams. Since Reuniclus doesn't require any specific stat donation, it can work with gods like Zamazenta-C, Ho-Oh, and Yveltal by taking their dump stat. Due to Reuniclus's reliance on Assault Vest, Knock Off absorbers like Clefable, Tangrowth, Skarmory, and the aforementioned Zamazenta-C are great teammates. Moreover, their physical bulk allows them to check threatening wallbreakers such as Alolan Persian, Zygarde-10%, Pangoro, and Weavile, respectively, which prey on Reuniclus easily; in return, Reuniclus checks special attackers like Tapu Lele, Mewtwo, and Tapu Koko for them. Defoggers like Yveltal and Ho-Oh prevent Reuniclus from being overwhelmed by entry hazards, letting it switch in more freely; furthermore, they deal with prominent threats like Blacephalon and Pheromosa for Reuniclus. Future Sight support from Reuniclus lets wallbreakers like Urshifu-R, Kartana, and Weavile bypass their checks, such as Tangrowth, Tornadus-T, and Buzzwole, respectively.

Calm Mind (Defense, Speed).description:
Reuniclus is a devastating Calm Mind sweeper after receiving either a Defense or Speed donation: the former lets it set up on prominent physical attackers like Zamazenta-C, Zeraora, and Excadrill much more safely, while the latter allows it to get the jump on foes like Heatran and Giratina. Psyshock is the preferred STAB attack to let Reuniclus contest with opposing Calm Mind users like Clefable and Suicune, as well as immediately threaten specially defensive Gastrodon, which can remove its Calm Mind boosts with Clear Smog. Focus Blast shreds Dark- and Steel-types like Pangoro, Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Heatran. Life Orb works exceptionally well with Magic Guard to bolster Reuniclus's damage output without causing recoil and net remarkable odds to 2HKO Unaware Quagsire with Focus Blast. Magic Guard also keeps Reuniclus healthy from status moves like Heatran and Ho-Oh's Toxic and Ferrothorn's Leech Seed, giving it more setup opportunities so it doesn't have to expend turns using Recover.

Reuniclus fits well on balance teams that appreciate its defensive qualities and ability to become a dangerous wincon. Gods with high Defense stats like Necrozma-DM, Zamazenta-C, and Groudon make for great teammates; Reuniclus can also take Speed donations to bolster its immediate offensive presence. Particularly, Zamazenta-C can switch into Dark-type attacks from Pokemon like Weavile, Yveltal, Bisharp, and Alolan Persian and Trick from foes trying to cripple Reuniclus with a Choice item. Even with a Defense donation, Reuniclus can still be overwhelmed by strong physical wallbreakers like Zygarde-10%, Pheromosa, and Rayquaza; teammates like Tangrowth, Clefable, and Skarmory are good choices to cover them. Entry hazard support from Ferrothorn and Skarmory significantly chips foes like Necrozma-DM, Gastrodon, and Victini, either forcing them to use their recovery move PP in longer games or putting them into KO range of Reuniclus. Steel-types like Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Zamazenta-C appreciate Reuniclus switching into Fighting-type attacks from opposing Zamazenta-C and Choice-locked Pheromosa, Urshifu-R, and Buzzwole. The likes of Rotom-W and Heatran can run Toxic to lure in and permanently cripple Gastrodon and Unaware Quagsire, which can stop Reuniclus from setting up with their Clear Smog and Haze, respectively.

uu.overview: Vanilluxe is a unique wallbreaker in UU, as it takes advantage of Snow Warning to use perfectly accurate Blizzards and crush many unprepared teams. When backed by Choice Specs, it becomes very difficult to switch into, as even Ice-resistant Pokemon like Cobalion, physically defensive Scizor, and Chandelure are 2HKOed by Blizzard. Further, many common Steel-types like Celesteela, Excadrill, and Skarmory are neutral to Ice, meaning they cannot switch in safely at all. Water-types like Slowking and Primarina also can't switch into it due to Freeze-Dry. Since Vanilluxe only needs those two moves to 2HKO most of the tier, it can run Sleep Talk in the third—and last—moveslot, making it a fantastic sleep absorber against Amoonguss and letting it save Blizzard PP. Due to Vanilluxe's reliance on Choice Specs, poor defensive typing, mediocre bulk, and Stealth Rock weakness, it struggles greatly to safely come onto the field. Because of this, Vanilluxe requires the support of pivots and double entry hazard removal cores. Its Speed tier also lets it down, since it is outsped by common offensive Pokemon like Nihilego and Keldeo.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Vanilluxe can run Never-Melt Ice with Taunt and Ice Shard to bluff the Choice Specs set, shut down Chansey's recovery, and surprise Zygarde-10%. However, this makes it much easier to PP stall Blizzard and sacrifices power, notably missing out on 2HKOing physically defensive Scizor. Choice Scarf instead of Choice Specs makes Vanilluxe a great revenge killer against faster Pokemon like Crobat, Keldeo, and Zarude. However, this set can be harder to fit due to its lower damage output.

Checks and Counters

Chansey: Chansey takes every attack, can stall out Blizzard with Soft-Boiled, and cripples Vanilluxe with Toxic or Thunder Wave.

Steel-types: Specially defensive Scizor can take on Vanilluxe well, recover the damage off with Roost, and hit it with priority Bullet Punch. However, variants lacking Special Defense investment are 2HKOed by Blizzard. Offensive Scizor always OHKOes it with Bullet Punch, but it can't switch in directly. Jirachi can force Vanilluxe out with Iron Head, which lets it pivot out freely or set up a Substitute. Cobalion outspeeds and KOes Vanilluxe, but it cannot switch in on it. Registeel's massive Special Defense lets it set up Iron Defense, Amnesia, or Stealth Rock freely.

Fire-types: Fire-types like Chandelure, Rotom-H, and Moltres outspeed Vanilluxe and KO it, but the former two can't take repeated hits, and the latter is OHKOed by Blizzard.

Stealth Rock and Knock Off: Since Vanilluxe needs Choice Specs, it can’t run Heavy-Duty Boots, making it very easy to wear down. Without Choice Specs, Vanilluxe is notably weaker, making it risky to switch into a Pokemon that it should beat, like Tangrowth.

Faster Offensive Threats: Vanilluxe's middling Speed makes it very easy to revenge kill with Pokemon like Nihilego, Keldeo, and Hydreigon.

Choice Specs.description:
Blizzard is incredibly powerful, OHKOing common walls like Tangrowth and Hippowdon while 2HKOing Cobalion, Celesteela, and Nihilego. Freeze-Dry gives it important super effective coverage on Water-types like Primarina, Slowking, and Tentacruel. Sleep Talk lets it absorb Spore from Amoonguss and use Blizzard more often without wasting PP. Vanilluxe only runs three moves on this set so that Sleep Talk calls Freeze-Dry more often against Water-types. Ice Beam can have some use for a fourth move, since a foe like Chansey can easily stall out Blizzard's PP, but it is always the worst move to get when calling Sleep Talk, and Vanilluxe doesn't have much longevity for Ice Beam's PP to be necessary.

Vanilluxe is used on bulky offense teams as a wallbreaker that can get past teams that rely on Scizor, Skarmory, and Celesteela as Steel-types, or on bulky Water-types like Slowking and Primarina as their primary special walls. Its Stealth Rock weakness means that entry hazard removal from Excadrill and Salamence is necessary for it to stay healthy and find opportunities to wallbreak. They can also handle Jirachi for Vanilluxe to more easily use its Ice-type moves. Both of these entry hazard removers are commonly used on the same team, since Salamence can handle Skarmory and Hippowdon, while Excadrill counters Nihilego, and having these entry hazard setters beaten helps with Vanilluxe's longevity greatly. Zarude lures in Skarmory and Amoonguss and uses U-turn for Vanilluxe to blast them away with Blizzard. Azelf can more easily deal with other Steel-types like Scizor and faster threats like Keldeo, as well as removing Eviolite from Chansey. It also can bring Vanilluxe in on Mandibuzz, giving it more wallbreaking opportunities. Swampert and the aforementioned Excadrill can set up Stealth Rock, which lets Vanilluxe guarantee a 2HKO on defensive Celesteela with Blizzard, as well as nearly always OHKOing Slowking with Freeze-Dry after hail chip damage. Both entry hazard setters take on Rotom-H, and Swampert lures in Tangrowth and Amoonguss for Vanilluxe. Slowking and Chansey provide a defensive backbone against Cobalion and Nihilego, and they let Vanilluxe get in safely with Teleport. Physical attackers like Swords Dance Scizor and Cobalion can take advantage of Chansey for Vanilluxe.

Wallbreaker.description:
By summoning hail, Vanilluxe can enable dangerous Slush Rush sweepers such as Arctovish and Alolan Sandslash. On its own, Vanilluxe can be quite a formidable wallbreaker that takes advantage of common Steelix teams, as such teams usually lack Ice-resistant Pokemon bar Water-types, which fall to Freeze-Dry. However, against teams with Steel-types such as Registeel, Metagross, and Bronzong, Vanilluxe will struggle to make significant progress. Its pure Ice typing leaves Vanilluxe without any defensive utility, which can make it hard to fit on teams and bring onto the field to wallbreak. Freeze-Dry bypasses bulky Water-types like Milotic, Gastrodon, and Jellicent, along with offensive Water-types such as Sharpedo, Golisopod, and Starmie. Ice Shard helps with picking off foes on low HP. Taunt stops walls like Umbreon and Milotic from healing up or inflicting status upon Vanilluxe, while Aurora Veil can help your teammates set up more easily. Icy Rock maximizes hail turns for it and its teammates, while Never-Melt Ice boosts the power of all of its attacks, most notably snatching 2HKOs on Milotic and Steelix with Freeze-Dry and Blizzard, respectively. This makes Never-Melt Ice the preferred item if Vanilluxe chooses to be a standalone wallbreaker. A Timid nature with 232 Speed EVs allows Vanilluxe to outpace Timid Nidoqueen, as there are no relevant Pokemon it outspeeds with maximum Speed. The HP investment ensure it survives Golisopod's First Impression after Stealth Rock and, if Timid, the same for Noivern's Draco Meteor. If running a Naive nature, Vanilluxe should run an EV spread of 8 HP / 16 Atk / 252 SpA / 232 Spe and Never-Melt Ice to survive Golisopod's First Impression after Stealth Rock and KO Flygon after Stealth Rock and hail damage as well as better KO weakened foes generally.

Vanilluxe fits best on semi-hail teams, since Abomasnow and Aurorus support full hail teams better, so it should be partnered with either Arctovish or Alolan Sandslash. Together, they weaken each other's checks such as bulky Water- and Steel-types. Vanilluxe also prefers Ground-types such as Flygon, Nidoqueen, and Rhyperior, which take care of opposing Fire- and Steel-types, and Vanilluxe deals with bulky Water-types in return. Fire Blast Nidoqueen can help with Bronzong. Any entry hazard removers such as Flygon, Starmie, Xatu, and Crobat, along with partners that can bring it in safely, mitigate Vanilluxe's difficulty coming in as a pure Ice-type. Vanilluxe also appreciates bulkier Steel-types like Metagross and Registeel being whittled down; therefore, Spikes setters like Golisopod and Klefki work well with it. Calm Mind Raikou wears down special walls for Vanilluxe, and it can take advantage of Vanilluxe's hail with Weather Ball to surprise Grass- and Ground-types.

nu.overview: Thanks to a powerful STAB Blizzard, Freeze-Dry, and the extra chip from hail, Vanilluxe has separated itself as a potent special wallbreaker capable of muscling past many of the tier's Water- and Steel-types, such as Mantine, Gastrodon, and Stakataka. Despite these traits, Vanilluxe can find it difficult to break past special walls like Snorlax and Sylveon, and because of a terrible defensive typing and Stealth Rock weakness, Vanilluxe struggles to come in safely against many of the tier's defensive staples. On top of that, Vanilluxe faces harsh competition from other special wallbreakers such as Exploud and Starmie that bait in bulky Steel- and Water-types, respectively.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf Vanilluxe can make for a fast and dangerous cleaner with an added benefit of surprise factor, but it is slower than common Choice Scarf users like Passimian and Rotom-C and loses a lot of the immediate wallbreaking power of Choice Specs.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Thanks to Overcoat adding a Hail immunity, Escavalier is the biggest answer to Vanilluxe, but other Steel-types such as Stakataka, Copperajah, and Silvally-Steel are all capable of consistently switching into Vanilluxe and threatening it out.

Fire-types: Although Vanilluxe can scare Salazzle and Arcanine from hitting the field with Water Pulse, both can come in on a Blizzard and reliably force Vanilluxe out. Talonflame can't switch into Vanilluxe, but Flare Blitz variants can consistently KO Vanilluxe after Stealth Rock.

Faster Wallbreakers: Because of Vanilluxe's poor defensive typing and middling Speed tier, many of the tier's offensive wallbreakers such as Jolly Toxicroak, Tauros, Silvally-Ground, and Starmie are powerful offensive answers to Vanilluxe.

Special Walls: Special sponges such as Thick Fat Snorlax and Sylveon are extremely difficult for Vanilluxe to break past without a ton of prior chip damage and entry hazard support.

Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Water Pulse is the coverage move of choice on Vanilluxe in order to hit Stakataka, but it also comes with the added benefit of targeting Fire-types like Salazzle and Arcanine, which are capable of eating an Ice-type attack if needed. In the last slot, Aurora Veil can be used in order to help powerful sweepers like Salazzle and Silvally-Ground set up, but Ice Shard can be used to help pick off weakened threats like Rotom-C and Aerodactyl. Although Choice Specs is usually the preferred item, Heavy-Duty Boots can be run to alleviate entry hazard pressure and ease the need for prediction. Despite the drop in strength, Timid is the preferred nature on Vanilluxe, allowing it to outspeed Pokemon such as Adamant Toxicroak, Tsareena, and Jolly Tyrantrum.

Because of its terrible defensive typing and Stealth Rock weakness, Vanilluxe appreciates pivot support from Pokemon like Rotom-C and Xatu, both of which are capable of clearing away entry hazards for Vanilluxe. Other pivots such as Silvally-Ground, Passimian, and Talonflame help deal with the Steel-types that like to switch into Vanilluxe. Vanilluxe also pairs fantastically with late-game cleaners that want Steel-types chipped such as Ninjask and Tauros. Because Vanilluxe gets scared out by the plethora of faster offensive threats in the tier, having Fighting-, Fire-, and Rock-type answers such as Mantine, Talonflame, and Mudsdale is key to using Vanilluxe on more balanced builds. Escavalier is another phenomenal partner for Vanilluxe because its ability Overcoat stops damage from hail, while Knock Off punishes common checks in Fire- and Steel-types that try to switch in on it.

zu.overview: If you really want to use Emolga in ZU, consider playing BW where it is a top threat. In SS, however, Emolga's stats are underwhelming; it is both too weak to break anything and too frail to use its great typing for defensive purposes. It is outclassed as an offensive Electric-type by Rotom and Manectric, as a Flying-type pivot by Articuno, and as a fast pivot by Alolan Persian; there is truly nothing to save about this flying rat.

Offensive Utility.description: Emolga attemps to make some progress by removing items from opposing walls and generating momentum with U-turn. This set is highly inconsistent because Emolga is both too slow and too weak to force anything out, unless it's been very chipped, and it is too frail to switch into most threats in the tier. Alolan Persian and Rapidash are much more consistent as offensive utility options due to their superior stats, while Palossand, Rhydon, and Stunfisk are better Electric immunities. Will-O-Wisp Rotom is better as a Ground-immune, Electric-type offensive utility option, while Alolan Persian is a more effective fast pivot with access to Knock Off and a better Speed tier. These two also aren't crippled much by entry hazards, unlike Emolga, whose strongest STAB move in Acrobatic is anti-synergistic with Heavy-Duty Boots.

Swords Dance.description:
Escavalier's great defensive typing, Swords Dance, and sufficient coverage let it threaten top-tier threats in RU, such as Reuniclus and Celebi. However, unlike other Steel-types such as Registeel and Stakataka, Escavalier can't set Stealth Rock and isn't a sufficient check to common Flying-types like Togekiss and Crobat, making it harder to justify using. Swords Dance helps Escavalier break past passive foes like Registeel and Gastrodon. Iron Head beats Flying-types such as Noivern, Togekiss, and Crobat. Close Combat dents Steel-types such as Steelix, Registeel, and Lucario, as well Incineroar. Megahorn threatens Reuniclus without setup; however, foes like Bewear and Lucario can capitalize on a lack of Close Combat. Knock Off lets Escavalier cripple checks such as Incineroar, Noivern, and Golisopod, removing their Heavy-Duty Boots, and gives it super effective coverage against Chandelure. 64 Speed EVs and 16 Attack EVs allow Escavalier to outspeed and 2HKO Reuniclus with Swords Dance boosted Knock Off, and 160 Special Defense EVs let it avoid a 2HKO from Calm Mind-boosted Life Orb Reuniclus's Focus Blast.

Escavalier thrives on bulky teams with entry hazard setters, like Nidoqueen, as they appreciate it checking Calm Mind Reuniclus and removing Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off. Diancie and Rhyperior are notable for their ability to handle Fire-types like Chandelure and Incineroar, with Diancie also providing cleric support, and cover Escavalier's shortcoming as a Steel-type that does not resist Flying-types. Jellicent and Milotic appreciate Escavalier's ability to check Grass-types like Roserade and Celebi. Jellicent is particularly valuable as a partner if Escavalier has Megahorn, as without Close Combat, it is setup fodder for Bewear and Lucario. Crobat is an especially good teammate, as it can lure in Rock- and Steel-types like Diancie and Registeel with U-turn for Escavalier. Electric-types like Raikou and Xurkitree can pivot Escavalier in against Grass-types with Volt Switch and also cover Flying-types.

nu.overview: Escavalier offers a useful blend of offensive and defensive traits that makes it an excellent answer to common foes like Snorlax and Diancie. Its Swords Dance sets are potent wallbreakers that can easily dispatch physical walls like Vileplume and Mudsdale whereas its specially defensive set provides teams with a sturdy answer to special attackers such as Starmie, Kingdra, and Choice Specs Decidueye. Additionally, Escavalier is fantastic at luring in and crippling defensive staples like Talonflame, Mudsdale, and Mantine with Knock Off, which makes them much easier to overwhelm throughout a battle. In spite of this, however, Escavalier itself struggles to successfully deal with its counterplay on its own; it can't outduel defensive Fire-types, and bulky Water-types like Mantine and Vaporeon can force it out with the threat of a Scald burn. Additionally, Escavalier is vulnerable to being lured in and heavily damaged or OHKOed by Pokemon like Sylveon and Exploud that it otherwise is a solid answer to. Escavalier's also very reliant on its item for recovery, which makes item removal from the likes of Vileplume and Guzzlord problematic. Lastly, Escavalier's poor Speed makes it easy for faster foes like Salazzle and Toxicroak to dispatch.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band turns Escavalier into an extremely potent wallbreaker with minimal defensive counterplay, although this set is very prediction reliant and can struggle to reliably get by bulky Fire-types like Talonflame and Arcanine. RestTalk gives Escavalier improved longevity, helps if Escavalier loses its Leftovers to Vileplume's Corrosive Gas, and can remove burn inflicted by Talonflame's Flame Body and Rotom-C's Will-O-Wisp. Heavy-Duty Boots is an especially good item on such sets, making Escavalier much harder to wear down through entry hazard damage.

Checks and Counters

Fire-types and Fire-type Coverage: Arcanine and Talonflame are consistent switch-ins to Escavalier thanks to their bulk and abilities, although Knock Off is bothersome for them both. Salazzle is a poor switch-in, but it easily OHKOes Escavalier with Flamethrower. Other Pokemon with Fire-type coverage like Alolan Exeggutor, Sylveon, and Exploud are problematic too, especially since Escavalier frequently switches into them.

Bulky Water-types: Mantine and Vaporeon can switch into an unboosted Escavalier with relative ease and threaten it with a Scald burn. However, if they fail at inflicting a burn, Escavalier can muscle past them with its boosted attacks. Bulky Escavalier sets can also hamper the longevity of such Water-types with Toxic.

Physical Wallbreakers: Despite Escavalier's physical bulk being passable, powerful attackers like Choice Band Tyrantrum, Passimian, and Golurk can still muscle past it, the former not even needing prior chip damage to do so.

Specially Defensive.description:
Set Details

The combination of Knock Off and Toxic makes it difficult for Pokemon like Talonflame, Mantine, and Arcanine to take advantage of Escavalier. Protect complements this move combination well, letting Escavalier poison stall foes and scout powerful Choice item attackers like Tyrantrum, Gallade, and Guzzlord. Swords Dance instead of Toxic is also viable so that Escavalier can take advantage of passive foes like Vileplume and Xatu.

Escavalier is very effective at luring in and crippling bulky Water-types like Mantine and Vaporeon with Toxic; this makes Pokemon like Starmie, Salazzle, and Inteleon effective teammates. In return, Starmie and Inteleon can easily get rid of Fire-types, while Salazzle can work alongside Escavalier to bypass said foes. Despite Escavalier not being helpless against opposing Fire-types, it still appreciates teammates like Guzzlord, Vaporeon, and Diancie that can directly deal with them. Escavalier also benefits from physically defensive teammates such as Sylveon and Mudsdale to take on powerful physical attackers. Cleric support from teammates like Sylveon and Vaporeon is helpful so Escavalier doesn't have to worry as much about burns; these two can also supply Wish support for it, greatly boosting its longevity.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Close Combat provides necessary coverage for Copperajah and opposing Escavalier, while Knock Off prevents Fire-types like Talonflame, Salazzle, and Arcanine from freely switching into Escavalier. The listed EV spread allows Escavalier to outpace Dhelmise, but other spreads are possible too. For example, Escavalier can also opt for much bulkier spreads so it can better take attacks like Exploud's Boomburst and Rotom-C's Thunderbolt.

Escavalier appreciates the removal of Fire-types like Salazzle, Talonflame, and Arcanine so it can more freely wallbreak; teammates like Inteleon, Mantine, and Guzzlord are effective here. Late-game cleaners like Dragon Dance Tyrantrum and Swords Dance Decidueye benefit from Escavalier shredding opposing defensive cores and weakening physical walls like Mudsdale and Vileplume. In return, the former helps pressure Fire-types, whereas the latter can deal with Water-types. Pokemon such as Ninjask appreciate Escavalier's ability to handle Fairy-types; in return, Ninjask can bring Escavalier in against such foes with U-turn.
The Attack investment allows it to OHKO standard Milotic with Megahorn after a Swords Dance boost.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Foongus can run more Speed EVs to outspeed foes like Timburr and Mareanie while helping in the Foongus mirror. 124 HP EVs make it easier to deal with threats like Mudbray. Foongus's movepool isn't good, and it is usually limited to the four listed moves. Stun Spore and Clear Smog can be used as alternative move options, but they are extremely situational; Stun Spore cripples multiple foes, and Clear Smog prevents setup sweepers like Galarian Ponyta from setting up on Foongus.

Checks and Counters

Ferroseed: Ferroseed is probably the most effective check against Foongus, as it resists Giga Drain and is immune to Sludge Bomb and Spore. It can easily switch into Foongus and start setting its entry hazards or remove Foongus's Eviolite with Knock Off. Ferroseed paired with Mienfoo can be very difficult for Foongus to make progress against.

Other Steel-types: Steel-types like Magnemite and Pawniard resist both of Foongus's listed attacks, and Pawniard also threatens it with Knock Off. However, none of them appreciate Spore.

Koffing: Koffing resists both Foongus's STAB moves, does a lot of damage in return, and wears down Foongus with Neutralizing Gas.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types such as Abra, Galarian Ponyta, and Psychic coverage from Staryu threaten Foongus, but they dislike Spore.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Ponyta, Vulpix, and Charmander threaten Foongus offensively but have a difficult time switching into Spore and Sludge Bomb.

Tank.description:
Foongus is one of the best walls in LC, being able to take on dangerous threats like Mienfoo, Diglett, and Grookey with its combination of decent bulk, amazing typing, and Spore. Spore cripples a non-Grass-type foe, preventing setup sweepers like Tyrunt from performing their role, and it gives Foongus's teammates a chance to switch in safely. Giga Drain and Synthesis provide recovery and both increase Foongus's longevity. Regenerator lets it pivot into opposing threats like Mienfoo and Mareanie repeatedly. The given EV spread denies Porygon from getting a Special Attack boost from Download.

Foongus forms a great defensive core with bulky Water-types such as Frillish and Staryu, as it checks physical threats like Grookey for them; in return, they check Fire-types like Ponyta and Vulpix. Mienfoo forms a great Regenerator core with Foongus, and it can eliminate annoying Steel-types like Pawniard and Ferroseed. Fire-types like Ponyta are also a solid choice for dealing with Steel-types. Trapinch and Ponyta are both reliable partners to deal with the troublesome Ferroseed; Ponyta punishes it clicking entry hazards and can click its STAB moves to cook Ferroseed, while Trapinch can trap and eliminate it. Foongus struggles against Psychic-types like Abra, so Pawniard makes a great teammate for it. Pawniard in return benefits from Foongus's ability to deal with Fighting-types.

uu.overview: Amoonguss is a potent defensive wall due to its good defensive typing, which enables it to check dangerous foes such as Azumarill, Primarina, and Zarude, combined with its access to Regenerator. Access to Spore allows Amoonguss to shut down an opposing foe completely, making it harder to play around and offensively check due to pressuring opponents to choose sleep fodder. Its Poison typing additionally gives it an edge over other common Grass-types, as it is able to threaten Tangrowth and Zarude with Sludge Bomb, which also prevents them from switching in to absorb Spore. However, despite Amoonguss's good defensive typing, it struggles against metagame staples like Salamence and Crobat. It can also be overwhelmed by Pokemon it is supposed to check due to their access to coverage, such as Ice Punch from Azumarill, Psychic from Primarina, and Air Slash from Keldeo. After using Spore, Amoonguss is easy to take advantage of by Pokemon that take little from its other moves such as Galarian Slowbro, Celesteela, Skarmory, and Cobalion. Amoonguss faces competition from Tangrowth as a defensive Grass-type wall, which can opt to run Assault Vest sets to check specially offensive foes such as Thundurus-T better, not be neutral to Excadrill and Zygarde-10%'s Ground-type STAB, and avoid being setup bait for Swords Dance Cobalion if something else has been hit with Spore.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Seed Bomb keeps Amoonguss from being set up on by Substitute + Calm Mind Primarina, but it does less damage to most other Water-types and loses out on the recovery of Giga Drain, not to mention a burn from Scald can render this move useless. Stomping Tantrum is an option to hit Nihilego and Cobalion for solid damage rather than rely on Spore to neuter them. Assault Vest allows Amoonguss to act as an even better check to special attackers like Keldeo and Thundurus-T, and it can still run utility moves like Spore due to Amoonguss's tendency to get hit with Knock Off.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types and Psychic-type coverage: Offensive Psychic-types like Necrozma and Azelf can force out Amoonguss with their powerful attacks. If it has Safety Goggles, Galarian Slowbro can easily setup on Amoonguss. Psychic-type coverage like Psychic Fangs on Lycanroc-D and Psychic on Primarina and Thundurus-T also dent Amoonguss.

Fire-types: Rotom-H threatens Amoonguss with Overheat and can gain momentum with Volt Switch. Moltres and Chandelure can threaten to OHKO Amoonguss with their powerful STAB.

Flying-types and Flying-type Coverage: Salamence and Togekiss deal heavy damage to Amoonguss with their STAB attacks. Skarmory, Crobat, and Celesteela don't fear anything from Amoonguss barring Spore and can easily take advantage of it when Spore is used. Flying-type coverage like Air Slash on Keldeo and Dual Wingbeat on Scizor keep Amoonguss from reliably taking them on, leaving it to be careful switching into them.

Strong Wallbreakers: While Amoonguss is bulky, it can be overwhelmed by wallbreakers such as Nidoking, Mamoswine, Zygarde-10%, and Hydreigon. These Pokemon all fear Spore, however, so they can only effectively threaten Amoonguss if a teammate has been put to sleep or they are brought in safely. Conkeldurr is able to overwhelm Amoonguss with Facade and is immune to Spore once its Flame Orb activates. Cobalion completely counters Amoonguss after Spore and can freely use it to boost with Swords Dance.

Defensive.description:
Spore shuts down Pokemon such as Moltres and Scizor, deterring them from wanting to pivot into it. This often requires an opposing team to use a Pokemon as sleep fodder, making it easier for Amoonguss's teammates to capitalize on. Stun Spore is an option that can be run over Spore to potentially cripple Pokemon like Celesteela, Cobalion, and Nihilego that would otherwise wall it once a Pokemon has been slept. It can also be used more often due to Sleep Clause. Giga Drain heavily damages Rotom-W and Keldeo, which Amoonguss naturally checks by virtue of its typing and bulk. It also enables Amoonguss to regain some HP, reducing the need for it to continually pivot for Regenerator recovery. Alternatively, Synthesis can be run to instantly regain health, though its low PP should be noticed, and Hippowdon's sand can limit the amount of health recovered by it. Sludge Bomb threatens Primarina, Zarude, and Azumarill. It is also useful for the chance to poison switch-ins such as Salamence and Mandibuzz. Foul Play dents physical attackers such as Gyarados and Scizor and prevents them from setting up on Amoonguss, and it is also Amoonguss's best way to damage other Steel-types such as Jirachi. Rocky Helmet punishes physical attackers Amoonguss switches into such as Azumarill and Zarude. Black Sludge is an alternative option that reduces Amoonguss's reliance on switching out to regain HP with Regenerator. Eject Button can be run so Amoonguss can pivot into a foe, take a hit, and bring in a teammate safely. 36 Special Defense EVs guarantee that Amoonguss can take a Choice Specs-boosted Psychic from Primarina as well as better check Keldeo.

Amoonguss fits best on bulky offense, balance, and stall teams that appreciate its ability to blanket check dangerous metagame staples such as Tangrowth and Primarina. Chansey can take on special attackers like Nidoking, Moltres, and Salamence that can overwhelm Amoonguss. Checks to Moltres and Salamence, such as Hippowdon and Primarina, are useful partners that can switch into them and force it out. They also can take on Cobalion after Spore has been burned. Krookodile and Mandibuzz can check Psychic-types like Galarian Slowbro and Azelf. Mandibuzz also helps Amoonguss not get overwhelmed by Zygarde-10%. Slower wallbreakers like Conkeldurr appreciate Salamence and Skarmory being crippled by Stun Spore. Amoonguss is heavily threatened by Fire-types such as Moltres and Rotom-H, so checks to these such as Slowking and Swampert make good partners. Amoonguss is vulnerable to Stealth Rock and Spikes chip damage, and gives free opportunities for Pokemon such as Nihilego and Skarmory to set these after Spore has been used, so entry hazard removal support from partners such as Salamence and Excadrill enables it to switch in more often and prevents entry hazards from cancelling out its Regenerator recovery.

Regenerator in tandem with solid defensive stats and typing makes Amoonguss a fine defensive pivot and a nice check to the likes of Clefable, Zeraora, and Rillaboom. Since it has access to all of Spore, Toxic, and Stun Spore, it is not easy to switch into either. It fits best on balance teams looking for a sturdy check to Zeraora. Slowbro is one of Amoonguss's most common partners to form a Regenerator core, and it is able to check threats like Excadrill and Alakazam.

monotype.overview:
Grass

Amoonguss is a great pivot for Grass teams because of Regenerator and its defensive typing providing a Bug neutrality and resistances to check physical attackers like Heracross and Azumarill. Furthermore, its Fighting resistance is great because Grass teams have common Fighting weaknesses like Ferrothorn, Cradily, and Zarude. Its Poison typing absorbs Toxic Spikes, which is useful since Grass teams lack a good entry hazard remover. Its access to Spore cripples opposing Pokemon, giving teammates like Zarude and Rillaboom opportunities to come in. Unfortunately, Amoonguss is forced out by Pokemon carrying super effective coverage such as Hydreigon, Zapdos, and Heatran and special attackers like Nihilego, Spectrier, and Kingdra. Furthermore, Amoonguss easily becomes bait for setup sweepers like Galarian Moltres and Volcarona and hazard setters like Klefki and Mew after it has used Spore on a foe already. Finally, it has a hard time making progress against defensive Grass-types like Ferrothorn and opposing Amoonguss.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Grass

Clear Smog is an option to prevent setup sweepers like Clefable and Tapu Fini from using Amoonguss as setup fodder. Stun Spore slows down fast Pokemon like Latios, Choice Scarf Heatran, and Galarian Zapdos to help offensive teammates like Zarude and Rillaboom revenge kill more easily. A pinch Berry like Occa Berry or Payapa Berry has a use in surviving a Fire- or Psychic-type attack from Cinderace or Tapu Lele, respectively.

Checks and Counters

Grass

Steel-types: Many Steel-types like Celesteela, Heatran, and Melmetal take very little damage from Amoonguss and can retaliate with their respective attacks; however, they don't appreciate switching into Spore.

Dragon types: Kyurem, Choice Specs Dragapult, and Hydreigon can threaten Amoonguss with powerful special attacks. Kyurem and Hydreigon can notably use Substitute and avoid Amoonguss's Spore.

Taunt: Taunt users like Corviknight, Tapu Fini, and Mew can cripple Amoonguss from using status moves. They can also use Amoonguss as setup fodder after using Taunt.

Electric Terrain and Misty Terrain: Electric Terrain and Misty Terrain prevent grounded Pokemon like Alolan Raichu and Klefki from being affected by Spore.

Residual Damage: If Amoonguss isn't wearing Heavy-Duty Boots, it makes it difficult to switch into physical attackers like Excadrill on Steel and Zarude on opposing Grass, both types which are known for stacking Stealth Rock and Spikes. Will-O-Wisp also factors in longevity when switching into attacks.

Defensive Pivot (Grass).description:
Spore allows Amoonguss to cripples many Pokemon to give teammates chances to come in. Sludge Bomb synergizes well with Spore, since it targets Pokemon immune to Spore like the Guardian Deities. Foul Play checks physical attackers like Bisharp and Dragapult that could try using it as setup fodder. Heavy-Duty Boots is used to help with durability, since Grass teams don't run entry hazard removal; however, Black Sludge is an alternative.

All of Amoonguss's teammates, especially its offensive teammates in Zarude and Rillaboom, appreciate its Spore to give them opportunities to come in and ability to absorb Toxic Spikes. Amoonguss forms a defensive core alongside Ferrothorn and Cradily, and both notably can check Ice-types like Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales and provide entry hazard support. Ferrothorn's typing allows it to check Psychic-, Dragon-, and Flying-types such as Tapu Lele, Dragapult, and Dragonite. It also has utilities like Thunder Wave, Toxic, and Knock Off to cripple defensive Pokemon like opposing Ferrothorn and Skarmory that Amoonguss relies on teammates to get rid of. Cradily checks special attackers like Zapdos, Volcarona, and Heatran and Substitute users like Hydreigon, Galarian Moltres, and Togekiss with Rock Blast. Whimsicott checks Fighting-, Dragon-, and Dark-types like Guts Heracross, Dragonite, and Mandibuzz along with Substitute users like Galarian Moltres and Kommo-o. Zarude and Rillaboom gets rid of defensive Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Aegislash thanks to their Fighting + Dark coverage. Zarude checks Psychic-types like Latios and Tapu Lele thanks to its Dark typing, while Rillaboom revenge kills threats like Nihilego, Alolan Ninetales, and Mamoswine for Amoonguss. Zarude notably appreciates Amoonguss's ability to check Fairy- and Fighting-types like Tapu Bulu and Buzzwole.

Defensive Pivot (Poison).description:
Amoonguss is a fantastic defensive pivot for Poison teams thanks to Regenerator and its Grass typing, allowing it to take neutral damage from Ground-type attacks and switch into attacks such as Choice Scarf Excadrill's Earthquake even with Stealth Rock up. Spore allows Amoonguss to put threats such as Diggersby and Excadrill to sleep and avoid becoming set up bait against setup sweepers such as Bisharp. Giga Drain allows Amoonguss to target Ground- and Water-type Pokemon such as Hippowdon, Krookodile, Seismitoad, and Keldeo. Foul Play allows Amoonguss to punish physical setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Scizor and Pokemon weak to Dark such as Dragapult. Stomping Tantrum is an option to punish Salazzle, a pain to face for Poison teams, but it is not good in any other matchup. Synthesis gives Amoonguss a reliable form of recovery and also allows it to switch into Choice Scarf Excadrill through the match continually. Black Sludge gives Amoonguss a form of passive recovery, and Regenerator allows Amoonguss to excel as a defensive pivot. Its EVs and Bold nature allow Amoonguss to avoid a 2HKO from physical attacks such as Choice Scarf Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock damage.

Toxapex and Amoonguss form the Regenerator core on Poison teams. Toxapex also provides Amoonguss with a switch-in to Fire- and Ice-type attacks from Pokemon such as Charizard and Weavile. In return, Amoonguss can tank Electric-type attacks for Toxapex, such as Zeraora's Plasma Fists. Galarian Weezing can switch into powerful Dragon-type attacks for Amoonguss, such as Hydreigon's Draco Meteor. Galarian Weezing also switches into Ground-type attacks that Amoonguss cannot, such as Choice Band Diggersby's Earthquake, as well as cripple physical attackers such as Terrakion with Will-O-Wisp. Skuntank provides a switch-in to Psychic-type attacks and can check dangerous threats to Amoonguss with Sucker Punch, such as Alolan Raichu and Dragapult. Both can also clear entry hazards for Amoonguss with Defog. Amoonguss can put foes to sleep for Gengar with Spore, allowing Gengar to break through the opposing team more easily. Gengar can, in return, cripple walls for Amoonguss like Toxapex by using Trick, making them near deadweight. Salazzle keeps faster foes in check and can check Pokemon such as Excadrill with Flamethrower, taking the burden off Amoonguss to switch into its Earthquake. Salazzle can also significantly improve the Poison- and Steel-type matchup by crippling foes such as Corviknight and Toxapex with Toxic thanks to its ability Corrosion. Scolipede is a powerful setup sweeper that can break through walls such as Chansey with Megahorn and threaten Psychic teams very effectively thanks to Speed Boost and its ability to OHKO or 2HKO all Psychic-type Pokemon. While not incredibly viable, Toxtricity can take on Flying-type Pokemon such as Corviknight, Mantine, and Mandibuzz with Overdrive, which otherwise wall Amoonguss.

vgc2022.overview: With access to Spore, Rage Powder, and Regenerator, Amoonguss acts as a great support Pokemon on teams that take advantage of the free turns that it provides through redirection and status. Amoonguss's low Speed also makes it one of the strongest Trick Room checks in VGC 2022, as once Trick Room is set up, it can move before almost every common Pokemon and put them to sleep with Spore. Amoonguss is often paired with some of the most potent Restricted Pokemon in the metagame like Zacian-C, Kyogre, and Palkia due to its ability to buy extra turns for them and them checking threats to it like Incineroar and Rotom-H. However, a few prominent weaknesses prevent Amoonguss from being a complete menace to the format. Pokemon like Incineroar, Rotom-H, and Zapdos deal heavy damage to Amoonguss and commonly use Safety Goggles to be immune to Spore and Rage Powder. Amoonguss also has a glaring weakness to Max Airstream—one of the most common Max Moves used in the format. Amoonguss can also simply be OHKOed by powerful attackers like Charizard, Calyrex-I, and Calyrex-S before they Dynamax.
vgc2022.comments:
Other Options

Amoonguss has a fair amount of flexibility, commonly tailoring its set towards a team's specific needs. Instead of the typical EV spread, Amoonguss can run 252 Speed EVs with a Timid nature to surprise opponents with fast Spores, especially when paired with speed control such as Tailwind or Max Airstream. Instead of using Giga Drain, Amoonguss can use Energy Ball to provide additional damage against Pokemon like Gastrodon, Kyogre, and Blastoise, although Energy Ball does not hit any specific benchmarks and may not be worth giving up the recovery from Pollen Puff or Giga Drain. Foul Play is another option that can deal considerable damage to Calyrex-S and common Weakness Policy users like Solgaleo and Necrozma-DM, especially at +2, but Amoonguss's weaknesses to those Pokemon makes this is a niche option. Foul Play is best utilized on teams with Trick Room modes, where Amoonguss can move before those Pokemon. Occa Berry is another option for teams that want to shore up matchups against Pokemon like Incineroar and Rotom-H, although Amoonguss can already survive many Fire-type attacks. Also, many common Fire-type Pokemon oftentimes run Safety Goggles, limiting Amoonguss's efficacy against them, even if Occa Berry is activated.

Support.description:
• Spore is an incredibly powerful move in VGC 2022 due to its ability to incapacitate an opponent's Dynamaxed or Restricted Pokemon for multiple turns, which can massively swing the momentum of battles.

  • Rage Powder is a staple move in Doubles, allowing Amoonguss to use its high bulk to shield its partner from attacks.

  • Pollen Puff heals allies, which is especially effective when opposing Pokemon are asleep. Pollen Puff also ensures that Amoonguss isn't completely neutralized by Taunt, breaks potential Focus Sashes, and chips in for small amounts of damage. However, teams that have difficulty dealing with bulky Water-type Pokemon like Gastrodon may opt to use Giga Drain to chunk them down and provide some recovery to Amoonguss.

  • Coba Berry is Amoonguss's primary item due to the ubiquity of Max Airstream in VGC 2022, allowing it to survive the move from Pokemon like Landorus-T and Thundurus and put them to sleep or provide further Rage Powder support for its allies. Alternatively, Focus Sash trades the ability to potentially survive multiple other attacks after a Max Airstream for the ability to survive a plethora of super effective Max Moves and other powerful moves such as Expanding Force from Calyrex-S.

  • The given EV spread allows Amoonguss to always survive a Behemoth Blade from maximum Attack Zacian-C, with the rest of the EVs being used to maximize Special Defense. 27 Speed IVs ensure that Amoonguss is slower than minimum Speed Calyrex-I, allowing Amoonguss to move before it under Trick Room and use Spore while also allowing Amoonguss to outspeed and use Spore on Torkoal outside of Trick Room.

Utility.description:
Amoonguss's good bulk and good utility make it a great support Pokemon with the tools to deal with the majority of the metagame. Clear Smog resets the boosts of Geomancy Xerneas and Cosmic Power Eternatus. Amoonguss will always carry Rage Powder, redirecting powerful attacks such as Zacian's Behemoth Blade and Regieleki's Thunder away from its common allies like Xerneas and Kyogre. Spore is used to disrupt the enemy team with sleep while also breaking Trick Room setups. Other options are Pollen Puff to heal your own Pokemon and Grass Knot to hit Groudon and Kyogre hard. Amoonguss will usually carry a Mental Herb to shake off Taunt from threats such as Whimsicott, Tornadus, and Incineroar, but it can also run an Occa Berry to survive Groudon's Heat Crash, Volcarona's Overheat, and Incineroar's Flare Blitz and put them to sleep in return. Regenerator provides Amoonguss longevity, while its EV spread makes it survive a +1 Behemoth Blade from Zacian-C and a Hurricane from Tornadus, although it can never survive a Calyrex-S Expanding Force. Unfortunately, Amoonguss's low offensive presence makes it rely heavily on its partners to deal significant damage. This makes Volcarona and Rillaboom often preferred over it.

Amoonguss is a great partner for Zacian-C and Xerneas, since both Pokemon appreciate its redirection and support for setting up or preserving their health. Kyogre is another good option, since its rain weakens Fire-type moves. Fire-types such as Entei and Incineroar are also appreciated, since they can power through opposing Grass-types like Rillaboom and Tsareena easily, which can disrupt Amoonguss because they're immune to Rage Powder and Spore. Landorus, Palkia, and Urshifu-R are other good allies to KO opposing Fire-type Pokemon such as Incineroar and Volcarona.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

A more physically defensive spread with a Rocky Helmet can be run to check Mega Lopunny and do a bit better against Rillaboom and Kartana, but it isn't even that great against the latter two and leaves Amoonguss vulnerable to Ash-Greninja. Stun Spore can be used to spread paralysis, but Amoonguss tends to miss out on important targets if it drops any of its moves. Toxic can also be run to spread the status onto threats that are generally crippled by it, such as Mega Latias, Hydreigon, Slowbro, Slowking, and Zapdos, but this runs into the same moveslot issues as Stun Spore. An Assault Vest set makes Amoonguss an even bulkier check to threats such as Ash-Greninja and Tapu Koko while also allowing it to lure Heatran via Stomping Tantrum; however, losing out on Spore is annoying, and the Heatran luring strategy can fall apart if your opponent sees that your Amoonguss isn't running Black Sludge. Hidden Power Ice can be used to hit Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Gliscor, but losing Hidden Power Fire prevents Amoonguss from checking Kartana or pushing any sort of meaningful damage onto Ferrothorn or Mega Mawile

Checks and Counters

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Heatran, Victini, Mega Charizard X, Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona all threaten Amoonguss with their STAB moves, although none of them want to get put to sleep.

Flying-types: Flying-types threaten Amoonguss with their STAB moves, and many of them take very little damage from its standard moves. Corviknight, Landorus-T, and Hawlucha all fit with this. Gliscor, while not running any Flying-type STAB moves, can't be put to sleep after its Toxic Orb activates and easily sets up on variants not running Clear Smog or Hidden Power Ice.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types, such as Mega Medicham, Tapu Lele, Reuniclus, and Mega Latias can all threaten Amoonguss greatly. Slowbro and Slowking can also use Future Sight to apply extra pressure and prevent Amoonguss from switching into what it's normally tasked with. They all have to beware of Spore, however.

Ice-types: Weavile and Kyurem force out Amoonguss with their powerful STAB moves. Weavile struggles to switch in more than once even if Amoonguss has already used Spore, but SubRoost Kyurem doesn't always have its Substitutes broken by Amoonguss, making it an especially dangerous foe.

Specially Defensive.description:
Amoonguss is a bulky special wall that is hard to wear down thanks to Regenerator. It is capable of checking dangerous threats such as Ash-Greninja, Clefable, and Tapu Koko. Spore is capable of almost guaranteeing putting a non-Grass-type foe out of commission via sleep. This is especially effective considering most Grass-types, as well as the sleep blocking Tapu Fini, cannot safely switch into Amoonguss. This also makes Pokemon that would otherwise be able to absorb Sludge Bomb easily, such as Corviknight and Toxapex, hesitant to switch in due to the threat of Spore. Hidden Power Fire hits Kartana and Ferrothorn while also applying some chip to other Steel-types, such as Mega Scizor, Magnezone, and Mega Mawile. Clear Smog can be used over Sludge Bomb to shut down setup attempts from Calm Mind Clefable, Calm Mind Tapu Fini, Swords Dance Gliscor, and a reckless Manaphy, but Sludge Bomb's poison chance and ability to apply more damage to Rillaboom, Tangrowth, and Serperior makes it the preferred option. 56 Defense EVs allow Amoonguss to tank a +2 Smart Strike from Kartana and a +2 Life Orb Knock Off from Rillaboom. 204 Special Defense EVs and a Calm nature allow Amoonguss to tank two Dark Pulses from a transformed Ash-Greninja if at full health. Regenerator is the preferred ability, as it allows Amoonguss to regain health every time it switches out, therefore letting it pivot into threats such as Ash-Greninja, Tapu Koko, and Zeraora consistently.

Amoonguss is bait for most of the metagame's Fire-types, especially if Spore has already been used. Water-types such as Slowking and Tapu Fini are capable of checking the very threatening Heatran, while a bulky Dragon-type such as Garchomp or Kommo-o can help out against Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. The aforementioned Water-types appreciate Amoonguss checking Electric-types such as Tapu Koko, Magnezone, and Zeraora, while the Dragon-types appreciate Amoonguss dealing with Fairy-types such as Clefable and Tapu Fini. Slowking also appreciates Amoonguss checking Ash-Greninja, while the two of them can work together to form a Regenerator core that is tough to break. A Ground-type, such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, or Gliscor, can also prevent Amoonguss from being pivoted on by Volt Switch by the aforementioned Electric-types. A Dark-resistant Pokemon, such as Clefable or Mega Tyranitar, can also help Amoonguss pivot around Ash-Greninja effectively. Amoonguss is a Grass-type that is incapable of properly checking Ground-types, such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Gliscor, as well as Rillaboom. A bulky Flying-type, most notably Corviknight, can help out with this, as can a powerful offensive Ice-type, such as Weavile or Kyurem. Corviknight can also help out Amoonguss against Psychic-types such as Tapu Lele and Mega Latias.

doublesou.overview: Amoonguss is one of the best support Pokemon in the metagame, capable of redirecting attacks with Rage Powder or putting foes to sleep with Spore. It is bulky enough to live most attacks, and the added survivability from Regenerator allows it to perform its role repeatedly throughout a match. Additionally, Pollen Puff ensures Amoonguss's teammates can also remain healthy. Setup Pokemon, such as Dragon Dance Zygarde or Kyurem-B and Calm Mind Tapu Fini, benefit the most from Amoonguss's support and can make up for its minimal damage output. Due to its low Speed and Spore, Amoonguss also works well both with and against Trick Room teams, as it can then send most Pokemon to sleep before they move. Trick Room users such as Porygon2 and Diancie also appreciate the redirection support while setting it. Despite being able to stomach most hits, Amoonguss must be wary of Fire-types such as Heatran and Incineroar as well as Psychic-types such as Tapu Lele and Necrozma, requiring teammates to deal with them such as Urshifu-R and Heatran, respectively. The presence of Misty Terrain hampers Amoonguss's Spore, so terrain setters such as Tapu Lele and Indeedee-F, or Metagross with Steel Roller, are essential to remove it. Opposing Grass-types such as Rillaboom, or Pokemon holding Safety Goggles, can also be troublesome, as immunity to powder moves lets them mostly ignore Amoonguss and attack its partner. Blastoise, its biggest competitor as a redirector, doesn't share this drawback.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Resist berries such as Occa and Papaya allow Amoonguss to live certain attacks that it would not otherwise. Eject Button lets Amoonguss redirect a hit and then immediately switch out, e.g. for helping to set Trick Room or Tailwind and then getting an attacker in to benefit right away. However, Eject Button can be awkward if Amoonguss intends to use Spore and gets forced out instead or needs to redirect two attacks. Another option is Rocky Helmet, which provides chip damage on physical attackers such as Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Genesect. These alternate item choices are not as generally useful as the recovery from Sitrus Berry, though. Clear Smog is a weaker Poison-type STAB move compared to Sludge Bomb, but it can be used instead to help deal with opposing setup. A Grass-type STAB move such as Energy Ball could also be considered, but it cannot effectively hit the Pokemon immune to Spore, while the Pokemon it does hit harder than Sludge Bomb are vulnerable to Spore, so there is little reason to use it.

Rage Powder Support.description:
• Sludge Bomb is Amoonguss's primary offensive option, hitting Tapu Fini as well as Grass-types like Rillaboom, which are immune to Spore. Protect can be used instead to scout for moves such as Choice Scarf Genesect locking into Ice Beam, but this leaves Amoonguss quite passive.

  • Pollen Puff heals Amoonguss's partner.

  • Rage Powder keeps partners safe from attacks and is most effective when used alongside setup Pokemon, or while setting field conditions such as Trick Room and Tailwind.

  • Besides critically putting foes out of action, Spore helps ensure Amoonguss is not too passive while on the field.

  • Sitrus Berry complements Amoonguss's bulk, turning many would-be 2HKOs into 3HKOs instead, such as Ice Beam from non-Life Orb Kyurem-B.

  • Regenerator also helps Amoonguss's longevity on switching out, which can let it give future utility even when at low health.

  • The given EV spread and nature, combined with Sitrus Berry, allow Amoonguss to live two Heat Waves from Volcanion, with the remaining EVs placed in Defense. 28 Speed IVs let it underspeed Diancie to move first under Trick Room while still being able to outspeed foes with the help of speed control.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Psychic can beat one of Frillish's checks, Mareanie, and also can deal heavy damage to Fighting-types. Strength Sap can provide more recovery than Recover against certain foes, but is inconsistent and risks activating Pawniard's Defiant.

Checks and Counters

Ferroseed: Ferroseed is an effective Frillish check, thanks to its Water resistance and general bulk. It also threatens Frillish with Knock Off and Giga Drain, taking turns spent on Recover to set entry hazards. However, it has to be careful of being burned by Scald or Will-O-Wisp, which strengthens Hex.

Carvanha: Carvanha is the best offensive check to Frillish, due to the pressure its powerful Crunch exerts. However, its frailty and fear of burns mean it cannot switch in easily.

Grookey: Similarly to Carvanha, Grookey can threaten Frillish with its powerful super-effective attacks, but it can't switch into Frillish safely.

Pawniard: Pawniard is one of the biggest threats to Frillish with Knock Off. Although it must be generally wary of Will-O-Wisp and Scald, it can still cause issues for Frillish when burned.

Magnemite: Magnemite threatens Frillish with its super effective Electric-type attacks and can preserve momentum with Volt Switch.

Super Effective Coverage: Frillish needs to be careful even against threats it is supposed to check. Ponyta and Psychic-types like Abra and Natu can have Wild Charge or Shadow Ball. It should also be cautious of Knock Off from other Pokemon, such as Mienfoo and Mareanie. Pokemon like Koffing, Staryu, and Porygon also pose a threat with Thunderbolt.

Tank.description:
Frillish is a tank that can shrug off powerful special hits and take physical hits decently well. Frillish's typing makes it a deterrent for Porygon and Mienfoo, preventing them from spamming Tri Attack and Ice Beam or High Jump Kick. Its Fire resistance causes issues for sun teams as well. Scald and Will-O-Wisp make physical attackers with good matchups such as Pawniard and Grookey hesitant to switch into Frillish in fear of a burn. Burns also empower Hex, which hits statused unresisted targets very hard. Cursed Body lets Frillish sometimes win one-on-one against lesser offensive threats like Mienfoo or Staryu by disabling their super effective moves.

Pokemon that appreciate Frillish's presence include Grookey and Steel-types such as Pawniard and Ferroseed, since they are weak to Fire-types, which Frillish can switch into repeatedly. Fighting-types such as Mienfoo and Timburr appreciate Frillish's ability to deal with Psychic-types like Abra and Natu. They return the favor by switching into Steel-types that cause Frillish trouble. Fire-types like Ponyta and Poison-types like Koffing and Foongus are the best ways to deal with Grookey and Ferroseed, which force Frillish out. Morelull deserves a special mention for its ability to reliably switch into Carvanha, and it can also help spread status to let Frillish deal more damage with Hex.

Choice Scarf.description:
With a Choice Scarf, Frillish outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame, becoming an excellent attacker and revenge killer with some surprise factor. Water Spout devastates most Pokemon when Frillish is at full health, while Hydro Pump deals less damage initially but is stronger at lower HP. Shadow Ball deals good damage to Psychic-types such as Abra and Natu, as well as opposing Frillish, and is Frillish's best option against Ferroseed. Ice Beam can be used to hit Grass-types such as Grookey and Morelull. However, the fourth move slot is flexible; Trick can be used to debilitate walls such as Ferroseed and Trace Porygon.

Frillish does not enjoy entry hazards weakening Water Spout, so Pokemon such as Drilbur and Natu that can provide hazard control make excellent teammates. Dark-types and Knock Off users also naturally scare out Frillish, so Fighting-types such as Mienfoo and Timburr are useful. Trappers such as Trapinch trap Steel-types that can counter Frillish, such as Pawniard. Grookey and Ferroseed completely counter Frillish, so Fire-types such as Ponyta and Poison-types such as Koffing are helpful teammates.

uu.overview: Jellicent establishes itself a niche in UU on balance and stall teams through its combination of valuable defensive typing and stallbreaking capabilities. Its typing and Will-O-Wisp allow it to check a variety of highly viable Pokemon such as Scizor, Cobalion, and Keldeo, while Taunt lets it shut down defensive Pokemon such as Chansey, Celesteela, and Skarmory; shutting down the first in particular gives it a great matchup versus opposing bulky teams. Jellicent has two useful abilities as well. Cursed Body Jellicent can eventually overpower certain defensive Pokemon such as Amoonguss and RestTalk Primarina by potentially disabling their only moves that can harm it. Cursed Body also lets it switch into Scald and potentially take a burn to avoid being poisoned later on. On the other hand, Water Absorb makes Jellicent an even more reliable Water-type check, countering rarer threats such as rain wallbreakers or SubCM Keldeo and deterring Choice Specs Primarina from spamming a Water-type attack. While Jellicent has an impressive defensive profile, its need to invest heavily into Speed to outspeed Skarmory and Conkeldurr leaves it with less-than-ideal bulk, which can make it struggle to reliably and comfortably check Pokemon such as Excadrill, Swords Dance + Stone Edge Cobalion, and Swords Dance + Knock Off Scizor if lacking Colbur Berry. Jellicent must also be wary of status, especially on balance teams lacking cleric support. Multiple Pokemon it would otherwise like to pressure such as Hippowdon, Chansey, non-Giga Drain Amoonguss, and Galarian Slowbro can potentially poison Jellicent if it hasn't taken a Scald burn. This forces Jellicent to be more predictable with Taunt versus Toxic users, such as the former two, and more careful around Sludge Bomb users like the latter two. With cleric support on stall teams, status is less of an issue, but Jellicent's need for passive turns is still very much present, and it can offer wallbreakers such as Thundurus-T and Hydreigon free entry still.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Jellicent can consider running Scald over Will-O-Wisp to more directly threaten certain Pokemon such as Nihilego, Nidoqueen, and Nidoking, alongside the ability to burn Hatterene, but the unreliable burn chance gives up a lot of solidity against dangerous physical attackers such as Scizor and Cobalion.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Amoonguss and Tangrowth dislike Will-O-Wisp but can force Jellicent out with the threat of their Grass-type moves or Sludge Bomb poisons, although Amoonguss can struggle to deal with a Jellicent burned by Scald, especially in the absence of Giga Drain.

Dark-types: Zarude's Jungle Healing makes it a particularly problematic counter to Jellicent, although it can be forced to burn its PP over a longer match. Hydreigon takes very little damage from anything Jellicent can use and can force it out, but Choice item sets lacking Roost will find themselves worn down quickly over a longer game.

Electric-types: Rotom-W takes very little damage from anything Jellicent can use and can safely pivot into it. However, it can't make damage stick on Jellicent, as Recover can negate the damage Volt Switch does. Thundurus-T can easily threaten Jellicent but lacks enough power to truly dissuade Recover with Volt Switch, unless it carries Nasty Plot and/or Thunderbolt. Rotom-H is immune to Will-O-Wisp and can threaten Jellicent with Toxic. Raikou cannot switch into Jellicent particularly safely but, due to running Heavy-Duty Boots, it is unfazed by entry hazards and can threaten it with Thunderbolt or Volt Switch.

Poison: Jellicent has to be very careful in practice around Toxic and Sludge Bomb users, as its lack of Leftovers can make poison a severe hindrance. This can limit Jellicent's ability to directly switch into Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Chansey that it can pressure, and it lets Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Galarian Slowbro pressure Jellicent with Sludge Bomb. When facing Cursed Body Jellicent, one must not let it take a Scald burn against Pokemon such as Primarina or Slowking if wishing to poison it, though; Jellicent will be able to reliably face these Poison-types afterwards.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Due to investing many EVs in Speed, Jellicent can struggle to check Pokemon its base stats suggest it can, such as Mamoswine and Excadrill. Therefore, they can potentially overwhelm Jellicent if they catch it trying to switch into an Icicle Crash or Iron Head, and Jellicent can't comfortably spinblock against the latter.

Defensive Utility.description:
Taunt lets Jellicent deny the recovery of Pokemon such as Chansey and Hippowdon, stifle entry hazard setters such as Skarmory and Hippowdon, and block debilitating Toxic from users such as Chansey, Celesteela, and Hippowdon. Will-O-Wisp lets Jellicent check Pokemon such as Swords Dance Cobalion and Scizor, and it combines with Hex to give Jellicent wallbreaking potential versus a range of threats like Amoonguss. Night Shade is an option over Hex for more direct and consistent damage to targets such as Hydreigon. Cursed Body is preferred to improve Jellicent's matchup versus Pokemon such as RestTalk Primarina. The ability to receive Scald burns, unlike Water Absorb Jellicent, also lets it better face Pokemon such as Amoonguss, with Cursed Body potentially shutting down Giga Drain variants too. On more balanced teams, Water Absorb is an option to better deter Choice Specs Keldeo and Primarina from spamming Water-type moves. Water Absorb can also improve the matchup versus rain teams and rare threats such as SubCM Keldeo, but neither of these are common enough to usually justify running it in isolation. It also lets Jellicent block Flip Turn from Swampert. Heavy-Duty Boots ensures that Jellicent can reliably switch into Pokemon like Cobalion, no matter the entry hazards situation. Colbur Berry is an option if one is confident in their team's hazard removal, letting Jellicent better check Swords Dance + Knock Off Scizor, check Conkeldurr to a degree, and freely stay in on Hydreigon once. 200 Speed EVs let Jellicent outspeed Azumarill, Skarmory, and Conkeldurr, while the remaining EVs beyond HP improve Jellicent's Defense for threats such as Scizor and Cobalion.

Jellicent fits best on stall teams, which appreciate its defensive utility versus threats such as Cobalion and Scizor and wallbreaking versus opposing bulky teams, and these teams provide it plenty of cleric, entry hazard, and status support. It can, however, also fit on certain balance teams that appreciate a reliable check to Cobalion and Keldeo. Cleric support from Articuno or Chansey helps greatly on stall, as Jellicent is prone to Sludge Bomb poisoning from Pokemon such as Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss, and it lets Jellicent be more aggressive against Toxic users such as Hippowdon. Articuno can also dominate the entry hazards war with its Pressure + Defog combination, letting Jellicent consider running Colbur Berry instead of Heavy-Duty Boots. Entry hazard setters like Hippowdon, Chansey, and Skarmory can make the most of Jellicent's wallbreaking potential. Hippowdon can help check Raikou, Thundurus-T, and Rotom-H for Jellicent, while Skarmory can cover Grass-types such as Zarude and Amoonguss, and it helps versus Excadrill, which Jellicent can struggle to spinblock against. Chansey offers a reliable Primarina and Hydreigon answer, and having Hippowdon set Stealth Rock lets it fit the aforementioned Heal Bell. Wish support from Umbreon can massively help Jellicent reliably stay at high HP. Jellicent also traditionally checks some of the main Umbreon switch-ins, such as Cobalion. Umbreon solidly answers Pokemon such as Hydreigon that check Jellicent, handles Pokemon Jellicent struggles to reliably check like Mamoswine and Salamence, and has Toxic to support Hex in return. On balance teams, Toxic spreaders include Salamence, Hippowdon, and Excadrill. Setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Galarian Slowbro and Slowking appreciate Jellicent softening up the opposing team so they can clean late-game. Slowking, in particular, offers a more reliable check to Pokemon such as Mamoswine with its superior bulk and Regenerator, while Galarian Slowbro can support Jellicent mid-game by spreading status with Sludge Bomb and Scald. On balance teams, checks to Zarude and Amoonguss are especially useful, such as Swords Dance Cobalion, which appreciates Jellicent pressuring or wearing down checks such as Hippowdon and Salamence. Skarmory can also fill this role well on stall teams, with its Spikes support being very valuable to these balance teams too.

ru.overview: Jellicent largely serves as a physical wall, being able to handle Heracross, Rhyperior, and Golisopod, but unlike most other bulky Water-types, it prevents Calm Mind Reuniclus, Cosmic Power Metagross, Calm Mind Suicune, and other setup sweepers from boosting with Taunt. Similarly to Milotic and Vaporeon, it can also cover certain special attackers, such as Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Nidoqueen lacking Toxic and Taunt. Jellicent's Ghost typing helps it deal with Fighting-type wallbreakers like Lucario, Bewear, and Heracross that Seismitoad, Milotic, and Gastrodon can struggle with. It can stallbreak through passive walls with Taunt and status, including Registeel, Umbreon, and Gastrodon, and spinblock utility Starmie and Dhelmise, outright walling the former and burning the latter. Unfortunately, unlike most bulky Water-types, Jellicent does not serve as a Knock Off absorber, struggling to deal with Knock Off from Incineroar and Heracross. Jellicent also doesn't provide as much utility as other bulky Water-types, like Rapid Spin with Starmie or Stealth Rock with Seismitoad. Its poor Speed also restricts the pool of Pokemon it can stallbreak against, as Milotic, Metagross, and Seismitoad can use Toxic before Jellicent's Taunt.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Cursed Body can be used over Water Absorb if a team can deal with powerful Water-type attacks, which includes having a good matchup against rain teams, Suicune, and Milotic. Cursed Body can stop foes from breaking through Jellicent by disabling their best attacks—especially if said attack would ever critically hit—and helps it stallbreak by increasing the chance a foe is forced to use Struggle. Night Shade can be used to better deal with Dark-types like Umbreon and Pangoro, but losing Hex makes Jellicent worse against Reuniclus. Choice Specs Jellicent with Water Spout and Trick can also be used as a solid wallbreaker and surprise option, but such a set is usually outdone by other offensive Water-types like Starmie and Sharpedo.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Roserade and Celebi can switch in and handle a Hex or Scald and remove burn with Natural Cure. Other Grass-types such as Dhelmise, Tsareena, and Decidueye can also beat Jellicent, though they must fear Will-O-Wisp, as they are physical attackers.

Dark-types: Incineroar is one of the best Jellicent switch-ins if it lacks Scald, setting up with Swords Dance for free. Mixed Sharpedo switches in nicely too, as burns don't weaken its Dark Pulse.

Electric-types: Xurkitree, Raikou, and Heliolisk can all force out Jellicent and gain momentum. However, if Raikou and Xurkitree are statused, Hex can 3HKO and 2HKO them, respectively. Heliolisk, however, completely walls Jellicent unless it carries Toxic.

Ghost-types: Although Ghost-types like Mimikyu, Chandelure, and Polteageist cannot directly switch in, they can very easily force Jellicent out.

Knock Off: Many common threats that Jellicent otherwise wall run Knock Off, such as Heracross and Golisopod. Aside from the super effective damage, Jellicent losing its item worsens its longevity and makes it more passive, as Jellicent will be forced to use Recover more often.

Residual Damage: Toxic poison and burn from Pokemon such as Nidoqueen, Milotic, and Galarian Weezing wear down Jellicent. Furthermore, if it lacks Heavy-Duty Boots, entry hazards quickly rack up damage. This forces Jellicent to constantly use Recover to be healthy enough to take on Pokemon like Nidoqueen and Bewear.

Defensive Utility.description:
Jellicent runs a burning move to complement Hex, typically Will-O-Wisp to reliably weaken physical attackers like Bewear, Golisopod, and Flygon. Taunt allows Jellicent to overcome setup sweepers like Calm Mind Reuniclus and Metagross while also stopping slower Steel- and Water-types like Registeel and Gastrodon from using Toxic, which could otherwise debilitate Jellicent. Scald can be used over Will-O-Wisp to prevent Fire-types like Incineroar and Entei from safely switching in. Toxic can also be used to better threaten Pokemon like Incineroar and Heliolisk, but it can't hit Steel- and Poison-types like Registeel and Crobat to boost Hex. Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers help Jellicent deal with chip damage, lowering its need to use Recover and thus lowering its passivity. Colbur Berry allows Jellicent to tank Knock Off from Heracross, Golisopod, and Tornadus and stall offensive Dark-types like physical Sharpedo and Pangoro to burn them. Alternatively, running no item also lowers Knock Off damage and makes Jellicent immune to Poltergeist, which is handy when dealing with Golurk and Alolan Marowak, but neither is particularly common. Jellicent runs 44 Speed EVs to outspeed Umbreon, which is crucial in denying Umbreon's Wish passing. When using Leftovers, Jellicent should use 36 Special Defense EVs to prevent a 2HKO from Nidoqueen's Earth Power after Stealth Rock.

Jellicent, like other bulky Water-types, works best on balance teams, but it can fit on bulky offensive teams. However, on these offensive teams, it competes with Seismitoad and Golisopod; they have more utility in Knock Off and entry hazards in Stealth Rock and Spikes, and they are less passive. Jellicent supports teams without Flying-types, as it can handle Fighting-types such as Heracross, Lucario, and Toxicroak itself. However, Jellicent enjoys having a Flying-type teammate like Crobat or Togekiss to take Knock Off from Heracross and Golisopod. Electric-types such as Raikou, Xurkitree, and Heliolisk punish Jellicent well; having a Grass-type such as Roserade or Celebi alongside a Ground-type such as Steelix, Rhyperior, or Flygon can mitigate this issue. Opposing Roserade can take advantage of Jellicent to put up a layer of Spikes. Crobat and Reuniclus can force out Roserade quickly and gain momentum with U-turn or set up with Calm Mind. Despite not enjoying Hex, Celebi can switch in too and potentially threaten any given team with Nasty Plot. Guzzlord or Umbreon can help force the Celebi out. Umbreon can also remove any status Jellicent might receive. Entry hazard removal from Crobat and Flygon will also help Jellicent when it's not running Heavy-Duty Boots.

pu.overview: Jellicent is one of the best defensive Water-types in PU. Compared to its competition in Wishiwashi and Lanturn, Jellicent brings to the table an excellent Ghost typing further enhanced by its myriad of supportive options such as Will-O-Wisp, Taunt, and Recover. Because of this, Jellicent is an effective switch-in to to various physical attackers such as Gallade and Perrserker. Jellicent also provides teams additional utility by punishing Water-types or Choice-locked attackers, depending on if it's running Water Absorb or Cursed Body. Jellicent can also become an incredible offensive threat when equipped with Choice Specs thanks to its access to the rare and powerful Water Spout. However, defensive Jellicent can be rather passive due to its low offensive capabilities and reliance on status as the typical way of dealing damage. Furthermore, Jellicent struggles versus common special attackers such as Whimsicott and Vikavolt, as many of them can comfortably switch in and typically are not overly bothered by Will-O-Wisp or Toxic.

Defensive Utility.description: Will-O-Wisp is the preferred status move as a way to catch many physical attackers that threaten Jellicent such as Absol and Silvally-Ghost; however, Toxic can be used here in order to better cripple bulkier checks such as Lanturn and opposing Jellicent. Hex is the sole attacking move on this set because it pairs well with its status moves versus bulkier defensive answers such as Lanturn. Colbur Berry is the optimal item in order to weaken Knock Off from the likes of Sneasel and Gallade, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used in order to be immune to entry hazards. 76 Speed EVs allow Jellicent to outspeed Jolly Glastrier. Gigalith makes a fantastic partner for Jellicent, as not only is it a good check to special attackers like Haunter, but with Sand Stream and hazard support, the residual damage Jellicent can spread with Will-O-Wisp and Toxic can severely cripple offensive answers like Whimsicott and Vikavolt. Conversely, Gigalith appreciates Jellicent's ability to check threats such as Perrserker and Sandaconda. Silvally-Fairy is also a fine partner, since it acts as a Knock Off absorber if Jellicent isn't running Colbur Berry and handles Dark-types such as Absol.
