Poison Jab can be run to beat Quiver Dance Ribombee while also being able to fish for poison on Pokemon immune to Scald such as Jellicent. Haze allows Mareanie to beat Doublade one-on-one, provided there are no critical hits. Infestation can be used to trap and remove defensive Pokemon such as Weezing and Eldegoss, allowing teammates such as Swords Dance Sandslash to sweep easier. A Calm nature is usually preferred, as this preserves Mareanie's Speed tier, allowing it to outspeed Doublade. However, a Sassy nature is better when running Poison Jab, as this allows Mareanie to do over 50% damage to Ribombee, meaning it can't Quiver Dance on it. Mareanie pairs particularly well with Gigalith + Sandslash cores, as Mareanie can absorb Toxic Spikes for them while dealing with the tier's Water-types such as Jellicent and Wishiwashi. Mareanie's passivity means it can be a detriment into setup sweepers that immediately threaten it, such as Sandslash. Grass-types that can handle these such as Eldegoss and Tangela are good partners.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

Toxic over Toxic Spikes punishes targets like Marshtomp and Tangela immediately rather than relying on an entry hazard to status them. Sludge Bomb damages and also spreads status on targets like Vullaby and Thwackey to prevent them from switching in as easily, but Knock Off is usually better for the general utility. As a physical wall, Mareanie is more reliable at checking Pokemon like Gurdurr and Raboot. However, specially defensive sets already check these attackers and are overall more effective.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Mareanie usually fails as a special wall when up against Duosion and Hattrem, as they target its Psychic weakness and have either immunities or Magic Bounce to work around Toxic Spikes.

Ground-types: Especially without Scald, Ground-types like Piloswine, Marshtomp, and Krokorok are switch-ins to Mareanie that hit hard with Earthquake.

Wallbreakers: Many of the meta’s strongest attackers like Choice Band Piloswine, Choice Specs Electabuzz, and Choice Band Thwackey break through Mareanie with their STAB attacks.

Special Wall.description:
Mareanie functions as a great special wall thanks to its multiple recovery options and supportive coverage. Recover gives Mareanie the opportunity to regain its HP immediately, while its ability Regenerator can help Mareanie regain HP when pivoting. Scald can burn physical attackers like Piloswine and Thwackey, while Toxic Spikes offers an opportunity to spread status against vulnerable teams once opposing Poison-types are eliminated. Knock Off debilitates walls like Vullaby and Galarian Corsola and also threatens special wallbreakers like Lampent and Galarian Corsola. Haze prevents some sweepers such as Shell Smash Wartortle, RestTalk Klang, and Calm Mind Lampent from setting up and breaking past Mareanie.

Mareanie should be played as defensive pivot that switches into attackers like Lampent and Raboot in order to force them out. Try pairing Mareanie with physically defensive Pokemon like Galarian Corsola, Clefairy, and Tangela to help deal with attackers like Thwackey, Gurdurr, and Electabuzz. Clefairy and Galarian Corsola also form a great entry hazard-stacking core with Toxic Spikes Mareanie, with the former luring in Hattrem for a Knock Off, and the latter trapping and removing Hattrem with Whirlpool to let Mareanie spam its status moves far more freely. Other bulky Pokemon like Gurdurr and Klang appreciate Mareanie scouting stronger attacks for them, as it can easily switch into Moonblast and Flamethrower from Clefairy and Lampent, respectively. While Mareanie has a weakness to Earthquake, it could be worthwhile to stay in and use Knock Off on tanks that use Earthquake, such as Piloswine and Marshtomp, if removing their Eviolite is essential for the team’s win condition; in these cases, pair Mareanie with offensive sweepers like Electabuzz and Raboot. Otherwise, Ground-type checks such as Thwackey and Galarian Corsola can help. Late-game, it could be beneficial to sack Mareanie by spamming Haze in the face of Shell Smash Wartortle or Dragon Dance Fraxure so that they do not sweep and remain slow enough to be revenge killed by offensive teammates like Electabuzz and Piloswine.

ubers.overview: Toxapex is a solid defensive pivot for balance and stall teams thanks to its typing, great defenses, and Regenerator, which allow it to blanket check common threats such as Dracovish, Marshadow, and Ho-Oh. It has access to a great utility moves, including Toxic Spikes, Haze, Recover, Knock Off, and Scald. However, Toxapex is very passive, letting many common threats such as Calyrex-S, Zekrom, and Groudon switch in for free when it uses Recover or Haze. It also faces rough competition as a status spreader with Eternatus, which actually has an offensive presence.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

A set with Block and Spite lets Toxapex lure in and PP stall passive switch-ins such as defensive variants of Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and Yveltal lacking U-turn and Taunt. However, its utility against offensive teams is really low. Baneful Bunker punishes direct contact from many physical attackers that can 2HKO or OHKO Toxapex, including Ho-Oh, Dracovish, and Zekrom. However, it is more prediction reliant than Toxic and Toxic Spikes.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Strong Psychic-types like Mewtwo, Calyrex-S, and Lunala heavily threaten Toxapex, though they must be wary of switching into Knock Off and Toxic.

Eternatus: With great bulk, immunity to Toxic, and a high Special Attack, Eternatus is a threat for Toxapex. It doesn't mind losing its item and is able to PP stall Toxapex thanks to Pressure. Finally, Eternatus can absorb Toxic Spikes.

Ground-types: Even though they don't want to switch in and get statused, both Groudon and Zygarde-C are top threats for Toxapex. They can both attempt to set up with Bulk Up, Dragon Dance, or Coil. Both Landorus and Landorus-T can force Toxapex out with either Earthquake or Earth Power, and both can set up Stealth Rock.

Super Effective Coverage: Toxapex can be overwhelmed quickly if Pokemon like Kyogre, Xerneas, Necrozma-DM, and Ho-Oh predict it switching in and land coverage moves like Thunder and Earthquake.

Setup Special Attackers: Despite its high Special Defense, Toxapex struggles at absorbing boosted strong special attacks. Offensive variants of Eternatus can use Meteor Beam on the switch and threaten to 2HKO with Dynamax Cannon. Meanwhile, Xerneas can use Toxapex as setup fodder with Substitute and does massive damage with a boosted Thunder, though these variants have to be wary of Haze.

Taunt: Taunt users like Yveltal can severely hinder Toxapex, leaving it unable to threaten foes with Toxic; specially-oriented Yveltal in particular can easily heal off any damage dealt by Toxapex with Oblivion Wing.

The Pex.description:
Toxapex's great bulk allows it to switch in on many physical attackers and cripple them with Knock Off, Toxic, or a Scald burn. Haze prevents physical sweepers such as Bulk Up Marshadow and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM from setting up and overwhelming Toxapex. Recover and Regenerator allow Toxapex to check threats like Ho-Oh and Marshadow. Toxic and Toxic Spikes are, admittedly passive, ways to better deal with Dracovish and Ho-Oh and cripple switch-ins such as Zekrom, Zygarde-C, and Giratina. The two can be used together, with Toxic punishing opposing threats that would switch in anticipation of Toxic Spikes, such as Zekrom, Groudon, and Kyogre. Rocky Helmet is the preferred item to punish most attacks from physical attackers such as Marshadow's Spectral Thief, Dracovish's Fishious Rend, Ho-Oh's Brave Bird, and Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike. Black Sludge can be used to give Toxapex better longevity, notably reducing the chance that Dracovish's Fishious Rend 2HKOes it.

Blissey and Chansey offer solid answers to special attackers like Xerneas, which Toxapex cannot handle. They also offer Wish and Stealth Rock, which can complement Toxic Spikes from Toxapex. Ferrothorn can switch into most Zekrom and Groudon sets and provides entry hazards and Knock Off support. Bulky Dark-types can check Psychic-types like Calyrex-S and Mewtwo. Yveltal provides Defog and Knock Off, and Knock Off can remove Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots to increase the effectiveness of Toxic Spikes, while Tyranitar offers Stealth Rock support. Both formes of Giratina are great teammates with Toxapex. Giratina can phaze dangerous setup sweepers like Zekrom and Zygarde-C, which Toxapex cannot handle alone; Giratina-O benefits from Toxapex spreading status thanks to Hex, has no trouble switching into Groudon thanks to Levitate, and offensively checks Calyrex-S with Shadow Sneak. Setup sweepers like Zygarde-C and defensive variants of Kyogre and Groudon can also take advantage of status spreading, as well as checking threats like Ho-Oh and Zekrom.

ou.overview: In spite of all that has been developed to counteract its presence, Toxapex still endures as an easy-to-fit metagame staple in SS OU. Blessed with absurd defenses and Regenerator, Toxapex can soft check just about anything and threatens item removal with Knock Off, status in Toxic and Scald, and the removal of stat boosts with Haze. This titanic bulk also means that Toxapex can pivot into an extensive amount of Pokemon and scout them, easing prediction against threats like Blaziken, Choice Specs Dragapult, Blacephalon, and Choice Band Tyranitar. As the metagame has developed, countermeasures have been mounted against the living bunker: Future Sight from the likes of Slowbro, Galarian Slowking, and Tapu Lele paired with strong attackers is a common tactic to try and break through Toxapex. However, much like the animal it takes its inspiration from, it adapts to the environment around it, most notably reinventing itself as a Light Screen pivot to halve damage from Future Sight, allowing it to effectively wall Future Sight chains by staying in and healing just before the attack hits. However, compared to other Regenerator users, Toxapex suffers from a severe case of four-moveslot syndrome that can make it very passive, often finding itself treated as set up fodder by the likes of Swords Dance Kartana, Calm Mind Clefable, and Substitute Volcarona, as it struggles to fit Scald and Haze together in the modern metagame. Additionally, its typing is both a blessing and a curse; while checking or flat out countering physical attackers like Urshifu-R and Blaziken is a large boon, it is prone to being overwhelmed by the attackers it is supposed to check by virtue of the common Future Sight support these wallbreakers often are paired with. This passivity also means most Toxapex sets are free entry points for strong offensive Ground-types like Excadrill and Garchomp. The choice of what Toxapex has to run on a given team is quite the conundrum, and every moveset Toxapex runs has some hole it can't effectively cover without the help of its teammates.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Baneful Bunker can appear to be an enticing way for Toxapex to punish contact moves such as U-turn and Knock Off and scout coverage moves, but this is often redundant, as Toxapex is already a dedicated physical sponge, so it should only really be considered on teams weak to some specific wallbreakers with contact moves like Victini and Rillaboom. A rare albeit potent item Toxapex can choose to run is Payapa Berry, allowing it to survive a STAB Psychic or Psyshock from Tapu Lele and remove its item with Knock Off or status it with Toxic. Toxapex can run Block + Spite with Knock Off and Recover, which allows it to trap and PP stall common switch-ins like Ferrothorn and Clefable while still being able to pivot in and remove items effectively. Finally, Toxapex can choose to run Toxic Spikes, which will critically forces status on grounded targets such as Tapu Fini, Garchomp, Arctozolt, and Tyranitar.

Checks and Counters

Future Sight: If there's one continuous fact that will always plague Toxapex's viability in the tier, it is the prevalence of Future Sight paired with breakers. In spite of Toxapex often being a dedicated utility piece that can set Light Screen, it is prone to being overwhelmed by the likes of Tapu Lele, Galarian Slowking, and Slowbro using Future Sight and pivoting to the physical or special attackers they enable. Even Pokemon that Toxapex has a beneficial type matchup against such as Blaziken and Urshifu-R will have good odds of breaking through it once it has to come in and check them if there's a Future Sight ready.

Magma Storm Heatran: Heatran is synonymous with ruining Toxapex that can't afford to run Shed Shell, seeing as Magma Storm + Earth Power will trap and KO Toxapex with little to no effort. However, this matchup changes if Toxapex chooses to run Shed Shell, as it can come in and soft check Heatran, while Heatran has to respect Knock Off removing its Leftovers.

Strong Choice Item Attackers: Some threats can circumvent Toxapex's incredible bulk with their own immense attacks. Choice Band Tyranitar can threaten to 2HKO Toxapex with both of its STAB moves, but it is uncomfortable switching directly into Toxapex, as it has to contend with Toxapex using Scald or Toxic to cripple it or put it on a timer. Similar to Tyranitar, Choice Band Grass-types such as Kartana and Rillaboom can quickly overwhelm Toxapex with their strong STAB moves, but they too have to respect Toxapex using moves such as Scald and Knock Off to neuter their ability to threaten it. The rare Galarian Zapdos can pull similar stunts, with its Brave Bird threatening a clean 2HKO on Toxapex. Choice Specs Blacephalon's Shadow Ball will cleanly 2HKO Toxapex, as will Choice Specs Volcanion's Earth Power. In the case of Blacephalon, it can also use Trick on Toxapex on the switch in, crippling it for the remainder of the game. These Pokemon have to respect Toxapex's utility options, as both hate having their Choice Specs removed with Knock Off and struggle to break through Toxapex should it set Light Screen. Trick Pokemon such as Blacephalon have to ensure that the Toxapex isn't using Black Sludge, which will cripple the Trick user much like Trick hampers Toxapex.

Choice Specs Tapu Lele: No special attacker without setup hits Toxapex as hard as Choice Specs Tapu Lele. Its Psychic will OHKO Toxapex, and given that Toxapex is one of the best leads in the tier, it often does this in the beginning of the game, and there is very little Toxapex can do about it. An option some Toxapex choose to run to match Tapu Lele is Payapa Berry, allowing Toxapex to survive one Psychic or Psyshock and remove Tapu Lele's Choice Specs with Knock Off or status it with Toxic. However, using Knock Off comes with the caveat that Toxapex has just given a Tapu Lele the choice in picking whatever move it wants for the rest of the game, and using Toxic means that Tapu Lele will still be a formidable wallbreaker in spite of it being put on a timer.

Arctozolt: Arctozolt is one of few physical attackers that will often bust straight through Toxapex with its Bolt Beak, and given how Arctozolt will always be paired with hail and Stealth Rock, it will just about always force a KO, should the Toxapex be forced to stay in. Arctozolt does, however, have to respect Toxapex having the ability to set Toxic Spikes, giving it less room to come in and attack it, or run Baneful Bunker to punish Bolt Beak. Moves such as Baneful Bunker are rare, however, and should Toxapex reveal it early, Arctozolt will quite readily be able to play around it. Arctozolt can also circumvent these mind games by running Substitute + Freeze-Dry to scout Toxapex attempting to stay in, and Freeze-Dry is also a good option that can catch the Ground-types that Toxapex is often paired with.

Strong Electric-types: Zapdos and Tapu Koko are immensely threatening to Toxapex, scaring it out with their strong STAB Thunderbolts, and can use Toxapex to create momentum with Volt Switch. However, both of them hate getting statused by Toxic and have to play with that in mind before switching in.

Offensive Ground-types: Pokemon like Garchomp and Landorus-T are incredibly threatening for Toxapex, as its only real way to manage them is to attempt to burn them with Scald or use Toxic before they begin setting up or threaten to 2HKO it with their STAB moves.

The Pex.description:
Set Description

Toxapex has an extensive movepool and a lot of different choices it can pick and choose from. Light Screen is excellent support for both itself and its teammates, halving the damage from the ubiquitous Future Sight and allowing Toxapex to come in on special attackers such as Volcanion and Blacephalon effectively. Knock Off is a fantastic move that allows Toxapex's teammates some much needed reprieve by removing items from the likes of Urshifu-R, Dragapult, and Landorus-T. Scald is Toxapex's best immediate damaging option, chipping away at the health of Water-weak Pokemon, and can critically punish switches with burns, potentially crippling physical attackers like Rillaboom and Garchomp while also ensuring Ferrothorn and Corviknight can't come in on Toxapex risk-free. Poison Jab is necessary on some structures to ensure that Toxapex isn't setup fodder for Calm Mind Tapu Fini. Toxic is an enticing move for Toxapex, as it will put common pivots like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T on a timer and has inherent synergy with Knock Off, which allows Toxapex to either remove items from Pokemon that are Toxic-immune or put problematic Pokemon such as Tapu Lele and Volcarona on a timer. Haze is an alternative that lets Toxapex remove boosts and PP stall setup sweepers like Volcarona. The only mandatory move Toxapex has is Recover; it is reliant on the move to stay healthy in longer matches. The choice of nature will mostly depend on what moves Toxapex is running; Impish means Knock Off and Poison Jab will hit a bit harder, Bold means that Scald will deal a bit more damage, and a Relaxed nature will mean Toxapex isn't picking and choosing between natures that hamper its attacking stats and can allow it to scout Pokemon that are otherwise slower than it like Slowbro and Slowking. The item Toxapex chooses is extremely important, as every single one has different advantages. Shed Shell means that Toxapex won't be trapped by Magma Storm Heatran and allows it to cripple Heatran's longevity with Knock Off or wear it down with Scald before switching out. Rocky Helmet will deal significant damage to attackers like Urshifu-R and Weavile that are reliant on contact moves and can punish pivoting moves like U-turn with heavy chip damage. Finally, Black Sludge gives Toxapex even more longevity and allows it to punish Trick users like Blacephalon and Tapu Fini.

Team Options

Toxapex fits on an extensive number of teams and forms synergistic defensive cores with a large amount of Pokemon. Tornadus-T pairs well with Toxapex, forming a potent Regenerator core that can check Kartana, Rillaboom, and Ferrothorn, all of which Toxapex can otherwise struggle to do anything noteworthy to without Scald. Toxapex will, in return, check strong wallbreakers like Blaziken and Weavile that can threaten to break through Tornadus-T. Corviknight and Zapdos similarly pair well with Toxapex, and all three Flying-types provide consistent entry hazard removal with Defog, which Toxapex appreciates. The aforementioned Flying-types also check bulky Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Garchomp, which Toxapex can't realistically manage on its own. Clefable is another utility piece that works well with Toxapex and can allow Toxapex to keep its item, since Clefable is a good Knock Off absorber. Toxapex synergizes incredibly well with bulky Ground-types like Landorus-T, Garchomp, Hippowdon, and Gastrodon, since they scare out and check some of Toxapex's worst matchups like Tapu Koko, Magma Storm Heatran, and Zapdos. A final teammate to consider is Blissey, as it checks Pokemon that Toxapex can't realistically manage on its own such as Choice Specs Volcanion, Blacephalon, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele.

Specially Defensive.description:
Set Description

This set aims to turn Toxapex into a strong special wall that can check a large swath of special attackers such as Volcanion, Dragapult, Blacephalon, and Volcarona while still being able to handle physical attackers like Urshifu-R and Weavile with its incredible defensive typing and good physical bulk even without investment. Knock Off lets Toxapex hamper wallbreakers like Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Band Urshifu-R while also removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from the likes of Zapdos and Landorus-T. Toxic puts switch-ins like Slowbro and Tornadus-T on a timer. The burn chance from Scald is noteworthy, as Toxapex will have a lot of opportunities to come in and fire off the move, giving it chances to burn switch-ins like Galarian Slowking and Ferrothorn. Poison Jab gives Toxapex the ability to beat Calm Mind Tapu Fini. Haze and Recover ensure that Toxapex can keep up its walling capabilities, as without Haze, it will critically fail to check setup sweepers like Substitute + Quiver Dance Volcarona effectively. Should your team have appropriate counterplay versus these setup sweepers, Light Screen can be considered to support the team with counterplay against Future Sight while also easing prediction against special attackers like Zapdos and Tapu Lele. The given special bulk investment ensures that Toxapex can shrug off special hits from the likes of Dragapult and Volcanion effectively. 20 Defense EVs let Toxapex survive unboosted Modest Tapu Lele's Psyshock at full health, allowing Toxapex to either poison it with Toxic or remove its item with Knock Off. Shed Shell enables Toxapex to avoid being trapped by Heatran's Magma storm and irritate it with STAB Scald or Knock Off before switching out, while Black Sludge can allow Toxapex to effectively disrupt Trick users like Blacephalon and gives Toxapex even more longevity.

Team Options

Seeing as this Toxapex set is not a catch-all for physical attackers, you will need to account for this when picking teammates. Physically defensive Corviknight is a standard pairing with specially defensive Toxapex, as it can check threats like Landorus-T, Rillaboom, Kartana, and Melmetal while also clearing away entry hazards with Defog. Zapdos can fill a similar role to the aforementioned Corviknight while also acting as a good special attacker, which makes up for Toxapex's passivity. Tornadus-T is another option that can allow Toxapex to drop Knock Off for Toxic, as Tornadus-T is incredibly efficient at removing items. It can also set up with Nasty Plot and KO Pokemon like Heatran which would otherwise check Toxapex. Clefable is a good partner to Toxapex, as it can check threats like Garchomp and Weavile while having the ability to set Stealth Rock effectively, remove items with Knock Off, or be an Unaware tank that can effectively match them. Buzzwole is a physical tank that can check Weavile and Kartana, as well as key threats like Choice Band Tyranitar, which specially defensive Toxapex cannot effectively handle. Offensive Steel-types like Melmetal also help out Toxapex by a fair amount, as Toxapex is deathly afraid of staring down Tapu Lele, which Melmetal can handily scare out. Toxapex has good type synergy with bulky Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Garchomp that can threaten its checks like Magma Storm Heatran, Galarian Slowking, and Electric-types like Tapu Koko with their strong STAB Earthquakes.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Gastro Acid is a good option in tandem with Toxic, as it punishes Toxic-immune Pokemon that try to set up on Toxapex, like Clefable, Reuniclus, and Gliscor; it can also remove other abilities that might hinder Toxapex's effectiveness, such as Natural Cure from Blissey. However, a lot of the time, Gastro Acid is less useful than simply running Haze and Toxic. Shed Shell can be useful to escape Heatran's Magma Storm, however; in most situations, the passive recovery from Black Sludge is better. Physically defensive variants can be used to better check Pokemon like Hawlucha, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Mawile, but Toxapex is generally best used to tank special hits. Papaya Berry is an option that allows Toxapex to sponge a hit from foes like Mega Medicham, Latias, and Tapu Lele and cripple them with Toxic, Knock Off, or a Scald burn; however, this tends to be incredibly situational. Lastly, Baneful Bunker can be used to scout moves from Choice-locked foes like Greninja, Landorus-T, Magnezone, and Tapu Lele, as well as punish physical attackers like Mega Medicham and Zeraora. However, this makes Toxapex significantly more passive and unable to handle Pokemon that come in on it freely such as Mega Charizard Y and Magnezone.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, Gliscor, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill can OHKO Toxapex with Earthquake and force it out. Gliscor deserves a special mention, as it can freely use Toxapex as setup fodder and cannot be hurt by burn or poison after Toxic Orb has been activated due to Poison Heal. However, the other Ground-types fear getting burned or poisoned.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types such as Tapu Lele, Reuniclus, Mega Latios, and Mega Medicham threaten Toxapex with their super effective attacks and force it out. Slowbro and Slowking can use Future Sight to scare Toxapex from coming into Pokemon it wants to check, like Ash-Greninja and Mega Charizard Y.

Magic Guard Users: Magic Guard users like Clefable and Reuniclus are not affected by Toxapex's status moves and can use it as an opportunity to set entry hazard or boost with Calm Mind. However, if Clefable lacks Thunder or gets its Life Orb removed, it can be forced into a stalemate with Haze.

The Pex.description:
Toxapex is one of the premier defensive Pokemon in the tier due to its amazing ability in Regenerator, huge defensive stats, good defensive typing, and great utility moves. These traits make it an excellent wall for bulkier teams that can check and counter many key Pokemon in the metagame such as Ash-Greninja, Mega Scizor, Mega Charizard Y, and Weavile. Scald burns physical attackers and discourages Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Mega Medicham from switching into Toxapex. Toxic wears down foes and gives Toxapex more turns to use Recover, Knock Off cripples foes like Tapu Fini and Heatran, and Toxic Spikes spreads status and forces Defog if the opponent does not have a Poison-type to absorb them. Haze thwarts setup attempts from foes like Clefable and Hawlucha. The given EV spread allows Toxapex to survive two Knock Offs from Choice Band Weavile and +2 Kartana's Leaf Blade from full HP.

Toxapex fits very well on bulky teams, as it pairs well with fellow Regenerator users like Tangrowth. Bulky Pokemon like Skarmory, Chansey, Hippowdon, and Mega Latias form an incredibly hard-to-break defensive core with Toxapex. Toxapex appreciates having teammates that can switch into its very few weaknesses. Ground-resistant and -immune partners like Tangrowth, Corviknight, Gliscor, Skarmory, and Mega Latias are excellent switch-ins into Garchomp, Landorus-T, and opposing Gliscor, while Electric-immune teammates like Gliscor and Landorus-T can deal with Electric-types such as Magnezone, Tapu Koko, and Zeraora. Ferrothorn is an amazing partner due to it being able to handle Electric- and Psychic-types like Tapu Koko and Mega Latias for Toxapex. Toxapex appreciates having entry hazard removal on its side, as Spikes and Stealth Rock can bother it long term; Pokemon like Corviknight and Zapdos make a good core with it. Toxic Spikes variants have great synergy with bulky setup sweepers such as Reuniclus, Mega Latias, Gliscor, and Clefable due to Toxic Spikes wearing down their counters over time. In return, the former two are able to handle Mega Medicham, which is a threat to Toxapex.

monotype.overview:
Poison

An amazing typing, above average defensive stats, Regenerator, and a plethora of utility moves such as Recover, Haze, and Toxic all make Toxapex one of the best defensive Pokemon Monotype has to offer and allow it to fit on almost every Poison team. Thanks to its part-Water typing, it is able to better deal with Fire-, Rock-, and Ground-types, while Haze allows it to deal with setup users like Dragapult. However, Toxapex's offensive stats are feeble and it's extremely susceptible to stallbreakers such as Mew and Zarude.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Poison

Baneful Bunker can be used over Toxic to better deal with physical threats like Choice Band Rillaboom and Choice Band Victini. Knock Off can be opted for to cripple Heavy-Duty Boots users and other Pokemon that heavily rely on their items. However, the utility provided by Toxic is generally appreciated more. A specially defensive spread along with a Calm nature can be used to better deal with special attackers like Volcarona.

Water

Scald can be used on Toxapex to spread burns against Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Celesteela, as well as setup sweepers like Bisharp and Dragonite. Toxic Spikes can be used for types such as Fairy and Ice, in particular, that do not have a good absorber. Toxic directly punishes offensive threats such as Thundurus-T and Garchomp, which would otherwise take advantage of Toxapex's passivity. However, all of these moves require Toxapex to give up a crucial moveslot, and the aforementioned Pokemon and types can be taken care of by other teammates. Wacan Berry and Payapa Berry are both decent options: Wacan Berry allows Toxapex to stay in on Choice Specs Tapu Koko to retaliate with Poison Jab, and Payapa Berry means Toxapex can stay in on Tapu Lele and do the same, which is especially useful if the team lacks Slowking. Rocky Helmet is good for punishing attacks from U-turn users such as Urshifu-R, as well as putting Tapu Bulu into Poison Jab range after one of its attacks. Eject Button can be used on rain teams in order to generate momentum. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used to ignore Spikes against Fairy, letting Toxapex switch into the likes of Tapu Bulu more easily. However, Black Sludge is preferred over all these items to help Toxapex stand up to Pokemon such as Dragapult, and another item can only really be considered on teams that are not weak to it. If Toxapex does run another item or replaces Knock Off, Tapu Fini is a decent partner to serve as a good Dragapult answer.

Defensive (Poison).description:
Scald gives Toxapex some sort of offensive presence, threatening to burn offensive Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu and Bisharp that might try to take advantage of its passivity. Toxic nails both offensive and defensive Pokemon, including Volcarona, specially ones that Scald fails to do much against, such as Hydreigon and Gastrodon. Haze helps against setup users such as Dragapult and Mimikyu. Recover in tandem with Regenerator allows Toxapex to be a solid defensive pivot throughout the game.

Heavy-Duty Boots Amoonguss forms a potent Regenerator defensive core with Toxapex and provides the only reliable switch-in to Mold Breaker Excadrill available on Poison teams. Amoonguss also provides a resistance to Electric-type attacks from the likes of Tapu Koko and Zeraora. Drapion provides a much needed Psychic immunity and helps against Ghost-types such as Spectrier that can overpower Toxapex. Drapion also provides Toxic Spikes support. Galarian Weezing provides Defog support and a beneficial Dragon immunity against Pokemon such as Dragonite, as well as dealing with Substitute + Nasty Plot Hydreigon, which may take advantage of Toxapex. Nidoking is a great special wallbreaker and helps greatly in matchups like Flying, Steel, and Water thanks to its wide range of coverage options in Ice Beam, Thunderbolt, and Flamethrower. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking provides a great specially defensive pivot against Pokemon such as Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Choice Specs Zapdos, which otherwise threaten the entirety of Poison-type teams. Gengar aids greatly against Psychic-type Pokemon such as Victini and Slowbro, while Nihilego is great in matchups like Flying and Water, as it can deal with Pokemon such as Zapdos, Thundurus-T, and Swampert.

Physically Defensive (Water).description:
Thanks to its amazing defensive stats, good typing, and excellent ability in Regenerator, Toxapex is key to Water teams' success by serving as one of the type's best possible walls. With its Poison typing and bulk, Toxapex can wall threats to Water teams such as Aegislash, Tapu Bulu, and Dragapult, and it can use Regenerator to outlast teams by switching. Knock Off is Toxapex's main utility move, and it is crucial for removing many items such as Celesteela's Leftovers, Galarian Slowking's Assault Vest, Tornadus-T's Heavy-Duty Boots, and Dragapult's Dragon Fang. The combination of Knock Off + Black Sludge is crucial for taking down a huge threat in Dragon Dance Dragapult, with Knock Off letting Toxapex remove Dragapult's Dragon Fang before using Haze, and Black Sludge allowing Toxapex to outstall it. Poison Jab prevents Toxapex from being setup fodder against Tapu Bulu, Hatterene, and Tapu Fini and helps spread status against other Pokemon such as Tyranitar and Slowking. Haze is crucial to the set, as it prevents Toxapex from losing to the setup sweepers that it excels at checking, such as the aforementioned Dragapult as well as Zarude, Dragonite, and Volcarona. A physically defensive EV spread is used to allow Toxapex to wall the aforementioned physical attackers, which would otherwise be hard to switch into.

Toxapex pairs well with other defensive Pokemon to form defensive backbones for Water teams. Swampert and Gastrodon are two Pokemon that can switch into Electric-type attacks from Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, Zeraora, and Thundurus-T, while Toxapex can switch into Grass-type Pokemon such as Zarude and Tapu Bulu in return. Slowking is another great Pokemon that pairs well with Toxapex thanks to its resistance to Psychic and even better special bulk, which allow it to come in on attacks such as Tapu Lele's Psychic and Substitute Kyurem's Freeze-Dry. It also has Regenerator, just like Toxapex, allowing the Water user to outstall opposing defensive cores just by switching in and out between the two Pokemon. Volcanion is a good partner that beats Steel-types such as Celesteela, Melmetal, Klefki, and Ferrothorn for Toxapex, and it can Defog away the entry hazards Ferrothorn gets up for free against Toxapex. It also forms a good Fairy-breaking core with Toxapex by offensively threatening Pokemon such as Clefable with Sludge Bomb. Toxapex's defensive backbones pair will with many offensive Pokemon, but Urshifu-R in particular is a really good partner for Toxapex, as it can commonly take on Pokemon that punish Toxapex's passivity such as Ferrothorn, Arctozolt, Kyurem, Galarian Moltres, and Hydreigon.

cap.comments:
Other Options

Poison Jab can be run in place of either Scald or Knock Off to deal with Calm Mind Tapu Fini; if used over Scald, Toxapex can run an Impish nature as well. Shed Shell lets Toxapex switch into Heatran and Whirlpool Tapu Fini much more comfortably. Toxic Spikes over Scald pressures grounded Pokemon that don't run Heavy-Duty Boots, like Dragapult, Tapu Fini, and Tapu Lele. Baneful Bunker can be used over Knock Off to catch physical attackers like Weavile and U-turn users such as Dragapult by surprise, though it is often inconsistent and loses out on Knock Off's great general utility. Finally, the combination of Block + Spite can be used over Scald + Haze to trap and PP stall foes like Clefable and opposing Toxapex to enable Toxapex's own teammates; however, this set forgoes much of Toxapex's general utility and is inconsistent and niche.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Electric-types like Zeraora, Tapu Koko, Zapdos, Rotom-W, Krilowatt, Magnezone, and Arctozolt are some of the most common and effective methods of threatening Toxapex. However, Zeraora and Arctozolt despise being burned, and most of these Pokemon don't enjoy losing their item to Knock Off and aren't safe switch-ins.

Ground-types: Landorus-T, Garchomp, Colossoil, and Equilibra threaten Toxapex. However, none of them are safe switch-ins, as Toxapex can survive any one hit from them and threaten back with Scald or Knock Off; Landorus-T and Garchomp especially despite this interaction.

Strong Wallbreakers: Pokemon like Tapu Lele, Nidoking, and Air Balloon Heatran can immediately force Toxapex out, but these three cannot safely switch in, fearing losing their item or accruing undesirable chip damage. Venomicon can switch in on Toxapex and set up on it, though Venomicon may lose its Heavy-Duty Boots in the process. Swords Dance Kartana is one of the few physical attackers capable of threatening Toxapex, as +2 Leaf Blade has a chance to OHKO; however, it can never directly switch in and must set up first.

Taunt: Taunt users like Calm Mind Tapu Fini, Cosmic Power Mew, Taunt + Magma Storm Heatran, and certain Tornadus-T variants are highly effective options at dealing with Toxapex; Taunt prevents Toxapex from using Recover and removing boosts from the former two with Haze.

Future Sight: Future Sight users like Slowbro, Slowking, Galarian Slowking, and occasionally Tapu Lele enable teammates normally walled by Toxapex such as Urshifu-R and Weavile to break past it. The former two Pokemon also do not particularly mind losing their item or being burned, making them decent switch-ins.

The Pex.description:
Set Details

Toxapex is the premier defensive Water-type in the metagame. Its massive physical bulk allows Toxapex to switch into some of the tier's most threatening physical attackers such as Urshifu-R, Venomicon-E, Weavile, and Melmetal and force them out with the threat of burn from Scald and Knock Off. Beyond checking strong wallbreakers, Scald and Knock Off also allow Toxapex to not be passive and make important progress over the course of a game. Haze is necessary to check prominent setup sweepers like Weavile, Dragonite, Volcarona, and Galarian Moltres. A set with maximum Defense and Rocky Helmet is best for punishing physical attackers such as the aforementioned Weavile, Venomicon-E, and Urshifu-R; however, Black Sludge can also be run for valuable passive recovery. An EV spread of 252 HP / 124 Def / 132 SpD with a Sassy nature prevents Toxapex from being 2HKOed by Weavile's Knock Off, as well as helping it against special attackers like Dragapult by letting it survive two Shadow Balls after Stealth Rock and two Draco Meteors without entry hazards.

Toxapex is most commonly ran on balance and certain bulky offense teams. Landorus-T is a great teammate that forms a sturdy defensive backbone with Toxapex, checking Electric-types such as Zeraora; in return, it appreciates Toxapex's good matchup against Water-types and Ice-types. Bulky Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Heatran are strong partners, checking Psychic-types like Tapu Lele while benefiting from Toxapex dealing with Fire-types. Clefable forms a defensive core with Toxapex that is highly difficult to wear down with status, hazards, or other residual damage. Pokemon with Regenerator like Astrolotl and Tornadus-T are potent teammates that are useful for scouting opposing attackers. Kartana, especially its Choice Scarf set, is a good partner; Toxapex can often remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Kartana's Flying-type checks like Tornadus-T and Zapdos and benefit from its ability to threaten checks like Tapu Lele and Arctozolt. Finally, many offensive Pokemon such Garchomp and Venomicon-E appreciate Toxapex's ability to check Weavile, while Dragapult, Dragonite, and other Dragon-types benefit from Toxapex's good matchup into Fairy-types.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B+ Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Physical Wall.description:
• Toxapex's extremely passive playstyle and unfortunate weakness to Ground-type attacks may not make it the first choice for a bulky Water-type, but its excellent support movepool and incredible defensive capabilities make a staple on stall teams.

  • Scald is Toxapex's ideal way to spread burns, and ensure that Ground-types don't switch into it for free.

  • Haze is very effective at stopping set-up opportunities.

  • Toxic lets Toxapex cripple a wide variety of defensive and support Pokemon, such as Porygon2, Cresselia, and Hippowdon.

  • Baneful Bunker is a good way to help stall out Dynamax turns, with a bonus of poisoning foes that use contact moves.

  • Poison Jab may be weak, but with a Relaxed nature, it deals good chip damage to incoming Tapu Fini, Tapu Koko, and Rillaboom. Tapu Fini in particular is an important target due to its habit of running Taunt.

The Pex.description: Toxapex is one of the best pivots in STABmons, thanks to Flip Turn. It's also a fantastic check to a lot of common attackers like Urshifu-R, Buzzwole, and non-Nasty Plot Tornadus-T. Flip Turn lets Toxapex generate momentum and pivot in wallbreakers like Kyurem, Aerodactyl, and Tyranitar. Moreover, Toxapex can almost always make progress against the opposing team; Toxic lets it wear down almost everything in the tier, notably Seismitoad, Gastrodon, and Rotom-W, which are otherwise fine switch-ins to it. Knock Off can also be ran to remove items from the likes of Ferrothorn and Clefable. Lastly, Scald can be run to try and burn physical attackers such as Excadrill; it also lets Toxapex status other Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon that are immune to Toxic, such as Ferrothorn, Corviknight, and opposing Toxapex. Haze lets Toxapex thwart setup sweepers like Clefable, Buzzwole, and Gyarados that attempt to use it as setup fodder. Depending on your team, it is also possible to drop Haze and run one of the aforementioned options, such as Scald or Toxic. Toxapex works best on more defensive teams and teammates like Buzzwole, Mudsdale, and Ferrothorn can help patch up its weaknesses against wallbreakers like Excadrill and Zeraora. A Relaxed nature alongside 0 Speed IVs make Toxapex as slow as possible for Flip Turn.

Assault Vest.description: Toxapex can use its wide movepool and good bulk alongside Regenerator to be a fantastic special wall, further boosting its Special Defense with Assault Vest to check common Special Attackers like Keldeo, Gengar, and Cloyster. Poison Fang lets it potentially poison Tornadus-T, Kyurem, and Water-immune foes like Gastrodon and Seismitoad that try to switch into Flip Turn. Scald can also be used to try and deter physical attackers like Zeraora and Tyranitar and Steel-types like Ferrothorn from switching in. Knock Off lets Toxapex pressure the likes of Thundurus-T, Galarian Slowking, and Reuniclus while also doing good damage against Gengar and Slowking. Flip Turn lets it pivot out against wallbreakers it can'(apostrophe)t handle and safely get wallbreakers like Aerodactyl and Nidoking onto the field. Clear Smog lets it prevent sweepers like Calm Mind Clefable and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T from getting out of hand. Due to Toxapex mostly being used to handle special attackers, physical walls like Mudsdale, Cotton Guard Ferrothorn, and Buzzwole make for fantastic teammates as they cover each others weaknesses. Steel- and Dark-types like Corviknight and Tyranitar can also help it against Psychic-type foes like Reuniclus, Latios, and Future Sight Slowking. A Relaxed nature with 64 Defense EVs lets Toxapex avoid getting OHKOed by Zeraora while helping it take on other physical attackers like Rillaboom and Urshifu-R. 0 Speed IVs are used to ensure the slowest possible pivots with Flip Turn.

camomons.comments:
Other Options

Rocky Helmet on Water / Poison Toxapex accumulates extra chip on physical attackers, particularly Extreme Speed and U-turn users such as Scizor, Entei, Pheromosa, and Arcanine. Water / Poison Toxapex can also utilize Knock Off over Haze, but without Haze it fails to check Calm Mind Clefable and Latias.

Checks and Counters

Ground-type Attackers: Ground-type attackers such as Landorus-T, Melmetal, and Heatran easily break past Toxapex. However, Scald from Water / Poison Toxapex can somewhat deter physical Ground-types.

Tapu Lele: Tapu Lele is a huge threat to Water / Poison Toxapex due to its powerful Psychic-type attacks. Choice Specs Tapu Lele is especially threatening, as it's also difficult for Toxapex's partners to deal with, and it can even break Dark / Poison Toxapex in some cases.

Garchomp: Garchomp breaks past Toxapex with little effort. Offensive Stealth Rock sets, such as Ground / Steel and Dragon / Steel, are generally immune to Toxic, and some run Lum Berry to avoid a burn from Scald as well. After just one Swords Dance, any Garchomp set can 2HKO either Toxapex set.

Heracross: Heracross can break past either Toxapex set easily with STAB Guts Facade. Additionally, thanks to Guts, Heracross doesn't care about burns from Scald. It can fear Knock Off if Flame Orb hasn't activated yet, but otherwise it is a solid check to Toxapex.

Hydreigon: Most of Hydreigon's type configurations do not struggle with Toxapex at all. While Hydreigon generally runs Ground-type, it sets itself apart from other Ground-type attackers, as its Water / Dragon set breaks Toxapex as well. Ground / Steel Hydreigon in particular is able to threaten Toxapex without fear of being poisoned.

Electric-type Attackers: Electric-type attackers such as Tapu Koko, Latios, and Clefable are all able to threaten Toxapex in some way, though they can struggle to break past Dark / Poison Toxapex in some cases. Clefable is less secure, as it can't break past Dark / Poison Toxapex reliably and runs the risk of Toxapex using Knock Off. Choice Specs Tapu Koko can 2HKO Toxapex if Stealth Rock is up or gain momentum with Volt Switch.

Substitute and Taunt: Since Toxapex is passive, relying heavily on chipping opponents with Toxic damage and usually needing mulitple hits to break Substitutes, Substitute and Taunt are both strong tools to exploit it.

Specially Defensive Wall.description:
With high bulk and only one weakness, Dark / Poison Toxapex is a potent defensive Pokemon in the metagame. Its typing allows it to be one of the most effective walls to strong special attackers such as Tapu Lele, Magearna, Alakazam, Volcarona, and Spectrier. Regenerator and Recover give it multiple tools to increase its longevity. Knock Off gives Toxapex its Dark typing while providing valuable team support. Toxapex's Poison-type moveslot is flexible, with Toxic Spikes providing the most team support. Toxic is a secondary option that more immediately poisons foes like Heavy-Duty Boots Volcarona and affects Flying-type and Levitate foes. Baneful Bunker is a less common option that allows Toxapex to scout moves from Choice item users and physical attackers or stall another turn of burn or poison damage. Haze is necessary to effectively stop special attackers such as offensive Clefable, Steel-type Magearna, and Poison-type Latias from setting up, as each is immune to Toxic damage. Haze also allows Toxapex to check a number of setup sweepers in a pinch, though it has to be cautious to not lose too much HP in the process.

Toxapex fits on most playstyles, but it truly thrives on balance and bulky offense teams, providing crucial support for both. Physically defensive Steel / Flying Pokemon such as Salamence and Buzzwole are great partners for Toxapex because they cover Ground-type Pokemon, which are easily the biggest threats to Toxapex. Offensive Flying-type and Levitate Pokemon like Tornadus-T, Latios, and Hydreigon can threaten defensive Ground-types that threaten Toxapex, such as Heatran, Landorus-T, and Coalossal. Offensive Pokemon that appreciate Toxic Spikes support, such as Victini, Garchomp, and Ground-type Hydreigon, are very valuable partners to Toxapex on bulky offense, as they can force opposing teams into difficult positions and capitalize on Toxic damage.

Physically Defensive Wall.description:
Water / Poison Toxapex is a pivot and wall that checks a various offensive Pokemon such as Entei, Arcanine, Pheromosa, and Latias. Scald is spammable thanks to its high burn chance, which threatens physical attackers such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Lycanroc-D. Toxic Spikes gives Toxapex a support option that prevents defensive Pokemon from coming in safely, which can greatly benefit Toxapex's teammates. Toxic is a secondary option that more immediately poisons foes like Heavy-Duty Boots Volcarona and affects Flying-type and Levitate foes. Baneful Bunker allows Toxapex to scout moves or stall another turn of burn or poison damage. Recover increases Toxapex's longevity and allows it to check threats more readily. For the last slot, Haze allows Toxapex to check a plethora of setup sweepers such as Fire / Fairy Clefable, Water / Poison Latias, and Cresselia.

Psychic-type attackers such as Tapu Lele and Volcarona can be huge threats to Toxapex, so it's important to have switch-ins to these attacks; bulky Steel-type Pokemon, namely Heatran, Hydreigon, Coalossal, and Magearna, are good examples. Additionally, Ground-type Heatran, Hydreigon, and Coalossal double as checks to offensive Electric-types such as Clefable, Tapu Koko, Latios, and Dragapult that Toxapex struggles to deal with. Similarly to specially defensive Toxapex, this set benefits greatly from offensive Pokemon that appreciate Toxic Spikes support such as Entei, Hydreigon, and Victini.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Toxapex can run Regenerator to better handle opposing pivots, but this set is worse at checking setup sweepers. A specially defensive Volt Absorb set is an option on more defensive teams to counter Tapu Koko and Zapdos.

Checks and Counters

Ground-type Setup: Swords Dance Garchomp and Bulk Up Landorus-T are able to reliably 2HKO Toxapex with their STAB moves, preventing it from safely removing their boosts.

Electric- and Psychic-type Attackers: Toxapex is vulnerable to common offensive attackers in Azelf, Tapu Koko, and Zapdos, as they exploit its uninvested Special Defense with their powerful STAB moves.

Offensive Pivots: Pivots like Zarude and Barraskewda, especially when used in conjunction with entry hazard support, can wear down Toxapex and prevent it from recovering by pivoting to a teammate that forces it out.

Magic Guard: Toxapex relies almost exclusively on passive damage to threaten foes and its Recover can get PP stalled by Magic Guard Attackers like Talonflame. However, they dislike having their Life Orb removed.

Prankster Wall.description:
Thanks to its fantastic defensive typing and bulk, in conjunction with priority recovery and stat clearing with Haze, Prankster Toxapex is a great physical wall and setup deterrent. Its typing provides important resistances to Fire-, Fighting-, and Water-types, checking dangerous physical attackers like Cinderace, Terrakion, and Barraskewda. Toxapex's most significant role lies in deterring setup with Prankster Haze, which stops dangerous threats like Cosmic Power Mew and Quiver Dance Volcarona from making progress. It can also serve as an emergency check to threats it does not outright beat like Dragon Dance Power Construct Zygarde-10% and Swords Dance Garchomp by sacrificing itself to remove their boosts. Recover also benefits from Prankster, allowing Toxapex to switch in, sponge a hit, and heal off the damage before taking a second one. Knock Off provides utility by removing items, which can be especially useful against Choice Band users and defensive Pokemon that rely on utility items. The last move slot is more flexible; Scald threatens physical attackers that might consider staying in with a burn, Toxic Spikes help wear down offensive teams, and Toxic weakens potential sweepers. Black Sludge is the preferred item to provide extra recovery, while Rocky Helmet is an option to punish physical attackers, especially if Toxapex is the main Barraskewda switch-in. Maximum HP and Defense investment is necessary to repeatedly switch into dangerous physical attackers, while zero Speed IVs allow Toxapex to outspeed opponents in Trick Room; this is especially important to remove Marowak-Alola's Thick Club with Knock Off.

Toxapex is best utilized on balance and bulky offense teams that want to counter a wide range of opposing setup sweepers without devoting space to an elaborate defensive core. Toxapex is a great backstop when an attacker gets forced out; Prankster Haze removes the threat of the opponent using the free turn to set up, and Prankster Recover, plus Toxapex's great bulk, makes it difficult to KO. As such, Toxapex makes a great partner to Choice item wallbreakers such as Terrakion and Azelf. These wallbreakers also appreciate Toxapex's Knock Off and Toxic Spikes, as they wear down the opposing team even faster. Toxapex can also cover for other passive defensive partners like Blissey by denying sweepers that can set up on Blissey. Due to its Ground weakness, Toxapex is unable to check Garchomp, Landorus-T, or Zygarde-10%, so a secondary physically defensive switch-in like Intimidate Corviknight or Dauntless Shield Mew is appreciated. Toxapex is also a poor switch-in to Psychic- and Electric-type attacks, but these tend to be specially-oriented and should be handled by a special wall like Jirachi instead. Since Toxapex is heavily reliant on using Recover to stay healthy, it is vulnerable to entry hazards and opposing pivots. Reliable Defog support from Corviknight and the ability to punish pivots with entry hazard support&mdashwhich includes its own Toxic Spikes&mdash is strongly advised. Since Toxapex does not have access to a pivot move and can often be a momentum drain, it pairs well with other defensive pivots, such as Corvikinght and RegenVest Jirachi, which can generate momentum.

nationaldexmonotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Poison Jab targets Calm Mind Tapu Fini, while Sludge Bomb targets Tapu Bulu. Knock Off can be used to cripple Pokemon such as Galarian Corsola; all three options are niche options that can be used over Scald. Eject Button can be used on rain teams, allowing Toxapex to effectively generate momentum for the team without unnecessarily risking the offensive Pokemon while still regaining health through Regenerator.

Checks and Counters

Water

Super Effective Coverage: Super Effective STAB attacks such as Latios's Psychic, Landorus-T's Earthquake, and Thundurus-T's Thunderbolt easily break through Toxapex.

Stallbreakers: Taunt and Trick users such as Gliscor and Latias prevent Toxapex from freely using its utility moves, hindering its ability to act as a wall.

Wallbreakers: Strong attackers with neutral coverage such as Choice Band Rillaboom easily beat Toxapex.

Defensive (Water).description:
Toxapex is the premier defensive pivot for Water teams, as its good utility options and natural bulk alongside Regenerator allow it to constantly switch in through the game and support its teammates. Scald prevents Toxapex from becoming too passive while also allowing it to fish for burns against physical threats such as Rillaboom. Recover allows Toxapex to stay healthy through the match, especially alongside Regenerator recovery. Toxic Spikes allow Toxapex to support its offensive teammates by poisoning and chipping grounded foes. Toxic Spikes are especially useful in matchups such as Fairy, Psychic, and Dragon. Toxic, on the other hand, allows Toxapex to hit Flying-types and Levitate users such as Zapdos, Mega Latias, and Hydreigon, which can be a problem for Water teams. Haze allows Toxapex to check setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Mega Charizard X, Autotomize Celesteela, and Swords Dance Aegislash. Baneful Bunker can be used to scout Choice-locked attackers such as Choice Specs Tapu Koko, gain recovery, and further take advantage of Toxic. Baneful Bunker can also help provide useful chip against physical attackers such as Mega Lopunny. Regenerator allows Toxapex to act as a sponge by switching into attacks and regaining health upon switching out.

Toxapex's teammates appreciate its ability to act as a defensive pivot, remove Toxic Spikes from the field, and set its own Toxic Spikes. Slowking and Toxapex forms a great Regenerator core; under Toxapex's Toxic Spikes, Future Sight from Slowking is nearly impossible for opposing Pokemon to handle. Slowking also acts as a specially defensive wall for Toxapex and provides a crucial resistance to Psychic-type attacks such as Tapu Lele's Psychic and Future Sight. Pelipper, Mantine, and Rotom-W are important teammates to Toxapex, as they provide Ground immunities and Defog. Mantine allows Toxapex to use Baneful Bunker, as it can check Azumarill with Haze. Mantine's Haze also allows it to check a plethora of other setup sweepers such as Nasty Plot Hydreigon and Volcarona. Swampert provides Electric immunity and Stealth Rock. Additionally, it can also take on Electric-types such as Zeraora with Earthquake. Offensive teammates such as Greninja, Mega Swampert, Urshifu-R, and Mega Sharpedo appreciate Toxapex's ability to wear down the opposing team, allowing them to clean up late-game. Defensive setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Suicune and Mega Slowbro also appreciate Toxic Spikes. They can specifically take advantage of their bulk and Toxic poison to set up with more ease. Gastrodon and Empoleon are other defensive teammates that can help Toxapex wear down the foe. Empoleon can remove items with Knock Off, while Gastrodon can run Sticky Hold, allowing it to switch into Trick for Toxapex. Gastrodon also provides immunity to Electric-type attacks directed at Toxapex.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Black Sludge can be used to increase Toxapex's longevity further, and Sitrus Berry lets it counter Poltergeist from Marshadow, but Rocky Helmet and Shed Shell are usually better.

Checks and Counters

Strong Special Attackers: Choice Specs Kyogre, Calyrex-S, Kyurem-W, and most other special wallbreakers can force out Toxapex, although they need to be careful of Toxic or Knock Off if switching in.

Ground- and Electric-types: Groudon, Zygarde-C, and Zekrom can pressure Toxapex with their incredibly strong and super effective STAB moves, and Rest variants of the former two don't even fear burns from Scald too much.

Ditto: Combined with other pivots, Ditto can PP stall Toxapex incredibly effectively, as it refreshes its PP every time it switches into Toxapex. Regenerator lets it heal off any damage dealt, and taking Knock Off lets it stall even longer with the ability to switch moves, using Recover and trying for Scald burns of its own.

Gothitelle: Gothitelle can eliminate Rocky Helmet variants of Toxapex and threatens even ones with Shed Shell, as Toxapex commonly has to switch into Knock Off from Yveltal or Necrozma-DM, leaving it vulnerable.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Toxapex has a niche in the AG metagame as a defensive pivot, with Regenerator giving it incredible longevity to soft check and pivot around many offensive threats. Knock Off and its ability to spread status make it a nuisance to a lot of Pokemon, chipping down teams slowly and taking advantage of passive Pokemon that can't damage it heavily like Thunder Wave Necrozma-DM, defensive Eternatus, and Ho-Oh. It can check all of Marshadow, defensive Yveltal, and Calm Mind Kyogre, and it can chip Zacian-C heavily with Rocky Helmet and Wild Charge recoil if it tries taking Toxapex down. Scald is required to make Toxapex less passive, threatening burns on Pokemon that otherwise set up freely such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM. Even with it, though, Haze is mandatory to prevent setup sweepers such as Bulk Up Marshadow and Calm Mind Kyogre from turning Toxapex into a liability for a team. Knock Off provides item displacement and a strong way to hit Calyrex-S trying to set up on Toxapex, which is very valuable to reduce passivity and make that matchup less detrimental. Toxic and Toxic Spikes chip down the opposing team more quickly than Scald, but the heavy presence of Eternatus make these options rarely reach their full potential. Rocky Helmet can wear down Pokemon like Zacian-C, Urshifu-S, and U-turn pivots in Pheromosa and Galarian Darmanitan, while Shed Shell prevents Toxapex from being trapped by Gothitelle, otherwise being essentially a guaranteed KO for it.

Necrozma-DM appreciates Toxapex scouting for Assurance on Zacian-C and chipping it more with Rocky Helmet. Toxapex can also remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Ho-Oh and Yveltal, the most common Defog users, making them easier to wear down. Toxapex also checks Marshadow and most Dark-types, which threaten Necrozma-DM, unless they Dynamax. Offensive wallbreakers like Kyogre and Yveltal checked by Eternatus enjoy Toxapex pressuring it with Knock Off and Scald burns. Yveltal also helps by being immune to Ground and switching into Calyrex-S, covering for two of Toxapex's greatest weaknesses. Lunala is a good wall for Zekrom, Groudon, and Zygarde, which can all threaten Toxapex with strong super effective STAB moves, and Toxapex in return can pivot into Marshadow, Urshifu-S, and Yveltal, which pressure Lunala. Blissey is the sturdiest special sponge in the metagame, walling special attackers that can muscle past Toxapex like Life Orb Eternatus, Geomancy-boosted Xerneas, and Choice Specs Kyogre. Ho-Oh and Toxapex can form a Regenerator core that shuts down most defensive teams with infinite passive healing and spreading status.

lc.comments:
Other Options

Counter, which should be used alongside Berry Juice, trades a coverage move for a surprise KO on physical attackers like Mienfoo. Facade is an option, usually on Choice Scarf Mudbray, to maintain offensive pressure after Mudbray has been burned by an attack like Koffing's Will-O-Wisp.

Checks and Counters

Grookey: With its ability to set up Grassy Terrain, which reduces the power of Earthquake, and deal massive damage with Grassy Glide, Grookey is easily one of the biggest checks to Mudbray. However, Grookey cannot switch in multiple times, as it takes a lot of damage from Heavy Slam and Close Combat.

Natu: While it takes considerable damage from Heavy Slam, Natu can outlast Mudbray with Roost and prevent it from setting Stealth Rock and using Earthquake.

Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Staryu, Frillish, and Slowpoke can switch into Mudbray and punish it with Scald, although they take a lot of damage from Earthquake if they lose their Eviolite. Offensive Water-types such as Carvanha and Life Orb Staryu can bypass Mudbray's ability to tank hits and OHKO it.

Air Balloon Diglett: Air Balloon Diglett can exploit Choice Scarf Mudbray if it is locked into a Ground-type attack by trapping and subsequently KOing it.

Stealth Rock.description:
Mudbray's natural bulk allows it to safely set Stealth Rock against many different Pokemon. Close Combat threatens Ferroseed, while Heavy Slam covers Natu and Grookey. Alternatively, Rock Slide can hit Natu harder, but it is weaker against Grookey. High Horsepower can be used instead of Earthquake to do more damage in Grassy Terrain, but it is less accurate than Earthquake and can be unreliable at times. Eviolite is usually preferred to maximize Mudbray's bulk, but Berry Juice can provide it with much-needed recovery.

Stealth Rock Mudbray is amazing on certain offensive teams, as it allows Steel-types like Pawniard and Ferroseed to forgo Stealth Rock for other utility options. Furthermore, its ability to switch into Koffing is appreciated by certain defensive cores such as Mareanie + Ferroseed. Mudbray greatly struggles against Grookey and should be paired with partners such as Koffing, Natu, and Foongus that handle it. It also has difficulty beating Natu one-on-one consistently, so checks such as Frillish and your own Natu are good options.

Choice Scarf.description:
Mudbray is one of LC's best Choice Scarf users, as it outspeeds another popular Choice Scarf user in Porygon. This allows Mudbray to threaten KOs on fast, offensive threats like Abra, Ponyta, and Diglett. Mudbray's coverage moves seek to pave the way for its late-game sweep with Earthquake. Close Combat greatly damages Ferroseed and prevents Mudbray from being taken advantage of by Air Balloon Diglett. Heavy Slam provides great neutral coverage against foes like Natu and Grookey, while Rock Slide can be used to deal slightly more damage to Natu and for a useful flinch chance.

Choice Scarf Mudbray fits well with other threats like Porygon to overwhelm shared checks like Ferroseed or to take advantage of Mudbray's checks like Grookey and Natu. Mudbray is relatively frail and appreciates pivot support from Mienfoo and Natu, as they can provide it a free switch into Pokemon like Koffing and Pawniard. It is imperative that Mudbray be played carefully around Air Balloon Diglett, as recklessly using Earthquake or High Horsepower to KO a foe like Mareanie can leave Mudbray trapped.

RestTalk.description:
A RestTalk set greatly improves Mudbray's longevity, allowing it to beat several Pokemon, such as Mienfoo and Natu, one-on-one. It can even survive hits from threatening special attackers such as Abra thanks to its Special Defense investment and retaliate with a powerful hit. Heavy Slam is the best coverage to hit Flying-types and Ground-immune foes like Air Balloon Diglett.

RestTalk Mudbray usually finds itself on more offensive teams like Fighting spam as a way to keep offensive momentum and provide a much-needed defensive backbone. Grookey is still a terror for Mudbray, so pairing it with Koffing, Foongus, and Natu is recommended. RestTalk Mudbray also struggles against Water-types such as Frillish and Staryu because they can take advantage of it using Rest or force it out. As such, partners like Pawniard and Ferroseed are recommended; they also help it by checking threats like Abra and Porygon.

Defensive.description: Mudsdale is a solid Pokemon on defensive teams, blanket checking a wide variety of physical threats including Zeraora and Aerodactyl thanks to its Ground typing and useful ability. Stamina combined with its solid bulk also gives it an edge over other Ground-types like Hippowdon and Seismitoad, as it checks Fire Lash Cinderace. Shore Up lets it stay healthy throughout a game. Stealth Rock or Spikes provide entry hazard support, assisting wallbreakers like Aerodactyl, Clefable, and Reuniclus. Thousand Waves lets Mudsdale threaten the likes of Heatran, Toxapex, and Tyranitar and its trapping effect prevents the opponent from double switching. Body Press takes advantage of the Defense boosts from Stamina and lets Mudsdale force out Ferrothorn after enough boosts are accumulated. Toxic is an alternative that cripples switch-ins like Rotom-W, Thundurus-T, and Rillaboom. Ferrothorn is able to switch in on Seismitoad and Rotom-W and is able to run another move like Cotton Guard or Spikes because Mudsdale already sets Stealth Rock. Knock Off users like Tornadus-T and Clefable remove items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from Pokemon like Tornadus-T and Corviknight, making it even harder to deal with Mudsdale's entry hazards. Clefable also provides solid entry hazard removal in Rapid Spin, keeping Spikes up for other teammates to take advantage of. Teammates that can cover Mudsdales common weaknesses, ranging from strong special attackers like Thundurus-T and Latios to Pokemon with strong super effective coverage like Keldeo and Cloyster, make for good teammates. The likes of Blissey, Heatran, Toxapex, and Ferrothorn all do this job well enough, as well.

nu.overview: Mudsdale differentiates itself from other Stealth Rock setters like Copperajah, Galarian Stunfisk, and Diancie by better handling physical attackers such as Drapion, Tyrantrum, and Stakataka. Mudsdale's solid physical bulk, ability in Stamina, and typing help it match offensive power with defensive might to check these wallbreakers. Mudsdale also lacks passivity issues thanks to its high Attack and strong moves in STAB Earthquake and Body Press, the latter of which can take advantage of Stamina boosts. Mudsdale is otherwise far too easily to overwhelm with common special attackers like Starmie, Alolan Exeggutor, and Nasty Plot Salazzle. Additionally, Mudsdale is an ineffective Volt Switch deterrent because the most common Volt Switch users, Rotom-C and Heliolisk, can easily OHKO it with Leaf Storm and Grass Knot, respectively, and it's also very slow.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Roar prevents Substitute users like Braviary and Araquanid from taking advantage of Mudsdale as easily as well as bulkier setup sweepers like Scrafty and Snorlax. Iron Defense is similar, although limited to physical setup sweepers, and makes Mudsdale a potent bulky setup sweeper. Payback helps against foes like Decidueye and Dhelmise, but Toxic gets the job done well enough. Choice Band sets make use of Mudsdale's incredible Attack stat and solid coverage moves to turn it into a good wallbreaker, although it's very prediction reliant and at risk of being setup fodder for foes like Rotom-C and Decidueye.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Rotom-C and Decidueye are immune to or resist Earthquake, force Mudsdale out, and can set up with Nasty Plot and Swords Dance. Vileplume has immense physical bulk augmented by Strength Sap, and it's immune to Toxic. Dhelmise can spin away Mudsdale's Stealth Rock, although doing so may negatively affect its ability to beat Toxic + Protect Mudsdale one-on-one due to Stamina.

Water-types: Defensive Water-types such as Mantine and Vaporeon have little issue taking on Mudsdale, only disliking being poisoned by Toxic. Offensive Water-types like Starmie and Inteleon, meanwhile, can easily dispatch Mudsdale.

Ground-immune Pokemon: Braviary can fairly easily set up against Mudsdale, especially if it has Substitute, although it must use Bulk Up a couple of times before attacking because of Mudsdale's Stamina. Levitate Weezing has a good matchup against Mudsdale with its combination of Will-O-Wisp + Taunt, preventing Mudsdale from doing significant damage to it with Earthquake and denying Stealth Rock. Xatu simply denies any Mudsdale variant from setting Stealth Rock.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Toxic prevents common switch-ins like Dhelmise, Decidueye, and Mantine from easily exploiting Mudsdale. Protect helps Mudsdale accumulate poison damage, gain extra health from Leftovers, and scout Choice item attackers like Rotom-C and Choice Specs Decidueye. Alternatively, Body Press has good synergy with Stamina and helps against Guzzlord and Braviary. You can consider running 64 Special Defense EVs to avoid Salazzle from OHKOing Mudsdale with +2 Fire Blast, although this benchmark is rarely necessary. A Relaxed nature with 0 Speed IVs minimizes Stakataka's Gyro Ball damage.

Mudsdale is vulnerable to powerful special attackers such as Inteleon, Rotom-C, and Starmie, so it benefits from teammates like Sylveon, Assault Vest Copperajah, and Mantine that can take attacks from such foes. Mudsdale is a great answer to opposing Rock-types such as Diancie and Tyrantrum, so pair it with Fire-types like Talonflame, Salazzle, and Arcanine. In return, these Pokemon help against Grass- and Ice-types. Similarly, Mudsdale is effective at luring in and crippling bulky Water-types with Toxic; teammates like Inteleon and Swords Dance Escavalier appreciate this. Mudsdale appreciates the support of Grass-types like Vileplume and Decidueye, which handle opposing Water- and Grass-types.

nu.overview: Araquanid's natural Special Defense and typing allow it to set up on many passive Pokemon, namely Vaporeon, and it can also take on many attackers such as Inteleon and Salazzle. It also manages to maintain an offensive presence with Water Bubble-boosted Liquidation. However, its low base Attack and Speed leave it outmatched by opposing wallbreakers like Golurk and Toxicroak, and it struggles if the opposition lacks Pokemon for it to use Substitute on. Its subpar physical bulk also leaves it struggling to capitalize on many of its resistances, so it can take heavy damage trying to switch into the likes of Copperajah and Passimian.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Araquanid is a rare user of Sticky Web, which can be really useful for partners in competitive Speed tiers, like Exploud and Drapion; it can even pull off a dedicated lead set with moves like Magic Coat in such cases. However, such a set is generally regarded as a waste of Araquanid's other talents.

Checks and Counters

Sound Move Wallbreakers: Araquanid needs to be wary of Exploud and Choice Specs Sylveon; both can bypass Substitute, potentially landing OHKOs after Substitute damage.

Electric-types and Electric-type Coverage: Despite Leech Life offensively pressuring them, Rotom-C and Heliolisk are generally safe switch-ins to Liquidation and threaten heavy damage with their STAB attacks.

Faster Physical Attackers: If Araquanid struggles to get a Substitute up, its low Speed and physical bulk leave it vulnerable to the STAB and coverage moves of faster attackers like Golurk and Tauros; even the likes of Diancie and Rhydon can invest in Speed to demolish it before it gets a chance to use Liquidation.

Poison-types: Between Dry Skin and its Poison typing, Toxicroak is utterly unfazed by anything Araquanid could try to do to it. Other Poison-types like Weezing and Vileplume also have solid matchups against it. Garbodor also annoys Araquanid with Rocky Helmet and Aftermath.

Residual Damage: Mudsdale and Vaporeon can poison Araquanid with Toxic on the switch and completely ruin its chances of stallbreaking if its team lacks a cleric. Chip damage from Xatu's or Weezing's Rocky Helmet can also give Araquanid issues. Additionally, Passimian can remove Araquanid's Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, forcing it to take entry hazard damage.

Substitute Attacker.description:
Set Details

Substitute should be used against foes that cannot break past Araquanid, such as Vaporeon; it can also be used against Pokemon that it comfortably scares out, like Mudsdale and Salazzle. From behind a Substitute, Araquanid should use a combination of Liquidation and Toxic to wear down foes. Leech Life provides some extra recovery and is Araquanid's best move against Water-resistant foes like Starmie, Rotom-C, and Guzzlord. 188 Speed EVs are used to outspeed uninvested Vaporeon.

Araquanid is most at home when taking advantage of and crippling passive Pokemon like Vaporeon and Mudsdale; this is a great boon for sweepers like Nasty Plot Salazzle. Pokemon like Mudsdale and Diancie also benefit from Araquanid switching into stray Scalds and checking Inteleon. In exchange, they can take on various physical attackers that threaten Araquanid; Mudsdale easily takes on the likes of Tyrantrum and Aerodactyl, while Diancie takes care of Flying-types such as Ninjask. Because Araquanid is still vulnerable to Exploud and Sylveon when behind a Substitute, it appreciates the support of Steel-types like Copperajah and Escavalier to take their attacks. In return, Araquanid threatens the opposition's Ground- and Fire-types.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bug

Scald may be used with a Modest nature, as it allows Araquanid to fish for burns. However, Liquidation lets it check Spectrier and Roost Volcarona well. A trapping set with Infestation, Soak, Toxic, and Rest, holding a Grip Claw, traps and removes bulky walls such as Celesteela and Toxapex that normally give Araquanid a difficult time; however, if such targets are not present on the opposing team, it turns Araquanid into a liability. Water Absorb may be considered to pivot into threats such as Barraskewda, but Water Bubble's resistance to Fire-type moves is Araquanid's main appeal. Wacan Berry may be used to lure in Tapu Koko and Choice Band Victini, but since Bug can choose to not run dedicated entry hazard removers, forgoing Heavy-Duty Boots may hurt Araquanid's ability to check threats such as Blacephalon and Spectrier in the long run.

Sticky Web (Bug).description:
Araquanid is the best defensive Sticky Web setter available for Bug teams, and it differentiates itself from Galvantula by taking on special attackers such as Blacephalon, Spectrier, and Nidoking. Thanks to Water Bubble, it checks threats such as Volcarona and Heatran, which greatly trouble Bug teams. Liquidation deals with Calm Mind and Quiver Dance users such as Spectrier and Volcarona, and it generally threatens Fire-types. Mirror Coat takes advantage of Araquanid's excellent Special Defense, allowing it to retaliate against threats that don't mind Liquidation such as Thundurus-T and Volcanion. Toxic debilitates switch-ins such as Slowbro, Mantine, and Gastrodon. Magic Coat can be used over Toxic, as it bounces back Taunt, Leech Seed, and Stealth Rock from Cobalion, Celesteela, and Garchomp, allowing Araquanid to set Sticky Web uncontested and maximize its longevity. 156 Speed EVs let Araquanid outspeed and beat non-Air Slash Celesteela one-on-one, while maximum HP EVs allow it to survive attacks such as Choice Specs Tapu Koko's Volt Switch, Hurricane from Tornadus-T, and non-Choice Band Victini's Bolt Strike.

Setup sweepers such as Scizor, Volcarona, and Heracross make great teammates for Araquanid, as these all benefit from Sticky Web and a Fire resistance. Swords Dance Scizor deals with Ice- and Rock-type threats such as Kyurem and Tyranitar, can clean types such as Dragon and Fairy, and uses Sticky Web to outspeed Heatran. Volcarona greatly appreciates Araquanid dealing with Heatran and Victini, as this allows it to sweep types such as Steel and Psychic late-game. Guts Heracross deals with walls such as Toxapex, Slowbro, and Galarian Corsola, and Sticky Web allows it to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, removing threats such as Dragapult, Choice Band Victini, and Choice Scarf Heatran. Araquanid setting Sticky Web frees a moveslot for Galvantula, allowing it to run Agility. Thanks to Sticky Web, Galvantula even outspeeds Swift Swim Barraskewda at +2, making it a potent late-game wincon against Water and Flying teams. Galvantula also appreciates Araquanid's ability to heavily damage Thundurus-T and pressure Ground-types like Landorus-T. Choice Scarf Buzzwole deals with threats such as Cinderace and Excadrill, and Sticky Web lets it clean frailer types such as Electric, Dragon, Dark, and Fire, which have limited defensive counterplay against it.

Sticky Web (Water).description:
Araquanid takes on the role as a Sticky Web setter for Water-type teams. Thanks to Sticky Web, slow, hard-hitting Pokemon like Crawdaunt and Choice Specs Pelipper become more threatening, as they are able to outspeed opposing Pokemon more easily. Araquanid should be used as a lead most of the time to get up Sticky Web early. Its ability Water Bubble not only boosts its Water-type moves, making Liquidation hit much harder, but it also makes it immune to burns from Scald and Will-O-Wisp, making it harder for defensive Pokemon like Toxapex and Sableye to deal with it. With Liquidation, Araquanid is also able to deal with Magic Bounce users like Hatterene, which can block Sticky Web.
