Leech Life lets Araquanid threaten Dark- and Psychic-type Pokemon like Hydreigon and Indeedee while also healing itself. Magic Coat allows it to bounce back status moves like Taunt against common lead Pokemon such as Froslass and Kommo-o. It is also useful against Spikes and Toxic Spikes setters like Ferrothorn and Toxapex. Mirror Coat allows Araquanid to beat threats to Water-type teams, like Duraludon, Heliolisk, Noivern, Hatterene, and Choice Specs Dragapult. Maximum Attack investment optimizes its overall damage output. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature makes it as fast as possible to outspeed Pokemon like Mandibuzz and Corviknight, and Focus Sash ensures that it can set up Sticky Web most of the time.

Potent wallbreakers and setup sweepers like Keldeo, Gyarados, Pelipper, Crawdaunt, and Cloyster appreciate Araquanid's Sticky Web support because they are able to threaten opposing teams more and become much harder to get revenge killed. Since Araquanid is weak to Electric- and Rock-type Pokemon such as Zeraora and Tyranitar, Seismitoad makes for a good partner, as it can cover for its weakness against them and set Stealth Rock while also benefiting from Araquanid's Sticky Web support.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Focus Sash can be run to turn Araquanid into a Sticky Web lead, but Shuckle usually does the job better. Giving Araquanid a Speed donation allows it to outspeed many Pokemon without the need for Trick Room, however Araquanid's low natural attacking stats make it easy to wall.

Checks and Counters

Pokemon Immune to Water: Pokemon with Storm Drain and Water Absorb, the most common being Volcanion and Gastrodon, force mind games with Araquanid and discourage it from using its Water-type moves even if they can be vulnerable to its other attacks.

Entry Hazards: Due to usually forgoing Heavy-Duty Boots, entry hazards, especially Stealth Rock, wear down Araquanid and get it in range of priority moves.

Revenge Killers: Outside of Trick Room, Araquanid is prone to getting revenge killed by most strong offensive threats. Rayquaza, Zeraora, and Tapu Koko can all hit it super effectively and OHKO it.

Special Attacker (Special Attack).description:
Special Araquanid is a powerful wallbreaker under Trick Room with few switch-ins, capable of breaking even the most defensively sturdy teams. Water Bubble boosts its Water-type STAB moves to an astronomical level, with Hydro Pump capable of OHKOing Rayquaza and Dialga. Bug Buzz is a solid secondary STAB option and its best option to hit Tangrowth and Slowbro. Giga Drain is necessary to nail Gastrodon and Seismitoad, which would otherwise wall it with ease. Surf is used for consistency and conserving PP, trading power for accuracy. Ice Beam is an alternative that hits a few sturdy walls, notably Giratina, for significant damage. Since Araquanid usually only needs Hydro Pump, Choice Specs is the preferred item to maximize its damage output; resisted Hydro Pump is still stronger than neutral Bug Buzz and almost as strong as super effective Ice Beam. Minimum Speed is run to make Araquanid outspeed as many Pokemon as possible under Trick Room.

Necrozma-DW is the best god to complement Araquanid, as it has access to Trick Room and sports impressive Special Attack stat; it also appreciates Araquanid's ability to beat or soften opposing special walls to clean up late-game. Other Trick Room users are also required for Araquanid to function. Slowking and Porygon2, in particular, also learn Teleport, allowing Araquanid to get in without having to take damage, and they are also bulky enough to take on revenge killers when Trick Room runs out. Hatterene supports Araquanid by providing Healing Wish support and also prevents opposing entry hazards with Magic Bounce. Even though Araquanid can 2HKO Ferrothorn and Tangrowth, they can annoy it with Knock Off or switch in to scout its attack, respectively; as such, teammates that take care of them such as Victini and Buzzwole are recommended.

Physical Attacker (Attack).description:
Physical Araquanid is a threatening wallbreaker, especially under Trick Room, capable of punching holes through sturdy defensive stalwarts like Skarmory and Clefable thanks to an Attack donation. Liquidation is its strongest attack thanks to Water Bubble, which notably hits neutral targets even harder than super effective coverage moves, reducing the need to predict. Leech Life is Araquanid's best option against Tangrowth, Slowking, and Pokemon immune to Water such as Gastrodon and Seismitoad. Crunch provides super effective damage against Giratina, which could otherwise stall Liquidation's PP. In its last moveslot, it can either go with Poison Jab, which also possesses a high poison chance, to deal more damage to Tapu Fini and Volcanion, or Toxic to cripple Vaporeon, which completely walls it. Choice Band is the preferred item to maximize its damage output, as it usually only needs to use Liquidation. While usually used in Trick Room teams, Araquanid can still be used without a dedicated team, as its defensive utility and Water Bubble's ability to prevent burn and halving Fire-type damage provide it a lot of opportunities to switch in against foes, namely Heatran and Clefable. In those cases, Araquanid should run Sticky Web over Crunch and opt for Heavy-Duty Boots to negate entry hazards. Minimal Speed is run if Araquanid is used in Trick Room teams; otherwise, it should run 31 Speed IVs, 148 Speed EVs, and Adamant nature to outpace uninvested Clefable.

Araquanid best fits in Trick Room teams where it can take advantage of its low Speed. Calyrex-I and Necrozma-DM are mandatory partners to maximize Araquanid's damage output, and they can also set Trick Room. In return, Araquanid can wear down physical walls, in particular Skarmory and opposing Necrozma-DM, for them. Other bulky Trick Room setters, especially Porygon2 and Slowking, are also needed to take hits after Trick Room has ended; they also have Teleport, allowing Araquanid to come in without having to take damage. Hatterene has Magic Bounce, preventing entry hazards from limiting Araquanid's opportunities to switch in. Other offensive Trick Room attackers that can deal with Ferrothorn and physically bulky Pokemon immune to Water are needed, making Conkeldurr and Speed-received Kartana and Blacephalon great teammates. If Araquanid finds itself on teams without Trick Room, then it can take the leftover Attack slot from gods like Kyurem-W and Giratina-O. Entry hazard deterrents, including Ghost-types to spinblock such as Blacephalon and Defiant users in Bisharp and Galarian Zapdos, are recommended to prevent Sticky Web from being easily cleared.

Suicide Lead.description: This set is often found in hyper offense teams that get advantage of the opposing Pokemon being affected by Sticky Web.

zu.comments:
Other Options

If entry hazard removal isn’t needed, Lurantis can run Aromatherapy over Defog to remove status that could cripple a Contrary sweep while curing its teammates in the process. Knock Off is also a useful fourth move to cripple switch-ins like Altaria and Tangela. Toxic is an option to put a timer on bulkier foes that resist Lurantis’s moves like Articuno but only compounds its weakness to opposing Poison-types. Setup support like Substitute and Safeguard can be useful, but Lurantis is often too slow to use these moves well and generally gains more advantage by simply using Leaf Storm or Superpower. Lurantis can also run a specially defensive set to check Rotom with the expectation that Superpower will then improve its Defense after one use. Heavy-Duty Boots is a good item for getting the most out of Defog, but Leftovers synergizes better with the high likelihood of staying in multiple turns to take advantage of Contrary. Leppa Berry can be used to remedy the PP issues Lurantis faces with Leaf Storm and Superpower and works especially well against Articuno's attempts to Pressure stall.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Pure Poison-types like Silvally-Poison resist Lurantis’s combo of Grass- and Fighting-type coverage, and others like Skuntank and Qwilfish resist just one of Grass or Fighting. Silvally-Poison and Skunktank can comfortably switch into even Knock Off variants of Lurantis, and all three Pokemon threaten Lurantis with super effective STAB Poison moves.

Flying-types: Articuno and Altaria resist Lurantis’s Grass STAB moves and Altaria resists Superpower too. Both Pokemon threaten Lurantis with STAB Hurricane and Articuno can even opt for a more accurate Freeze-Dry if needed. Roost also allows these Pokemon to stay healthy throughout a game, though Articuno must beware of Superpower when it loses its Flying typing and both Pokemon are significantly crippled by Knock Off.

Fire-types: Rapidash, Ninetales, and to a lesser extent Coalossal all threaten Lurantis with Fire STAB moves. Rapidash and Ninetales can boost alongside Lurantis, and Rapidash's Flame Body can punish repeated uses of Superpower.

Ice-types: Jynx, Froslass, and Cryogonal generally fear Lurantis's attacks but with momentum can force it out with Ice Beam or Freeze Dry. Articuno threatens Lurantis similarly but with the added benefit of resisting Leaf Storm. Abomasnow can switch into Leaf Storm too and immediately threaten to OHKO Lurantis with Blizzard.

Fast Special Attackers: Lurantis is a slow Pokemon and Superpower only boosts it Defense stat, making it susceptible to super effective attacks targeting its Special Defense from faster Pokemon like Poliwrath, Cramorant, or Manectric.

Grass-types: Lilligant can set up Quiver Dances and strike with a super effective Pollen Puff. Tangela and Roselia can stall out Leaf Storm and threaten with Sludge Bomb. Gourgeist can 2HKO with Poltergeist and is immune to Superpower. Chlorophyll sweepers like Ivysaur and Exeggutor can take advantage of Lurantis too.

Defog.description:
Lurantis combines a pure-Grass typing, serviceable mixed bulk, and strong Contrary move pool to effectively check common entry hazard setters like Rhydon, Stunfisk, and Qwilfish to either clear hazards with Defog or threaten to sweep. Leaf Storm is a strong STAB attack that boosts Lurantis’s Special Attack by two stages after each use due to Contrary. Superpower also benefits from Contrary, providing super effective Fighting coverage for Sap Sipper Miltank and Klinklang while also hitting Fire-types, Grass-types, and Articuno for neutral damage. Synthesis ensures Lurantis can remain healthy enough to repeatedly clear entry hazards or sustain itself for a Contrary sweep. 216 Speed EVs lets Lurantis outpace Adamant Rhydon and uninvested Alcremie. The remaining EVs are invested into bulk to better check physical entry hazard setters, notably allowing Lurantis to survive hits like +2 Stone Edge from standard Stealth Rock Rhydon.

Lurantis is most valuable when clearing entry hazards but thanks to Contrary, Leaf Storm, and Superpower, Lurantis can often scale its damage output enough to break through the healing moves of bulkier cores. Rhydon, Palossand, and Stunfisk all specifically have trouble defeating Lurantis, which opens opportunities for teammates like Silvally-Poison and Rotom which are usually stopped by these Pokemon. Lurantis struggles greatly against bulky Poison- and Flying-type foes like opposing Silvally-Poison and Altaria. Lurantis is also quite slow, so it is forced out by any faster Pokemon, such as Rapidash, Ninetales, Froslass, Jinx, and Articuno. Klinklang is a good partner because of its resistances and ability to OHKO Ice-types with an unboosted Gear Grind. In return, Lurantis handles Stunfisk, Galarian Stunfisk, and Palossand, all of which commonly shrug off Klinklang’s moves. Rapidash and Coalossal are good teammates too because they check offensive Fire- and Ice-types, and Lurantis can handle opposing Rock- and Ground-types in turn.

doublesou.overview: Lurantis has a niche as a Trick Room attacker with its low Speed and the capability to snowball damage with the combination of Superpower and Contrary, boosting its Attack and Defense every time it hits. Contrary also gives Lurantis Attack boosts from Intimidate, making opposing Incineroar hesitant to switch in. With Trick Room being essential for Lurantis to be effective, bulky Trick Room setters like Porygon2 and Diancie work great as teammates. Tapu Fini also works well as a partner, as it can set Misty Terrain to prevent Luratis from getting burned by Will-O-Wisp from Mew and checking Fire-types like Heatran. Dragapult, meanwhile, can check some of Lurantis's greatest threats outside of Trick Room, outspeeding and OHKOing Landorus and Naganadel with Draco Meteor when they would otherwise OHKO Lurantis with Sludge Bomb. Lurantis's main downsides are its mediocre stats and need for boosts from Intimidate or Superpower to be particularly threatening—which can make it difficult to justify using over other Pokemon—and reliance on Trick Room. Even with Trick Room active, Amoonguss can move before it and either take away its stat boosts with Clear Smog or do heavy damage with Sludge Bomb.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Grassy Glide can be used over Leaf Blade if run alongside Rillaboom to give Lurantis a priority attack, making it more effective outside of Trick Room, though it is less powerful than Leaf Blade. Leaf Storm is another move Lurantis can use that pairs well with Contrary—boosting Lurantis's Special Attack by two stages—but has shaky accuracy and uses the lower of Lurantis's attacking stats.

Trick Room Attacker.description:
• Leaf Blade is Lurantis's most powerful physical STAB attack, able to hit Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Diancie for super effective damage.

  • Superpower, while being slightly weaker than Leaf Blade, is often Lurantis's primary attack, since it wants to get stat boosts as soon as possible. It also serves as coverage for Incineroar and Kyurem-B.

  • Knock Off covers targets that resist both Grass and Fighting like Amoonguss, Dragapult, and Zapdos and provides utility in removing items. Substitute can be used instead to capitalize on passive play from opponents attempting to stall out Trick Room and keeps Lurantis safe against powerful special attackers.

  • Protect can keep Lurantis safe while Trick Room being is set up or can allow you to reposition and bring in a partner that checks Lurantis's threat.

  • Sitrus Berry provides burst healing for Lurantis.

Defensive.description: Morelull's niche over Foongus is being a check to Fighting-types and Grookey that isn't weak to Psychic, letting it also check Psychic Fangs Tyrunt and Carvanha. Morelull also offers teams key resistances to Ground- and Dark-type moves. Effect Spore gives Morelull a chance to punish Pokemon using contact moves, such as Flip Turn Carvanha and Mienfoo. Foongus and Ferroseed both wall Morelull and are immune to Spore; Natu can deal with these Pokemon thanks to Magic Bounce and Heat Wave. Morelull is greatly threatened by Poison-types such as Koffing and Mareanie and Fire-types such as Ponyta and Vulpix. Ground-types such as Diglett and Onix and Water-types such as Frillish and Staryu can deal with these Pokemon. In return, they benefit from Morelull dealing with Grookey and Staryu.

zu.comments:
Other Options:

Choice Specs sets can surprise opponents expecting the standard set, and have decent breaking power. However, they lose out on most of what makes Shiinotic effective and are usually outclassed by other options such as Exeggutor and Appletun.

Checks and Counters:

Poison-types: Poison-types like Silvally-Poison, Qwilfish, and Ivysaur are immune to Toxic, resist Moonblast, and threaten to OHKO Shiinotic.

Steel-types: Steel-types are immune to Toxic, resist Shiinotic's STAB moves, and hit it super effectively. Most of them also have other ways to abuse it, like Substitute + Toxic Alolan Dugtrio or Klinklang's Clear Body, which denies Strength Sap.

Ice-types: Ice-types such as Abomasnow and Froslass threaten Shiinotic with their strong, super effective STAB attacks and do not grant much recovery if Strength Sap is used against them. Most of them also have ways to prevent or alleviate the status Shiinotic inflicts.

Super Effective Coverage: Shiinotic needs to be wary of foes running super effective coverage for it, like Iron Head Silvally-Dark, Ice Beam Poliwrath, and Sludge Bomb Tangela.

Strong Attackers: Some powerful breakers whose STAB moves are not resisted by Shiinotic, like Choice Band Lycanroc, Choice Specs Exeggutor, and Choice Specs Rotom, can brute-force their way through it.

Physical Wall.description:
Shiinotic is a great physical wall due to its unique typing and moveset letting it check a number of threats like Sawk, Thwackey, and Appletun. Spore can put switch-ins like Silvally-Poison and Ninetales out of commission, and the move itself forces many switches. The last moveslot can be dedicated to either Toxic, which punishes Pokemon that are immune to Spore like Tangela and Sap Sipper Miltank and puts foes on a timer, or Giga Drain, which makes Shiinotic more reliable at dealing with Ground- and Water-types, such as Rhydon and Poliwrath. No item is run to avoid Poltergeist from Gourgeist formes and Trevenant; however, Rocky Helmet can be used to punish Pokemon that use contact moves such as Kangaskhan and Gurdurr.

Slower wallbreakers, like Thievul and Swords Dance Rhydon, that are weak to common fast Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Sawk and Thwackey appreciate Shiinotic's ability to answer them and create opportunities for them to wallbreak with Spore and Effect Spore. Popular Ground-types and Water-types such as Stunfisk and Poliwrath easily fold to threats handled by Shiinotic like Appletun, Morpeko, and Silvally-Water. In return, they answer Poison- and Flying-types like Skuntank and Unfezant and Steel- and Fire-types like Klinklang and Ninetales, respectively, that Shiinotic is weak to. Offensive teammates like Rotom and Jynx as well as defensive options like Rhydon and Hattrem greatly appreciate Shiinotic's ability to absorb Knock Off. Setup sweepers like Ninetales and various Silvally formes also get an immense advantage out of the free turns provided by Spore, and enjoy walls getting crippled by a surprise Toxic.

uu.overview: Salazzle's good Speed tier, ability in Corrosion, and solid offensive utility make it a decent support Pokemon in UU. It can outspeed many offensive threats such as Zarude and Azelf, and it takes advantage of defensive staples like Amoonguss and Skarmory. The combination of Knock Off and Toxic lets it outlast Pokemon that would otherwise counter it, such as Tentacruel and Nihilego, and open up counters like Hippowdon for teammates. However, due to its weakness to Stealth Rock, Salazzle is forced to run Heavy-Duty Boots as opposed to a power-boosting item, which makes it heavily reliant on chip damage to make an impact. Its poor bulk also leaves it unable to contribute defensively in most games, and its typing makes it susceptible to priority users like Azumarill and Lycanroc-D. Salazzle's frailty also makes it reliant on pivots to safely enter the battlefield. This frailty also deters it from switching directly into most Pokemon it would otherwise check, especially Scizor and Tangrowth, who both carry Knock Off and can remove its Heavy-Duty Boots. Therefore, it would rather be preserved as a secondary check to the aforementioned Pokemon. It is also extremely difficult for Salazzle to make progress against bulkier Pokemon like Slowking and Hippowdon, but its Toxic support and chip damage can help mid-game wallbreakers and offensive pivots like Mamoswine and Azelf, respectively, break through or pressure them.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Pulse can OHKO Zygarde-10% but should only be used if your team is weak to it. Nasty Plot over Toxic can make Salazzle a threatening wallbreaker or cleaner, but due to its frailty, it struggles to set up because even resisted attacks sting. Substitute + Toxic Salazzle can be annoying, but Salazzle struggles to make an impact when lacking one of its STAB moves, leaving it to pick and choose its good matchups and lose out on valuable utility. Substitute + Toxic also requires very solid entry hazard control, if running Black Sludge, and is still vulnerable to sand chip damage. A Choice Specs set has powerful wallbreaking potential, OHKOing threats like Conkeldurr and Thundurus-T from full health, but Salazzle can't follow up with Toxic and becomes weak to Stealth Rock, cutting into its longevity. It is also extremely prediction reliant, heavily limiting its wallbreaking potential against common defensive staples like Slowking and Hippowdon.

Checks and Counters

Faster Threats and Priority: Pokemon that commonly run Choice Scarf, such as Hydreigon and Diggersby, take advantage of Salazzle's extreme frailty and revenge kill it with ease. Priority users like Lycanroc-D and Zygarde-10% revenge kill Salazzle as well. Crobat and Noivern naturally outspeed and nail Salazzle for heavy damage.

Special Walls: Chansey can switch into Salazzle thanks to its reliable recovery and Natural Cure, proceeding to force Salazzle out. However, it hates taking Knock Off. Mandibuzz, specially defensive Hippowdon, and Nihilego are all able to switch in comfortably; however, they all hate Knock Off and Toxic.

Water-types: Water-types such as Slowking, Tentacruel, and Swampert can all switch into Salazzle multiple times but despise taking Toxic. Azumarill can KO Salazzle with Aqua Jet.

Offensive.description:
Salazzle's solid STAB combination lets it threaten common UU Pokemon including Amoonguss, Celesteela, Scizor, and Primarina. Knock Off makes Salazzle more difficult to pivot around with common checks such as Chansey, Mandibuzz, and Swampert. Toxic alongside Corrosion lets Salazzle cripple switch-ins like Nihilego, Tentacruel, Hippowdon, and Slowking, allowing itself or a teammate to overwhelm them and enhancing its offensive potential. Maximum Speed investment is needed to outspeed offensive threats like Azelf, Zarude, and Cobalion. Heavy-Duty Boots alleviates Salazzle's crippling Stealth Rock weakness and helps with its longevity, giving it more opportunities to enter the field safely.

Salazzle fits best on bulky offense teams that appreciate it heavily chipping the opposing team, paving the way for teammates to break holes with ease. Mamoswine is an excellent partner for Salazzle, beating checks like Chansey and Mandibuzz and wearing down their shared answers in Swampert and Slowking. Chip damage from Stealth Rock setters, such as Nihilego, Cobalion, and Swampert, is valuable to make switching into Salazzle even more of a pain. Knock Off absorbers, such as the aforementioned Cobalion, Amoonguss, and Tangrowth, are all appreciated due to how punishing it is for Salazzle to lose Heavy-Duty Boots. Cobalion in particular can draw in Grass-types to give Salazzle entry points to fire off an attack. Meanwhile, Amoonguss and Tangrowth check Swampert and Azumarill. Thundurus-T and Zarude are great partners, as both offensively pressure Slowking and Swampert while pivoting on Amoonguss and Tangrowth, giving Salazzle safe entry points despite its frailty. Celesteela and Slowking both reliably check Nihilego and Zygarde-10% for Salazzle. Slowking is able to pivot out on Grass-types with Teleport to let Salazzle in. Checks to defensive Scizor like Celesteela, Cobalion, and Salamence all pair well with Salazzle, as it cannot function as the sole Scizor check on most teams. Salamence also appreciates Salazzle wearing down Hippowdon and Slowking through Knock Off + Toxic, as this makes it extremely difficult for them to switch into repeated Hurricanes.

Wallbreaker.description:
Salazzle's high Speed, powerful STAB combination, and access to Nasty Plot give it immense wallbreaking potential. Toxic and Corrosion allow Salazzle to pressure most of its checks, including Gastrodon, Milotic, and Dragalge. Knock Off can be used over Nasty Plot to further punish Salazzle's switch-ins by removing items such as Leftovers, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Assault Vest.

Salazzle appreciates Fighting-type wallbreakers that help it with specially defensive walls such as Umbreon and Snorlax, with Heracross, Bewear, and Lucario being good options. Salazzle has bad defensive stats, so it appreciates having pivots like Milotic, Raikou, and Noivern to bring it in unharmed. Salazzle relies on entry hazard support from Klefki, Roserade, or Golisopod so it can OHKO foes with its powerful STAB attacks. Grass-types such as Dhelmise, Celebi, and Decidueye help Salazzle against Water- and Rock-type checks such as Gastrodon and Diancie. Electric-types such as Toxtricity and Xurkitree are also good teammates because they can pressure Water-type Pokemon, get Salazzle onto the field safely with Volt Switch, and further wear down special sponges such as Porygon2 and Umbreon.

nu.overview: Salazzle's access to Nasty Plot and incredible offensive stats make it a premier setup sweeper in NU. Despite having difficulty bypassing common Water-types, very few other foes can stand up to Salazzle's boosted attacks; for example, +2 Overheat gets past Mudsdale, while +2 Dragon Pulse deals with Guzzlord. Additionally, Salazzle possesses a very convenient defensive typing, which helps it avoid being revenge killed by Rotom-C's Leaf Storm and Passimian's Close Combat. Despite all of this, other fast foes like Inteleon, Talonflame, and Choice Scarf Heliolisk give Salazzle trouble, and Salazzle lacks any effective way to bypass bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Mantine on its own.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A set with the moves Substitute / Toxic / Protect / Flamethrower and Black Sludge is good at crippling the opposition and letting Salazzle scout foes. Choice item sets are workable thanks to Salazzle's great natural Special Attack and Speed, but it lacks good coverage moves beyond its STAB attacks and Dragon Pulse and dislikes locking into moves such as Toxic and Knock Off.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Foes like Mantine and Vaporeon are effective walls versus Salazzle and can KO it with Scald. Offensively, Inteleon is faster and easily OHKOes Salazzle with Hydro Pump, while Starmie can tank a single hit and OHKO in return.

Rock-types: Gigalith and Rhydon wall Salazzle's STAB moves with ease but are quite annoyed by a Knock Off or Toxic long-term. Diancie, despite its Poison neutrality, can defensively answer Salazzle and OHKO it with Diamond Storm. Choice Scarf Tyrantrum and Aerodactyl outspeed and OHKO Salazzle with their Rock-type attacks and Earthquake.

Revenge Killers: Salazzle's terrible bulk means faster foes like Talonflame, Choice Scarf Rotom-C, and Inteleon can pick it off.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Picking between STAB attacks is mostly up to preference. Overheat picks up notable KOs on the likes of Mudsdale, Stakataka, and Silvally-Ground after a Nasty Plot, whereas Fire Blast can be used consecutively without reducing the user's Special Attack. Similarly, Sludge Bomb offers a higher poison chance, while Sludge Wave is slightly stronger. Knock Off and Toxic both cripple common checks like Mantine, Vaporeon, and Gastrodon. Encore can also be considered to lock slow setup sweepers like Snorlax into unhelpful moves, making it easy for Salazzle to set up against and break through them. Heavy-Duty Boots means Salazzle is less reliant on effective entry hazard control, but Focus Sash helps avoid being revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Inteleon, Aerodactyl, and Choice Scarf users such as Passimian.

Xatu is a great teammate for Salazzle, especially Focus Sash variants, for its ability to deny entry hazards. Similarly, other hazard removers like Rotom-C and Mantine are good to have. Salazzle cannot reliably get by bulky Water-types on its own; teammates like Heliolisk and Decidueye are good as a result. On hyper offense teams, Froslass is a great lead to set Spikes and deny entry hazards with Taunt.

SubToxic (Poison).description:
Salazzle benefits Poison teams greatly by spreading status, threatening a plethora of defensive Pokemon along with Steel-type Pokemon thanks to its ability Corrosion. Salazzle should try to inflict Toxic on the opposing Pokemon then use Substitute and Protect to build up damage. Flamethrower is effective against Steel-type Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Corviknight along with various Grass-, Ice-, and Bug-type Pokemon such as Roserade, Frosmoth, and Ribombee. Before sending in Salazzle, you should try to get rid of any hazards, as it gets chipped especially heavily by Stealth Rock. It's best to avoid strong attacks because Salazzle doesn't have amazing bulk, even with maximized HP. Maximum Speed along with a Timid nature allows Salazzle to outspeed Pokemon like Hydreigon, Galarian Mr. Mime, and Froslass in setting up Substitute and stalling Toxic.

Poison teams love spreading status with Pokemon like Toxapex, Drapion, and Galarian Weezing. Salazzle contributes to spreading Toxic to all types and dealing with Steel. In return, Poison's defensive Pokemon support Salazzle because it has poor bulk. Galarian Weezing provides Ground-type immunity thanks to its ability Levitate and can Defog away hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes, allowing Salazzle to come in safely. Galarian Weezing also serves as a Dragon-type check, with it having access to Strange Stream as a STAB move. Drapion provides decisive immunity to Psychic-type moves. Choice Scarf Drapion uses Knock Off to get rid of opposing Choice items from Pokemon like Excadrill and helps inflict status with Toxic Spikes or Toxic. Toxapex resists Water-type moves and also is effective in inflicting status by having access to Baneful Bunker, Toxic Spikes, Toxic, and Scald. Toxapex is an amazing wall that is fit to survive an attack from and potentially status Pokemon such as Tyranitar and Dragapult. Vileplume resists Water-type moves and takes neutral damage from Ground-type moves, which allows it to take attacks from Pokemon like Excadrill and Dracovish. Vileplume is used to stall out damage with Strength Sap and Leech Seed from an ally's Toxic.

SubToxic (Fire).description:
Salazzle is a good option on Fire teams because of its ability in Corrosion along with its good Speed stat, allowing it to effectively spread status using Toxic. Corrosion is particularly useful for crippling Poison- and Steel-type Pokemon such as Toxapex, Skuntank, Jirachi, and Aegislash, which would otherwise switch into Toxic. Salazzle can also it to outspeed fast threats such as Keldeo and Hydreigon in order to beat them with Substitute + Protect after they have been badly poisoned by Toxic. Protect + Substitute enables Salazzle to wear down Pokemon once they have been crippled by Toxic. Protect is also used to scout against common Choice item users like Excadrill and Galarian Darmanitan, as well as to gain more passive recovery using Black Sludge. Sludge Wave lets Salazzle take on Fairy-types like Hatterene and Rest Grimmsnarl that do not mind Toxic. Salazzle should try to come in once entry hazards are gone to avoid getting worn down by Spikes and severely chipped by Stealth Rock. It should not try to switch into strong attacks because of its poor bulk and should instead be brought in through U-turn and Volt Switch. Salazzle should try to use Substitute on a predicted switch in order to get more opportunities to spread status. Having 252 HP EVs maximizes Salazzle's poor bulk in order to spread status comfortably, while having 252 Speed EVs with a Timid nature makes Salazzle able to outpace fast Pokemon such as Keldeo, Terrakion, Gengar, and Alolan Ninetales.

Salazzle appreciates Torkoal and Ninetales because of their ability to set sun with Drought and therefore weaken Water-type attacks like Toxapex's Scald for Salazzle. The former can use Yawn to make it easier for Salazzle to come in, Rapid Spin to get rid of hazards, and Stealth Rock to help damage foes to make it easier for Salazzle to stall them out, while the latter can use Hypnosis to help Salazzle come in and can use Solar Beam to take care of Ground- and Water-types such as Seismitoad and Mamoswine. Cinderace, Arcanine, and Darmanitan are all fast physical attackers that appreciate Salazzle badly poisoning walls such as Galarian Corsola, Toxapex, and Mandibuzz that give them trouble, and they can all beat Pokemon such as Tyranitar and Snorlax for Salazzle in return. Cinderace is able to use Sucker Punch to help wear down fast Pokemon like Dragapult, use U-turn to bring in Salazzle safely, and use Court Change to move hazards to the other side of the field for Salazzle. Choice Scarf Darmanitan can outspeed and beat faster Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Zeraora, and Choice Scarf Excadrill, and it can also bring in Salazzle safely with its fast U-turn. Choice Scarf Charizard can be used to help in the Dragon-type matchup, as it can take care of most Dragon-types such as Dragapult and Dracovish once sun and Stealth Rock are up with Dragon Pulse. Choice Band Arcanine can be used, as it can use Extreme Speed to take care of weakened Pokemon such as Hydreigon, Keldeo, and Alolan Raichu for the team mid- to late-game. Rotom-H is a good partner, as it can pressure Water-types such as Pelipper and Primarina with Thunderbolt and come in on Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Mamoswine, Flygon, and Hippowdon.

Swords Dance.description:
Bewear is an incredibly strong wallbreaker that uses Fluffy and its typing to take advantage of staples like Golisopod, Steelix, and Registeel. However, its low Speed and Special Defense leaves it easy pickings for common faster special attackers such as Noivern, Nidoqueen, and Xurkitree. Drain Punch mitigates damage from tanking physical attacks and recoil from using Double-Edge. At +2 Attack, Close Combat gets OHKOs that Drain Punch misses out on such as against Steelix and Diancie after Stealth Rock. Darkest Lariat covers Ghost-types like Chandelure, Mimikyu, and Dhelmise while also providing a hard-hitting move without recoil for Psychic-types like Reuniclus and Celebi. Chople Berry prevents faster threats such as Heracross and Lucario from easily revenge killing Bewear, while Silk Scarf boosts Double-Edge for an almost guaranteed OHKO on Reuniclus and Galarian Weezing after Stealth Rock. Jolly is the preferred nature to outspeed Pangoro and Choice Band Metagross. Silk Scarf variants can run an Adamant nature to OHKO Reuniclus after Swords Dance while ensuring the OHKO on Galarian Weezing after Stealth Rock.

VoltTurn support is invaluable for Bewear, as it often struggles to safely switch in. Raikou, Noivern, and Crobat are notable examples, as they can provide a free switch against Pokemon that Bewear takes advantage of such as Steelix and Registeel. Stealth Rock support is crucial for important KOs like against Galarian Weezing with +2 Silk Scarf-boosted Double-Edge. Diancie can check Fire-types such as Entei and Chandelure, while Nidoqueen can check other revenge killers like Xurkitree and Raikou. Steel-types such as Metagross, Registeel, and Klefki also set up hazards and deal with major nuisances for Bewear like Togekiss, Noivern, Crobat, and Gardevoir. Klefki is also notable for providing Thunder Wave to slow down faster threats like Noivern. Other Spikers such as Roserade and Golisopod help wear down walls while the latter provides additional support in Knock Off. Roserade also checks Electric-types trying to revenge kill Bewear such as Raikou and Xurkitree. Pokemon such as Flygon, Noivern, and Sharpedo appreciate Bewear denting Fairy-types like Togekiss and Galarian Weezing. Bewear is an excellent Knock Off absorber and can come in on Knock Off users trying to remove valuable items from Pokemon like Togekiss, Noivern, and Reuniclus.

Choice Band.description:
Without wasting a turn, Choice Band Bewear utilizes its Fluffy ability and typing to switch into common Pokemon such as Golisopod and immediately fire off incredibly strong attacks. However, as a wallbreaker, it is greatly hindered by its prediction-reliant nature, and with its average Speed, faster special attackers such as Noivern, Togekiss, and Toxtricity can effortlessly revenge kill it. The recovery from Drain Punch prevents Bewear from quickly getting worn down from tanking physical attacks and using Double-Edge. Darkest Lariat nails Ghost-types such as Chandelure, Mimikyu, and Jellicent. A Jolly nature is used to outspeed Pangoro.

VoltTurn support is invaluable for Bewear, as it often struggles to safely switch in. Raikou, Noivern, and Xurkitree are notable examples, as they can provide a free switch against Pokemon that Bewear takes advantage of such as Assault Vest Reuniclus, Steelix, and Registeel. Steel-types such as Metagross, Registeel, and Klefki deal with a major nuisance for Bewear in Flying-types like Togekiss, Noivern, and Crobat. Klefki is also notable for providing Spikes support and Thunder Wave to slow down faster threats like Noivern. Spikes support is appreciated to punish attempts to pivot around Bewear's Choice-locked attacks. Spikers such as Roserade and Golisopod also provide great additional support. Golisopod can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from shared switch-ins such as Crobat and Togekiss. Roserade, on the other hand, checks Electric-types trying to revenge kill Bewear such as Raikou and Xurkitree. Pokemon such as Flygon, Noivern, and Sharpedo appreciate Bewear denting Fairy-types like Togekiss and Galarian Weezing.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Normal

Heavy-Duty Boots is another option on teams without Braviary to help Bewear switch in and take on physical attackers such as Terrakion, notably avoiding Spikes from Ferrothorn and Toxic Spikes from Dragalge.

Bulk Up (Normal).description:
Bewear is a fantastic asset for Normal teams due to its ability, Fluffy, letting it check physical attackers such as Choice Band Zeraora, Zarude, Barraskewda, and Weavile. Drain Punch deals with Steel-types, 2HKOing Ferrothorn and Melmetal and OHKOing Terrakion and Excadrill after a Bulk Up while providing recovery. Darkest Lariat hits Psychic- and Ghost-types that attempt to switch in on Drain Punch, such as Mew and Aegislash, while ignoring defensive stat boosts, meaning that Bewear can face off against non-Taunt Corviknight. Bulk Up lets Bewear greatly threaten Steel-types, while Substitute allows it to set up without fearing moves such as Toxic from Aegislash and Leech Seed from Ferrothorn. Toxic can be run over Darkest Lariat to pressure walls that don't mind Bewear's boosted attacks, such as Slowbro and Hippowdon, while Roar lets it force out these walls alongside Amoonguss and Celesteela, which are immune to Toxic. Pain Split is an option to provide Bewear more instant recovery. Leftovers is standard, but Rocky Helmet can be run to punish contact moves such as Weavile's Triple Axel or Melmetal's Double Iron Bash. 60 Speed EVs let Bewear outspeed Corviknight, while the rest of the EVs go into making it as bulky as possible. On a set with Pain Split, zero HP EVs and maximum Defense and Special Defense EVs can be run to maximize Pain Split's recovery.

Heliolisk is a great teammate, as it can break through Water- and Flying-types such as non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Toxapex, and Celesteela, and uses Dry Skin to help Bewear deal with Pokémon such as Kingdra and Volcanion. In return, Bewear can break through Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Assault Vest Melmetal, which shrug off Heliolisk's attacks. Chansey, Porygon2, and Braviary can all safely pivot Bewear into a foe it can set up against such as Ferrothorn. Chansey can soak up status that would limit Bewear, take on special attackers such as Tapu Lele, Choice Specs Jirachi, and Hydreigon, and set Stealth Rock. In return, Bewear can defeat Pokemon that Chansey draws in, such as Terrakion and Melmetal. Porygon2 can spread paralysis through Discharge, while checking Flying- and Dragon-types such as Landorus-T and Dragonite with Ice Beam. Braviary removes entry hazards, helping Bewear switch in repeatedly and have better longevity. Diggersby and Obstagoon are threats that help Bewear break through Steel teams while also dealing with physically defensive walls such as Toxapex and Slowbro. Snorlax is a good soft check to Fire- and Ice-types that give Bewear trouble such as Blacephalon, Victini, and Kyurem. It can also set up on Fairy-types that force Bewear out. In return, Bewear can pressure Steel-types that can stop Snorlax's sweep such as Ferrothorn. Finally, Ditto can copy and punish setup sweepers with Imposter, such as Bulk Up Zeraora, Galarian Moltres, and Swords Dance Garchomp.

Swords Dance.description: Speed investment outspeeds Gligar and Cresselia.

Choice Band.description: Speed investment outspeeds Gligar and Cresselia.

Rapid Spin.description:
In a tier filled to the brim with viable Grass-types, Tsareena's access to Rapid Spin, Knock Off, good coverage, and a decent Speed tier are just enough to carve itself a niche. In particular, its higher Speed stat is what differentiates it from Dhelmise and lets it outspeed the whole unboosted metagame after a Rapid Spin. Tsareena's vulnerability to Toxic and difficulty to fit Synthesis make it unable to naturally switch into Electric- and Water-types like Raikou, Xurkitree, and Gastrodon unlike other Grass-types such as Roserade, Vileplume, and Celebi. Knock Off removes crucial items like Heavy-Duty Boots from switch-ins such as Incineroar while not giving away any free switches to Chandelure and Metagross. Triple Axel catches Flying- and Grass-types such as Togekiss, Noivern, and Vileplume on the switch. High Jump Kick, U-turn, and Synthesis are all great options, but without either Knock Off or Triple Axel, Tsareena is left completely vulnerable to common threats like Metagross and Togekiss. With Heavy-Duty Boots, Tsareena can repeatedly switch into entry hazards to remove them with Rapid Spin. Queenly Majesty protects Tsareena from priority moves like Golisopod's First Impression, which lets it win the matchup and keep entry hazards off the field.

On its own, Tsareena isn't a very reliable switch-in to Electric- and Water-types like Raikou and Milotic, but more reliable checks such as Gastrodon and Guzzlord can pick up the slack. While Flying-types such as Togekiss, Crobat, and Tornadus need to watch out for Triple Axel, they all outspeed and threaten Tsareena with their STAB moves. Metagross, Raikou, and Diancie can check said Flying-types for Tsareena. Poison-types such as Roserade, Toxicroak, and Galarian Weezing can either threaten or wall Tsareena. Roserade is especially a nuisance, as it's a Spikes setter that Tsareena loses to. Pokemon such as Crobat can check Roserade while Gastrodon helps with the latter two. Pokemon such as Tornadus, Suicune, and Heracross are ravaged by entry hazards and greatly appreciate Tsareena spinning them away.

nu.overview: Tsareena's an incredible spinner and matches up well against common Stealth Rock setters like Mudsdale and Diancie. In addition, it's very effective at forcing in Talonflame and removing its Heavy-Duty Boots and a great pivot that synergizes with some of NU's best wallbreakers because of the Pokemon it draws in. Despite offering so much role compression, though, Tsareena faces heavy competition from Rotom-C, a Pokemon that fills many of the same roles as it but with more efficiency and defensive utility. Many teams opt for Choice Scarf Rotom-C as their entry hazard remover because it can double as a revenge killer too, and Tsareena lacking that function makes building with it awkward at times. Also, Tsareena can't make very good use of its resistances because Pokemon it'd otherwise switch into well, like Silvally-Ground and Starmie, simply outspeed and heavily damage or KO it the following turn with their coverage.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Aromatherapy can be used if your team is particularly weak to status ailments, but Tsareena loses to common status inflictors like Talonflame and Vileplume, which makes it an inconsistent cleric. High Jump Kick fits well on sets more dedicated to maximizing Tsareena's coverage while hitting Stakataka and Copperajah extremely hard; a set of Power Whip / Triple Axel / High Jump Kick / Rapid Spin with Wide Lens is a good example of this, but losing Knock Off's utility is very punishing against foes like Weezing and Talonflame.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Weezing completely shuts down Tsareena, chipping at it with Rocky Helmet and maintaining Toxic Spikes against it. Toxicroak and Drapion outspeed it and can take a hit if needed. Vileplume can switch into any move other than Triple Axel and beat it one-on-one.

Fire-types: Salazzle and Talonflame switch into Power Whip easily, but Knock Off severely cripples them both; in addition, Salazzle is at risk of losing to Tsareena after minimal chip damage if it switches in on Rapid Spin.

Steel-types: Other than Copperajah, Tsareena struggles against most Steel-types. Escavalier walls it with ease and wins any exchange, although Knock Off is bothersome for Toxic + Protect variants. Stakataka takes even Power Whip well and can keep Stealth Rock up against Tsareena because of how much damage its Gyro Ball does. Even Duraludon can be problematic for Tsareena because it outspeeds and heavily damages Tsareena with Draco Meteor.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Knock Off prevents Rocky Helmet users like Xatu, Weezing, and Vileplume from constantly punishing Tsareena for pivoting, denies foes like Escavalier their Leftovers recovery, and greatly cripples Talonflame. It also prevents Dhelmise and Decidueye from safely spinblocking Tsareena. U-turn keeps momentum up against common defensive answers like Vileplume and Escavalier, applying constant pressure with offensive teammates like Galarian Articuno and Salazzle that beat them. Alternatively, Triple Axel makes Tsareena a good lure for Dragon- and Grass-types like Guzzlord and Vileplume, although it mandates Protective Pads as Tsareena's item for foes like Flame Body Talonflame and Rocky Helmet users. Synthesis is another option that helps keep Tsareena healthy, staving off damage from pivots like Rotom-C and Silvally-Ground and making it easier to run other items. In particular, Yache Berry makes Tsareena an effective emergency check to Inteleon and other offensive Water-types, whereas forgoing an item gives Tsareena an immunity to Golurk's and Decidueye's Poltergeists.

Golurk and Silvally-Ground are great teammates, capitalizing on Tsareena drawing in Poison-types and pivoting them in with U-turn. Other pivots like Talonflame, Silvally-Ground, and Togedemaru are good partners too, creating VoltTurn loops that can do a great job of swinging momentum in your favor. Talonflame also benefits from Tsareena's Rapid Spin support making Knock Off less detrimental to its longevity. Tsareena's a bad defensive answer to Water-types like Starmie, Inteleon, and Araquanid because of its middling bulk and vulnerability to their coverage, so make sure to pair it with Pokemon like Vaporeon, Sylveon, and Mantine; the former two also provide it much-wanted cleric support.

doublesou.overview: Tsareena provides a strong niche to teams with its ability in Queenly Majesty, which lets it protect its allies from priority such as Fake Out and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide. It also functions as a solid check to the likes of Rillaboom, Zygarde, and Tapu Fini, threatening all three out, as well as taking away the biggest tools from the first two. Tsareena works best on offensive teams where it can protect Urshifu-R and weakened teammates from getting sniped down from Rillaboom's Grassy Glide, as well as Choice Band Zygarde and Choice Scarf Genesect from getting slowed down by Fake Out. Tsareena's middling Speed tier in conjunction with its mediocre bulk, often relying on an Assault Vest or a Sitrus Berry for longevity, make it extremely vulnerable to the myriad of strong attackers in the tier, such as Heatran and Genesect. Tsareena also faces large competition from the dominant Grass-types of the tier in Rillaboom and Amoonguss, which provide more overall utility in the form of Fake Out and Grassy Surge for the former and redirection and Spore for the latter.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

A Choice Band set utilizing Grassy Glide can be used alongside Rillaboom to increase Tsareena's offensive prowess, but by taking on a more offensive role, it becomes less reliable at blocking priority. Rapid Spin is another option that can be handy in some cases, removing entry hazards that can be detrimental long term as well as boosting its middling Speed, although it is useless against hazardless teams and is generally less viable compared to Tsareena's other move options. Feint and Helping Hand enable Tsareena's teammates to pick up KOs by breaking Protect and boosting their damage output, respectively, but at the cost of other valuable moves. Wide Lens can also be used to make up for Tsareena's low accuracy moves, but it cuts into its longevity greatly.

Pivot.description:
• Power Whip is Tsareena's strongest STAB option, allowing it to force out threats such as Tapu Fini and Urshifu-R, as well as netting heavy damage on neutral targets such as Necrozma and Zeraora.

  • U-turn lets Tsareena pivot out of unfavorable positions while maintaining momentum to bring another teammate in safely. This can lead to scenarios where Tsareena can block Fake Out and Grassy Glide at the start of the turn and then bring in something with a better matchup.

  • Triple Axel threatens the likes of Landorus, Zygarde, and Amoonguss and shifts these matchups a lot more in Tsareena's favor.

  • High Jump Kick is used to threaten common Grass-resistant Pokemon such as Kyurem-B, Incineroar, and Heatran, but Tsareena must be wary of Protect. Taunt is another option on Sitrus Berry sets to shut down Trick Room setters such as Porygon2 as well as redirection users such as Amoonguss, Blastoise, and Volcarona.

  • The given spread allows Tsareena to survive a Close Combat from Choice Band Urshifu-R while also giving it a solid offensive presence. The Attack EVs can be moved into Speed to allow Tsareena to outspeed the likes of Rillaboom, Tapu Fini, and Zeraora under Tailwind, but this cuts into its offensive capabilities.

Rapid Spin Pivot.description: 248 Speed EVs still outspeed Honchkrow, Tyrantrum, and base 70 Pokemon like Hoopa and Volcanion.

pu.overview: Calm Mind and Triage-boosted Draining Kiss make Comfey a dangerous Terrain sweeper that can revenge kill weakened threats like Sandslash and Archeops while simultaneously remaining healthy. Between its typing and decent bulk, Comfey can be hard to take down and can reliably check Dark- and Fighting-types such as Sneasel and Gallade that pose a threat to Terrain teams. These same defensive traits also allow Comfey to serve as a decent bulky Defogger, trading much of its offensive presence for more self-sufficiency and utility. However, when not boosted or hitting foes super effectively, Comfey tends to be very passive due to its mediocre Special Attack. Comfey also lacks coverage for Steel-types like Doublade and Ferroseed, allowing them to easily cut its sweep short or keep entry hazards up against it. Gigalith being so common hurts defensive Comfey, since Synthesis restores less HP in sand on top of already having low PP. Other Fairy-types like Ribombee and Whimsicott generally outclass Comfey, offering much of the same utility as it while being faster, more versatile, and less exploitable.

Calm Mind.description: Stored Power nails Poison-types like Weezing, prevents Charizard and non-Haze Quagsire from walling Comfey, and hits special walls like Audino harder than Draining Kiss with enough boosts. Aromatherapy keeps Comfey and its teammates from being ruined by status, while Taunt completely shuts down slow walls like Wishiwashi and Eldegoss. Giga Drain is a niche option over Stored Power that hits harder under Grassy Terrain, threatens Gigalith, and still destroys Quagsire. Stored Power provides better coverage and tends to be more devastating, though. With 64 Speed EVs, Comfey outspeeds Jolly Sandslash. Thwackey is a required partner, immediately setting Grassy Terrain for Comfey upon switch-in. Thwackey also shares a number of checks with Comfey, mainly Poison- and Steel-types, and can weaken them for it with Knock Off and U-turn. Comfey can't deal meaningful damage to Steel-types such as Doublade and Ferroseed, so Pokemon like Thievul and Hitmonlee are valuable teammates to have. These Pokemon also more immediately threaten foes like Gigalith and appreciate Comfey annoying walls like Audino and Quagsire. Coalossal can support Comfey by both setting and removing entry hazards and taking hits from foes like Charizard and Togedemaru.

Defog.description: Rest has more PP than Synthesis, always fully restores Comfey's HP, and synergizes well with Natural Cure. However, the move virtually forces Comfey to switch out upon use lest it be totally helpless, thus offering foes free turns. 16 Speed EVs let Comfey outrun Modest Magneton. Since Comfey is walled by Steel- and Poison-types like Togedemaru and Garbodor, Pokemon like Charizard and Galarian Articuno are great teammates. Charizard notably gains the ability to drop Defog thanks to Comfey and also appreciates it switching into Knock Off, while Galarian Articuno benefits a lot from the pivoting support that Comfey provides. Pokemon that are especially vulnerable to Dark- and Fighting-types, such as Jellicent, Doublade, and Sneasel, like having Comfey to fall back on against such threats and can help make up for its passivity. Wish support from the likes of Togedemaru and Audino helps Comfey remain healthy without quickly burning through Synthesis's limited PP. These Pokemon also form a good defensive core with Comfey, switching into irksome foes like Ribombee for it. Comfey can potentially run either Aromatherapy or Toxic instead of Defog to act as a cleric or punish switch-ins like Charizard, respectively; however, such a tradeoff requires dedicating another teamslot to entry hazard removal and takes away from this set's main niche.

zu.overview: Despite certain unique traits it possesses like its Normal / Psychic typing and its decent bulk, Oranguru finds itself outclassed by other setup Psychic-types like Jynx, Uxie, and Galarian Rapidash, due to these Pokemon having better traits such as a higher Speed stat or more immediate power.

SubPlot.description: Oranguru is able to make use of its decent defensive stats thanks to Substitute, which can protect it from status, letting it set up more freely with Nasty Plot. Unfortunately, Oranguru's low Speed and initial power, combined with the lack of reliable recovery, mean that it can be stopped easily before inflicting too much damage. It is also outclassed by other Psychic-type setup users like Jynx, Galarian Rapidash, and Uxie, which are either faster, have reliable recovery, or have more initial power.

nu.overview: Passimian is the only Fighting-type Pokemon in the tier that can perform the roles of a revenge killer and pivot with U-turn. Its access to coverage moves like Rock Slide and Gunk Shot allows it to punish its checks in Flying- and Fairy-types like Talonflame and Sylveon. With a Choice Scarf, it's able to outpace Pokemon like Tauros, Talonflame, and Tyrantrum after a Dragon Dance and KO them with its attacks. With a Choice Band, Passimian becomes capable of breaking past traditional Fighting-type checks like Talonflame and Sylveon with its raw power. Choice Scarf Passimian, though, cannot revenge kill certain threats like +1 Silvally-Ground and Choice Scarf Rotom-C. Meanwhile, Choice Band Passimian still cannot reliably bypass certain Fighting-type checks such as Vileplume and Weezing. Passimian faces a lot of risk-reward situations by being Choice locked like using Rock Slide to predict the Flying-type switch-in in front of a Steel-type like Copperajah. Passimian also must avoid status effects from foes like Talonflame's Flame Body and Vileplume's Effect Spore, which discourage U-turn.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Protective Pads gives Passimian the freedom to mispredict more safely against potential switch-ins like Sylveon and Xatu while also preventing adverse contact effects like Weezing's Rocky Helmet, Talonflame's Flame Body, and Vileplume's Effect Spore. Facade is an option so Passimian isn't completely useless if it gets a status ailment, notably a burn.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Fairy-types like Sylveon, Comfey, and Diancie can OHKO Passimian with Moonblast, but the first two risk switching into a Gunk Shot.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Passimian has a hard time getting past physically defensive foes like Xatu, Mantine, Arcanine, and Mudsdale. They all have their ways of statusing Passimian, and the first three notably have recovery in Roost and Morning Sun to keep them healthy throughout the match. Note, however, that these foes are much worse against Choice Band Passimian.

Poison-types: Poison-types like Weezing and Vileplume can stomach all of Passimian's attacks and status it with Will-O-Wisp, Sleep Powder, and Stun Spore. They also have adverse effects like Rocky Helmet from Weezing and Effect Spore from Vileplume, which can lower its longevity and potentially status it. Offensive Pokemon like Salazzle and Toxicroak can make use of Passimian being Choice locked to set up with Nasty Plot or Swords Dance, respectively.

Status: Status ailments, notably paralysis from Pokemon like Xatu and burn from Vaporeon's Scald, cripple Passimian. Abilities that can trigger adverse effects like Talonflame's Flame Body and Vileplume's Effect Spore can potentially status Passimian when using a contact move.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Knock Off prevents Psychic- and Ghost-types like Xatu, Starmie, and Golurk from safely switching in on a predicted Close Combat. Rock Slide hits Flying- and Bug-types like Talonflame and Ninjask. Gunk Shot is an option over Rock Slide to hit Fairy-types like Sylveon. Earthquake is also an option in the last moveslot to hit Poison-types like Toxicroak, Garbodor, and Salazzle, notably OHKOing the latter as compared to Rock Slide.

Poison- and Steel-types like Garbodor, Escavalier, and Copperajah can switch into Fairy-types like Sylveon and Diancie. They all also provide entry hazard support to help wear down Pokemon and allow Passimian to pick up KOs. Rock-types such as Aerodactyl, Diancie, and Tyrantrum are appreciated to deal with Flying-types like Ninjask, Xatu, and Talonflame. Although Passimian has Knock Off for Psychic-types, running a Dark-type like Guzzlord or Drapion is encouraged to help with Pokemon like Starmie and Decidueye. Passimian helps Dark-types deal with opposing Dark-types they struggle to break with Close Combat. Psychic-types also make great teammates, as they can KO Poison-types like Salazzle, Vileplume, and Weezing. Wallbreakers like Choice Specs Exploud, Golurk, and Silvally-Ground appreciate opportunities to come into play with U-turn. Pokemon like Sylveon, Vaporeon, and Diancie are useful clerics to remove status ailments with Heal Bell.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Knock Off weakens and cripples common checks in Talonflame, Weezing, and Sylveon, making it easier to wallbreak later on. Gunk Shot primarily targets Sylveon, though it is also a strong, non-contact move that eases prediction against teams with status ailment abilities or Rocky Helmet users. Alternatively, Rock Slide OHKOes Talonflame and can induce flinching against foes such as Xatu and Mantine. Earthquake may also be a coverage option, specifically targeting Garbodor, a road block for Passimian.

Due to Passimian's reliance on contact moves, clerics in Diancie, Sylveon, and Vaporeon are excellent partners to prevent foes like Vileplume and Talonflame from punishing it with their abilities. Partners such as Escavalier, Salazzle, and Xatu can help to accommodate for Passimian's weaknesses to Poison-, Fairy-, and Flying-types. Furthermore, protection against Salazzle and Silvally-Ground is necessary, since they can exploit Passimian if it locks into a bad move. As such, defensive staples such as Vaporeon and Mantine are appreciated. Offensive partners such as Rotom-C and Decidueye can also help form offensive cycles to pressure the opposing team, with the latter's checks overlapping with many of Passimian's.

ru.overview: First Impression Golisopod is a reliable revenge killer for many common threats such as Dragon Dance Flygon, Celebi, and Xurkitree. Additionally, its combination of the crippling Knock Off and Spikes makes it a great offensive supporter able to punish nearly every switch-in and play around of some of its typical checks. Golisopod's typing and physical bulk allow it to check some strong threats such as Metagross, physical Sharpedo, and Flygon as well. However, after First Impression is used, Golisopod is easy to revenge kill due to its low Speed stat and mediocre special bulk. Golisopod also struggles against many common bulky Pokemon such as Milotic, Gastrodon, and Vileplume, particularly the Water-types. Although its Emergency Exit might be helpful in some situations, getting forced to switch out is disadvantageous in most cases.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Close Combat allows Golisopod to 2HKO Registeel, OHKO Lucario, and hit Water-types for decent damage.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Bulky Water-types such as Seismitoad, Milotic, and Gastrodon take very little from Golisopod's moves and threaten it with a Scald burn or Toxic poison. However, they do not want to lose their items to Golisopod's Knock Off.

Various Bulky Pokemon: Various bulky Pokemon such as Vileplume, Galarian Weezing, and Bewear can easily switch into Golisopod's STAB moves and quickly KO it or activate Emergency Exit. Toxicroak deserves a special mention despite not being bulky, as it easily takes advantage of Golisopod due to its typing and ability. However, none of these Pokemon like having their items removed by Knock Off. Pokemon such as Galarian Weezing and Bewear are easy to wear down due to their lack of reliable recovery.

Flying-types: Flying-types such as Noivern, Togekiss, and Crobat easily revenge kill Golisopod and switch into its First Impression. However, they should watch out for Knock Off because they rely a ton on their Heavy-Duty Boots to prevent Stealth Rock damage.

Electric-types: Once they get a safe switch in, Electric-types such as Raikou, Heliolisk, and Xurkitree OHKO Golisopod or activate Emergency Exit.

Strong Attackers: Although Golisopod has respectable bulk, strong wallbreakers such as Chandelure, Heracross, and Golurk easily defeat it or force it out by activating its ability. Indeedee deserves special attention, because its Psychic Terrain prevents Golisopod from using First Impression against grounded targets.

Revenge Killer.description:
Leech Life gives Golisopod the option to heal itself and, more importantly, check Calm Mind Reuniclus and hit Grass-, Psychic-, and Dark-types such as Celebi and Umbreon super effectively after First Impression is used. Aqua Jet makes Golisopod more difficult to revenge kill and able to revenge kill Pokemon such as Chandelure, Salazzle, and Aerodactyl. However, without a strong and reliable STAB move in Liquidation, Golisopod becomes a bit too weak against bulky Pokemon such as Registeel, Klefki, and Escavalier. Knock Off punishes Golisopod's typical switch-ins such as Noivern, Togekiss, and Milotic. In addition, removing Heavy-Duty Boots from grounded switch-ins such as Gastrodon enables Golisopod to wear them down with Spikes. Heavy-Duty Boots gives Golisopod more switch-in opportunities by negating its severe entry hazard weakness. The listed Speed EVs allow Golisopod to outspeed Pokemon with uninvested base 50 Speed such as Diancie, Registeel, and Vileplume. The remaining EVs are dumped into HP, allowing Golisopod to better switch into Metagross's and Flygon's attacks.

Golisopod works well on balance and bulky offensive teams that need a reliable revenge killer for common threats such as Xurkitree, Dragon Dance Flygon, and Nasty Plot Celebi and appreciate a reliable Spikes setter. Powerful wallbreakers such as Metagross, Toxtricity, and Gardevoir appreciate Golisopod's Spikes support. In return, they handle troublesome bulky Pokemon such as Vileplume, Galarian Weezing, and Gastrodon. Strong late-game cleaners like Mimikyu, Sharpedo, and Xurkitree are also good examples of Pokemon that appreciate Spikes support. Grass- and Electric-types such as Vileplume, Celebi, and Xurkitree check bulky Water-types that Golisopod struggles with such as Milotic, Gastrodon, and Suicune. Bulky Rock- and Steel-types such as Diancie, Stakataka, and Metagross, on the other hand, check strong Flying-types such as Togekiss, Noivern, and Crobat. These Pokemon also form a great hazard stacking core with Golisopod, as they are reliable Stealth Rock setters. Beyond that, they appreciate Golisopod's ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off. Specially defensive Pokemon such as Steelix, Assault Vest Reuniclus, and Snorlax are great to reliably check the tier's strong Electric-types.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Liquidation can be used over Leech Life to combat Steel-type Pokemon such as Heatran, but Leech Life is preferred, as it allows Golisopod to defeat Grass- and Psychic-type Pokemon like Rillaboom and Slowbro. Taunt is another optionto stop foes such as Ferrothorn and Klefki from freely setting Spikes, as well as stopping Calm Mind users such as Clefable.

Utility (Water).description:
Golisopod finds itself a niche on Water teams thanks to its Spikes and First Impression, which revenge kills threatening Pokemon that can sweep Water-type teams such as Rillaboom, Zarude, and Alolan Raichu. Knock Off helps make progress against bulkier Pokemon that utilize Leftovers such as Celesteela, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Fini, gets rid of Rocky Helmet from Pokemon such as Slowbro, and removes Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Victini, making Spikes more potent. Leech Life makes up for Golisopod's lack of recovery and also helps defeat the aforementioned Grass-type sweepers, alongside Psychic-type Pokemon such as Slowbro and Celebi. 172 Speed EVs allow Golisopod to outspeed Celesteela, so it can remove its Leftovers with Knock Off before potentially being forced out by Emergency Exit.

Swampert is an excellent teammate on any Water team thanks to its ability to switch into Electric-type attacks from Zapdos and Regieleki. Its Stealth Rock also benefits Golisopod removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Mantine and Leftovers from Celesteela with Knock Off, which helps make progress against Flying- and Steel-type teams. Urshifu-S is a great wallbreaker that defeats Steel-types that Golisopod cannot, such as Ferrothorn and Heatran, while also benefitting from the extra chip damage Golisopod provides with Spikes. Toxapex can switch into Grass-type moves such as Power Whip from Zarude reliably, stops setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Dragapult with Haze, and deals with Tapu Bulu and Tapu Fini with Poison Jab. Tapu Fini provides Misty Terrain for its teammates, which helps them deal with the aforementioned Dragon-type sweepers, and Calm Mind Tapu Fini can use chip damage from Golisopod's Spikes and Swampert's Stealth Rock to sweep easily. Volcanion can also be used to deal with Grass- and Steel-type Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Aegislash, which are troublesome defensive Pokemon for Water teams to handle. Due to Golisopod's Spikes being rendered completely useless against Flying teams, Cloyster and Rotom-W make for excellent teammates, as they can easily dismantle Flying teams with Shell Smash and Nasty Plot, respectively. Slowking can switch into Psychic-type attacks from Tapu Lele, Ground-type Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Excadrill, and Garchomp, and also Kyurem's Freeze-Dry. Slowking can also pressure foes with Future Sight, especially Poison-type Pokemon such as Toxapex and Amoonguss, while easily pivoting wallbreakers such as Urshifu-S in with Teleport.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots is an option to give Golisopod better protection against entry hazards, but the loss off power compared to Choice Band makes it difficult to revenge kill would-be targets. If using Heavy-Duty Boots, Regenerator can be used to properly check Ground-types like Zygarde-10% and Swampert; it can also run Scald to threaten a burn on them.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Water-types: Toxapex and Tapu Fini avoid being 2HKOed by Golisopod's coverage and threaten it with Scald burns. However, they do not appreciate having their items removed with Knock Off.

Flying-types: Golisopod cannot OHKO common Flying-types who OHKO it in return like Zapdos, Galarian Zapdos, and Talonflame.

Psychic Surge Users: While they typically cannot safely switch into Golisopod, Azelf and Alakazam prevent First Impression from activating against themselves and grounded teammates, making it difficult to successfully revenge kill opponents.

Revenge Killer.description:
Golisopod's powerful Choice Band Tinted Lens First Impression makes it a niche but threatening revenge killer for threats like Zapdos, Tapu Koko, and Cinderace after minor chip. First Impression is also excellent for picking off neutral or weak targets like Tapu Lele and Zarude. Leech Life is a great STAB option that Golisopod can also use to heal. Knock Off + Spikes enables Golisopod to cripple and punish targets it struggles to weaken, such as Intimidate Corviknight, Tapu Fini, and Toxapex, on switch in. Liquidation can be used as a secondary STAB move to better hit bulky switch-ins like Hippowdon and non-Desolate Land Heatran if Spikes is deemed unnecessary. 40 Speed EVs outspeeds minimum Speed Corviknight, and the rest of the EVs are assigned to HP so that Golisopod can more easily check Zygarde-10%.

Golisopod is most effective on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its combination of revenge killing and entry hazard setting services. Stealth Rock setters like Garchomp and Heatran can form a hazard stacking core; they also benefit from Golisopod checking Barraskewda for them. Strong wallbreakers like Pixilate Tapu Koko and Tough Claws Galarian Zapdos are empowered by Golisopod removing Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from their common switch-ins, then subsequently setting up Spikes to weaken grounded ones, such as Ferrothorn and Mew. Golisopod cannot OHKO Zapdos and struggles versus powerful special attackers, so specially defensive Pokemon like Blissey and RegenVest Jirachi make excellent partners. Entry hazard removal is crucial to keeping Golisopod healthy over the course of a battle, so Rapid Spin support from Dhelmise and Excadrill is appreciated; alternatively, Defoggers like Corviknight and Mandibuzz can both remove entry hazards and pivot Golisopod into Pokemon it matches up well against.

Offensive Spikes.description: Speed investment lets Golisopod outspeed base 50 Pokemon like Registeel.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Toxic can be used over Stealth Rock to put Pokemon that wall Palossand, such as Appletun, Cramorant, and non-Aromatherapy Alcremie, on a timer. This forces teams to pair Palossand with another Stealth Rock setter, though, making Palossand less easy to fit onto defensive cores. Palossand can run different items, with Kasib Berry surprising Rotom and Leftovers making Palossand less reliant on Shore Up for recovery. Unfortunately, these items only have very situational uses, whereas Colbur Berry and Rocky Helmet are more versatile.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Palossand's weakness and lack of coverage for Grass-types give it a hard time. Tangela, Thwackey, and Appletun can switch into Earth Power and directly threaten it. The Gourgeist formes do the same, but do fear Shadow Ball.

Ice-types: While Froslass and Jynx cannot switch into Palossand's Shadow Ball, they both are massive threats to Palossand once they safely enter. Piloswine isn't as inherently powerful, and should be weary of a Scorching Sands burn, but it can safely switch into variants without it. Articuno can directly switch into it and use Freeze-Dry and Defog to mitigate Palossand's progress.

Special Wallbreakers: In general, special attackers can excel at threatening Palossand. Common special wallbreakers like Rotom, Poliwrath, and Exeggutor threaten to deal large amounts of damage to Palossand, often forcing Palossand to either switch out or get KOed.

Special Walls: Without super effective coverage, Palossand has a difficult time getting past most specially defensive Pokemon. It doesn't have any way to break past walls that can wear it down through Toxic, like Miltank, Altaria, and Clefairy.

Dark-types: Even with Palossand holding a Colbur Berry, it still gets threatened out by Dark-types like Silvally-Dark, Thievul, and Shiftry. Without Colbur Berry, then Palosand also struggles to check Skuntank and Morpeko.

Water-types: Despite having Water Compaction, Palossand has a poor matchup versus most of the metagame's Water-types, like Poliwrath, Silvally-Water, and Cramorant.

Physical Wall.description:
Palossand's solid bulk, great typing, and instant recovery make it a great physical wall. Its Ghost / Ground typing lets it switch into common physical threats, including Sawk, Lycanroc-N, and multiple Silvally formes. Its raw bulk also allows it to handle neutral hits well, weathering attacks from Klinklang, Rapidash, Rhydon, and more. This makes it easy for it to come in and set up entry hazards while also using Shore Up to retain its longevity. Colbur Berry makes Palossand a premier Knock Off absorber, notably letting it hard counter Sawk and Gurdurr. Rocky Helmet's chip damage makes Palossand a better check to Klinklang, as well as U-turn pivots like Uxie and the Silvally formes. Scorching Sands can be run alongside Rocky Helmet to get a burn chance, as the extra damage from the item compensates for Scorching Sands's lower power.

A variety of teams use Palossand to complete defensive cores, ranging from bulky offense to semi-stall. Defensive partners including Articuno, Appletun, and Rapidash absorb attacks from Grass-, Water-, and Ice-types, respectively. These teammates also appreciate Palossand's ability to handle hits from Rock- and Electric-types. Clerics like Miltank and Alcremie can also heal Palossand from Toxic and enjoy Palossand checking Klinklang and Lycanroc-N. Knock Off users like Sawk, Thwackey, and Gurdurr put on offensive pressure versus walls like Altaria and Articuno which Palossand is forced out by. Offensive pivots including Morpeko, Unfezant, and the Silvally formes love being able to switch out safely and bring out Palossand to defend their team against wallbreakers like Sawk and Manectric.

nu.overview: Palossand's forte in NU is eating physical attacks and setting Stealth Rock due to its excellent defensive typing and bulk. It's also great at checking some of the tier's common Pokemon like Copperajah, Diancie, and Toxicroak. Unlike other Ground-types in the tier, like Mudsdale, Palossand does not let Xatu and Dhelmise in for free. It also has a reliable form of recovery in Shore Up. However, Palossand is very slow and is extremely susceptible to special wallbreakers like Exploud and Decidueye, along with many other common special threats in the tier like Rotom-C, Vaporeon, and Starmie.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Palossand can potentially run a Choice Specs set along with Trick to utilize its decent Special Attack stat. However, due to its sluggish Speed, Palossand will need to predict the right move every time to be an effective wallbreaker.

Checks and Counters

Dark- and Ghost-types: Pokemon like Guzzlord, Decidueye, Dhelmise, and Golurk can make life tough for Palossand by not letting it set up Stealth Rock or heal with Shore Up. Said Ghost-types need to be mindful of Shadow Ball, however.

Bulky Grass- and Water-types: Vileplume, Vaporeon, and Mantine are just a few common threats that can take advantage of Palossand's poor special bulk and weaknesses.

Braviary: Barring Toxic variants of Palossand, Braviary freely switches into it because of its Ghost and Ground immunities.

Special Wallbreakers: Threats like Exploud, Sylveon, and Starmie can do serious damage or even OHKO Palossand outright with their STAB attacks.

Physically Defensive.description:
Set Details

Palossand is great at setting up Stealth Rock on common Pokemon like Diancie, Talonflame, and Stakataka. If Stealth Rock is not needed, Palossand can run Toxic to cripple common switch-ins like Vaporeon and Mantine. Colbur Berry is the preferred item to stomach one Dark-type move like Knock Off or Dark Pulse from threats like Drapion or Heliolisk. Going itemless, however, lets Palossand switch into Poltergeist users like Choice Band Golurk.

Guzzlord has excellent defensive synergy with Palossand, as it can switch in on Ghost- and Dark-type moves from the likes of Decidueye and Drapion. Guzzlord can also switch in on the Grass- and Water-type moves that Palossand loathes. Since Grass-types like Rotom-C, Vileplume, and Decidueye offensively force out Palossand, partners like Ninjask, Xatu, and Salazzle are appreciated. Similarly, Water-types like Vaporeon, Mantine, and Starmie take advantage of Palossand's lackluster special bulk. Teammates like Toxicroak, Choice Scarf Heliolisk, and Rotom-C work very well here to scare them off. Because of Palossand's ability to set up Stealth Rock on Diancie, Talonflame, and Xatu, having a partner like Talonflame to pivot on such threats and bring in Palossand is nice. Special wallbreakers like Sylveon and Exploud love to feast on Palossand's mediocre Special Defense. Partners like Stakataka and Copperajah can force them out.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Klutz alongside Assault Vest and Trick allows Palossand to cripple a Defogger that doesn't fear it such as Tapu Fini or Corviknight. Palossand can run some other abilities such as Unaware to better handle Swords Dance Garchomp or Wandering Spirit to punish U-turn, but they generally aren't as useful as the aforementioned abilities.

Checks and Counters

Grass-type Pokemon: Zarude, Dhelmise, and Tapu Bulu all threaten to deal heavy damage to Palossand with their Grass-type STAB attacks. However, they don't want to switch in directly as they fear burn except for Zarude if it runs Jungle Healing.

Specially Offensive Pokemon: Strong special attackers like Zapdos and Tapu Lele target Palossand's lower Special Defense stat and can all easily 2HKO it at worst.

Water-type Pokemon: If Palossand doesn't run Water Absorb, Barraskewda forces it out, and even defensive Water-types like Toxapex and Swampert threaten Palossand with Scald.

Physically Defensive.description:
Palossand is one of the best answers to Terrakion and has several useful utility options. Shore Up allows it to stay healthy throughout a match to consistently check physical attackers. Scorching Sands is preferred over Earth Power thanks to its high burn chance, which deters physical attackers from switching in, especially Zarude. Shadow Ball hits Flying-type Pokemon and works well with Scorching Sands by threatening those with Roost like Talonflame and Corviknight. Toxic can be used instead to punish common switch-ins like Zapdos and Mandibuzz. Palossand has several ability options. Water Absorb allows it to wall Barraskewda, as well as block Flip Turn and Scald from defensive stalwarts like Swampert and Toxapex.
