It can also provide an emergency switch in to Choice Specs Primordial Sea Pokemon like Inteleon, although it risks getting KOed by a coverage move. Dauntless Shield is another option that gives Palossand better odds against dangerous physical attackers like Adaptability Zygarde-10%, Galarian Zapdos, and Pixilate Tapu Koko. Rocky Helmet is its item of choice to punish U-turn from offensive threats, while Leftovers helps it gain extra recovery. 2 Speed IVs helps Palossand deal with Stakataka better while still outspeeding Ferrothorn.

Palossand fits best on bulkier builds that need a Terrakion counter. Flying-type Pokemon such as Corviknight and Mandibuzz make for good partners for Palossand, as they can deal with physical Grass-types like Zarude and Dhelmise, while Palossand can check Barraskewda and Terrakion for them. Additionally, Dauntless Shield Palossand can handle Zygarde-10% for its Flying-type teammates, while they can provide entry hazard removal with Defog. Offensive Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Talonflame that struggle against Barraskewda appreciate Water Absorb Palossand handling it and setting Stealth Rock to chip their checks. Special walls are required to cover for Palossand. In particular, Blissey can handle Zapdos, Chandelure, and Hydreigon. Jirachi takes on Psychic-type special wallbreakers such as Latios, Tapu Lele, and Azelf that give Palossand problems. If Palossand doesn't run Water Absorb, teammates that can repeatedly switch into Flip Turn are appreciated. Examples include Tapu Fini and Desolate Land Moltres. It's also fairly passive and thus requires bulky teammates with a pivot option to regain momentum, notably the aforementioned Mandibuzz and Blissey.

pu.overview: Pyukumuku is a decent option on stall teams to ward off common setup sweepers like Ribombee, Thievul, and Sandaconda. Pyukmuku's considerable defenses combined with Unaware can make it difficult to break through. Compared to its Unaware competition in Quagsire, Pyukumuku's typing has the pros of letting it better take Seed Bomb from Perrserker and take Shadow Ball from offensive Jellicent in a pinch. However, most of the time Quagsire still has the superior typing, and it also has more versatility with its moveslots. Also, Pykukumuku is completely shut down by Taunt, which is found on the tier staple Jellicent.

Unaware Trapper.description: Block allows Pyukumuku to trap and KO foes, stalling them out with Spite or Toxic. Rest is preferred in the last moveslot so Pyukumuku is not easily worn down by Toxic Ferroseed or Gigalith, and it gives an additional form of recovery. Further, since Pyukumuku won't use PP while asleep, Rest can contribute nicely to PP stalling. Alternatively, Toxic can be useful to wear down Pokemon like Jellicent, which cannot be trapped and hates taking it on the switch, and it makes Pyukumuku not dead weight against Pokemon with pivot moves, which get around Block. Pyukumuku only fits on stall teams, and it needs sturdy walls like Audino and Aromatisse to handle Pokemon that get past Pyukumuku despite Unaware, like Galarian Articuno and Gallade. Aromatisse and Audino are also good partners, since they can provide Heal Bell support. This is especially important when not running Rest to remedy opposing Toxic. Answers to Doublade such as Charizard and Weezing are also necessary since Pyukumuku cannot trap it nor Toxic it. Consistent entry hazard removal from Pokemon such as Articuno avoids having Pyukumuku overwhelmed before it can stall out attacks too.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Running Soak in tandem with Toxic allows Pyukumuku to chip down the likes of Toxapex, Heatran, and Mega Scizor, as well as spreading status through the opposing team. Unfortunately, not having Spite and Rest means it can't beat opposing Toxic users and Pokemon with Pressure such as Suicune and Corviknight. Gastro Acid and Toxic may seem appealing to beat Toxic-immune setup sweepers such as Clefable, Gliscor, and Reuniclus, but aside from Stored Power Reuniclus, the Spite set already handles these Pokemon better. Running Mirror Coat and Counter allows Pyukumuku to more directly punish attackers reduces its passivity. However, this set is prone to status and being worn down long-term.

Checks and Counters

Taunt: Taunt variants of Heatran and Tapu Fini entirely shut down Pyukumuku, as it runs only status moves.

Electric-types: Electric-types such as Tapu Koko, Zeraora, and Magnezone are able to overwhelm Pyukumuku with their powerful STAB attacks.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Serperior, Kartana, and Rillaboom are able to overwhelm Pyukumuku with their powerful STAB attacks.

Powerful Wallbreakers: Powerful wallbreakers like Mega Mawile, Mega Medicham, and Hoopa-U threaten to KO Pyukumuku due to their insane wallbreaking power.

Unaware Trapper.description:
Pyukumuku is a decent pick on stall teams, as Unaware allows it to check setup sweepers such as Manaphy, Mega Garchomp, and Volcarona, and its Water typing lets it pivot into the likes of Ash-Greninja, Melmetal, and Mega Scizor. However, due to it only having status moves, it's an incredibly passive Pokemon that can be easy to play around. Block and Spite allow Pyukumuku to effectively trap and PP stall a lot of Pokemon that cannot outright 2HKO it. Recover is its primary recovery move, but Rest curing status lets it trap and beat the likes of Blissey, Toxapex, and Gliscor. The sleep turns from Rest also stop Pyukumuku from wasting its precious PP, helping it out stall opposing Pokemon. The given EV spread lets it survive two Energy Balls from Manaphy while remaining as physically bulky as possible.

Pyukumuku is excellent at punishing small mistakes, such as setting up a Substitute with the likes of Hawlucha and Corviknight or trying to status it with Toxapex or Gastrodon, which let it remove these Pokemon from the match. Due to Pyukumuku's passive nature, it tends to be put on stall teams with teammates such as Toxapex, Mega Sableye, and Clefable that defensively answer Pokemon that tend to overwhelm it. The latter two also keep the field clear of entry hazards and cure it of status conditions, respectively. Taunt users such as Heatran and Tapu Fini completely ruin Pyukumuku, so it needs teammates that are able to hande them, such as Gastrodon and Toxapex. These Pokemon, as well as many other common stall teammates for Pyukumuku, also appreciate it trapping and PP stalling the likes of Gliscor, Clefable, and non-Stored Power variants of Reuniclus. Flying-types such as Corviknight, Zapdos, and Skarmory are stellar to switch into Grass-types such as Kartana, Rillaboom, and Serperior, which bother Pyukumuku. Ground-types such as Gastrodon and Hippowdon are similarly able to handle Electric-types such as Magnezone and Tapu Koko that bother Pyukumuku.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Pyukumuku can sometimes forgo Block to run Rest with both Spite and Toxic. Soak lets Pyukumuku inflict Toxic poison on Steel- and Poison-types Klinklang and Silvally-Poison and helps it better take on Pokemon such as Kangaskhan, Klinklang, and other Silvally formes by making them lose their STAB bonus.

Checks and Counters

Taunt: Pyukumuku is forced to use Struggle if it gets afflicted by Taunt. Taunt users like Skuntank, Alolan Persian, and Qwilfish beat Pyukumuku, but some of them should be wary of being inflicted by Toxic poison on the switch.

Substitute: Substitute users such as Rotom, Klinklang, and Articuno are major threats to Pyukumuku due to them being immune to Block and Toxic; however, PP stalling with Spite and Rest can help against them.

Electric- and Grass-types: Since Pyukumuku is weak to Grass- and Electric-type moves, Pokemon such as Rotom formes, Shiftry, and Flapple are big threats to it.

Strong Wallbreakers: Strong wallbreakers such as Choice Band Sawk and Lycanroc-N 2HKO Pyukumuku.

Stored Power Users: After several Calm Minds, Alcremie, Uxie, and Swoobat can overcome Pyukumuku's Unaware with Stored Power. They also have Substitute or Rest to combat Toxic.

Unaware Wall.description:
Pyukumuku is the sole viable user of Unaware in ZU, making it a cornerstone on stall teams. Unaware allows Pyukumuku to take on setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Rhydon, non-Stored Power Alcremie, and Silvally formes. Block prevents the foe from switching and allows Pyukumuku to remove them with Toxic or PP stall with Spite. Rest removes status and helps to PP stall foes that cannot 3HKO Pyukumuku, such as Choice Scarf Sawk. Leftovers is normally preferred when entry hazard removal is prevalent on the team, while Heavy-Duty Boots may be used to help against entry hazard stacking matchups.

Pyukumuku's passive nature limits it to fitting exclusively on stall teams. Specially defensive clerics such as Clefairy and Articuno form a good core with Pyukumuku. Physically defensive Pokemon such as Altaria, Tangela, and Golbat, which can take on offensive Grass-types, make for good partners with Pyukumuku. Pokemon that can beat Electric-types such as Rotom-S and block Volt Switch such as Stunfisk are also great partners. If not running Heavy-Duty Boots, or if the item gets removed, Pyukumuku can take big damage from entry hazards and have a harder time checking Silvally-Dark and Rapidash. To avoid this, entry hazard removers such as Altaria and Articuno are essential on stall teams.

zu.comments:
Other Options

A set with Iron Defense / Swords Dance / Crush Claw / Rest and an EV spread of 248 HP / 8 Def / 252 SpD is sometimes used to turn Type: Null into an unbreakable and powerful sweeper. However, this set is not consistent due to it only having Normal-type coverage and is walled by the common Ghost-types in the tier; in addition, it is passive thanks to the lack of Sleep Talk. This set also lacks the utility of the pivot set, and Type: Null also needs multiple boosts to become threatening due to its low Attack stat.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-type Pokemon: Type: Null is weak to Fighting, so it should be careful of Pokemon like Sawk, Gurdurr, and Poliwrath.

Strong Physical Wallbreakers: Strong physical wallbreakers such as Sawk and Swords Dance Silvally formes can muscle their way through Type: Null.

Knock Off: Any Pokemon with Knock Off is a threat, as losing Eviolite significantly decreases Type: Null's bulk.

Taunt: Taunt users such as Skuntank and Qwilfish stop Type: Null from recovering and spreading status, forcing it to pivot.

Setup Sweepers that Bypass Toxic: Setup sweepers with Substitute such as Rotom formes can freely set up in front of Type: Null. Poison- and Steel-types such as Skuntank and Klinklang, as well as Pokemon that can cure status like Spiritomb and Aromatherapy Alcremie, can also set up for free.

Entry Hazards: Although Type: Null is not weak to Stealth Rock, its lack of passive recovery and constant pivoting cause it to get easily chipped down, limiting the amount of times it can switch in and lowering its usefulness as a wall.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Type: Null acts as a solid defensive pivot in the metagame thanks to its sizable bulk with Eviolite and access to U-turn. This bulk allows it to check top-tier special wallbreakers such as Jynx, Ninetales, and Thievul. Type: Null's slow U-turn allows it to pivot and safely bring in a teammate. Toxic cripples foes and prevents Pokemon such as Rhydon, Rapidash, and Silvally formes from freely setting up in front of it. RestTalk is Type: Null's only form of recovery and lets it consistently pivot. A Sassy nature and 0 Speed IVs minimize Type: Null's Speed, allowing for the slowest U-turns.

Type: Null is a great pick for teams looking for a pivot, special wall, and status absorber condensed into one Pokemon. It pairs well with other pivots, forming a VoltTurn core. Uxie is an excellent pivot to pair with Type: Null, as it benefits from Type: Null's immunity to Ghost and ability to sponge strong special hits; in return, Uxie is able to switch into strong Fighting-types such as Sawk and Gurdurr that trouble Type: Null. Wallbreakers such as Thievul, Jynx, and Sawk appreciate Type: Null's slow U-turn safely bringing them in. Although Type: Null can sponge special wallbreakers, it cannot do much damage back and is heavily dependent on pivoting into revenge killers to adequately check special sweepers. Thus, priority users like Kangaskhan and Gurdurr are necessary when dealing with foes such as Alcremie and Ivysaur. Finally, Knock Off absorbers such as Qwilfish and Silvally formes work as partners, as they prevent Type: Null from losing its Eviolite.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Silk Scarf feigns Choice Band, but significantly decreases the power of Silvally’s coverage moves. A fully physical Swords Dance set alongside Flame Charge allows Silvally to be a threatening late-game cleaner, though it faces significant competition with its other formes.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: Physically bulky Ghost-types like Cofagrigus, Palossand, and Gourgeist formes can freely switch in against most Silvally variants. Life Orb sets with Shadow Ball can 2HKO them, however. Frailer Ghost-types like Froslass and Choice Scarf Rotom can revenge kill it but cannot handle super effective attacks. Sableye, in particular, is not hit super effectively by any of its moves and can easily wall it.

Phyiscal Walls: Physical walls like Tangela and Qwilfish can status it before whittling it down with residual damage from either Leech Seed, entry hazards, or attacks. Miltank and Alolan Persian can outpace non-Choice Scarf sets and cripple it with status or wear it down with chip damage.

Rock-types: Without Surf, Rock-types like Rhydon and Coalossal can switch into Silvally without much risk. They can proceed to set up Stealth Rock or whittle it down with attacks. Shell Smash users like Carracosta and Crustle can set up on it freely if Silvally is locked into the wrong move.

Steel-types: Klinklang and Pawniard resist Multi-Attack and Crunch and can beat it in a one-on-one situation. However, both are 2HKOed by Flamethrower.

Faster Pokemon: Faster Choice Scarf users like Manectric and Alolan Persian can revenge kill Choice Scarf Silvally with enough prior chip. If Silvally lacks a Choice Scarf, then Pokemon like Alolan Dugtrio, Galarian Rapidash, and Ninetales can similarly pick off Silvally with sufficient prior residual damage.

Status: Toxic wears Silvally down even faster, burns neuter its offensive capabilities, and paralysis hampers its good Speed.

Choice Scarf.description:
Silvally uses its good Speed, Attack, and coverage along with Choice Scarf to function as a solid revenge killer and offensive pivot. U-turn maintains momentum on Normal-resistant foes such as Galarian Stunfisk, Rhydon, Sableye, and Tangela. Explosion deals heavy damage to most neutral targets and prevents Defoggers like Altaria, Articuno, and Cramorant from clearing entry hazards. Crunch provides super effective damage against Ghost-types like Froslass, Rotom, and Gourgeist-S.

Silvally pairs well with pivots such as Thwackey, Articuno, and Rotom, forming VoltTurn cores to chip down the opposition. As it invites and pivots out on Rock-, Steel-, and Ghost-types such as Rhydon, Klinklang, and Rotom with U-turn, teammates that can take advantage of them like Alolan-Dugtrio and Thievul are appreciated. Similarly, physical walls like Tangela, Cofagrigus, and Palossand can switch in on Silvally without too much trouble, so special wallbreakers that can threaten them like Jynx, Thievul, and Choice Specs Exeggutor are also good partners.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band amplifies Silvally’s wallbreaking prowess while still making it an effective pivot. U-turn allows Silvally to escape bad matchups against Pokemon like Tangela, Cofagrigus, and Sableye. Crunch hits frailer Ghost-types such as Froslass and Rotom. Flamethrower targets Tangela and Steel-types such as Klinklang and Perrserker, while Surf discourages Rock- and Ground-types like Rhydon, Palossand, and Coalossal from switching in.

Pivots like Rotom, Thwackey, and Articuno can help get Silvally onto the field safely and form VoltTurn cores. Pokemon that can deal with Rock- and Ghost-types like Tangela, Lurantis, and Alolan Persian ease the need for prediction, allowing Silvally to use its powerful Multi-Attack more freely as the game progresses. While Silvally does have coverage to discourage Rock-types and bulky Grass-types from freely switching in, it still appreciates Pokemon that can switch into them, such as Tangela and Altaria. In return, Silvally can threaten slower wallbreakers like Skuntank and Exeggutor. Physical attackers like Sawk, Rapidash, and Alolan Dugtrio appreciate Silvally weakening physical walls for them.

Mixed Attacker.description:
With either Swords Dance or Work Up, Silvally becomes an imposing physical or mixed attacker thanks to its diverse coverage choices. Flamethrower hits Klinklang and Pawniard super effectively, preventing them from safely switching in. Crunch hits Rotom and Froslass, while Shadow Ball targets physically defensive Ghost-types like Cofagrigus, Palossand, and Gourgeist formes. However, opting for Shadow Ball encourages Silvally to run Work Up to boost the power of all its coverage moves. Surf targets Rock-types like Rhydon and Coalossal. Life Orb boosts all of Silvally's attacks at the cost of wearing it down whenever it attacks.

Silvally appreciates other wallbreakers like Sawk or Skuntank spreading chip damage and providing Knock Off utility, as even at +1, it can have difficulty securing KOs on defensive Pokemon like Stunfisk and Altaria. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Miltank and Rhydon can help rack up residual damage, letting Silvally more easily set up as the game progresses. Due to Silvally's four-moveslot syndrome, Pokemon that can cover specific threats are appreciated to make it as difficult to wall as possible. If Silvally decides to run Shadow Ball or Crunch for the last moveslot, Water- and Grass-types like Poliwrath and Kabutops would be appreciated to handle Rock-types. However, if Surf is chosen, Pokemon to deal with Ghost-types like Rotom and Froslass, such as Throh and Qwilfish, are appreciated.

zu.overview: Despite Silvally-Bug's decent stats, its horrific defensive typing and useless item and ability make it completely outclassed. Other Silvally formes like Silvally-Dark and Silvally-Poison have better offensive and defensive utility by virtue of their superior typings. Crustle serves as a much better Bug-type physical sweeper thanks to its access to Shell Smash and Knock Off and additional Rock STAB. Silvally-Bug also suffers from being unable to fit all of its desired coverage and being terribly weak to entry hazards without being able to run Heavy-Duty Boots.

Swords Dance.description: Silvally-Bug can attempt to leverage its decent bulk, Speed, and power to clean late-game and use its coverage to overwhelm the opposition. Due to its atrocious typing, vulnerability to residual damage, and awkward coverage choices, it is outclassed as a Bug-type physical sweeper by Crustle, which has Smell Smash, Knock Off, and additional STAB in Rock.

zu.comments:
Other Options

X-Scissor is an option over U-turn for a stronger move to threaten opposing Dark-types. Toxic can be used to cripple physical walls such as Tangela and Pyukumuku, but it makes Silvally-Dark less effective at wallbreaking. Defog provides role compression, and it is a niche option on certain teams. A bulkier Swords Dance with RestTalk replacing its coverage options can set up on passive foes like Miltank and defensive Qwilfish more easily at the cost of making it more passive itself.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Although they do not appreciate U-turn, Dark-types such as Alolan Persian and Skuntank can take Multi-Attack from Silvally-Dark and threaten it back with status or a powerful hit.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Sawk, Poliwrath, and Gurdurr are able to take Multi-Attack and pressure back with their STAB moves. Gurdurr can also revenge kill Silvally-Dark with Mach Punch, even after it has set up; Choice Scarf Sawk can similarly revenge kill it due to outspeeding it. However, all Fighting-types should be wary of +2 Psychic Fangs.

Fairy-types: Fairy-types such as Alcremie, Clefairy, and Galarian Rapidash can threaten Silvally-Dark with their STAB options, but they have to watch out for Iron Head variants.

Revenge Killers: Faster attackers such as Alolan Dugtrio, Rapidash, and Froslass can outspeed and threaten Silvally-Dark. Pokemon with priority moves such as Kangaskhan and Thwackey can similarly KO it once it has been weakened enough.

Swords Dance Sweeper.description:
Silvally-Dark finds a niche in ZU as a powerful setup sweeper, capable of setting up with Swords Dance and utilizing its Multi-Attack to threaten prominent Pokemon such as Froslass, Palossand, and Rotom. However, it faces competition from other Silvally formes. U-turn allows Silvally-Dark to function as an early-game pivot and lets it weaken Dark-types such as Alolan Persian and Skuntank, while Flame Charge allows it to outspeed revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Sawk and Rotom. Psychic Fangs can threaten Fighting-types such as Poliwrath and Sawk, while Iron Head weakens Fairy-types such as Alcremie and Galarian Rapidash.

Silvally-Dark fits best on offensive teams as an early-game pivot that can wallbreak with its powerful Multi-Attack. If running Flame Charge, Silvally-Dark should be preserved for late-game, when it can set up with both Swords Dance and Flame Charge and sweep. Silvally-Dark has trouble with Dark-types such as Alolan Persian and Skuntank, so checks to them such as Alcremie and Piloswine, respectively, are appreciated. Checks to Fighting-types such as Choice Scarf Rotom, Qwilfish, and the aforementioned Alcremie are also appreciated, with Rotom forming a VoltTurn core with Silvally-Dark and Qwilfish providing Spikes support, weakening foes such as Qwilfish into the range of +2 Multi-Attack. As Silvally-Dark lacks recovery, entry hazard removal from the likes of Cryogonal and Cramorant is necessary to keep Silvally-Dark healthy to keep pivoting with U-turn. Memento support from Uxie can help Silvally-Dark more easily set up with both Swords Dance and Flame Charge.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Silvally-Electric has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Stunfisk is the best of the Ground-types to counter Silvally-Electric, being 4HKOed by Silvally-Electric's coverage moves. Rhydon and Piloswine also work well to check Silvally-Electric, however both need to be vary of switching into Surf. Alolan Dugtrio outspeeds Silvally-Electric and OHKOes with Earthquake, but also cannot switch into Surf.

Bulky Foes: Miltank can comfortably tank any of Silvally-Electric's attacks and can chip it down with Seismic Toss or stall it out with Toxic. Alcremie can also survive Silvally-Electric's attacks relatively easily and can boost up alongside Silvally-Electric's Work Up with Acid Armor and Calm Mind.

Faster Threats: Choice Scarf Sawk and Rotom can outspeed and revenge kill Silvally-Electric. Naturally faster Pokemon such as Froslass and Rapidash can also revenge kill once it is sufficiently chipped down.

Mixed Wallbreaker.description:
Silvally-Electric functions as a solid mixed wallbreaker thanks to its great coverage breaking down common Fire / Water / Grass cores. Multi-Attack is Silvally-Electric's strongest STAB move with no drawbacks, hitting specially bulky Pokemon such as Articuno and Clefairy harder than Thunderbolt. Surf targets Ground-types like Rhydon, Piloswine, and Alolan Dugtrio, and Ice Beam provides coverage against Altaria, Tangela, and Thwackey. Flamethrower can be used to hit Shedinja, Klinklang, and the aforementioned Grass-types at the cost of not being able to hit Altaria as hard. Work Up allows Silvally-Electric to boost pass walls such as Clefairy, Miltank, and Alcremie depending on their sets.

Silvally-Electric fits best on balance teams that can use its wallbreaking prowess to break down opposing cores on balance builds. Stunfisk can be problematic for Silvally-Electric, as Ice Beam and Surf only 4HKO it. Skuntank and Choice Scarf Rotom can help wear down Stunfisk as well as cripple it with Corrosive Gas and Trick, respectively. Thwackey can also pressure Stunfisk and also pivot in Silvally-Electric safety. In return, Silvally-Electric threatens out Pokemon that wall Thwackey such as Tangela and Altaria. Switch-ins to Ground-types Rhydon, Piloswine, and Alolan Dugtrio are needed, so teammates like Tangela, Poliwrath, and Miltank fit well to help cover them.

pu.overview: Silvally-Fairy is a very versatile threat in PU thanks to a myriad of factors. Solid base stats across the board and a wide movepool allow it to be easily constructed to fit a specific team's needs. With access to Defog, Parting Shot, and Thunder Wave, it can be a great support Pokemon, while access to Swords Dance and super effective coverage to hit common Fairy-type checks such as Togedemaru and Charizard let it be a great offensive Pokemon. A pure Fairy typing means it's great for checking and setting up on Dark- and Fighting-types such as Absol and Hitmonlee. Silvally-Fairy's biggest flaw is its lack of any form of recovery. It is also susceptible to all entry hazards and status afflictions, making it easy to wear down and unable to check what it needs to consistently. Finally, it cannot fit all of what it wants on one set, limiting its options.

Utility.description: Parting Shot allows Silvally-Fairy to pivot out on would-be threats such as Togedemaru and Aggron. If Defog is unneeded, then Silvally-Fairy can run a status move of its choice to cripple an opposing Pokemon. Despite the Jolly nature, Flamethrower is chosen to target Steel-types, hitting them harder than Fire Fang. The Speed investment allows Silvally-Fairy to outspeed Timid Magmortar in addition to slower Pokemon like Absol and Shiftry, and the rest is invested into physical bulk. Notably, it is only 3HKOed by Muscle Band Gallade's Psycho Cut. Silvally-Fairy pairs best with Steel-types, building a solid defensive core with them. Togedemaru is a great option, as it can sponge Poison- and Steel-type attacks while healing Silvally-Fairy with Wish, and in return, Silvally-Fairy can tank Fighting-type attacks for it. Psychic- and Dark-type attackers such as Mesprit and Sneasel heavily appreciate Silvally-Fairy due to the absence of Dark- and Fighting-type checks in PU as well as the Parting Shot support it provides, making it easier for them set up without fear of being punished.

Swords Dance.description: A strong STAB move, great coverage, and two boosting moves let Silvally-Fairy tear through teams. Flame Charge is not only useful for hitting Steel-types, but it lets Silvally-Fairy boost its Speed, making it harder to revenge kill by Choice Scarf users such as Mesprit and Rotom. Rock Slide allows it to OHKO Charizard, while Psychic Fangs is a niche alternative that can take out a weakened Weezing. U-turn is also an option if Silvally-Fairy finds itself in a bad situation; however, this means forgoing important coverage. Swords Dance Silvally-Fairy can be used as both a sweeper and a wallbreaker, but it struggles to break past bulky physically defensive Pokemon such as Regirock and Aggron. Wallbreakers such as Shiftry and Basculin take advantage of these due to their super effective STAB moves while also weakening Fire- and Poison-types, making them solid partners for Silvally-Fairy. Cleaners such as Sneasel and Dragon Dance Charizard also appreciate walls such as Regirock and Palossand being weakened by Silvally-Fairy so they can efficiently sweep.

zu.comments:
Other Options

A fully physical Swords Dance set alongside Flame Charge and either Iron Head or Psychic Fangs makes Silvally-Fighting a late-game sweeper. At +2, a healthy Silvally-Fighting can lure in and defeat Alcremie with Iron Head, something other Fighting-types like Sawk cannot do, though this set can't beat defensive Pokemon like Qwilfish, Tangela, and Altaria. This set also faces tough competition from other Silvally formes due to their better offensive or defensive typings.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Alcremie and Clefairy do not take much damage from any of Silvally-Fighting's attacks and can freely set up on it, forcing it to switch. Galarian Rapidash can use it as setup fodder and heal damage inflicted with Morning Sun.

Bulky Pokemon: Articuno, Stunfisk, and Uxie don't take much damage from even Silvally-Fighting's super effective coverage attacks, with the former healing off damage with Roost, though Stunfisk and Uxie lack reliable recovery.

Ghost-types: Spiritomb can switch into any of Silvally-Fighting's attacks with impunity and use it as setup fodder. More offensive Ghost-types, like Rotom and Gourgeist-S, are immune to its STAB move and can revenge kill it with prior damage, though they can't repeatedly switch into Silvally-Fighting's coverage.

Faster Pokemon: With some chip damage, faster Pokemon like Manectric, Ninetales, and Galarian Rapidash can revenge kill Silvally-Fighting, though they do not want to directly switch into any of its attacks.

BoltBeam Pivot.description:
Silvally-Fighting is an excellent mixed wallbreaker and pivot thanks to its typing and movepool beating common Silvally checks, Defoggers, and entry hazard setters like Rhydon, Altaria, and Qwilfish in one teamslot. U-turn maintains momentum and chips bulkier checks like Alcremie, Stunfisk, and Articuno. Thunderbolt 2HKOes Qwilfish and 3HKOes Poliwrath, while Ice Beam targets Tangela, Altaria, and Gourgeist-S. These coverage moves allow Silvally-Fighting to beat common Fighting-type checks that would otherwise switch in safely.

Silvally-Fighting fits well on VoltTurn teams thanks to its good Speed tier, bulk, and coverage against defensive staples like Cramorant, Qwilfish, and Alolan Persian. Fast and slow pivots like Rotom formes, Type: Null, and Uxie chip down checks like Articuno, Stunfisk, and Rotom. Silvally-Fighting heavily struggles to break through Fairy-types and generally bulky Pokemon like Articuno or Stunfisk without support, so partners that can take these Pokemon on, like Alolan Dugtrio and Piloswine, can help it pivot more easily. In return, Silvally-Fighting can take on bulky staples weak to its coverage, like Tangela and Poliwrath, which the aforementioned Steel-types struggle against. Checks to Rotom and Gourgeist-S, such as Stunfisk and Sap Sipper Miltank, are appreciated. Stunfisk and Miltank can use Toxic to wear down checks to Silvally-Fighting, like Articuno and opposing Stunfisk. Miltank can provide cleric support to alleviate Silvally-Fighting's vulnerability to residual damage.

zu.overview: Silvally-Fire might look appealing to use thanks to a powerful STAB Multi-Attack and good stats all around. However, its vulnerability to residual damage, which includes a weakness to Stealth Rock, lack of reliable recovery, and fixed item slot and ability make it too unviable to warrant a teamslot. As a setup sweeper, Rapidash and Ninetales both eclipse it, with both of them possessing higher Speed, better movepools, and the ability to run actually useful items and abilities like Heavy-Duty Boots and Flash Fire, respectively.

Swords Dance.description: Silvally-Fire could muster its decent coverage and stats to become a suboptimal Swords Dance sweeper, able to break teams lacking Fire-resistant Pokemon and threaten Dragon-types such as Altaria and Appletun that other Fire-types fail to beat. Its vulnerability to all entry hazards and limited movepool makes it pale in comparison to preferred Fire-types like Rapidash and Ninetales, which both possess higher Speed and better coverage to target common Fire-resistant foes such as Qwilfish and Rhydon.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Silvally-Flying has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Electric-type Pokemon such as Rotom, Manectric, and Stunfisk resist Multi-Attack and can force Silvally-Flying out with their own STAB attacks. Choice Scarf Manectric is especially notable, outspeeding Silvally-Flying after a Flame Charge.

Rock-types: Rock-type Pokemon such as Rhydon, Coalossal, and Kabutops resist Multi-Attack and can threaten Silvally-Flying back. Rhydon and Coalossal can only check it, however, as they cannot switch into Surf.

Steel-types: Steel-type Pokemon such as Klinklang, and Alolan Dugtrio resist Multi-Attack. Silvally-Flying can break through them with Flame Charge after a Swords Dance boost, though.

Ice-types: Ice-type Pokemon such as Jynx and Articuno can check Silvally-Flying with their super effective STAB attacks. However, Jynx needs a Choice Scarf to be a consistent check. Piloswine, on the other hand, can easily take a hit and retaliate with Icicle Crash or just threaten it with a priority Ice Shard.

Swords Dance.description:
Silvally-Flying carves its niche out in ZU as a strong setup sweeper and wallbreaker. Its powerful STAB Multi-Attack especially threatens Pokemon such as Tangela and Throh. Flame Charge enables Silvally-Flying to outspeed revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Rotom, Sawk, and Kabutops. U-turn allows it to retain momentum against Pokemon that handle its attacks like Kabutops. Surf is the coverage move of choice, allowing Silvally-Flying to 2HKO Rhydon and Coalossal.

Silvally-Flying fits well on offense teams as a late-game sweeper, although it can function as a standalone wallbreaker too. Unfezant and Nasty Plot Rotom-S can aid Silvally-Flying by forming an offensive Flying-type spam core, wearing down shared checks and physical walls such as Rhydon, Qwillfish, and Miltank. This core, however, makes the team very weak to Stealth Rock, so it's important to have entry hazard removers such as Kabutops and Rotom. Hattrem is also a great partner, preventing Stealth Rock thanks to Magic Bounce and providing Healing Wish, which is great for offensive teams. Electric-type foes that threaten Silvally-Flying such as Rotom and Manectric can be covered by Stealth Rock setters in Rhydon and Piloswine. Fire-type Pokemon such as Rapidash and Ninetales can help cover the Ice weakness, in addition to Steel-types like Klinklang. Neither covers these weaknesses perfectly, however, due to Alolan Dugtrio and Piloswine threatening them out. A bulky Water-type such as Poliwrath fill in these gaps. Pokemon such as Sawk, Rotom, and Thwackey appreciate wallbreaking from Silvally-Flying opening up a path for a late-game sweep.

pu.overview: With access to boosting moves in Swords Dance and Flame Charge alongside a good offensive typing and strong stats, Silvally-Ghost makes for a strong setup sweeper. However, it faces stiff competition from the likes of Silvally-Fairy, which offers teams a stronger defensive typing with a plethora of useful resistances for a setup sweeper whilst maintaining the same coverage, meaning it's much more versatile and can fit on a wider variety of teams. Defensively, it falls short compared to other Ghost-types, such as Doublade and Jellicent, which provide solid secondary typings with useful immunities and, in Jellicent's case, a greater supportive movepool.

Swords Dance.description: Explosion is outstanding for its ability to provide a one-time nuke versus defensive checks such as Audino. However, U-turn can be used as a way to gain momentum against the aforementioned Ghost-resists without sacrificing Silvally-Ghost's life in the process. Substitute allows Silvally-Ghost to avoid status from the likes of Lanturn and is a strong option against Sucker Punch users like Absol, but leaves Silvally-Ghost with no way to threaten other bulky Pokemon like Quagsire. Ribombee makes a great partner thanks to its ability to not only offensively check Dark-types like Sneasel, but it also provides Sticky Web support. Additionally, Silvally-Ghost can act as a spinblocker against the likes of Eldegoss and use it as setup fodder if it lacks Sleep Powder. Fighting-types like Gallade and Poliwrath can pressure defensive checks to Silvally-Ghost such as Regirock, especially when safely brought in with U-turn.

pu.overview: Out of all the Swords Dance Silvally formes you may choose from, only Silvally-Grass can OHKO Unaware Quagsire. That feat is notable on hyper offense teams, and Silvally-Grass is also great at pressuring defensive staples like Wishiwashi, Regirock, Sandaconda, and Jellicent. Some passive Pokemon like Ferroseed and Eldegoss struggle even more, possibly lacking any means to deter its setup, and at +1 Speed, Silvally-Grass has the coverage to clean most teams. What is missing from Silvally-Grass's arsenal is the strength to get past Doublade and defensive Poison-types. These roadblocks are huge concerns for Silvally-Grass, as it risks never securing progress if Quagsire and Gigalith can just switch to Doublade and Weezing with minimal risk. There's also the downsides to the Grass typing, which include susceptibility to status, entry hazards, and, without boosts, faster revenge killers such as Ninjask and Sneasel. Offensively, there's also competition with other Silvally types like Fairy and Ghost, which fare better outside of bulky matchups.

Swords Dance.description: Flame Charge is crucial for cleaning late-game, and it's also necessary for hitting Grass- and Steel-types like Ferroseed and Togedemaru. Rock Slide nails most of what Multi-Attack can't: it OHKOes offensive Charizard, and it's good coverage versus the likes of Ribombee and Galarian Articuno. Specially offensive sweepers like Turtonator, Meteor Beam Archeops, and Nasty Plot Mespirit are some of the most essential teammates for Silvally-Grass. They force out the likes of Doublade, Weezing, and Garbodor while also benefiting from Silvally-Grass checking Gigalith and Sandslash. While not necessarily getting past these walls themselves, sweepers like Ribombee and Sneasel may force enough damage onto Poison- and Steel-types that they succumb to +2 Silvally-Grass. Additional physical sweepers like Swords Dance Doublade benefit from Silvally-Grass getting past Quagsire, and they are also good at forcing damage against shared checks, namely Poison-types.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Flamethrower deals more damage to Grass-resistant Pokemon like Klinklang, Tangela, and Ivysaur, but losing Flame Charge worsens Silvally-Grass's cleaning potential.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Grass-types like Tangela, Gourgeist-S, and Lurantis can freely switch into all of Silvally-Grass's standard attacks and can whittle it down with their own. All of them can heal damage off with their recovery moves, with Tangela gaining additional recovery with Regenerator.

Poison-types: Poison-types like Silvally-Poison, Skuntank, and Ivysaur resist Multi-Attack and can heavily threaten Silvally-Grass with their STAB attacks. While Qwilfish is neutral to Multi-Attack, it can cripple Silvally-Grass with Thunder Wave or chip it with entry hazards and Rocky Helmet.

Fire-types: Rapidash and Ninetales can outspeed Silvally-Grass and revenge kill it. Coalossal can cripple it with Flame Body. All of them dislike switching into a boosted Rock Slide, however.

Sap Sipper Pokemon: Miltank and Bouffalant can switch in comfortably against any of Silvally-Grass's moves and proceed to wear it down with status or attack it directly.

Faster Pokemon: While Silvally-Grass has good bulk and Speed, it can be picked off by naturally faster Pokemon like Accelgor, Froslass, and Rapidash, as well as Choice Scarf users like Sawk, Rotom, and Alolan Persian.

Swords Dance.description:
Silvally-Grass serves as a decent cleaner thanks to beating Ground-types like Rhydon, Piloswine, and Palossand, all common Silvally checks. Rock Slide nails Flying-types like Articuno, Altaria, and Golbat that would comfortably switch into Multi-Attack. Flame Charge increases Silvally-Grass's cleaning potential, with it outpacing Rapidash, Accelgor, and Choice Scarf users like Sawk and Rotom after a boost. Flame Charge also is its this set's strongest move against some Grass-resistant Pokemon like Klinklang and Ivysaur.

Silvally-Grass fits nicely on hyper offense teams looking for a Water-, Ground-, and Grass-resistant sweeper. Specially offensive wallbreakers and cleaners such as Lunatone, Skuntank, and Rotom work well with it, taking advantage of their typing or power to force out the walls Silvally-Grass struggles with, gaining setup opportunities. In return, Silvally-Grass can break through special walls like Articuno and Cryogonal. Before a boost, faster Pokemon like Froslass, Rapidash, and Choice Scarf users like Sawk and Jynx can revenge kill it without too much trouble. Teammates like Piloswine, Alcremie, and Articuno that can switch into them and threaten them off. Other physical attackers like Swords Dance Rapidash and Lycanroc-N can weaken Grass-type checks like Tangela and Ivysaur so Silvally-Grass can sweep late-game. Tangela is particularly difficult to deal with; Knock Off users like Sawk and Uxie can make progress and make it easier to deal with later on.

nu.overview: Silvally-Ground is a threatening and versatile Pokemon; strong EdgeQuake coverage threatens most of the tier, and it can either act as a sweeper with Flame Charge or an offensive pivot with U-turn that successfully blocks Rotom-C's Volt Switch. It finds plenty of opportunities to come in and threaten NU staples such as Copperajah, Diancie, and Stakataka, and its bulk allows it to take one attack from walls like Vaporeon and subsequently break through them. However, its inability to hold a useful item makes it quite susceptible to status and entry hazard damage, which can interfere with its ability to sweep; it is also held back by the existence of revenge killers like Inteleon, Heliolisk, and Choice Scarf Rotom-C.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Defog can take advantage of Silvally-Ground's positive matchup versus entry hazard setters like Garbodor, Copperajah, and Diancie but is generally a waste of its offensive potential. Facade turns Weezing into setup fodder and makes Talonflame's Will-O-Wisp less threatening, but the guaranteed damage from Rock Slide against Flying-types is usually better.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Rotom-C dislikes switching into Silvally-Ground's U-turn, but it is able to survive a +2 Flame Charge and OHKO back with Leaf Storm. Bulkier Grass-types like Decidueye and Dhelmise have access to recovery and can reliably fend off Silvally-Ground in the long-term.

Water-types: Vaporeon tanks one +2 Multi Attack and 2HKOes with Scald, preventing Silvally-Ground from getting an Attack and Speed boost if it is fully healthy.

Physical Walls: The combination of Stamina, Toxic, and Protect allows Mudsdale to stall out Silvally-Ground; Quagsire's Unaware lets it do the job as well. Levitate Weezing completely shuts down Silvally-Ground and cripples it with Will-O-Wisp. Talonflame's 4x weakness to Rock Slide makes it an unreliable answer, but it can revenge kill Silvally-Ground or pivot in on a Multi-Attack and chip it with U-turn.

Entry Hazards: Spikes can make it easier to offensively pressure Silvally-Ground or stall it out with Toxic poison due to its inability to run Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots. Toxic Spikes ruin its ability to sweep or pivot if they are not removed.

Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf Inteleon can outspeed and OHKO Silvally-Ground even after a Speed boost; Choice Scarf Heliolisk also outspeeds Silvally-Ground but cannot OHKO it. Without Flame Charge, Silvally-Ground can be revenge killed by a wider variety of fast offensive threats. Starmie and Choice Scarf Rotom-Mow can OHKO it, and Talonflame, Salazzle, and Choice Scarf Passimian are able to KO it after a moderate amount of chip damage.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Swords Dance and 120-Base Power Multi-Attack combine to make Silvally-Ground a massive offensive threat. Rock Slide takes down Flying-types like Xatu and Talonflame; it also hits Mantine super effectively but does not OHKO at +2 without prior damage. U-turn chips down checks like Rotom-C, Vaporeon, and Tsareena, making it easier for Silvally-Ground to sweep later. Alternatively, Flame Charge buffs Silvally-Ground's late-game potential, giving it a Speed boost and making it harder to revenge kill with Pokemon like Choice Scarf Passimian.

Spikers like Garbodor, Froslass, and the more niche Ferroseed can pave the way for a Silvally-Ground sweep, especially when paired with Knock Off users like Drapion and Passimian. Teammates that struggle with Water- or Grass-types, such as Swords Dance Talonflame and Nasty Plot Rotom-C, appreciate U-turn Silvally-Ground's ability to weaken those walls. Silvally-Ground appreciates having Flying-types like Xatu and Mantine weakened or removed before attempting to sweep; Fighting-types like Passimian and Toxicroak can force damage onto them and put them in range of +2 Rock Slide.

zu.overview: Silvally-Ice's good offensive typing, all-around stats, and movepool are let down by its abysmal defensive utility, as well as its fixed item and ability. These factors cause it to get worn down quickly by residual damage, which includes Stealth Rock, and make it very difficult to switch in safely. Silvally-Ice also faces overwhelming competition as a setup sweeper from its other formes, such as Silvally-Dark and Silvally-Poison, both of which have better typings to be overall better offensively and defensively.

Swords Dance.description: Silvally-Ice can use its good coverage and stats to try to clean mid- or late-game, forcing out Pokemon like Altaria, Tangela, and Stunfisk. However, its vulnerability to all entry hazards and terrible defensive utility make it difficult to pull off a sweep with it. Silvally formes like Silvally-Dark and Silvally-Poison can both do the same thing but better because of their superior typings.

pu.overview: Silvally-Poison is primarily a niche breaker, but can also be a Defogger. Its typing works decently in a tier with prevalent Fairy-, Grass-, and Fighting-types such as Ribombee, Eldegoss, and Hitmonlee, respectively. Silvally-Poison's Toxic immunity makes it a potent threat against passive teams, as it can freely setup on clerics such as Audino and Aromatisse and still have coverage for checks like Togedemaru. Being able to fit Grass Pledge comfortably to counter Quagsire distinguishes it from other Silvally formes. However, Silvally-Poison often is outperformed as a breaker by other Silvally formes with more intimidating offensive typings like Silvally-Ghost and Silvally-Fairy. As a Defogger, Silvally-Poison fits nicely on bulkier teams as a Knock Off and Toxic Spikes absorber; even so, it tends to get worn down over time and faces competition from other bulky Poison-types like Garbodor and Qwilfish.

Work Up.description: Silvally-Poison fits nicely on bulky offense and balance teams in need of a stallbreaker. It is great at dismantling bulky teams through Work Up. Multi-Attack allows it to muscle through specially defensive Pokemon like Articuno and Audino. Flamethrower nails Steel-types like Togedemaru and Ferroseed. Grass Pledge is useful for targeting Quagsire and Palossand. Surf, as an alternative to Grass Pledge, does more damage to Aggron in exchange for not breaking Quagsire. Ferroseed is a good partner for Silvally-Poison by providing Spikes support. They compliment each other defensively as well, as Ferroseed can switch into Psychic-types like Mesprit and Silvally-Poison can switch into Fighting-types like Hitmonlee. Jellicent is also a solid fit for dealing with opposing Fighting-types and spreading burns for easier setup later. Other partners such as Galvantula and Whimsicott can lure in defensive Pokemon like Audino for Silvally-Poison to set up on. Charizard benefits from Silvally-Poison tanking Knock Off and pressuring common defensive cores. In return, Charizard offers more immediate power and can wear down shared checks like Gigalith.

Defog.description: Defogger Silvally-Poison checks common Pokemon like Ribombee and makes for decent hazard removal on bulkier teams. The Speed investment allows Silvally-Poison to Defog before Qwilfish can Taunt it. Poison-type Multi-Attack pressures common threats like Silvally-Fairy. Flamethrower hits Steel-types like Perrserker and Ferroseed super effectively. U-turn allows Silvally-Poison to pivot without triggering Competitive Galarian Articuno. Silvally-Poison is worn down fast by entry hazards when removing them, so clerics like Aromatisse and Audino are valuable partners. Tangela and Gourgeist check common Ground-types that Silvally-Poison is vulnerable against such as Sandaconda. Unaware Quagsire nullifies the various setup sweepers in the tier and reciprocally benefits from Silvally-Poison dealing with Grass-types.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Ice Beam is an option over Surf for mixed sets, allowing Silvally-Poison to OHKO Altaria while keeping neutral coverage on the whole tier bar Piloswine when paired with Thunderbolt. However, this leaves Silvally-Poison far less consistent versus Ground- and Rock-types such as Rhydon, Stunfisk, and Coalossal. Parting Shot can be used over U-turn on Defog sets, but U-turn's damage is often preferred and Klinklang's Clear Body would prevent Silvally-Poison from freely pivoting. Surf and Thunderbolt are options over U-turn and Flame Charge on Swords Dance Silvally-Poison, giving it better coverage. Grass Pledge is a coverage move hitting Ground-types like Rhydon and Stunfisk while still hitting Water-types like Kabutops and Qwilfish, but it is signficantly weaker than Surf + Thunderbolt.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Even if carrying Surf, Silvally-Poison needs to heavily weaken Ground-types like Rhydon, Piloswine, and Stunfisk before sweeping.

Rotom: Rotom resists Silvally-Poison's STAB Multi-Attack and can threaten it back with its STAB moves or a burn with Will-O-Wisp. However, sets without Choice Scarf get outspeed by Silvally-Poison and are quickly put in range of a +1 Surf.

Qwilfish: If Silvally-Poison isn't running Thunderbolt, it gets hard walled by Qwilfish, which can cripple it with paralysis and chip it down with Rocky Helmet damage.

Rock-types: If Silvally-Poison doesn't carry Surf, it can't significantly damage Coalossal and risks a Flame Body burn with its contact moves. On the other hand, if it does not have Thunderbolt, it struggles with Kabutops, which can hit it hard.

Mixed Walls: Very bulky Pokemon like Altaria, Miltank, and Uxie can stomach Silvally-Poison's hits and heavily damage it with their repeated attacks, even if Silvally-Poison can break through them after several boosts.

Steel-types: If Silvally-Poison isn't using Flamethrower, it can't really deal damage to Klinklang, and it can significantly weaken Silvally-Poison with its powerful STAB moves.

Faster Attackers: Pokemon like Froslass, Alolan Persian, and Rapidash outspeed Silvally-Poison and can 2HKO it while avoiding an OHKO from it.

Work Up.description:
Work Up Silvally-Poison is a powerful mixed attacker thanks to its great bulk and coveted Poison typing, which let it take advantage of common threats like Alcremie and Thwackey. Flamethrower lets Silvally-Poison 2HKO Tangela and OHKO Steel-types like Klinklang after a boost. Thunderbolt is an alternative for massive damage to Qwilfish, Kabutops, and Cramorant, the former resisting every other move Silvally-Poison commonly runs. Surf removes Ground- and Rock-types like Piloswine, Rhydon, and Coalossal after chip damage, as well as beating Rapidash without risking a burn from Flame Body.

Since Silvally-Poison misses a lot of OHKOs after a Work Up, it works better as a mid- or late-game wallbreaker, so it appreciates early-game wallbreakers like Black Belt Sawk and Thwackey weakening walls and removing their items with Knock Off. Rotom formes make for great partners, weakening Ground-types with Will-O-Wisp and their secondary STAB moves so Silvally-Poison can OHKO them later with Surf. Furthermore, most Electric-types like Rotom, Stunfisk, and Manectric can force in Grass-types like Thwackey and Tangela for Silvally-Poison to take advantage of. That said, Tangela can put it to sleep with Sleep Powder on the switch, so Silvally-Poison should be careful setting up versus it. These Electric-types also take care of Steel-types for Silvally-Poison. Defensive pivots like Uxie, Clefairy, and Tangela are appreciated to switch into revenge killers like Froslass and Choice Scarf Sawk or defensive checks like Stunfisk and Miltank, in addition to providing it switch-in opportunities.

Defog.description:
Silvally-Poison makes a good pivot with its great bulk and useful set of resistances letting it check attackers like Sawk and Thwackey. It is also one of the few Pokemon packing both a pivoting move and entry hazard removal, bringing great role compression. Surf lets it threaten common hazard setters such as Rhydon, Piloswine, and Coalossal, while Thunderbolt hits Qwilfish, another premier Spikes setter.

Silvally-Poison's key defensive utility, along with its pivoting, makes it a premier choice for VoltTurn teams. As a result, other staples of this archetype like Alolan Persian, Rotom, and Articuno make for great partners to consistently chip the opposing team. Thwackey is a particularly noticeable partner, forcing in Grass-types such as Shiinotic and Tangela, which Silvally-Poison takes advantage of, and providing Grassy Terrain support, negating Silvally-Poison's weakness to Earthquake and providing it passive recovery. Wallbreakers such as Thievul, Arctovish, and Jynx love getting safe switch-in opportunities from pivoting moves, and Silvally-Poison can switch into their checks like Sawk and Thwackey.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Silvally-Poison doubles up as an offensive pivot and late-game cleaner. U-turn allows it to generate momentum and chip its checks like Rhydon and Alolan Persian early-game. Flame Charge lets it outspeed common Choice Scarf users like Sawk and Rotom, and it also provides coverage for Steel-types like Klinklang.

This set fits better on offensive teams due to how immediately threatening it is. It appreciates Pokemon able to take advantage of Rock-, Ground-, and Steel-types such as Thwackey, Poliwrath, and Sawk, which help it sweep late-game, while they enjoy Silvally-Poison forcing these checks in. Offensive pivots like Rotom, Articuno, and Klinklang make for great partners, forming VoltTurn cores with Silvally-Poison. Thievul is a noticeable partner that can heavily weaken physically bulky foes like Rhydon and Miltank, opening the way for a Silvally-Poison sweep, while in return Silvally-Poison can take advantage of the Fighting- and Fairy-types such as Sawk and Alcremie that Thievul forces in.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Silvally-Psychic has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-type Pokemon such as Alolan Persian, Morpeko, and Skuntank can all threaten Silvally-Psychic with their STAB attacks while being immune to Multi-Attack. In addition, Alolan Persian deters Swords Dance thanks to Foul Play, making it a very consistent counter.

Ghost-types: Ghost-type Pokemon such as Gourgeist-S and Rotom can revenge kill Silvally-Psychic with their STAB attacks. Choice Scarf Gourgeist-S is especially notable, outspeeding Silvally-Psychic even after a Flame Charge.

Steel-types: Steel-type Pokemon such as Klingklang and Alolan Dugtrio easily take most of Silvally-Psychic’s attacks and hit hard back. However, Silvally-Psychic can break through them with Flame Charge after a Swords Dance boost.

*Physical Walls: Miltank, Rhydon, and Tangela can often trade hits with Silvally-Psychic thanks to their great bulk. However, they are threatened by a boosted Multi-Attack.

Swords Dance.description:
Silvally-Psychic acts as a powerful offensive pivot, wallbreaker, and late-game cleaner, threatening common walls such as Qwilfish, Throh, and Poliwrath; however, being vulnerable to Sucker Punch and faster Ghost-types in Choice Scarf Rotom and Gourgeist-S limits its sweeping capabilities. Silvally-Psychic is also often outclassed by better Silvally formes with more desirable types such as Dark and Poison. Flame Charge allows Silvally-Psychic to outspeed Alolan Persian and Choice Scarf users, such as Sawk and Rotom, while also providing coverage for Steel-types such as Klinklang and Alolan Dugtrio. U-turn retains momentum and weakens its checks such as Alolan-Persian, Skuntank, and Uxie. X-Scissor provides coverage for the aforementioned Dark- and Psychic-types and hits harder than U-turn while also not forcing Silvally-Psychic out after it sets up.

Silvally-Psychic fits best on offense teams, where it can break through Fighting-type foes such Gurdurr, Throh, and Poliwrath. Removing them allows Steel- and Normal-types such as Klingklang and Kangaskhan to wreck havoc. Dark-types such as Alolan Persian, Spiritomb, and Skuntank are problematic, so checks to them such as Alcremie and Rhydon are welcomed, as are Dark- and Ghost-type teammates like Skuntank and Gourgeist-S to draw in and chip these threats. Opposing Ghost-types such as Choice Scarf Rotom and Gourgeist-S can revenge kill Silvally-Psychic, so checks to them including Rhydon and Miltank and are appreciated.

zu.overview: Silvally-Rock's poor defensive typing makes it wholly inferior to other Swords Dance sweepers in the tier. Other Silvally formes like Silvally-Poison and Silvally-Dark as well as both Rapidash formes are all significantly better than Silvally-Rock due to the defensive utility they provide for their team. It is also outclassed by Rhydon and Lycanroc-N as a Rock-type due to their significantly better bulk and access to priority, respectively, while both being overall stronger.

Swords Dance.description: Silvally-Rock aims to set up with Swords Dance and then either break teams with Multi-Attack + Psychic Fangs or go for a sweep with Flame Charge. However, Rhydon and Lycanroc-N have better options to hit common physical walls like Palossand and Tangela after a Swords Dance with their superior physical coverage. In addition, Silvally-Poison, Silvally-Dark, and both Rapidash formes outclass Silvally-Rock as a Swords Dance wallbreaker and sweeper while also providing excellent defensive utility for their team.

pu.overview: Silvally-Steel has a great movepool that includes a powerful STAB attack alongside good coverage as well as solid stats all-around, with base 95 Speed allowing it to outspeed a lot of the unboosted metagame. However, what really sets Silvally-Steel apart from other Silvally formes is its typing due to its resistances to STAB attacks from various common Pokemon like Ribombee, Galarian Articuno, and Whimsicott, allowing Silvally-Steel to more easily remove entry hazards, set up, or gain momentum. With its powerful physical STAB attack and great special coverage, Silvally-Steel can utilize Work Up to break through physical and special walls alike such as Quagsire, Ferroseed, and Gigalith. Its utility options like Defog and Parting Shot also make it a great glue option, being able to gain momentum and notably being the only Steel-type hazard remover. However. Silvally-Steel's inability to hold an item is a large hindrance, as it makes Silvally-Steel easier to wear down than other hazard removers like Eldegoss and Charizard and reduces its overall damage output. Finally, it is worth noting that while species clause can make for some mind games as to which Silvally forme you are using, is also somewhat limiting with the inability to use other viable Silvally formes like Silvally-Ghost and Silvally-Fairy.

Work Up.description: Work Up is Silvally-Steel's preferred setup move as its coverage pairs exceptionally well with its typing. Furthermore, it is preferred over Swords Dance due to its competition in Silvally-Ghost and Doublade having a better STAB typing and physical movepool, respectively. With 144 Special Attack EVs, Silvally-Steel's Grass Pledge 2HKOes Wishiwashi at +1 and has a chance to OHKO Quagsire, with the rest being put into Attack. Flamethrower rounds out the coverage, being able to hit Steel-types like Doublade and certain walls like Weezing. With Silvally-Steel's wide movepool, there are other options such as Rock Slide for taking out Charizard and Substitute for an easier time setting up and sweeping. As a sweeper, Silvally-Steel pairs well with wallbreakers like Vikavolt and Trevenant that can weaken defensive threats like Lanturn and Aggron, giving Silvally-Steel an easier time cleaning up the opposing team. On the other hand, Silvally-Steel can also act as a wallbreaker to open up opportunities for late-game cleaners like Ribombee and Sneasel. Entry hazards like Qwilfish's Spikes and Sandslash's Stealth Rock give Silvally-Steel an easier time sweeping and wallbreaking. Faster Pokemon like Charizard and Archeops can stop a weakened Silvally-Steel in its tracks, so checks and other means of crippling them like Gigalith and Sleep Powder Eldegoss can be helpful.

Utility.description: As an entry hazard remover, Silvally-Steel has the benefits of resisting Stealth Rock and being immune to Toxic Spikes. The given spread lets Silvally-Steel outspeed Timid Jellicent and Modest Magneton while furthering its ability to check special attackers like Ribombee and Whimsicott. While this set is often used for Defog alongside a better matchup against hazard setters like Ferroseed courtesy of Flamethrower, Toxic is another option for crippling threats like defensive Jellicent and Eldegoss. Parting Shot is able to keep momentum while also weakening the foe's attacks for your incoming Pokemon, although U-turn has the situational benefit of not triggering Galarian Articuno's Competitive, which already takes advantage of Defog. Other pivots like Wishiwashi and Vikavolt pair well with Silvally-Steel for maintaining momentum, with Wishiwashi and other walls such as Tangela and Audino forming a good defensive core. Audino is especially notable, since it can provide Silvally-Steel with some much-needed recovery with Wish and Heal Bell. Pokemon like Choice Specs Jellicent and Choice Band Sneasel appreciate Silvally-Steel's hazard removal and additional slow pivoting to give them free turns.

nu.overview: Silvally-Steel's the only specially bulky Defogger in NU that can pivot. It can also handle one of the more common Stealth Rock setters in Diancie and the rare Gigalith, discouraging them from setting entry hazards. It's also able to eat up STAB moves from common special wallbreakers like Exploud, Choice Specs Sylveon, and Alolan Exeggutor. Unfortunately, Silvally-Steel lacks any form of recovery and must rely on Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon for this. Additionally, Silvally-Steel often finds itself pivoting out of many defensive threats like Mudsdale, Vaporeon, and Guzzlord and thus can struggle to find opportunities to use Defog.
nu.comments:
Other Options

An alternate EV spread of 252 HP / 216 SpD / 40 Spe to outspeed Timid Exploud works as well at the expense of Speed. Silvally-Steel can forgo Flamethrower for Rock Slide to nail Talonflame and Salazzle, but it loses out on hitting opposing Steel-types. Silvally-Steel can also run another utility move like Toxic or Thunder Wave to cripple opposing teams.

Checks and Counters

Fire-types: Talonflame, Salazzle, and Arcanine force Silvally-Steel out with their STAB moves.

Stealth Rock Setters: Common Stealth Rock setters like Mudsdale and Rhydon can keep setting up Stealth Rock with little to no issue while also pressuring Silvally-Steel offensively.

Fighting-types: Passimian and Toxicroak are among the Fighting-types that offensively pressure Silvally-Steel with their respective STAB moves. Even against slower Fighting-types like Scrafty, Silvally-Steel can do little but pivot out with Parting Shot unless they're sufficiently weakened.

Fire-type and Fighting-type Coverage: Special wallbreakers like Exploud, Alolan Exeggutor, and Choice Specs Sylveon can carry super effective coverage to nail Silvally-Steel.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Defog is best used once Pokemon like Mudsdale and Rhydon are out of commission, since both of them reliably set Stealth Rock on Silvally-Steel. Flamethrower hits opposing Steel-types like Copperajah, Doublade, and Escavalier, as well as Rotom-C, for decent damage. Parting Shot lets Silvally-Steel pivot on Silvally-Ground, Mudsdale, and Copperajah to bring in a wallbreaker and force them out. Alternatively, U-turn stops Magic Bounce Xatu from blocking Silvally-Steel's pivoting and gaining momentum. The given EV spread with a Jolly nature allows Silvally-Steel to outspeed Jolly Tyrantrum.

Since Silvally-Steel lacks any kind of recovery, Wish-passing partners like Vaporeon and Sylveon are appreciated to give it more longevity. Talonflame, Ninjask, and Heliolisk form a VoltTurn core with Silvally-Steel to lure in and pivot on Diancie. Fighting-types like Choice Scarf Passimian and Toxicroak offensively pressure Silvally-Steel with their respective STAB moves. Therefore, having a partner like Vileplume or Garbodor to eat up said moves is appreciated. Wallbreakers like Starmie and Alolan Exeggutor can take advantage of Mudsdale and Copperajah by coming in via Silvally-Steel's pivots. Conversely, special wallbreakers with Fire- or Fighting-type coverage, like Exploud and Choice Specs Sylveon, can be problematic for Silvally-Steel if they predict it switching in. A teammate like Diancie or Vaporeon can give you more leverage when switching around their attacks.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Silvally-Water has no viable other options.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Manectric, Morpeko, and Choice Scarf Rotom all outspeed Silvally-Water and threaten it with their STAB attacks. They all need to be wary of switching in, however, due to their frail nature.

Grass-types: Offensive Grass-types like Thwackey and Gourgeist-S can nail Silvally-Water with their super effective STAB moves before it can attack. Defensive Grass-types like Gourgeist-XL and Tangela can wall it with ease.

Special Walls: Articuno, Clefairy, and Alcremie can all switch into Silvally-Water's special moves with ease and pivot out into the aforementioned Grass- and Electric-type checks. They can also stall Silvally-Water out with Toxic and recovery moves.

Physical Walls: The likes of Miltank, Sableye, and Altaria can easily take on Swords Dance sets and can afford to scout Silvally-Water's set by taking a special attack.

Residual Damage: Unlike most entry hazard removal options, Silvally-Water isn't protected from taking entry hazard damage due to its mandatory held item and lack of recovery. This can give it a bit of trouble in long games and forces it to try to come in when minimal layers of hazards are up. It also doesn't enjoy status like poison or burn adding onto this residual damage.

Defog.description:
Silvally-Water can serve a support role when running a Defog set. Its stats and great defensive typing allow it to stifle strong physically offensive Pokemon such as Klinklang, Rapidash, and Qwilfish. Surf can be utilized over Multi-Attack to deal with physically defensive Ground-types. Thunderbolt is great coverage to hit opposing Water-types such as the aforementioned Qwilfish as well as Poliwrath and Cramorant. Its slow U-turn and good bulk can help provide some chip damage while bringing in its teammates safely. With Water + Electric coverage, Silvally-Water has a favorable matchup into the top entry hazard setters in the tier.

Defog Silvally-Water can fit well on bulky offense team styles looking for an entry hazard removal option that can keep up the pressure. It can pair well with the likes of Rapidash, Skuntank, and Klinklang to help deal with Grass-types that it invites in. Also, Pokemon such as Rhydon and Morpeko can help deal with the Electric-types that check Silvally-Water. With its physically defensive build, Silvally-Water can struggle against hard-hitting special attackers; specially defensive walls such as Clefairy, Articuno, and Stunfisk make for great teammates to combat this issue. Also, Pokemon that outspeed popular threats to Silvally-Water can help force them out or take them down when the former are brought in by U-turn; these include Alolan Persian, Rapidash, Jynx, and any fast Pokemon that covers the weaknesses mentioned above. Silvally-Water can help form a great VoltTurn core with the likes of Rotom and Manectric, as they can help put on pressure by covering each other's weaknesses.

Swords Dance.description:
Silvally-Water serves as a niche physical wallbreaker sporting a Swords Dance set. Psychic Fangs is a great coverage move for dealing with common Water-resistant walls such as Qwilfish, Roselia, and Poliwrath. Bug-type coverage helps with Grass-types that resist Multi-Attack, such as Appletun, Thwackey, and Lurantis. U-turn lets Silvally-Water pivot and chip its checks like Altaria and Gourgeist formes, while X-Scissor is more useful for facilitating a sweep.

Swords Dance Silvally-Water fits best in bulky offense teams looking for a physical Water-type wallbreaker. Grass-type checks such as Tangela, Rapidash, and Skuntank can take advantage of the Grass-types that Silvally-Water invites in. Similarly, Ground-types like Rhydon and Piloswine are appreciated to cover Electric-types like Rotom and Manectric. Special wallbreakers like Thievul, Jynx, and Exeggutor can take advantage of the physical walls that Silvally-Water forces in, especially if Silvally-Water can provide safe switch-ins for them with U-turn.

Special Attacker.description:
Thanks to Silvally-Water's solid defensive typing and great BoltBeam coverage, it is a special attacker in ZU. Thunderbolt is great at targeting opposing Water-types such as Qwilfish, Poliwrath, and Cramorant. Ice beam strikes Grass-types such as Tangela, Thwackey, and Gourgeist-S hard. Flamethrower can be used to hit Klinklang harder while still targeting the aforementioned Grass-types, but it leaves Silvally-Water unable to hit Altaria hard. U-turn allows Silvally-Water to pivot out of unfavorable matchups such as Articuno, Clefairy, and Type: Null while retaining momentum.

Silvally-Water fits well on bulky offense and balance teams looking for a Water-type that provides bulk while also keeping up pressure and momentum. It also fits within VoltTurn cores, so staples such as Uxie, Rotom, and Thwackey work as great partners to help chip down the opposing team. Strong physical wallbreakers such as Lycanroc-N, Klinklang, and Sawk also work well as teammates, taking advantage of Silvally-Water's pivoting on special walls such as Articuno, Clefairy, and Type: Null. As Silvally-Water is vulnerable to faster Electric- and Grass-type attacks, Eject Pack Appletun can help cover them while keeping up momentum. Further switch-ins to Grass-types include Rapidash, Tangela, and Altaria with Rhydon, Stunfisk, and Manectric being switch-ins for Electric-types.

pu.overview: Turtonator carves a small niche as a Fire-type on hyper offensive teams over the more commonly seen Charizard thanks to a great boosting move in Shell Smash, which allows it to outspeed most of the unboosted metagame, making it difficult to revenge kill reliably. An excellent STAB combination along with high-powered STAB moves and valuable coverage in Flash Cannon makes it incredibly dangerous after a boost. However, Turtonator is held back by its low Speed, meaning it will most likely take heavy damage before safely setting up. It also has issues breaking through many top defensive Pokemon such as Gigalith, Wishiwashi, and Jellicent. Along with this, even after a Shell Smash it is still outsped by the commonly seen Ribombee as well as Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Mesprit, and it will either have a drop in its defensive stats after a boost or take heavy hazard damage upon switching in, depending on which item it's using.

Shell Smash.description: Flash Cannon hits Fairy-types such as Silvally-Fairy hard and deals good damage to Pokemon that resist Fire such as Archeops and Gigalith without the drawback of lowering Turtonator's Special Attack. White Herb reduces damage Turtonator takes after setting up, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used to avoid hazard damage upon switching in. One of Turtonator's best offensive checks is Ribombee, so partners that can check it are useful partners to have, such as Togedemaru and Doublade. Doublade in particular is also a great partner, as it can safely switch into Pokemon that can revenge kill Turtonator, such as opposing Lycanroc. Offensive Grass-types such as Thwackey and Silvally-Grass naturally scare out Water-types that otherwise check Turtonator, making them useful partners as well, while Frosmoth's natural special bulk allows it to safely Quiver Dance against Ribombee, and it can also set up on bulky Water-types that check Turtonator, such as Quagsire.

pu.overview: Togedemaru stands out as one of the best Choice Scarf users in the tier thanks to its solid Speed tier, great offensive and defensive typing that allows it to check Pokemon such as Archeops and Whimsicott, ability to gain momentum through U-turn, and good abilities. Its unique defensive typing and access to recovery in Wish also makes Togedemaru a useful special wall for taking on certain difficult threats such as Ribombee and Vikavolt. However, despite its excellent set of resistances, its mediocre bulk and an unreliable recovery move limits Togedemaru's ability to directly switch into threats. Sitting at base 96 Speed, it is one of the fastest Choice Scarf users and can outspeed boosted setup sweepers like Modest Ludicolo and Silvally-Fairy. However, Togedemaru fails to OHKO many of these Pokemon due to its only average Attack stat and coverage options. Togedemaru faces strong competition as a specially defensive Steel-type from Aggron and Galarian Stunfisk, who can set up Stealth Rock, and as a Wish passer from Audino due to its much higher HP stat.

Choice Scarf.description: Toxic is useful for crippling switch-ins like Quagsire and Vikavolt rather than merely pivoting out with U-turn, while Encore is more effective at annoying bulky setup sweepers such as Sandaconda. Lightning Rod is useful for pivoting into Volt Switch users such as Rotom and Vikavolt, but the chip damage from Iron Barbs is preferred if there is already an Electric-immune Pokemon on the team. Iron Barbs also helps defeat opposing Choice Scarf Togedemaru. While Togedemaru can be used throughout the match to tank some resisted hits, it is best brought in as a revenge killer or through slow pivots such as Lanturn and Silvally-Fairy, which form a VoltTurn core with it. Due to Togedemaru's poor damage output, it appreciates entry hazards from the likes of Gigalith and Froslass to help wear down its foes. Wallbreakers such as Whimsicott and Magmortar can also help wear down the opposing team so Togedemaru can potentially clean late-game, and they also serve as checks for threats to Togedemaru such as Palossand and Vikavolt, respectively.

Wish Passer.description: Iron Head is Togedemaru's attacking move of choice because it better threatens Pokemon Togedemaru is aiming to check such as Frosmoth and Whimsicott and does not leave Togedemaru unable to hit Ground-types. U-turn allows Togedemaru to slightly circumvent its passivity by pivoting on predicted switches, but Toxic cripples many Pokemon that Togedemaru cannot do much damage to such as Vikavolt. Heavy-Duty Boots significantly decreases Togedemaru's weakness to Spikes, Leftovers helps make it slightly less reliant on Wish, and Rocky Helmet in tandem with Iron Barbs allows Togedemaru to punish a wide variety of contact attackers. However, Lightning Rod is preferred to stop Volt Switch users such as Vikavolt and Rotom. 8 Speed EVs allow Togedemaru to outspeed Adamant Centiskorch and Modest Frosmoth. Togedemaru can support many teammates lacking recovery with Wish, such as Weezing and Mesprit, both of which also help against the Fighting-and Ground-types that threaten Togedemaru. Setup sweepers that can take advantage of Fighting- and Ground-types, such as Nasty Plot Mesprit and Quiver Dance Ribombee, appreciate being brought in through Togedemaru's U-turn.

nu.overview: Togedemaru is a versatile Steel-type pivot capable of multiple roles thanks to its rare defensive traits and great movepool. With Wish + Spiky Shield, it's one of the only Steel-types with reliable recovery, and its ability Lightning Rod also means it can wall Rotom-C and block Volt Switch. Offensively, Togedemaru makes a great pivot and revenge killer to threats like Talonflame and Starmie. Unfortunately, unlike other Steel-types that it competes with, Togedemaru is quite frail. While it can deter STAB attacks from special wallbreakers like Exploud and Choice Specs Sylveon, it struggles to tank their stronger coverage: Exploud's Overheat will OHKO Togedemaru. Choice Scarf Togedemaru is especially frail and cannot afford to switch into even resisted attacks from the likes of Galarian Articuno and Vanilluxe. Togedemaru isn't necessarily the strongest either and will struggle versus anything bulky enough that carries strong coverage for retaliation.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Super Fang is one way to hit walls on the switch in and force them to recover health or, in the case of Mudsdale, do worthwhile damage early-game. Substitute + Toxic work together for a stallbreaking set that finds setup opportunities versus the Electric- and Fairy-types that Togedemaru walls.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types and Ground-type Coverage: Bulkier Ground-types like Mudsdale and Quagsire tank Togedemaru's attacks and easily OHKO it with Earthquake. Silvally-Ground is especially notable for its Speed tier and how offensively punishing it can be if it nets a free switch in on Togedemaru's weaker or ineffective moves. Other Pokemon that run Ground-type coverage like Aerodactyl and Drapion will also force out Togedemaru and revenge kill non-Choice Scarf sets.

Bulky Attackers: Given its frailty, Togedemaru often fails to defeat anything bulky enough with strong coverage for it. Fighting-types like Toxicroak, Passimian, and Virizion are an issue for it, and so are other bulky attackers like Copperajah and Guzzlord.

Physical Walls: Togedemaru lacks wallbreaking power and won't easily deal with walls like Vileplume and Weezing. Even some other defensive foes like Talonflame and Vaporeon are troublesome because they can burn Togedemaru, struggle little with its bulkier sets, and can take advantage of certain moves Choice Scarf sets lock into.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Iron Head lets Togedemaru force out Fairy-types, though Zing Zap is sometimes used instead for its coverage versus Steel- and Water-type walls like Copperajah and Vaporeon. U-turn is essential for gaining momentum after switching into special attackers like Rotom-C and Heliolisk. Otherwise, Toxic punishes most switch-ins like Mudsdale and works well with Spiky Shield. U-turn + Toxic is doable at the expense of recovery from Wish. 56 Speed EVs with a Jolly nature mean that Togedemaru will outspeed wallbreakers like Tyrantrum and Exploud.

Flying-types like Talonflame, Mantine, and Xatu rely on Togedemaru to switch into Electric-types like Rotom-C and Heliolisk. In return, these teammates check Fighting- and Ground-types like Passimian and Silvally-Ground. Defensive Poison-types like Vileplume and Weezing also offer similar synergy.
