Horn Leech allows Tapu Bulu to remain healthy while also taking on Pokemon such as Clefable and Porygon2. Close Combat defeats threatening Steel-type Pokemon after a Swords Dance boost, such as Ferrothorn and specially defensive Heatran, and also heavily pressures Celesteela. Zen Headbutt allows Tapu Bulu to take on Poison-type foes after a Swords Dance boost such as Toxapex, Amoonguss, and Galarian Weezing, allowing it to muscle past Poison teams, which its teammates appreciate. Life Orb gives Tapu Bulu a boost to damage without much drawback, as the recovery from Horn Leech in tandem with Grassy Terrain allows it to ignore the recoil. Grassy Terrain also boosts Horn Leech, and it gives recovery and boosts Grass-type moves for the rest of the team. Maximum Speed EVs outspeed offensive Celesteela, Volcanion, and Adamant Bisharp, which can all be troublesome for Grass teams.

Rillaboom provides Grassy Terrain alongside Tapu Bulu for the rest of its team, and it can remove Leftovers from bulky Pokemon that take a +2 hit from Tapu Bulu, such as Celesteela and Corviknight, with Knock Off. Also, its Grassy Glide threatens offensive Pokemon such as Galarian Darmanitan and Nidoking, which can help Tapu Bulu break through teams without being forced out. Choice Scarf Zarude provides valuable revenge killing for Grass teams and defeats Psychic-type Pokemon that threaten Tapu Bulu, such as Victini and Tapu Lele, while pivoting on bulky Pokemon it lures in such as Ferrothorn, which Tapu Bulu can beat. Ferrothorn is great in making the defensive backbone of a Grass team, switching into Ice- and Bug-type moves from Pokemon such as Weavile and Golisopod, as well as setting an entry hazard in either Stealth Rock or Spikes. Cradily is able to switch into special-attacking Pokemon such as Zapdos, Galarian Moltres, and Kyurem, which can all prove troublesome to Grass, while also providing Stealth Rock to help Tapu Bulu break through teams more easily. Amoonguss switches into physical attackers that can threaten the rest of Grass such as Dragon Dance Dragapult and Mimikyu, provides utility in Spore and Clear Smog to stop setup sweepers such as Zarude and Dragonite, and can absorb Toxic Spikes.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Synthesis provides instant recovery to Tapu Bulu, but extra coverage is generally preferred. Bulk Up is an option to boost Defense as well as Attack, but the more immediately threatening nature of Swords Dance is usually better. High Horsepower is also an option to hit Heatran harder that does not lower defenses, but Close Combat and Stone Edge are usually preferred.

Checks and Counters

Intimidate / Dauntless Shield physical walls: Intimidate or Dauntless Shield users, such as Corviknight and Mew, are solid checks to Tapu Bulu. They can, however, be overwhelmed by Swords Dance; this is especially the case for Mew if Tapu Bulu is running Darkest Lariat, but it can usually, at worst, force a trade.

Fast Grass-resistant Pokemon: Faster Flying-, Fire-, and Steel-types such as Talonflame, Zapdos, and Genesect all outspeed Tapu Bulu, resist Horn Leech, and OHKO it back. However, they have a hard time directly switching in for fear of Stone Edge.

Psychic Surge Users: Psychic Surge users such as Azelf block Horn Leech, outspeed Tapu Bulu, and can KO it with their boosted STABs.

Wandering Spirit: Wandering Spirit Landorus-T and Corviknight frustrate Tapu Bulu by removing Triage and forcing it out. They are often only one-time checks, but that can be enough to deny a sweep.

Triage.description:
Thanks to Triage and its powerful Horn Leech, Tapu Bulu is a strong cleaner with great power in AAA. +3 priority Horn Leech makes up for Tapu Bulu's poor Speed and outpaces most forms of speed control, allowing it to clean up weakened teams in addition to wallbreaking for teammates. Due to its decent bulk and useful set of resistances, plus the threat of Horn Leech, Tapu Bulu is able to set up with Swords Dance on many prominent attackers including Tapu Koko, Barraskewda, and Zarude. Thanks to Horn Leech's significant recovery, Tapu Bulu is able to utilize Life Orb and even take damage while setting up and still power through opposing teams. Close Combat provides strong coverage, OHKOing Heatran after Stealth Rock and doing significant damage to Corviknight when boosted. The last moveslot is flexible; Stone Edge hits common Grass-resistant Pokemon like Zapdos, Mandibuzz, Talonflame, and Volcarona, while Darkest Lariat beats Dauntless Shield Mew and defense boosters like Bulk Up Corviknight. 132 Speed EVs outspeeds defensive Heatran and Moltres while still maintaining extra bulk to help with setup. A faster spread of 72 HP / 252 Atk / 184 Spe with a Jolly nature is another option to outspeed Modest Heatran.

Tapu Bulu is a great choice for balance and offense teams that want a cleaner that can also serve as a wallbreaker. Due to its ability to lure in and weaken common physical walls like Intimidate Corviknight, it pairs well with other strong physical attackers like Terrakion and Barraskewda. Tapu Bulu struggles to beat fast Fire- and Flying-types such as Entei, Cinderace, Talonflame, and Zapdos, as they resist Horn Leech and can OHKO it back. Strong answers to these, like Primordial Sea Zapdos, Flash Fire Corviknight, and Blissey make good partners. Tapu Bulu enjoys coming in on special walls that it can threaten out, giving it a free turn to attack or set up; Tapu Koko is a great option to lure in and pivot out on Blissey and Assault Vest Jirachi. Partners that can set and keep Stealth Rock up like Mold Breaker Heatran help Tapu Bulu clean by chipping foes over time. Mandibuzz and Choice Scarf Regenerator Genesect are both strong checks to Tapu Bulu, so solid switch-ins to these like Corviknight and Heatran can help check these threats. Psychic Surge Azelf is difficult for Tapu Bulu to handle due to it blocking Horn Leech, making partners like Jirachi solid choices.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Fairy

Tapu Fini can also run a set consisting of Calm Mind, Iron Defense, Draining Kiss, and Stored Power. This set can surprise offensive teams that don't run phazing, like Dragon teams, and decimates Ground teams that forgo Clear Smog on Gastrodon. However, this set is prone to Haze from Mantine and Toxapex due to the lack of Taunt.

Water

Defog can be used in place of Knock Off on Choice Scarf Tapu Fini if the team doesn't have any entry hazard removal.

Calm Mind (Fairy).description:
Taking advantage of Tapu Fini's ability, good defensive typing, and high defensive stats, this set is a powerful setup sweeper in the Monotype metagame and poses a threat to many types, including Fire and Flying. Scald deals with Steel- and Ground-types such as Corviknight and Nidoking, and it threatens to burn incoming physical attackers such as Celesteela, which Tapu Fini can then use as setup fodder. Draining Kiss hits Dragon-types like Dragapult and Hydreigon super effectively and lets Tapu Fini regain health. Taunt allows Tapu Fini to thwart Haze attempts from foes like Toxapex and Mantine. Substitute can be used over Taunt to prevent foes like Toxic Victini from statusing it once Misty Terrain runs out, in addition to blocking Celesteela's Leech Seed. It also lets Tapu Fini safely damage offensive checks such as Thundurus-T, and it prevents Clear Smog Gastrodon from clearing Tapu Fini's boosts. 184 Defense EVs ease the matchup against Celesteela and Dragonite, and 8 Special Attack EVs guarantee Scald 2HKOes Thundurus-T when Tapu Fini is at +1. 8 EVs in Special Defense prevent Gastrodon from breaking its Substitute with Earth Power. 56 Speed EVs let Taunt Tapu Fini outspeed Jolly Azumarill to prevent it from using Belly Drum, as well as Mantine to stop its Haze.

Klefki is a superb teammate for Tapu Fini, as not only does it set dual screens to let Tapu Fini set up more easily, but it is also immune to Poison. It can also set Spikes to assist Tapu Fini's sweep attempts. Tapu Bulu is also a great teammate, as it can deal with Toxapex and Mantine, both of which cause trouble for Tapu Fini. However, the latter is only problematic if using Substitute. Tapu Bulu can also deal with troublesome Steel- and Poison-types, such as Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking, with Close Combat and High Horsepower. Tapu Lele is another solid option, as it threatens Poison- and Water-types such as Toxapex, Amoonguss, and Mantine with Psychic and Thunderbolt, all while pressuring Kyurem and drawing in Dragalge to chip it. Tapu Koko threatens Water-types and Cinderace and brings Tapu Fini in against foes such as Landorus-T with U-turn. Clefable is a strong utility option, providing Knock Off and Stealth Rock support while threatening Steel-types such as Ferrothorn with Flamethrower. Azumarill is also a good teammate for Tapu Fini, as it can remove items from foes like Tornadus-T and Thundurus-T, making them prone to Stealth Rock wearing them down. In addition, it is a physical wallbreaker that can take on Victini, Galarian Slowking, and Steel- and Poison-types for the team.

Choice Scarf (Water).description:
Choice Scarf Tapu Fini outspeeds and removes threats like Kyurem, Dragapult, and Bulk Up Zarude. Trick cripples defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex, which can switch into Tapu Fini's attacks with ease. Ice Beam threatens Flying-types such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, and non-Choice Scarf Thundurus-T. Knock Off removes key items like Leftovers, Assault Vest, and Black Sludge from common switch-ins like Celesteela, Galarian Slowking, and Dragalge.

Choice Scarf Tapu Fini acts as a reliable revenge killer for Water teams and usually fits on balance teams with Slowking + Toxapex as the main defensive core. Slowking pressures Poison-types such as Toxapex and Amoonguss with Future Sight, as well as bringing in Tapu Fini and other teammates safely with Teleport. Toxapex deals with Choice Scarf Zarude and Tapu Bulu, which give Tapu Fini trouble. Swampert forms a solid defensive backbone with Slowking and Toxapex, as it provides an Electric immunity, sets Stealth Rock, deals with defensive Pokemon such as Aegislash, and handles Poison-types such as Nidoking and Nihilego. Urshifu-R breaks through defensive Steel-types like Celesteela and Ferrothorn for Tapu Fini. Volcanion deals with Grass- and Steel-types such as Ferrothorn, Amoonguss, Celesteela, and Aegislash. Golisopod deals with Grass-types such as Rillaboom and Choice Scarf Zarude, and it also provides Spikes support for Tapu Fini to sweep late-game.

Calm Mind (Water).description:
Calm Mind Tapu Fini acts as a bulky stallbreaker and late-game wincon for Water teams against types such as Dragon and Steel, once checks such as Dragalge and Ferrothorn are dealt with. Calm Mind makes Tapu Fini a threatening sweeper, allowing it to take on Pokemon such as Kyurem, Galarian Moltres, and Aegislash. Draining Kiss lets Tapu Fini stay healthy, making it harder to take down, and it also targets Dragon- and Dark-types such as Kyurem and Hydreigon, which shrug off Scald. Scald deals with Steel- and Poison-types such as Corviknight and Nidoking, and it can spread burns, making Tapu Fini harder to break down. Taunt shuts down phazers such as Mantine and Toxapex, allowing Tapu Fini to use them as setup fodder. The bulk EVs let Tapu Fini survive a Power Whip from Choice Scarf Zarude at full health and have a good chance to beat SubRoost Kyurem after a boost, while 12 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed uninvested Rotom-W. Leftovers helps Tapu Fini stay healthy throughout the match, which is useful for setting up multiple Calm Minds.

Swampert sets Stealth Rock to wear down opposing teams, as well as dealing with defensive Pokemon Tapu Fini struggles with, such as Aegislash and Poison-types. Slowking forms the team's defensive core with Swampert and deals with Poison-types like Toxapex, Amoonguss, and Nidoking with Future Sight and Teleport. Golisopod deals with common Grass- and Psychic-type threats like Rillaboom, Zarude, Mew, and Jirachi with its powerful First Impression and Knock Off. Urshifu-R removes other defensive Pokemon like Celesteela and Corviknight, which Tapu Fini fails to break through. Volcanion supports Tapu Fini by dealing with popular threats such as Amoonguss, Ferrothorn, and Celesteela with its powerful Fire-type moves.

Support.description: Tapu Fini is a great bulky Water-type due to its support options that can effectively deal with threats such as Kyogre and Calyrex-S. Moonblast is its main STAB move, hitting Urshifu-R while being able to lower Calyrex-S's and Xerneas's Special Attack. Nature's Madness patches Tapu Fini's lack of offensive presence, being able to damage Zacian-C and Xerneas for half of their remaining HP. Icy Wind aids slower allies such as Landorus in outspeeding and threatening Zacian-C, while Heal Pulse is great for healing Tapu Fini's partners and punishing defensive play. Misty Surge enables Tapu Fini to soft check Pokemon that rely on status conditions such as Amoonguss, Volcarona and Zapdos. Wiki Berry paired with Tapu Fini's EV spread allows it to take many hits such as +1 Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, +2 Xerneas's Moonblast, +1 Nihilego's Sludge Bomb, and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide in Grassy Terrain. For restricted partners, Zacian-C, Groudon, and Necrozma-DM are great allies, being able to check Rillaboom easily while Tapu Fini threatens Urshifu-R and protects them from burns. As for non-restricted Pokemon, Incineroar and Entei are great to quickly check Grass-types like Tsareena and Rillaboom for Tapu Fini, while it checks Urshifu-R and Kyogre in return. Landorus is another good option, being able to OHKO Nihilego, Zacian-C, and Stakataka. Rillaboom's and Incineroar's Fake Out pressure offers Tapu Fini opportunities to easily damage opposing threats, leaving them in range for a potential Grassy Glide or Flare Blitz.

ubers.overview: Tapu Fini can trap a number of bulky Pokemon in Ubers such as Eternatus and Yveltal, opening up holes for teammates to take advantage of. By virtue of its Fairy typing and Misty Surge, Tapu Fini can reliably check Zygarde and Yveltal, although it doesn't appreciate Yveltal's Knock Off. Misty Surge is highly appreciated by teammates like Groudon that do not want to be affected by status conditions and prevents Zygarde and Xerneas from using Rest. However, Tapu Fini's poor Speed and damage output mean that it does not have a good matchup against the more dangerous offensive staples like Calyrex-S, Groudon, and Kyogre. Furthermore, Misty Terrain preventing status from defensively checking opposing setup sweepers limits Tapu Fini's potential teammates.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

A Choice Scarf set with Trick over Taunt allows Tapu Fini to potentially surprise an offensive Pokemon like Marshadow while still letting it trap most of its defensive targets and potentially cripple another by using Trick. Defog can be used over Moonblast to provide extra hazard control if necessary, but it also removes Misty Terrain and makes Tapu Fini far too passive.

Checks and Counters

Strong Offensive Pokemon: Tapu Fini cannot take many neutral hits in Ubers, and Pokemon like offensive Necrozma-DM, Xerneas, Groudon, and Kyogre can overwhelm it fairly easily.

Zekrom: Zekrom's Bolt Strike OHKOes Tapu Fini, it is not OHKOed by Moonblast, and it even appreciates Misty Terrain. Zekrom doesn't like its Dragon-type STAB being weakened by Misty Terrain, though.

Setup Sweepers: Tapu Fini's poor damage output and Speed mean it can be set up on by most dangerous sweepers like Nasty Plot Calyrex-S and Geomancy Xerneas.

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM can 3HKO Tapu Fini with Sunsteel Strike after Stealth Rock, preventing it from being trapped by Tapu Fini, although Tapu Fini can trap Iron Head variants very reliably.

Ho-Oh: While Ho-Oh dislikes not being able to burn or paralyze its targets, it will take on Tapu Fini fairly reliably thanks to Regenerator and Brave Bird. It can even use Defog to remove Misty Terrain.

Eternatus: Sludge Bomb Eternatus can easily come in on Tapu Fini and prevent it from making progress by threatening an OHKO and recovering off any chip damage taken in the process. However, without Sludge Bomb, Eternatus is one of Tapu Fini's targets.

Trapper.description:
Whirlpool allows Tapu Fini to trap bulky foes that cannot significantly threaten it such as specially defensive Eternatus, some Necrozma-DM sets, and Ferrothorn without Grass-type coverage. Nature's Madness combined with Taunt and the residual damage from Whirlpool lets Tapu Fini KO most defensive Pokemon in Ubers. Moonblast helps Tapu Fini defensively check Zygarde, Yveltal, and Marshadow, although its lack of reliable recovery means it cannot do so consistently throughout a game. The lack of reliable recovery also means it can only normally trap one Pokemon per game, as it will normally take significant damage in the process. 56 Speed EVs guarantee that Tapu Fini will outspeed Calyrex-I and paralyzed Calyrex-S.

Tapu Fini partners best with offensive wallbreakers that appreciate its Misty Surge and trapping capabilities. Kyogre in particular appreciates Misty Surge both halving Eternatus's damage output with Dynamax Cannon and Draco Meteor and making Toxic fail, allowing it to potentially set up on Eternatus. Tapu Fini can also trap Blissey, one of Kyogre's sturdiest defensive answers. Marshadow and offensive Ho-Oh enjoy Tapu Fini preventing Zygarde, as well as other defensive Pokemon like Xerneas, Giratina, and Kyogre, from recovering with Rest. Galarian Darmanitan appreciates Tapu Fini potentially trapping Necrozma-DM and not having to fear paralysis. Galarian Darmanitan can also bring Tapu Fini onto the field frequently with U-turn, giving Tapu Fini an easier time trapping its targets. Heatran can be used alongside Tapu Fini to trap a wider range of Pokemon, including all defensive Eternatus sets. Tapu Fini can protect Groudon from status so it can set up more easily, and Tapu Fini checks one of Groudon's better answers in Zygarde.

ou.overview: With a good typing and solid defenses, Tapu Fini is a strong defensive Pokemon that can check many of the metagame's offensive threats, such as Urshifu-R, Buzzwole, and Weavile, while supporting its own team with Misty Terrain, keeping them safe from status. Tapu Fini further supports its team with access to a handful of powerful utility moves, like Trick, allowing it to cripple opposing defensive Pokemon with a Choice Scarf set, and Taunt, which lets it take advantage of more passive foes to set up and shut down opposing setup sweepers. However, Tapu Fini lacks reliable recovery, only learning Draining Kiss, which is a significant Base Power downgrade from Moonblast, and Rest, which is blocked by Misty Terrain. This makes it reliant on Leftovers and susceptible to being chipped down if it loses them or opts for a Choice Scarf set, which can eventually lead to it being overwhelmed by the Pokemon that it is supposed to check, like Weavile and Urshifu-R. Additionally, many prominent metagame threats like Rillaboom, Kartana, and Tapu Koko pose a serious threat to Tapu Fini.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Tapu Fini can serve as an entry hazard remover with Defog, but it lacks recovery and doesn't run Heavy-Duty Boots, so other Defoggers like Corviknight are preferred. Tapu Fini can also opt to run Knock Off as a way to hinder opponents, but it tends to get more utility out of Taunt, as many of its common teammates, like Kartana and Weavile, already run Knock Off. Surf or Hydro Pump can be used over Scald for more power, but they trade off the potential to burn incoming Rillaboom, and, in the case of Hydro Pump, very reduced accuracy. Substitute is a niche option on Calm Mind sets to allow Tapu Fini to set up safely but comes at the cost of Taunt's utility. Ice Beam is another niche choice that can let Tapu Fini take Zapdos and Rillaboom switching in by surprise, but both of these Pokemon still outspeed and threaten Tapu Fini while recovering off damage through Roost or Grassy Terrain.

Checks and Counters

Galarian Slowking: Galarian Slowking is one of the metagame's truest counters to Tapu Fini, as it takes negligible damage from any attacks, especially if it's running an Assault Vest, and easily heals with Regenerator while 2HKOing Tapu Fini with Sludge Bomb. Nasty Plot sets can also overwhelm Tapu Fini, quickly wearing it down with Psyshock or Sludge Bomb. It is crippled by being receiving a Choice Scarf from Trick sets, though Tapu Fini should be wary of hindering its own utility by taking on an Assault Vest or hurting itself by receiving Black Sludge from either its own Trick or Galarian Slowking's.

Steel-types: Most Steel-types can survive any attack from Tapu Fini and threaten it back, particularly Melmetal with Double Iron Bash, while mostly being immune to a Scald burn thanks to Misty Terrain. Ferrothorn can easily take Tapu Fini's attacks and deal huge damage back with Power Whip, though not all Ferrothorn sets include Power Whip, and these sets in particular hate being Taunted. Corviknight can live any one hit from Tapu Fini, but fears being burned and will struggle to damage it back. Additionally, any of these Steel-types are severely hindered by taking a Choice Scarf from Trick Tapu Fini variants.

Electric- and Grass-types: The metagame has a plethora of offensive Electric- and Grass-types like Tapu Koko, Zeraora, Arctozolt, Rillaboom, and Kartana, all of which outspeed and deal significant damage to Tapu Fini.

Chip Damage: Because Tapu Fini is fully reliant on Leftovers and the weak Draining Kiss for recovery, it can be quickly worn down by entry hazards and U-turn and Future Sight from opposing Pokemon like Landorus-T, Tornadus-T, Tapu Lele, and Slowbro, especially if it is running a Choice Scarf set. There are a number of Pokemon that threaten Tapu Fini's Leftovers with Knock Off, including Toxapex and Tornadus-T, the former of which can usually act as a hard counter to Tapu Fini thanks to its typing and access to moves like Haze and Poison Jab.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Description

With Calm Mind, Tapu Fini bolsters its already high Special Defense, helping it better check Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Dragapult after a couple of boosts. Scald can deter Rillaboom and Kartana from switching in with the threat of a burn. Draining Kiss helps keep Tapu Fini from being worn down, especially if it has lost its Leftovers. Taunt blocks the likes of Blissey and Toxapex from using healing moves in front of Tapu Fini, letting it use these Pokemon as setup fodder, while preventing Pokemon like Volcarona and Clefable from setting up in front of it. 64 Speed EVs allow Tapu Fini to outspeed Tyranitar, with the rest invested to maximize Tapu Fini's physical bulk.

Team Options

Tapu Fini fits well on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its ability to check a variety of offensive threats. Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus-T are necessary to check Electric-types like Zeraora and Tapu Koko, while Zapdos and Tornadus-T are appreciated to help against Rillaboom and Kartana. All of these in turn benefit from Tapu Fini being able to handle Weavile. Tapu Fini also struggles against Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Melmetal, so teammates like Magnezone and Heatran that can take care of them are needed. Additionally, Tapu Fini does not appreciate taking Knock Off because it relies on the weak Draining Kiss for recovery, so teammates that are less reliant on their items like Skarmory and Corviknight can be considered.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Description

Choice Scarf Tapu Fini acts as speed control that can also switch into threats like Urshifu-R and Barraskewda in the short-term. Trick has wonderful disruptive potential against passive switch-ins like Ferrothorn, Toxapex, and Gastrodon by limiting their move choices if the speed control of Choice Scarf is not needed. The final moveslot has a number of options. Taunt is the move of choice, as it prevents the likes of Ferrothorn and Blissey from setting up entry hazards or inflicting status with Thunder Wave or Toxic once Misty Terrain is inactive. This also amplifies the power of Trick, as Pokemon will be forced to Struggle if they are Taunted when Choice-locked. Calm Mind is a viable alternative that turns Tapu Fini into a bulky setup sweeper after using Trick. 252 Special Attack EVs allow Tapu Fini to OHKO Dragapult and Weavile, two of the main Pokemon that this set seeks to revenge kill. 216 Speed EVs are used to outspeed Jolly Dragonite at +1, while the remaining EVs are invested into HP to maximize bulk.

Team Options

Choice Scarf Tapu Fini fits well on teams that desire speed control that can also provide defensive utility. Wallbreakers that appreciate it forcing out the likes of Dragapult and Weavile make for good teammates, such as Blacephalon and Kartana. Kartana particularly appreciates Tapu Fini's Misty Terrain warding off status like burn from Scald and paralysis from Static. As Choice Scarf Tapu Fini does not have the bulk of its defensive sets, it requires a defensive backbone behind it to stave off opposing threats. Ferrothorn is a fantastic partner, as it can act as a Knock Off absorber against the dangerous Weavile as well as be the first line of defense against threats like Barraskewda and Crawdaunt. It can also wear down Tapu Fini's switch-ins, such as Gastrodon and opposing Ferrothorn, with Spikes. Ground-types like Landorus-T and Garchomp can check Electric-types like Zapdos and Zeraora, and they reduce pressure on Tapu Fini to switch into Heatran. Much like Kartana, Garchomp enjoys Misty Terrain preventing it from being statused by moves like Scald, Will-O-Wisp, and Toxic. Finally, switch-ins to faster Choice Scarf users that can threaten Tapu Fini are necessary due to Tapu Fini's middling Speed tier. Tornadus-T and Zapdos can stave off Grass-types like Rillaboom and Kartana while providing Defog support, which is important, as Choice Scarf Tapu Fini lacks any form of recovery. Heatran is a sturdy Tapu Lele and Blacephalon check that can also annoy Weavile if running Flame Body. Moreover, it can wear down Gastrodon with Toxic and threaten out Ferrothorn, helping Tapu Fini break through these checks. Attackers that benefit from Trick disrupting shared checks also make for good teammates, with Zapdos appreciating Gastrodon being locked into moves other than Toxic and Weavile enjoying setup opportunities afforded by Toxapex and Ferrothorn being locked into Recover and Spikes, respectively.

Whirlpool Trapper.description:
Set Description

By utilizing the combination of Whirlpool, Nature's Madness, and Taunt, Tapu Fini becomes an incredibly dangerous stallbreaker that can trap bulky Pokemon like Toxapex, Blissey, Clefable, Slowbro, and Slowking; stop them from healing; and force their removal from the game. Nature's Madness also has the benefit of punishing checks like Melmetal and Ferrothorn with heavy chip damage should they attempt to come in and force Tapu Fini out. Moonblast rounds out the moveset, allowing Tapu Fini to finish off these bulky Pokemon after putting them within KO range and check Dragapult, Garchomp, and Urshifu-R. The given EV spread allows Tapu Fini to avoid a 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Dragapult's Shadow Ball after Stealth Rock and outpace Adamant Tyranitar, while the rest of its EVs are dumped into HP and Defense. Leftovers is necessary to extend Tapu Fini's longevity, allowing it to continue sticking around to handle the aforementioned targets.

Team Options

Tapu Fini is a valuable asset on offense and bulky offense teams, where it is tasked with breaking holes open and forcibly removing bulky targets for the benefit of its wallbreaking and sweeping teammates. Blacephalon and Volcarona greatly benefit from the removal of Blissey and Toxapex and Dragapult and Urshifu-R being forced out; the former becomes a much more menacing wallbreaker, while the latter sweeps through and cleans up the opposition without much standing in its way. A multitude of grounded physical attackers like Blaziken, Kartana, Weavile, and Garchomp synergize very well with Tapu Fini's Misty Terrain support, protecting them from status ailments like paralysis from Zapdos's Static and burns from Heatran's Flame Body and Toxapex and Slowbro's Scald. Much like Volcarona, they, except for Kartana, are also protected from Toxic from all of these Pokemon. Additionally, they can set up on targets weakened by Nature's Madness, such as Swords Dance Kartana taking advantage of the setup opportunities provided against a weakened Ferrothorn that cannot do much back in return. These physical attackers also benefit from Tapu Fini pressuring and removing their answers like Slowbro and Toxapex for Blaziken; Fire-types for Kartana; Buzzwole and Urshifu-R for Weavile; and Corviknight and Weavile for Garchomp. Weavile appreciates Tapu Fini weakening shared checks like Melmetal and Ferrothorn for it to clean up later in the game. In return, Blaziken takes on Grass-types that give Tapu Fini major trouble, like Rillaboom and Kartana, while Garchomp handles Electric-types like Zapdos and Tapu Koko. Dragonite also forms a strong partnership with Tapu Fini; while it can't take advantage of Misty Terrain due to its Flying typing, it makes up for this by easily handling the likes of Rillaboom and Kartana, and in return, Tapu Fini takes on Corviknight, Weavile, and Dragapult. Tapu Fini handling the latter also allows Dragonite to more easily run an Adamant nature over Jolly. Pivots like Tornadus-T, Landorus-T, Zeraora, and Zapdos are also beneficial, as they grant Tapu Fini free entry with U-turn and Volt Switch. Additionally, Tornadus-T and Zapdos check Rillaboom and Kartana and keep entry hazards off the field with Defog, while Landorus-T and Zeraora handle Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Zapdos and block Volt Switch thanks to their Electric immunity. Heatran sets up Stealth Rock, utilizes its solid special bulk to check Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele and make progress against them, aids Tapu Fini in pressuring Blissey and Toxapex, and benefits from Tapu Fini handling offensive Water-types like Urshifu-R, Barraskewda, and Crawdaunt.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

A Whirlpool set with Choice Scarf and Trick over Taunt can also revenge kill Pokemon such as Ash-Greninja and Mega Medicham, trapping foes after it sheds its Choice Scarf with Trick, but it is much less reliable at trapping. The EV spread on the Choice Scarf set can be altered according to what the team needs; Tapu Fini can run maximum Special Attack if the team needs a more solid revenge killer to OHKO Landorus-T, Mega Medicham, and Gliscor, or it can run more Special Defense investment to better check Ash-Greninja and Heatran.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type Coverage: Bulky Grass-types such as Tangrowth, Ferrothorn, Amoonguss, and Tapu Bulu can reliably switch into Tapu Fini and force it out, and can they easily recover off the damage dealt. However, they all fear losing their item to Knock Off, and Tapu Bulu doesnt want to switch into a Scald, fearing a burn. Offensive Grass-types such as Serperior, Rillaboom, and Kartana all force it out, but the latter two are threatened by a Scald burn and don't appreciate a Moonblast, so they can't switch in as easily. Grass-type coverage from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and Manaphy also greatly threatens it.

Electric-types and Electric-type Coverage: Pokemon such as Zeraora, Magnezone, and Tapu Koko all can threaten Tapu Fini out with their STAB moves, but they can get easily worn down by switching in multiple times. Zapdos is especially a good switch-in due to it easily recovering off the damage dealt to later pressure Tapu Fini out again. Electric-type coverage moves from the likes of Clefable, Blaziken, and Victini can also force it out.

Poison-types: Poison-types such as Mega Venusaur, Galarian Slowking and Gengar all pressure Tapu Fini consistently with their STAB moves, although Gengar struggles to switch in repeatedly due to its frailty, and Galarian Slowking fears being rendered much less effective by a Knock Off.

Chip Damage: Due to Tapu Fini’s lack of reliable recovery, chip damage can easily rack up, eventually wearing it down into range of the likes of Greninja and Heatran. Since Tapu Fini is going be removing opposing entry hazards, it also has to worry about switching into them, worsening its longevity as the game goes on.

Strong Wallbreakers: Strong wallbreakers such as Z-Move Heatran, Mega Medicham, and Tapu Lele can dent Tapu Fini massively, greatly reducing its lifespan.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Tapu Fini is a terrifying late-game sweeper, using its immense bulk, typing, and ability to summon Misty Terrain to find multiple setup opportunities throughout the match. It also checks offensive behemoths such as Ash-Greninja and Heatran. However, due to its low Speed stat and time needed to become a huge threat, it is prone to being revenge killed. Calm Mind, besides boosting Tapu Fini's offense, makes it harder for special attackers to revenge kill. Taunt stops Toxapex's Haze from removing its boosts, as well as denying recovery from the likes of Chansey, Blissey, Clefable, and Toxapex. It also blocks status moves after its Misty Terrain wears off. Scald allows Tapu Fini to effectively check Heatran, as well as threatening burns on Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Rillaboom, and Tapu Bulu. Draining Kiss allows Tapu Fini to consistently recover HP alongside its Leftovers while wearing down the foe, as well as outhealing the likes of Chansey and Blissey. The given EV spread lets it outspeed Modest Heatran.

Tapu Fini fits best on bulky offense teams that appreciate having a sturdy wincon as well as a check to the likes of Heatran and Ash-Greninja. Pokemon that appreciate Tapu Fini pressuring bulkier teams work well with it, including Pokemon that can pressure offense such as Mega Lopunny and Zeraora. Pokemon that can wear down or remove bulky Grass-types such as Tangrowth, Amoonguss, and Ferrothorn are great partners, such as Mega Latios and Heatran. Mega Medicham, Ash-Greninja, and Rillaboom break holes in opposing teams to pave the way for Tapu Fini to clean. Magnezone works great with Tapu Fini due to it removing the likes of Ferrothorn for it. Pokemon such as Mega Mawile and Gliscor that appreciate Heatran and Ash-Greninja being pressured are also good partners.

Defog.description:
Tapu Fini is an excellent Defogger that pressures and beats a large number of entry hazard setters such as Heatran, Landorus-T, and Kommo-o. Its amazing typing and multiple utility moves in Taunt and Nature's Madness, as well as its great bulk, allow it to be a sturdy check to terrifying threats such as Ash-Greninja, Weavile, and Heatran as well. However, due to its lack of consistent recovery and its vulnerability to all entry hazards, it is easily worn down throughout the match. Scald allows Tapu Fini to threaten burns on the likes of Tapu Bulu, Landorus-T, Corviknight, and Rillaboom, as well as pressuring Heatran consistently. Nature's Madness greatly chips its switch-ins like Amoonguss and Ferrothorn for its teammates. Taunt lets Tapu Fini prevent Pokemon such as Ferrothorn from setting up entry hazards in front of it and the likes of Mega Scizor and Clefable from setting up on it; Taunt also lets it force out Pokemon like Toxapex and Slowking in combination with Nature's Madness. Knock Off is another option that can punish common switch-ins such as Tangrowth and Galarian Slowking by removing their items, as well as removing Leftovers, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Black Sludge from the likes of Toxapex, Amoonguss, Slowking, and Tapu Bulu, greatly reducing their longevity and effectiveness. The given EV spread allows Tapu Fini to live a boosted Acrobatics from Hawlucha and OHKO it back, as well as outspeeding and 2HKOing offensive Heatran with Scald, with the remaining EVs in Special Defense to check the likes of Heatran and Ash-Greninja better.

Tapu Fini fits on bulky offense teams, which appreciate it checking big offensive threats such as Heatran and Ash-Greninja, as well as providing good Defog support. Physical attackers that fear being burnt such as Kartana, Garchomp, Mega Scizor, and Melmetal, as well as Pokemon generally susceptible to status like Tangrowth, Volcarona, and Mega Tyranitar, synergize well with Tapu Fini due to Misty Terrain protecting them from status. Due to Tapu Fini being weak to Electric- and Grass-type moves, Pokemon that can take these attacks such as Gliscor, Ferrothorn, Zapdos, and Mega Latias are solid teammates. In return, Tapu Fini takes the Ice- and Fire-type attacks directed at them. Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny and Mega Scizor that appreciate its reliable Defogging are also good partners. Lastly, it checking offensive behemoths like Greninja and Heatran makes Volcarona and Gliscor stellar partners.

Whirlpool Trapper.description:
Whirlpool Tapu Fini aims to trap and KO Pokemon that cannot really hurt it such as Toxapex, Clefable lacking Thunder, Heatran, and Slowbro with the combination of Whirlpool, Nature's Madness, Taunt, and status immunity from Misty Terrain. It also retains the ability to check threats like Heatran and Ash-Greninja. However, it is prone to being worn down due to its lack of reliable recovery and the chip damage it takes when trying to eliminate these Pokemon. Taunt prevents Pokemon like Clefable, Toxapex, Slowbro, and Blissey from using recovery moves, letting Tapu Fini efficiently KO them after trapping them. Moonblast is run to effectively check Ash-Greninja and Hydreigon. The given Speed EVs let it outspeed Modest Heatran, with the other non-HP EVs dumped in Special Defense to optimally deal with threats like Ash-Greninja.

Tapu Fini fits best on bulky offense teams, where it partners up with offensive Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny, Ash-Greninja, Hawlucha, and Weavile that appreciate it trapping checks such as Toxapex and Clefable. Tapu Fini hates entry hazards, so Defoggers like Corviknight and Kartana make for good teammates. Tapu Fini is vulnerable to Grass-types like Rillaboom, Serperior, and Kartana, so good checks to them like Tangrowth, Mega Scizor, and Corviknight are great partners. In return, Tapu Fini checks Heatran for them. Pokemon like Gliscor, Amoonguss, and Galarian Slowking can check Electric-types like Tapu Koko, Magnezone, and Zeraoara for it. Lastly, physical threats appreciate Misty Terrain, like Mega Medicham, Mega Mawile, and Weavile.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Tapu Fini can outspeed and revenge kill threats like Mega Gyarados and non-Choice Scarf Kartana. While Tapu Fini is traditionally known for other roles, it has a decent offensive presence thanks to its great defensive typing and good bulk, which allow it to check a variety of threats like Mega Lopunny, Heatran, Weavile, and Ash-Greninja to an extent. Misty Surge protects the team from status moves such as Thunder Wave from Clefable and Toxic from Toxapex. Hydro Pump is Tapu Fini's strongest move and chunks Gliscor, Heatran, and Landorus-T. However, Surf is a more reliable option and still does decent damage. Defog allows Tapu Fini to clear entry hazards, but it clears Misty Terrain too. Taunt is an option over Defog to further mess with the defensive Pokemon mentioned, denying them healing or preventing them from setting entry hazards. Hidden Power Fire can also be used to 2HKO Ferrothorn and better revenge kill Kartana. Trick debilitates defensive switch-ins to Tapu Fini such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Clefable. The EV spread allows Tapu Fini to survive a +2 Acrobatics from Hawlucha, guarantees an OHKO on Greninja with Moonblast, and still outspeeds +1 Mega Gyarados.

Tapu Fini fits best on more offensive teams, as they appreciate it acting as a defensive switch-in to top threats while also being a respectable revenge killer. Pokemon like Weavile, Mega Lopunny, and Kartana that fear Scald burns from the likes of Toxapex are ideal teammates, since they enjoy Misty Terrain. Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, and Heatran that can cover Tapu Fini's weakness to opposing Mega Scizor, Kartana, and Serperior make wonderful teammates. In return, Tapu Fini can remove Ash-Greninja and Mega Lopunny for them. Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T, are amazing partners as they cover Tapu Fini's weakness to Electric and appreciate it switching into Ice- and Water-types like Ash-Greninja and Weavile. Setup sweepers such as Quiver Dance Volcarona, Calm Mind Mega Latias, and Swords Dance Landorus-T appreciate Tapu Fini ruining shared checks such as Blissey and Skarmory via Trick. This Tapu Fini set lacks defensive investment, so it can't check many Pokemon it wants to long-term such as Ash-Greninja and Heatran. Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Garchomp can provide extra insurance against these Pokemon.

cap.comments:
Other Options

Protect can be used on a Defog set over Taunt to mitigate Tapu Fini's lack of reliable recovery by giving it another turn of Leftovers, but it also gives the opponent a free turn. The Whirlpool set can run Knock Off over Moonblast to remove Toxapex's Shed Shell, Galarian Slowking's Assault Vest, and other walls’ Leftovers, but it makes Tapu Fini too passive otherwise. A bulkier EV spread of 248 HP / 44 SpD / 216 Spe can be used on the Choice Scarf set if there is another teammate who can check Cawmodore.

Checks and Counters

Galarian Slowking: Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can take any of Tapu Fini's attacks and threaten it out with Sludge Bomb and Future Sight. Losing Assault Vest to Trick or Knock Off makes it much easier to deal with, however, as it dislikes being Choice-locked .

Ferrothorn: Ferrothorn can take Tapu Fini's attacks and either set entry hazards, recover its health back with Leech Seed, or threaten Tapu Fini with Power Whip. It does not appreciate receiving a Choice Scarf through Trick, however.

Electric-types: Zeraora, Tapu Koko, and Krilowatt can all outspeed non-Choice Scarf sets and threaten to 2HKO Tapu Fini with their attacks while always surviving any hit from Choice Scarf sets and KOing back.

Grass-types: Kartana, Rillaboom, and Jumbao can all force Tapu Fini out with their Grass-type attacks and can stomach any of its attacks. Rillaboom has to be careful of being burned by Scald, though.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Hydro Pump allows Tapu Fini to OHKO Cawmodore after it has used Belly Drum. Trick allows Tapu Fini to cripple walls such as Slowking, Ferrothorn, and Blissey as well as slower setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Dragonite and Geomancy Necturna, locking them into their setup move. Taunt stops Clefable and opposing Tapu Fini from setting up after it has already removed its Choice Scarf with Trick. Defog is an option over Taunt on teams that desperately need entry hazard control. 224 Speed EVs with a Timid nature and Choice Scarf allow Tapu Fini to outspeed Jolly Dragonite and Blaziken at +1 as well as Modest +2 Necturna. Maximum Special Attack EVs allow Tapu Fini to OHKO Dragapult with Moonblast, with the rest of the EVs put into HP and Speed to survive +6 Cawmodore's Bullet Punch after switching into Stealth Rock twice and outspeed Modest Choice Scarf Tapu Lele.

This set role compresses a revenge killer and check to wallbreakers such as Weavile, Urshifu-R, and Garchomp. Teammates that appreciate Tapu Fini luring in and crippling walls such as Galarian Slowking, Blissey, and Ferrothorn such as Jumbao and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T make for excellent partners, with both of them acting as good checks to Rillaboom. Krilowatt and Tapu Koko can pressure Water-types such as Slowking for Tapu Fini and pivot into it to deal with Blissey. Ground-types such as Colossoil, Landorus-T, and Garchomp can take on Electric-type attacks for Tapu Fini and appreciate it checking Weavile, Urshifu-R, and Arghonaut.

Utility.description:
Set Details

The combination of Whirlpool, Nature's Madness, and Taunt allows Tapu Fini to trap opposing walls such as Toxapex, Slowking, and Blissey. Moonblast is a mandatory move to check Urshifu-R and Weavile while effectively threatening out Dragon-types. Nature's Madness can deal hefty damage against the aforementioned bulky foes and punishes switch-ins such as Galarian Slowking, Assault Vest Melmetal, and Ferrothorn. Taunt shuts down Toxapex, Slowking, and Blissey from recovering their HP or pivoting out with Teleport. If trapping foes is not a priority, Defog in conjunction with Scald can be run over Whirlpool and Nature's Madness, respectively; this allows Tapu Fini to act as a serviceable entry hazard remover for its team, gives it a more reliable Water-type STAB option, and lets it threaten to burn foes unaffected by Misty Terrain such as Zapdos, Corviknight, and Tornadus-T. Knock Off can be run over Defog to displace foes' items. These EVs allow Tapu Fini to avoid being 3HKOed by Choice Band Urshifu-R's Close Combat and Choice Specs Dragapult's Shadow Ball after switching into Stealth Rock.

Teammates that appreciate Toxapex and Slowbro being removed such as Weavile and Urshifu-R pair up nicely with this set. Similarly, Jumbao and Dragapult greatly appreciate Blissey being gone. Ground-types such as Colossoil and Landorus-T can take Electric-type attacks thrown Tapu Fini's way and force Galarian Slowking out, while Tornadus-T and Corviknight help deal with Rillaboom and Jumbao and can bring Tapu Fini in safely with U-turn. Scizor also has great defensive synergy with Tapu Fini, taking on Ferrothorn, Melmetal, and Kartana, while Tapu Fini deals with Astrolotl and Heatran nicely.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Details

Taunt allows Tapu Fini to shut down passive foes such as Blissey and Toxapex and set up in front of them. It additionally prevents foes like Slowking, Slowbro, and Blissey from safely pivoting into a revenge killer with Teleport. Scald is weaker than Hydro Pump but punishes switch-ins such as Landorus-T, Rillaboom, and Zapdos by threatening to burn them. Draining Kiss keeps Tapu Fini healthy, but Moonblast can be considered for its higher damage output. 140 Speed EVs allow Tapu Fini to outspeed Timid Magnezone and defensive Landorus-T. Investment in Defense is preferred, as Tapu Fini boosts its Special Defense with Calm Mind.

Magnezone can trap and remove Ferrothorn, Calm Mind Tapu Fini's greatest counter. Ground-types like Landorus-T, Hippowdon, and Colossoil can deal with Electric-types as well as Galarian Slowking. In return, Tapu Fini can switch into Urshifu-R and Weavile for them. Tornadus-T can help deal with offensive Grass-types such as Kartana and Rillaboom, threaten Ferrothorn with Heat Wave, and remove Galarian Slowking's Assault Vest with Knock Off, making it a fantastic partner.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a newly introduced Pokemon. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: S Rank

Reserved for the best Pokemon in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon are usually able to perform a variety of roles effectively, or can just do one extremely well. Their use has low risk involved and high reward exerted. Pokemon in this rank have very few flaws that are patched up by numerous positive traits.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Calm Mind.description:
• With an excellent typing and ability to set up Misty Terrain, Tapu Fini is the premier bulky Water-type of the metagame.

  • Surf is the obvious reliable choice for a Water STAB, but Scald can burn floating Pokemon, and others when Misty Terrain expires.

  • Moonblast is Tapu Fini's most reliable Fairy-type STAB. Draining Kiss isn't nearly as powerful, but it restores enough health that it can give Tapu Fini an extra edge against less defensive threats.

  • Taunt is important for shutting down more defensive threats such as Hippowdon, Leech Seed Celesteela, and opposing Tapu Fini.

  • Substitute on the flip side, does a great job of punishing more offensive Tapu Fini switch-ins.

  • Nature's Madness reliably damages switch-ins, even if it isn't boosted by Calm Mind.

Items

  • Leftovers provides a reliable amount of healing while it sets up Calm Mind.

  • Sitrus Berry and berries such as Iapapa Berry give Tapu Fini a quicker burst of recovery, which can improve its match-up against more offensive threats.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 100 Def / 156 Spe Bold: This EV spread allows Tapu Fini to outspeed up to Timid Celesteela, letting it get an important Taunt in before Celesteela attempts to stall with Leech Seed. If needed, more EVs can be shifted to Defense if Celesteela is handled by the team. The rest goes into Defense to increase Tapu Fini's ability to set up Calm Mind.

  • 252 HP / 100 SpA / 156 Spe Modest: This EV spread makes Tapu Fini a better offensive threat while Dynamaxed, notably OHKOing offensive Dynamaxed Landorus-T with a boosted Max Geyser after Stealth Rock damage.

Choice Attacker.description:
• Tapu Fini may not seem strong, but it makes a shockingly capable offensive threat due to its typing and good coverage.

  • Ice Beam is Tapu Fini's best option against a wide variety of threats, mainly Grass- and Flying-types such as Rillaboom and Thundurus-T. Nature's Madness on the other hand, provides reliable damage output against unfavorable switch-ins for Choice Scarf Tapu Fini.

  • Trick is essential, allowing Tapu Fini to cripple bulky Pokemon such as Porygon2 and Celesteela.

  • Modest is the prefered nature for the most damage output possible, but Timid does gurantee that Tapu Fini can outspeed Dracovish, and Dragapult provided that Tapu Fini is holding a Choice Scarf.

Items

  • Choice Specs give Tapu Fini much more power than usual, making it into an effective bulky special attacker.

  • Choice Scarf is a valuable alternative to outspeed major threats such as Landorus-T and Nihilego, and tends to punish defensive Pokemon more when Tricked onto them.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe Modest or Timid: This EV spread gives Tapu Fini the best combination of power and Speed.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 Spe Modest: This is Tapu Fini's bulkiest offensive spread for Choice Specs.

  • 100 HP / 252 SpA / 156 Spe Modest: This spread ensures that Tapu Fini outspeeds Timid Celesteela, while giving it decent bulk.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

A defensive set with support moves like Defog, Knock Off, and Taunt, while viable, is outclassed by Pokemon with recovery such as Corviknight and Ho-Oh. A trapping set without Choice Scarf featuring Whirlpool and Nature's Madness can whittle down passive Pokemon, however a lot of these carry pivot moves, in particular U-Turn, and Tapu Fini's weak offensive presence means even offensive threats like Tapu Koko can switch in and force it out. Iron Defense and Stored Power are alternate options on the boosting set, however that would make Tapu Fini vulnerable to more Pokemon like Heatran.

Checks and Counters

Offensive Electric-type Pokemon: Electric-types like Zeraora and Tapu Koko threaten to deal massive damage to Tapu Fini provided that it hasn't boosted enough. However, they struggle to switch in directly if Tapu Fini is a Special Attack receiver.

Grass-type Pokemon: Defensive Grass-type Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Ferrothorn have no trouble beating Tapu Fini one-on-one. To a lesser extent, Assault Vest Tangrowth can beat Tapu Fini if it switches in directly on the turn it first uses Calm Mind. Regardless, they still need to watch out for Trick, which can cripple them. Offensive Grass-types like Rillaboom and Kartana also force it out, however they can't switch in repeatedly, especially Rillaboom, as it is vulnerable to a Scald burn.

Poison-type Pokemon: Galarian Slowbro and Galarian Slowking take little damage from Tapu Fini's attacks and can hit hard back in return. They also sometimes carry Black Sludge, which punishes Tapu Fini's Trick.

Fast Trick and Taunt: Calm Mind variants need multiple boosts to truly function so Taunt or Trick from a faster Pokemon can stop Tapu Fini's sweep. Examples include Slowking in the Speed slot and Mewtwo.

Calm Mind (HP, Special Attack).description:
Calm Mind Tapu Fini is a dangerous wincon capable of setting up on passive Pokemon such as Giratina and Skarmory. It also has great bulk, especially if it receives HP, and a fantastic defensive typing, allowing it to check common attackers like Urshifu-R and Weavile. Calm Mind gradually boosts Tapu Fini's Special Defense, allowing it to shrug off weak special hits from the likes of Slowking and Clefable. Draining Kiss is preferred over Moonblast since it increases Tapu Fini's longevity and helps keep it out of range of being revenge killed by faster threats like Tapu Koko and Rayquaza. Taunt stops status effects, opposing setup, and phazing attempts aimed at Tapu Fini. Scald discourages Pokemon not protected by Misty Terrain from switching in and risking a burn, such as Rillaboom and Tornadus-T. 44 Speed EVs allow Tapu Fini to outrun common base 90 Speed Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, the aforementioned Giratina, and their Speed receivers.

Tapu Fini fits best on bulkier builds that want a solid late-game wincon. Gods with a high HP stat like Yveltal and Ho-Oh make for great partners. They can also handle Grass-types that Tapu Fini struggles against such as Ferrothorn and Amoonguss. In return, Tapu Fini walls Weavile. Alternatively, a Special Attack donation from Kyurem-W or Dialga lessens the number of boosts needed to overwhelm the opposing team, which comes in handy against Clear Smog Gastrodon. Landorus-T also has great synergy with Tapu Fini, as it checks various Electric-type Pokemon such as Zeraora and Dracozolt. Entry hazards, especially Toxic Spikes, hinder Tapu Fini's ability to switch in, so entry hazard removal like Excadrill's Rapid Spin and Corviknight's Defog are necessary. Poison-type Pokemon such as Nihilego and Galarian Slowking beat Tapu Fini one-on-one if it doesn't have enough boosts, which sturdy special walls like Ho-Oh and Assault Vest Reuniclus can take on. If Gastrodon is a concern, offensive Tornadus-T invites it in and removes its Leftovers, allowing Tapu Fini to beat it. Magnezone traps and eliminates Ferrothorn, which is a common Tapu Fini answer, as well as Corviknight to prevent it from pivoting out against Tapu Fini.

Choice Scarf (Special Attack).description:
With a Choice Scarf, Tapu Fini outspeeds Pheromosa and its Speed receivers, making it a nice revenge killer when combined with a better Special Attack stat. Moonblast is its preferred Fairy STAB attack that deals great damage to many dangerous Ubers such as Yveltal and Kyurem-W, as well as frail receivers like Zeraora and Alolan Persian. Scald is more reliable and can threaten a burn on unprotected switch-ins such as Rillaboom and Corviknight, however Hydro Pump is still a usable alternative to increase its damage output. Trick cripples common defensive walls that can easily take Tapu Fini's attacks such as Gastrodon and Tangrowth. Taunt works well in tandem with Trick to deny recovery moves like Gastrodon's Recover and also prevent Slowbro and Slowking from using Teleport and gaining momentum. Whirlpool can surprise defensive Pokemon and potentially let Tapu Fini KO them should they lock themselves into an unfavorable move like entry hazards or Defog. Defog is another option if the team needs an entry hazard control option, which also helps Scald by removing Misty Terrain. While Misty Surge negates Tapu Fini's ability to spread burn, it also allows Tapu Fini to be played more aggressively by switching in directly against a predicted status inducing move or Rest.

Choice Scarf Tapu Fini finds its place on bulky offense builds that enjoy its role compression. Gods with a high Special Attack stat like Yveltal and Dialga are great partners to maximize Tapu Fini's revenge kill capabilities. Yveltal and Dialga also have great defensive synergy with Tapu Fini, as the former can take on dangerous Grass-types like Rillaboom and Kartana while the latter can check Electric-types such as Zapdos. In turn, Tapu Fini can check Weavile and Pheromosa for them. Tangrowth handles a myriad of Grass- and Electric-type Pokemon Tapu Fini struggles with, and it also appreciates Misty Terrain to avoid status effects. Magnezone can capitalize on defensive Steel-types that have already been given a Choice Scarf, and also traps Ferrothorn, which is one of Tapu Fini's best counters. Bulky Pokemon with a setup option also like Misty Terrain to set up safely, which makes Kartana and Buzzwole great partners. If Tapu Fini doesn't run Defog, a teammate with an entry hazard removal option like Excadrill or Rotom-H is necessary.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Toxic is another option on defensive sets to hit opposing Tapu Fini, Blissey, and Desolate Land Pokemon such as Moltres and Cinderace. Eject Button is a great option on offensive teams to grab momentum. Hydro Pump can be run on Choice Scarf sets to pose a larger threat offensively and notably OHKOes Talonflame, but gives up burn chance, accuracy, and PP. Triage is an option that makes Tapu Fini a bulky setup wincon, but its 95 Special Attack makes it weak even when boosted.

Checks and Counters

Desolate Land Fire-types: Desolate Land users such as Moltres, Heatran, and Cinderace are not threatened by Tapu Fini's STAB moves. Offensive Heatran gets a special mention because it doesn't mind its item being removed by Tapu Fini in exchange for being able to trap and KO with Magma Storm. Cinderace either can pivot into a teammate or carry Gunk Shot to 2HKO Tapu Fini. Volcarona can use Quiver Dance repeatedly in the face of Tapu Fini, and offensive variants can 2HKO even with unboosted Solar Beam or Giga Drain. However, Knock Off or Trick from Tapu Fini can greatly cripple these Pokemon by removing their items of choice.

Grass-types: Zarude, Dhelmise, and Tapu Bulu can all threaten to outspeed and OHKO Tapu Fini.

Electric-types: Tapu Koko and Zapdos both threaten Tapu Fini with their strong STAB attacks, though they cannot switch into its attacks very easily.

Trick users: Although they would rather not be burned by Scald, Mew, Jirachi, and opposing Tapu Fini can run a Choice Scarf + Trick set of their own and thus switch into Tapu Fini with relative ease.

Regenerator Pivot.description:
Tapu Fini's access to utility moves such as Defog, Haze, and Knock Off allows it to excel as a defensive pivot to a wide array of attackers. The combination of Moonblast and Knock Off in particular enables Tapu Fini to cripple Heavy Duty Boots and Assault Vest users while retaining a strong Fairy-type STAB move. Tapu Fini's typing and bulk allow it to serve as a blanket check to prominent physical attackers like Garchomp, Barraskewda, and Terrakion; the use of Rocky Helmet serves as a means for Tapu Fini to switch in and passively limit the amount of times they can attack successfully. Leftovers allows Tapu Fini to slightly increase its passive recovery so that it doesn't have to switch immediately versus opposing attackers. Tapu Fini also serves as one of the most effective counters to Barraskewda, as it can easily restore chip damage from Flip Turn with Regenerator while punishing Barrskewda with Rocky Helmet. Because common Stealth Rock users such as Swampert and Garchomp don't tend to carry moves that are immediately threatening to Tapu Fini, it's able to Defog Stealth Rock away consistently with the option of also removing potential Swords Dance boosts or threatening to burn with Scald. Tapu Fini also retains the ability to check setup sweepers in general: Quiver Dance Volcarona for example can be dealt with to an extent by resetting its stat changes with Haze, but Tapu Fini is not the most reliable long-term answer to them. Knock Off can also be used to potentially remove useful items like Leftovers and Rocky Helmet from Pokemon that rely on them, making Tapu Fini a very versatile utility user.

Tapu Fini fits onto virtually any type of team; it can work on balance, offense, and even stall. Ground-types such as Swampert and Garchomp enjoy having Tapu Fini as a teammate because they cover for its weakness to Electric-type attacks and can make progress by going for Stealth Rock. Tapu Fini also largely benefits from teammates like Mandibuzz, Zapdos, and Moltres that can patch up its weakness to Grass-type attacks from common users such Volcarona, Tapu Bulu, and Zarude. It's also worth noting that despite being a Water-type, Tapu Fini struggles versus especially powerful Fire-type attacks from Pokemon like Choice Specs Volcanion and offensive Heatran, so Flash Fire and Primordial Sea users like Corviknight and Zapdos can alleviate the pressure for it.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf + Trick enhances Tapu Fini's defensive profile by making it an aggressively played revenge killer to offensive threats like Galarian Zapdos and Belly Drum Kommo-o, and it can also punish walls like Chansey, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight by severely limiting their utility. Having a Choice Scarf also allows Tapu Fini to play much more aggressively, as it can outspeed and threaten to KO foes like Galarian Zapdos and Terrakion. Moonblast and Scald are the preferred STAB options, dealing decent damage to or KOing everything Tapu Fini outspeeds, such as Barraskewda, Terrakion, and Talonflame; Scald also threatens to burn physical attackers that Tapu Fini outspeeds but cannot always beat one-on-one, such as Garchomp and Terrakion, and potentially punishes switch-ins like Blissey and Ferrothorn with extra chip damage from burn. Defog fills out the last slot by making sure Tapu Fini can still fulfill its role as one of best Defoggers in the tier. 8 Special Attack EVs are enough to OHKO Terrakion with Moonblast after it drops its defenses with Close Combat while 172 Speed EVs and Choice Scarf outpace Barraskewda; the rest of the EVs are dumped into HP and Defense to maximize bulk.

Tapu Fini primarily excels on bulky offense and balance teams, most notably as a check to strong physical attackers like Terrakion, Galarian Zapdos, and Tough Claws Zarude. Fire-types like Volcarona, Heatran, and Moltres all appreciate its ability to switch into Fighting- and Water-type attacks for them; their Desolate Land variants can then pivot into the Water-type Pokemon, overriding Primordial Sea. Bulky teammates like Blissey and Swampert pair well with Tapu Fini since it can switch into opposing Trick users like Mew, Jirachi, and Tapu Fini for them; in return, they check Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Zapdos. Other physically and specially defensive walls are important teammates: Dauntless Shield Mew, Intimidate Corviknight, RegenVest Jirachi, and Chansey are able to cover for Tapu Fini's lack of defensive investment. In particular, Intimidate Corviknight can switch into Grass-types like Zarude, Tapu Bulu, and Dhelmise for Tapu Fini. The versatility of Trick also means Tapu Fini can cripple common defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, for teammates like Pixilate Tapu Koko and Primordial Sea Barraskewda. Any viable entry hazard setter, such as Heatran, Ferrothorn, or Garchomp, capitalizes on Tapu Fini forcing frail offensive threats to switch by weakening them with entry hazard damage. Secondary entry hazard control measures, such as Rapid Spin Dhelmise and Defog Mandibuzz, are useful to alleviate pressure off of Tapu Fini to remove entry hazards, especially in matchups where it would rather keep its Choice Scarf and does not want to be Choice-locked into Defog.

doublesou.overview: Tapu Fini is an important asset of balance teams thanks to its defensive and offensive utility, which stems from its typing and ability. A Water / Fairy typing lets it easily take attacks from the likes of Heatran, Urshifu-R, and Volcanion, especially when considering its great natural bulk, which also allows it to take neutral attacks from the likes of Zygarde and Dragapult relatively well. In return, it can threaten the aforementioned Pokemon back with its STAB moves, giving it offensive utility as well. Misty Surge allows Tapu Fini to exert Terrain control, with Misty Terrain removing priority from Rillaboom's Grassy Glide and turning Necrozma's Expanding Force into a single target move. Misty Terrain also has the benefit of blocking Amoonguss's Spore and weakening Dragon-type moves from the likes of Dragapult and Kommo-o. Tapu Fini can take advantage of Pokemon it walls with a Calm Mind set, which lets it function as a dangerous wincon while maintaining its defensive and offensive utility. It can also take on a support role and utilize its great support movepool with moves like Heal Pulse and Nature's Madness. The Calm Mind set can take a bit to get going and relies on Leftovers to keep it healthy, while the support set is mostly passive. Further, both sets have a tendency to be and share a considerable weakness to one of the best Pokemon in the tier, Rillaboom. It threatens Tapu Fini with its powerful STAB Grassy Glide and resets Misty Terrain. Tapu Fini also has a tendency to get overwhelmed and chipped while it switches in to take resisted hits and change the terrain, a problem made worse by its lack of instant recovery. Pokemon that can handle Rillaboom make excellent partners for Tapu Fini. Kyurem-B and Incineroar in particular are great partners, as Tapu Fini beats Urshifu-R for them as well.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs and Choice Scarf can both exert immediate offensive pressure as well as potentially pick up a surprise KO. Trick is an option on both sets and can cripple its switch-ins like Rillaboom. However, both items are generally less consistent than the Calm Mind or Support sets. Muddy Water is an option over Nature's Madness on the support set to hit Heatran, but it has a lower overall damage output.

Calm Mind.description:
• Muddy Water and Moonblast allow Tapu Fini to effectively exert offensive pressure the opposing team. Moonblast is a single target move that hits many threats like Urshifu-R, Zygarde, and Kommo-o, while Muddy Water hits both targets and nails Pokemon that aren't too threatened by Moonblast like Heatran and Incineroar. However, both need boosts to become significantly threatening.

  • Tapu Fini can set up Calm Mind on a wide variety of Pokemon, like Volcanion and the aforementioned Urshifu-R and Heatran. Keep in mind that this will force a lot of attention on Tapu Fini, which can open up a hole for a teammate.

  • Protect allows Tapu Fini to accumulate Leftovers recovery safely, along with bringing in a teammate that can better support it, such as a Fake Out user like Zeraora.

  • Leftovers recovery is greatly appreciated, as it helps Tapu Fini switch in more, and it's likely to spend several turns on the field attacking or using Calm Mind.

  • Summoning Misty Terrain makes it considerably harder to prevent Tapu Fini from setting up via moves like Toxic.

  • 144 Special Attack EVs let Tapu Fini always OHKO Urshifu-R with Moonblast. The Defense EVs and Bold nature allow it to take more physical hits, which Calm Mind doesn't help against, such as Pokemon like Zygarde and Fusion Bolt Kyurem-B. EVs can be shifted from Defense to Speed to outspeed certain threats with speed control.

Support.description:
• Moonblast hits Fairy-weak Pokemon like Zygarde and Urshifu-R and can claim KOs against foes weakened by Nature's Madness.

  • Nature's Madness weakens foes for Tapu Fini or its teammates to pick off.

  • Icy Wind allows Tapu Fini to provide speed control for its teammates along with punishing and forcing switches.

  • Heal Pulse is particularly useful for Pokemon that lack recovery and and take a lot of hits like defensive Kyurem-B, along with setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Zygarde.

  • Taunt is also an option over ether Icy Wind or Heal Pulse, as it can prevent Trick Room, Tailwind, and other status moves from Pokemon slower than Tapu Fini. However, it can be useless against faster Tailwind setters like Zapdos.

  • Sitrus Berry's burst recovery is preferred over Leftovers's gradual recovery due to this set's tendency to repeatedly switch in-and-out of battle

  • Summoning Misty Terrain is great against Pokemon that rely on Terrain, like Necrozma and Rillaboom.

  • 144 Special Attack EVs allow Tapu Fini to always OHKO Urshifu-R with Moonblast. The Defense EVs and Bold nature are used to increase its lower Defense. EVs can be shifted to outspeed certain threats in Tailwind or after Icy Wind.

ubers.overview: Solgaleo's unique combination of Teleport and Future Sight coupled with its Steel typing gives it a defined role in Ubers as a defensive Steel-type that Magnezone cannot trap. Its decent bulk allows it to check both Xerneas and Eternatus. Unfortunately, Solgaleo is almost entirely outclassed by Necrozma-DM and other Steel-types like Ferrothorn, both offensively and defensively. Solgaleo has a niche on defensive teams for its ability to use Teleport to pivot against Magnezone, making it not lose to Xerneas teams with Magnezone, and it partners well with Kyogre and Marshadow thanks to Future Sight helping them break through their checks, most notably Eternatus.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Metal Burst allows Solgaleo to potentially OHKO Yveltal, which is especially useful if Solgaleo is paired with Calyrex-S. Choice Scarf Solgaleo could be used as an offensive Choice Scarf user that outspeeds Galarian Darmanitan and is not affected by Sticky Web. Dropping Sunsteel Strike makes Solgaleo a lot worse against Xerneas, but dropping anything else makes Solgaleo even more outclassed by Necrozma-DM.

Checks and Counters

Yveltal: Yveltal threatens to OHKO Solgaleo, is immune to Future Sight, and can also comfortably recover off Sunsteel Strike damage.

Ghost-types: Calyrex-S and Marshadow threaten to OHKO Solgaleo, while Lunala can comfortably take it on defensively, shrugging off all hits and spreading status to Solgaleo's teammates without fearing anything it can do in return.

Groudon: Groudon threatens to OHKO Solgaleo and can be difficult to switch into without wasting Future Sight.

Kyogre: Kyogre reduces Morning Sun recovery and forces Solgaleo out. It also resists Sunsteel Strike and can shrug off Future Sight damage comfortably.

Zygarde: Zygarde can set up on Solgaleo comfortably with both Dragon Dance and Coil sets, while Dragon Tail annoys Solgaleo attempting to pivot with Teleport.

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM can comfortably take on Solgaleo's attacks and threaten it with Knock Off and Earthquake while also setting entry hazards to limit switch-ins.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh immediately threatens Solgaleo and can keep itself healthy throughout the game thanks to Regenerator, and Whirlwind can disrupt Teleport.

FuturePort.description:
The combination of Future Sight and Teleport helps Solgaleo distinguish itself from Necrozma-DM. Future Sight hits targets like Eternatus and Buzzwole and is useful chip damage for many wallbreakers, while Teleport allows Solgaleo to safely bring in frail teammates. It is uncommon for Solgaleo to both set Future Sight and pivot with Teleport due to its weaknesses to common Pokemon like Yveltal, Groudon, and Kyogre, but both are useful tools to provide momentum to Solgaleo's team. Sunsteel Strike is required to check Xerneas.

When trying to execute a Future Sight-based strategy in Ubers, teammates that can force Yveltal and Necrozma-DM out are critical, since Yveltal is immune to Future Sight and Necrozma-DM resists both of Solgaleo's STAB options. Good partners for this include Groudon, Zygarde, and Kyogre. Phazers can help by preventing certain foes from absorbing Future Sight, so teammates like Dragon Tail Eternatus can be useful. Eternatus is especially useful in defensively answering Yveltal and not allowing Necrozma-DM to absorb Future Sight thanks to Dragon Tail. Kyogre, most notably Choice Scarf variants, really appreciates Future Sight support helping it break past Eternatus. Frailer wallbreakers, like Marshadow, Dracovish, and Rayquaza appreciate Solgaleo bringing them in safely and the additional damage that Future Sight provides on their checks. Other offensive pivots like Galarian Darmanitan, Yveltal, and Urshifu-S are also good teammates, potentially forming a good momentum-based offensive core.

Offensive Trick Room.description: • The given EV spread outspeeds max Speed neutral nature base 90s like Kyogre, Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Dialga.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This set is for one of the final Battle Stadium Singles metagames for this generation. If you feel there is anything wrong or missing, please post in this thread.

Bulky Calm Mind.description:
EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Bold: This maximizes Lunala's physical bulk for potentially stalling Zacian-C out with paralysis, while outspeeding paralyzed Choice Scarf Kyogre.

  • 252 HP / 52 SpA / 204 Spe with Timid: This spread allows Lunala to outspeed +Speed Nature base 90s such as Kyogre, Groudon, and Zekrom.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

A more offensive set with Calm Mind or Meteor Beam is possible; however, Tyranitar, Gastrodon, and Tangrowth still easily shrug off its attacks. It's also prone to getting revenge killed by the likes of Pangoro and Kartana.

Checks and Counters

Dark- and Ghost-type Pokemon and Coverage: Even with Shadow Shield up, Lunala is still preyed on by Yveltal, Dhelmise, and Alolan Persian. However, they all struggle to switch in safely against Lunala's attacks and status moves. Tyranitar shrugs off its attacks, deals heavy damage back, and can even use Rest to cure its status. Knock Off is extremely common on defensive and offensive Pokemon alike and also makes Lunala vulnerable to entry hazards.

Chip Damage: Lunala's ability to handle wallbreakers is severely limited without Shadow Shield. Alolan Ninetales and Tyranitar can set hail and sand to negate it, respectively, while most walls can inflict poison or burn. Many offensive threats can also pivot with U-turn or Volt Switch, punishing Lunala as it switches in without losing momentum.

Special Walls: Gastrodon, Tangrowth, and Ho-Oh have little to fear from Lunala outside of Toxic, although Ho-Oh has to watch out for the rare Meteor Beam. They can effectively force Lunala out with their own status.

Multi-hit Moves: While not common, multi-hit moves only suffer the damage penalty from Shadow Shield on the first hit. Shell Smash Cloyster and Choice Band Urshifu-R have the power to break through Lunala, although the latter risks a Speed tie. Scale Shot users like Rayquaza also have a chance to 2HKO Lunala, but they are inconsistent.

Defensive.description:
Lunala sports good bulk, a great ability, and a neutrality to most attacks, letting it blanket check numerous threats such as Rayquaza and Kyurem-W. Roost helps keep Shadow Shield intact, with Lunala's Speed meaning it can often go before these wallbreakers should they stay in. Depending on team choices, Lunala can either opt for Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave. The former immediately deters dangerous physical attackers such as Necrozma-DM and Kyurem-B, while the latter facilitates slower teammates like Obstagoon, Urshifu-R, and its Speed receivers. Hex's higher PP and synergy with Lunala's status spreading are usually preferred over Moongeist Beam's initial power. Ice Beam OHKOes Rayquaza and Landorus-T, while Toxic annoys Gastrodon, Tangrowth, and specially defensive Tyranitar, which don't mind its other options. Defog is another alternative for role compression. Heavy-Duty Boots ensures entry hazards don't break Shadow Shield.

With well-rounded stats, Lunala lends itself to bulky offense and balance teams. Common defensive Pokemon in Rotom-W, Tangrowth, Clefable, and Landorus-T all benefit from Lunala's defensive stat donations, and they bolster Lunala's Hex with their status moves. Tapu Koko, Tapu Fini, Celesteela, and Galarian Moltres make great use of its impressive Special Attack; its Speed donation, while not stellar, is enough to outpace Rayquaza and Kyurem-W, thus allowing slower teammates like Galarian Slowking and Dhelmise to pressure foes more easily. Dark-type teammates are necessary to cover for Lunala's weaknesses. Galarian Moltres and Bisharp check Dhelmise and benefit from Lunala spreading paralysis to make up for their middling Speed; defensive ones such as Mandibuzz and Alolan Persian also provide pivoting to make up for Lunala's predictability and momentum drain. Skarmory and Ferrothorn cover faster physical threats that can 2HKO it through Shadow Shield like Urshifu-R and Weavile. Lunala's middling Speed can be problematic against fast teams, making Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Kartana great partners. Since Lunala can be overwhelmed due to its reliance on Roost and fear of chip damage, Clefable, Gastrodon, and Corviknight alleviate some pressure by dealing with foes such as Tyranitar, Zeraora, and Kartana. They can also absorb Knock Off and status effects that Lunala wants to avoid.

ubers.overview: Lunala is a mainstay defensive Pokemon often paired with the classic core of Yveltal, Eternatus, and Necrozma-DM, forming a defensive backbone that is very difficult to break. Its typing may look terrible, compounding weaknesses to Calyrex-S and Marshadow; however, it provides two immunities and a neutrality to most types. These defensive traits, Shadow Shield, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Roost let Lunala blanket check some of the most dangerous threats in the tier, such as Fire-type move Groudon, Zygarde-C, Zekrom, offensive Necrozma-DM, Rayquaza, and Mewtwo. Lunala excels in long games, where its unmatched reliability in checking strong threats gives it a unique niche. Shadow Shield also makes it a "get out of jail free" card, even stopping a Geomancy Xerneas sweep in an emergency. Lunala can also opt for a more offensive set that surprises common switch-ins like Yveltal with Meteor Beam while still offering defensive utility. However, Lunala's reliance on constantly using Roost to maintain Shadow Shield makes it one of the more predictable Pokemon in the tier. This tendency also sacrifices momentum; thus, more flexible defensive options such as Landorus-T are sometimes preferred. Lunala is also vulnerable to lure options, especially status moves such as Toxic from Groudon. Overall, the key to Lunala is using its defensive presence to let other teammates be more offensive while, at the same time, running teammates with some defensive utility of their own to make Lunala more flexible.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Moongeist Beam can be used over Hex for a stronger attack against foes without status afflictions. It can also be useful to check Lum Berry Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM when Lunala lacks Roar. Teleport is an interesting option to gain momentum on predicted switches. You must use it carefully because, since Teleport will always make Lunala move last, it can lead to Lunala taking damage and forcing a future Roost when a regular switch would have sufficed. Psyshock may be used on the Meteor Beam set to hit Blissey and Eternatus harder, but the other coverage options and Roost generally provide more utility.

Checks and Counters

Ghost- and Dark-type Pokemon and Attacks: Lunala's 4x weaknesses to Ghost and Dark leave it extremely vulnerable to Calyrex-S, Marshadow, Yveltal, Urshifu-S, less obvious threats like Knock Off users, and lure options like Shadow Ball on Mewtwo.
