Flamethrower is another option to threaten Steel-, Bug-,and Grass-type switch-ins such as Aegislash, Mega Scizor, and Ferrothorn. A Relaxed nature is used with Flamethrower so Celesteela's Special Attack is not lowered. Beast Boost provides Celesteela with Defense boosts, which can be useful for absorbing hits from physical attackers such as Mega Gallade.

Every Pokemon on Steel teams appreciates Celesteela's ability to switch into threatening Ground- and Fighting-types suchu as Excadrill. Celesteela is forced out by offensive Fire-types, so Heatran makes for a great partner that can threaten them with Earth Power or Toxic. In return, Celesteela covers its Ground- and Fighting-type weaknesses. Celesteela also struggles against Electric-types like Tapu Koko, so Excadrill and Ferrothorn are good switch-ins to these Pokemon. Excadrill can also offensively check Fire-types, while Ferrothorn can help wear down the opposition with Spikes. If Celesteela is the sole Fighting-type check, it can get worn down very easily, so other switch-ins such as Aegislash and Mega Scizor are valuable partners. Mega Scizor also provides an additional check to Ground-types, alleviating pressure from Celesteela. If Celesteela is running Toxic, Magnezone is another good partner to trap and remove Steel-types like the aforementioned Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor, preventing them from taking advantage of Celesteela.

Autotomize Sweeper (Steel).description:
Celesteela has the potential to become a fearsome sweeper for hyper offensive Steel teams due to Autotomize drastically boosting its speed and Flyinium Z giving it a powerful one-time nuke. Air Slash can severely hurt Fighting-types such as Urshifu-R and has a useful flinch chance. Flyinium Z mitigates Air Slash's low damage and lets it OHKO Flying-weak Pokemon such as Keldeo and Zarude, as well as weakened walls such as Mandibuzz and Toxapex, to start snowballing with Beast Boost. Flamethrower threatens Steel-types such as Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, Magnezone, and Aegislash. Giga Drain targets popular Water-, Ground-, and Rock-types such as Rotom-Wash, Swampert, and Mega Diancie. The passive recovery can also be useful when facing bulky Pokemon such as defensive Tyranitar and Hippowdon. Maximum Speed investment with a Timid nature lets Celesteela outspeed non-Choice Scarf Magnezone and Primarina before Autotomize and Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan and Choice Scarf Victini after Autotomize. Maximum Special Attacks EVs ensure Celesteela will gain Special Attack boosts from Beast Boost.

Autotomize Celesteela is a better fit for offensive Steel teams rather than balanced ones, as it cannot reliably switch into offensive threats. Heatran is still the best partner for Celesteela, as it can deal with Fire-types such as Choice Scarf Blacephalon and Heatran. Offensive Heatran is particularly better because it can weaken and dispose of Toxapex and Zapdos thanks to Magma Storm and Taunt. Strong physical wallbreakers like Mega Scizor, Bisharp, Aegislash, and Excadrill can deal with special walls such as Blissey and Mantine; in return, Celesteela deals with physical walls like Skarmory. Choice Scarf Excadrill also revenge kills Electric- and Fire-types like Tapu Koko and Infernape, while Aegislash serves as a situational switch-in to Fighting-type attacks. Klefki provides dual screens and Spikes to make it easier for Celesteela to set up with Autotomize and sweep. Skarmory can provide Stealth Rock and Spikes to assist Celesteela. Jirachi's Healing Wish allows Celesteela to be played more aggressively early-game.

Dynamax Attacker.description: Kartana's high Attack stat and access to great Max Moves make it an excellent addition to Kyogre teams, where it can remove Gastrodon from play and boost Kyogre's Speed with Max Airstream. Kartana works best as a late-game sweeper, KOing a weakened foe and gaining enough momentum withBeast Boost for it and its partner to sweep through the game. Kartana really needs all four of its coverage moves, as Smart Strike does the most damage to Zacian-C and Calyrex-I, Sacred Sword is necessary to hit Incineroar, and Aerial Ace—via Max Airstream—is essential for winning Speed wars against other common Dynamax users on opposing Kyogre teams like Thundurus, Tornadus, Landorus-T, and opposing Kartana. Max Knuckle from Sacred Sword also helps Kartana snowball through teams quickly, particularly if Zacian-C is in with Kartana to also gain the Attack boosts. White Herb and Life Orb help Kartana maximize its damage output, with the former cancelling out Intimidate and the latter giving it the strongest possible attacks while. Dynamaxed. Assault Vest is an option to patch Kartana's laughable Special Defense, though note that Assault Vest Kartana should use 244 Special Defense EVs to further weather special attacks.

Assault Vest.description:
Kartana has a niche on Kyogre teams, separating itself from other Grass-types such as Venusaur thanks to its access to Max Airstream and stronger matchup against Calyrex-I. Smart Strike grants Kartana Max Steelspike while Dynamaxed to boost its Defense and slam Fairy- and Ice-types such as Grimmsnarl and Calyrex-I. Sacred Sword turns into Max Knuckle and allows Kartana to hit Incineroar super effectively and neutralize Intimidate from it and Landorus-T by raising its Attack. Aerial Ace is used for Max Airstream, which is especially good alongside Kyogre, allowing it to rain down fast and powerful Water Spouts. Assault Vest with Special Defense investment allows Kartana to take strong special attacks such as Kyogre's Water Spout and Dynamaxed Regieleki's Life Orb-boosted Max Lightning.

Kartana and Kyogre pair well together, as Kartana provides a check to Electric- and Grass-types such as Regieleki, Amoonguss, and Rillaboom, while Kyogre checks Fire-types such as Incineroar and Charizard as well as Landorus-T. Other common teammates include Tornadus and Regieleki, both providing great speed control with Tailwind and Electroweb, respectively. Tornadus also appreciates the Kartana checking opposing Regieleki, while Regieleki appreciates it checking opposing Grass-types. Kartana cannot properly check Venusaur in sun due to Weather Ball, so Incineroar is a solid teammate that can alleviate this problem.

ou.overview: Kartana is one of the tier's most potent wallbreakers thanks to its titanic Attack and a Speed tier that allows it to outspeed a significant portion of the unboosted metagame. Beast Boost compounds Kartana's offensive capabilities, letting it take advantage of weakened foes to get Attack boosts and tear through opposing teams. Swords Dance and Choice Band sets let it threaten even switch-ins like Zapdos and Corviknight, while Choice Scarf sets utilize its already-high Speed to make it a threatening revenge killer and late-game sweeper. Despite its huge offensive presence, Kartana is extremely frail, especially specially, making finding opportunities to set up a potential challenge and requiring pivot support, since it shouldn't be switching into attacks. Additionally, Choice Band and Choice Scarf sets are vulnerable to being punished by contact-based abilities like Ferrothorn's Iron Barbs, Heatran's Flame Body, and Zapdos's Static, all of which have the ability to severely hinder Kartana's wallbreaking capabilities.
ou.comments:
Other Options

On more offensively oriented teams, Swords Dance Kartana sets can opt to run Life Orb instead of Protective Pads to further enhance its offensive potency, allowing it to OHKO Clefable and Toxapex after Stealth Rock, though this runs the risk of triggering Static or Flame Body. It can also run a Timid nature with 19 Attack IVs and no Attack investment to get Speed boosts from Beast Boost, letting it outspeed Pokemon like Dragapult and Tapu Koko that might otherwise revenge kill it, though this comes at the cost of a huge part of its power. Adrenaline Orb is also a niche option on offensive teams to receive a one-time Speed boost without sacrificing any of Kartana's power. Aerial Ace can be run on Swords Dance variants to hit Kartana's most common check in Buzzwole, which otherwise resists Kartana's commonly run moves. Defog can be run, most commonly on Choice Scarf sets, to allow Kartana to provide entry hazard removal support, though Kartana's general frailty can make this difficult to pull off.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Most of Kartana's common checks are Flying-types like Tornadus-T, Zapdos, Corviknight, and Skarmory, as they resist most of its attacks. They are, however, susceptible to being weakened with the combination of Knock Off and entry hazards, and they can also be overwhelmed by Swords Dance sets.

Buzzwole: Buzzwole can check most Kartana variants thanks to its huge Defense and resistance to Kartana's most commonly run moves, but it doesn't appreciate taking Knock Off, as it is vulnerable to entry hazard damage, and it can also be overwhelmed by Swords Dance + Aerial Ace sets.

Contact Abilities and Rocky Helmet: Abilities like Static and Flame Body from Zapdos, Volcarona, and Heatran can instantly cripple Kartana if it's not running Protective Pads, drastically reducing its wallbreaking capabilities. Iron Barbs from Ferrothorn, Rough Skin from Garchomp, and Rocky Helmet from users like Buzzwole and Clefable can all also wear down Kartana.

Revenge Killers: Kartana's frailty means that it's susceptible to being revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Dragapult and Tornadus-T, as well as Choice Scarf users like Urshifu-R.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Description

Swords Dance in conjunction with excellent coverage, a solid Speed tier, and Protective Pads keeping it from getting damaged, burned, or paralyzed by contact abilities make Kartana a terrifying wallbreaker. Leaf Blade can OHKO a number of defensive staples like Gastrodon, Rotom-W, and Tapu Fini, as well as offensive Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Tapu Lele, threatening them and forcing them out. Knock Off can cripple common switch-ins like Zapdos and Tornadus-T by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots, making them easier to wear down, as well as hitting Ghost-types like Dragapult and Aegislash that would otherwise resist Kartana's attacks. Sacred Sword threatens Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Melmetal that would otherwise wall Kartana, potentially OHKOing all of them after a Swords Dance.

Team Options

Swords Dance Kartana fits well on bulky offense and balance teams thanks to its massive wallbreaking power helping against bulkier teams, in turn benefitting from the presence of slow pivots to get it in safely. Kartana provides potent Knock Off support for its team, as it can easily force repeated switches and gradually wear down checks that are required to be as healthy as possible to handle it. Due to this, it pairs well with entry hazard setters like Landorus-T and Heatran, the former helping weaken Zapdos and Tornadus-T and the latter easily keeping up Stealth Rock against them to maintain pressure after Kartana removes their Heavy-Duty Boots. Due to its frailty, Kartana also benefits from slow pivots like Landorus-T and Slowbro that can safely bring it in.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Description

With a Choice Scarf, Kartana efficiently zeroes in on its role as a revenge killer and cleaner; its great natural Speed makes it one of the fastest Choice Scarf users, which allows it to outspeed and revenge kill opposing Choice Scarf users like Urshifu-R, Tapu Lele, and Blacephalon. It can force out Dragapult by threatening it with a super effective Knock Off, as well as pick off other lightning-fast offensive Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Weavile, Zeraora, and +1 Garchomp with Leaf Blade. Kartana can also punish incoming Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Melmetal, Heatran, and opposing Kartana with Sacred Sword. Smart Strike is a useful late-game move, as it can hit Grass-, Fighting-, and Dark-resistant foes like Dragapult, Buzzwole, Weavile, and Clefable in the same slot. This is important because Kartana wants to lock itself into a move and clean without switching out, due to the nature of Beast Boost. Kartana excels at cleaning up weakened teams late-game, as it only needs one opportunity for a free KO to start snowballing out of control.

Team Options

A wide variety of offensive teamstyles can appreciate Kartana's revenge killing capabilities and provide wallbreaking support that paves a way for Kartana to clean up. Future Sight support from the likes of Galarian Slowking and Slowbro allows Kartana to bust through checks like Zapdos and Buzzwole, and Slowbro can provide free entry for Kartana with Teleport. Kartana synergizes well with physical wallbreakers like Swords Dance variants of Weavile, Landorus-T, Bisharp, and Garchomp; physical Dragapult; and Melmetal, which can help wear down or break past checks like Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Corviknight; these teammates are potentially assisted by Kartana removing items from the aforementioned foes. Pivots like Landorus-T and Rotom-W generate momentum and attacking opportunities for both Kartana and the wallbreakers it is paired with. Magnezone can remove Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Skarmory, and Corviknight to make Kartana a bigger threat. Tapu Lele can provide wallbreaking support for Kartana by helping to overwhelm shared checks like Ferrothorn and Corviknight, luring in the latter and hitting it with Thunderbolt while also protecting Kartana from priority moves like Weavile’s Ice Shard with Psychic Terrain. Rillaboom can work in tandem with Kartana to overwhelm shared checks and provide pivoting support while boosting the power of Leaf Blade with Grassy Terrain.

Choice Band.description:
Set Description

With Choice Band, Kartana becomes much more of an immediate threat, giving it absurd instant breaking power with its STAB Leaf Blade slicing through Water-types like Slowbro and Tapu Fini in one hit and threatening neutral targets like Landorus-T, Toxapex, and Garchomp with a 2HKO. Smart Strike mows down Fairy-types, being able to OHKO Clefable, and is a solid midground that hits all of Tornadus-T, Dragapult, and Rillaboom in the same slot, finishing off the last after minor chip damage. Knock Off smacks Aegislash and Dragapult trying to switch in, but more importantly, it removes Heavy-Duty Boots from checks like Zapdos and Buzzwole, opening them up to entry hazard damage that will give Kartana and its team an easier time breaking through them. Sacred Sword puts the hurt on the likes of Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Melmetal, 2HKOing them without any issue.

Team Options

Choice Band Kartana is a great pick for offense teams, using its unmatched immediate power to break holes for fast cleaners like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Dragapult, and Weavile to take advantage of and leveraging its solid physical bulk to take strong physical hits like Zeraora’s Close Combat and Choice Band Weavile’s Triple Axel in a pinch. Future Sight from the likes of Slowbro, Galarian Slowking, and Tapu Lele is incredibly beneficial to Kartana, blowing past Buzzwole and removing defensive counterplay from the opponent by easing prediction. The way to get the most mileage out of Kartana is by pairing it with pivots that can get it in safely against its ideal targets; offensive pivots like Dragapult, Tornadus-T, and Tapu Koko can force switches with their offensive presence to get Kartana in against easy marks like Clefable and Blissey, and slow pivots like Landorus-T and Slowbro can take a hit first before bringing in Kartana safely. Additionally, Tapu Koko can remove Flying-types like Corviknight and Tornadus-T and threaten out Buzzwole while appreciating Kartana's removal of Ground-types like Landorus-T and Gastrodon. Entry hazard setters like Landorus-T, Heatran, and Garchomp synergize well with Kartana's strong Knock Off, as it opens up switch-ins like Zapdos and Tornadus-T to Stealth Rock damage by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots. Heatran is a notable option, as it has the additional benefit of threatening Defoggers like Corviknight and Tornadus-T that can switch into Kartana, with Kartana being able to help against Defoggers like Tapu Fini and Rotom-W that can force out Heatran.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Darkinium Z along with a Swords Dance boost enables Kartana to remove Mega Latios and a Mega Latias in its base form on the switch. However, forgoing both Normalium Z and Fightinium Z means Kartana will be unable to adequately pressure its two most common checks in Zapdos and Mega Scizor. Toxic can be used on Choice Scarf sets to cripple checks like Zapdos and Tangrowth, but it’s undesirable to lock into due to the number of Pokemon in the tier that are immune to poison. Swords Dance Kartana can explore other item options, such as Life Orb for more power or Salac Berry with Endure to beat Pokemon like Mega Lopunny, Tapu Koko, and Choice Scarf Magnezone. However, these options often need to forgo too much of Kartana’s longevity or coverage. A Swords Dance set with 19 Attack IVs and a Timid nature to boost Kartana’s Speed with Beast Boost may seem desirable, as it allows Kartana to outspeed checks such as Weavile, Mega Latias and Latios as well as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny and Greninja. However, it can struggle to properly wallbreak, and can often feel outclassed by Swords Dance and Choice Scarf sets.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Corviknight, Zapdos, Moltres, Skarmory, and Mega Charizard Y are some of the best checks to Kartana due to their resistance to Leaf Blade. On top of that, Zapdos can heavily cripple Kartana with Static. However, Corviknight and Skarmory must be cautious of boosted Sacred Swords and Zapdos, Moltres, and Mega Charizard Y are pressured heavily by Normalium Z variants and Choice Band-boosted Return. On top of that, none of Zapdos, Moltres, Skarmory, or Corviknight appreciate their item being removed by Knock Off. Landorus-T can soft-check Kartana for a while as well, but its lack of reliable recovery makes it prone to being worn down in the long run.

Mega Latias and Mega Latios: Both Mega Latias and Mega Latios can stomach all of Kartana's attacks relatively easily, bar a Choice Band-boosted Knock Off or the rare Black Hole Eclipse. As they outspeed non-Choice Scarf variants, they can both proceed to use Kartana as setup bait or force it out with strong moves, respectively. However, they must be wary of taking too much damage, as Knock Off from Choice Scarf sets can rip through them.

Steel-types: Steel-types that aren't weak to Sacred Sword such as Mega Scizor and Mega Mawile are capable of checking Kartana to a degree. However, they can all be overwhelmed by +2 All-Out Pummeling. Other Steel-types can prevent Choice variants of Kartana from spamming Leaf Blade, but they need to be wary of its coverage.

Grass-types: The likes of Tangrowth and Amoonguss can easily scout any of Kartana's attacks and force it out while keeping healthy with Regenerator. Neither of them appreciate a boosted Breakneck Blitz, however. Serperior cannot switch into Kartana, but it can revenge kill all variants without a Choice Scarf.

Magnezone: Choice Scarf Magnezone is able to trap every non-Choice Scarf Kartana set courtesy of Magnet Pull and Hidden Power Fire. A healthy non-Choice Scarf Magnezone is also capable of surviving non-Choice Band Sacred Sword and finishing Kartana off.

Faster threats: Although they cannot switch into Kartana safely, many offensive Pokemon that can outspeed non-Choice Scarf Kartana will more than likely force it out. Examples include Ash-Greninja, Mega Lopunny, Hawlucha, and Choice Scarf Victini.

Contact Items/Abilities: Kartana is easily worn down by contact effects such as Tangrowth, Corviknight and Landorus-T's Rocky Helmet, Ferrothorn's Iron Barbs, Tank Garchomp's Rough Skin as well as Volcarona and Moltres' Flame Body and Zapdos' Static. The highest threat would be status effects and therefore Kartana should be very careful if it's a non-z variant.

Swords Dance.description:
Kartana is a menacing presence due to its magnificent Attack, high Speed, a great ability in Beast Boost, and Swords Dance. On top of that, Kartana also has a very good offensive and defensive typing. Defensively, its many resistances and good physical bulk aid Kartana in setting up against the likes of Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Ferrothorn. Offensively, Kartana's typing and coverage are also very good, as it is capable of pressuring common bulky Water- and Steel-types, such as Tapu Fini, Slowbro, Heatran, and Ferrothorn, with Leaf Blade and Sacred Sword, respectively. Giga Impact alongside Normalium Z allows Kartana to overwhelm some of its best checks in Zapdos and physically defensive Tangrowth after a Swords Dance boost. On the other hand, Fightinium Z can be used to easily remove Mega Scizor, Skarmory, and Corviknight, with Knock Off in the fourth slot to cripple Pokemon like Volcarona, Zapdos, and Moltres.

Kartana fits best on balance and bulky offensive teams that are capable of providing it with proper support it needs to break open teams. Mega Tyranitar is extremely useful for Kartana, as it is capable of removing many roadblocks to Kartana's sweep with Pursuit, such as Mega Latias and Mega Latios, and heavily pressures Zapdos in case Kartana needs to preserve its Z-Move for another target. It can also set Stealth Rock, which is particularly important for Knock Off variants, as it allows Kartana to punish Zapdos more effectively after removing Heavy-Duty Boots. In a similar vein, Magnezone is a potent teammate due to its ability to trap Mega Scizor, Corviknight, and Skarmory, which are some of the very few hard-checks to Normalium Z Kartana. Pokemon that can pressure Kartana's other common checks in Tangrowth and Landorus-T such as Garchomp, Greninja, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Mawile are great partners. In turn, Kartana can heavily pressure some of their checks in Tapu Fini, Slowbro, and Heatran. Kartana requires a good defensive backbone, as it is quite specially frail and prone to being revenge killed by the likes of Mega Lopunny, Ash-Greninja, and Mega Latias. As a result, the likes of Tapu Fini, Toxapex, and Mega Tyranitar make for good teammates. Given Kartana’s poor special bulk, Pokemon that can pivot Kartana into battle such as Mega Lopunny, Rotom-W, and Landorus-T are useful teammates. Lastly, late-game cleaners appreciate Kartana's wallbreaking prowess such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Ash-Greninja, and Mega Lopunny and make for good teammates as well.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Kartana harshly pressures most of its usual checks without having to dedicate a turn to set up. After the boost from Choice Band, Leaf Blade 2HKOes almost every single neutral target in the metagame, making it a very risk-free and spammable move once Kartana's checks have been weakened. A strong Knock Off is another draw of this set, allowing Kartana to greatly damage checks in Mega Latias and Mega Latios and punish sturdier checks such as Zapdos, Corviknight, and Tangrowth by removing their item. Sacred Sword takes care of Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Heatran, as well as some other Grass-resistant Pokemon in Hydreigon and Kyurem. Return gives Kartana a strong neutral hit on Pokemon like Zapdos, Tangrowth, and Moltres that would otherwise tank its attacks. Alternatively, Smart Strike can be used to hit the likes of Mega Mawile and Tangrowth harder than anything else, while almost always OHKOing physically defensive Clefable.

Kartana fits well on balance and bulky offensive teams as a fearsome wallbreaker that can make great amounts of progress throughout the game if it predicts correctly. Stealth Rock setters are very important, since they allow Kartana to heavily pressure Zapdos and Moltres after removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Thus, the likes of Mega Tyranitar, Heatran, Clefable, and Landorus-T pair well with Kartana. Weavile and Mega Tyranitar can trap and weaken or dispose of Mega Latias, Heatran, and Zapdos, making Kartana's job easier and less prediction-reliant. Magnezone is a notable partner due to its ability to trap some of the best checks to Kartana in Mega Scizor, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Other wallbreakers that can pressure Kartana's checks in Zapdos, Tangrowth, and Mega Scizor can also prove to be good teammates. Examples include Heatran and Ash-Greninja. Pivoting support from the likes of Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and Landorus-T can greatly increase the amount of opportunities for Kartana to break walls by granting it safe ways to enter a match. Lastly, late-game cleaners that can wrap up the game after Kartana has done its job such as Mega Lopunny, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Swords Dance Weavile are good options as well.

Synthesis Utility.description:
With Synthesis, Kartana can reliably check the metagame's dangerous Ground-types in Garchomp, Landorus-T, Mega Swampert, and Gliscor, as well as Mega Tyranitar lacking Fire Punch. Leaf Blade alongside Grassium Z allows Kartana to properly threaten the Ground-types it checks, taking them out after little-to-no chip with Bloom Doom. Knock Off gives Kartana additional utility in punishing common switch-ins such as Zapdos and Corviknight, as well as removing items from the likes of Ferrothorn and Heatran. Alternatively, Sacred Sword may be used to directly threaten Ferrothorn and Heatran, but dropping the utility of Knock Off is undesirable. Defog enables Kartana to fully check Garchomp, Landorus-T, Mega Tyranitar, and Ferrothorn by nullifying their attempts at setting up entry hazards. 120 Attack EVs allow Kartana to OHKO Garchomp with Bloom Doom. The remaining EVs are allocated to HP so that Kartana can check Ground-types more consistently.

Kartana fits best on balance and bulky offensive teams in need of a sturdy check to Ground-types. As such, Pokemon that appreciate Ground-types out of the picture such as Heatran, Mega Mawile, and Toxapex can prove to be good teammates. Pursuit support from Mega Tyranitar and Weavile is useful, as it pressures Mega Latias and weakens Zapdos, which are some of Kartana's best checks, especially for non-Knock Off variants. However, when pairing Kartana with Mega Tyranitar, be careful with your timing and positioning, as Synthesis recovers less HP in sand. Kartana is easily forced out by special attackers or faster threats such as Ash-Greninja, Mega Latias, and Mega Lopunny. As such, it requires a sturdy defensive backbone to take these threats on, which may consist of Pokemon such as specially defensive Heatran, Slowbro, and Toxapex. All of these bar Slowbro are susceptible to entry hazards due to the amount of times they are required to pivot into various threats throughout a match and therefore appreciate Kartana’s Defog support. Lastly, Kartana has the tendency to force Knock Off on Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Heatran, Toxapex, and Tangrowth, so partners like Calm Mind Clefable and Tapu Lele are good options to consider as well.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Kartana functions as a revenge killer early on in games by outpacing common offensive Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny, Ash-Greninja, Tapu Koko, +1 Mega Gyarados, and Weavile and either defeating them or forcing them out. Once the opponent's team has been weakened sufficiently, Kartana can then clean up late-game with the assistance of its enhanced Speed and Beast Boost. Knock Off is a great move that punishes checks such as Zapdos, Corviknight, and Moltres. It is also Kartana's best option against Mega Latias and Mega Latios. Sacred Sword is a crucial coverage move, enabling Kartana to hit opposing Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Heatran, as well as almost always OHKOing Mega Lopunny. Smart Strike rounds out the set as a reliable secondary STAB move that provides the strongest hit against threats such as Clefable and Kyurem. Defog may be used instead to remove entry hazards for more offensive teams.

Kartana fits best in offensive teams in need of a revenge killer and late-game sweeper in one. As Kartana is a good late-game cleaner once the opposing team has been weakened, it is a good idea to pair it with early-game wallbreakers that can threaten or take advantage of Kartana's checks in Zapdos, Mega Latias, Tangrowth, and Corviknight. Good examples include Garchomp, Kyurem, Weavile, Mega Medicham, and Tapu Lele. Pursuit support from the likes of Mega Tyranitar and Weavile is appreciated in order to trap the likes of Mega Latias, Mega Latios, and Heatran, as this allows Kartana to spam Leaf Blade late-game. Mega Tyranitar also provides Stealth Rock support, which is important to pressure Zapdos and Moltres once Kartana has removed their Heavy-Duty Boots. Similarly, Magnezone is a notable partner due to its ability to trap Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Corviknight, Ferrothorn, and Skarmory. Kartana is incapable of revenge killing a healthy Mega Mawile, Mega Scizor, and Volcarona, so running Pokemon that can deal with them such as Heatran and Toxapex is very advisable.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Kartana can run Synthesis as its fourth move on Life Orb sets, helping it avoid being worn down over the course of a game, but sacrificing coverage. Aerial Ace is also an option to hit Buzzwole and Tangrowth super effectively. Protective Pads can also be used over Life Orb, trading damage output for avoiding damage from Rough Skin, Iron Barbs, and Rocky Helmet. A Timid Nature and 19 Attack IVs can also be used to have Beast Boost increase Kartana's Speed, turning it into a better sweeper at the cost of less initial damage.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Flying-types: Corviknight, Skarmory, and Ho-oh all resist both of Kartana's STAB moves, and can threaten it with either Body Press or Sacred Fire.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Kartana has difficulty breaking through Amoongus, Tangrowth, and Buzzwole, which have enough Defense to check all of its sets.

Contact Effects: Contact effects such as Static, Flame Body, Iron Barbs, and Rocky Helmet make it difficult for Kartana to make progress.

Revenge Killers: Swords Dance sets can be revenge killed by faster threats such as Choice Scarf Victini and Zeraora. Choice Scarf sets can also be easily checked offensively, as opponents are able to take advantage of Kartana being locked into the same move.

Swords Dance (Special Defense).description:
Kartana's monstrous 181 base Attack stat, boosted even further via Life Orb and Swords Dance, makes it a fantastic wallbreaker. Inheriting Special Defense makes it much less susceptible to chip damage from resisted attacks like Tapu Koko's Thunderbolt. Kartana's Speed tier also allows it to outspeed many common Pokemon including Yveltal, all Kyurem formes, and Volcarona. Swords Dance helps it beat would-be checks such as Landorus-T inheriting Defense. Leaf Blade is its main form of damage, hitting Water-types like Slowbro and Rotom-W super effectively and dealing large amounts of damage to neutral targets. Knock Off is used to damage Flying- and Fire-type Pokemon such as Corviknight, Ho-oh, and Volcarona, removing their items like Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, respectively, allowing Kartana to wear them down more easily. Sacred Sword hits Steel-type Pokemon like Ferrothorn super effectively, while also Flying-type Pokemon who are neutral to Fighting such as Skarmory.

Swords Dance Kartana fits best on offensive teams, as it is excellent at wearing down opposing walls like Landorus-T and Corviknight so another teammate can sweep. Kartana is able to work with most gods, but is most commonly paired with more offensive gods such as Yveltal and Rayquaza, as they can also take advantage of the pressure Kartana puts on opposing teams and provide Kartana with a solid Special Defense donation. However, it is important to understand that Kartana does not work with every god, such as Ho-oh, as Kartana does not have much longevity. Offensive entry hazard setters such as Cloyster make great partners, as entry hazards help wear down Kartana’s checks. Kartana also compliments entry hazard setters well by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from walls, especially Ho-oh. Teammates such as Zygarde-10% who share common checks with Kartana are useful, as together they can slowly wear down their shared checks until one of them has an opportunity to sweep or pick up multiple KOs. Kartana also pairs well with powerful cleaners such as Bisharp inheriting Speed and Weavile inheriting Attack, as they excel at capitalizing off of Kartana's wallbreaking power. While Kartana has a good Speed tier, it is still outsped by common offensive Pokemon such as Tapu Koko and Pheromosa, making other fast Pokemon such as Mewtwo or Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Lele good teammates.

Choice Scarf (Special Defense).description:
With a Choice Scarf, Kartana becomes a deadly late-game cleaner and revenge killer. Thanks to its high Attack and good Speed tier, it is able to outspeed and threaten to KO the majority of the tier's offensive threats like Weavile and Zeraora. With its Special Defense patched up, it also is able to stomach weak hits in the process, such as Rotom-W's Volt Switch and Tapu Koko's Thunderbolt. Leaf Blade OHKOes common Pokemon like Zygarde-10%., while Smart Strike threatens Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele and Clefable. Knock Off hits Flying-type switch-ins like Corviknight and Ho-Oh, who resist Kartana's STAB moves, and Sacred Sword hits Steel- and Flying-type Pokemon neutral to Fighting such as Heatran and Yveltal. Defog is an option to allow Kartana to serve as an emergency entry hazard remover.

Choice Scarf Kartana fits well on bulky offense and balance teams which appreciate its ability to outspeed and revenge kill common threats. It is often paired with offensive gods such as Yveltal and Rayquaza, but can work with many different gods. The exception to this is that some gods with very high Special Defense stats such as Ho-oh and Zamazenta-C would much rather donate their Special Defense to a defensive Pokemon. Magnezone is a great partner, as it is able to trap and remove Steel-types that Kartana has trouble breaking. Powerful wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Weavile are also good partners, as they are able to help weaken Kartana's checks like Corviknight, making it easier to sweep late-game. Special attackers like Kyurem-W and Nidoking are also great partners for Kartana, as they can pressure physical walls such as physically defensive Tangrowth. Teammates who can use Future Sight such as Slowking and Slowbro also pair well with Kartana, taking advantage of the fact that many of Kartana's checks, such as Landorus-T and Skarmory, have lower Special Defense.

cap.comments:
Other Options

On the Swords Dance set, Kartana can run a Timid nature with 19 Attack IVs to receive a Speed boost from Beast Boost; however, this causes Kartana to lack critical immediate breaking power. Aerial Ace is an option over Smart Strike on the Choice Band set to lure Buzzwole; however, its usefulness is limited to this one matchup. Similarly, Psycho Cut can be used to bait Venomicon and Buzzwole, but it OHKOes neither.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Walls: Kartana has an incredibly difficult time breaking through physically bulky walls like Buzzwole, Skarmory, and Corviknight. Corviknight and Skarmory can be KOed by Swords Dance variants if they have been chipped, but Buzzwole is nigh impossible to break through.

Flying-types: Flying-types like Zapdos, Venomicon, and Tornadus-T can switch into Kartana's STAB moves safely and force it out with their strong special attacks. Venomicon is particularly difficult to break due to Stamina. None of these Pokemon enjoy losing their Heavy-Duty Boots to Knock Off, however.

Contact Effects: Zapdos's Static, Volcarona and Heatran's Flame Body, Ferrothorn's Iron Barbs, Garchomp's Rough Skin, and Toxapex's Rocky Helmet all can either cripple Kartana with status or accrue meaningful chip damage.

Revenge Killers: Non-Choice Scarf Kartana can be revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Dragapult, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Astrolotl, and Tornadus-T. Choice Scarf variants of Astrolotl even outspeed Choice Scarf Kartana, making it a particularly good check.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Kartana is one of the most threatening cleaners in CAP, leveraging Beast Boost and its sky-high attack excellently as the second fastest Choice Scarf user in the metagame. Knock Off importantly hits Dragapult and Blacephalon super effectively while removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Tornadus-T, Venomicon, Astrolotl, and Zapdos. Sacred Sword allows Kartana to get past bulky Steel-types like Heatran and Ferrothorn. Defog is an option over Smart Strike on teams that require entry hazard removal that otherwise lack it, but it is a significant opportunity cost, as Smart Strike is often an excellent midground option that also hits Clefable and Tapu Lele super effectively.

Choice Scarf Kartana is most commonly found on offense and bulky offense teams. Due to its extremely poor bulk, pivots like Dragapult and Landorus-T are excellent choices for safely getting Kartana in on foes like Blissey and Tapu Fini. Dragapult threatens physically defensive walls like Zapdos and Ferrothorn for Kartana, while Landorus-T can force out Heatran and cripple Zapdos and Tornadus-T with Toxic. Air Balloon Heatran is another excellent teammate that can stonewall opposing Heatran and Astrolotl and trap and eliminate Toxapex. Pairing Kartana up with similarly menacing physical attackers like Weavile and Venomicon-E allows them to weaken their shared checks. Venomicon-E is particularly notable for its ability to guarantee damage on Zapdos. Entry hazards from Pokemon like Garchomp and Astrolotl do amazing work towards enabling Kartana to sweep late-game, particularly Stealth Rock. Both are notable choices for their ability to switch into Heatran effectively. Trick + Sticky Barb Clefable is another excellent option that excels at guaranteeing chip onto foes that normally check Kartana like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Heatran. Finally, setup sweepers like Volcarona, Stratagem, and Dragonite greatly enjoy Kartana chipping foes into range of a sweep.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance turns Kartana into the most powerful attacker in the metagame. After one Swords Dance, Kartana is capable of OHKOing Toxapex, and it can make quick work of teams that lack a faster Pokemon. Knock Off is necessary coverage that hits Corviknight, Zapdos, Venomicon, and Tornadus-T neutrally. Sacred Sword is necessary for bulky Steel-types like Heatran and Ferrothorn. Life Orb is the preferred item to give Kartana a chance to OHKO Toxapex with +2 Leaf Blade; however, Protective Pads is another option that prevents Kartana having its sweep ended early by contact effects like Zapdos's Static or Heatran's Flame Body.

Swords Dance Kartana fits best on offensive teams that appreciate the holes it creates. Because Swords Dance Kartana is easier to revenge kill, specially bulky teammates like Landorus-T and Melmetal are necessary for dealing with potential revenge killers like Dragapult, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Melmetal, in particular, is a good option that does quite well at breaking for Kartana. Choice Scarf Blacephalon and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele are great offensive teammates that threaten revenge killers like Zeraora and Dragapult and physical walls like Buzzwole. Bulk Up Zeraora and Dragon Dance Dragonite both appreciate the fact that, if Kartana's sweep is unsuccessful, it will have done enough damage to open up a sweep opportunity for them. Aurora Veil support from Alolan Ninetales can ease Kartana's setup, particularly in the face of special attackers whose moves it resists like Clefable and Tapu Koko.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Kartana is an immensely threatening wallbreaker that can burst through the opposition with the correct read. Knock Off importantly cripples Flying-types like Zapdos, Venomicon, and Tornadus-T while hitting Dragapult on the switch. Sacred Sword demolishes bulky Steel-types like Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Melmetal.

Choice Band Kartana excels at breaking open opposing walls; accordingly, faster wallbreakers like Dragapult and Blacephalon and sweepers like Weavile and Zeraora are good teammate options. Kartana immensely enjoys pivot support from Pokemon like Corviknight and Landorus-T due to its frailty. Tapu Fini is another good teammate that can switch into Heatran while providing Misty Terrain, protecting Kartana from status it would incur from Zapdos's Static or Heatran's Flame Body. Future Sight support from Tapu Lele or Slowbro makes Kartana near unwallable and lessen how reliant Choice Band Kartana is on prediction. Eject Button Toxapex is an interesting option that can give Kartana a free switch; this is especially potent with Tapu Lele's Future Sight support.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a newly introduced Pokemon. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: B+ Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are great in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame. These Pokemon have more notable flaws than those above them that affect how they function in the format. Their positive traits still outshine their negatives, but they require a bit more team support to bring out their full potential.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Physical Sweeper.description:
• Kartana's impressive Attack stat and Beast Boost make it a capable late-game physical sweeper, only held back by its awful Special Defense and low base power attacks.

  • Aerial Ace may seem weak, but it gives Kartana access to Max Airstream while Dynamaxed, giving it a good shot of sweeping late-game. Smart Strike is weak for a STAB Attack, but it OHKOs Nihilego, and grants access to the useful Max Steelspike while Dynamaxed. While difficult to fit in, Giga Impact is Kartana's best hope of doing decent damage to Zapdos with Max Strike.

  • Swords Dance makes Kartana less reliant on Dynamax and Beast Boost to sweep, and pairs especially well with Focus Sash.

Items

  • Focus Sash lets Kartana survive in match-ups that may normally be difficult for it to win, mainly against special attackers.

  • Life Orb makes Kartana a better late-game sweeper when Dynamaxed.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Kartana's access to Beast Boost makes it a reasonable choice for Choice Scarf revenge killing and late-game sweeping.

  • Guillotine is an emergency attack to have a 30% shot at destroying bulky Pokemon, while Aerial Ace gives Kartana a Speed boost if Dynamax sweeping presents itself to Kartana.

ru.overview: Guzzlord is a solid Pokemon in RU, with its enormous bulk and defensive typing letting it check various common Pokemon like Celebi, Chandelure, Heliolisk, and Raikou. It's pretty good at taking even powerful special attacks, like Sludge Bomb from offensive Roserade and Ice Beam from Nidoqueen and wallbreaker Starmie. Knock Off has great utility, removing Heavy-Duty Boots or Leftovers from Pokemon like Milotic and Gastrodon. Offensive Guzzlord also has Heavy Slam, Earthquake, and Toxic for the Fairy-type, Steel-type, and bulky Pokemon that can take Knock Off. Guzzlord can also run a good RestTalk set that has better longevity and withstands Toxic users such as Raikou and Milotic. However, RestTalk Guzzlord is more passive, notably becoming setup bait for one of the tier's best Pokemon in Nasty Plot Togekiss. Guzzlord is destroyed by common Fighting-types such as Bewear, Heracross, and Lucario. Additionally, despite being Dark-type, it's potentially a liability against Psychic-type setup sweepers like Reuniclus, Cosmic Power Metagross, and Psycho Shift Sigilyph. All can take Knock Off, heal off the damage, and set up. RestTalk Guzzlord does beat Psycho Shift Sigilyph, but Metagross and Reuniclus can take advantage of a sleeping Guzzlord, as it'll need to get lucky with Sleep Talk rolling Dragon Tail to phaze them without taking significant damage.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Fire Blast is an option over Earthquake that puts more pressure on Steelix and defensive Roserade, and it 2HKOes Heracross. Guzzlord could function as a wallbreaker with Choice Band or Choice Specs that checks Grass- and Electric-types like Dhelmise and Heliolisk. However, as a wallbreaker it competes with Incineroar and Pangoro, which are stronger, get past Water-types more easily, and can take advantage of Umbreon with Swords Dance.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Lucario, Bewear, Heracross, and Pangoro can switch into and easily destroy Guzzlord. However, Lucario and Heracross dislike Earthquake and Heavy Slam, respectively, and all besides Lucario are crippled by Toxic—Lucario easily takes advantage of these variants. Sharpedo destroys a chipped Guzzlord with Close Combat.

Knock Off and Toxic: Knock Off and Toxic heavily cripple non-RestTalk Guzzlord because it lacks recovery outside of Leftovers. Salazzle and Seismitoad cripple Guzzlord with Knock Off and Toxic, and Milotic and Gastrodon cripple it with Toxic.

Fairy-types and Fairy-type Coverage: Galarian Weezing and Klefki can take Guzzlord's attacks and threaten it with Fairy-type attacks, though they're 2HKOed by Heavy Slam and Earthquake, respectively. Gardevoir outpaces and OHKOes Guzzlord. Galarian Weezing, Klefki, and Togekiss cannot be phazed by Dragon Tail and wall RestTalk Guzzlord easily. Klefki and Togekiss can even set up Spikes or use Nasty Plot. Xurkitree's Dazzling Gleam OHKOes a slightly chipped Guzzlord.

Setup Sweepers: Cloyster and Barbaracle take Guzzlord's attacks and set up Shell Smash; however, they dislike the combination of Toxic and Protect quickly wearing them down, and non-White Herb Barbaracle is left at low health after Earthquake. Guzzlord cannot break through Cosmic Power Metagross due to Defense boosts and Reuniclus due to its bulk, letting them set up. Sigilyph burns Guzzlord with Psycho Shift and Flame Orb, preventing Knock Off from outdamaging Roost, for easy setup. RestTalk Guzzlord counters Sigilyph and can temporarily check the other Psychic-type setup sweepers by phazing them, but it takes significant damage from all of their boosted attacks and cannot phaze them if they're the last Pokemon standing.

Dragon-types: Noivern can switch into Guzzlord and thwart it with Draco Meteor, but it dislikes losing Heavy-Duty Boots to Knock Off and being hit by Dragon Tail. Flygon and Tyrantrum can use non-RestTalk Guzzlord to set up Dragon Dance, though Flygon being forced to use Outrage lets Guzzlord's teammates check it.

Tank.description:
Heavy Slam 2HKOes Fairy-types like Togekiss and Galarian Weezing. Earthquake is Guzzlord's best option against Steel-types like Steelix and Registeel after they've taken Knock Off, and it keeps Lucario from setting up freely. On the other hand, Toxic cripples bulky Pokemon like Milotic, Gastrodon, and Incineroar. Protect scouts against Choice-locked Pokemon like Gardevoir, Flygon, and Pangoro, lets Guzzlord safely heal with Leftovers, and racks up damage if running Toxic. Dragon Tail could be run in the third moveslot to rack up entry hazard damage and soft check setup sweepers like Reuniclus and Nasty Plot Crobat. Earthquake and Toxic can be run together without Heavy Slam on teams adequate against Nasty Plot Togekiss. Because Guzzlord's HP stat is so naturally high, investing EVs in its defenses is far more efficient. 152 Defense EVs let Guzzlord survive Mimikyu's +2 Drain Punch with Stealth Rock, the Special Defense helps with Heliolisk, Nidoqueen, and Life Orb Sigilyph, and the other EVs are thrown into Attack, importantly being more than enough to OHKO Chandelure.

Guzzlord pairs well with entry hazard setters like Roserade, Heavy-Duty Boots Heracross, and Steelix, since Knock Off removes Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Gastrodon and Noivern. Checks to Fighting-types like Lucario, Bewear, and Heracross are critical; Togekiss and Galarian Weezing check Pangoro and Heracross, Crobat checks Heracross and revenge kills Lucario, Noivern effectively revenge kills all the Fighting-types, and Chandelure and Jellicent check Bewear and Lucario. Haze Milotic can check the setup sweepers that beat Guzzlord, like Psycho Shift Sigilyph, Cosmic Power Metagross, and Reuniclus. Electric-types like Raikou and Xurkitree also cover Sigilyph. Golurk and Chandelure check Reuniclus and Metagross. Nidoqueen, Roserade, and Salazzle take advantage of Galarian Weezing for Guzzlord. Klefki can be handled with Ground-types like Seismitoad and Steelix, or Rapid Spin Starmie. Steel-types like Registeel and Steelix switch into Gardevoir; Steelix is especially good because it also checks Xurkitree well, which can threaten Guzzlord with Dazzling Gleam.

RestTalk.description:
Rest helps remedy Guzzlord's lack of recovery and lets it deal with Toxic users like Raikou and Milotic, while Sleep Talk reduces the passiveness of Rest. Guzzlord's extremely high HP stat means that investing EVs in its defenses is more effective. Special Defense investment is prioritized because Guzzlord is good against special attackers like Sigilyph and Nidoqueen that are difficult to check otherwise, but the Defense EVs still make Guzzlord notably more resilient against physical attackers like Crobat and Metagross. The Attack EVs are enough to OHKO Sigilyph and then further optimize the stat slightly. Heavy Slam could be run over Dragon Tail on teams that need to prevent Togekiss from setting up freely.

Spikes and Stealth Rock users like Steelix, Roserade, Registeel, and Golisopod pair well with Guzzlord, since it uses Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots and Dragon Tail to accrue entry hazard damage. Electric- and Steel-types like Raikou, Stakataka, and Registeel are important to cover Togekiss. Steelix is a particularly notable teammate, because it also checks Xurkitree well, which threatens Guzzlord via Dazzling Gleam. Spikes Klefki and Galarian Weezing are other troublesome Fairy-types. Klefki can be checked by Pokemon like Incineroar and Dhelmise, while Nidoqueen, Roserade, and Chandelure can check Galarian Weezing. Covering Fighting-types is critical for Guzzlord. Togekiss and Galarian Weezing check Heracross and Pangoro, while Crobat switches into only Heracross but revenge kills Lucario. Jellicent and Chandelure cover Lucario, and Jellicent can also soft check Heracross.

nu.overview: Guzzlord has solidified itself as a fantastic, versatile threat in the NU metagame thanks to its amazing offensive and defensive typing. It has excellent bulk to check a plethora of incredibly menacing, top-tier Pokemon including Rotom-C, Salazzle, and Decidueye. Formidable base Attack, Beast Boost, and a colorful movepool with tons of utility make it an exceptionally capable attacker; STAB Knock Off punishes common switch-ins such as Talonflame and Mudsdale, for example, and Heavy Slam deals heavy damage to Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Diancie. Guzzlord's overall defensive properties give it a lot of opportunities to directly switch in and wallbreak. However, its low base Speed makes it prone to being revenge killed by common wallbreakers such as Sylveon, Tauros, and Toxicroak. Moreover, despite Guzzlord's typing's advantages, it's weak to common moves such as Body Press and U-turn. Furthermore, many of the foes Guzzlord tries to check can pivot out on it, such as Rotom-C and Decidueye, which makes it harder to truly capitalize on its positive matchup against them.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Non-Choice Band offensive options such as Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots Guzzlord are also options to increase the glutton's longevity while maintaining high offensive pressure. Choice Specs makes Guzzlord an effective lure for traditional switch-ins like Vileplume, Mudsdale, and Weezing at the cost of Knock Off's general utility, worsening its matchup against foes like Sylveon, Vaporeon, and Diancie.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Pokemon such as Diancie and Sylveon are big nuisances to Guzzlord thanks to their super effective Fairy-type moves. Moreover, both use Heal Bell, so Guzzlord's Toxic is more or less ineffective against them. Heavy Slam prevents them from always safely switching in, though.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Scrafty and Passimian can force out Guzzlord with their super effective moves. However, they must all watch out for Knock Off or Toxic.

Physical Walls: Physically bulky Pokemon such as Mudsdale, Vileplume, and Weezing are able to sponge hits from Guzzlord and punish it with coverage moves or status conditions. However, they need to beware of specially offensive variants of Guzzlord, which can take advantage of and bypass them.

Faster Wallbreakers: Pokemon such as Tauros, Toxicroak, and Choice Specs Sylveon can exploit Guzzlord's Speed tier to punish it with strong, spammable moves.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Knock Off provides Guzzlord with a spammable STAB move that punishes bulkier walls such as Mudsdale and Tangela. Heavy Slam allows Guzzlord to punish common Fairy-type switch-ins in Sylveon, Diancie, and Grimmsnarl. Earthquake is a spammable coverage option that nails Steel-types such as Copperajah and Stakataka. Heat Crash may also be used to harshly punish the likes of Vileplume and Escavalier. Outrage gives Guzzlord an extremely potent option to muscle through bulkier foes such as Silvally-Ground, Weezing, and Sandaconda. Dragon Claw is a more consistent alternative that doesn't lock Guzzlord into staying in.

Guzzlord greatly appreciates Wish and Heal Bell support from the likes of Vaporeon, Sylveon, and Diancie to maintain its decent defensive utility and consistent wallbreaking, clearing status conditions such as Toxic poison and burn from the likes of Mudsdale and Rotom-C's Will-O-Wisp. Garbodor, Talonflame, and Salazzle are also potent partners for Guzzlord, as they can take U-turn directed at it and beat its Fairy- and Fighting-type checks in Passimian, Toxicroak, and Sylveon. Late-game cleaners such as Silvally-Ground, Ninjask, and Tauros appreciate Guzzlord's ability to soften up foes early-game.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Dragon Tail lets Guzzlord phaze setup sweepers like Salazzle, Nasty Plot Rotom-C, and Snorlax. RestTalk allows Guzzlord to consistently exploit bulky Water-types like Mantine, Gastrodon, and Vaporeon. Guzzlord can also opt for Toxic + Protect to better pressure physical walls like Mudsdale and Quagsire, although it becomes much more vulnerable to status ailments. The Speed investment lets Guzzlord outrun Vaporeon.

Checks to Guzzlord's weaknesses such as Fighting, Fairy, and Bug include Talonflame, Garbodor, and Salazzle. Garbodor is a great partner, as it can punish Fairy- and Fighting-types as well as incoming U-turn with Rocky Helmet while supplying Spikes support to increase Dragon Tail's potency. In turn, Guzzlord takes on Psychic-types and is overall a solid special wall to compensate for Garbodor's average special bulk. Wallbreakers such as Tauros, Starmie, and Silvally-Ground appreciate Guzzlord not just forcing in bulkier Pokemon such as Mudsdale, Vileplume, and Drapion, but also punishing them with Knock Off and Toxic, allowing for easier late-game sweeps. Wish passers like Sylveon and Vaporeon make Guzzlord less reliant on Rest for longevity and can wake it up if needed with Heal Bell.

uu.overview: Necrozma is a solid sweeper in UU thanks to its offensive versatility, allowing it to bypass traditional answers like Chansey and Celesteela with its unpredictability. Its Dragon Dance set is a strong sweeper, powering through metagame staples like Slowking and Amoonguss. On the other hand, its Meteor Beam set is equally as potent, allowing it to lure in and slam answers to the Dragon Dance set like Celesteela and Mandibuzz. Its Calm Mind set can utilize its high bulk to act as a sweeper while also blanket checking threats like Scizor. Necrozma's high natural bulk and Prism Armor allow it to set up on many Pokemon like Nihilego and take super effective hits from threats like Cobalion and Scizor. Necrozma also has a solid matchup against common entry hazard removers like Salamence and Tentacruel, letting it act as an offensive Stealth Rock setter capable of supporting its team. However, Necrozma heavily dislikes status from threats like Chansey and Hippowdon, which limits its chance to sweep. Necrozma is also limited by the number of Dark-types in the tier like Zarude, Mandibuzz, and Hydreigon, which can all hinder at least one of its sets. Overreliance on Power Herb on Necrozma's Meteor Beam set makes it hard to pull off a sweep at times with Pokemon like Hydreigon and Slowking being common, while the Dragon Dance set can be worn down it accumulates multiple boosts.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Necrozma can run Expanding Force over Photon Geyser on its Meteor Beam set on Psychic Terrain teams for more devastating damage, but the limited viability of the playstyle and reliance on Terrain being active make Photon Geyser the preferred option. A final option is a Stored Power set with Cosmic Power or Calm Mind to boost Necrozma's stats, but it lacks the dangerous immediate sweeping potential of Necrozma's other sets and can be inconsistent at times.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Zarude can easily revenge kill Necrozma, even at +1 Speed from Dragon Dance. However, if Necrozma uses Autotomize, it can threaten them before they attack. Still, Hydreigon forces Necrozma to conserve its Power Herb as it can take advantage of Meteor Beam requring two turns. Umbreon can tank hits from all sets and cripple it with Toxic. Although it must watch out for Meteor Beam, Mandibuzz can take on Necrozma well.

Special Walls: Special walls like Chansey and Slowking take on the Meteor Beam set with ease. However, they must watch out for the Dragon Dance set. Celesteela walls the Dragon Dance set and can take a boosted Heat Wave while wearing down Necrozma with Leech Seed, but it can get overwhelmed easily. Hippowdon can take boosted hits, cripple Necrozma with Toxic, and outlast it by healing with Slack Off.

Status: Status is detrimental to Necrozma's attempts to sweep, so moves like Thunder Wave from Togekiss, Scald from Slowking, and Toxic from Hippowdon, Excadrill, and Chansey greatly hinder it.

Dragon Dance.description:
Dragon Dance boosts Necrozma's Attack to incredible levels, letting it power through Pokemon like Hippowdon, Primarina, and Chansey. X-Scissor OHKOes Zarude and deals great damage to Hydreigon, Slowking, and Tangrowth. Heat Wave prevents Steel-types like Celesteela, Scizor, and Skarmory from walling Necrozma. With a Lum Berry, Necrozma can set up on Pokemon like Amoonguss, Rotom-W, and Slowking, which would normally stay in to cripple it with status. Alternatively, since Prism Armor lets Necrozma take weak super effective hits like Knock Off from Nihilego with ease, Necrozma can employ a Weakness Policy to get a huge boost to its Attack. Naughty is the preferred nature, since Necrozma outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame barring Choice Scarf users like Hydreigon after a Dragon Dance and prefers to not lower its Special Attack to boost the power of Heat Wave.

Necrozma best fits on offense teams as a late-game cleaner once its answers have been removed. Celesteela is problematic for this particular set, so powerful wallbreakers like Thundurus-T can remove it. Thundurus-T also beats Mandibuzz and helps wear down walls like Hippowdon and Primarina for Necrozma to bypass them more easily. Sticky Web support from Ribombee help offset Necrozma's average Speed tier, allowing it to outspeed Choice Scarf users like Zarude after a Dragon Dance. Stealth Rock support from Pokemon like Excadrill and Cobalion wears down Pokemon like Celesteela and Hatterene. Dark-type checks like the aformentioned Cobalion, Primarina, and Azumarill make great partners for Necrozma, beating threats like Umbreon and Hydreigon.

Meteor Beam.description:
In conjunction with Power Herb, Meteor Beam is a powerful attack capable of wiping out Pokemon like Salamence, Mandibuzz, and Thundurus-T while simultaneously giving Necrozma a boost to its Special Attack in one turn. Since Power Herb is single use, it should be saved until special walls like Chansey and Slowking are gone. Photon Geyser is Necrozma's primary move to power through many Pokemon like Keldeo and Amoonguss. It is also able to ignore abilities like Quagsire's Unaware. Heat Wave melts Steel-types like Scizor and Jirachi as well as Grass-types like Zarude and Tangrowth. It is also Necrozma's most reliable option for damaging Hatterene. Autotomize lets Necrozma boost its Speed to outpace threats like Zarude and Choice Scarf Diggersby. Alternatively, Necrozma can utilize Stealth Rock to act as an entry hazard setter for its team thanks to its good matchup against common entry hazard removers like Salamence and Rotom-H. Modest is the preferred nature to maximize damage output, since after an Autotomize, Necrozma outspeeds the fastest Choice Scarf users. Even if Stealth Rock is chosen, Modest is still preferred, since Necrozma doesn't miss out on many important Speed tiers.

This set also fits on offense teams as a powerful late-game sweeper. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Excadrill wears down Pokemon like Celesteela and Hatterene for Necrozma to break through them more easily and allows Necrozma to drop Stealth Rock for Autotomize. Excadrill can also beat special walls like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro and cripple Slowking and Mandibuzz with Toxic. Early-game wallbreakers like Belly Drum Azumarill, Swords Dance Scizor, and Nasty Plot Thundurus-T can muscle through special walls like Chansey and Slowking for Necrozma. Cobalion can bring in Necrozma on Pokemon it can set up on like Amoonguss while also threatening Umbreon, Hydreigon, and Chansey for Necrozma. Sticky Web support from Ribombee help offset Necrozma's average Speed tier, allowing it to forego Autotomize for Stealth Rock if the team needs to as well as outspeed and remove threats like Keldeo and Raikou.

Calm Mind.description:
Necrozma can set up with Calm Mind against Pokemon that cannot OHKO it like Thundurus-T and Nihilego, making it harder to bypass with by special attacking threats such as Primarina and Salamence as well as become more threatening to Hippowdon. Heat Wave provides crucial coverage against Steel-types like Celesteela and Scizor. It is also Necrozma's best option to damage Dark-types like Zarude and Mandibuzz. Moonlight allows Necrozma to sustain itself throughout a match, although its limited PP means it should be used conservatively. Colbur Berry allows Necrozma to take Dark-type attacks from Pokemon like Scizor and Zarude and retaliate with a powerful attack. Leftovers is an alternative option that lets Necrozma preserve more longevity as it tries setting up. Even if Necrozma's Colbur Berry gets used up, the given HP and Defense EVs allow it to avoid the 2HKO from Zarude's Darkest Lariat as well as other attacks like Choice Band Zygarde-10%'s Thousdand Arrows. 28 Speed EVs let Necrozma outspeed Skarmory, with the rest put into Special Attack to boost its damage output.

This set best fits on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate Necrozma acting as a late-game sweeper. Dark-types like Hydreigon and Mandibuzz are problematic for this set, so wallbreakers like Cobalion and Azumarill can remove them. They both also threaten Chansey and overwhelm Slowking. Togekiss also counters these Dark-types and can rid Necrozma of status with Heal Bell. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Nihilego and the aforementioned Cobalion wears down threats like Hydreigon and Primarina. Similarly, entry hazard removers like Salamence, Rotom-W, and Tentacruel are great for keeping Necrozma from getting worn down, allowing it to conserve Moonlight PP when absolutely needed. Tentacruel can remove items from threats like Chansey with Knock Off and check Celesteela, while Salamence handles Zarude. Pivots like the previously mentioned Rotom-W and Zarude can bring Necrozma in against Pokemon it can set up on like Amoonguss, Tangrowth, and Scizor. They both also can shut down Hippowdon. Choice Scarf Hydreigon can revenge kill faster threats to Necrozma like Zarude as well as check Slowking. Assault Vest Tangrowth can serve as a great defensive pivot for Necrozma, switching in on powerful wallbreakers like Keldeo and Primarina.

doublesou.overview: Necrozma is one of the most powerful attackers in Doubles OU, threatening to 2HKO the entire tier with Expanding Force under Psychic Terrain at +1, which it can easily get to with the combination of Power Herb and Meteor Beam. With many common Psychic-resistant and -immune Pokemon in the metagame such as Heatran and Incineroar folding to its coverage options like Earth Power and Meteor Beam, Necrozma can easily plow through teams once if it gets the necessary support. It fits best of on hyper offense builds where the goal is to win games in as few turns as possible. Psychic Terrain support, which powers up Expanding Force and blocks priority, is critical to Necrozma's success, making either Tapu Lele or Indeedee-F mandatory teammates. Pokemon that can break through Steel- and Dark-types such as Urshifu-R and Heatran also make excellent partners, enabling Necrozma to keep using Expanding Force without worry. While Necrozma can end games once it gets going, it can be slowed down in multiple ways. Rillaboom and Tapu Fini can reliably switch in multiple times and reset Terrain, which heavily weakens Expanding Force, with the former also threatening Necrozma with Fake Out. Opposing Tailwind setters such as Zapdos and Mew also work well against it, as well as other forms of speed control users such as Icy Wind Kyurem-B and Trick Room Diancie. Additionally, while Pokemon such as Incineroar, Heatran, and Metagross must fear Necrozma's coverage, they can all switch into Expanding Force and slow it down.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Trick Room gives Necrozma a way to control its own Speed and decide the pace of the game, but it comes at the cost of valuable coverage. Weakness Policy is another way to boost that has a bigger payoff, but it's less reliable and Necrozma loses the one-time Meteor Beam nuke. Heat Wave is an alternative coverage option that's better against Genesect, but it is generally inferior to Earth Power's ability to hit Heatran and Incineroar. Stealth Rock can be used to secure chip damage on incoming foes, notably Incineroar, but it can be a momentum loss to uses and Necrozma prefers using its coverage to take down its foes.

Power Herb.description:
• Expanding Force is a decimating STAB attack under Psychic Terrain that is able to 2HKO almost the entire tier after a Special Attack boost, including threats such as Assault Vest Kyurem-B. It also has the added benefit of hitting both foes when Psychic Terrain is up, though keep in mind that it's much weaker if a different Terrain is active.

  • Meteor Beam, in conjunction with Power Herb, boosts Necrozma's Special Attack by one stage and cripples common switch-ins such as Assault Vest Kyurem-B and Incineroar.

  • Earth Power hits many common Psychic-resistant and -immune Pokemon such as Heatran, Metagross, and Incineroar for super effective damage.

  • Protect shields Necrozma for a turn, letting its partner reposition, set Tailwind, or target one of Necrozma's checks. It can also be used for stalling out adverse field conditions, such as Trick Room and opposing Tailwind.

  • Prism Armor helps keep Necrozma safe from Dragapult and Genesect's STAB moves. Notably, Necrozma can always take a Choice Specs-boosted Shadow Ball from Dragapult at full health.

  • A Modest nature is preferred to maximize Necrozma's damage output, but Timid can be used to always outspeed Heatran. A Quiet nature, along with shifting EVs from Speed to HP and lowering its Speed IVs, can be used if Necrozma is on a Trick Room-oriented build.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: These sets are for one of the final Battle Stadium Singles metagames for this generation. If you feel there is anything wrong or missing, please post in this thread.

HEAVY METAL (Bulky Dragon Dance).description:
Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Necrozma-DM deal damage to Zacian-C as it switches in.

  • Weakness Policy: With Weakness Policy, Necrozma-DM becomes a far more fearsome Dynamax sweeper.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 140 Def / 116 Spe: The given Speed EVs allow Necrozma-DM to outspeed Timid Yveltal after one Dragon Dance, while surviving 2 hits from Zacian-C 73.6% of the time.

Support.description:
EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe This spread avoids a 2HKO from Zacian-C's Close Combat.

  • 252 HP / 140 Def / 116 Spe: This spread sacrifices some bulk to outspeed Calyrex-S after paralysis, while still avoiding a 2HKO from Adamant Zacian-C 73.6% of the time.

Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
EV Spreads

  • 140 HP / 252 Atk / 116 Spe with Adamant: The Speed EVs allow Necrozma-DM to outspeed Timid Yveltal after Dragon Dance.

  • 60 HP / 252 Atk / 196 Spe with Jolly: With some bulk sacrificed, this spread allows Necrozma-DM to outspeed Marshadow and Eternatus after Dragon Dance.

Cosmic Power.description:
Items

  • Rocky Helmet: This item is Necrozma-DM's best way of dealing daamage to Zacian-C while setting up.

  • Utility Umbrella: Utility Umbrella ensures that Necrozma-DM can recover 50% of its health, even under Kyogre's rain.

Calm Mind.description:
• With this set, Necrozma-DM utilizes its great bulk and serviceable Special Attack to become a rather threatening Calm Mind sweeper.

  • Stored Power already matches Photon Geyser's Base Power after activating Weakness Policy and getting one Calm Mind boost, or after getting three Calm Mind boosts. Continually increasing its Base Power also effectively bypasses Unaware.

  • Heat Wave can be used as coverage for Ferrothorn, other Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C.

  • This set uses Dynamax particularly well , as Stored Power becomes a 130 BP Max Mindstorm, and Max Steelspike's Defense boosts contribute to both Necrozma-DM’s survivability and Stored Power's Base Power.

Items

  • Weakness Policy is the preferred item, providing huge boosts to both Necrozma-DM's Special Attack and Stored Power's base power upon taking a super effective attack.

  • Leftovers can be used to provide some passive recovery, better conserving Necrozma-DM's limited Morning Sun PP.

  • Kee Berry also deserves a mention, as the Defense boost pairs nicely with the Special Defense boosts from Calm Mind, increasing Necrozma-DM's survivability.

  • Utility Umbrella makes setting up against Kyogre a more feasible task thanks to ignoring the impact of rain. This lets Necrozma-DM take less damage and restore 50% of it's health against Kyogre.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Necrozma-DM can opt to run physically defensive set with a Rocky Helmet to more reliably wall physical threats like Rillaboom. Photon Geyser can be run over Earthquake on Necrozma-DM’s Dragon Dance set to target specific Pokemon like Nidoqueen, which threaten it with Ground-type moves, but is generally inferior to Earthquake’s coverage. Defensive sets can run Stealth Rock if their team lacks entry hazard setters, but being forced to give up one of its utility moves is usually not worth it.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Ground-types: Physically defensive Ground-types like Landorus-T can switch into Necrozma-DM and threaten it with Earthquake. However, they should be wary of Toxic.

Water-types: Bulky Water-types like Slowking, Slowbro, Tapu Fini, and Rotom-W can wall Necrozma-DM, Tapu Fini being notable for blocking Toxic and the rest for being able to burn it. However, Slowking and Slowbro must be wary of Knock Off, and Tapu Fini can be 2HKOed by a +1 Sunsteel Strike from offensive sets.

Steel-types: Steel-types like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn resist Sunsteel Strike and take insignificant amounts of damage from Necrozma-DM’s coverage. Skarmory and Corviknight can set up on defensive Necrozma-DM with Bulk Up and Iron Defense, and Ferrothorn can eternally outlast it with a combination of Leech Seed, Protect, and Leftovers.

Setup Sweepers: Powerful setup sweepers like Garchomp and Rayquaza can overwhelm even defensive Necrozma-DM with strong super effective moves, threatening all variants with a +2 Earthquake or a +1 V-create, respectively.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh resists Sunsteel Strike, is immune to Earthquake, and can hit back hard with Sacred Fire. However, Ho-Oh must fear heavy damage from Stone Edge from offensive sets.

Dragon Dance.description:
Weakness Policy Necrozma-DM is a fearsome wallbreaker and mid- to late-game cleaner. Dragon Dance is an excellent tool to boost Necrozma-DM’s damage while also fixing its subpar Speed tier. Sunsteel Strike is a powerful STAB move that threatens most of the tier at +1. Necrozma-DM’s coverage options help break down common Pokemon that resist it, with Earthquake hitting Heatran and opposing Necrozma-DM and Stone Edge hitting Ho-Oh and Corviknight, which otherwise completely wall it. Prism Armor allows Necrozma-DM to shrug off super effective attacks and activate Weakness Policy more easily, putting it in a position to sweep.

Necrozma-DM is best utilized on balance or bulky offense teams as a mid- or late-game cleaner, capable of shredding defensive cores after its checks have been removed. Necrozma-DM's solid defensive stats bolster teammates like Defensive Clefable and Assault Vest Tangrowth immensely, making for some very tough defensive cores. Many Pokemon such as Rillaboom, Victini, and Zeraora appreciate inheriting Necrozma-DM's high Attack stat and its ability to pressure common Pokemon such as Clefable. In turn, these Pokemon threaten the Water- and Steel-types that Necrozma-DM has trouble beating, such as Slowbro, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Necrozma-DM fears fast offensive Pokemon that carry super effective moves such as Rayquaza and Garchomp, whose sheer strength can overwhelm Necrozma-DM. Unaware users like Clefable are useful to ignore setup from these threats, and Pokemon with super effective priority such as Weavile can clean them up after chip.

Specially Defensive.description:
Necrozma-DM's typing, bulk, and access to reliable recovery make it a great specially defensive wall. Sunsteel Strike lets Necrozma-DM still do respectable damage, and Knock Off is a handy utility move to punish common switch-ins like Ho-Oh and remove damage boosting items from wallbreakers. Toxic cripples defensive Pokemon like Rotom-W and Landorus-T, while Thunder Wave cripples switch-ins like Heatran. Earthquake provides good coverage to hit offensive switch-ins like Heatran, but generally isn’t as useful as spreading status. Morning Sun improves Necrozma-DM’s longevity greatly, but must be used sparingly, for it has very low PP. Leftovers is necessary to provide much needed passive recovery.

Necrozma-DM can form well-rounded defensive cores with Pokemon such as Tangrowth and Buzzwole, who love to receive Necrozma-DM’s Special Defense stat. Both resist Ground, with the latter resisting Dark as well, which helps cover Necrozma-DM's weaknesses. Rotom-W and Necrozma-DM have good defensive synergy, with Rotom-W providing a resistance to Fire, an immunity to Ground, and sporting great bulk with an HP donation, while Necrozma-DM walls Grass-types such as Rillaboom, as it resists their STAB moves. Necrozma-DM is great at spreading status and removing items from switch-ins like Ho-Oh, which helps teammates that struggle with these threats pick up KOs on the weakened foes. Tapu Koko is a great Special Attack receiver to break past various Water-types that are not threatened by Necrozma-DM. Victini is a good choice to receive Attack and counter Steel-types such Skarmory and Corviknight, which wall Necrozma-DM and turn it into setup fodder, while also hitting Water-types with Bolt Strike.

Bulky Booster.description:
This set combines Necrozma-DM's offensive and defensive utility to create something that can take a hit and hit back hard. Dragon Dance allows Necrozma-DM to become a threatening cleaner versus weakened teams, while Swords Dance is helpful to wallbreak early-game. Sunsteel Strike is an excellent STAB move with great power and good coverage. Knock Off has great neutral coverage with Sunsteel Strike and weakens its checks by removing their items, while Stone Edge hits Flying-types such as Ho-oh and Earthquake hits Steel-types such as Heatran. Morning Sun and Leftovers give Necrozma-DM respectable longevity, but Morning Sun must be rationed so its low PP doesn't run out. Maximum Attack and an Adamant nature maximize damage output while the Speed investment outspeeds base 100 Speed foes after a Dragon Dance.

Pokemon such as Buzzwole and Tangrowth are excellent defensive presences if they receive Necrozma-DM's Special Defense stat, as they resist the Ground moves that threaten Necrozma-DM. Victini loves receiving Necrozma-DM's Attack stat and can threaten many Pokemon that Necrozma-DM can't beat like Ferrothorn and Skarmory. Entry hazard setters like Ferrothorn and Landorus-T help Necrozma-DM wear down its checks faster, with the latter being able to pivot it in with U-turn. This set struggles with Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus-T, so teammates like Rotom-W, Landorus-T, and Skarmory are recommended. Skarmory and Ho-Oh are especially troublesome Pokemon for Necrozma-DM to face, as both resist Sunsteel Strike and wall sets that lack Stone Edge, so Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Zeraora that can handle these threats for Necrozma-DM, while also keeping up momentum with pivot moves, make great partners. Magnezone is also a valuable partner, as it traps and removes Skarmory and Corviknight.

ubers.overview: Necrozma-DM is the premier Ubers Steel-type and one of the best Pokemon in the tier. It checks a myriad of powerful offensive threats, such as Xerneas, Calyrex-I, Galarian Darmanitan, and Eternatus. With a good ability in Prism Armor, useful utility options including Stealth Rock and status moves, and reliable enough recovery, Necrozma-DM functions as a critical glue Pokemon for the vast majority of teams. Offensive sets are also not to be underestimated, as Necrozma-DM packs an impressive base 157 Attack on top of its good bulk and has great boosting options in Swords Dance and Dragon Dance. Since it's one of the most common defensive Pokemon in the tier, powerful threats like Groudon, Zygarde, Zekrom, and Kyogre often look to take advantage of Necrozma-DM. As such, it is critical to pick Necrozma-DM's coverage options and teammates well in accordance with your team structure, lest you leave big openings in your defensive core.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Morning Sun is functionally identical to Moonlight. Sunsteel Strike can be run on the Specially Defensive set, trading higher PP and a flinch chance for more power and the ability to hit Shedinja. If Necrozma-DM does not need to run Stealth Rock due to a teammate such as Groudon, Clefable, or Blissey already having it, then a boosting move such as Dragon Dance or Swords Dance is possible on defensive sets as a surprise option to win late-game scenarios. Expert Belt and Knock Off can be run on Dragon Dance sets to secure the OHKO on Lunala. Colbur Berry is a decent option for offensive Dragon Dance sets to better take on Choice Scarf or Sucker Punch Yveltal.
