Bulk Up can be used to prevent Urshifu-R from being Choice-locked, but it forces Urshifu-R to use up a turn and drop Aqua Jet or Thunder Punch.

Checks and Counters

Water

Status: Burn reduces Urshifu-R's power, paralysis lowers its speed and lets more threats outspeed and KO it, and Toxic decreases Urshifu-R's wallbreaking turns.

Physically Defensive Walls: Pokemon like Slowbro, Galarian Corsola, Amoonguss, and Toxapex take very little from Urshifu-R's STAB moves and can punish it in return with status.

Revenge Killers: Faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Tapu Koko, and Thundurus-T outspeed and OHKO Urshifu-R with a super effective move.

Contact Damage: Pokemon that punish contact moves like Skarmory and Ferrothorn are annoying for Urshifu-R to deal with, as Surging Strikes forces it to take a lot of chip damage when hitting these targets.

Choice Band (Water).description:
Close Combat allows Urshifu-R to fend off Pokemon like Kyurem, Ferrothorn, Galarian Moltres, and Rotom-W. Surging Strikes hits Pokemon Close Combat can't dent, like Landorus-T, Aegislash, and Galarian Slowking. It also allows Urshifu-R to break Pokemon that can boost their Defense, like Iron Defense Corviknight, and break Shuckle's Sturdy, which lets Urshifu-R KO it before it sets any entry hazards. Aqua Jet allows Urshifu-R to pick off weakened foes or revenge kill faster Pokemon like Volcarona and Alolan Raichu. U-turn is nice for keeping momentum against foes like Celebi and Slowbro, which tank Urshifu-R's other moves. Thunder Punch hits Mantine, Pelipper, and other Water-types. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows Urshifu-R to outspeed Pokemon like Mimikyu, Tapu Lele, and Kyurem.

Urshifu-R greatly appreciates defensive pivots to absorb hits for it and bring it in safely. Slowking in particular is a great pivot, with Teleport and Future Sight to assist Urshifu-R. Teleport allows Slowking to bring Urshifu-R in safely, and Future Sight allows Urshifu-R to force progress in the Poison and Water matchups. Urshifu-R helps Slowking by checking threats like Kyurem and Weavile. Pelipper sets rain for Urshifu-R, allowing Surging Strikes to OHKO Pokemon like Aegislash and Clefable. Pelipper can also provide Defog and clear entry hazards like Spikes and Sticky Web, which limit Urshifu-R's chances to come in. Swampert and Gastrodon provide switch-ins to attacks from foes like Tapu Koko and Alolan Raichu with their Electric immunities; Swampert also sets Stealth Rock. Tapu Fini sets Misty Terrain for Urshifu-R, preventing it from getting statused, and also revenge kills Pokemon like Hydreigon and Garchomp with Choice Scarf. Rotom-W deserves a special mention as a Choice Scarf user, being able to check threats like Thundurus-T and Zapdos. Wallbreakers like Crawdaunt pressure checks to Urshifu-R like Slowbro and Toxapex. Crawdaunt especially can help in the Psychic matchup with its Psychic immunity. Other Knock Off users like Toxapex are incredibly helpful to remove opposing Leftovers and Rocky Helmet. On a weatherless team, it is a good idea to use another wallbreaker like Volcanion that can beat Steel-types, since Urshifu-R has a lot more trouble OHKOing Pokemon like Aegislash without rain.

Protective Pads.description: With high Attack and Speed, Urshifu-R serves as a powerful offensive threat with STAB moves like Surging Strikes, which pressures walls like Hippowdon, Buzzwole, and Mudsdale while ignoring Defense boosts. Close Combat lets Urshifu-R threaten Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Melmetal, as well as broadly damaging Water-resistant foes like Hydreigon, Rotom-W, and Seismitoad. U-turn allows Urshifu-R to escape defensive Pokemon it struggles to break through, like Toxapex, while maintaining momentum. No Retreat can be used instead to turn it into a sweeper. However, since Urshifu-R will be unable to switch out after using No Retreat, it is wise to make sure defensive checks like Haze Toxapex have been removed beforehand. Urshifu-R has several options for its last moveslot: Taunt can stop opposing setup sweepers like Reuniclus or prevent Urshifu-R from taking a status move, Aqua Jet allows Urshifu-R to revenge kill weakened foes, notably Aerodactyl, and Thunder Punch gives coverage against Pokemon like Gyarados and Slowking that otherwise don't fear it. Using Protective Pads keeps Urshifu-R safe from chip damage from Iron Barbs and Rocky Helmet users, which is especially helpful against Ferrothorn, which could otherwise switch into Surging Strikes and chip Urshifu-R with every hit. Urshifu-R supports teammates like Thundurus-T and Rotom-H that struggle against Tyranitar and Ground-types. It benefits from teammates like Heatran and Rillaboom that can pressure opposing Grass- and Electric-types. Entry hazard setters like Ferrothorn and Seismitoad can help weaken checks such as Buzzwole. Due to its lack of recovery, Urshifu-R also benefits from entry hazard removers like Corviknight and Tornadus-T to keep it from getting worn down when pivoting. Urshifu-R can also be used on rain teams, where teammates like Pelipper and Kingdra benefit greatly from its ability to remove Ferrothorn.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Urshifu-R can use Protective Pads alongside Taunt, allowing it to disturb defensive presences like Toxapex and Tapu Fini while maintaining momentum with U-turn without being subject to chip damage from using its contact moves. Bulk Up sets using Electrium Z can be used to lure in Toxapex, Tapu Fini, Slowbro, and Slowking, but they can often falter against fast-paced offensive teams and struggle to set up against defensive teams. In addition, the set requires multiple Bulk Ups to achieve success due to the initial lack of power.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Toxapex, Tapu Fini, Slowbro, and Slowking are incredibly annoying to Urshifu-R, as they resist its STAB moves and can retaliate with a Scald burn or threaten it with their other STAB moves. Toxapex and Tapu Fini can also remove Urshifu-R's Choice Band with Knock Off, while Slowbro and Slowking can gain momentum with Teleport. However, Tapu Fini can be chipped easily, and Slowbro and Slowking are smacked by U-turn.

Grass-types: Tangrowth and Amoonguss easily take anything Urshifu-Rbcan throw at them, although the latter dislikes Zen Headbutt. Both can also put Urshifu-R to sleep or use Giga Drain to dispatch it. Offensive Grass-types like Rillaboom, Serperior, and Kartana, while not safe switch-ins, are great revenge killers to Urshifu-R.

Faster Pokemon: Urshifu-R's average Speed tier means that faster Pokemon like Mega Diancie, Tapu Koko, Mega Medicham, and Zeraora can easily outrun and KO it. However, they are not safe switch-ins.

Mega Latias: Mega Latias eats both Surging Strikes and Close Combat comfortably while not fearing Future Sight and denting Urshifu-R with Psyshock. However, it takes a decent amount from U-turn.

Contact Damage and Status: Rocky Helmet, Garchomp's Rough Skin, and Ferrothorn's Iron Barbs severely damage Urshifu-R if it locks into Surging Strikes. Zapdos's Static and Volcarona's Flame Body similarly cripple it with paralysis or a burn.

Choice Band.description:
Urshifu-R's high-powered STAB moves, in conjunction with its decent Speed tier and U-turn, make it a solid early-game wallbreaker. In addition, Unseen Fist makes Urshifu-R difficult to scout properly despite being Choice-locked. U-turn dents Slowbro and Slowking while allowing Urshifu-R to keep momentum against Pokemon it can't touch, such as Toxapex, Tangrowth, and Tapu Fini. Aqua Jet lets Urshifu-R revenge kill faster Pokemon and setup sweepers like Mega Diancie, weakened Tapu Koko, and Volcarona. Zen Headbutt dents Toxapex and Amoonguss, which have no issue taking Urshifu-R's STAB moves.

Urshifu-R fits on offense teams that appreciate its great power and ability to maintain momentum with U-turn. Because of its inability to damage Toxapex, Tangrowth, and Tapu Fini with its STAB moves, Urshifu-R mandates Future Sight support from Slowking, Slowbro, or Galarian Slowking. Water-types like Toxapex, Slowking, and Tapu Fini can easily take Urshifu-R's STAB moves, so Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Kartana, and Rillaboom make for solid teammates. Tapu Koko is also notable for handling Zapdos, which can often shut down Urshifu-R with paralysis. Pokemon like Heatran, Corviknight, and Mega Scizor deal with Grass-types like Tangrowth and Amoonguss. The latter two also form potent VoltTurn cores that let their team keep momentum and maintain offensive pressure against the opposing team.

cap.comments:
Other Options

Protective Pads can be used to avoid common contact-punishing Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Zapdos, and Rocky Helmet Tomohawk, Skarmory, and Buzzwole. A Choice Scarf variant can also be run, as it turns Urshifu-R into a fast revenge killer and tool against hyper offense teams, being able to easily revenge kill the likes of Cawmodore, Arctozolt, and Weavile. However, the power loss of not running Choice Band will make Urshifu-R unable to break through Tapu Fini, Arghonaut, and Buzzwole.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Walls: Dragonite, Tomohawk, and Buzzwole are able to switch into Urshifu-R's attacks with relative ease and force it out with their STAB options or punish it with Rocky Helmet in the case of the latter two.

Bulky Water-types: Toxapex, Tapu Fini, and Slowbro can safely switch into both of Urshifu-R's STAB moves and force it to switch out; however, Tapu Fini gets worn down relatively quickly if Urshifu-R is running Thunder Punch. Arghonaut resist Urshifu's Surging Strikes and narrowly avoids the 2HKO from Thunder Punch, but it cannot safely switch into Close Combat.

Grass-types: Bulky Grass-types such as Tangrowth, Amoonguss, and Ferrothorn are able to switch into Urshifu's Water-type attacks, though the latter is risky as it is OHKOed by Close Combat. Meanwhile, offensive Grass-types such as Rillaboom, Kartana, and Jumbao are able to easily threaten Urshifu-R out with their powerful STAB attacks, though the former two cannot switch directly into it.

Faster Pokemon and Priority: Faster Pokemon such as Zeraora, Tornadus-T, Dragapult, and Tapu Koko are able to revenge kill Urshifu-R due to their higher Speed and their super effective moves or strong special attacks.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Urshifu-R is a threatening wallbreaker; its high base power STAB moves and stellar Attack stat in tandem with Choice Band make it incredibly hard to safely switch into. U-turn allows for Urshifu-R to keep momentum as well as chip Slowking and Jumbao. Aqua Jet allows Urshifu-R to revenge kill Volcarona and weakened Cawmodore, Weavile, and Garchomp. Thunder Punch is an option that allows Urshifu-R to work around its usual bulky Water-type checks such as Slowking, Toxapex, and Tapu Fini. An Adamant nature can be used if more power is desired, but this leaves Urshifu-R outsped by the likes of Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Jumbao.

Urshifu-R appreciates being paired up with Weavile, Dragapult, and Kartana, as they are able to clean through opposing teams after it has weakened down walls like Toxapex and Ferrothorn. These Pokemon also appreciate being brought in for free via U-turn. Pokemon such as Landorus-T and Corviknight make for a stellar combination with Urshifu-R, as they are able to pivot it in safely and can deal with the Electric- and Fairy-types that threaten it out, respectively. Slowking and Galarian Slowking are able to help Urshifu-R break through the likes of Toxapex, Arghonaut, and Buzzwole thanks to Future Sight. Urshifu-R's weakness to Grass-types such as Kartana, Rillaboom, and Jumbao make pairing it up with Grass-resistant Pokemon like Astrolotl and Corviknight pivotal, while other Steel-types like Heatran, Ferrothorn, and Equilibra can help ward off threatening Psychic- and Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis covers a Pokemon in a very new metagame. The metagame may shift rapidly. If you have any suggestions for this analysis, please post them in the current Battle Stadium Singles Analysis Thread.

Viability Ranking: A- Rank

Reserved for Pokemon that are fantastic in the Battle Stadium Singles metagame, and can sweep, support, or wall significant portions of the metagame. These Pokemon require less support than most others to be used effectively and have few flaws that can easily be overlooked when compared to their positive traits.

For more information on viability rankings, check out the full rankings here.

Focus Sash.description:
• This Urshifu-R does a great job of checking Dynamaxed physical threats such as Cinderace and Landorus-T, with Counter taking care of them as long as Focus Sash is intact.

  • Close Combat's power makes it a great complementary STAB move with Surging Strikes.

  • Aqua Jet's priority ensures that even Focus Sash foes that survive Counter will usually lose the matchup.

  • Surging Strikes is not only Urshifu-R's strongest Water-type STAB attack, but it also lets Urshifu-R break through Focus Sash and ignore Intimidate Attack drops.

Choice Attacker.description:
• Surging Strikes is a powerful STAB attack that lets Urshifu-R blast through Focus Sash Pokemon and ignore Intimidate.

  • Despite its good physical bulk, Urshifu-R prefers to maximize its damage with a STAB Close Combat.

  • Thunder Punch is Urshifu-R's best hope against Tapu Fini and Gyarados.

  • U-turn is great for pivoting while also enhancing Urshifu-R's lead potential.

  • Aqua Jet is useful for picking off weakened threats when using the Choice Band set.

  • Aerial Ace ensures that Urshifu-R can increase its Speed while Dynamaxed with Max Airstream.

Items

  • Choice Scarf lets Urshifu-R perform better against Cinderace and Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and is a good revenge killer in general.

  • Choice Band gives Urshifu-R a huge boost in power, being able to OHKO offensive Mimikyu and Dynamaxed offensive Landorus-T with Surging Strikes.

4 Attacks Dynamax User.description:
• With Aerial Ace, Urshifu-R can be a threatening Dynamax attacker thanks to Max Airstream's Speed boost. Acrobatics can be used instead if using Weakness Policy, for a stronger attack against Grass-types after Weakness Policy is consumed.

  • This Urshifu-R is focused on sweeping, so Close Combat's power is worth it despite the Defense drop.

  • Surging Strikes is useful for busting through Focus Sash and ignoring Intimidate.

  • Thunder Punch is needed for Urshifu to have a fighting chance against Tapu Fini and Gyarados.

  • Iron Head's Defense boost as Max Steelspike is great for surviving against physical threats like Life Orb Mimikyu and works particularly well with Weakness Policy.

  • Both Dynamax and Gigantamax formes of Urshifu-R are viable. With just Dynamax, Urshifu-R can further boost the power of its Water-type attacks with the Rain set up from Max Geyser. However, Gigantamax Urshifu-R can ruin Max Guard stalling tactics with G-Max Rapid Flow.

Items

  • Weakness Policy takes advantage of Urshifu-R's many weaknesses while Dynamaxed

  • Life Orb's power boost makes Urshifu-R more useful when not Dynamaxed.

godlygift.comments:
Other Options

Thunder Punch can be used on the Choice Band set to hit a Defense-donated Slowking, though it still fails to properly damage it without support and has to forgo either Aqua Jet or Ice Punch. Bulk Up turns Urshifu-R into a setup sweeper, but this comes at the opportunity cost of forgoing a strong pivot. Taunt can shut down its defensive checks like Skarmory, Giratina, and Buzzwole by denying their recovery or attempts at crippling Urshifu-R with status.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Water-types: Slowbro, HP-donated Tapu Fini, and Defense-donated Slowking have huge physical bulk and the defensive typing to shrug off both of Urshifu-R's STAB combination reliably. Slowbro and Slowking also possess incredible longevity between Slack Off + Regenerator, making them harder to whittle down with U-turn.

Physically Bulky Pokemon: HP-donated Skarmory, Buzzwole, and Clefable can withstand Urshifu-R's attacks consistently thanks to their typing and reliable recovery. Giratina in particular possess a unique defensive typing that makes it unfazed by any Urshifu-R's attacks and can cripple it back with Will-O-Wisp.

Faster Revenge Killers: Without Choice Scarf or a Speed donation, Urshifu-R's middling Speed tier can be quite apparent; it is easily revenge killed by fast foes like Tapu Koko, Zeraora, Mewtwo, and Yveltal. Even with Choice Scarf, faster Choice Scarf users such as Kartana can still outrun it. They have to be cautious of being put into KO range of Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet, however.

Contact Effects: If not running Protective Pads, all of Urshifu-R's attacks, especially the multi-hit nature of Surging Strikes, can be punished by common roadblocks like Iron Barbs Ferrothorn, Static Zapdos, and Rocky Helmet from the likes of Tangrowth and Buzzwole.

Offensive Pivot (Any).description:
Urshifu-R is one of the best offensive pivots thanks to the combination of typing, high Base Power attacks with great coverage, and U-turn to generate momentum. Its dual STAB combination threatens to deal at least neutral damage to most Pokemon, with Close Combat also nailing foes like Zamazenta-C, Kyurem-B, and Ferrothorn, while Surging Strikes takes care of Ho-Oh, Landorus-T, and Victini. Its typing and natural bulk also lets it act as a team's emergency check to prominent threats like Necrozma-DM, Calyrex-I, Weavile, and Volcarona. Aqua Jet is used to pick off faster threats like Pheromosa, Tapu Koko, Sand Rush Excadrill, and a Speed-donated Heatran and Landorus-T, while Ice Punch can be used to OHKO Dragon-types like Rayquaza and Garchomp and is Urshifu-R's strongest attack to hit Giratina. Choice Band turns it into a wallbreaker, notably capable of OHKOing defensive Ho-Oh and 2HKOing Lunala and offensive Necrozma-DM, and is an especially great item with a Speed donation. Choice Scarf allows Urshifu-R to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Kartana, Zeraora, and Mewtwo and revenge kill a boosted Kyurem-B; it most often runs Choice Scarf when taking a dump stat. Protective Pads can be used to keep Urshifu-R healthy, letting it safely fire off attacks or pivot out of foes such as Iron Barbs Ferrothorn, Rough Skin Garchomp, Static Zapdos, and Rocky Helmet users like Tangrowth, Skarmory, and Buzzwole.

Urshifu-R fits in on any offensive team archetype, ranging from bulky offense to hyper offense. It appreciates Attack donation from gods like Necrozma-DM and Rayquaza, but also loves the Speed donation from gods like Pheromosa, Mewtwo, and Zamazenta-C. However, Urshifu-R's reliability to perform well regardless of which stat it receives means it can easily be placed into less valuable teamslots like Rayquaza's Special Defense. Weavile is an incredible partner, as they can overwhelm a shared check in Tapu Fini together and it appreciates Urshifu-R's ability to bring it in on Slowking, Slowbro, and Giratina safely with U-turn. Tapu Koko forms a strong VoltTurn core with Urshifu-R, as it can bring the latter in safely on Ground-types like Landorus-T and Groudon, and, in return, Urshifu-R can bring Tapu Koko in on bulky Water-types like Slowking and Tapu Fini. Tapu Koko can also lure in Gastrodon and significantly damage it with Grass Knot, which opens up Urshifu-R to use its Water-type attacks freely. Due to its propensity of getting threatened by faster threats like Tapu Koko, Mewtwo, and Kartana, a solid defensive backbone consisting of teammates like Landorus-T, Heatran, and Tornadus-T, respectively, is needed; moreover, Landorus-T and Tornadus-T provide pivoting with U-turn, while Ferrothorn lays Spikes down to punish the foe's switches that Urshifu-R tend to force.

doublesou.overview: Urshifu-R is one of the most threatening offensive Pokemon in Doubles, possessing a monstrous base 130 Attack, a great offensive typing, and the unique ability to bypass most traditional defensive counterplay such as Intimidate, Protect, and Defense boosting thanks to the combination of Unseen Fist ignoring protection and Surging Strikes's guaranteed critical hits. This makes it one of the strongest candidates to answer metagame staples like Kyurem-B, Incineroar, Porygon2, and Diancie. Due to Urshifu-R's excellent offensive prowess, defensive answers are limited to mainly just Amoonguss and Tapu Fini, two Pokemon that resist all of its STAB attacks. Instead, it is often answered offensively by the likes of Rillaboom, Dragapult, and Necrozma. Urshifu-R is held back by a fairly middling Speed tier, meaning pairing it with speed control and priority will be very helpful. As such, Zapdos and Naganadel are excellent partners, providing Tailwind support and a way to match up well against Water-types. Other examples of good teammates include Tapu Lele and Indeedee-F for providing Psychic Terrain, which keeps Urshifu-R safe from priority moves like Fake Out and Grassy Glide, and Heatran, which is excellent for hitting Grass-types.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band allows Urshifu-R to make the most out of its offensive potential, notably scoring the OHKO on physically defensive Porygon2, which Life Orb sets cannot. Urshifu-R can outrun the entire unboosted metagame with a Choice Scarf; however, this comes at a significant decrease in power, as it loses its ability to OHKO Porygon2 and Genesect. U-turn is a decently hard-hitting move that is an option over Protect on Choice Band or Choice Scarf sets that allows Urshifu-R to pivot out of unfavorable situations. This can be especially useful for the opposing Grass-types it baits in, letting it switch out to proper checks. An Adamant nature can be used to deal even more damage, but runs the risk of being outsped by Jolly Kyurem-B, Timid Tapu Lele, and opposing Urshifu-R.

Offensive.description:
• Surging Strikes is incredibly free to use thanks to its guaranteed critical hits bypassing any form of damage reduction, like Intimidate. It can easily pick up OHKOs on Incineroar, Landorus-T, and Diancie.

  • Close Combat is Urshifu-R's strongest attack, possessing the rare ability to OHKO Kyurem-B and Porygon2. Even neutral foes like Rillaboom and Volcanion will take a large amount of damage from it.

  • Aqua Jet is reliable priority that can pick off foes with low Defense like Landorus and Nihilego, while Ice Punch is useful for securing the OHKO on Zygarde and Dragapult.

  • Protect is important for keeping Urshifu-R safe from the Grass- and Electric-type attacks that it often baits in.

  • Life Orb allows Urshifu-R to switch moves and run Protect, but comes at the cost of recoil. 252 Speed EVs and a Jolly nature let Urshifu-R outspeed base 95s like Kyurem-B and Tapu Lele.

Urshifu-R has strong stats and an excellent offensive movepool, enabling it to function as perhaps the lone non-Restricted offensive Water-type that is not dependent on Dynamax in Series 11. Unseen Fist is a fantastic ability for an offensive Pokemon in VGC due to the ubiquity of Protect, and consequently Urshifu-R is able to put tremendous pressure on opposing teams that have limited options of mitigating Urshifu-R's damage output. Surging Strikes is Urshifu-R's best move, as being able to guarantee critical hits is fantastic in a metagame inundated with Intimidate users and screens setters, being able to OHKO Landorus-T and do heavy damage to or outright OHKO Incineroar. Close Combat offers a powerful secondary STAB move and can target Water-types and other Pokemon that resist Surging Strikes. Aqua Jet is a useful move to finish off weakened Pokemon and is oftentimes used to activate a partner Pokemon's Weakness Policy, such as Coalossal. Despite not Dynamaxing often, Urshifu-R opts to use its Gigantamax forme due to its ability to take out important Pokemon like Coalossal through Max Guard. Focus Sash is Urshifu-R's most common item and is useful to mitigate its mediocre bulk and defensive drops from Close Combat. However, while less common, Urshifu-R can run other items such as Mystic Water, Choice Band, and Choice Scarf to boost damage output or Speed and will opt for U-turn over Detect on Choice item sets.

In Series 11, Urshifu-R is most commonly used as an offensive support Pokemon on Coalossal teams, as it can utilize Aqua Jet to activate Coalossal's Weakness Policy and offer strong damage output to KO Pokemon weakened by G-Max Vocalith damage. The pair also have strong synergy, as Coalossal and Urshifu-R can threaten each other's most common checks, such as Landorus-T for Coalossal and Grass-types like Venusaur for Urshifu-R. The best choice for a Restricted Pokemon on these teams tends to be Zacian-C or Yveltal, and the rest of the team is typically filled out with Dragapult, Incineroar, and one of either Amoonguss or Rillaboom. However, Urshifu-R can also be a strong Pokemon on other teams that don't use Coalossal, as it still offers stellar offensive pressure that can compliment many Pokemon.

uu.overview: Zarude's great Speed alongside U-turn allows it to be an excellent pivot and revenge killer. Its high Speed enables it to outspeed common Pokemon such as Nihilego, Thundurus-T, and Excadrill, and its good bulk and defensive typing lets it check many dangerous threats such as Rotom-W, Slowking, and Hippowdon, while also discouraging Zygarde-10% from spamming Thousand Arrows. The ability to heal status conditions and HP with Jungle Healing can allow Zarude to consistently pivot around defensive Pokemon such as Swampert and Hippowdon. Zarude's ability to synergize with other common pivots like Thundurus-T, Slowking, and Moltres has made it one of the defining components of offensive teams. However, it often struggles to break defensive Pokemon, such as Skarmory, Tangrowth, and Salamence, due to them resisting Power Whip and taking minimal damage from Darkest Lariat. Many teams naturally fit multiple Grass-type resistant Pokemon such as Mandibuzz, Cobalion, and Moltres, leaving Zarude with limited opportunities to use its strongest STAB attack. If it is running Choice Scarf, Zarude can risk being locked into an undesirable move, losing momentum. Flame Body from Moltres and Rocky Helmet from Amoonguss and Cobalion can punish U-turn, forcing momentum to be sacrificed to use Jungle Healing. Zarude's inability to answer threats like Keldeo and Primarina as a Grass-type can strain building at times, limiting its flexibility compared to Tangrowth and Amoonguss.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Rock Slide allows Zarude to OHKO Moltres while also dealing good damage to Salamence. Choice Band allows Zarude to function as a powerful wallbreaker, suprising usual switch-ins like Crobat and Amoonguss with a 2HKO. However, the increased prediction-reliance is problematic, and it still struggles to break through Skarmory and Mandibuzz. A Bulk Up set with Jungle Healing, Acrobatics, and Darkest Lariat allows Zarude to deal heavy damage and potentially tank super effective hits. Taunt is an option that can completely shut down Chansey's recovery and prevent Roost from Salamence, but Zarude would have to give up Jungle Healing or valuable coverage.

Checks and Counters

Faster threats and Priority: Faster Pokemon such as Keldeo, Azelf, Lycanroc-D, and Choice Scarf Diggersby are able to put Zarude in a tough spot, outspeeding and dealing heavy damage to it. However, they must watch out to see if Zarude is running a Choice Scarf set. Priority from Mamoswine and Conkeldurr can pick off a chipped Zarude.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Tangrowth take little damage from Zarude's STAB attacks, while Tapu Bulu resists both. Amoonguss and Tangrowth can threaten Zarude out with Sludge Bomb, with Tapu Bulu threatening it out with Close Combat, or set up on it with Swords Dance.

Flying-types: Salamence, Mandibuzz, and Togekiss can switch into Zarude's attacks easily. Salamence can weaken Zarude's hits with Intimidate, while Mandibuzz and Togekiss resist both STAB attacks. Moltres has to watch its health around Zarude but it can threaten a burn with Flame Body and KO Zarude. Crobat and Noivern outspeed and heavily threaten Zarude.

Steel-types: Cobalion, Skarmory, and Celesteela all take minimal damage from Zarude's STAB attacks, with the former two being able to chip Zarude with Rocky Helmet. Bulky variants of Swords Dance Scizor can set up on Zarude and threaten it with Bullet Punch.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Zarude's STAB combination allows it to threaten many tier staples like Primarina, Excadrill, and Slowking. U-turn grabs momentum on usual switch-ins such as Celesteela and Salamence. Jungle Healing allows Zarude to remove status conditions from moves such as Toxic from Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-W, while restoring 25% of its health. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Zarude to not worry about entry hazards, letting it constantly pivot throughout the game. Jolly is the required nature on the set so that Zarude can outspeed Nihilego and Thundurus-T.

Zarude is commonly seen on balance and bulky offense due to the easy pivoting provided by Heavy-Duty Boots and its ability to act as a status sponge against Toxic from Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-W. Secondary pivots like Moltres, Thundurus-T, and Swampert all form potent pivoting cores with Zarude. Moltres appreciates Zarude luring in Grass- and Steel-types like Amoonguss, Scizor, and Skarmory, while Thundurus-T heavily pressures Celesteela and Moltres. Swampert can pivot into attacks from Celesteela and set entry hazards for Zarude to soften up Pokemon like Amoonguss with Stealth Rock. Other entry hazard setters like Cobalion and Excadrill also set Stealth Rock and appreciate Zarude dealing with Water-types such as Slowking and Swampert, while Zarude appreciates them dealing with Scizor and Rotom-H. Slowking and Celesteela provide a strong defensive backbone to support Zarude, checking threats like Azelf, Salamence, and Cobalion that hinder it. Zygarde-10%, Mamoswine, and Azelf are wallbreakers that appreciate Zarude bringing them in on Salamence, Tangrowth, and Amoonguss, as they often have trouble switching in safely due to their frailty.

Choice Scarf.description:
Zarude's high Speed allows it to be a great user of Choice Scarf that can revenge kill Pokemon such as Keldeo and Azelf in addition to boosted sweepers such as Gyarados and Dragon Dance Necrozma. Power Whip OHKOes Lycanroc-D and Keldeo. Darkest Lariat is Zarude's strongest Dark-type STAB move and can hit Jirachi and Azelf for huge damage. U-turn allows Zarude to pivot out on potential switch-ins such as Tangrowth and Salamence, allowing it to gain momentum. Close Combat is able to hit Cobalion, an otherwise easy switch-in, for heavy damage. Jungle Healing can get rid of status conditions such as a burn from Moltres's Flame Body and Slowking's Scald while regaining HP so that Zarude can be used in the long run in a battle but it is not ideal to lock into. It also allows Zarude to act as a reliable status sponge if it takes a Knock Off when Choice Scarf is not needed.

Choice Scarf Zarude is a solid pivot and revenge killer on bulky offense teams. It appreciates additional pivots such as Moltres, Slowking, and Thundurus-T that can form momentum cores and pivot out of unfavorable matchups. For example, Moltres can bring Zarude in on Water-types such as Slowking and Swampert. Entry hazard control from the likes of Salamence, Excadrill, and Mandibuzz allows Zarude to consistently pivot without worrying about hazard damage. They can also check threats like Scizor and Tapu Bulu. Thundurus-T, Keldeo, and Nidoking are wallbreakers that appreciate Zarude's pivot support and its ability to check Pokemon such as Swampert, with the wallbreakers KOing Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Skarmory in return. Swampert is an entry hazard setter that appreciates Zarude dealing with Keldeo, Gyarados, and Hydreigon for it, while Swampert can set Stealth Rock in return and also help deal with Pokemon like Salamence. Primarina and Azumarill can help deal with some of Zarude's checks such as Salamence.

ubers.overview: Zarude provides solid role compression in Ubers. It checks a lot of threats, such as Calyrex-S, Groudon, Calm Mind Kyogre, and Zekrom, as well as more passive Pokemon like Necrozma-DM and Ferrothorn depending on its set. Its high base Speed lets it get the jump on a lot of targets like positive-natured base 90s with a good amount of investment and slower targets like Choice Band Dracovish with minimal investment. Its typing also gives it resistances to strong offensive types like Electric, Ground, Ghost, and Water, giving it a wide range of uses depending on what it wants to check. Its typing also comes with a lot of weaknesses, though, leaving it susceptible to getting lured by niche coverage moves on Pokemon like Calyrex-S and Groudon while also being weak to coverage commonly thrown out by the top Dark-type in the metagame, Yveltal.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

U-turn can be used as a pivoting option, maintaining momentum even if Zarude is crippled by Calyrex-S's Trick, but losing Bulk Up makes Zarude fairly susceptible to strong wallbreakers like Zygarde.

Checks and Counters

Eternatus: With access to strong super effective coverage, Dragon Tail, and Toxic, Eternatus can force a lot of damage on Zarude while deterring setup and taking minimal damage from even boosted Darkest Lariat.

Xerneas: Defensive Xerneas completely shuts down Zarude, and Geomancy variants can use it as setup fodder.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh can threaten a lot of damage on Zarude with Brave Bird and Sacred Fire and phaze Bulk Up variants with Whirlwind.

Defensive Fighting-types: With their recovery options and great natural bulk, Buzzwole and Zamazenta-C can both switch into Zarude multiple times and force it out with their strong STAB options.

Offensive Fighting-types: Marshadow, Urshifu-S, and Pheromosa all can threaten Zarude with Close Combat and force it out, but they can be quickly worn down if switched in on an attack.

Amoonguss and Ferrothorn: Unlike other Grass-types that can't offensively threaten Zarude, Iron Defense + Body Press Ferrothorn pressures it and weakens it with Iron Barbs, and Amoonguss can threaten it with Sludge Bomb or remove its boosts with Clear Smog.

Specially Defensive.description:
Bulk Up and Darkest Lariat let Zarude break Zygarde, bypassing defensive sets trying to set up Coil against it and checking offensive sets more reliably. Jungle Healing makes Zarude a true counter to Dragon Dance + Toxic Zygarde sets. It also allows Zarude to switch into Thunder Wave Necrozma-DM and be a status absorber in many cases. Alternatively, Synthesis gives Zarude more healing, letting it better check Choice Specs Calyrex-S and other Pokemon. 136 Speed EVs give Zarude the jump on positive-natured base 90s like Kyogre and Groudon, with maximum HP for overall bulk and the rest of the EVs in Special Defense to better check Calyrex-S and Kyogre.

Ho-Oh is a great natural partner, scouting what move a Choice-locked Calyrex-S uses and absorbing Trick so Zarude continues consistently checking it as well as other wallbreakers like Kyogre. Offensive Yveltal can be used with Zarude, utilizing Hone Claws to break through Eternatus so Zarude can sweep; it also appreciates Zarude checking Calyrex-S. Groudon is an important teammate if Synthesis is used, increasing Synthesis's recovery and activating Zarude's Leaf Guard. A cleric like Blissey, Xerneas, or Calyrex-S can also make up for Jungle Healing being dropped for Synthesis. Necrozma-DM is another excellent partner, checking Xerneas and Eternatus, which easily threaten Zarude. With Zarude outspeeding Groudon and checking opposing Zygarde, your own Zygarde can run a Dragon Dance set instead of a defensive one. Eternatus checks Fighting-types like Marshadow and switches into Ho-Oh, making it a great and almost mandatory teammate to check some of the biggest threats to Zarude.

Physically Defensive.description:
Physically defensive Zarude goes all-in on using its typing and Bulk Up to check dangerous physical threats, namely Zekrom, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Zygarde, and non-Life Orb and non-Fire-type coverage Groudon. Darkest Lariat lets Zarude beat Coil Zygarde and Bulk Up Groudon one-on-one while also reliably damaging Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Power Whip gives Zarude a better matchup against Life Orb Groudon, at worst letting Zarude net some damage against it. Power Whip is also helpful because Zarude can act as a last-ditch Kyogre check, although it can't take repeated hits very well. Synthesis is needed to check Life Orb Zekrom, as Zarude very narrowly takes it on with the extra recovery compared to Jungle Healing. 16 Speed EVs let Zarude outrun Adamant maximum Speed Dracovish, while the rest maximize its physical bulk.

As physically defensive Zarude is a Dark-type that fails to reliably check Choice Specs Calyrex-S, Yveltal is a pivotal teammate that beats it as well as other foes such as Lunala and Special Attacking Giratina-O. Groudon is an incredible teammate for providing reliable sun to boost Zarude's Synthesis recovery and make it immune to status. Fighting-types like Marshadow, Urshifu-S, and Buzzwole are some physical attackers that Zarude can't handle, meaning teammates like Eternatus and Xerneas are helpful for covering those matchups. Without any Speed or Special Defense investment, Zarude can't reliably pressure Kyogre. This makes teammates like Blissey and specially defensive Eternatus necessary to have.

nationaldex.comments:
Other Options

Zarude can utilize Leftovers for extra longevity so it isn't overly reliant on Jungle Healing for recovery; however, this greatly reduces its wallbreaking power. Grassium Z can also be used in order to beat Unaware Clefable and and have an even stronger nuke; however, you sacrifice its matchup versus much more common threats like Zapdos, Heatran, and Tangrowth. Heavy-Duty Boots is another option to repeatedly set up without being bothered by hazards, but you lose out on the power of Z-moves.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Pokemon such as Mega Mawile, Tapu Koko, and Mega Diancie can all either take a boosted hit from Zarude or outspeed it and KO. Mega Mawile in particular is an exceptional check due to Intimidate before Mega Evolving, good bulk, resistance to both of Zarude's moves, and the power to OHKO even after Defense boosts, which allow it to switch in multiple times and force it out. Unaware Clefable stonewalls Zarude and can use it as setup fodder. Clefable must be wary of Grassium Z though, and it must remain at full HP to avoid being 2HKOed by Power Whip.

Fire-types: Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, and Heatran can KO Zarude, but Zarude outspeeds them and can OHKO with a boosted Black Hole Eclipse. Heatran can stomach an unboosted Black Hole Eclipse and OHKO Zarude in return with Magma Storm or Inferno Overdrive. Both Moltres and Volcarona can burn Zarude with Flame Body, making it waste a turn removing the status instead of outright KOing them.

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Hawlucha, Galarian Zapdos, and Mega Lopunny all can switch into Zarude multiple times and threaten to KO it. Furthermore, Fighting-type coverage on the likes of Alakazam, Kartana, and Melmetal can force it out also.

Bug-types and Bug-type Coverage: Due to Zarude's crippling 4x Bug weakness, it is extremely prone to being U-turn fodder for the likes of Landorus-T and Rillaboom. Mega Scizor and Mega Heracross also force Zarude out due to their strong Bug-type STAB moves.

Ice-types: Weavile can revenge kill Zarude if brought in safely, but, due to its frailty, it struggles to switch in. Kyurem can force out Zarude and take a boosted Darkest Lariat, but it fears a boosted Z-Move. Both are also prone to Stealth Rock chip damage.

Entry Hazards: Entry hazards can easily overwhelm and wear Zarude down long term due to its reliance on its relatively poor recovery move.

Bulk Up.description:
Zarude functions as a late-game wincon that's hard to stop once it gets going, since the combination of Bulk Up and Jungle Healing bolsters its good bulk to outlast bulkier foes. Bulk Up and its amazing Speed tier also make it hard to revenge kill. It outpaces many common threats such as Volcarona, Kyurem, and Tapu Lele, even if it's outsped by common revenge killers such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and Greninja. However, Zarude faces competition as an offensive Grass-type from Rillaboom, Kartana, and Serperior due to it lacking immediate power. Jungle Healing allows it to shrug off crippling status, like paralysis and Toxic, and recover any chip damage it has sustained from Scald burns; however, it isn't a reliable source of recovery long term. Darkinium Z allows it to nuke would-be checks such as Zapdos, Mega Scizor, and Corviknight, and Darkest Lariat beats the likes of Iron Defense Skarmory and Corviknight by bypassing their Defense boosts. Power Whip is Zarude's strongest move, hitting Dark-resistant Pokemon such as Tyranitar, Clefable, and Tapu Fini. Furthermore, it lets Zarude hit neutral targets such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Tapu Lele much harder than Darkest Lariat.

Zarude fits on bulkier balance teams, which can provide it with long-term support in the form of entry hazard stacking and other sweepers. Strong hazard support from the likes of Toxic Spikes Toxapex and Spikes Skarmory is extremely beneficial to wear down Zarude's checks in the long run, such as Tangrowth and Unaware Clefable. Pokemon such as Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and Ash-Greninja appreciate Zarude breaking down bulkier teams and help its struggles with faster-paced teams. Other setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Clefable, Bulk Up Corviknight, and Mega Latias all appreciate Zarude weakening or KOing their checks, with Clefable especially enjoying it KOing Heatran and Mega Scizor. Zarude also needs sturdy Fire-resistant Pokemon because they force it to switch out or waste its Z-Move, so partners such as Toxapex, Mega Latias, and Heatran are greatly appreciated. Lastly, Pokemon such as Corviknight and Skarmory that can switch into revenge killers that threaten Zarude, such as Mega Lopunny, Hawlucha, Landorus-T, and Kartana, are required. Zarude’s typing gives it amazing defensive utility, allowing it to solidly check Ash-Greninja and switch into Slowbro and Slowking; however, Scald burns forcing it to use Jungle Healing can easily be taken advantage of. It can also reliably switch into Ground-types such as Gliscor and Garchomp and threaten them out. These defensive capabilities make it a good partner with the likes of Heatran, Gliscor, and Mega Diancie.

monotype.overview:
Dark

Zarude's Grass typing, good natural bulk, and favorable Speed tier make it a great check to Water- and Ground-types that would otherwise give Dark teams trouble such as Urshifu-R, Tapu Fini, and Nidoking. Thanks to this, it can be useful in matchups such as Water, Ground, and Rock. Jungle Healing and Taunt make Zarude a formidable stallbreaker as well, allowing it to use foes that rely on status ailments to wear it down such as Toxapex, Slowking, Slowbro, and Gastrodon as setup fodder while preventing them from using status moves like Recover and Haze. However, Zarude's Grass typing brings it many weaknesses, leaving it particularly weak to Pokemon like Blacephalon, Victini, and Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan. It also heavily struggles in matchups like Steel and Fire, as it mainly relies on Power Whip to deal damage. Its Speed tier is good, but not fast enough to outspeed many prominent fast attackers such as Tapu Koko, Dragapult, Weavile, and Cinderace, making it vulnerable to being revenge killed by them.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark

(Bulk Up) Choice Band significantly increases Zarude's damage output, giving it the means of 2HKOing Toxapex with Power Whip and specially defensive Celesteela with Darkest Lariat. However, Zarude then misses out on the ability to remove status conditions like burn and Toxic poison using Jungle Healing, which leaves it more easily crippled.

(Choice Scarf) Rock Slide may be considered, as it allows Zarude to revenge kill +1 Volcarona and pick off Fire- and Flying-types such as Cinderace and Dragonite, but Darkest Lariat gives better damage and coverage overall. A Choice Band set may also be considered, as it allows Zarude to terrorize slower teams such as rainless Water, Fairy, and sandless Ground teams, with the boost from Choice Band letting it threaten Toxapex, Tapu Bulu, and Landorus-T.

Grass

Rock Slide may be used over Power Whip in Choice Scarf sets to revenge kill Volcarona after a Quiver Dance boost, as well as dealing more damage to Flying-types like Dragonite, Zapdos, and Galarian Moltres, but Power Whip allows Zarude to pick off weakened threats like Clefable and OHKO Tapu Lele after Stealth Rock damage. Roseli Berry or Chople Berry can be considered in Bulk Up sets to survive a Fairy- or Fighting-type lure move and remove threats such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Zeraora, and opposing Zarude, but the lack of Leftovers hurts Zarude's ability to set up consistently. Substitute may also be used over Jungle Healing, as it also allows Zarude to avoid status, but it reduces Zarude's longevity and ability to set up multiple times in a match.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Walls: Zarude struggles to deal great damage to physically defensive walls such as Skarmory, Galarian Weezing, and Porygon2. In return, Skarmory is able to heal off its attacks with Roost and phaze it with Whirlwind, Galarian Weezing can weaken it with Strange Stream, and Porygon2 can weaken it with Ice Beam and use Teleport to bring in another teammate if Zarude switches out.

Grass-resistant Pokemon: Pokemon that resist Zarude's Power Whip such as Victini, Torkoal, and Buzzwole all threaten Zarude with their STAB moves while it struggles to deal massive damage to them. However, some foes that resist Power Whip such as Bisharp, Kyurem, and Hydreigon can all be hit super effectively by Drain Punch.

Physically Defensive Walls: Physically defensive Pokemon such as Celesteela and Mandibuzz take minimal damage from Zarude's attacks and threaten to chip it down.

Revenge Killers: Faster Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Blacephalon, Choice Scarf Weavile, and Choice Scarf Galarian Zapdos outspeed Zarude and OHKO it with a super effective move. Priority moves like First Impression from Golisopod will OHKO Zarude, while Ice Shard from Choice Band Weavile and Mamoswine can pick off Zarude if it is weakened.

Bulk Up (Dark).description:
Zarude can use Bulk Up on Water-types like Toxapex, Gastrodon, Slowking, and Slowbro, becoming a decent setup sweeper while increasing its already impressive physical bulk. Power Whip deals immediate damage to Water-types such as Urshifu-R, Slowbro, Tapu Fini, and Swampert. Taunt shuts down passive foes such as Galarian Corsola and Toxapex by preventing them from using status moves like Strength Sap and Haze. Drain Punch is an alternative over Taunt, hitting Steel- and Dragon-types like Bisharp, Kyurem, and Hydreigon super effectively. Jungle Healing gets rid of status ailments such as burn and Toxic poison while providing Zarude with useful longevity. Chople Berry enables Zarude to survive Fighting-type attacks from many threats such as Choice Scarf Terrakion, Keldeo, and Barraskewda and KO them back with Power Whip. Leftovers is another option over Chople Berry to provide passive recovery, letting Zarude heal off much more damage in conjunction with Jungle Healing. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows Zarude to outspeed foes like Mimikyu, Garchomp, and Tapu Lele.

Mandibuzz handles threats such as Scizor and Dragonite for Zarude due to its good bulk and typing allowing it to take multiple Fighting- and Bug-type attacks. It can also get rid of entry hazards for Zarude with Defog and pivot out with U-turn, giving it opportunities to use Bulk Up. Tyranitar's amazing special bulk coupled with Sand Stream allows it to take on threatening special attackers such as Choice Specs Dragapult, Blacephalon, and Alolan Ninetales. Its Sand Stream and Toxic support can also wear down foes quickly, which Zarude appreciates. Hydreigon is a mandatory wallbreaker for Zarude, as it's able to pressure many physically defensive walls such as Skarmory, Avalugg, and Bewear that give Zarude and the rest of Dark teams trouble. It can also pressure Dragon- and Fire-types such as Dragalge, Kyurem, and Torkoal for Zarude. Drapion can deal with Fairy-types such as Tapu Bulu, Clefable, and Alolan Ninetales, which Zarude finds difficult to beat, and provide Toxic Spikes support. Weavile is also a neat revenge killer for Zarude thanks to its Ice typing, taking out Dragon-types such as Dragapult, Dragonite, and Latias while picking off weakened foes like Tapu Koko with Ice Shard. It also covers Flying-types like Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Dragonite.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description:
Due to its above average Speed tier and excellent coverage, Zarude performs as a great Choice Scarf user for Dark teams, outspeeding and removing threats such as Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan, Urshifu-R, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Power Whip nails Water- and Ground-types such as Urshifu-R, Tapu Fini, and Mamoswine, as well as OHKOing Choice Scarf Tapu Lele after Stealth Rock and picking off threats such as Tapu Koko and Zeraora. Close Combat deals with Ice- and Steel-types such as Slush Rush Arctozolt and Choice Scarf Excadrill. U-turn lets Zarude preserve momentum, pivoting out of switch-ins such as Amoonguss, Toxapex, and Corviknight.

Zarude is walled by Flying-types such as Zapdos and Dragonite, so Weavile makes for an excellent teammate, as it deals with these threats with a Choice Band or Swords Dance set. Zarude can lure in and pivot out of bulky walls like Toxapex, Skarmory, Celesteela, Mantine, and Amoonguss, turning them into setup fodder for Pokemon such as Galarian Moltres and Hydreigon. Specially defensive Tyranitar checks special attackers like Blacephalon, Volcarona, and Hatterene and sets Stealth Rock to wear down the opposing team. Zarude can pivot Dragon Dance Tyranitar into bulkier Pokemon such as Mandibuzz, Zapdos, and Kyurem to facilitate its sweep. Mandibuzz checks physical attackers such as Dragonite, Tapu Bulu, and Buzzwole, utilizes Defog to improve Zarude's longevity, and pivots it in safely with U-turn. Drapion deals with Fairy-types such as Clefable and Hatterene, sets Toxic Spikes to wear down types such as Electric and Ice, and absorbs Toxic Spikes for it.

Grass

Zarude is the premier revenge killer and setup sweeper for Grass-type teams. Thanks to its Speed and bulk, it greatly improves the Steel-, Psychic-, and Ghost-type matchups. Its also an excellent late-game cleaner with a Choice Scarf set due to its wide movepool and Speed, only being outsped by a few revenge killers like Choice Scarf Weavile and Blacephalon. However, Choice Scarf Zarude has trouble breaking past physically defensive Pokemon like Porygon2 and Ferrothorn, while Bulk Up Zarude struggles with common revenge killers like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Dragapult. Zarude's coverage also makes it hard to break through some physical walls such as Skarmory and setup sweepers such as Hatterene and Corviknight, which can be threatening for Grass teams.

Choice Scarf (Grass).description:
Darkest Lariat removes Ghost- and Psychic-type threats such as Spectrier and Victini. Close Combat deals with Steel-, Ice-, and Dark-types such as Heatran, Galarian Darmanitan, and Hydreigon. U-turn allows Zarude to gain momentum, pivoting out of potential switch-ins such as Galarian Weezing, Celesteela, and Kommo-o. Choice Scarf allows Zarude to outspeed threats such as Dragapult, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Choice Scarf Galarian Darmanitan.

Ferrothorn is a good teammate, as it covers for Zarude's weakness to Ice and Fairy by taking on threats such as Kyurem and Hatterene, and it sets Spikes to wear down the opposing team further alongside U-turn. Rillaboom is an excellent wallbreaker that can deal with slower but bulkier walls such as Toxapex and Clefable, and it can pick off weakened threats such as Choice Scarf Blacephalon with Grassy Glide. Amoonguss covers for Zarude's Fighting weakness against Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu and Zeraora. Cradily is a great special wall that can take on threats such as Choice Specs Zapdos, Galarian Moltres, and Blacephalon, and it also sets Stealth Rock. Swords Dance Tapu Bulu can deal with walls such as Galarian Weezing, Celesteela, and Ferrothorn, improving the Poison, Flying, and Steel matchups, respectively.

Bulk Up (Grass).description:
Bulk Up Zarude can become an excellent late-game wincon against bulkier types such as Steel and Normal. Drain Punch gives Zarude longevity while threatening Steel- and Dark-types such as Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Hydreigon. Alternatively, Taunt stops phazers and hazers like Skarmory, Toxapex, and Mantine, which is useful in the Steel, Poison, and Flying matchups. Furthermore, Taunt also stops setup sweepers like Corviknight from boosting alongside it. Jungle Healing allows Zarude to shrug off status and provides recovery. Leftovers improves Zarude's longevity, allowing it to set up and wallbreak multiple times in a match.

Ferrothorn covers for Zarude's weaknesses to Ice and Fairy by checking threats like Weavile and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and sets Spikes to let Zarude break down defensive cores of Steel and Ghost teams more quickly. Rillaboom provides Grassy Terrain for additional recovery, which helps Zarude set up, and checks threats like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Clefable. Additionally, it can work together with Zarude to pressure defensive cores of Steel and Poison teams with a Choice Band set. Both Rillaboom and Ferrothorn can also utilize Knock Off to remove Leftovers from Zarude's checks in Celesteela and Heatran, allowing Zarude to overwhelm them more easily. Amoonguss can create setup opportunities for Zarude with Spore, and it can cover for Zarude's Fighting weakness against foes such as Gengar and Buzzwole. Cradily is a great special wall that can take on SubRoost Kyurem, Galarian Moltres, and Blacephalon, and provides Stealth Rock. Whimsicott provides a fast teammate, cripples passive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Celesteela with Switcheroo, provides a Dragon immunity and Fighting resistance, and threatens Kyurem behind a Substitute with Infiltrator.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf + Tough Claws is usable to surprise fast wallbreakers such as Tapu Koko and Barraskewda, but Grassy Surge sets are more consistent. Choice Band + Tinted Lens is another option in conjunction with a Grassy Terrain setter such as Tapu Fini, letting Zarude easily pass through Grass-resistant foes such as Zapdos, Latios, and Cinderace with either Power Whip or Grassy Glide. Choice Scarf + Regenerator is an option to provide longevity and make the most of Zarude's unique typing defensively, but it lacks the power of Choice Band sets.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Dark-resistant Foes: Kommo-o and Mandibuzz can reliably switch into any of Zarude's moves, even from Tough Claws variants, and force it out. Repeated pivoting can wear them down, however.

Physically Defensive Steel-types: Corviknight, especially with Intimidate, takes minimal damage from Zarude. Other Steel-types like Ferrothorn require significant chip damage for Zarude to break through them without Close Combat.

Flying-types: Resisting Grassy Glide, common Flying-types like Zapdos, Togekiss, and Mandibuzz can either outspeed and force out Zarude or completely wall it.

Faster Pokemon: Zarude often finds itself unable to threaten common fast pivots with Grassy Glide, such as Choice Scarf Jirachi and Talonflame. Both carry super effective moves to hit Zarude in return. Additionally, Zarude is forced out by U-turn users given its glaring 4x Bug weakness, especially Azelf, which replaces its Grassy Terrain with Psychic Terrain: this weakness often gives free momentum to offensive pivots, as they can freely use U-turn without taking Grassy Glide.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Zarude is a formidable offensive pivot and doubles as one of the strongest priority users in the metagame. With Choice Band and a Terrain-boosted Grassy Glide, Zarude can force out the majority of relevant wallbreakers, such as Tapu Koko and Azelf, as they risk getting OHKOed. U-turn capitalizes on the switches Zarude forces, bringing in offensive partners like Heatran. Power Whip is the strongest STAB move available, OHKOing or 2HKOing common defensive pivots like Swampert, Tapu Fini, Zapdos, and Toxapex. Darkest Lariat is a spammable STAB move that also bypasses Dauntless Shield boosts, scoring 2HKOs on Heatran, Mew, and Moltres. However, Close Combat is a strong alternative over either Power Whip or Darkest Lariat, allowing it to break through specific checks like Ferrothorn and Incineroar. An Adamant nature is preferred to augment the power of Zarude's attacks, notably having a better chance to OHKO Tapu Koko with Grassy Glide; however, Jolly is an option to outspeed Zapdos.

Zarude provides valuable utility including priority, Terrain control, and passive recovery, making it a great fit on balance and bulky offense teams. As Zarude cannot switch into most attackers, a strong defensive core often helps bring it in safely. Zarude also handily beats Swampert and Tapu Fini, making it a great partner for a multitude of wallbreakers, such as Heatran, Zapdos, and Tapu Koko. In return, Zarude gives them good switch-in opportunities by using U-turn on the Flying-types it invites in, mainly Corviknight and Mandibuzz. Zarude appreciates any teammates that can set entry hazards, chipping down foes like Ferrothorn and Corviknight into OHKO or 2HKO range. Teammates carrying Rocky Helmet such as Corviknight and Swampert also provide chip damage, and they can notably punish offensive pivots such as Landorus-T and Cinderace freely clicking U-turn on Zarude. Lastly, teammates running Knock Off such as Tapu Fini and Toxapex are useful to remove opposing Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots, respectively allowing Zarude to attack more freely and better chip walls—especially Flying-types—in combination with hazards.

Tough Claws.description:
Choice Band + Tough Claws Zarude is a fast and powerful wallbreaker that puts tremendous pressure on the opposing team. Darkest Lariat is its most consistent attack and 2HKOes most of the metagame, as bulky Dark-resistant foes are few and far between; it has the added benefit of bypassing Dauntless Shield. Power Whip is Zarude's strongest attack, securing the OHKO against offensive Garchomp and 2HKO against Toxapex, and provides important coverage against Tapu Fini. U-turn generates momentum against Zarude's few reliable checks such as Kommo-o and Mandibuzz; Mandibuzz, in particular, will be unable to use Roost and is susceptible to being worn down by repeated pivots. Close Combat secures the OHKO against Heatran and has a high chance to OHKO common Ferrothorn variants. Jolly is the preferred nature to reliably force out other fast offensive threats like Zapdos, Garchomp, and Tapu Lele, but Adamant still outspeeds fully invested base 90 Speed Pokemon, and it gets more favorable 2HKO odds against Ferrothorn and Skarmory.

Choice Band + Tough Claws Zarude functions best on pivot-heavy balance and offense teams, which can provide it with multiple switch-in opportunities. It pairs especially well with specially-oriented pivots like Azelf and Tapu Koko, as they can each pivot on their checks and put the other in an advantageous position. Defensive pivots like Corviknight and Blissey can switch in when Zarude gets forced out, and they safely bring it in against slower wallbreakers like Zapdos and Garchomp. Zarude struggles against bulky Dark-resistant foes like Kommo-o and Mandibuzz, making Fairy-type wallbreakers like Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko excellent partners. Physically defensive Steel-types like Intimidate Corviknight and Regenerator Ferrothorn hold up decently well against Zarude, so it pairs well with Zygarde-10% and Zapdos, which blow through them. Zarude greatly appreciates entry hazard and Knock Off support to weaken its checks and take advantage of the high number of switches it forces. Because Zarude is heavily threatened by U-turn, it risks getting forced out and pivoted on by faster threats such as Azelf, Talonflame, and Tapu Koko; reliable answers to these threats that do not need a turn to recover, like Regenerator Blissey and Heatran, are strongly recommended. As Zarude lacks any form of recovery, it appreciates reliable entry hazard removal to keep it healthy.

uu.overview: Zarude's great Speed alongside U-turn allows it to be an excellent pivot and revenge killer. Its high Speed enables it to outspeed common Pokemon such as Nihilego, Thundurus-T, and Excadrill, and its good bulk and defensive typing lets it check many dangerous threats such as Rotom-W, Slowking, and Hippowdon, while also discouraging Zygarde-10% from spamming Thousand Arrows. The ability to heal status conditions and HP with Jungle Healing can allow Zarude to consistently pivot around defensive Pokemon such as Swampert and Hippowdon. Zarude's ability to synergize with other common pivots like Thundurus-T, Slowking, and Moltres has made it one of the defining components of offensive teams. However, it often struggles to break defensive Pokemon, such as Skarmory, Tangrowth, and Salamence, due to them resisting Power Whip and taking minimal damage from Darkest Lariat. Many teams naturally fit multiple Grass-type resistant Pokemon such as Mandibuzz, Cobalion, and Moltres, leaving Zarude with limited opportunities to use its strongest STAB attack. If it is running Choice Scarf, Zarude can risk being locked into an undesirable move, losing momentum. Flame Body from Moltres and Rocky Helmet from Amoonguss and Cobalion can punish U-turn, forcing momentum to be sacrificed to use Jungle Healing. Zarude's inability to answer threats like Keldeo and Primarina as a Grass-type can strain building at times, limiting its flexibility compared to Tangrowth and Amoonguss.
uu.comments:
Other Options

Rock Slide allows Zarude to OHKO Moltres while also dealing good damage to Salamence. Choice Band allows Zarude to function as a powerful wallbreaker, suprising usual switch-ins like Crobat and Amoonguss with a 2HKO. However, the increased prediction-reliance is problematic, and it still struggles to break through Skarmory and Mandibuzz. A Bulk Up set with Jungle Healing, Acrobatics, and Darkest Lariat allows Zarude to deal heavy damage and potentially tank super effective hits. Taunt is an option that can completely shut down Chansey's recovery and prevent Roost from Salamence, but Zarude would have to give up Jungle Healing or valuable coverage.

Checks and Counters

Faster threats and Priority: Faster Pokemon such as Keldeo, Azelf, Lycanroc-D, and Choice Scarf Diggersby are able to put Zarude in a tough spot, outspeeding and dealing heavy damage to it. However, they must watch out to see if Zarude is running a Choice Scarf set. Priority from Mamoswine and Conkeldurr can pick off a chipped Zarude.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Tangrowth take little damage from Zarude's STAB attacks, while Tapu Bulu resists both. Amoonguss and Tangrowth can threaten Zarude out with Sludge Bomb, with Tapu Bulu threatening it out with Close Combat, or set up on it with Swords Dance.

Flying-types: Salamence, Mandibuzz, and Togekiss can switch into Zarude's attacks easily. Salamence can weaken Zarude's hits with Intimidate, while Mandibuzz and Togekiss resist both STAB attacks. Moltres has to watch its health around Zarude but it can threaten a burn with Flame Body and KO Zarude. Crobat and Noivern outspeed and heavily threaten Zarude.

Steel-types: Cobalion, Skarmory, and Celesteela all take minimal damage from Zarude's STAB attacks, with the former two being able to chip Zarude with Rocky Helmet. Bulky variants of Swords Dance Scizor can set up on Zarude and threaten it with Bullet Punch.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Zarude's STAB combination allows it to threaten many tier staples like Primarina, Excadrill, and Slowking. U-turn grabs momentum on usual switch-ins such as Celesteela and Salamence. Jungle Healing allows Zarude to remove status conditions from moves such as Toxic from Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-W, while restoring 25% of its health. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Zarude to not worry about entry hazards, letting it constantly pivot throughout the game. Jolly is the required nature on the set so that Zarude can outspeed Nihilego and Thundurus-T.

Zarude is commonly seen on balance and bulky offense due to the easy pivoting provided by Heavy-Duty Boots and its ability to act as a status sponge against Toxic from Hippowdon and Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-W. Secondary pivots like Moltres, Thundurus-T, and Swampert all form potent pivoting cores with Zarude. Moltres appreciates Zarude luring in Grass- and Steel-types like Amoonguss, Scizor, and Skarmory, while Thundurus-T heavily pressures Celesteela and Moltres. Swampert can pivot into attacks from Celesteela and set entry hazards for Zarude to soften up Pokemon like Amoonguss with Stealth Rock. Other entry hazard setters like Cobalion and Excadrill also set Stealth Rock and appreciate Zarude dealing with Water-types such as Slowking and Swampert, while Zarude appreciates them dealing with Scizor and Rotom-H. Slowking and Celesteela provide a strong defensive backbone to support Zarude, checking threats like Azelf, Salamence, and Cobalion that hinder it. Zygarde-10%, Mamoswine, and Azelf are wallbreakers that appreciate Zarude bringing them in on Salamence, Tangrowth, and Amoonguss, as they often have trouble switching in safely due to their frailty.

Choice Scarf.description:
Zarude's high Speed allows it to be a great user of Choice Scarf that can revenge kill Pokemon such as Keldeo and Azelf in addition to boosted sweepers such as Gyarados and Dragon Dance Necrozma. Power Whip OHKOes Lycanroc-D and Keldeo. Darkest Lariat is Zarude's strongest Dark-type STAB move and can hit Jirachi and Azelf for huge damage. U-turn allows Zarude to pivot out on potential switch-ins such as Tangrowth and Salamence, allowing it to gain momentum. Close Combat is able to hit Cobalion, an otherwise easy switch-in, for heavy damage. Jungle Healing can get rid of status conditions such as a burn from Moltres's Flame Body and Slowking's Scald while regaining HP so that Zarude can be used in the long run in a battle but it is not ideal to lock into. It also allows Zarude to act as a reliable status sponge if it takes a Knock Off when Choice Scarf is not needed.

Choice Scarf Zarude is a solid pivot and revenge killer on bulky offense teams. It appreciates additional pivots such as Moltres, Slowking, and Thundurus-T that can form momentum cores and pivot out of unfavorable matchups. For example, Moltres can bring Zarude in on Water-types such as Slowking and Swampert. Entry hazard control from the likes of Salamence, Excadrill, and Mandibuzz allows Zarude to consistently pivot without worrying about hazard damage. They can also check threats like Scizor and Tapu Bulu. Thundurus-T, Keldeo, and Nidoking are wallbreakers that appreciate Zarude's pivot support and its ability to check Pokemon such as Swampert, with the wallbreakers KOing Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Skarmory in return. Swampert is an entry hazard setter that appreciates Zarude dealing with Keldeo, Gyarados, and Hydreigon for it, while Swampert can set Stealth Rock in return and also help deal with Pokemon like Salamence. Primarina and Azumarill can help deal with some of Zarude's checks such as Salamence.

ubers.overview: Regieleki is the fastest Pokemon in the game and can wallbreak with powerful Transistor-boosted STAB moves, so it can serve as an effective offensive spinner and revenge killer on hyper offensive teams. However, Regieleki suffers from a near-complete lack of coverage, rendering it near helpless against Ground-type Pokemon and bulky Electric-resistant Pokemon. It is also extremely frail, leaving it weak to priority moves, and provides no defensive utility.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

A dual screens set can be used to take advantage of Regieleki's high Speed, access to Rapid Spin, and the ability to threaten Defoggers. However, it cannot fit all of Rapid Spin, Wild Charge, and Explosion. Furthermore, it faces heavy competition from Grimmsnarl, which can set up dual screens more consistently thanks to its more useful defensive typing and utility moves such as Taunt and Thunder Wave. Thunder can be used on the special attacking set for increased firepower, achieving feats such as an OHKO on Yveltal and Ho-Oh and on Calyrex-S and offensive Necrozma-DM after Stealth Rock chip damage, though the accuracy is prohibitive. If used, Kyogre is a great partner to provide rain to ensure it connects. Rising Voltage can also be used on the special-oriented set in conjunction with Tapu Koko over Rapid Spin or Explosion.

Checks and Counters

Ground-type Pokemon: Ground-types such as Zygarde-C, Groudon, Excadrill, Landorus, and Gastrodon completely nullify Regieleki's powerful STAB moves.

Ferrothorn: Ferrothorn not only resists Electric-type moves but also withstands Explosion easily, and it can punish Rapid Spin with Iron Barbs.

Dragon-type Pokemon: Dragon-types such as Eternatus and Zekrom resist Regieleki's Electric-type STAB moves, though they often have to be wary of Explosion.

Ghost-type Pokemon: Ghost-types can prevent Regieleki from spinning away hazards, though they must be wary of Assurance and Electric-type moves. Giratina and Giratina-O notably resist Regieleki's STAB moves and threaten it with Shadow Sneak.

Priority: Regieleki takes heavy damage from priority attacks such as Yveltal's Sucker Punch and Marshadow's Shadow Sneak. Though priority users are often hard-pressed to switch in, Marshadow can take advantage of a Rapid Spin and force Regieleki out.

Physical Attacker.description:
A decently powerful Transistor-boosted Wild Charge and a phenomenal Speed tier let Regieleki revenge kill fast threats such as Choice Scarf Kyogre and Calyrex-S. It can also threaten common Defoggers such as Yveltal and Ho-Oh to keep entry hazards up. Wild Charge is used over Thunderbolt to hit specially defensive targets such as Yveltal harder while maintaining Attack EVs to power up Explosion. Assurance allows Regieleki to revenge kill Calyrex-S or smack it as it tries to switch in and spinblock while also nailing Shedinja. Thanks to Life Orb, Assurance also KOes 252 HP Lunala if it switches into Wild Charge. Explosion allows Regieleki to generate momentum, block Defog, and dent Electric-resistant Pokemon such as Eternatus, Zekrom, and Zygarde.

Regieleki should be used on hyper offense teams, which appreciate its Rapid Spin support and revenge killing capabilities while not suffering too much from its lack of defensive utility, and is a nice teammate to Sticky Web setters such as Shuckle and Slurpuff. It often has to use Explosion against Electric-resistant Pokemon, so teammates that can take advantage of the free switch are great partners, such as Xerneas for Dragon-types and Kyogre for Ground-types. Regieleki also struggles against physically defensive Steel-type Pokemon that can take Wild Charge, such as Necrozma-DM, which can notably chip it down with Rocky Helmet; therefore, teammates that can offensively deal with them such as Groudon are helpful.

Special Attacker.description:
A special set helps Regieleki utilize Volt Switch, which allows it to damage and pivot out against Electric-resistant Pokemon such as Eternatus and Zekrom so that a teammate can take advantage of them. Transistor-boosted Thunderbolt makes Regieleki a powerful revenge killer that can OHKO threats such as Kyogre and take out a lot of slightly weakened Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Yveltal, Calyrex-S, and offensive Necrozma-DM. Rapid Spin allows Regieleki to clear entry hazards in a pinch. Explosion prevents it from being total setup bait for Electric-resistant Pokemon such as Zygarde-C and Zekrom. A Rash nature is used instead of Mild in order to take priority attacks such as Marshadow's Shadow Sneak a little better and increase damage output. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead of Life Orb to pivot more freely throughout a match.

As Regieleki often pivots out against bulky Electric-resistant Pokemon, Pokemon such as Xerneas and Eternatus that can threaten them out help Regieleki wear them down over time. Similarly, Pokemon such as Kyogre and Calyrex-I that can take advantage of Ground-types after an Explosion are useful partners. Pokemon that appreciate Eternatus being worn down such as Kyogre benefit from Regieleki's support. As Regieleki provides offensive and Rapid Spin support, it pairs well with Sticky Web setters such as Shuckle and Slurpuff.

1v1.comments:
Other Options

Running Thunderbolt over Electro Ball is an option, giving Regieleki a reliable Electric-type STAB move that cannot miss. However, this comes at the cost of several significant matchups, like Aromatisse and Registeel, which is generally not worth the slight increase in accuracy in those few matchups where it matters.

Regieleki can run a fast specially defensive stall set with a Maranga Berry, Substitute, Eerie Impulse, Rest, and Thunder Cage. This allows it to lure some would-be counters like Sylveon, Nihilego, Goodra, and Mirror Coat Avalugg while retaining solid matchups against most other special attackers. However, this set loses to many physical attackers, and the bulk requirements mean that several Choice Scarf users can now outspeed Regieleki.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Description

Regieleki's amazing Speed stat and powerful Electric-type moves give it an unique niche in the metagame. Thunder Cage is its main STAB move, dealing solid damage and beating Endure users like Primarina, Blaziken, and Porygon-Z. Thunder deals more damage, which matters against Pokemon like Spectrier. Hyper Beam deals with some frail Pokemon that resist Electric, like Naganadel, Haxorus, and opposing Regieleki. Electro Ball covers for a few slow Pokemon like Registeel and specially defensive Aromatisse.

EVs

252 SpA EVs let Regieleki maximize its damage output, while 252 Speed EVs let it tie opposing Regieleki and maximize Electro Ball damage. The remaining EVs are put in Defense, as most priority moves and the few Choice Scarf users that outspeed Regieleki skew physically.

Usage Tips

Regieleki's matchups are simple: figure out what move can OHKO and use it. Against potential Endure users like Primarina and Galarian Moltres, Regieleki should use Thunder Cage to KO them with trapping damage if they use Endure. In situations where Thunder Cage deals sufficient damage to KO, it should be used over Thunder, as it has a smaller risk to miss.

monotype.overview:
Electric

With the highest base Speed stat in the game at 200, Regieleki can even outspeed boosted Pokemon such as +1 Quiver Dance Volcarona, Choice Scarf Gengar, and Choice Scarf Latios. Its ability Transistor combined with its gargantuan Speed stat, decent Special Attack, high-power Rising Voltage, and Choice Specs makes Regieleki a formidable wallbreaker that can shred apart teams with no Electric-type immunity; even bulky resistant Pokemon and dedicated special walls like Kyurem and Blissey swiftly get 2HKOed. It does well against types like Fighting, Dark, Psychic, and Ghost that have trouble taking on Electric-type attacks. However, Regieleki suffers from having a very sparse movepool that does not include proper coverage moves to hit Ground-types for decent damage and, as a result, is left walled by Ground-type Pokemon. This forces the Regieleki user to think twice before attacking, since a Ground-type Pokemon could switch into it for free. It also has a horrendous bulk, which makes it prone to being KOed by any decent offensive Pokemon, especially priority users such as Bisharp, Dragonite, Rillaboom, and Crawdaunt. Regieleki faces a ton of overlap for improving matchups, as Electric teams are naturally good against types without immunities. It's a niche choice at best due to this.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Electric

A suicide lead set with dual screens, Explosion, and Light Clay as an item is an option for more offensive Electric teams.

Checks and Counters

Electric

Electric-immune Pokemon: Ground-type Pokemon have an easier time beating Regieleki; since it has a poor movepool, it cannot deal good damage to them reliably and is therefore hard-walled. Other Electric-immune Pokemon like Zeraora and Alolan Marowak with Lightning Rod can also beat Regieleki, though the latter has to careful of switching in on Ancient Power.

Strong Priority Users: Owing to its horrible bulk, powerful priority users like Bisharp, Azumarill, Urshifu-R, and Dragonite can all deal with Regieleki easily once it is chipped.

Grass-types: Tapu Bulu can reliably check Regieleki, since it overrides Electric Terrain, removing the boost to Regieleki's STAB moves. Grassy Glide Rillaboom is another check to Regieleki.

Wallbreaker.description:
The boosts from its ability, its held item, and Electric Terrain allow Regieleki to hit like a truck with Rising Voltage, OHKOing neutral targets and 2HKOing bulky Electric-resistant Pokemon like Kyurem and Ferrothorn. Thunderbolt is a safe move to use outside of Electric Terrain and also hits non-grounded Pokemon like Latias for good damage. Volt Switch lets it keep up momentum for the team and bring in a teammate against Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Cradily when Electric Terrain is not active. Ancient Power lets Regieleki hit certain Pokemon like Lightning Rod Alolan Marowak for a 2HKO, letting Regieleki beat it on the switch. It is also Regieleki's best attack to hit Landorus-T. Rapid Spin can be used over Ancient Power to compress roles on offensive Electric-type teams. Maximum Speed investment with a Timid Nature makes it as fast as possible, letting it outspeed fast Pokemon like Choice Scarf Latios. Choice Specs boosts Regieleki's decent Special Attack to greater heights, making its attacks harder to tank.

Tapu Koko is a crucial teammate, as it provides Regieleki with Electric Terrain, which further boosts the power of its moves—especially Rising Voltage. Tapu Koko can also deal with Dragon- and Dark-type Pokemon for Regieleki such as Garchomp and Hydreigon as well as Ground-type Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon with Grass Knot. Teammates like Zeraora and Alolan Raichu greatly benefit from Regieleki's wallbreaking capabilities, as it's able to blow past Pokemon that check those two such as defensive Zapdos, Amoonguss, Ferrothorn, Blissey, and specially defensive Drapion. In return, Zeraora provides Knock Off support and can use its Choice Band set to form a wallbreaking core with Regieleki. Alolan Raichu, on the other hand, can capitalize on Regieleki's wallbreaking ability to clean teams late-game and take care of Ground-type Pokemon like Gastrodon, Swampert, and Hippowdon with Grass Knot, which Regieleki dislikes facing. Rotom-W and Zapdos provide a good defensive backbone and pair of Ground immunities for Regieleki to rely on while also providing Defog support to keep it healthy and not slowed down by Sticky Web. Defensive Zapdos with Static also checks problematic Pokemon like Grassy Glide Rillaboom and Tapu Bulu for Regieleki and takes care of them with Heat Wave.
